To serve, divide the arugula between plates or bowls, and top with pasta salad. Drizzle balsamic vinaigrette over salad and sprinkle with remaining basil. Enjoy!

name: Caribbean Black Bean Stew with Mango Salsa & Rice
ingredients: 16 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add water and salt, then bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce the heat to low. Cook the rice until the liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove the rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Drain and rinse beans in a colander; set aside to drain further.
Peel and small dice onion. Peel and mince garlic.
Preheat a medium saucepan over medium-high heat.
Seed and small dice bell pepper.
Once the saucepan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add onion, garlic, and bell pepper; cook, stirring occasionally, until veggies begin to soften, about 3 minutes.

Meanwhile, peel and chop sweet potato into ½-inch pieces. Add to the pan with the veggies along with the beans, broth, and spices. Stir and bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce heat to a simmer and cook, stirring occasionally, until potatoes are fork-tender, about 10 minutes.
Peel mango and slice the flesh away from the pit, starting with the flat sides; small dice and place in a medium bowl.
Trim and mince green onions; add to the bowl with the mango.
Shave the cilantro leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl.

Quarter jalapeño pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs of the jalapeño with a spoon. Finely dice and add to the bowl. (Be careful, with jalapeños, do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Juice lime into the bowl and stir to combine the salsa.
To serve, divide rice, stew, and mango salsa between bowls. Enjoy!

name: Carrot, Beet & Goat Cheese Salad with Lemon Poppy Seed Vinaigrette
instructions: Place eggs in a small saucepan, cover with water, and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to a simmer and cook for 8 minutes. Drain hot water and add ice or run under cold water to cool.
Wash and dry the fresh produce (skip the mixed greens if they came pre-washed).
Juice the lemon into a small bowl.
Add the oil, Dijon, maple syrup, salt, and poppy seeds to the bowl with the lemon juice. Whisk to combine the dressing.
Peel the carrots and beet, then trim off and discard the ends. Use a julienne peeler or box grater to coarsely cut or grate the carrots, followed by the beet; set aside.
Shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard the stems and coarsely chop the leaves.
Peel and quarter the eggs lengthwise.
To serve, divide the mixed greens between plates, top with hard boiled egg, carrots, beets, crumbled goat cheese, and parsley. Drizzle with poppy seed vinaigrette. Enjoy!

name: Carrot Salad Lettuce Wraps with Hard-Boiled Eggs, Mayo & Capers
instructions: Place eggs in a small saucepan, cover with water, and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to a simmer and cook for 8 minutes. Drain hot water and add ice or run under cold water to cool; set aside.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Juice lemon into a medium bowl. Add oil, honey, Dijon, and spices, then whisk to combine the dressing.
Shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl with the dressing.
Peel, trim, and coarsely grate carrots. Add to the bowl, stir to combine the salad, and set aside.
Peel and halve the eggs. Season with salt.
Place mayo, water, and additional salt in a small bowl. Whisk to combine.
Separate the lettuce into leaves. Pile leaves, in stacks of two per wrap, onto plates; fill with carrot salad and eggs. Spoon mayo sauce over eggs, top with capers, and season with pepper. Enjoy!

name: Cauliflower-Asparagus Baked Penne with Ricotta, Mozzarella & Parsley
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Fill a medium saucepan halfway with hot water (from the tap), cover, and bring to a boil.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Cut cauliflower head into quarters, then trim off and discard the leaves and thick stem. Roughly chop into ½-inch pieces.
Once the water in the saucepan is boiling, uncover, add cauliflower, pasta, and salt; stir for a few seconds. Cook until pasta is almost tender, about 7 minutes.
Meanwhile, snap or cut off the woody ends of the asparagus and cut into 1-inch pieces. Set aside.
Peel and mince garlic; place in a medium bowl.
Shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add half to the bowl with the garlic (reserving the rest for garnish).
When the pasta is almost tender, add asparagus to the pan; continue to cook until the pasta and veggies are tender, 3-4 minutes more.
Meanwhile, add tomato sauce, ricotta, and spices to the bowl with the garlic and parsley; whisk to combine the sauce.
Coarsely grate mozzarella.
When the pasta and veggies are done, drain in a colander. Add pasta and veggies to the bowl with the sauce; stir to combine.
Transfer the saucy pasta to a baking dish, spread out in an even layer, and sprinkle with cheese. Place baking dish in the oven and bake until cheese is melted and bubbly, 10-12 minutes.
To serve, divide pasta bake between bowls and top with reserved parsley. Enjoy!

name: Cauliflower-Bacon "Mac & Cheese" Gratin with Mixed Greens
ingredients: ½ (5 oz) pkg spring mix (mixed greens)
instructions: Fill a medium saucepan about halfway with hot water (from the tap); add salt, cover, and bring to a boil over high heat.
Meanwhile, wash, dry, and cut the cauliflower head into quarters, then trim off and discard the leaves and thick stem. Cut into bite-sized pieces.
Once the water is boiling, add cauliflower and cook until tender-crisp, 6-8 minutes. Drain in a colander and set aside.
While the cauliflower is cooking, preheat an ovenproof skillet over medium-high heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add bacon and cook until crispy, 3-5 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate lined with paper towels, crumble or chop into small pieces, and set aside.
Meanwhile, preheat oven to broil on high and position rack under the broiler.
Cut cream cheese into small pieces. Coarsely grate cheddar; set both aside.
Return skillet (with bacon fat) to medium heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add milk and spices; whisk to combine and bring to a simmer. Once simmering, add cream cheese, a few pieces at a time, whisking until melted and combined, 2-3 minutes.
Add half the cheddar to the skillet and whisk until melted.
Add cooked cauliflower to the skillet and stir to combine. Sprinkle with remaining cheddar and place in the oven; broil until the top is golden and bubbly, 2-3 minutes. Remove from the oven.
Meanwhile, place oil, vinegar, Dijon, salt, and pepper in a medium bowl; whisk to combine the dressing.
Wash and dry the spring mix (skip this step if it came pre-washed). Add to the bowl with the dressing and toss to combine the salad.
Divide cauliflower between plates and sprinkle with bacon. Serve with salad on the side and enjoy!

name: Cauliflower & Chickpea Coconut Curry with Couscous
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
½ (13.5 fl oz) can coconut milk
instructions: Wash cauliflower and tomatoes. Cut the cauliflower into bite-sized florets. Medium dice the tomatoes.
Heat a sauté pan over medium-high heat.
Peel and mince onion and garlic.
Coat bottom of pan with oil. Add onion and cook, stirring frequently, until softened, 3-4 minutes.
Drain and rinse chickpeas.
Add garlic and curry powder to pan and stir with onion until fragrant, 15-30 seconds.
Add cauliflower and chickpeas and stir until heated through, 1-2 minutes.
Add tomatoes, coconut milk, salt, and pepper; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to a simmer and cover. Cook until cauliflower is tender and liquid thickens, about 10 minutes.
In a small saucepan, bring broth to a boil. Remove from heat, add couscous, and stir. Cover and let stand for 10 minutes.
Wash and dry cilantro. Shave the leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves. Stir ½ into the curry (save the rest for garnishing).
Uncover couscous and fluff with a fork.
To serve, place couscous in a bowl, top with curry and garnish with remaining cilantro. Enjoy!

name: Cauliflower Macaroni & Cheese with Lemon-Parsley Butter Lettuce Salad
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Fill a medium saucepan about halfway with hot water (from the tap); cover and bring to a boil.
While the water is heating, cut the cauliflower head into quarters, then trim off and discard the leaves and thick stem. Using a box grater or food processor, coarsely grate the cauliflower.
Once the water in the saucepan is boiling, uncover, and add cauliflower, pasta, and salt; stir for a few seconds. Cook until pasta reaches desired firmness, 8-10 minutes.
Meanwhile, juice lemon into a medium bowl.
Shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add half of the parsley to the bowl with lemon juice (reserving the rest for the pasta).
Add oil, honey, salt, and pepper to the bowl; whisk to combine the dressing and set aside.
Coarsely grate cheddar. Cut cream cheese into small pieces.
Preheat a small saucepan over medium heat.
Once the pan is hot, add milk, cheddar, cream cheese, and spices. Cook, whisking frequently, until cheeses melt and combine, 2-3 minutes; remove cheese sauce from heat.
When the cauliflower and pasta are done, drain in a strainer, and return to the pan. Add cheese sauce and stir to combine the cauliflower macaroni & cheese. Cover and set aside.
Chop or tear lettuce into bite-sized pieces and add to the bowl with the dressing; toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide cauliflower macaroni & cheese and salad between plates. Top pasta with reserved parsley and crushed red pepper. Enjoy!

name: Cauliflower & Red Lentil Soup with Avocado and Cilantro Yogurt
ingredients: 16 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and medium dice the carrot and onion; place both in a medium bowl.
Trim off and discard the leaves and thick stem of the cauliflower, then roughly chop it into bite-sized pieces; add to the bowl with the carrot and onion.
Preheat a medium saucepan over medium-high heat.
Once the saucepan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add veggies and cook, stirring occasionally, until soft, about 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel and mince or grate the ginger; peel and mince the garlic.
Coarsely chop the tomato.
Once the veggies are soft, add the ginger, garlic, and tomato to the pan. Cook, stirring frequently, until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Stir in broth, water, lentils, and spices. Cover and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to a simmer and cook until lentils are tender, about 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, shave the cilantro leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves.
Place cilantro, yogurt, and salt in a small bowl; whisk to combine.
Halve and pit the avocado; slice crosswise while still in the skin and scoop out with a spoon.
Using an immersion (hand) blender, process the soup until smooth. Alternatively, transfer soup to a regular blender and blend on high until smooth.
To serve, divide the soup between bowls and top with yogurt and avocado. Enjoy!

name: Celery-Apple Quinoa Salad with Peanuts, Dates, Parmesan & Parsley
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: In a small saucepan, combine quinoa and broth; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to a simmer, cover, and cook for 15 minutes. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Place oil, vinegar, maple syrup, and spices in a medium bowl. Whisk to combine the dressing.
Peel and slice shallot crosswise into thin rounds. Add to the bowl with the dressing.
Trim and thinly slice celery crosswise. Add to the bowl.
Quarter, core, and thinly slice apples. Add to the bowl.
Shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl.
Roughly chop peanuts and dates. Add both to the bowl and set aside.
Transfer the cooked quinoa to a baking sheet pan. Spread out in an even layer and let cool for 5 minutes.
Finely grate Parmesan. Add to the bowl, along with the cooled quinoa, and stir to combine the salad.
To serve, divide the salad between plates or bowls. Enjoy!

name: Charbroiled Beef Kebabs with Curried Vegetables & Basmati Rice
ingredients: ¾ lb striploin (New York strip) steak
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Season the rice with salt, add water and bring to a boil over high heat.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Preheat oven to broil and position rack under the broiler.
Season steak with salt and pepper and cut into 1 inch cubes.

Once the liquid with the rice comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce the heat to low. Cook the rice until the liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove the rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Peel the onion, cut it into quarters and separate it into slices; place in a medium bowl.
Trim off the ends of the zucchini then cut in half lengthwise; Cut into 2 inch pieces and add to the bowl with the onion.
Cut peppers into quarters, remove seeds and membranes; cut in half crosswise and add to bowl with zucchini and onion.
Add oil, curry powder, pepper and salt to the bowl with the veggies, toss to coat.
Thread beef, onion, squash and peppers onto skewers and place onto the broiler pan. If you don't have skewers, spread veggies and steak on the broiler pan.
Broil in preheated oven, turning every 3 minutes, until done, about 12 minutes. If you aren't using skewers simply toss the vegetables and beef every 3 minutes.
Shave the cilantro leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves.
Uncover the rice and fluff with a fork; gently fold in minced cilantro, reserving 1 tbsp for garnish.
To serve, divide rice and skewers between plates and garnish with reserved cilantro. Enjoy!

name: Charred Broccoli Bowl with Chicken, Edamame, Almonds, Cilantro & Lime
instructions: Preheat oven to broil on high; position rack under the broiler.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.

Separate broccoli crowns into bite-sized florets and cut stems into smaller pieces; place in a large bowl. Add oil, salt, and pepper, and toss to combine; transfer to a baking sheet and spread out in a single, even layer. Reserve bowl for later use.
Place broccoli in the oven and broil, turning halfway through, until broccoli is crisp-tender and lightly charred around the edges, 12-15 minutes.
Meanwhile, zest the lime into the large bowl, then juice half the lime into the same bowl. Cut remaining lime into wedges and set aside.
Peel and mince the shallot and garlic. Peel and grate or mince the ginger; transfer everything to the bowl with the lime juice.
Add fish sauce, soy sauce, chili-garlic sauce, and sugar to the bowl and whisk to combine the sauce.
When the broccoli is done cooking, remove from the oven and transfer to the bowl with the sauce; stir to combine.
Cut chicken into bite-sized pieces and place in a medium bowl. Add cornstarch, salt, and pepper to the bowl and gently toss to coat the chicken.
Preheat a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add the chicken and cook, stirring often, until golden and almost cooked through, 5-6 minutes.
Meanwhile, shave the cilantro leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl with the broccoli.

Add edamame to the skillet with the chicken and continue to cook, stirring often, until chicken and edamame are cooked through, 2-3 minutes. Transfer to the bowl with the broccoli, making sure to scrape all of the chicken juices into the bowl; toss to combine.
To serve, divide the broccoli mixture between bowls or plates; top with almonds and garnish with lime wedges. Enjoy!

name: Charred Broccoli Flatbread with Lemony Ricotta, Chili Honey & Salad
ingredients: ½ (5 oz) pkg spring mix (mixed greens)
instructions: Preheat oven to broil on high and position the rack in the upper third of the oven.
Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the mixed greens if they came pre-washed.)
Arrange flatbreads on a baking sheet pan. Place in the oven and broil, flipping once, until golden and slightly crispy, 1-2 minutes per side. Remove from oven and set aside.

Meanwhile, separate broccoli into bite-sized florets and cut stems into smaller pieces; transfer to another baking sheet. Drizzle with oil, season with salt and pepper, and toss to coat; spread out in a single layer.
When the flatbreads are done, place broccoli in the oven and broil, tossing halfway through, until crisp-tender and lightly charred around the edges, about 10 minutes. Remove from oven.
While the broccoli is cooking, place honey, vinegar, crushed red pepper, and salt in a small bowl; whisk to combine the chili honey and set aside.
Zest lemon into another small bowl (set lemon aside for later use).
Add ricotta, salt, and pepper to the bowl with the lemon zest; stir to combine the lemony ricotta. Set aside.
Juice lemon into a medium bowl; add oil, Dijon, salt, and pepper. Whisk to combine the dressing and set aside.
Spread lemony ricotta over each flatbread, then top with the charred broccoli. Slice flatbreads into wedges.
Add mixed greens to the bowl with the dressing and toss to combine the salad.
Divide flatbreads between plates and drizzle with chili honey. Serve with mixed greens on the side and enjoy!

name: Cheddar, Apple & Onion Quesadilla with Arugula-Radish Salad
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the arugula if it came pre-washed.)
Preheat a large skillet over medium heat.
While the skillet heats up, peel, halve, and thinly slice onion into half-moons.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add onion, salt, and pepper; cook, stirring occasionally, until onions are soft and golden brown, 6-7 minutes. Remove from heat.
Meanwhile, quarter and core apple, then thinly slice.
Coarsely grate cheese.
Place tortillas on a flat surface and divide onion, apple, and cheese between them, arranging the filling on one half of each tortilla; fold in half to close.
Wipe the skillet clean with paper towels and return to medium heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add quesadillas and cook until cheese is melted and tortillas are golden, 2½-3 minutes per side. Remove to a plate.
Meanwhile, place oil, vinegar, Dijon, salt, and pepper in a medium bowl; whisk to combine the dressing.
Trim and thinly slice radishes; add to the bowl with the dressing.
Halve and pit avocado; scoop out with a spoon and medium dice the flesh. Add to the bowl, along with arugula, and toss to combine the salad.
Cut each quesadilla into wedges and divide between plates. Serve with salad on the side and enjoy!

name: Cheddar Crusted Chicken with Mashed Sweet Potatoes & Roasted Broccoli
ingredients: ¾ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F. Line a baking sheet pan with aluminum foil to make cleanup easier (optional), then coat with oil.
Coarsely grate cheese into a medium bowl; add bread crumbs and spices. Stir to combine the coating.
Pat chicken dry with paper towels and place on a cutting board. Holding a knife parallel to the cutting board, cut the chicken in half horizontally to form thin cutlets.
Spread mayo over both sides of the cutlets, then dredge in the bread crumb coating, pressing firmly to adhere. Transfer cutlets to one side of the baking sheet and drizzle with oil.
Wash and dry broccoli; using a clean cutting board, separate broccoli into bite-sized florets and cut stems into smaller pieces. Add to the other side of the baking sheet with the chicken.
Drizzle broccoli with oil, season with salt and pepper, then toss to coat; spread out in an even layer.
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and bake, flipping chicken and tossing broccoli halfway through, until chicken is cooked through, 15-18 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, wash, dry, peel, and medium dice sweet potato; place in a medium saucepan. Cover with hot water (from the tap) and bring to a boil over high heat.
Once the liquid in the saucepan is boiling, reduce heat to medium, cover, and simmer until sweet potatoes are tender, about 10 minutes.
When the sweet potatoes are done, drain in a colander, and return to the pan. Add oil, salt, and pepper, then mash until smooth.
To serve, divide mashed sweet potatoes, chicken, and broccoli between plates. Enjoy!

name: Cheddar-Panko Crusted Pork Cutlets with Bell Pepper & Broccoli Slaw
instructions: Place egg in a medium bowl and beat with a whisk or fork until smooth. Set aside.
Grate cheese into another medium bowl. Add bread crumbs and spices, then stir to combine. Set aside.
Pat pork dry with paper towels and place on a cutting board. Holding a knife parallel to the cutting board, cut the chops in half horizontally to form thin cutlets.
Preheat a large skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, dip the cutlets into the beaten egg (letting the excess drip off), then into the bread crumb mixture, pressing gently to adhere. Transfer to a plate.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add the breaded cutlets and pan-fry until golden brown and cooked through, about 3 minutes per side. Remove from heat.
While the chops are cooking, place mayo in a clean medium bowl. Add vinegar, salt, and pepper, then whisk to combine the dressing.
Wash and dry bell pepper; using a clean cutting board, trim, seed, and slice lengthwise into thin strips. Add to the bowl with the dressing, along with the broccoli slaw, and stir to combine.
To serve, divide slaw between plates or bowls. Top with pork cutlets and enjoy!

name: Cheeseburger Quesadilla with Pico de Gallo & Greek Yogurt
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Quarter the tomatoes and transfer to a medium bowl (that will hold the salsa).
Quarter the jalapeño pepper lengthwise; remove and discard the stem, seeds, and membranes. Finely dice the pepper and add to the salsa bowl.
Using a knife, shave the cilantro leaves off the stems at a downward angle, working away from your body; discard the stems and finely chop the leaves. Add to the salsa bowl.
Heat a nonstick skillet over medium heat.
Trim off and discard the ends of the onion and remove the outer layer; small dice the onion (cut into ¼-inch pieces). Add ½ of the onion to the salsa bowl and leave the rest on the cutting board.
Once the skillet is hot, add coconut oil to the skillet and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add the remaining diced onion to the skillet; cook, stirring frequently, until softened, 3 to 5 minutes.
Juice the lime and add to the salsa bowl.
Season the salsa with salt and pepper; mix together and set aside.

Add the ground beef to the skillet and season with chili powder, cumin, salt, and pepper. Cook, breaking apart with a spoon, until the beef is browned and crumbly, 3 to 4 minutes. Once done, transfer the mixture to a bowl.
While the beef cooks, coarsely grate 1 cup of cheddar.
Once the beef mixture has been transferred, remove any leftover bits from the skillet.
Place the tortillas on a flat surface. Layer one half of each tortilla with ¼ of the cheese, ½ of the beef mixture, and another ¼ of the cheese. Fold tortillas over to close.

Place both quesadillas in the skillet, straight edges next to each other. Cook until golden brown on both sides and the cheese is melted, 2-4 minutes per side. Once done, transfer the quesadillas to a cutting board.
Cut each quesadilla into 4 wedges.
To serve, divide the quesadillas between plates and serve with the pico de gallo and Greek yogurt. Enjoy!

name: "Cheesesteak" Bake with Peppers, Mushrooms, Onions & Melted Mozzarella
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim, seed, and slice bell peppers into thin strips; transfer to a baking sheet pan.
Slice mushrooms into ¼-inch thick pieces; add to the baking sheet with the peppers.
Peel and mince garlic; peel, halve, and thinly slice onion into half-moons. Add both to the baking sheet, toss to combine the veggies, then spread out in an even layer.
Cut butter into small pieces and sprinkle over the veggies; season with salt and pepper.
Place veggies in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and bake, stirring halfway through, until tender, about 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the steak dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with spices on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add butter and swirl to coat the bottom. Add steak and cook until desired doneness, 2-5 minutes per side. Transfer to a clean plate and let rest for 5 minutes.
While the steak is cooking, coarsely grate mozzarella.
Shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves.
When the veggies are done, remove from the oven. Turn oven to broil on high and position rack under the broiler.

Thinly slice steak against the grain. Arrange steak slices over the roasted veggies and sprinkle with cheese. Return baking sheet to the oven and broil until cheese is melted, about 1 minute. Remove from oven.
To serve, divide the cheesesteak bake between plates and top with parsley. Enjoy!

name: Cheesy Asparagus Lemon Chicken Bake
ingredients: ¾ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
In a small bowl, mix together the spices.

Holding a knife parallel to the cutting board, cut the chicken in half horizontally to form thin fillets. Place chicken fillets in a baking dish and season with the spice mixture (save the bowl to use later).
Cut (or snap off) and discard the woody ends of the asparagus. Divide asparagus and arrange on top of each chicken breast.

Grate the zest from the lemon and transfer to the bowl used for the spices. Juice the lemon into the same bowl. Add oil and whisk to combine. Pour the lemon oil mixture over the chicken and asparagus.
Grate mozzarella cheese.
Sprinkle the cheese over the asparagus and place in the oven; bake until chicken is cooked through, about 20 minutes.
Shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves.
A few minutes before the end of the cooking time, change setting to broil and continue baking until the chicken and cheese are golden, 1-2 minutes.
To serve, divide the chicken topped with asparagus between plates and garnish with parsley and crushed red pepper. Enjoy!

name: Cheesy "Baked Beans on Toast" with Mixed Greens & Celery Salad
ingredients: ½ (5 oz) pkg spring mix (mixed greens)
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F. Position racks in the upper and lower thirds of the oven.
Drain and rinse beans in a colander, then transfer to a small baking dish.
Peel, halve, and mince shallot; add to the baking dish along with tomato sauce, maple syrup, Dijon, Worcestershire, and spices. Stir to combine.
Place baking dish on lower rack of the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and bake, stirring halfway through, until beans are soft and sauce has thickened, about 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Place yogurt, mayo, water, vinegar, salt, and pepper in a medium bowl; whisk to combine the dressing.
Trim and slice celery crosswise into thin pieces; trim and medium dice cucumber. Add both to the bowl with the dressing and set aside.
Coarsely grate cheddar.
Arrange bread slices on a baking sheet pan; place on upper rack of the oven and toast, flipping once, until golden, 4-5 minutes. Remove from oven.
When the baked beans are done, remove from oven and stir well. Divide beans between toast slices and top each with an even layer of cheese.
Return baking sheet to upper rack of the oven and bake until cheese is melted, 3-4 minutes. Remove from oven.
Just before serving, add mixed greens to the bowl with the dressing and toss to combine the salad.
Divide "baked beans on toast" between plates and serve with salad on the side. Enjoy!

name: Cheesy Beef & Cilantro-Lime Cauliflower Rice Burrito Bowl
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add ground beef and spices. Cook, breaking apart with a spoon, until browned and crumbly, 3-4 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel and mince garlic. Once the beef is done cooking, add the garlic and stir to combine. Transfer to a medium bowl and loosely cover with foil.
Peel and small dice onion.
Return skillet to medium-high heat, add butter and swirl to coat the bottom. Add onion and cook, stirring often, until it begins to soften, 3-4 minutes.
Meanwhile, cut the cauliflower head into quarters, then trim off and discard the leaves and thick stem. Using a box grater or food processor, coarsely grate the cauliflower.
Add cauliflower and spices to the skillet with the onion. Continue to cook, stirring often, until cauliflower is lightly golden and cooked through, 5-7 minutes more.
Grate the cheese.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves.
Cut half the lime into wedges, reserving the rest for the cauliflower rice.
When the cauliflower rice is done, juice remaining lime into the skillet. Add cilantro and beef; gently stir to combine and continue to cook until heated through, 1-2 minutes more.
Meanwhile, halve tomatoes. Halve and pit avocado; slice thinly while still in skin, then scoop out with a spoon.
To serve, divide cauliflower rice mixture between bowls or plates and top with grated cheese, tomatoes, and avocado. Garnish with lime wedges and enjoy!

name: Cheesy Broccoli Quinoa Patties with Tangy Cucumber Salad
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: In a small saucepan, combine quinoa and broth; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to a simmer, cover, and cook for 15 minutes. Remove from heat and spread onto a baking sheet in a thin layer to cool.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Preheat a large skillet over medium heat.
Peel and small dice the onion; set half aside in a medium bowl for the salad.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add the other half of the onion to the skillet; cook, stirring frequently, until softened, 3-4 minutes.
Finely mince the broccoli (you should have about 2 cups). Add to the skillet along with the onion and cook another 3-4 minutes, stirring frequently. Remove from heat and set aside.
Grate the cheddar.
In a large bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, onion, broccoli, cheese, panko, and eggs.
Form the quinoa vegetable mixture into patties using a ¼-cup measure, firmly pressing the mixture together between your hands.
Wipe out the skillet with a paper towel and heat over medium-high heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Place the patties in the skillet and cook for 5-6 minutes; flip and cook another 2-3 minutes, until golden brown on both sides.
Trim the ends of the cucumber, then thinly slice.
Add cucumber, oil, vinegar, salt, and pepper to the bowl with the onion. Stir to combine.
To serve, divide the quinoa patties and cucumber salad between plates. Enjoy!

name: Cheesy Cheddar Broccoli & Chicken
ingredients: ½ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F.
Wash the broccoli and cut into bite-sized florets; transfer to a large pot. Fill with just enough water to cover florets and add salt to season.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to a simmer and cook until the broccoli is fork-tender, 5-6 minutes.
Add yogurt, mayo, curry powder, salt, pepper and garlic powder to a medium mixing bowl.
Coarsely grate the cheddar, set aside.
When broccoli is done, drain well in a colander and add to a baking dish.
Pour yogurt mixture over broccoli and top with cheddar cheese. Bake in the oven for 10 minutes.
While broccoli mixture cooks, heat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Pat the chicken breasts dry with paper towel and place on a plate; season with salt and pepper on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Carefully place the chicken breasts in the skillet; cook until the chicken is golden brown and cooked through, 4-5 minutes per side.
To serve, divide broccoli and chicken between plates. Enjoy!

name: Cheesy Chicken Asparagus Bake with Sun-Dried Tomatoes & Olives
ingredients: ¾ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Wash, dry, and snap (or cut) off woody ends of the asparagus; place in a baking dish, arranging the spears in an even layer.

Pat the chicken dry with paper towels and place on a cutting board. Holding a knife parallel to the cutting board, cut the chicken in half horizontally to form thin cutlets. Season both sides with spices and arrange on top of the asparagus in an even layer.
Using a clean cutting board, peel and mince garlic; place in a small bowl.
Mince sun-dried tomatoes and olives; add both to the bowl with the garlic, along with cream cheese, and mash with the back of a spoon to combine. Spread over the top side of the chicken cutlets.
Finely grate Parmesan and sprinkle over the chicken.
Wash, dry, and juice lemon over the chicken, then drizzle with oil.
Place baking dish in the oven and bake until the asparagus is tender and chicken is cooked through, about 20 minutes.
When the chicken is done, change oven setting to broil on high; continue to cook until topping is golden, 1-2 minutes more.
To serve, divide asparagus and chicken between plates; drizzle with sauce from the dish and enjoy!

name: Cheesy Chicken Taquitos with Pico de Gallo Corn Salad & Yogurt Crema
ingredients: ¾ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat chicken dry with paper towels and place on a cutting board. Cut chicken into bite sized cubes.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add chicken to the skillet and season with spices. Stir-fry until golden brown and cooked through, 3-4 minutes. Remove from heat.
Meanwhile, warm tortillas in another skillet, oven, or microwave (optional), 15-30 seconds.
Coarsely grate cheddar.
Coat baking sheet with a thin layer of oil to prevent sticking.
Fill tortillas with chicken and cheese. Roll tightly and place seam-side down on the sheet pan. Place in the oven and bake until golden and crispy, 10-12 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Place corn in a colander and run under cold water to thaw. Pat dry with paper towels and transfer to a medium bowl.
Using a clean cutting board, halve tomatoes. Peel and small dice onion. Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince leaves. Add everything to the bowl with the corn.
Juice half the lime into the bowl with the corn, season with salt, and toss to combine the salad.
Juice the other half of the lime into a small bowl, add yogurt, and whisk to combine the crema.
To serve, divide taquitos between plates, top with pico de gallo salad, and drizzle with yogurt crema. Enjoy!

name: Cheesy Chicken Tortilla Bake
ingredients: ¾ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
instructions: Preheat oven to broil and position rack under the broiler.
Add chicken and salt to a medium saucepan. Cover with water and bring to a boil.
Turn heat down to medium and simmer until chicken is cooked through, about 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat oil in a second saucepan over medium heat.
Peel and small dice onion. Peel and mince garlic. Add both to second preheated pan.

Wash and dry bell pepper and jalapeno. Seed and remove ribs with a spoon. Be careful, with jalapenos, not to touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.
Small dice all peppers and add to the pan.
Season with chili powder, cumin, and salt. Cook until vegetables are softened, about 5 minutes.
Drain diced tomatoes; discard juice and add tomatoes to the pan.
Add yogurt, mayo, and flour to the pan, stirring to combine. Bring mixture to a boil and then reduce heat to minimum.
When chicken is done, drain and shred with a fork. Add to vegetable and yogurt mixture.
To assemble, place a tortilla on the bottom of a baking dish. Cover with half of the chicken mixture. Add a second tortilla and remainder of the chicken mixture.
Top with cheese. Broil for 3 minutes until cheese on top melts and becomes golden brown.
Trim off and discard the ends of the green onions; cut the onions crosswise into ¼-inch pieces at an angle.
Shave the cilantro leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves.
To serve, divide the tortilla between plates, top with green onions, cilantro, and a drizzle of yogurt. Enjoy!

name: Cheesy Chicken Tortilla Burger with Special Sauce & Side Salad
instructions: Place chicken, bread crumbs, Worcestershire, salt, and pepper in a medium bowl; mix with your hands until well combined. Divide the chicken mixture into 2 portions and form into ½-inch thick patties; place on a plate and set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats, up thinly slice cheese.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add burger patties and cook, undisturbed, until golden underneath, 3-4 minutes; flip patties, top with cheese, and cook an additional 3-4 minutes, until cooked through. Remove to a clean plate.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Place oil, vinegar, Dijon, honey, and spices in a clean medium bowl. Whisk to combine the dressing.
Slice one tomato crosswise into thin rounds; medium dice remaining tomato. Place slices on another plate and add diced tomato to the bowl with the dressing.

Separate lettuce into leaves. Set aside a few leaves per burger and chop (or tear) remaining leaves into bite-sized pieces. Add whole leaves to the plate and chopped lettuce to the bowl. Set the plate aside.
Trim and quarter cucumber lengthwise, then cut crosswise into bite-sized pieces. Add to the bowl and toss to combine the salad. Set aside.
Place mayo, ketchup, Dijon, and cayenne in a small bowl. Whisk to combine the special sauce and set aside.
Warm tortillas in another skillet, oven, or microwave (optional).

To assemble the burgers, place half of the tortillas on a flat surface, then top with cheesy burger patties, lettuce leaves, tomato slices, and special sauce. Close with the remaining tortillas and cut in half.
To serve, divide chicken burgers and salad between plates. Enjoy!

name: Cheesy Egg Toast with Lemony Dill, Spinach, Radish, & Mixed Pea Salad
ingredients: ½ (8 oz) pkg sugar snap peas
instructions: Place eggs in a small saucepan, cover with water, and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to a simmer and cook for 8 minutes. Drain hot water and add ice or run under cold water to cool.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)
Place peas in a colander and run under cold water to thaw; set aside to drain.
Juice lemon into a medium bowl.
Peel and mince garlic and shallot. Add both to the bowl with the lemon, along with oil, honey, Dijon, salt, and pepper; whisk to combine the dressing.
Trim and thinly slice radishes and celery; add both to the bowl.
Cut sugar snap peas crosswise into ½-inch pieces; add to the bowl, toss to combine, and set aside.
Preheat oven to broil on high and position rack in the upper third of the oven.
Peel and mince additional garlic; place in a small bowl along with mayo, salt, and pepper. Stir to combine.
Peel and coarsely grate eggs. Coarsely grate cheese; add both to the bowl with the mayo and stir to combine.
Split rolls in half and arrange, cut-side up, on a baking sheet pan. Place in the oven and broil until lightly toasted, 1-2 minutes.
Remove toasted rolls from the oven and spread with cheesy egg mixture. Return to the oven and broil until warmed through and cheese is melted, 1-2 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, using a knife, shave dill leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl with the veggies, along with thawed peas and spinach; toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide cheesy egg toasts and salad between plates. Enjoy!

name: Cheesy "French Onion" Beef & Potato Skillet with Sautéed Spinach
ingredients: 4 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.

Wash, dry, and quarter potatoes; place in a medium saucepan, along with salt, and cover with hot water (from the tap). Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, and simmer until fork-tender, about 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, preheat an ovenproof skillet over medium heat.
While the skillet heats up, peel, halve, and slice onion crosswise into thin half-moons. Peel and mince garlic.
Once the skillet is hot, add butter and swirl to coat the bottom. Add onion and garlic to the skillet; cook, stirring occasionally, until starting to soften, 3-4 minutes.
Add beef and spices to the skillet. Cook, breaking the meat apart with a spoon, until browned and crumbly 4-5 minutes. Remove from heat.
While the beef is cooking, coarsely grate mozzarella.

When the potatoes are done, drain and add to the skillet with the beef and onions. Gently crush some of the potatoes using a fork or potato masher. Add broth and Worcestershire to the skillet and stir to combine. (Reserve pan for later use.)
Sprinkle mozzarella over the beef and potatoes. Place skillet in the oven and bake until the mozzarella is melted and golden, 7-8 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the spinach. (Skip this step if it came pre-washed.)
Return the saucepan to medium heat.

Once the pan is hot, add additional butter and swirl to coat the bottom. Add spinach to the pan in handfuls, waiting for the spinach to wilt slightly before adding the next handful. Season with salt and pepper, stir to combine, and remove from heat.
To serve, divide beef-potato skillet and spinach between plates. Enjoy!

name: Cheesy "French Onion" Chicken Thighs with Mushrooms, Thyme & Parsley
ingredients: 4 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Preheat an ovenproof skillet over medium heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season with salt and pepper on both sides.

Once the skillet is hot, add butter and swirl to coat the bottom. Add chicken to the skillet and pan-fry until golden brown and cooked through, 3-4 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate and loosely cover with aluminum foil. (Reserve skillet with drippings.)
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel, halve, and thinly slice onion into half-moons.
Return skillet to medium heat. Add more butter and swirl to coat the bottom. Add onion and salt; cook, stirring occasionally, until soft and caramelized, 15-20 minutes.
While the onions cook, peel and mince garlic; place in a small bowl.
Thinly slice mushrooms and add to the bowl with the garlic.
Slide thyme leaves off the stems; discard the stems and add leaves to the bowl.
Shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves.

When the onions are done, add garlic, mushrooms, thyme, half of the parsley (reserving the rest for garnish), broth, and Worcestershire to the skillet; stir to combine. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to a simmer and cook, stirring occasionally, until liquid is reduced by half, 4-5 minutes.
Meanwhile, thinly slice mozzarella. Finely grate Parmesan.
Preheat oven to broil on high and position rack in the upper third of the oven.

When the veggies are done, nestle chicken into the mushrooms; top chicken with mozzarella and Parmesan. Place skillet in the oven and broil until cheese is melted and bubbly, 3-4 minutes. Remove from oven.
To serve, divide veggies and chicken between bowls or plates. Top with reserved parsley and enjoy!

name: Cheesy Fried Shallot Burger with Lemony Asparagus & Peppers
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Peel, halve, and slice shallot into very thin half-moons. Place in a small bowl and sprinkle with salt; using your hands, massage the shallot until it starts to soften. Set aside.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Snap or cut off the woody ends of the asparagus; trim, seed, and slice bell pepper into thin strips. Transfer both to a baking sheet pan, spreading them out in an even layer.
Peel and mince garlic. Sprinkle garlic over the veggies and drizzle with oil. Squeeze lemon over top, then season with salt and pepper.
Place veggies in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast, tossing halfway through, until crisp-tender, 12-15 minutes. Remove from the oven.
While the veggies are roasting, grate cheese into a medium bowl.
Add beef and spices to the bowl with the cheese; mix with your hands until well combined. Form the beef mixture into 2 equal-sized patties and place on a plate.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, use paper towels or a clean cloth to squeeze excess moisture out of the shallots. Divide shallots into 2 portions, then press into the top of each burger patty.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add patties, shallot-side down, and cook, undisturbed, until shallots are golden, about 4 minutes.

Using a metal spatula, carefully slide underneath the shallots and flip the patties (place any loose shallots back on top of the burgers); cook an additional 4-5 minutes, until cooked through. Once done, transfer to a clean plate.
Meanwhile, toast the buns if desired. Slice tomato into rounds.
Place bottom half of each bun on a plate, then top with sliced tomato and burgers. Close with the top half of the bun and serve with roasted veggies on the side. Enjoy!

name: Cheesy Garlic Chicken with Broccoli & Spinach
ingredients: ¾ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
instructions: Fill a medium saucepan about halfway with hot water (from the tap); cover and place over high heat.
Wash and dry the spinach. (Skip this step if it came pre-washed.)
Wash and separate broccoli into bite-sized florets and cut stems into smaller pieces.

Once the water in the saucepan is boiling, add the spinach, and stir. Cook 30-60 seconds, then remove to a colander with a slotted spoon. Rinse spinach under cold water, then press out excess water with the back of a spoon or your hands; transfer to a small bowl.
When the water in the saucepan returns to a boil, add the broccoli, cover, and reduce heat to medium. Cook until broccoli is fork-tender, about 4 minutes. Drain and set aside.
Coarsely grate the mozzarella.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Pat chicken dry with paper towels and cut into 1-inch pieces.
Once the skillet is hot, add butter and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add chicken and spices to the skillet. Cook, stirring occasionally, until golden and cooked through, 4-5 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel and mince the garlic. When the chicken is done, add the garlic to the skillet and cook 1 minute more.
Add spinach, broccoli, mozzarella, and ricotta to the skillet; continue to cook, stirring frequently, until cheese is melted and starting to bubble.
To serve, divide chicken sauté between plates, sprinkle with crushed red pepper, and enjoy!

name: Cheesy Ground Beef "Taco" Stuffed Peppers with Lettuce & Tomato Salad
instructions: Preheat oven to broil on high and position rack about 6-inches from the top.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim, seed, and halve bell peppers lengthwise. Transfer to a baking sheet pan, drizzle with oil, season with salt and pepper, then arrange cut-side down.
Place baking sheet in the oven and broil, flipping once, until peppers are lightly charred and tender, 5-6 minutes. Remove from oven and set aside to cool.
Meanwhile, preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add beef and spices; cook, breaking the meat apart with a spoon, until browned and crumbly, 4-5 minutes. Remove from heat.
While the beef is cooking, juice lime into a medium bowl. Add oil and spices; whisk to combine the dressing.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add half to the bowl with the dressing (reserving the other half for the beef).
Coarsely grate cheese.
When the beef is done, add reserved cilantro and half of the cheese (setting the rest aside for topping the peppers) to the skillet; stir to combine the filling.
Divide beef mixture between pepper halves and top with remaining cheese. Return baking sheet to the oven and broil until cheese is melted and bubbly, 2-3 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, halve lettuce lengthwise, then chop crosswise into thin (shred-like) strips; add to the bowl with the dressing and cilantro.
Halve tomatoes and add to the bowl; toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide stuffed peppers and salad between plates. Enjoy!

name: Cheesy Lasagna-Style Gnocchi Bake with Spinach & Fresh Basil
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.

Fill a medium saucepan about halfway with hot water (from the tap); cover and bring to a boil over high heat. Uncover, add gnocchi and salt, and stir for a few seconds. Cook, stirring occasionally, until gnocchi begins to float to the surface, about 3 minutes. Drain in a colander and set aside.
Meanwhile, wash, dry, and roughly chop the spinach (skip washing if using pre-washed spinach). Transfer to a medium bowl.
Peel and mince garlic and shallot.
Preheat an ovenproof skillet over medium-high heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add garlic and shallot to the skillet; cook, stirring frequently, until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add spinach to the skillet in handfuls, waiting for the spinach to wilt slightly before adding the next handful. Remove from heat and set aside. (Reserve bowl for later use.)
Place tomato sauce, Italian seasoning, and salt in a small bowl; whisk to combine and set aside.
Wash, dry, and pick basil leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and thinly slice into ribbons.
Place ricotta, egg, and spices in the reserved bowl; whisk until smooth. Add the cooked spinach and half the basil (reserving the rest for garnish); stir to combine.

Wipe the skillet clean with paper towels and coat the bottom with oil. Transfer half the gnocchi to the skillet and spread it out in an even layer. Spoon half the spinach-ricotta mixture over the gnocchi, followed by half the tomato sauce. Repeat this process once more, creating two layers.
Coarsely grate mozzarella and sprinkle on top of the gnocchi layers.
Place skillet in the oven and bake until cheese is melted and gnocchi is heated through, about 10 minutes.
To serve, divide gnocchi bake between plates and garnish with reserved basil. Enjoy!

name: Cheesy Mashed White Beans with Sautéed Kale & Fried Eggs
ingredients: 4 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Fold each kale leaf lengthwise, slice away and discard the stems, and slice the leaves crosswise into ⅛-inch strips and transfer to a medium bowl.
Trim off and discard the root ends of the garlic; peel and mince or press the garlic and transfer to a small bowl.
Preheat a small saucepan over medium heat.
While the saucepan heats up, drain and rinse the beans.
Finely grate ¼ cup of Parmesan.
Once the saucepan is hot, add butter and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add ½ of the garlic to the saucepan (save the rest for the kale); cook until fragrant, 15 to 30 seconds.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat.
Add the beans and ½ of the broth to the saucepan; bring to a boil, then mash the beans with a potato masher.
Add the remaining broth, most of the Parmesan (save a little for garnishing), salt, and pepper to the bean mash; stir to combine. Remove the saucepan from the heat and cover to keep the mash warm.
Once the skillet is hot, add olive oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Gently crack the eggs into the skillet. Cook until the tops of the whites are set but the yolks are still runny, 2 to 3 minutes. Once done, separate the eggs and transfer to a plate.
Once the eggs have been transferred, add more oil to the skillet.
Add the remaining garlic and kale to the skillet; season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring frequently, until the kale is wilted, 3 to 4 minutes.
Juice the lemon and pour over the kale; stir to combine.
To serve, spoon the mashed beans into a bowl, top with the kale and fried eggs, and sprinkle with the remaining Parmesan. Enjoy!

name: Cheesy One-Pot Gnocchi with Italian Sausage & Spinach
instructions: Heat a medium saucepan over medium heat.
Peel and small dice the onion. Peel and mince the garlic.
Once the pan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add the onion and garlic to the pan; cook, stirring frequently, until slightly softened, 3-4 minutes.

Use the tip of a knife to slice down the length of the sausages. Peel off the casings and discard. Add the pork to the pan and break apart with a spoon. Cook, stirring occasionally, until pork is browned and crumbly, 5-7 minutes.
Coarsely grate the mozzarella. Finely grate the Parmesan.
Add gnocchi, diced tomatoes with their juices, water, Italian seasoning, and salt to the pan. Cover and cook on medium heat until gnocchi is cooked through, 3-5 minutes. Remove from heat.
Wash and dry the spinach (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.) Add spinach to the pan; stir until wilted and the ingredients are combined, 1-2 minutes.
Sprinkle both cheeses over the gnocchi and cover. Let sit for 3-5 minutes until cheese is melted.
To serve, divide gnocchi between bowls and enjoy!

name: Cheesy Orzo Skillet Bake with Zucchini, Bell Pepper, Basil & Eggs
instructions: Fill a medium saucepan halfway with hot water (from the tap), cover, and bring to a boil. Uncover, add salt and orzo, and stir for a few seconds. Cook until desired firmness, 8-10 minutes. Drain and set aside.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim and small dice zucchini. Place in a small bowl.
Trim, seed, and small dice bell pepper. Add to the bowl with the zucchini and set aside.
Preheat an ovenproof skillet over medium heat.
While the skillet heats up, peel, halve, and small dice onion. Peel and mince garlic.
Once the skillet is hot, add butter and swirl to coat the bottom. Add onion, garlic, and spices to the skillet. Cook, stirring frequently, until onion begins to soften, 2-3 minutes.
Add zucchini and bell pepper to the skillet. Continue to cook, stirring often, until veggies are tender, 5-6 minutes. (Reserve bowl for the next step.)
While the veggies are cooking, coarsely grate cheese. Place in the reserved bowl and set aside.
Pick basil leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and thinly slice into ribbons.
Preheat oven to broil on high and position the rack in the upper third of the oven.
Add cooked orzo, tomato sauce, and half of the basil to the skillet (reserve remaining basil for serving). Cook, stirring occasionally, until sauce is warmed through, 2-3 minutes. Remove from heat.
Using a stirring spoon, make a well for each egg in the orzo. Crack an egg into each well.
Place skillet in the oven and broil until egg whites are just set, 3-4 minutes. Top with cheese and continue to broil until melted, 1 minute more. Remove from oven.
To serve, divide orzo and eggs between plates or bowls; top with reserved basil. Enjoy!

name: Cheesy Penne with Zucchini, Corn & Basil
instructions: Fill a large pot halfway with water, cover, and bring to a boil. Uncover, add salt and pasta, and stir for a few seconds. Cook until desired firmness, 8-10 minutes. Once the pasta is finished, drain and return to pot and set aside.
Preheat a large skillet over medium heat.
Peel and small dice onion. Peel and mince garlic.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add onion and garlic to the skillet, stirring frequently, cook until slightly softened, 3-4 minutes.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Add the frozen corn to the skillet, stirring frequently, cook until slightly softened, 3-4 minutes.
Trim zucchini; halve lengthwise and cut crosswise into thin half moons.
Add the zucchini and spices to the skillet. Increase heat to medium-high and sauté, stirring frequently, until the vegetables are soft and golden, 6-8 minutes.
Pick basil leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and thinly slice into ribbons; set aside.
Reduce the heat to low and stir the tomato sauce into the skillet, simmer for 3-4 minutes.
Grate the Parmesan and mozzarella.
Add the sauce and veggies to the pot with the cooked pasta, along with the Parmesan, mozzarella, and fresh basil (reserving a small amount for garnish); stir to combine.
To serve, divide between plates and garnish with reserved basil; enjoy!

name: Cheesy Polenta Bowl with Pinto Beans, Pico de Gallo Salad & Avocado
ingredients: 24 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: In a small saucepan, bring broth to a boil. Reduce heat to low and gradually add polenta in a thin steady stream, while whisking, until the polenta is incorporated into the broth. Cover and cook, stirring occasionally, until polenta is soft and the texture is creamy, 15-25 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Juice lime into a medium bowl. Add oil, salt, and pepper; whisk to combine the dressing.
Peel and mince garlic. Peel, halve, and thinly slice shallot into half-moons; add both to the bowl with the dressing.

Halve jalapeño pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon. Slice crosswise into thin half-moons; add to the bowl. (Be careful, with jalapeños, do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Trim, seed, and medium dice bell pepper; add to the bowl.
Halve tomatoes and add to the bowl. Trim, halve, and slice radishes into thin half-moons. Add both to the bowl.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl and stir to combine the salad; set aside.
Preheat another small saucepan over medium heat.
While the pan heats up, drain and rinse beans in a colander.
Once the pan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add beans and spices to the pan; cook, stirring occasionally, until beans are warmed through, 2-3 minutes. Cover and remove from heat.
While the beans are cooking, coarsely grate the cheese.
Add cheese, salt, and pepper to the polenta and stir to combine; if the polenta is too firm, add hot water, 1 tablespoon at a time, until you reach a desired consistency. Cover and remove from heat.
Halve and pit the avocado. Slice thinly while still in skin, then scoop out with a spoon.
To serve, divide polenta, beans, and salad between bowls. Top with avocado and enjoy!

name: Cheesy Pork Sausage & Bell Pepper Quesadilla with Lettuce & Tomato
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Preheat a large skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, trim, seed, and small dice bell pepper.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add bell pepper, pork, and spices; cook, breaking the meat apart with a spoon, until browned and crumbly, 4-5 minutes. Remove from heat.
Meanwhile, coarsely grate cheese.

To assemble the quesadillas, lay tortillas on a flat surface and divide pork and bell pepper between them, arranging on one half of each tortilla. Top with cheese and fold in half to close. (Reserve skillet for the next step.)
Wipe the skillet clean with paper towels and return to medium-high heat.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Place assembled quesadillas in the skillet and cook, flipping halfway through, until cheese is melted and tortillas are golden on both sides, 5-6 minutes. Remove to a plate.
Meanwhile, chop lettuce crosswise into thin (shred-like) strips. Transfer to another plate.
Small dice tomato. Add to plate with the lettuce.
To serve, cut each quesadilla into wedges and divide between plates; top with lettuce and tomatoes. Enjoy!

name: Cheesy Portobello Mushroom Burger with Blueberry BBQ Sauce & Salad
ingredients: ½ (5 oz) pkg spring mix (mixed greens)
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Juice half of the lemon into a blender. (Reserve remaining lemon for the dressing.)
Peel garlic; add to the blender along with blueberries, ketchup, sugar, soy sauce, and spices. Blend on high until very smooth, about 1 minute. Set BBQ sauce aside.
Remove stems from the mushrooms and carefully scrape out the gills; place on a plate.
Preheat a grill pan, outdoor grill, or regular skillet over medium-high heat.
While the grill pan heats up, peel and slice onion crosswise into ¼-inch thick rings; add to the plate with the mushrooms. Drizzle veggies with oil and season with salt and pepper on both sides.
Once the grill pan is hot, add the veggies and grill, undisturbed, until tender and lightly charred on one side, 3-4 minutes. (Reserve plate for later use.)
While the veggies are grilling, thinly slice cheese.

When the veggies are charred on one side, flip, then top each mushroom with cheese; continue to grill until veggies are tender and cheese is melted, 3-4 minutes more. Return to the plate and loosely cover with aluminum foil.
Meanwhile, juice the remaining lemon into a medium bowl; add oil, Dijon, and spices. Whisk to combine the dressing and set aside.
Halve tomatoes and add to the bowl with the dressing.
Halve and pit avocado; scoop out with a spoon and small dice the flesh. Add to the bowl along with mixed greens and almonds; toss to combine the salad. Set aside.
Toast buns if desired.
Spread half of the BBQ sauce over the bottom half of each bun; layer with mushrooms, onions, and remaining sauce. Close with the top half of each bun.
To serve, divide burgers and salad between plates. Enjoy!

name: Cheesy Portobello "Smash" Burger with Avocado, Sprouts & Romaine Salad
instructions: Place mayo, ketchup, and spices in a small bowl. Whisk to combine the special sauce and set aside.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, remove stems from portobello mushrooms. Place on a plate, drizzle with oil, and season with salt and pepper on both sides.

Once the skillet is hot, add mushrooms, cap-side down. Cook until starting to soften, about 3 minutes. Flip and continue to cook, occasionally pressing down with the bottom of a spatula, until golden underneath, 2-3 minutes more.
While the mushrooms are cooking, place oil, vinegar, Dijon, honey, and salt in a medium bowl. Whisk to combine the dressing and set aside.
Thinly slice cheese.
When the mushrooms are golden underneath, flip once more and top with cheese. Continue to cook until cheese melts and mushrooms are fork-tender, 3-4 minutes more. Remove from heat.
Meanwhile, chop (or tear) lettuce into bite-sized pieces. Add to the bowl with the dressing.
Slice one tomato crosswise into thin rounds; medium dice remaining tomato. Place slices on a clean plate and add diced tomato to the bowl with the lettuce and dressing; toss to combine the salad.
Halve and pit avocado; using a spoon, scoop out the flesh and slice lengthwise into thin slices. Add to the plate with the tomato.
Toast buns if desired.

Spread special sauce over the bottom half of each bun; top with cheesy portobellos, then layer with tomato, avocado, and sprouts. Close with the top half of each bun. Serve with salad on the side and enjoy!

name: Cheesy Prosciutto Chicken with Grape Tomato Pan Sauce
ingredients: ¾ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F. Coat a baking sheet pan with a thin layer of oil.
Finely grate Parmesan. Place in a medium bowl along with almond meal and Italian seasoning; stir to combine.
Pat the chicken dry with paper towels. Holding a knife parallel to the cutting board, cut the chicken in half horizontally to form thin cutlets.
Spread mayo over both sides of each cutlet, then dredge in the parmesan mixture, pressing to adhere. Transfer to the baking sheet.
Place chicken in the oven and bake until golden brown and cooked through, 10-12 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, using a clean cutting board, peel and mince garlic.
Place garlic, broth, tomato paste, oil, and spices in an ovenproof skillet. Whisk to combine the sauce and bring to a simmer over medium-high heat.
Meanwhile, wash, dry, and halve tomatoes.
Wash, dry, and pick basil leaves off the stems; discard stems and roughly chop the leaves (reserving a few whole leaves for garnish).
Chop prosciutto and mozzarella into bite-sized pieces.
Preheat oven to broil on high.
Once the sauce is simmering, add the tomatoes and basil, then stir to combine. Place chicken on top of the tomato mixture and sprinkle with prosciutto and mozzarella.
Place the skillet in the oven and broil until cheese is bubbly and slightly golden, about 5 minutes.
To serve, divide chicken and pan sauce between plates and garnish with reserved basil leaves. Enjoy!

name: Cheesy Prosciutto, Tomato & Leek Frittata with Lemony Arugula Salad
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the arugula if it came pre-washed.)
Peel and mince shallot. Place in a medium bowl.
Zest and juice lemon into the bowl with the shallot. Add oil, salt, and pepper, then whisk to combine the dressing.
Halve tomatoes lengthwise. Add half to the bowl with the dressing and set aside. Place remaining tomatoes in another medium bowl.

Trim off the root ends and dark green tops of the leeks, leaving only the white and pale green parts. Cut the leeks in half lengthwise and rinse under running water, separating the layers to remove any dirt and grit. Slice crosswise into ¼-inch thick pieces. Add to the second bowl with the tomatoes.
Preheat an ovenproof skillet over medium-high heat.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add tomatoes, leeks, salt, and pepper; cook, stirring occasionally, until veggies start to soften and brown, about 8 minutes. (Reserve bowl for the next step.)
Meanwhile, shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Place in the reserved bowl.
Finely grate Parmesan. Add to the bowl with the parsley.
Add eggs, salt, and pepper to the bowl. Whisk to combine and set aside.
Preheat oven to broil on high and position rack in the upper third of the oven.
Chop (or tear) prosciutto into bite-sized pieces. When the veggies are done, add to the skillet and stir to combine.

Reduce heat to medium and pour the egg mixture into the skillet. As eggs set around the edge of the skillet, gently lift cooked portions with a spatula to allow uncooked egg to flow underneath. Cook until bottom and sides are firm but top is still runny, about 5 minutes.
Place skillet in the oven and broil until the top is set, 2-3 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, add arugula to the bowl with the dressing and tomatoes. Toss to combine the salad.
Cut frittata into wedges and divide between plates. Serve with salad on the side and enjoy!

name: Cheesy Shrimp, Mushroom & Tomato Stuffed Peppers with Mixed Greens
ingredients: ¾ lb raw peeled shrimp, fresh or frozen
½ (5 oz) pkg spring mix (mixed greens)
instructions: Preheat oven to broil on high and position rack about 6-inches from the top.
Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the mixed greens if they came pre-washed.)
Trim, seed, and halve bell peppers lengthwise. Transfer to a baking sheet pan, drizzle with oil, season with salt and pepper, then arrange cut-side down.
Place baking sheet in the oven and broil, flipping once, until peppers are lightly charred and tender, 6-8 minutes. Remove from oven and set aside to cool.
Meanwhile, thinly slice mushrooms and place in a medium bowl.
Peel, halve, and small dice onion; peel and mince garlic. Add both to the bowl with the mushrooms.

If using frozen shrimp, place them in a colander and run under cold water to thaw them slightly and remove any ice crystals. (If using fresh shrimp, skip this step.) Place the shrimp on a clean towel or paper towels and pat dry, then roughly chop into bite-sized pieces.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom; add shrimp, mushrooms, onion, garlic, and spices. Cook, stirring occasionally, until veggies are tender and shrimp is cooked through, about 5 minutes. Remove from heat. (Reserve bowl for the next step.)
Meanwhile, using a clean cutting board, medium dice tomato and place in the reserved bowl.
Coarsely grate cheese; add half to the bowl with the tomato (reserving the rest for topping the peppers).
When the shrimp and veggies are done, add tomato and cheese to the skillet; stir to combine the filling. (Reserve bowl for the salad.)
Divide shrimp filling between pepper halves and top with reserved cheese. Return baking sheet to the oven and broil until cheese is golden, 2-3 minutes; remove from oven.
Meanwhile, place oil, vinegar, Dijon, honey, salt, and pepper in the reserved bowl; whisk to combine the dressing.
Add mixed greens and pumpkin seeds to the bowl with the dressing; toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide peppers and salad between plates. Enjoy!

name: Cheesy Smashed Potatoes with Bacon, Mushrooms, Tomato & Green Onion
instructions: Wash potatoes; transfer to a medium saucepan, add salt, cover with hot water (from the tap), and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to medium and cook until potatoes can be easily pierced with a fork, about 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, preheat oven to 450°F.
Preheat a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat.
Add bacon to the skillet and cook until crispy, 3-5 minutes per side.
Meanwhile, grate the cheese.
Wash and dry the remaining fresh produce.
Thinly slice the mushrooms.
When the bacon is done, remove and set aside on a paper towel-lined plate. Transfer the bacon fat to a small bowl and set aside, leaving about 1 tsp in the skillet.
Return skillet to medium heat. Add mushrooms and season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring often, until tender, 3-4 minutes; remove from heat and set aside.
Crumble or chop bacon into small pieces.

When the potatoes are done, drain and transfer to a baking sheet pan. Using a fork or potato masher, gently crush each potato, flattening them to a 1-inch thickness. Drizzle with 1 ½ tbsp reserved bacon fat and season with salt and pepper; toss to coat.
Sprinkle cheese, mushrooms, and bacon over the potatoes. Place in the oven and bake until cheese is melted, 2-3 minutes.
Meanwhile, trim off and discard ends of green onions, then cut crosswise into ¼-inch pieces at an angle. Small dice the tomato.
To serve, divide smashed potatoes between plates or bowls. Top with green onion, tomato, and yogurt. Enjoy!

name: Cheesy Spaghetti Squash with Chickpea-Tomato Ragù & Parsley
instructions: Preheat oven to 500°F and place rack in the center position. Line a baking sheet pan with aluminum foil to make cleanup easier (optional).
Wash, dry, and trim squash, then halve lengthwise, and scrape out the seeds. Rub the inside of the squash with oil and season with salt and pepper. Arrange halves, cut-side down, on the baking sheet.
Place squash in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast until tender, so a knife can easily pierce through the flesh, 20-25 minutes.
While the squash is roasting, peel, halve, and medium dice onion. Place in a medium bowl.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, peel and thinly slice garlic. Add to the bowl with the onion.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add onion, garlic, crushed red pepper, and salt; cook, stirring occasionally, until starting to brown, 6-8 minutes. (Reserve bowl for later use.)
Meanwhile, drain and rinse chickpeas.

Once the onion is starting to brown, add chickpeas, tomatoes, and more salt to the skillet; stir to combine the ragù. Reduce heat to medium-low and continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until the squash is done.
Meanwhile, finely grate Parmesan. Place in the reserved bowl and set aside.
Remove squash from the oven and allow to cool slightly, about 5 minutes.

While the squash is cooling, wash, dry, and shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and roughly chop the leaves. Add half of the parsley to skillet, stir to combine, and remove from heat. (Reserve remaining parsley for serving.)

Once the squash has cooled slightly, scrape the inside with a fork to separate into spaghetti-like strands (use an oven mitt or towel to hold it with your other hand). Add squash to the bowl with the Parmesan and gently toss to combine.
To serve, divide squash and veggie ragù between plates or bowls. Top with reserved parsley and enjoy!

name: Cheesy Spinach & Rice Stuffed Portobello Mushrooms
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F.
Using a strainer or colander, rinse rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add broth and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
Once liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce the heat to low. Cook rice until the liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry mushrooms; remove stems and carefully scrape out gills, making sure not to damage the rim of the mushrooms. Place on a baking sheet and rub with oil; set aside.
Peel and mince garlic.
Preheat a large skillet over medium heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add garlic to the skillet and cook until fragrant, 15-30 seconds.
Wash and dry the spinach. (Skip if it came pre-washed.) Add to the skillet in handfuls, waiting for the spinach to wilt slightly before adding the next handful.
Finely grate Parmesan.
Add Parmesan, yogurt, salt, and pepper to the skillet and stir to combine; remove from the heat. When the rice is done, add to skillet and stir to combine.
Fill mushroom caps with equal portions of the rice mixture. Place in the oven and bake for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, grate mozzarella.
Remove baking sheet from oven and top mushrooms with mozzarella. Bake for another 5 minutes, until cheese is golden and melted.
To serve, divide mushrooms between plates. Enjoy!

name: Cheesy Sweet Potato "Tostadas" with Beans, Mango Salsa & Tangy Arugula
instructions: Preheat oven to broil on high and position rack in the middle of the oven. Line a baking sheet pan with aluminum foil.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim off and discard ends of sweet potatoes; peel and slice lengthwise into ½-inch thick pieces. Discard any small, outer slices, then place remaining slices on the baking sheet.
Drizzle sweet potato slices with oil and season with spices on both sides.
Place sweet potatoes in the oven and broil, flipping halfway through, until fork-tender, 8-12 minutes. (Keep a close watch on the sweet potatoes to avoid burning.)

Meanwhile, quarter jalapeño pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon. Finely dice and place in a medium bowl. (Be careful, with jalapeños, do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Peel and mince garlic and shallot. Add both to the bowl with the jalapeño.
Peel mango and slice flesh away from the pit, starting with the flat sides. Small dice and add to the bowl.
Seed and small dice bell pepper; add to the bowl.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl.
Juice half the lime (reserving the rest for the salad) into the bowl; add salt and stir to combine the mango salsa. Set aside.

Drain and rinse beans. Divide beans between sweet potato slices, spreading them out in an even layer; season with salt. Return sweet potatoes to the oven and broil until beans are heated through, about 2 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, peel and mince additional garlic; place in another medium bowl.
Juice remaining lime into the bowl with the garlic. Add oil, maple syrup, salt, and pepper; whisk to combine the dressing. Add arugula and toss to combine the salad.
Divide sweet potato "tostadas" between plates; top with mango salsa and crumbled goat cheese. Serve with salad on the side and enjoy!

name: Cheesy Tex-Mex Beef, Carrot & Zucchini Noodle Skillet with Yogurt
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim zucchini and carrot; use a julienne (or regular) peeler to make noodles. Place both in a medium bowl.
Trim, seed, and medium dice bell pepper; add to the bowl with the veggie noodles and set aside.
Preheat an ovenproof skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, peel, halve, and small dice onion; peel and mince garlic.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom; add onion, garlic, beef, and spices. Cook, breaking the meat apart with a spoon, until browned and crumbly, 4-5 minutes.
Meanwhile, grate cheddar and set aside.
Preheat oven to broil on high and position rack under the broiler.
When the beef is done, add veggie noodles, bell pepper, and water to the skillet; continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until the liquid has evaporated and veggies are tender, 3-4 minutes more.
Meanwhile, medium dice tomato.
When the veggies are tender, add tomato and tomato sauce to the skillet; stir to combine and bring to a simmer. Once simmering, remove from heat and sprinkle with cheddar.
Place skillet in the oven and broil until cheese is melted and golden, 2-3 minutes.
To serve, divide skillet between plates or bowls and top with a dollop of yogurt. Enjoy!

name: Cheesy Vegan Broccoli & Cashew Quinoa Burrito with Sun-dried Tomatoes
instructions: Boil water in a kettle. (If you do not have a kettle, boil water in a saucepan, starting with hot tap water.) In a small bowl, pour boiling water over cashews and set aside to soak.
In a small saucepan, combine quinoa and water. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15 minutes. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel and small dice onion. Peel and mince garlic.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat. Add oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add onions and garlic to the skillet and sauté until the onions are tender, about 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash, dry, and medium dice celery and broccoli.
Roughly chop the sun-dried tomatoes.
Increase the heat to medium-high and add the celery, broccoli, and sun-dried tomatoes to the skillet. Sauté until broccoli is tender, about 8 minutes.
Drain the cashews and transfer them to a blender.
Peel garlic. Add to the blender along with almond milk, nutritional yeast, Dijon, vinegar, salt, and onion powder. Blend until smooth; add water, 1 tbsp at a time, if needed, to make a thick sauce.
Add the cooked quinoa, pumpkin seeds, and sauce to the vegetables in the skillet and stir to combine.
Lay the tortillas on a flat surface and divide vegetable mixture between them. Roll tightly to close, folding in the ends.
Return the skillet or a grill pan to medium-high heat.
Place wraps on the grill and flip every 1-2 minutes, until tortilla is crispy and golden.
To serve, cut wraps on an angle and divide between plates. Enjoy!

name: Cheesy Vegan Burrito Bowl with Spanish Rice, Beans & Pico de Gallo
instructions: Peel and small dice onion. Place half in a small bowl and set aside for the pico de gallo.
Peel and mince garlic.
Preheat a medium saucepan over medium-high heat.

Once the saucepan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add rice, onion, and spices; cook, stirring constantly, until onions are soft and rice is golden and toasted (you should hear a slight sizzle and pop from the rice), about 3 minutes.

Add garlic, water, corn, tomato sauce, and salt to the saucepan and bring to a boil over high heat. Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir, cover, and reduce the heat to low. Cook the rice until liquid is fully absorbed, 18-20 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Juice lime into the bowl with the onion.
