Dip the chicken strips into the egg, then transfer to the dry mixture and turn to coat. Shake off excess and place on the baking sheet. Drizzle with olive oil.
Place in the oven and bake until the crust is golden brown and the chicken is cooked through, 15-20 minutes.

Wash the green beans and trim ends. Add to the boiling water and cook until bright green, 3-4 minutes. Drain in a colander and rinse under cold water to prevent further cooking. Set aside to drain further.
Peel and mince the garlic.
In small bowl, prepare the dip by whisking together ⅓ of the minced garlic (save the rest for the green beans), mayonnaise, Dijon, honey, salt, and pepper.
Wipe the saucepan dry and return to the stove over medium heat. Add oil and swirl to coat bottom. Add the remaining minced garlic and cook until fragrant, 15-30 seconds.
Add the green beans and season with salt and pepper; toss to combine.
Place the chicken tenders on a plate, arrange the green beans on the side, and serve with the honey mustard dip. Enjoy!

name: Chicken Tenders with Roasted Vegetables & Spicy Maple Mustard
ingredients: ¾ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
instructions: Preheat the oven to 425°F and position rack in the center. Line two baking sheets with parchment paper.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Cut the sweet potatoes in half lengthwise, then cut each half into ½-inch planks, then into sticks. Add to a medium bowl.

Drizzle sweet potatoes with oil and season with garlic powder, salt, and pepper and toss until evenly coated. Spread out in an even layer on one of the prepared baking sheets and place in the oven, cook for 10 minutes. Set the bowl aside for the broccoli.
Separate broccoli into bite-sized florets and cut stems into strips. Add to the bowl used for the sweet potatoes and toss with oil and spices. Set aside.
Meanwhile, measure out the cornstarch in a medium bowl for dredging.
In another medium bowl, whisk the egg.
In a third medium bowl, mix together the almond meal, garlic powder, paprika, salt, and cayenne pepper. Stir to combine.
Cut the chicken into 1-inch thick strips.

First, dredge the strips in cornstarch, shaking off any excess. Then, dip the chicken strips into the egg. Finally, dredge in almond meal mixture, pressing gently to adhere. Shake off excess and place on another prepared baking sheet. Place in the oven for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, in small bowl prepare the dip by whisking together Dijon, maple syrup, salt, and cayenne. Set aside.
When the potatoes have baked for 10 minutes, remove from oven and spread broccoli evenly over top. Return to oven and bake for another 15 minutes, until potatoes are fork tender.
Once the chicken has cooked for 10 minutes remove from oven and flip. Return to oven and bake an additional 8-10 minutes.
Using a knife, shave the parsley leaves off the stems at a downward angle; discard the stems and finely chop the leaves.
To serve, arrange chicken tenders, wedges and broccoli on a plate. Garnish with parsley and serve with the maple mustard dip. Enjoy!

name: Chicken, Turnip & Mushroom Stew with Garlic Bread
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Peel and medium dice onion. Peel and mince garlic.
Wash turnip and mushrooms. Peel and medium dice turnip. Slice mushrooms.
Heat a medium saucepan over medium-high heat.
Medium dice chicken. Season with salt and pepper.
Coat bottom of saucepan with oil. Add chicken and cook until lightly browned, 2-3 minutes. Transfer to a plate.
Add more oil to saucepan, then add onion, garlic, turnip, and mushrooms. Cook, stirring frequently, until onion is softened, 4-5 minutes.
Preheat the broiler and position rack about 6 inches from the top.
Wash rosemary and slide leaves off the stems.
Wash and dry spinach.

Add chicken, rosemary, spinach, and broth to saucepan. Season with salt and pepper. Stir to combine and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to a simmer, cover, and cook until turnips are tender, about 10 minutes.
Peel and mince remaining garlic. In a small bowl, mix together garlic, olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Place halves of bun or roll cut side up on a baking sheet pan. Spread the oil mixture over top. Place in the oven and broil until bread in golden brown, 2-3 minutes.
Pour stew into a bowl and enjoy with garlic bread!

name: Chicken Wrap with Curried Pineapple-Apricot Chutney & Mixed Greens
ingredients: ¾ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
½ (5 oz) pkg spring mix (mixed greens)
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the mixed greens if they came pre-washed.)
Cut off skin from pineapple; quarter, core, and small dice the flesh. Place half in a small saucepan. (Place the remaining pineapple in a medium bowl and set aside for later use.)
Small dice apricots and add to the pan with the pineapple.

Add water, vinegar, sugar, and spices to the pan. Stir to combine the chutney and bring to a simmer over medium-high heat. Once simmering, reduce heat to low and cook, stirring occasionally, until thickened, about 8 minutes. Remove from heat.
Meanwhile, preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.

While the skillet heats up, pat the chicken dry with paper towels and place on a cutting board. Holding a knife parallel to the cutting board, cut the chicken in half horizontally to form thin cutlets. Season cutlets with salt and pepper on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add chicken and pan-fry until cooked through, 3-4 minutes per side. Remove from heat.
While the chicken is cooking, add oil, vinegar, maple syrup, salt, and pepper to the bowl with the pineapple. Stir to combine the salad dressing.

Using a clean cutting board, shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl with the dressing, along with the mixed greens, and toss to combine the salad. Set aside.
Warm tortillas in a skillet, oven, or microwave (optional).
Thinly slice chicken into strips.
Place tortillas on a flat surface; spread each with a layer of mayo and chutney. Top with chicken and a small portion of salad. Roll tightly to close. (Reserve remaining salad for serving.)
Cut wraps in half and divide between plates. Serve with remaining salad on the side and enjoy!

name: Chicken Wrap with Feta, Dates, Lettuce, Parsley & Curried Carrot Salad
ingredients: ¾ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled feta cheese
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Juice lemon into a medium bowl.
Shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl with the lemon juice along with yogurt, oil, Dijon, and spices. Whisk to combine the dressing and set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat chicken dry with paper towels and cut into bite-sized pieces.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add chicken and spices; cook, stirring occasionally, until golden and cooked through, 4-5 minutes. Using a slotted spoon, remove chicken to a plate; set aside. (Reserve skillet with cooking juices for later use.)
Meanwhile, using a clean cutting board, peel, trim, and coarsely grate carrots. Add to the bowl with the dressing, stir to combine, and set aside.
Peel, halve, and slice onion crosswise into thin half-moons.
Return skillet (with cooking juices) to medium heat. Add onion and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, 3-4 minutes.
While the onion is cooking, roughly chop dates.
When the onion is soft, add vinegar to the skillet. Continue to cook, stirring constantly, until vinegar is reduced, about 1 minute.
Return chicken to the skillet, along with any accumulated juices, then add the dates and feta. Stir to combine and remove from heat.
Halve lettuce lengthwise, then slice crosswise into thin (shred-like) strips.

Place tortillas on a flat surface, then divide chicken-feta mixture and lettuce between them. Top with a small portion of carrot salad and roll tightly to close. (Reserve remaining salad for serving.)
Cut wraps in half and divide between plates. Serve with remaining salad on the side and enjoy!

name: Chickpea, Egg & Avocado Chopped Salad with Balsamic Vinaigrette
instructions: Place the eggs in a small saucepan and cover with cold water by about 1 inch. Cover with a lid and bring to a rolling boil over high heat.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim off and discard the root end of the lettuce and remove any blemished leaves; halve the head lengthwise, then chop crosswise into 1-inch pieces and transfer to a large salad bowl.
Trim off and discard the ends of the cucumber; large dice the cucumber (cut into ¾-inch cubes) and add to the salad bowl.
Halve the grape tomatoes and add to the salad bowl.
Halve the avocado lengthwise and twist the halves to separate, then remove the pit with a knife or spoon; scoop out and large dice the flesh. Add to the salad bowl.
Once the water is boiling, remove the pan from the heat and let the eggs sit, covered, for 6 minutes.
Trim off and discard the ends of the onion and remove the outer layer; medium dice the onion (cut into ½-inch pieces) and add to the salad bowl.
Drain and rinse the chickpeas, then place on a clean towel or paper towels and pat dry; add to the salad bowl.
Once the eggs are done, place them in a bowl of cold water to stop the cooking process and set aside for 2 to 3 minutes.
In a small bowl, combine and whisk together olive oil, balsamic vinegar, Dijon mustard, salt, and pepper.
Peel and roughly chop the eggs; add to the salad bowl.
To serve, spoon the salad onto a plate or into a bowl and drizzle with the dressing. Enjoy!

name: Chickpea & Kale Caesar Salad with Pumpkin Seeds
instructions: Wash and dry the kale leaves and lemon.

One kale leaf at a time, cut along the sides of the tough center ribs, then pull out and discard the ribs. When all the leaves are trimmed, chop them crosswise into 1-inch pieces and transfer to a large bowl.
Finely grate ¼ cup of Parmesan.
Trim off and discard the root end of the garlic; peel and mince or press the garlic.
Cut the lemon in half; juice one half into a small bowl (that is big enough for making the dressing) and cut the other half into wedges for serving.
Add ½ of the grated Parmesan (save the rest for garnishing), minced garlic, yogurt, Dijon, soy sauce, salt, and pepper to the bowl with the lemon juice; whisk together until smooth.
Pour the dressing over the kale and toss to combine. If the kale is tough, massage it with your hands to soften it.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat.
While the skillet heats up, cut the bun or roll into ¾-inch cubes.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom.

Add the bread cubes to the skillet; sprinkle with salt and toss to coat in the oil, then arrange in a single layer. Toast the bread, tossing occasionally, until the bread cubes are golden brown, 4 to 5 minutes. Once done, transfer the croutons to a bowl and return the skillet to the stove.
While the bread cubes cook, drain and rinse the chickpeas, then transfer them to a clean towel (or paper towels) and pat dry.
Once the croutons have been transferred, wipe out the skillet with a paper towel and heat over medium heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom.

Add the chickpeas to the skillet; season with salt and pepper and toss to coat in the oil. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the chickpeas are golden brown and crispy, 5 to 7 minutes. Once done, remove the skillet from the heat.
Measure out the pumpkin seeds and place in a small bowl.
To serve, arrange a bed of the kale on a plate and top with the croutons, chickpeas, pumpkin seeds, and remaining Parmesan. Garnish with lemon wedges for squeezing over the top.

name: Chickpea-Kale Sauté with Raisins, Couscous & Toasted Pine Nuts
ingredients: 12 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: In a small saucepan, bring broth to a boil. Once boiling, remove from heat, add couscous, and stir to combine. Cover and let stand for 10 minutes; fluff with a fork right before serving.
Meanwhile, preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add pine nuts and cook, stirring often, until golden and fragrant, about 2 minutes. Transfer toasted nuts to a small bowl. (Reserve skillet for later use.)
Peel, halve, and thinly slice onion crosswise into half-moons. Peel and mince garlic.
Return skillet to medium heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add onion and garlic; cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, 3-4 minutes.
While the onion is cooking, drain and rinse chickpeas.
When the onion is soft, add chickpeas to the skillet. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the chickpeas are golden and warmed through, about 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry kale. Fold leaves in half lengthwise and slice off the stems; chop or tear leaves into bite-sized pieces.
Add kale to the skillet in handfuls, waiting for the kale to wilt slightly before adding the next handful.
Add broth, raisins, and spices to the skillet. Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until raisins have softened and sauce has thickened, 3-4 minutes more.
Add vinegar to the skillet, stir to combine, and remove from heat.
To serve, divide couscous and chickpea-kale sauté between plates or bowls; sprinkle with pine nuts. Enjoy!

name: Chickpea Panzanella Salad with Cucumber, Bell Pepper & Tomatoes
instructions: Heat a skillet over medium heat.
Cut bread into cubes.
Coat bottom of skillet with oil. Add bread cubes, season with salt and pepper, and toss to coat. Stirring occasionally, cook until golden brown, 4-5 minutes.
Peel and mince garlic. In a large bowl, prepare dressing by whisking together garlic, oil, vinegar, Dijon, salt, and pepper.
Drain and rinse chickpeas; place on paper towels and pat dry. Add to bowl with dressing and toss to coat.

Wash and dry cucumber, tomatoes, bell pepper, and basil. Medium dice the cucumber and tomatoes. Seed and medium dice the pepper. Pick the basil leaves off the stems and thinly slice into ribbons. Peel and medium dice onion. Add to bowl.
Add bread and toss salad.
To serve, place salad in a bowl. Enjoy!

name: Chickpea Tacos with Avocado Cream
instructions: Drain and rinse the beans in a colander; set aside to drain further.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Seed and small dice the bell peppers; set aside.
Peel and small dice onion.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Peel and mince garlic.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add the bell peppers, onion, garlic, and chickpeas. Cook until the chickpeas are slightly golden, stirring occasionally, about 3-4 minutes.
Add soy sauce, chili powder, and paprika to the chickpeas and sauté for 5-7 more minutes, until golden brown.
Add the avocado, water, and salt to a blender. Juice the lime into the blender. Purée until smooth.
Wrap the tortillas in damp paper towels and microwave until heated through, 15-30 seconds.
To assemble, add the chickpea vegetable mixture to each tortilla. Top with a drizzle of the avocado cream. Enjoy!

name: Chickpea-Tomato Noodle Soup with Kale Caesar & Breadsticks
ingredients: 12 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Meanwhile, peel and mince shallot and garlic. Place half the garlic in a medium bowl and set aside for the salad dressing.
Preheat a medium saucepan over medium-high heat.
Once the pan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add shallot and remaining garlic to the pan; cook, stirring occasionally, until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add broth, tomato sauce, pasta, and spices to the pan; stir to combine. Bring to a simmer, reduce heat to medium, cover, and cook until noodles are just tender, about 8 minutes.

Meanwhile, cut flatbread into 1½-inch wide strips, place on a baking sheet pan, and drizzle with oil. Place in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and bake until crispy, 8-10 minutes. Remove from the oven and set aside.
While the breadsticks are baking, wash, dry, and juice lemon into the bowl with the garlic. Add mayo, Dijon, soy sauce, salt, and pepper; whisk to combine the dressing.

Wash, dry, and fold kale leaves in half lengthwise and slice off the stems. Chop or tear leaves into bite-sized pieces and transfer to the bowl with the dressing; toss to combine the salad and set aside.
Drain and rinse chickpeas. Once the pasta is tender, add chickpeas to the pan and stir to combine. Continue to cook until heated through, 1-2 minutes.
Finely grate cheese.
Ladle soup into bowls and serve with salad and breadsticks on the side. Top soup and salad with cheese and enjoy!

name: Chickpea Waldorf Salad with Apples, Celery, Grapes & Walnuts
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)
Drain and rinse the chickpeas, then set aside to drain further.
In a large salad bowl, combine and whisk together yogurt, apple cider vinegar, Dijon, honey, salt, and pepper.
Quarter the apple lengthwise, then cut out the core and stem from each section; medium dice the apple (cut into ½-inch cubes) and add to the salad bowl.
Trim off and discard the ends of the celery; medium dice the celery (cut into ½-inch cubes) and add to the salad bowl.
Halve or quarter the grapes (depending on the size) and add to the salad bowl.
Roughly chop the walnuts and add to the salad bowl.
Add the chickpeas to the salad bowl; toss the salad until thoroughly coated with the dressing.
To serve, divide the spinach between plates and top with the salad. Enjoy!

name: Chickpea & Zucchini Sauté with Couscous, Feta & Almonds
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled feta cheese
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim off and discard the ends of the zucchini; halve the zucchini lengthwise, then cut the halves crosswise into ¼-inch-thick half-rounds at a 45° angle. Transfer to a medium bowl.
Halve the grape tomatoes; transfer to a small bowl.
Trim off and discard the root ends of the garlic; peel and mince or press the garlic. Transfer to a small bowl.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat.
While the skillet heats up, trim off and discard the ends of the onion and remove the outer layer; medium dice the onion (cut into ½-inch pieces).
Once the skillet is heated, add olive oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add the onion to the skillet; cook, stirring occasionally, until it has softened, 3 to 5 minutes.
While the onion cooks, using a knife, shave the parsley leaves off the stems at a downward angle, working away from your body; discard the stems and roughly chop the leaves.
Add the broth to a small saucepan; bring to a boil over high heat.
Add the garlic and cumin to the skillet and stir until fragrant, 15 to 30 seconds.
Add the zucchini and broth to the skillet; season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the zucchini is tender, 6 to 8 minutes.
Once the liquid in the saucepan comes to a boil, add couscous and salt; give it a stir and cover with a lid. Remove from the heat and let it stand for 5 minutes.
Drain and rinse the chickpeas in a colander.
Measure out the feta into a small bowl.
Measure out the almonds into a small bowl.
Add the chickpeas, tomatoes, and parsley to the zucchini. Stir and cook until the mixture is heated through, 1 to 2 minutes.
Uncover the couscous and fluff with a fork.
To serve, place the couscous into a bowl or on a plate, top with the zucchini and chickpea sauté, and sprinkle with the crumbled feta and almonds. Enjoy!

name: Chili-Rubbed Pork Chops with Apple Salsa & Sweet Potato Mash
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and medium dice the sweet potatoes into ½-inch cubes; transfer to a small saucepan.
Add water to the saucepan, covering the potatoes, and bring to a boil. Cook until they are tender when pierced with a fork, 14 to 16 minutes.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
In a small bowl, combine and mix together chili powder, cumin, salt, and pepper.
Pat the pork chops dry with paper towels, then place on a plate; rub both sides with the spice mixture.
Add coconut oil to the skillet and swirl to coat the bottom.
Place the pork chops in the skillet; cook until browned and cooked through, 3 to 5 minutes per side. Once done, transfer to a plate and let them rest for 5 minutes.
While the pork chops cook, core and small dice the apple into ¼-inch cubes; transfer to a medium bowl.
Quarter the jalapeño lengthwise, then remove and discard the seeds and white membranes; finely dice the pepper and add to the bowl.

Trim and discard the ends of the green onions; chop the onions into ¼-inch pieces. Add ¾ of the onions to the apple and pepper mixture and transfer the rest to a small bowl (for garnishing the sweet potato mash).
Once the potatoes are tender, scoop out ¼ cup of the water and set aside, then drain the potatoes in a colander and return them back to the saucepan.
Add the reserved cooking water, coconut oil, salt, and pepper to the potatoes; mash with a potato masher until smooth.
Juice the lime and add to the bowl with the apple and jalapeño.
Add olive oil, honey, salt, and pepper to the apple salsa; toss to combine.
To serve, place the pork chops and sweet potato mash on a plate. Spoon the salsa overtop the pork and sprinkle the mash with the remaining green onions. Enjoy!

name: Chili-Rubbed Salmon with Warm Zucchini & Corn Salad
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim off and discard the ends of the zucchini; using a box grater, coarsely grate the zucchini. Transfer to a colander (with a bowl underneath) and season with salt; set aside to drain.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the salmon fillets dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with chili powder, salt, and pepper.
Once the skillet is hot, add coconut oil and swirl to coat the bottom.

Place the salmon, skin-side-down, in the skillet; cook until the flesh is opaque and flaky, 3 to 4 minutes per side (depending on thickness). Once done, transfer to a plate and cover with foil to keep warm.
While the salmon cooks, trim off and discard the ends of the shallot; peel and mince the shallot. Transfer to a small bowl.
Trim off and discard the ends of the green onions; cut the onions crosswise into ¼-inch pieces at an angle and transfer to a small bowl.
Once the salmon has been transferred, reduce the heat to medium. Add more oil and the shallots to the skillet; cook, stirring frequently, until softened, 30 to 60 seconds.
Once the shallots have softened, add the corn to the skillet; cook, stirring frequently, until warmed through and lightly charred, 1 to 2 minutes.
Cut the lime into 4 wedges.

Add the drained zucchini and about ¾ of the green onions (save the rest for garnishing) to the skillet; season with chili powder, salt, and pepper. Increase the heat to medium-high and cook until the zucchini is heated through, 2 to 3 minutes.
To serve, divide the zucchini and corn salad between plates or bowls, top with the salmon fillets, and garnish with the remaining green onions and lime wedges. Enjoy!

name: Chili-Spiced Pumpkin Soup with Pork, Cauliflower, Cilantro & Lime
ingredients: 24 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Separate cauliflower into bite-sized florets and cut stems into smaller pieces; place in a medium bowl and set aside.
Preheat a medium saucepan over medium-high heat.
While the pan heats up, shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add half of the cilantro to the bowl with the cauliflower (reserving the rest for serving).
Once the pan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom; add pork and spices. Cook, breaking the meat apart with a spoon, until browned and crumbly, 4-5 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel, halve, and small dice onion; peel and mince garlic. Add both to the bowl with the cauliflower and cilantro.
When the pork is done, add veggies to the pan and cook, stirring occasionally, until starting to soften, 3-4 minutes.

Add broth and pumpkin to the pan; stir to combine and bring the soup to a boil over high heat. Once boiling, reduce heat to medium and simmer, stirring occasionally, until the cauliflower is soft, about 10 minutes.
When the soup is done, juice lime into the pan, stir to combine, and remove from heat.
To serve, divide soup between bowls and sprinkle with reserved cilantro. Enjoy!

name: Chimichurri Chicken & Grilled Vegetable Kebabs
ingredients: ¾ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
instructions: If using wooden skewers, place 6-8 skewers in a shallow dish of water to soak until you are ready to use them.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Shave parsley and cilantro leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves; transfer to a medium bowl.
Peel and mince garlic and add to the bowl.
To make the chimichurri sauce, add olive oil, red wine vinegar, and spices to the bowl with the fresh herbs and garlic. Stir to combine. Pour half of the sauce into a small bowl and set aside.
Cut chicken into 1-inch cubes. Add to the medium bowl with half of the chimichurri sauce and stir to coat.
Peel and chop onion into 1-inch pieces and add to another medium bowl.
Seed the pepper and chop into 1-inch pieces. Halve zucchini lengthwise, then slice crosswise into 1-inch half rounds; halve the mushrooms. Add veggies to the bowl with the onions.
Add oil, salt, and pepper to the veggies and toss until well coated.
Thread chicken and veggies onto skewers and place on a plate. Alternatively, you can cook the chicken and veggies directly on the grill/skillet without using skewers.
Heat a grill pan, outdoor grill, or skillet over medium-high heat.

When hot, coat grill or bottom of grill/skillet with oil; add the kebabs (as many as will fit). Cook until vegetables are tender, and chicken is cooked through, 4-6 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate and loosely cover with foil. Repeat with remaining kebabs.
To serve, divide kebabs between plates, and top with the remaining chimichurri sauce. Enjoy!

name: Chinese Chicken Salad with Napa Cabbage, Carrots & Tortilla Strips
ingredients: ½ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Cut tortilla into thin strips and transfer to a sheet pan. Drizzle with oil, season with salt and pepper, and toss to coat. Arrange in a single layer.
Place in the oven and bake until golden and crispy, 10-12 minutes.
Heat a grill pan, outdoor grill, or skillet over medium-high heat.
Slice chicken in half horizontally to form thin fillets. Season with salt and pepper.
Coat grill or bottom of skillet with oil. Add chicken and cook until golden brown and cooked through, 2-3 minutes per side.
Peel and mince garlic and ginger. In a large bowl, prepare dressing by whisking together garlic, ginger, oil, vinegar, soy sauce, sesame oil, honey, and crushed red pepper.

Wash and dry cabbage, carrot, and cilantro. Thinly slice cabbage into shreds. Trim ends, peel, and coarsely grate carrot. Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves. Add everything to bowl with dressing and toss.
Slice chicken into strips.
To serve, place salad on a plate and top with tortilla chips and chicken. Enjoy!

name: Chinese Egg, Tomato & Green Onion Stir-Fry with Sesame Seeds over Rice
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add water and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Cook rice until liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
While the rice is cooking, peel and mince ginger and garlic. Place both in a medium bowl.
Halve tomatoes lengthwise, then cut into ½-inch thick wedges. Add to the bowl with the ginger and garlic, then set aside.
Crack eggs into another medium bowl. Add salt, then beat with a whisk or fork until smooth.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, trim and cut green onions crosswise into thin pieces.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add green onions (reserving a small handful for serving) and cook, stirring frequently, until beginning to soften, about 30 seconds.
Add eggs to the skillet and cook, stirring frequently, until just set, about 3 minutes. Remove to a plate. (Reserve skillet for the next step.)
Return skillet to medium-high heat, add more oil, and swirl to coat the bottom. Add tomatoes and soy sauce; cook, stirring occasionally, until beginning to soften, about 3 minutes.
Meanwhile, place water, ketchup, cornstarch, and sugar in a small bowl. Whisk to combine the sauce.
Once the tomatoes have softened, reduce heat to medium. Add sauce and continue to cook, stirring frequently, until sauce thickens slightly, 2-3 minutes.
Return eggs to the skillet, using a spoon to break them up. Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until warmed through, 1-2 minutes more. Remove from heat.
To serve, divide rice and stir-fry between plates or bowls. Top with reserved green onions and sesame seeds. Enjoy!

name: Chopped Veggie Salad with Sun-Dried Tomato Dressing & Breadsticks
ingredients: ½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled feta cheese
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and mince garlic. Mince the sun-dried tomatoes. Add both to a large salad bowl.
Zest and juice half the lemon into the salad bowl. Thinly slice remaining lemon into rounds and set aside for garnish.
Add oil, honey, Dijon, and spices to the bowl; whisk to combine the dressing.

Drizzle 1 tbsp dressing over the flatbread, then cut into 1½-inch wide strips and place on a baking sheet pan. Place in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and bake until crispy, 8-10 minutes. Remove from the oven.
Meanwhile, peel, halve, and thinly slice the onion. Peel and thinly slice carrot into rounds. Add both to the bowl with the dressing.
Trim celery, then cut crosswise into ¼-inch pieces. Add to the bowl.
Trim and medium dice cucumber. Medium dice tomato; add both to the bowl.
Halve romaine leaves lengthwise, then thinly slice crosswise into shreds; add to the bowl.
Shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and add leaves to the bowl.
Drain and rinse the beans; add to the bowl.
Drain and thinly slice artichokes; add to the bowl and toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide salad between plates and top with feta. Serve with breadsticks and lemon slices. Enjoy!

name: Chunky Vegetable and Bean Chili with Cool Greek Yogurt
ingredients: 4 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Heat a medium saucepan over medium-high heat.
Peel and small dice onion. Peel and mince garlic.
Coat bottom of saucepan with oil. Add onion and garlic.
Wash celery and bell pepper. Medium dice and add celery to a saucepan. Seed, medium dice, and add pepper to saucepan. Stirring frequently, cook until vegetables have softened, 4-5 minutes.
Drain and rinse beans.
In a small bowl, mix together chili powder, cumin, salt, black pepper, and cayenne pepper.

Add spice mixture, beans, tomatoes, and broth to saucepan. Stir to combine and bring to a boil. Then reduce heat to medium, cover, and simmer until vegetables are tender and chili has thickened, about 10 minutes.
Wash green onions, trim and discard root ends, and chop. Stir ½ into the chili and save the rest for garnishing.
Serve chili in a bowl, garnish with remaining green onions and spoonfuls of yogurt. Enjoy!

name: Cilantro Burger with Spicy Mayo & Jalapeño-Lime Zucchini Sauté
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems. Place half of the leaves in a small bowl and set aside for serving; mince remaining leaves and place in a medium bowl.
Add beef, salt, and pepper to the bowl with the minced cilantro; mix with your hands until well combined. Form the beef mixture into 2 equal-sized patties, place on a plate, and set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, place mayo and chili-garlic sauce in another small bowl; stir to combine the spicy mayo and set aside.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add burger patties and cook, undisturbed, for 5 minutes; flip patties, and cook an additional 2-3 minutes, until cooked through. Once done, transfer to a clean plate and loosely cover with aluminum foil. (Reserve skillet for later use.)
Meanwhile, trim and halve zucchini lengthwise, then cut crosswise into ¼-inch thick half-moons. Place in another small bowl.

Quarter jalapeño pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon. Small dice and add to the bowl with the zucchini; set aside. (Be careful with jalapeños; do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Peel, halve, and thinly slice onion. Peel and mince garlic.
Return the skillet to medium-high heat, add more oil, and swirl to coat the bottom. Add onion and garlic; cook, stirring occasionally, until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add zucchini, jalapeño, water, salt, and pepper to the skillet; continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until veggies are fork-tender, 3-4 minutes more.
Meanwhile, trim and thinly slice radishes.
When the veggies are done, juice lime into the skillet, stir to combine, and remove from heat.
Toast buns if desired.

Place bottom half of each bun on a plate; spread with spicy mayo, then layer with burger patties, radish, and reserved cilantro leaves. Close with the top half of each bun and serve with sautéed veggies on the side. Enjoy!

name: Cilantro Lime Chicken Salad with Mango, Avocado & Bell Pepper
ingredients: ½ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Shave the cilantro leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves.
Peel and mince the garlic.

Juice the lime into a small bowl, then add ½ of the cilantro (transfer the rest to a small bowl and save for garnishing), minced garlic, olive oil, honey, crushed red pepper, salt, and pepper; whisk together. Pour ½ of the sauce into a medium bowl and set the rest aside.
Holding a knife parallel to the cutting board, cut the chicken in half horizontally to form thin fillets.
Add the chicken to the medium bowl and coat with the sauce; set aside to marinade for 10 minutes.
Seed and cut the pepper into strips lengthwise; transfer to a plate.
Peel the mango and cut the flesh away from the pit; medium dice the flesh. Add to the plate next to the pepper.
Halve and pit the avocado; scoop out the flesh and medium dice. Add to the plate next to the pepper and mango.
Heat a skillet over medium heat.
Halve the lettuce lengthwise, then chop crosswise into 1-inch strips; transfer to a medium bowl.
Add olive oil to the skillet and swirl to coat the bottom.
Remove the chicken from the marinade and pat dry with paper towels; place the fillets in the skillet and cook until browned and cooked through, 3 to 4 minutes per side.
Slice the chicken crosswise into strips.

Divide the lettuce between two plates (or one plate and one lunch container) and layer the peppers, mangoes, avocado, and chicken over top. Drizzle with the remaining sauce and garnish with the remaining cilantro. Enjoy!

name: Cilantro-Lime Chicken Thighs with Avocado-Tomato Salsa
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Pat the chicken dry with paper towels and place in a medium bowl.
Juice the lime; add half of the juice to the bowl with the chicken and the other half to a separate medium salad bowl.
Using a knife, shave the cilantro leaves off the stems at a downward angle, working away from your body; discard the stems and finely chop the leaves. Add half to each bowl.
Trim off and discard the root end of the garlic; peel and mince or press the garlic. Add to the bowl with the chicken.
To the bowl with the chicken, add olive oil, salt, and pepper. Turn the chicken until well coated with the marinade. Set aside for 5 minutes.
Preheat a grill pan or regular skillet over medium-high heat.
While the chicken marinates, halve the grape tomatoes crosswise. Add to the salad bowl.
Once the grill pan / skillet is hot, add the chicken and cook until it is golden brown and cooked through, 3 to 5 minutes per side.
Halve the avocado lengthwise and twist the halves to separate, then remove the pit with a knife or spoon; scoop out and small dice the flesh. Add to the salad bowl.
Trim off and discard the ends of the onion and remove the outer layer; small dice the onion (cut into ¼-inch pieces). Add to the salad bowl.
Add olive oil, salt, and pepper to the salad bowl; toss to combine.
To serve, divide the chicken between plates and top with the salsa. Enjoy!

name: Cilantro-Lime Grilled Chicken with Thai Mango Salad
ingredients: ¾ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
instructions: Wash and dry the cilantro. Shave the leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves. Transfer one half to a medium bowl and the other half to a large bowl.
Grate zest from half of the lime. Add the lime zest and juice, olive oil, salt, and pepper to the medium bowl with the cilantro; mix together.
Holding a knife parallel to the cutting board, cut the chicken in half horizontally to form thin fillets. Place in the marinade and turn to coat. Set aside for a few minutes.
Preheat a grill pan or skillet over medium-high heat.
Wash the mango and bell pepper.
Coat the grill/skillet with oil. Add the chicken and cook until browned and cooked through, 2-3 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate.
Peel and julienne (or cut into thin sticks) the mango; add to the large bowl with the cilantro. Seed and julienne (or cut into thin sticks) the bell pepper; add to the bowl.
Peel and mince or press the garlic. In a small bowl, prepare the dressing by whisking together the minced garlic, lime juice, fish sauce, rice vinegar, honey, water, and crushed red pepper.
Pour the dressing over top the salad and toss to combine.
Serve the grilled chicken with salad on the side. Enjoy!

name: Citrus Chicken Quinoa Salad with Avocado & Orange
ingredients: ½ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: In a small saucepan, combine quinoa and broth; bring to a boil. Reduce heat a simmer, cover, and cook for 15 minutes. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Heat a skillet over medium heat.
Cube chicken into 1 inch pieces. Season with paprika, salt, and pepper; toss to coat.
Coat bottom of skillet with oil. Add chicken pieces and cook until browned and cooked through, 2-3 minutes per side. Remove from heat.
Halve and pit avocado. Scoop out the flesh, medium dice, and transfer to a salad bowl.

Slice off top and bottom from orange, then cut off the skin and white pith from the sides so you can see the orange flesh. Cut in between the thin membranes to release the segments and add to salad bowl.
Wash and dry cilantro. Shave leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves. Add to salad bowl.
Peel and mince garlic. In a small bowl, prepare dressing by whisking together garlic, lime juice, olive oil, honey, salt, and pepper.
Rinse quinoa in a stainer if there is excess water and add to salad bowl. Add chicken and pour dressing over top. Toss to coat.
Serve in a bowl and enjoy!

name: Citrus Marinated Chicken over Quinoa Salad with Berries & Oranges
ingredients: ¾ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: In a small saucepan, combine quinoa and broth; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to a simmer, cover, and cook for 15 minutes. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Zest orange into a medium bowl (set orange aside for later use). Juice lime into the same bowl.
Peel and mince garlic; add to the bowl with the lime juice, along with soy sauce, oil, and spices. Whisk to combine the marinade.
Holding a knife parallel to the cutting board, cut the chicken in half horizontally to form thin cutlets. Place chicken in the bowl with the marinade, turn to coat, and set aside.
Juice lemon into another medium bowl; add oil, honey, salt, and pepper. Whisk to combine the dressing.
Using a clean cutting board, trim and cut celery and green onions crosswise into ¼-inch pieces; add both to the bowl with the dressing.
Trim and thinly slice strawberries; add to the bowl along with the blueberries.
Remove peel from the zested orange; halve lengthwise, then slice crosswise into thin half-moons. Add to the bowl.
Shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl, stir to combine the salad, and set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add chicken and marinade to the skillet; pan-fry until the chicken is golden and cooked through, 3-4 minutes per side. Remove from heat.
Meanwhile, transfer the cooked quinoa to a baking sheet pan. Spread out in an even layer and let cool for 5 minutes.
Add cooled quinoa to the bowl with the salad and gently stir to combine.
Thinly slice chicken into strips.
To serve, divide quinoa salad and chicken between plates. Enjoy!

name: Classic Beef Burger with Chopped Salad
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Preheat a grill pan or regular skillet over medium-high heat.
In a medium bowl, combine and mix together the ground beef, Worcestershire, Dijon, salt, and pepper. Form the mixture into 2 patties and place on a plate.
Once the grill pan or skillet is hot, coat the bottom with coconut oil.
Place the beef patties on the grill pan or skillet and cook until desired doneness, 4 to 6 minutes per side. Once done, transfer the patties to a plate.

While the patties cook, rip off a couple lettuce leaves for the burgers and place on a plate. Then, trim off and discard the root end of the remaining lettuce and remove any blemished leaves; halve the head lengthwise, then chop crosswise into 1-inch pieces. Transfer the chopped lettuce to a medium salad bowl.

Slice one of the tomatoes crosswise into ¼-inch-thick rounds for the burgers and add to the plate with the lettuce leaves. Halve the other tomato lengthwise and cut out and discard the stem end; large dice the tomato and add to the salad bowl.
Trim off and discard the ends of the cucumber; quarter the cucumber lengthwise, then slice crosswise into ¼-inch-thick pieces on an angle and add to the salad bowl.
In a small bowl, combine and whisk together olive oil, red wine vinegar, Dijon, salt, and pepper.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss to coat.
Toast the buns if desired.
To serve, assemble the burger and add any desired condiments. Serve with the salad on the side. Enjoy!

name: Classic Beef Chili with Avocado & Crusty Bread
instructions: Heat a medium saucepan over medium heat.
Peel and small dice onion. Peel and mince garlic. Wash, seed, and mince jalapeño.
Coat bottom of saucepan with oil. Add onion and jalapeño. Stirring frequently, cook until softened, 3-4 minutes.
Drain and rinse beans.
Add garlic, chili powder, and cumin to saucepan. Stir and cook for 30 seconds.
Add beef and, breaking apart with a spoon, cook until crumbly and browned, 2-3 minutes.
Add beans, tomatoes, salt, and pepper. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to a simmer and cook until chili thickens, about 10 minutes.
Scoop out the avocado flesh and medium dice.
Toast bread if desired.
To serve, place chili in a bowl and garnish with avocado. Enjoy with bread!

name: Classic Beef Stew with Potatoes, Carrots, Celery & Crusty Bread
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
¾ lb striploin (New York strip) steak
instructions: In a medium bowl, combine flour, salt, and pepper.
Cube steak, add to bowl, and toss to coat.
Wash and dry potatoes, carrots, celery, and green onions. Peel and medium dice potatoes and carrots. Trim ends and medium dice celery. Trim root ends and chop onions. Peel and mince garlic.
Heat a small saucepan over medium-high heat.
Coat bottom of saucepan with oil. Add beef and cook until browned on all sides, 3-4 minutes total.
Add potatoes, carrots, celery, onions, and garlic. Stir and cook for 1-2 minutes.
Add broth, water, Worcestershire, salt, and pepper; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to a simmer and cook until vegetables are tender, 10-15 minutes.
Toast bread.
To serve, place stew in a bowl and have with crusty bread. Enjoy!

name: Classic Lentil Soup with Zucchini, Carrot, Celery & Breadsticks
ingredients: 32 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Preheat a medium saucepan over medium-high heat.
Meanwhile, peel and small dice onion.
Once the pan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add onion and cook, stirring occasionally, until starting to soften, 2-3 minutes.
While the onion is cooking, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Using a strainer or colander, rinse lentils under cold water; drain and transfer to the pan with the onion.
Add broth, diced tomatoes, and spices to the pan; stir to combine, cover, and bring soup to a boil over medium-high heat.
While the soup is heating, peel, trim, and slice carrots crosswise into ¼-inch pieces. Trim and slice celery crosswise into ¼-inch pieces. Add both to the soup.
Trim and medium dice zucchini; add to the soup.

Peel and mince garlic; add half the garlic to the soup (reserving the rest for the bread sticks) and stir to combine. Once the soup comes to a boil, reduce heat to a simmer, cover, and cook until veggies and lentils are tender, 15-20 minutes.
Meanwhile, preheat oven to 425°F.
Place reserved garlic in a small bowl along with oil and spices; stir to combine the garlic oil.

Drizzle garlic oil over the flatbread; cut into 1½-inch wide strips and transfer to a baking sheet pan. Place in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and bake until crispy, 8-10 minutes. Remove from the oven.
When the soup is done, add vinegar and stir to combine.
Divide soup between bowls and serve with breadsticks on the side. Enjoy!

name: Classic Sloppy Joes with Zesty Broccoli Slaw
instructions: Peel and small dice onion. Wash, seed, and small dice bell pepper. Peel and mince garlic.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Coat bottom of skillet with oil. Add onion and pepper. Stirring frequently, cook until softened, 3-4 minutes.
Add beef and garlic. Breaking apart with a spoon, cook until meat is browned and crumbly, 2-3 minutes.
Add tomato sauce, vinegar, honey, Worcestershire, Dijon, chili powder, salt, and pepper. Stirring occasionally, reduce heat to low and simmer until sauce thickens, 10-15 minutes.
Peel and mince garlic. In a medium bowl, prepare dressing by whisking together garlic, olive oil, vinegar, Dijon, honey, salt, and pepper.
Add broccoli slaw to bowl with dressing and toss to coat.
Toast buns or rolls if desired.
To serve, fill buns or rolls with sloppy joe mixture and enjoy with broccoli slaw on the side!

name: Classic Spaghetti & Meatballs with Tomato Sauce
instructions: Fill a medium saucepan about halfway with water, cover, and bring to a boil.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Shave the parsley leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves. Transfer half of the parsley to a medium bowl and the other half to a small bowl.
Peel and mince the onion.
Peel and mince the garlic; transfer half of the onion and garlic to the medium bowl with the parsley and the other half to another small bowl.
Add the ground beef, bread crumbs, and spices to the medium bowl with the parsley, onion and garlic mixture. Mix with your hands until well combined.
Preheat a sauté pan over medium heat.
Using a tablespoon measure, form the meat mixture into rounded meatballs.
Add olive oil to the pan and swirl to coat the bottom.
Once the water is boiling, season with salt and add the pasta. Cook the pasta until desired firmness, 8 to 10 minutes. Once done, drain in a colander.
Place the meatballs in the pan and cook, stirring occasionally, until they are browned on all sides and almost cooked through, 4 to 5 minutes total. Once done, transfer to a bowl or plate.
Once the meatballs have been transferred, add more olive oil to the pan, followed by the remaining onion and garlic. Cook, stirring frequently, until the onion is softened, 3 to 4 minutes.

Add the diced tomatoes, tomato sauce, and spices to the pan. Return the meatballs to the pan, reduce the heat to medium-low and cook until the meatballs are cooked through and the sauce is slightly thickened, 6 to 8 minutes.
Finely grate ¼ cup of Parmesan.
Add the spinach to the sauce and fold in until it is wilted. Remove pan from the heat.
To serve, divide pasta between bowls, spoon the sauce and meatballs over top, and sprinkle with the remaining parsley and grated Parmesan. Enjoy!

name: Coconut Curry Shrimp with Carrot Rice
ingredients: ½ (13.5 fl oz) can coconut milk
¾ lb raw peeled shrimp, fresh or frozen
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Season the rice with salt and add water; bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
If using frozen shrimp, place in a bowl and cover with cold water to thaw. Set aside.
Wash and dry green onions. Trim root ends and chop.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce the heat to low. Cook the rice until the liquid is fully absorbed, 15 to 18 minutes. Once done, remove the rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.

Drain and rinse shrimp under cold water until there are no more ice chunks. Place on paper towels and pat dry. Return to empty bowl. Add lime juice, ½ of the green onions (save the rest for garnishing), and pepper. Toss to coat.
Heat a skillet over medium heat.
Peel and mince garlic and ginger. In a small bowl mix together garlic, ginger, curry powder, salt, and water.
Coat bottom of skillet with oil. Add curry mixture and cook for about 1 minute. Add coconut milk, stir, and cook 2-3 minutes.
Add shrimp and cook until opaque, 4-5 minutes.
Wash, trim ends, peel, and coarsely grate carrots. Add to rice and stir to combine.
To serve, place rice and curry on a plate and garnish with remaining green onions. Enjoy!

name: Coconut-Turmeric Rice Noodles with Edamame, Veggies & Cilantro
ingredients: ½ (13.5 fl oz) can coconut milk
instructions: Fill a medium saucepan halfway with hot water (from the tap) and bring to a boil. Remove from heat and add rice noodles. Soak for 10 minutes or according to package directions; drain in a colander and rinse.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Place edamame in the colander and rinse under hot, running water (from the tap) to defrost; set aside to drain.
Separate broccoli into bite-sized florets and cut stems into smaller pieces. Place in a medium bowl.
Peel, trim, and cut carrot crosswise into ¼-inch thick rounds. Add to the bowl with the broccoli.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, trim, seed, and medium dice bell pepper; add to the bowl.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add veggies, salt, and pepper to the skillet; cook, stirring occasionally, until tender-crisp, about 5 minutes. (Reserve bowl for later use.)
Meanwhile, peel and mince ginger and garlic. Peel and small dice shallot.
When the veggies are done, return them to the reserved bowl.
Return skillet to medium-high heat, add more oil, and swirl to coat the bottom. Add garlic, ginger, and shallot to the skillet; cook, stirring occasionally, until starting to soften, about 2 minutes.
Add coconut milk, water, fish sauce, honey, and spices to the skillet; stir to combine the sauce and bring to a simmer.

Once the sauce is simmering, add drained rice noodles, edamame, and cooked veggies to the skillet; stir to combine. Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until noodles are warmed through and sauce has thickened slightly, 3-4 minutes.
Meanwhile, cut lime into wedges; set aside for serving.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add cilantro to the skillet, stir to combine, and remove from heat.
To serve, divide saucy noodles and veggies between bowls; top with a squeeze of lime and enjoy!

name: Cod à la Meunière with Roasted Green Beans & Potatoes
instructions: Preheat the oven to 450°F and place the rack in the center position.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Halve the potatoes lengthwise, then cut each half lengthwise into 6 wedges; transfer the wedges to a baking sheet.
Place the sheet in the oven and cook the potatoes for about 10 minutes (while you prepare the green beans).
Trim and discard the ends of the green beans; transfer to a medium bowl.
Trim off and discard the root ends of the garlic; peel and mince or press the garlic.
Remove the sheet from the oven; add the green beans and garlic to the potatoes.
Drizzle the vegetables with olive oil and season with salt and pepper; toss to coat, then spread out in an even layer.
Return the sheet to the oven; cook the vegetables, tossing once halfway through cooking time, until they are tender, another 10 to 15 minutes. Once done, remove from the oven.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat.
Pat the cod dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with salt and pepper on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add olive oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Place the fish in the skillet; cook until it is browned and crisp, 3 to 5 minutes per side. Once done, transfer to a plate.
While the fish cooks, juice the lemon into a small bowl.
Using a knife, shave the parsley leaves off the stems at a downward angle, working away from your body; discard the stems and finely chop the leaves.

Once the fish has been transferred, add butter to the skillet and let it turn a light brown, then remove the skillet from the heat and stir in the lemon juice and ½ of the parsley (save the rest for the green beans and potatoes).
Sprinkle the green beans and potatoes with the remaining parsley; toss to combine.
To serve, place the fish on a plate, spoon the butter sauce overtop, and add the roasted green beans and potatoes on the side. Enjoy!

name: Cod Poached in Fresh Tomato Sauce with Roasted Asparagus
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F and position rack in the center.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Snap or cut off and discard the woody ends of the asparagus; transfer the spears to a baking sheet.
Drizzle the asparagus with olive oil and season with salt and pepper; toss to coat, then spread out in a single layer. Set aside.
Peel and mince the garlic; transfer to a medium bowl.
Medium dice the tomatoes; add to the garlic.
Place the asparagus in the oven and roast until tender-crisp, 10 to 12 minutes.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat.
Peel and small dice the onion; transfer to a small bowl.
Add olive oil to the skillet and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add the onion and cook, stirring occasionally, until it softens and browns, 2 to 3 minutes.
While the onion cooks, measure out the olives and capers and add to the bowl with the tomatoes and garlic.
Add more olive oil to the skillet, followed by the tomatoes, garlic, olives, and capers. Season with salt and pepper.
Place the fish in the skillet and sink into the sauce; cook until it is opaque and flakes easily, 4 to 5 minutes per side.
Shave the parsley leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves.
Add most of the parsley to the skillet (save a little for garnishing) and stir into the sauce.
To serve, divide the asparagus between plates and place the fish fillets on top. Spoon the tomato sauce over top and garnish with the remaining parsley. Enjoy!

name: Cod, Spinach & Cilantro Coconut Curry with Spicy Mango-Cucumber Salad
ingredients: ½ (13.5 fl oz) can coconut milk
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)
Roughly chop spinach and transfer to a medium bowl; set aside.
Preheat a medium saucepan over medium heat.
Meanwhile, peel and mince garlic and ginger.
Once the pan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add garlic and ginger; cook, stirring constantly, until golden, about 1 minute.
Add spices to the pan and continue to cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant, 1 minute more.
Add coconut milk, then bring to a boil over medium-high heat.
While the coconut milk is heating up, pat cod dry with paper towels and cut into 1-inch pieces.
Once the coconut milk is boiling, reduce heat to medium-low, add cod, and simmer, undisturbed, until the fish is cooked through, 8-10 minutes.
Meanwhile, using a clean cutting board, zest and juice lime into another medium bowl; add oil, sugar, and spices. Whisk to combine the dressing.
Peel mango and slice flesh away from the pit, starting with the flat sides. Medium dice and add to the bowl with the dressing.
Trim cucumber, halve lengthwise, and thinly slice crosswise into half-moons; add to the bowl.
Peel, halve, and thinly slice shallot; add to the bowl.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add half to the bowl (reserving the rest for the curry) and stir to combine the salad.
When the curry is done, add spinach to the pan in handfuls, waiting for the spinach to wilt slightly before adding the next handful. Remove from heat.
To serve, divide the fish curry between bowls and sprinkle with reserved cilantro. Enjoy with mango-cucumber salad on the side.

name: Cod Tikka Masala over Pilau Rice with Cucumber, Tomato & Mint Salad
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add water, turmeric, and salt; bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Cook rice until liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
While the rice is cooking, preheat a medium saucepan over medium heat.
Meanwhile, peel and mince ginger and garlic.
Once the pan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add ginger, garlic, and spices; cook, stirring often, until fragrant, about 1 minute.

Add tomatoes, cream, and sugar to the pan. Stir to combine the tikka masala sauce and bring to a simmer. Once simmering, continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened, 4-5 minutes more.
While the sauce is cooking, pat cod dry with paper towels and cut into 2-inch pieces.
When the sauce is done, use a hand blender to purée until smooth. Alternatively, use a potato masher to crush the veggies (the sauce will be chunkier).
Return the sauce to medium-low heat. Add the cod and cook, stirring occasionally, until opaque and flesh flakes with a fork, 6-8 minutes. Remove from heat.
Meanwhile, using a clean cutting board, peel and mince shallot. Place in a medium bowl.
Juice lemon into the bowl with the shallot.
Pick mint leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl.
Trim and small dice cucumber; add to the bowl.
Halve tomatoes lengthwise. Add to the bowl along with salt and pepper, then stir to combine the salad.
Divide rice between plates and top with cod tikka masala. Serve with salad on the side and enjoy!

name: Coriander Chicken Thighs with Leeks, Snap Peas, Peppers & Cumin Toast
ingredients: 4 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F. Position racks in the upper and lower thirds of the oven.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.

Trim off the root ends and dark green tops of the leeks, leaving only the white and pale green parts. Cut the leeks in half lengthwise and rinse under running water, separating the layers to remove any dirt and grit. Slice crosswise into ¼-inch thick pieces and place in a small bowl.
Peel and mince garlic; zest lemon. Add both to the bowl with the leek and set aside. (Reserve lemon for later use.)
Preheat an ovenproof skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat chicken dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with salt and pepper on both sides.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom; add chicken and cook until golden, about 2 minutes per side. Once golden, transfer to a clean plate and cover with aluminum foil (the chicken will not be cooked all the way through). Reserve skillet (with juices) for the next step.

Return skillet to medium heat, add more oil, and swirl to coat the bottom. Add leek, garlic, lemon zest, and spices; cook, stirring occasionally, until the leek starts to soften, 3-4 minutes. (Reserve bowl for the next step.)
Meanwhile, trim, seed, and medium dice bell pepper; cut snap peas in half crosswise. Place both in the reserved bowl.
When the leek is soft, add bell pepper, snap peas, and broth to the skillet; stir to combine and bring to a simmer over medium-high heat.

Once simmering, return chicken to the skillet (along with any accumulated juices) and nestle into the veggies. Place skillet on lower rack of the oven and bake until veggies are tender and chicken is cooked through, about 10 minutes.

While the chicken is cooking, split buns in half and place on a baking sheet pan; drizzle with oil and season with spices. Place on upper rack of the oven and toast until golden, about 4 minutes. Remove from oven.
When the chicken is done, remove from oven and juice reserved lemon over top.
To serve, divide chicken, veggies, sauce, and toast between plates or bowls. Enjoy!

name: Coriander-Ginger Tomato Soup with Crispy Chickpeas, Cilantro & Yogurt
ingredients: ½ (13.5 fl oz) can coconut milk
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Peel, halve, and small dice onion.
Preheat a medium saucepan over medium-low heat.
Once the pan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add onion, coriander, and salt; cook, stirring occasionally, until golden, about 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, drain and rinse chickpeas. Transfer to a baking sheet pan and pat dry with paper towels.
Add whole (unpeeled) garlic cloves to the baking sheet with the chickpeas. Drizzle with oil, then season with additional coriander and salt. Stir to coat and spread out in an even layer.
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast, stirring chickpeas halfway through, until crispy and golden, 15-18 minutes.
While the chickpeas are roasting, wash, dry, peel, and mince ginger.

When the onions are golden, add ginger, tomatoes, water, and coconut milk; bring to a simmer over medium-high heat. Once simmering, reduce heat to medium and continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened, about 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash, dry, and shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and roughly chop the leaves. Place in a small bowl.

When the chickpeas and garlic are done, remove from oven. Carefully transfer roasted garlic to the cutting board. Using the back of a spoon, press on the cloves to remove the skins. Set aside the crispy chickpeas.

Add roasted garlic and half of the cilantro to the soup, stir to combine, and remove from heat. Use a hand blender to purée the soup until smooth. Alternatively, use a potato masher to crush the veggies (the soup will be chunkier).
To serve, divide soup between bowls; top with yogurt, crispy chickpeas, and remaining cilantro. Enjoy!

name: Cottage Cheese Flatbread with Bell Pepper, Tomato, Basil & Hot Honey
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, trim, seed, and slice bell pepper lengthwise into thin strips.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add bell pepper, tomatoes, and salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, until tender and starting to brown, 5-7 minutes.

Meanwhile, arrange flatbreads on a baking sheet pan. Place in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and bake, flipping halfway through, until slightly crispy, about 8 minutes. Remove from oven and set aside.
While the flatbreads are baking, place cottage cheese in a strainer to remove excess liquid. Transfer to a small bowl, season with salt, and stir to combine. Set aside.
Place honey, hot sauce, and salt in another small bowl. Whisk to combine the hot honey and set aside.
When the veggies are done, add vinegar to the skillet, stir to combine, and remove from heat.
Pick basil leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and thinly slice into ribbons. Add half to the skillet with the veggies and stir to combine. (Reserve remaining basil for serving.)
Spread the cottage cheese over each flatbread, then top with veggies.
To serve, cut flatbreads into wedges and divide between plates. Drizzle with hot honey and top with reserved basil. Enjoy!

name: Couscous Greek Salad with Spring Greens & Feta
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled feta cheese
instructions: In a small saucepan, bring broth to a boil. Remove from heat, add couscous, and stir. Cover and let stand for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the mixed greens if they came pre-washed.)
Mince olives and transfer to a large bowl.
Zest and juice lemon into the bowl with the olives.
Peel and mince garlic. Add to the bowl along with oil, vinegar, honey, and salt; whisk to combine the dressing.
Peel and thinly slice onion into half rings. Add to the bowl and toss to combine.
Trim and quarter cucumber lengthwise, then slice crosswise into ¼-inch pieces. Add to the bowl.
Halve tomatoes and add to the bowl.
Seed and slice bell pepper into thin strips; add to the bowl.
Once the couscous is done, transfer to a baking sheet pan and spread out in an even layer to cool.
Shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems, mince leaves, and add to the bowl.
Drain and rinse chickpeas; add to the bowl.
Add couscous and feta to the bowl; toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide mixed greens between bowls. Top with couscous salad and enjoy!

name: Couscous-Romaine Salad with Warm Peaches, Almonds, Feta & Dill
ingredients: ½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled feta cheese
instructions: In a small saucepan, bring water and salt to a boil over high heat. Once boiling, remove from heat, add couscous, and stir to combine. Cover and let stand for 10 minutes; fluff with a fork.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Juice lemon into a medium bowl.
Peel and mince garlic. Add to the bowl with the lemon juice along with oil, Dijon, sugar, and spices; whisk to combine the dressing.
Trim and small dice cucumber. Add to the bowl with the dressing.
Halve lettuce lengthwise, then slice crosswise into thin (shred-like) strips. Add to the bowl.
Shave dill leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add half to the bowl and set the salad aside. (Reserve remaining dill for serving.)
When the couscous is done, transfer to a baking sheet pan. Spread out in an even layer and let cool slightly.
Quarter peaches lengthwise (around the pit); twist quarters to separate, then remove and discard pits. Slice each quarter into ½-inch thick wedges.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat.
While the skillet heats up, roughly chop almonds.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add peaches, almonds, sugar, salt, and pepper; cook, stirring occasionally, until peaches are golden brown and fork-tender, 3-4 minutes. Remove from heat.
Add cooled couscous to the bowl with the salad and gently toss to combine.
To serve, divide salad between plates or bowls; top with warm peaches, almonds, feta, and reserved dill. Enjoy!

name: Cream of Chickpea Soup with Toasted Rosemary Pita
ingredients: 16 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and small dice onion. Peel, trim, and small dice carrots. Transfer both to a medium bowl.
Trim and small dice celery; add to the bowl.
Preheat a medium saucepan over medium heat.
While the saucepan heats up, peel and mince garlic. Place half in a small bowl and set aside.
Once the saucepan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add veggies, remaining garlic, and spices to the saucepan. Cook, stirring occasionally, until veggies are soft, 5-6 minutes.
Meanwhile, drain and rinse chickpeas; transfer to a blender, along with broth, and blend until smooth.
Trim and medium dice zucchini.
Add chickpea mixture and zucchini to the saucepan, stir to combine, and bring soup to a simmer. Cook, stirring occasionally, until veggies are tender, 5-7 minutes.
Meanwhile, preheat oven to broil on high.
Place pitas on a baking sheet pan, drizzle with oil, and sprinkle with reserved garlic, salt, and rosemary. Place in the oven and broil until golden and toasted, 2-3 minutes. Remove from the oven.
Cut pitas into quarters.
Divide soup between bowls and drizzle with oil. Serve with pita on the side and enjoy!

name: Cream of Fennel Soup with Potato, Leek, Celery & Pumpkin Seeds
ingredients: 32 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.

Trim off root end and dark green top of the leek, leaving only the white and pale green parts. Cut leek in half lengthwise and rinse under running water, separating the layers to remove any dirt and grit. Slice crosswise into ¼-inch thick pieces. Place in a medium bowl.
Trim off root end and dark green stalks of the fennel, leaving only the white bulbs. Halve fennel bulbs lengthwise and medium dice. Add to the bowl with the leek.
Preheat a medium saucepan over medium heat.
While the pan heats up, trim and small dice celery. Add to the bowl.
Once the pan is hot, add butter and swirl to coat the bottom. Add veggies and spices; cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, 4-5 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel and small dice potato.

When the veggies are soft, add potato and broth to the pan. Stir to combine and bring to a boil over high heat. Once the soup is boiling, reduce heat and simmer until potatoes are tender, 12-15 minutes.
When the potatoes are tender, using a hand blender, purée the soup until smooth. (If using a regular blender, work in batches as needed, then return soup to the pan.)
Add cream to the pan and continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until just warmed through, 1 minute more. Remove from heat.
To serve, divide soup between bowls. Top with pumpkin seeds and enjoy!

name: Creamy Avocado Fettuccine with Corn & Cherry Tomatoes
instructions: Fill a large pot halfway with water, cover, and bring to a boil. Uncover, add salt and pasta, and stir for a few seconds. Cook until desired firmness, 8-10 minutes. Add the frozen corn within the last 4 minutes of cooking. When the pasta and corn are finished, drain, return to pot, and set aside.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Pick basil leaves off the stems and place in the blender. Reserve several leaves for garnish.
Juice the lemon into the blender.
Halve avocado and remove pit; scoop the flesh into the blender.
Peel the garlic and add to the blender.
Finely grate Parmesan and add to the blender along with the olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Blend the ingredients until smooth, 30-60 seconds.
Add the sauce from the blender into the pot with the pasta and corn; stir to combine.
Halve the grape tomatoes and add to the pasta, stir once more to combine.
Divide the pasta mixture between bowls, garnish with reserved basil, and enjoy!

name: Creamy Beet, Potato & Apple Soup with Crispy Prosciutto
ingredients: 24 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel, trim, and small dice beets and carrot. Place both in a medium bowl.
Peel and small dice potatoes. Add to the bowl with the beets and carrot.
Quarter, core, and small dice apple. Add to the bowl.
Peel and mince garlic. Peel, halve, and small dice onion. Add both to the bowl.
Preheat a medium saucepan over medium-high heat.
While the pan heats up, shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add half to the bowl (reserve remaining parsley for garnish).
Once the pan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add veggies, apple, and spices; cook, stirring occasionally, until starting to soften, 4-5 minutes.
When the veggies are soft, add broth and bring to a simmer. Once simmering, reduce heat to medium and continue to cook until veggies are very tender, 10-12 minutes more.
Meanwhile, preheat a large skillet over medium heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add the prosciutto and cook until crispy, about 1 minute per side. Remove prosciutto to a plate and set aside.
When the soup is done, remove from heat and add cream. Use a hand blender to purée the soup until smooth. Alternatively, use a potato masher to crush the veggies (the soup will be chunkier).
Crumble or chop prosciutto into bite-sized pieces.
To serve, divide soup between bowls; top with crispy prosciutto and reserved parsley. Enjoy!

name: Creamy Bell Pepper, Jalapeño, Onion & Corn Sauté with Warm Tortillas
ingredients: 4 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Wash, dry, trim, and seed bell peppers. Cut into ½-inch thick strips and transfer to a baking sheet pan.

Wash, dry, and halve jalapeño pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon. Slice into thin strips and add to the baking sheet with the bell pepper. (Be careful with jalapeños; do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Drizzle the mixed peppers with oil and season with spices; toss to coat, then spread out in an even layer.
Place baking sheet in the oven and roast, tossing halfway, until peppers are soft and begin to brown, 15-20 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, preheat a skillet over medium heat.
While the skillet heats up, peel, halve, and thinly slice onion into half-moons.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add onion and cook, stirring occasionally, until soft, 4-5 minutes.
Meanwhile, place corn in a colander and run under hot water (from the tap) to thaw; set aside to drain.
Cut cream cheese into small pieces.
Add cream cheese, yogurt, cream, and broth to the skillet with the onion; cook, stirring frequently, until the sauce is smooth, 1-2 minutes.
When the peppers are done, add them to the skillet along with the corn; continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until heated through, 3-4 minutes. Remove from heat.
Meanwhile, warm tortillas in another skillet, oven, or microwave (optional).
Divide creamy veggie sauté between bowls; serve with warm tortillas on the side for dipping. Enjoy!

name: Creamy Black Bean, Kale & Bell Pepper Stuffed Acorn Squash
ingredients: 4 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Preheat oven to 500°F and place rack in the center position. Line a baking sheet pan with aluminum foil to make cleanup easier (optional).
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Halve acorn squash lengthwise, trim ends, then scoop out the seeds. Rub the inside of the squash with oil, then season with salt and pepper; arrange halves, cut-side down, on the baking sheet.
Place squash in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast until tender, so a knife can easily pierce through the flesh, 20-25 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, fold kale leaves in half lengthwise and slice off the stems. Chop or tear leaves into bite-sized pieces and place in a medium bowl.
Trim, seed, and small dice bell pepper. Add to the bowl with the kale.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, peel and mince garlic. Add to the bowl.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add kale, bell pepper, and garlic to the skillet in handfuls, waiting for kale to wilt slightly before adding the next handful. Cook, stirring often, until the veggies are tender, 4-5 minutes.
Meanwhile, drain and rinse beans.
Cut cream cheese into small pieces.

When the veggies are done, add beans, cream cheese, broth, and spices to the skillet; stir until cheese is melted and combined. Bring to a simmer and continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens, 3-4 minutes more. Remove from heat.
To serve, divide squash halves between plates, stuff with filling, and sprinkle with bread crumbs. Enjoy!

name: Creamy Black Bean Wraps with Sautéed Bell Peppers & Mango-Cabbage Slaw
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Place half in a medium bowl and half in a blender.
Juice half of the lime into the bowl with the cilantro; juice remaining lime into the blender and set aside.

Quarter jalapeño pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon. Mince and add to the bowl with the cilantro. (Be careful with jalapeños; do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Peel and mince shallot; add to the bowl along with oil, salt, and cumin; whisk to combine the dressing.
Peel mango and slice flesh away from the pit, starting with the flat sides; medium dice and add to the bowl with the dressing.
Quarter the cabbage lengthwise, then cut out and discard the core; slice crosswise into thin (shred-like) strips and add to the bowl. Stir to combine the slaw and set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, trim, seed, and thinly slice bell pepper.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom; add bell pepper and salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, 4-5 minutes. Remove from heat.
Meanwhile, drain and rinse beans; add to the blender with the cilantro and lime juice.
Peel garlic; add to the blender along with water, pumpkin seeds, and spices. Blend on high until smooth.
Place tortillas on a flat surface and spread each with an even layer of black bean spread. Top with bell peppers and a small portion of slaw (reserving the rest for serving); roll tightly to close.
Cut wraps in half and divide between plates; serve with remaining slaw on the side and enjoy!

name: Creamy Cajun Chicken with Bell Pepper & Kale Sauté
ingredients: ¾ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
4 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Meanwhile, holding a knife parallel to the cutting board, cut the chicken in half horizontally to form thin fillets. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Once the skillet is hot, add butter and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add chicken to the skillet and pan-fry, flipping once, until golden brown and cooked through, 6-8 minutes.
While the chicken cooks, using a clean cutting board, fold kale leaves in half lengthwise and slice off the stems. Chop or tear leaves into bite-sized pieces and transfer to a medium bowl; set aside.
Trim, seed, and slice bell peppers into thin strips.
Once the chicken is done, remove to a plate and cover with foil. Return skillet to medium-high heat, add more butter, and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add peppers to the skillet and cook, stirring occasionally, until starting to soften, about 3 minutes.
Add tomatoes, broth, and spices to the skillet. Stir to combine and bring to a simmer.
Meanwhile, cut cream cheese into small pieces.
Once simmering, reduce heat to medium. Add cream cheese, a few pieces at a time, and stir until melted and combined, 2-3 minutes.
Add kale to the skillet in handfuls, waiting for the kale to wilt slightly before adding the next handful.
Return chicken to the skillet and turn to coat in the sauce. Continue to cook, until heated through, 1-2 minutes.
To serve, divide chicken and veggies between plates. Enjoy!

name: Creamy Cajun-Style Shrimp Scampi with Bell Pepper & Spaghetti Squash
ingredients: ¾ lb raw peeled shrimp, fresh or frozen
instructions: Preheat oven to 500°F and place rack in the center position. Line a baking sheet pan with aluminum foil to make cleanup easier (optional).
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
