Trim squash, halve lengthwise, and scrape out the seeds. Rub the inside of each half with oil, then season with salt and pepper. Arrange halves, cut-side down, on the baking sheet.
Place squash in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast until tender, so a knife can easily pierce through the flesh, 20-25 minutes.

Meanwhile, if using frozen shrimp, place them in the colander and run under cold water to thaw them slightly and remove any ice crystals. (If using fresh shrimp, skip this step.) Place the shrimp on a clean towel or paper towels and pat dry. Set aside.
Peel, halve, and slice onion lengthwise into thin pieces. Peel and mince garlic. Place both in a medium bowl.
Trim, seed, and slice bell pepper lengthwise into thin strips. Add to the bowl with the onion and garlic.
Trim and slice celery crosswise into thin pieces. Add to the bowl with the other veggies and set aside.
About 10 minutes before the squash is done, preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add veggies and spices; cook, stirring occasionally, until veggies start to soften, 3-4 minutes.
Meanwhile, shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves.
Add shrimp to the skillet and cook, stirring often, until just cooked through, about 3 minutes.
Add parsley and cream to the skillet. Continue to cook, stirring constantly, until simmering, 1 minute more. Remove from heat.

Remove squash from the oven and allow to cool slightly, about 5 minutes. Scrape the inside of the squash with a fork to separate into spaghetti-like strands. (Use an oven mitt or towel to hold it with your other hand.)
To serve, divide squash, shrimp, veggies, and sauce between plates. Enjoy!

name: Creamy Cashew Zucchini Noodles with Vegan Sausage, Artichoke & Spinach
ingredients: 4 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Boil water in a kettle. (If you do not have a kettle, boil water in a small saucepan, starting with hot water from the tap.) In a small heat-safe bowl, pour boiling water over cashews and set aside to soak.
Meanwhile, preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add sausages and cook, turning occasionally, until warmed through, about 5 minutes (or cook sausages according to package instructions). Remove to a plate and cover with foil. (Reserve skillet for later use.)
While the sausages are cooking, wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)
Trim zucchini and use a julienne (or regular) peeler to make noodles; place in a medium bowl.
Drain and thinly slice artichoke hearts; add to the bowl with the zucchini and set aside.
Peel and mince garlic.
Return skillet to medium heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add more oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add garlic and cook, stirring occasionally, until fragrant, about 1 minute.

Add zucchini, artichokes, and spinach to the skillet in handfuls, waiting for the veggies to wilt slightly before adding the next handful. Cook, stirring occasionally, until veggies are tender, 3-4 minutes.
Meanwhile, drain cashews and place in a blender.
Juice lemon into the blender with the cashews. Add broth, nutritional yeast, flour, and spices to the blender; purée on high until the sauce is smooth.
Cut sausages crosswise into 1-inch pieces.
Add sauce and sausage to the skillet; stir to combine with the veggies. Continue to cook, stirring often, until warmed through, 2-3 minutes more. Remove from heat.
To serve, divide veggies, sauce, and sausage between plates or bowls. Enjoy!

name: Creamy Cheddar-Tuna Pasta with Sautéed Broccoli & Zucchini
ingredients: 1 (6 oz) can chunk light tuna in water
instructions: Fill a medium saucepan halfway with hot water (from the tap); cover and bring to a boil over high heat.
Uncover, add salt and pasta, and stir for a few seconds. Cook until desired firmness, 8-10 minutes. Drain pasta and transfer to a small bowl, reserving saucepan for later use.
Meanwhile, wash, dry, and separate broccoli into bite-sized florets; cut stems into smaller pieces. Place in another small bowl.
Wash, dry, trim, and halve zucchini lengthwise; slice crosswise into ¼-inch thick half-moons. Add to the bowl with the broccoli.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom; add broccoli, zucchini, salt, and pepper. Cook, stirring often, until veggies are tender-crisp, 6-7 minutes. Cover, remove from heat, and set aside.
Meanwhile, cut cream cheese into small pieces; coarsely grate cheddar.

Once the pasta has been drained, place both cheeses, milk, salt, and paprika in the reserved saucepan. Set over medium heat and bring the mixture to a simmer, whisking frequently, until cheeses melt and combine, 2-3 minutes.
Drain tuna and flake with a fork; add to the cheese sauce along with the cooked pasta. Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until warmed through, 2-3 minutes more.
To serve, divide pasta and veggies between plates or bowls. Top pasta with crushed red pepper and enjoy!

name: Creamy Chicken, Apple & Almond Salad in Lettuce Cups
instructions: Heat a skillet over medium heat.
Holding a knife parallel to the cutting board, cut the chicken in half horizontally to form thin fillets. Season with salt and pepper.
Add olive oil to the skillet and swirl to coat the bottom.
Place the chicken in the skillet and cook until browned and cooked through, 3 to 4 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate and set aside to cool.
While the chicken cooks, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Juice the lemon into a large bowl, then add the mayonnaise, Dijon, salt, and pepper; whisk together.
Cut the apple into 4 wedges lengthwise, core, and medium dice; add to the bowl.
Trim and discard the ends of the celery; medium dice and add to the bowl.
Trim and discard the ends of the green onions; chop on and angle into ¼-inch pieces and add to the bowl.
Measure out the sliced almonds and add to the bowl.
Separate the lettuce leaves and arrange into two-leaf stacks. Alternatively, you can chop the lettuce.
Once the chicken has cooled, pull apart with your hands or medium dice; add to the bowl. Mix the salad until well combined.
Spoon the chicken salad onto the leaf stacks and divide between two plates (or one plate and one lunch container). Alternatively, arrange the chopped lettuce on plates and top with the salad. Enjoy!

name: Creamy Chicken & Mushroom Soup with Rice
ingredients: ¾ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
20 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and mince garlic. Peel and small dice onion. Transfer both to a large bowl.
Slice mushrooms and add to the bowl.
Peel and slice carrots into thin rounds. Trim and small dice celery. Add both to the bowl.
Preheat a medium saucepan over medium heat.
Once the pan is hot, add butter and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add veggies to the pan and cook, stirring occasionally, until tender, 6-7 minutes.
Meanwhile, medium dice chicken and season with salt and pepper.
Slide thyme leaves off the stems; discard stems.
Add chicken and thyme to the pan and cook, stirring occasionally, 3-4 minutes.
Add flour to the pan and stir to coat the vegetables and chicken. Cook, stirring frequently, about 1 minute.
Add broth, milk, rice, and salt to the pan. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce heat to low and simmer, stirring occasionally, until rice is soft and chicken is cooked through, 10-15 minutes.
To serve, divide soup between bowls and enjoy!

name: Creamy Coriander Chicken, Bell Pepper & Celery Sauté with Red Lentils
ingredients: ¾ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
12 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse lentils under cold water; drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add broth, then bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce heat to a simmer, cover, and cook until tender, about 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, preheat a skillet over medium heat.
While the skillet heats up, cut chicken into bite-sized pieces. Season with salt and pepper.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom; add chicken and sauté until cooked through, 3-4 minutes. Using a slotted spoon, transfer chicken to a plate, cover with aluminum foil, and set aside. (Reserve skillet with cooking juices for later use.)
While the chicken is cooking, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Using a clean cutting board, trim, seed, and small dice bell peppers. Place in a medium bowl.
Trim and small dice celery. Add to the bowl with the bell pepper.
Shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl (reserving a small handful for garnish).
Peel, halve, and small dice onion; peel and mince garlic. Add both to the bowl.
Return skillet (with cooking juices) to medium heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add more oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add veggies and spices to the skillet; cook, stirring often, until veggies begin to soften, 4-5 minutes.
Add tomatoes and broth to the skillet. Reduce heat to low and simmer, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens, 6-7 minutes.
Return chicken to the skillet, stir to combine, and simmer until heated through, 2-3 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in cream.
To serve, divide lentils and chicken sauté between bowls. Garnish with reserved parsley and enjoy!

name: Creamy Coriander Chicken "Enchilada" Skillet with Spinach & Mushrooms
ingredients: ¾ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Preheat a small saucepan over medium-high heat. Once the pan is hot, add butter and swirl to coat the bottom; add flour and cook, whisking constantly, until lightly golden, about 1 minute.
Slowly whisk in broth, salt, and coriander. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until thickened, 2-3 minutes. Remove sauce from heat and set aside.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)
Medium dice tomato; thinly slice mushrooms. Place both in a medium bowl.
Peel, halve, and small dice onion; peel and mince garlic. Add both to the bowl with the veggies and set aside.
Preheat an ovenproof skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat chicken dry with paper towels and cut into bite-sized pieces.

Once the skillet is hot, add butter and swirl to coat the bottom; add veggies, chicken, and spices. Cook, stirring occasionally, until veggies have softened and chicken is cooked through, 6-7 minutes.
Meanwhile, preheat oven to broil on high and position the rack in the upper third of the oven.
Coarsely grate mozzarella.
Add yogurt to the pan with the sauce and whisk until smooth.
Using a clean cutting board, slice tortillas into 2-inch long strips. When the chicken is done, add tortillas and sauce to the skillet; stir to combine.
Add spinach to the skillet in handfuls, waiting for the spinach to wilt slightly before adding the next handful. Stir to combine and remove from heat.
Top skillet with cheese and place in the oven; broil until the cheese is melted and bubbly, 3-5 minutes.
To serve, divide "enchilada" skillet between plates or bowls and enjoy!

name: Creamy Corn Pasta Salad with Cucumber, Basil, Chives & Feta
ingredients: ½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled feta cheese
instructions: Fill a medium saucepan halfway with water, cover, and bring to a boil. Uncover, add salt and pasta, and stir for a few seconds. Cook until desired firmness, 8-10 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Juice lemon into a large bowl.
Add mayo, feta, salt, and pepper to the bowl; stir to combine the dressing.
Trim and small dice cucumber; add to the bowl with the dressing.
Pick basil leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and thinly slice into ribbons; add to the bowl.
Chop chives into small pieces; add to the bowl.
Add corn to the pot with the pasta during the last 3 minutes of cooking.
When the pasta and corn are done, drain and rinse under cold water; add to the bowl and toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide pasta salad between bowls and enjoy!

name: Creamy Dijon Kale-Peach Salad with Walnuts, Goat Cheese & Bread Crumbs
instructions: Preheat a skillet over medium heat.
While the skillet heats up, roughly chop walnuts.
Once the skillet is hot, add walnuts and cook, stirring frequently, until lightly browned, 2-3 minutes. Transfer to a small bowl. (Reserve skillet for the next step.)

Return skillet to medium heat, add oil, and swirl to coat the bottom. Add bread crumbs and cook, stirring frequently, until golden and crispy, 3-5 minutes. Transfer to the bowl with the walnuts and set aside to cool.
Meanwhile, place yogurt, Dijon, oil, water, honey, vinegar, salt, and pepper in a medium bowl. Whisk to combine the dressing.

Wash, dry, and fold kale leaves in half lengthwise and slice off the stems; cut leaves crosswise into thin (shred-like) pieces. Add to the bowl with the dressing. Using your hands, massage kale with the dressing until wilted, 1-2 minutes.
Wash, dry, and quarter peaches lengthwise (around the pit); twist quarters to separate, then remove and discard pit. Medium dice the flesh and add to the bowl with the kale.
Crumble goat cheese into the bowl and gently toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide the salad between plates or bowls; top with walnuts and crispy bread crumbs. Enjoy!

name: Creamy Dill Chickpea Salad Sandwich with Strawberries
ingredients: ½ (5 oz) pkg spring mix (mixed greens)
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spring mix if it came pre-washed.)
Drain and rinse the chickpeas; transfer to a medium bowl.
Shave dill leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl.
Add mayo, Dijon, vinegar, and spices to the bowl.
Use a fork or potato masher to crush the chickpeas, making a semi-smooth spread. Set aside.
Peel, trim, and julienne or coarsely grate the carrot.
Slice the tomato.
Place bread slices on a flat surface. Spread half of the slices with a thick layer of chickpea salad and top carrots, tomato, and spring mix. Cover sandwiches with remaining bread slices.
Slice strawberries in half.
To serve, divide sandwiches and strawberries between plates and enjoy!

name: Creamy Dill Pasta with Seared Scallops & Zucchini
ingredients: 4 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Fill a medium saucepan halfway with hot water (from the tap); cover and bring to a boil over high heat. Uncover, add salt and pasta, and stir for a few seconds. Cook until desired firmness, 8-10 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash, dry, and trim zucchini. Halve zucchini lengthwise, then slice crosswise into half-moons.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add zucchini and salt; cook, stirring occasionally, until zucchini starts to soften, about 4 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel and mince shallot. Add to the skillet with the zucchini and continue to cook, stirring often, until soft, about 1 minute.

Add broth and cream to the skillet. Bring to a simmer and cook, stirring often, until sauce thickens slightly, 2 minutes more. Transfer zucchini and sauce to a medium bowl and cover with foil. Set aside.
Wipe skillet clean with paper towels and return to medium heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat scallops dry with paper towels and place on a plate; rub with oil and season with salt and pepper on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add scallops in a single layer; cook until they develop a nice sear and are opaque throughout, 1½-2 minutes per side. Once done, transfer to a clean plate.
Meanwhile, wash and dry dill. Shave leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves.
Once the pasta is done, drain and return to the pan. Add dill, zucchini, and sauce to the pan; toss to combine.
Return pan to medium heat to warm through, 1-2 minutes.
To serve, divide pasta and scallops between plates. Enjoy!

name: Creamy Garlic-Parmesan Tuna Pasta & Peas
ingredients: 1 (6 oz) can chunk light tuna in water
instructions: Fill a large pot halfway with hot water (from the tap), cover, and bring to a boil. Uncover, add salt and pasta, and stir for a few seconds. Cook until desired firmness, 8-10 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat a medium saucepan over medium heat.
Peel and mince garlic.
Once the pan is hot, add butter and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add garlic to the pan and stir until fragrant, 15-30 seconds.
Add peas and salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, until peas are heated through, 3-4 minutes.
Meanwhile, finely grate Parmesan.
Add cream to the pan with the peas and bring to a simmer. Once pasta is done, drain and add to the pan along with the Parmesan.
Drain tuna, add to the pan, and gently stir to combine.
To serve, divide pasta between bowls. Enjoy!

name: Creamy Herbed Pumpkin Pasta with Garlic Green Beans
ingredients: ½ (15 oz) can pure pumpkin purée
instructions: Fill a large pot halfway with hot water (from the tap), cover, and bring to a boil. Uncover, add salt and pasta, and stir for a few seconds. Cook until desired firmness, 8-10 minutes.
Peel and mince the garlic.
Wash the green beans and trim ends.
Add water to a large skillet and bring to a boil, covered, over high heat.

Once the water is boiling, uncover and stir in the beans, oil, butter, and half the garlic. Simmer until beans are tender and water has evaporated, 4-5 minutes. Season with salt, then remove from heat and set aside.
Preheat a small saucepan over medium heat.
Once the saucepan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add remaining garlic to the saucepan and cook for 1 minute, then add the tomato paste and cook for an additional 30 seconds, stirring frequently.
Add the pumpkin, milk, and spices to the saucepan. Whisk to combine and let simmer for 2-3 minutes.
Grate the parmesan.
Add the parmesan cheese (reserving a small amount for garnish) and red pepper flakes to the saucepan; stir to combine. Remove from the heat and set aside.
Once the pasta is done, drain and return to the large pot. Pour the sauce into the pot with the pasta and stir to combine.
To serve, divide the pasta and green beans between plates. Top pasta with remaining Parmesan and enjoy!

name: Creamy Italian-Style Sausage & Mixed Vegetable Soup with Basil
ingredients: 16 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Preheat a medium saucepan over medium-high heat.
While the pan heats up, wash and dry the fresh produce.

Once the pan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add sausage and spices; cook, breaking the meat apart with a spoon, until brown and crumbly, 5-6 minutes. Using a slotted spoon, transfer sausage to a small bowl. (Reserve pan with drippings for later use.)
Meanwhile, peel, trim, and small dice carrot; place in a medium bowl.
Trim and small dice celery; add to the bowl with the carrot.
Trim, seed, and small dice bell pepper; add to the bowl.
Peel, halve, and small dice onion; peel and mince garlic. Add both to the bowl.
When the sausage is done, return the pan (with drippings) to medium heat. Add veggies and cook, stirring occasionally, until starting to soften, 4-5 minutes.
Add broth and tomatoes to the pan; stir to combine the soup and bring to a boil over high heat.
Once the soup is boiling, reduce heat to medium and simmer, stirring occasionally, until the veggies are soft, 6-7 minutes.
Meanwhile, pick basil leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and thinly slice into ribbons.
When the soup is done, add half of the basil to the pan (reserving the rest for garnish). Purée with an immersion or regular blender (return soup to the pan if using a regular blender).
Add cooked sausage to the soup along with cream, salt, and pepper. Reduce heat to low and cook, stirring occasionally, until warmed through, 2-3 minutes.
To serve, divide soup between bowls and top with reserved basil. Enjoy!

name: Creamy Leek & Bacon Pasta with Goat Cheese
instructions: Fill a medium saucepan about halfway with hot water (from the tap); cover with a lid and bring to a boil over high heat.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat.
Cut the bacon crosswise into ¼-inch-thick strips.

When the water in the saucepan comes to a boil, uncover the pan and season the water with salt, then add the pasta and stir for a few seconds. Cook the pasta, uncovered, for 11 to 12 minutes (or according to package directions). Drain the pasta in a colander, reserving ½ cup of the cooking water.
Add the bacon to the skillet; cook, stirring occasionally, until cooked through but not crispy, 2 to 4 minutes. Once done, transfer to a bowl, leaving the drippings in the skillet.
While the bacon cooks, trim off and discard the ends of the leeks; thinly slice the leeks crosswise.
Once the bacon has been transferred, add the leeks to the skillet and season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, until tender, 6 to 8 minutes.
Finely grate 1 cup of Parmesan and transfer to a small bowl.

Add the pasta, bacon, goat cheese, ¾ of the Parmesan (save the rest for garnishing) and reserved cooking water to the skillet; cook, stirring constantly, until the mixture is smooth and thoroughly combined, 1 to 2 minutes.
To serve, divide the pasta between bowls, sprinkle with the remaining Parmesan, and garnish with black pepper. Enjoy!

name: Creamy Leek, Prosciutto & Pea Linguine with Parmesan
instructions: Fill a medium saucepan halfway with water (from the tap), cover, and bring to a boil. Uncover, add salt and pasta, and stir for a few seconds. Cook until desired firmness, 8-10 minutes. (Reserve 1 cup of pasta cooking water before draining.)

Meanwhile, trim off the root end and dark green top of the leeks, leaving only the white and pale green parts. Cut leeks in half lengthwise and rinse under running water, separating the layers to remove any dirt and grit. Slice crosswise into ½-inch half-moons.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat.
While the skillet heats up, peel and mince garlic.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add leeks and garlic; cook, stirring occasionally, until leeks are soft, 8-10 minutes.
Meanwhile, cut the cream cheese into small pieces and set aside.
Roughly chop prosciutto into bite-sized pieces. Once the leeks have softened, add prosciutto to the skillet, and cook, stirring often, until slightly crispy, 1-2 minutes.
Add cream cheese, peas, and a ½-cup of the pasta cooking water to the skillet. Reduce heat to low, and continue to cook, stirring often, until cream cheese is melted, 3-4 minutes.
Finely grate Parmesan and add to the skillet (reserving a small handful for garnish); stir to combine.
Add drained pasta to the skillet and toss to combine; add additional pasta water, 1 tablespoon at a time, if necessary, to reach a saucy consistency.
To serve, divide pasta between bowls and garnish with remaining Parmesan. Enjoy!

name: Creamy Linguine with Crispy Prosciutto, Squash, Fennel & Parmesan
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim and peel squash; halve lengthwise, scrape out the seeds, and medium dice.

Fill a medium saucepan halfway with hot water (from the tap), cover, and bring to a boil. Uncover, add salt, squash, and pasta, then stir for a few seconds. Cook until squash is tender and pasta is desired firmness, 8-10 minutes. (Reserve a ¼-cup cooking water before draining and set aside.)
Meanwhile, preheat a large skillet over medium heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add prosciutto and cook until crispy, about 1 minute per side. Remove to a plate and set aside. (Reserve skillet for later use.)
Trim off root end and stalks of the fennel, leaving only the white bulb. Halve fennel bulb lengthwise, then slice crosswise into thin half-moons.
Return skillet to medium heat. Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add fennel and spices; cook, stirring occasionally, until soft and starting to brown, 5-6 minutes.
While the fennel is cooking, shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Place in a small bowl.
Finely grate Parmesan. Add to the bowl with the parsley.

When the fennel is done, add cooked squash, pasta, reserved pasta water, parsley, Parmesan, and cream to the skillet. Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until water has evaporated and Parmesan has melted, about 2 minutes. Remove from heat.
Meanwhile, crumble or chop prosciutto into bite-sized pieces.
To serve, divide pasta between plates or bowls and top with crispy prosciutto. Enjoy!

name: Creamy Mushroom Bacon Soup with Pear & Mixed Greens Salad
ingredients: 12 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
½ (5 oz) pkg spring mix (mixed greens)
instructions: Wash and slice the mushrooms.
Peel and small dice the onion. Peel and mince the garlic.
Melt butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add the mushrooms, onion, and garlic. Season with thyme, salt, and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, until tender, 5-6 minutes.
Heat a skillet over medium heat.
Chop the bacon into smaller pieces. Add to the skillet and cook until crispy, 3-4 minutes.
Sprinkle cornstarch over the mushrooms and stir to coat.
Pour in the broth and cream. Stir well and bring the soup to a simmer. Cook until thickened, 1-2 minutes.
Wash and dry the greens.
Wash, core, and thinly slice the pear.
Purée the soup with an immersion (hand) blender or regular blender if desired. Otherwise, leave as is.
Arrange a bed of greens on a plate, top with pear slices, and drizzle with olive oil. Pour soup into a bowl and sprinkle with bacon. Enjoy!

name: Creamy Pumpkin-Parmesan Chicken with Spinach & Crispy Sage
ingredients: ¾ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
4 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
½ (15 oz) can pure pumpkin purée
instructions: Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, wash, dry, and pick sage leaves off the stems; discard stems.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add sage leaves in single layer and cook until crispy, about 30 seconds. Using tongs or a slotted spoon, transfer crispy sage to a paper towel-lined plate and season with salt. (Reserve skillet with oil for later use.)

Pat the chicken dry with paper towels and place on a cutting board. Holding a knife parallel to the cutting board, cut the chicken in half horizontally to form thin fillets. Season both sides with salt and pepper.

Return skillet to medium-high heat. Once the skillet is hot, add chicken and pan-fry, without turning, until golden underneath, 5-6 minutes (the chicken will not be cooked all the way through). Remove to a plate. (Reserve skillet with sage oil for later use.)
Meanwhile, using a clean cutting board, peel and mince garlic.
Finely grate Parmesan.
Return skillet with sage oil to medium heat, add more oil, and swirl to coat the bottom. Add garlic and tomato paste; cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant, 15-30 seconds.
Add Parmesan, pumpkin, broth, cream, and salt to the skillet, then stir to combine. Cook, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly, 2-3 minutes.
Wash, dry, and add spinach to the skillet in handfuls, waiting for it to wilt slightly before adding the next handful.
Return chicken to the skillet and nestle into the sauce; cover with a lid. Cook, turning chicken occasionally, until cooked through, 5-7 minutes. Remove from heat.
To serve, divide chicken and sauce between plates or bowls. Top with crispy sage and enjoy!

name: Creamy Sesame-Ginger Spaghetti Squash with Shrimp & Edamame
ingredients: ¾ lb raw peeled shrimp, fresh or frozen
instructions: Preheat oven to 500°F and place rack in the center position. Line a baking sheet pan with aluminum foil to make cleanup easier (optional).
Wash, dry, and trim spaghetti squash, then halve lengthwise, and scrape out the seeds. Rub the inside of the squash with oil and season with salt. Arrange halves, cut-side down, on the baking sheet.
Place squash in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast until tender, so a knife can easily pierce through the flesh, 20-25 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash, dry, peel, and mince ginger. Place in a small bowl along with tahini, water, oil, vinegar, soy sauce, and maple syrup. Whisk to combine the sauce and set aside.

If using frozen shrimp, place them in a colander and run under cold water to thaw them slightly and remove any ice crystals. (If using fresh shrimp, skip this step.) Place the shrimp on a clean towel or paper towels and pat dry.
When the squash has about 5 minutes left, preheat a skillet over medium heat.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add shrimp, salt, and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, until shrimp are just opaque, 2-3 minutes. Remove to a plate. (Set skillet aside for later use.)
Meanwhile, place edamame in a clean colander and rinse under hot, running water (from the tap) to defrost; set aside to drain.
Remove squash from the oven and allow to cool slightly, about 5 minutes.
Scrape the inside of the squash with a fork to separate into spaghetti-like strands (use an oven mitt or towel to hold it with your other hand).
Return skillet to medium heat. Once the skillet is hot, add sesame-ginger sauce, spaghetti squash, and edamame. Cook, tossing occasionally, until warmed through, 2-3 minutes. Remove from heat.
To serve, divide spaghetti squash, shrimp, and edamame between plates or bowls. Enjoy!

name: Creamy Shrimp, Spinach & Bacon over Parmesan Cauliflower "Grits"
ingredients: ¾ lb raw peeled shrimp, fresh or frozen
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)

If using frozen shrimp, place them in a colander and run under cold water to thaw them slightly and remove any ice crystals. (If using fresh shrimp, skip this step.) Place the shrimp on a clean towel or paper towels and pat dry.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, medium dice bacon.

Once the skillet is hot, add bacon and cook, stirring occasionally, until crispy, 3-4 minutes. Using a slotted spoon, transfer crispy bacon to a paper towel-lined plate (leaving the drippings in the skillet). Set skillet aside for later use.
Meanwhile, finely grate Parmesan and set aside.

Using a clean cutting board, cut the cauliflower head into quarters, then trim off and discard the leaves and thick stem. Using a box grater or food processor, coarsely grate cauliflower and place in a medium saucepan.

Add hot water (from the tap) to the pan with the cauliflower, filling it about halfway; cover and bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Once the water is boiling, reduce heat to medium and simmer until the cauliflower is tender, 8-10 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel and mince garlic.
Return the skillet (with bacon drippings) to medium-low heat. Once the skillet is hot, add garlic and cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Add cream, shrimp, and spices to the skillet; cook, stirring occasionally, until the shrimp is just opaque, 3-4 minutes.

When the cauliflower is done, drain in a strainer and return to the pan. Add Parmesan, butter, salt, and pepper. Using a potato masher, gently mash the cauliflower into a "grits" consistency; cover and set aside.

When the shrimp is done, add spinach to the skillet in handfuls, waiting for the spinach to wilt slightly before adding the next handful. Juice lemon into the skillet, stir to combine, and remove from heat.
To serve, divide cauliflower "grits" and creamy shrimp between bowls; top with bacon and enjoy!

name: Creamy Shrimp & Veggie Soup with Parmesan Crisps
ingredients: 24 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
¾ lb raw peeled shrimp, fresh or frozen
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F. Line a baking sheet pan with parchment paper and set aside.
If using frozen shrimp, place them in a colander and run under cold water to thaw them slightly and remove any ice crystals. (If using fresh shrimp, skip this step.) Set aside to drain.
Wash, dry, peel, and small dice carrot. Peel and small dice onion; transfer both to a medium bowl.
Wash, dry, trim, and small dice celery; add to the bowl with the veggies.
Preheat a medium saucepan over medium heat.
While the pan heats up, peel and mince garlic; add to the bowl with the veggies.
Once the pan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add veggies and thyme to the pan; cook, stirring occasionally, until starting to soften, 4-5 minutes.
Meanwhile, finely grate cheese. To make the crisps, measure out 1 tbsp of grated cheese and place in a pile on the baking sheet. Repeat with remaining cheese, keeping the piles a few inches apart.
Place baking sheet in the oven and bake until cheese is lightly browned and crisp, 5-7 minutes. (Watch carefully because they can burn quickly.) Once done, remove from the oven and set aside to cool.

While the crisps are cooking, add broth, salt, and pepper to the pan with the veggies. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce heat to a simmer; cook, stirring occasionally, until veggies are tender, about 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, roughly chop the shrimp; add to the soup and continue to simmer until cooked through, about 3 minutes.
Cut cream cheese into small pieces and add to the pan; continue to cook, stirring constantly, until the cheese is melted and combined, about 3 minutes.
Divide soup between bowls and serve with cheese crisps on the side. Enjoy!

name: Creamy Soba Noodle Bowl with Rainbow Veggies
instructions: Fill a large pot halfway with water and bring to a boil.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and grate or mince the ginger; transfer to a medium bowl.
Add peanut butter, honey, water, tamari, vinegar, chili-garlic sauce, and sesame oil to the bowl with the ginger. Whisk until smooth, set aside.
Once water is boiling, add salt and noodles and stir for a few seconds. Cook according to package directions, 3 to 4 minutes. When cooked, drain and rinse well under cold water.
Trim off and discard the ends of the green onions; cut the onions crosswise into ⅛-inch pieces at an angle.
Cut the bell pepper lengthwise into quarters; remove and discard the seeds and white membrane. Julienne the pepper.
Trim and discard the ends of the cucumber; halve the cucumber lengthwise and then slice into ⅛-inch thick planks. Then, cut the planks ¼-inch wide julienne sticks.
Trim the stem ends of the carrot and peel; julienne or coarsely grate the carrot.
Trim off and discard the root end of the cabbage; halve the cabbage lengthwise, then thinly slice crosswise.
Roughly chop the cashews.
Add noodles, cashews, and veggies to the bowl with the dressing and toss to combine.
Divide noodles between plates, serve cold. Enjoy!

name: Creamy Sun-Dried Tomato Gnocchi with White Beans, Pepper, Peas & Basil
instructions: Drain and rinse beans; set aside to drain further.
Wash and dry bell pepper, then trim, seed, and small dice. Place in a small bowl.
Peel, halve, and small dice onion; peel and mince garlic. Add both to the bowl with the bell pepper.
Mince sun-dried tomatoes and add to the bowl.
Preheat a medium saucepan over medium-high heat.
Once the pan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add veggies to the pan; cook, stirring frequently, until softened, 4-5 minutes. (Reserve bowl for next step.)
Meanwhile, place water and cornstarch in the reserved bowl; whisk to combine the slurry.

When the veggies are soft, add cornstarch slurry, almond milk, nutritional yeast, salt, and pepper to the pan; stir to combine and bring to a simmer. Once simmering, cook, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens, 3-4 minutes.
While the sauce simmers, wash and dry basil. Pick leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and thinly slice into ribbons.
Add beans, gnocchi, peas, and half of the basil to the pan (reserve remaining basil for garnish). Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until warmed through, 4-5 minutes more.
To serve, divide creamy gnocchi between bowls. Top with remaining basil and enjoy!

name: Creamy Sundried Tomato & Spinach Linguine Pasta
instructions: Fill a medium saucepan halfway with water, cover, and bring to a boil. Uncover, add salt and pasta, and stir for a few seconds. Cook until desired firmness, 8-10 minutes.
Heat a sauté pan over medium heat.
Peel and small dice onion. Peel and mince garlic. Thinly slice sun-dried tomatoes.
Coat bottom of pan with oil. Add onion, garlic, tomatoes, and crushed red pepper. Stirring frequently, cook until onion is softened, 3-4 minutes.
Wash and dry spinach.
Add tomato sauce, basil, salt, and pepper to pan. Stir to combine and simmer for 3-4 minutes.
Finely grate ⅛ cup of Parmesan.
Add yogurt to pan, reduce heat to medium-low, and stir to combine.
Add spinach and fold in until wilted. Remove pan from heat until pasta is ready.
Drain pasta in a colander, reserving about ½ cup of the pasta water.
Add pasta and ½ of the water to sauce; toss to coat. If sauce is too thick, add more pasta water to thin it out.
Place pasta in a bowl or on a plate and garnish with grated Parmesan.

name: Creamy Thyme Chicken with Sweet Potato-Beet Mash & Dijon Kale Salad
ingredients: ¾ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
instructions: Wash, dry, peel, and trim beet. Medium dice, transfer to a medium saucepan, and cover with hot water (from the tap). Cover and bring to a boil over high heat.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the remaining fresh produce.
Peel, trim, and medium dice sweet potato; place in a small bowl and set aside.
Once the water in the saucepan is boiling, reduce to a simmer and cook until beets are starting to soften, about 10 minutes. Add sweet potatoes and cook until veggies are soft, 10-12 minutes more.
While the beets are cooking, juice lemon into a medium bowl. Add oil, Dijon, salt, and pepper; whisk to combine the dressing and set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.

While the skillet heats up, pat the chicken dry with paper towels and place on a cutting board. Holding a knife parallel to the cutting board, cut the chicken in half horizontally to form thin cutlets. Season with salt and pepper on both sides.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add cutlets to the skillet and pan-fry until cooked through and golden brown, 3-4 minutes per side. Remove to a plate and loosely cover with aluminum foil.

Meanwhile, using a clean cutting board, fold kale leaves in half lengthwise and slice off the stems. Chop or tear leaves into bite-sized pieces and add to the bowl with the dressing; toss to combine the salad and set aside.
Peel and mince garlic and shallot.
Return the skillet (with cooking juices), to medium heat; add garlic, shallot, and thyme. Cook, stirring occasionally, until shallot has softened, 2-3 minutes.
While the shallot is cooking, cut cream cheese into small pieces.

Add cream cheese and water to the skillet; stir until melted and combined, 1-2 minutes. (if needed, add additional water, 1 tablespoon at a time, to reach a saucy consistency). Return chicken to the skillet, along with any accumulated juices; stir to combine the chicken and sauce. Remove from heat.

When the beet and sweet potato are ready, drain in a colander and return to the saucepan; add salt and pepper, then use a hand (or regular blender) to purée until smooth. (Add water, a couple of tablespoons at a time, to reach desired consistency.)
To serve, divide sweet potato-beet mash, chicken, sauce, and salad between plates. Enjoy!

name: Creamy Tuscan Shrimp with Bacon, Tomatoes, Spinach & Zucchini Noodles
ingredients: ¾ lb raw peeled shrimp, fresh or frozen
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)

If using frozen shrimp, place them in the colander and run under cold water to thaw them slightly and remove any ice crystals. (If using fresh shrimp, skip this step.) Place the shrimp on a clean towel or paper towels and pat dry.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat.
While the skillet heats up, small dice bacon.
Once the skillet is hot, add bacon and cook, stirring occasionally, until crispy, 4-5 minutes. Using a slotted spoon, remove to a paper towel-lined plate, leaving the drippings in the skillet.
Meanwhile, trim zucchini and use a julienne (or regular) peeler to make noodles. Place in a medium bowl and set aside.
Halve the tomatoes.
Return skillet (with bacon drippings) to medium heat; add tomatoes and spices to the skillet. Cook, stirring occasionally, until tomatoes soften, 3-4 minutes.
Meanwhile, finely grate Parmesan.
Peel and mince garlic.
Add garlic and shrimp to the skillet; cook until shrimp are opaque, 1-2 minutes per side.
Add spinach to the skillet in handfuls, waiting for the spinach to wilt slightly before adding the next handful.
Add zucchini noodles, Parmesan (reserving a small handful for garnish), and cream to the skillet; stir to combine. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the sauce is melted and combined, 1-2 minutes.
Meanwhile, pick basil leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and thinly slice into ribbons. Add half the to skillet (reserving the rest for garnish) and stir to combine. Remove from heat.
To serve, divide shrimp, veggies, and sauce between bowls. Top with bacon and remaining Parmesan and basil. Enjoy!

name: Creamy Vegan Cashew "Parma Rosa" Penne with Fresh Basil & Side Salad
ingredients: 4 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Fill a medium saucepan halfway with water, cover, and bring to a boil. Uncover, add salt and pasta, and stir for a few seconds. Cook until desired firmness, 8-10 minutes.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Place cashews in a small bowl. Using a measuring cup, carefully remove 1 cup of boiling water from the pot and pour over the cashews; let sit for 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, place oil, vinegar, sugar, and spices in a medium bowl; whisk to combine the dressing.
Halve tomatoes and transfer to the bowl with the dressing.
Trim and halve cucumber, then thinly slice crosswise. Add to the bowl and set aside.
Drain cashews and place in a blender.
Add tomato sauce, broth, nutritional yeast, flour, and spices to the blender and purée until smooth.
Drain pasta, return to the saucepan, and set over medium heat. Add the sauce from the blender and stir to combine; cook, stirring occasionally, until warmed through, 3-4 minutes.
Meanwhile, pick basil leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and thinly slice into ribbons.
Chop or tear lettuce into bite-sized pieces and transfer to the bowl with the dressing; toss to combine the salad.
Divide pasta between plates and top with basil. Serve with salad on the side and enjoy!

name: Creamy Vegan Cashew, Potato & White Bean Soup with Mixed Vegetables
ingredients: ½ (15 oz) can cannellini (white kidney) beans
32 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Place a medium saucepan over high heat. Add broth, cover, and bring to a boil.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Place cashews in a small bowl. Carefully pour boiling broth over the cashews and set aside to soak for 15 minutes. Reserve saucepan for later use.
Meanwhile, peel and mince garlic. Peel and small dice onion. Transfer both to a medium bowl.
Peel and small dice carrot. Trim and small dice celery. Add both to the bowl.
Medium dice potatoes. Add to the bowl along with corn and peas.
Return saucepan to medium heat.
Once the pan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add veggies to the pan and cook, stirring occasionally, until starting to soften, 6-7 minutes.
Meanwhile, slide thyme leaves off the stems; discard stems.
Add broth, half the thyme (reserving the rest for garnish), and spices to the pan.
Drain and rinse beans; add to the pan.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce heat to low and simmer, stirring occasionally, until potatoes are fork-tender, 8-10 minutes.
Meanwhile, transfer the cashew-broth mixture to a blender and purée until smooth.
Add cashew cream to the pan and stir to combine. Cook, stirring occasionally, until soup begins to thicken, 5-7 minutes.
To serve, divide soup between bowls. Top with reserved thyme and enjoy!

name: Creamy Vegan Cashew Pumpkin "Alfredo" Linguine with Baby Spinach
ingredients: 6 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
½ (15 oz) can pure pumpkin purée
instructions: Fill a medium saucepan halfway with water, cover, and bring to a boil. Uncover, add salt and pasta, and stir for a few seconds. Cook until desired firmness, 8-10 minutes.
Meanwhile, place cashews in a small bowl. Using a measuring cup, carefully remove 1 cup of boiling water from the pot and pour over the cashews; let sit for 15 minutes.
Peel and slice garlic; transfer to a blender.
Once cashews are done soaking, drain and add to the blender.
Add pumpkin, broth, nutritional yeast, flour, and spices to the blender and purée until smooth.
Wash and dry the spinach. (Skip this step if it came pre-washed.)
Drain pasta and set aside to drain further.
Return saucepan to medium heat. Add the sauce from the blender and bring to a simmer.
Once simmering, add spinach to the pan in handfuls, waiting for the spinach to wilt slightly before adding the next handful.
Add pasta, stir to combine, and cook, stirring occasionally, until warmed through, 3-4 minutes.
Divide pasta between bowls and enjoy!

name: Creamy Vegan Mushroom Stroganoff with Thyme & Baby Spinach
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
½ (13.5 fl oz) can coconut milk
instructions: Fill a large pot halfway with water, cover, and bring to a boil. Uncover, add salt and pasta, and stir for a few seconds. Cook until desired firmness, 8-10 minutes.
Meanwhile, preheat a large skillet over medium heat.
Peel and small dice the onion.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add the onion to the skillet; cook, stirring frequently, until softened, 3-4 minutes.
Wash and slice mushrooms. Peel and mince garlic.
Add mushrooms, garlic, and spices to the skillet. Cook, stirring frequently, until mushrooms are softened, 4-5 minutes.
In a small bowl, whisk together the coconut milk and cornstarch.

Add coconut milk mixture, broth, soy sauce, and vinegar to the skillet. Stir and bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce heat to medium-low and cook, stirring occasionally, until the sauce has thickened, 5-6 minutes.
Wash and dry thyme. Slide leaves off the stems; discard the stems. Add leaves to the skillet and stir to combine.
Wash and dry the spinach (skip if it came pre-washed). Add spinach to the skillet in handfuls, waiting for the spinach to wilt slightly before adding the next handful.
Drain pasta and add to skillet with the sauce. Toss to combine.
To serve, divide the pasta and sauce between plates. Enjoy!

name: Crispy Chicken with Cauliflower Rice Pilaf and Fresh Greens
ingredients: 2 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
½ (5 oz) pkg spring mix (mixed greens)
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the mixed greens if they came pre-washed.)
Preheat a cast iron or oven-proof skillet (if available) over medium-high heat.
Meanwhile, pat the chicken dry with paper towel and place on a plate; season with salt and pepper on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add butter and swirl to coat the bottom. Add the chicken to the skillet and cook until skin is golden and crispy, about 4 minutes; flip and repeat on other side.
Place skillet in the oven and continue cooking for 15 minutes, or until cooked through. If your skillet is not oven proof, transfer to a baking dish with a wire rack.
Remove the leaves from the cauliflower. Using a food processor or box grater, grate to rice-like texture. Transfer to a large bowl and set aside.
Place a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add butter, onion powder, garlic powder, paprika, turmeric, cayenne pepper, and salt.
Once the butter is fully melted, add the cauliflower and cook for 2 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add broth to the cauliflower and cook for another 5-7 minutes.
Shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves. Stir into the cauliflower.
Cut lemon into wedges. Toss the mixed greens with oil and a squeeze of lemon.
To serve, arrange chicken, cauliflower-rice, and greens on plates. Serve with lemon wedges, if desired, enjoy!

name: Crispy Chicken Thighs & Maple-Mustard Roast Red Cabbage with Parsley
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Wash and dry cabbage; halve lengthwise, cut out the core, and slice crosswise into 1-inch thick wedges. Transfer to a baking sheet pan.
Place oil, Dijon, maple syrup, salt, and pepper in a small bowl. Stir to combine the glaze.
Spread half of the glaze over the top side of the cabbage wedges. Carefully flip wedges and repeat with remaining glaze. (Reserve bowl for later use.)
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast until cabbage is golden brown and tender, about 25 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, wash, dry, and shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Place half in the reserved bowl. (Set aside remaining parsley for serving.)
Peel and mince garlic. Add to the bowl with the parsley along with mayo, Dijon, and thyme, then stir to combine.
Pat chicken dry with paper towels, then season with salt and pepper on both sides. Transfer to a baking dish.
Spread Dijon mayo over the top side of the chicken, then sprinkle with bread crumbs, pressing gently to adhere. Drizzle with oil.
Add baking dish to the oven and roast until chicken is golden and cooked through, 18-20 minutes. Remove from oven.
To serve, divide cabbage and chicken between plates; top with reserved parsley. Enjoy!

name: Crispy Fish Sandwich with Garlic-Tartar Sauce & Side Salad
instructions: Peel and mince garlic; mince capers. Transfer both to a small bowl along with mayo, vinegar, Dijon, and pepper. Whisk to combine the tartar sauce; set aside.
Combine oil, vinegar, Dijon, maple syrup, salt, and pepper in a salad bowl; whisk to combine the dressing.
Peel and thinly slice onion into half rounds. Set half of the onions aside on a plate. Add the other half to the bowl with the dressing and stir to combine.
Wash and dry the tomatoes, then halve and slice them. Place half of the tomatoes on the plate; transfer the other half to the salad bowl.
Drain and thinly slice artichoke hearts; transfer to the salad bowl. Set aside while you prepare the fish.
Whisk egg in a medium bowl.
Place bread crumbs in a second medium bowl.
Pat the fish dry with paper towels and place on a plate. Season with salt and pepper on both sides.
Sprinkle flour over both sides of each fillet. Press gently to adhere.
Preheat a large nonstick skillet over medium heat.
To bread the fish, dip each fillet into the egg, and then the bread crumbs. Press gently to adhere.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add fish to the skillet and cook until golden brown and cooked through, about 4 minutes per side. Once done, transfer to a clean plate lined with paper towel.
Meanwhile, toast the rolls.
Wash and dry the lettuce; separate the leaves. Set aside 2 large leaves per sandwich. Chop or tear remaining leaves into bite-sized pieces, add to the salad bowl and toss to combine.
Place the bottom half of a roll on each plate. Layer with tartar sauce, lettuce, tomato, onion, and a crispy fish fillet; close with top half of the roll. Serve salad on the side and enjoy!

name: Crispy Pork Schnitzel with Ranch-Dressed Apple & Broccoli Slaw
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Mince chives and place in a medium bowl.
Juice lime into the bowl with the chives.
Add yogurt, mayo, and spices to the bowl. Whisk to combine the dressing.
Quarter and core apples; cut into matchsticks or coarsely grate. Add to the bowl with the dressing, along with the broccoli slaw, and stir to combine. Set aside.
Crack egg into another medium bowl and beat with a whisk or fork.
Place bread crumbs on a plate.
Holding a knife parallel to the cutting board, cut the chops in half horizontally to form thin cutlets. Season cutlets with salt and pepper on both sides.
Preheat a large skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, dip the seasoned cutlets into the beaten egg (letting the excess drip off), then into the bread crumbs, pressing to adhere. Transfer to another plate.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add the breaded cutlets and cook until golden brown and cooked through, 2-3 minutes per side. Remove from heat.
To serve, divide pork schnitzel and slaw between plates. Enjoy!

name: Crispy Shrimp Burrito (Chimichanga) with Tomatoes, Cilantro & Yogurt
ingredients: ¾ lb raw peeled shrimp, fresh or frozen
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.

If using frozen shrimp, place them in a colander and run under cold water to thaw them slightly and remove any ice crystals. (If using fresh shrimp, skip this step.) Place the shrimp on a clean towel or paper towels and pat dry.
Trim, seed, and slice bell pepper into thin strips; place in a medium bowl.

Quarter jalapeño pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon. Mince and add to the bowl with the bell pepper. (Be careful with jalapeños; do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Peel and mince garlic; peel, halve, and small dice onion. Add both to the bowl.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add bell pepper, jalapeño, garlic, and onion; cook, stirring occasionally, until veggies soften, 4-5 minutes. (Reserve bowl for next step.)
Meanwhile, coarsely grate cheddar; cut cream cheese into small pieces. Place cheeses in the reserved bowl and set aside.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves.
Add shrimp, half of the cilantro (reserve remaining cilantro for garnish), and spices to the skillet; cook until shrimp are opaque, 1-2 minutes per side.
Reduce heat to low and add the cheeses. Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until cheeses melt and combine, 2-3 minutes more. Remove from heat.
Place tortillas on a flat surface and divide shrimp filling down the center of each one. Fold in sides of tortillas and roll tightly to complete.
Wipe the skillet clean with paper towels and return to medium-high heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add more oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Lay burritos, seam-side down, and cook, rotating every 2-3 minutes, until golden brown and crispy on all sides. Remove from heat.
Meanwhile, medium dice tomatoes.
To serve, cut burritos in half and divide between plates. Top with tomatoes, reserved cilantro, and yogurt. Enjoy!

name: Crispy Tempeh Bowl with Roasted Beets, Maple-Lemon Kale & Couscous
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.

Peel and trim beets; halve lengthwise, then slice into ¼-inch thick wedges. Transfer to one half of a baking sheet pan, drizzle with oil, then season with salt and pepper. Toss to coat and spread out in an even layer.
Slice tempeh crosswise into ½-inch thick strips. Add to the other half of the baking sheet, then drizzle with soy sauce and oil. Season with pepper, then toss to coat and spread out in an even layer.

Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast, stirring each halfway through, until beets are tender and tempeh is crisp, about 20 minutes. Remove baking sheet from oven; season tempeh with additional soy sauce and toss to coat.
Meanwhile, in a small saucepan, bring broth to a boil. Remove from heat, add couscous, and stir. Cover and let stand for 10 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
While the couscous is cooking, juice lemon into a small bowl, then add mayo, oil, Dijon, maple syrup, salt, and pepper. Whisk to combine the dressing and set aside.
Fold kale leaves in half lengthwise and slice off the stems; chop or tear leaves into bite-sized pieces. Place in a medium bowl.
Add half of the dressing to the bowl with the kale and, using your hands, massage kale with the dressing until wilted, 1-2 minutes. (Reserve remaining dressing for serving.)
To serve, divide couscous between bowls; top with kale, beets, and crispy tempeh. Drizzle with reserved dressing and enjoy!

name: Crispy Tofu Sandwiches with Garlic Aioli & Arugula-Cucumber Salad
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F.

Cut tofu into ½-inch thick planks along the short side. Sandwich tofu between clean towels or paper towels and place on a baking sheet pan. Place a cutting board with something heavy on top and set aside to press out excess water.
Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the arugula if it came pre-washed.)
Zest lemon into a small bowl (reserve lemon for the dressing). Add mayo and spices, then stir to combine the aioli.

Place tofu on the baking sheet. Spread 1 tablespoon aioli over top side of the tofu, sprinkle with half of the bread crumbs, and drizzle with half of the oil. Carefully flip tofu and repeat with 1 tablespoon aioli, remaining bread crumbs, and remaining oil. (Reserve remaining aioli for sandwiches.)
Place tofu in the oven and bake, turning once, until the breading is crispy and golden brown, 15-18 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, juice the lemon into a medium bowl. Add oil, maple syrup, Dijon, salt, and pepper; whisk to combine the dressing.
Trim and thinly slice cucumber crosswise into rounds; add to the bowl with the dressing.
Add broccoli slaw and arugula to the bowl; toss to combine the salad.
Toast buns if desired.
Spread the remaining aioli over both halves of each bun. Layer each with a small portion of salad (reserving the rest for serving) and crispy tofu.
To serve, divide sandwiches and reserved salad between plates. Enjoy!

name: Crispy Tofu Sandwiches with Quick Pickles, Chili Sauce & Mixed Greens
ingredients: ½ (5 oz) pkg spring mix (mixed greens)
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F.

Cut tofu into ½-inch thick planks along the short side. Sandwich tofu between clean towels or paper towels and place on a baking sheet pan. Place a cutting board with something heavy on top and set aside to press out excess water.
Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the mixed greens if they came pre-washed.)
Place vinegar, sugar, and salt in a medium bowl; whisk to combine the pickling liquid.
Trim and thinly slice cucumber and radishes; add both to the bowl with the pickling liquid, stir to combine, and set aside.
Place mayo and spices in a small bowl; whisk to combine the spiced mayo.

Place tofu planks on the baking sheet. Spread half the spiced mayo over the top side of the tofu, sprinkle with half the bread crumbs (pressing them gently into the surface to adhere), and drizzle with half the oil. Carefully flip tofu and repeat with remaining spiced mayo, bread crumbs, and oil.
Place tofu in the oven and bake, turning once, until the breading is crispy and golden brown, 15-18 minutes. Remove from the oven.

Meanwhile, place oil, chili-garlic sauce, vinegar, and sugar in a small saucepan; whisk to combine the sauce and bring to a simmer over medium heat. Once simmering, remove from heat and cover with a lid to keep warm. (If the sauce separates, whisk together once more, right before serving.)
Toast buns if desired.
Spread mayo on both halves of each bun. Layer each with a small portion of pickled vegetables (reserving the rest for the salad), top with tofu, and drizzle with sauce.
To serve, divide sandwiches and mixed greens between plates. Drizzle greens with oil, then top with reserved pickled vegetables and a small portion of pickling liquid. Enjoy!

name: Crispy Tofu with Warm Broccoli Slaw, Cucumber & Bell Pepper Salad
instructions: Cut tofu in half along the long side. Sandwich tofu between clean towels or paper towels and place on a baking sheet pan. Place a cutting board with something heavy on top and set aside to press out excess water.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim and halve cucumber lengthwise, then slice crosswise into thin half-moons; place in a medium bowl.
Trim, seed, and slice bell pepper lengthwise into strips. Add to the bowl with the cucumber.
Trim green onions and cut crosswise into ¼-inch pieces; add to the bowl.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl.
Pick mint leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl.
Roughly chop peanuts and add to the bowl along with the broccoli slaw. Set aside.
Place bread crumbs and cornstarch in a small bowl; stir to combine.
Cut the tofu into ½-inch thick planks along the short side. Working in batches, roll tofu in the breadcrumb mixture, pressing gently to adhere; transfer to a plate.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add breaded tofu and pan-fry, turning occasionally, until browned and crispy, 5-7 minutes. Return crispy tofu to the plate.

Meanwhile, place vinegar, soy sauce, oil, sugar, and chili-garlic sauce in a small saucepan; stir to combine and bring the dressing to a boil over high heat. Once boiling, reduce heat to low and simmer, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened, about 2 minutes. Remove from heat.
Add half of the dressing to the bowl with the salad and toss to combine. (Reserve remaining dressing for serving.)
To serve, divide salad and crispy tofu between bowls. Drizzle with remaining dressing and enjoy!

name: Cuban-Spiced Steak with Garlicky Avocado, Tomato & Onion Salad
ingredients: ¾ lb striploin (New York strip) steak
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Juice the citrus into a medium bowl.
Peel and mince garlic. Add to the bowl with the citrus juice along with oil and spices; whisk to combine the dressing.
Peel, halve, and thinly slice onion. Add to the bowl with the dressing and toss to coat; set aside to marinate.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the steak dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with spices on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add steak to the skillet and cook until desired doneness, 2-5 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate and loosely cover with aluminum foil.
While the steak is cooking, cut tomatoes into wedges and add to the bowl with the onions.
Halve and pit the avocado. Scoop halves out with a spoon and cut into bite-sized pieces; add to the bowl.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl and gently stir to combine the salad.
Thinly slice steak against the grain.
To serve, divide steak between plates; use a slotted spoon to portion salad, then drizzle steak with leftover dressing. Enjoy!

name: Cumin Steak with Yellow Rice, Tomato-Cucumber Salad & Garlic Sauce
ingredients: ¾ lb striploin (New York strip) steak
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add water, turmeric, and salt; bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Cook rice until liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim and medium dice cucumber; transfer to a small bowl.
Medium dice tomato and add to the bowl with the cucumber.
Peel and small dice shallot; add to the bowl.
Juice lemon into the bowl, drizzle with oil, and season with spices. Stir to combine the salad and set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the steak dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with spices on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add steak and cook until desired doneness, 2-5 minutes per side. Transfer to a clean plate and let rest, about 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, place mayo, vinegar, and spices in another small bowl. Whisk to combine the garlic sauce.
Thinly slice steak against the grain.
Divide rice, salad, and steak between plates. Serve with garlic sauce on the side and enjoy!

name: Curried Cauliflower Quinoa Bowl with Arugula, Pistachios & Mint
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
In a small saucepan, combine quinoa and broth; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to a simmer, cover, and cook for 15 minutes. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, place oil and spices in a medium bowl. Stir to combine the spice oil.
Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the arugula if it came pre-washed.)
Separate cauliflower into bite-sized florets and cut stems into smaller pieces. Add to the bowl with the spice oil and stir to coat. Transfer to a baking sheet pan and spread out in an even layer.
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast, stirring halfway through, until cauliflower is fork-tender, 15-20 minutes. Remove from oven.
While the cauliflower is roasting, pick mint leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Place half of the mint in a small bowl. (Reserve remaining mint for serving.)
Add yogurt, tahini, water, vinegar, additional garlic powder, and salt to the bowl with the mint. Whisk to combine the sauce and set aside.
Trim and quarter cucumber lengthwise, then cut crosswise into bite-sized pieces.
Roughly chop pistachios.
To serve, divide quinoa, cauliflower, arugula, and cucumber between bowls. Drizzle with sauce, then top with pistachios and reserved mint. Enjoy!

name: Curried Chicken, Chickpea & Cauliflower Bake with Cilantro Raita
ingredients: ¾ lb chicken thighs, boneless skinless
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Place vinegar, honey, and salt in a small bowl; stir to combine the pickling liquid.
Peel, halve, and slice onion crosswise into thin half-moons. Add to the bowl with the pickling liquid, stir to combine, and set aside.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Drain and rinse chickpeas. Transfer to a baking sheet pan and pat dry with paper towels.
Separate cauliflower into bite-sized florets and cut stems into smaller pieces. Add to the baking sheet with the chickpeas.

Pat the chicken thighs dry with paper towels and cut into bite-sized pieces. Add to the baking sheet, drizzle with oil, then season with curry powder and salt. Stir to coat and spread out in an even layer.
Place baking sheet in the oven and roast, stirring halfway through, until chickpeas are crisp, cauliflower is fork-tender, and chicken is cooked through, 18-20 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, using a clean cutting board, peel, trim, and grate cucumber. Use paper towels or a clean cloth to squeeze excess moisture out of the grated cucumber. Place in another small bowl.
Juice half of the lime into the bowl with the cucumber. Cut remaining lime into wedges and set aside for serving.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl along with yogurt, additional honey, crushed red pepper, and salt; stir to combine the raita.
Divide chicken bake between plates or bowls; top with pickled onion. Serve with raita on the side and enjoy!

name: Curried Chickpea Salad Flatbread Wrap with Lettuce, Tomato & Dill
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Juice lemon into a medium bowl.
Drain and rinse chickpeas. Transfer half of the chickpeas to the bowl with the lemon juice, along with mayonnaise and spices. Using a fork or potato masher, mash until smooth.
Add remaining chickpeas to the bowl and stir to combine.
Small dice celery and add to the bowl.
Trim off and discard ends of the green onions; cut crosswise into ¼-inch pieces and transfer to the bowl.
Using a knife, shave dill leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl and stir to combine the chickpea salad.
Warm flatbreads in a skillet, oven, or toaster (optional).
Meanwhile, slice tomato into rounds.
Divide lettuce and tomato slices between flatbreads and season with salt and pepper. Top with curried chickpea salad.
To make wraps easier to eat, place flatbreads on individual squares of parchment paper. Use the paper to tightly roll and secure each wrap. Otherwise eat as is and get a little messy! Enjoy!

name: Curried Chickpea Salad with Mixed Greens, Apple, Pumpkin Seeds & Feta
ingredients: ½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled feta cheese
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the mixed greens if they came pre-washed.)
Juice half the lemon into a medium bowl. (Set remaining lemon aside for later.)
Drain and rinse chickpeas. Transfer half the chickpeas to the bowl with the lemon juice; add mayo and spices. Using a fork or potato masher, mash until smooth.
Add remaining chickpeas to the bowl and stir to combine.
Trim and small dice celery; add to the bowl.
Chop chives into small pieces and add to the bowl.
Using a knife, shave dill leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl and stir to combine the chickpea salad. Set aside.
Juice remaining lemon into another medium bowl. Add oil, honey, Dijon, salt, and pepper; whisk to combine the dressing.
Quarter and core apple, then thinly slice each quarter; add to the bowl with the dressing.
Add mixed greens, feta, and pumpkin seeds to the bowl. Toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide green salad between plates or bowls, top with curried chickpea salad, and enjoy!

name: Curried Coconut Pumpkin Soup with Chicken & Crusty Bread
ingredients: ½ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
½ (13.5 fl oz) can coconut milk
½ (15 oz) can pure pumpkin purée
instructions: Heat a small saucepan over medium heat.
Peel and mince onion and garlic.
Coat bottom of saucepan with oil. Add onion and, stirring frequently, cook until softened, 4-5 minutes.
Add garlic and cook until fragrant, 15-30 seconds. Add pumpkin, broth, curry powder, turmeric, and salt. Stir until well combined and cook for 2-3 minutes.
Add coconut milk and stir to combine. Simmer until rest of the meal is ready.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Slice chicken in half horizontally to form thin fillets. Season with salt and pepper.
Coat bottom of skillet with oil. Add chicken and cook until cooked through, 2-3 minutes per side.
Wash and dry parsley. Shave leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves.
Toast bread.
Shred chicken with your hands or cut into bite-sized pieces.
To serve, pour soup in a bowl, garnish with chicken and parsley, and have crusty bread on the side. Enjoy!

name: Curried Coconut-Red Lentil Soup with Veggies, Cilantro & Yogurt
ingredients: 24 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
½ (13.5 fl oz) can coconut milk
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and small dice onion; transfer to a medium bowl.
Peel, trim, and small dice carrots; add to the bowl with the onion.
Trim and small dice zucchini; add to the bowl.
Preheat a medium saucepan over medium-high heat.
While the pan heats up, peel and mince garlic.
Once the pan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add veggies, garlic, curry powder, and salt to the pan; cook, stirring often, until starting to soften, 3-4 minutes.
Add broth, coconut milk, tomatoes, and lentils to the pan; stir to combine, cover, and bring to a boil.
Once the soup is boiling, reduce heat to medium-low; simmer, stirring occasionally, until lentils and veggies are tender, about 15 minutes. Remove from heat.
Meanwhile, shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves.
When the soup is done, add cilantro and stir to combine.
To serve, divide soup between bowls, top with yogurt, and enjoy!

name: Curried Couscous, Kidney Bean & Maple Broccoli-Acorn Squash Bowl
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F. Line a baking sheet pan with aluminum foil for easier cleanup (optional).
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Place maple syrup, oil, salt, and pepper in a medium bowl; whisk to combine the sauce.
Separate broccoli into bite-sized florets and cut stems into smaller pieces; add to the bowl with the sauce.
Halve acorn squash lengthwise, trim off the ends, then scoop out the seeds. Cut crosswise into ¼-inch-thick slices and add to the bowl; toss vegetables to coat.

Transfer broccoli-squash mixture to the baking sheet and spread out in an even layer. Place in the oven and bake, tossing halfway through, until veggies are fork-tender, 15-20 minutes. Remove from oven.
While the veggies are roasting, peel and small dice onion. Trim, seed, and small dice bell pepper.
Preheat a medium saucepan over medium-high heat.
Meanwhile, drain and rinse beans; set aside to drain further.
Once the pan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add onion and bell pepper; cook, stirring occasionally, until soft, about 5 minutes.
Add beans, broth, and spices to the pan; stir to combine and bring to a boil over high heat.
Once the liquid is boiling, remove from heat; add couscous, and stir. Cover and let stand for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, cut lime into wedges and set aside.
To serve, divide curried couscous, roasted veggies, and lime wedges between bowls. Enjoy!

name: Curried Egg Salad Naan Wrap with Roasted Asparagus & Chives
instructions: Place eggs in a small saucepan, cover with water, and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to a simmer and cook for 8 minutes. Drain hot water and add ice or run under cold water to cool.
Meanwhile, preheat oven to 400°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Snap or cut off the woody ends of the asparagus and transfer to a baking sheet pan. Drizzle with oil and season with salt and pepper.
Place asparagus in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and bake until fork-tender, 10-12 minutes.
Meanwhile, place mayo, vinegar, Dijon, and spices in a medium bowl; whisk to combine the dressing.
Small dice celery and add to the bowl with the dressing.
Peel and mince shallot; add to the bowl.
Peel and roughly chop the eggs. Add to the bowl and stir to combine the egg salad.
Warm naan in a skillet, oven, or toaster (optional).
Chop chives into small pieces.
Layer each naan with asparagus, egg salad, and chives; roll to close.
To make wraps easier to eat, place each naan on a square of parchment paper. Use the paper to tightly roll and secure each wrap. Otherwise eat as is and get a little messy! Enjoy!

name: Curried Eggless Salad Sandwich with Spring Salad
ingredients: ½ (12 oz) pkg extra firm tofu
½ (5 oz) pkg spring mix (mixed greens)
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spring mix if it came pre-washed.)
Peel and mince (or press) the garlic into a medium salad bowl.
Add the mustard, maple syrup, olive oil, balsamic, salt, and pepper to the bowl with the garlic. Set aside.
Halve the grape tomatoes and set aside.
Shave the leaves off parsley stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves.
Trim off and discard the ends of the green onions; cut the onions crosswise into ¼-inch pieces and set both aside.
Halve and pit avocado, scoop flesh out into a medium bowl and mash with a fork  Add Dijon, curry powder, turmeric, cayenne, nutritional yeast, salt, and pepper. Mix well.
Drain tofu. Transfer to paper towels and gently pat dry. Using your hands, crumble tofu into the bowl with the avocado mixture.
Add parsley and green onion to bowl with the tofu and avocado, stir to combine.
Toast bread if desired.
Assemble the sandwiches by arranging several leaves of the spring mix on half the bread slices and topping with equal portions of the tofu salad and a second slice of bread.
Mix remaining spring mix with the dressing and tomatoes.
To serve, arrange a sandwich on each plate with the salad on the side. Enjoy!

name: Curried Lentil Dal with a Cucumber Salad
ingredients: 12 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Rinse lentils under cold water and transfer to a medium saucepan. Add broth and spices; stir and bring to a boil. Lentils should be covered by about 1 inch of liquid; add water if needed.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim off and discard the ends of the onion and remove the outer layer; small dice the onion. Add ¾ of the onion to the saucepan with the lentils. Put the other ¼ in a blender.
Peel, and small dice the carrots. Small dice the tomatoes. Add both to the saucepan with the lentils.
When lentil mixture comes to a boil, stir, cover with a lid and turn to low heat. Simmer for about 20 minutes or until lentils are tender.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Trim and discard the ends of the cucumber; halve the cucumber lengthwise, then thinly slice crosswise on an angle. Transfer to a small bowl.
Warm the whole chili in the preheated skillet, 1 minute per side. Remove the stem and add chili to blender. Turn the skillet to medium low heat.
Juice the lemon and add the juice to the blender. Blend with onion, chili, mustard, sugar, salt, and yogurt. Transfer to the small bowl with the cucumber. Gently mix until evenly coated.
Place naan bread in skillet, toasting both sides, about 1 minute per side.
Using a knife, shave the cilantro leaves off the stems at a downward angle, working away from your body; discard the stems and finely chop the leaves. Put aside in a small bowl.
Once lentils are tender, give them a quick pulse with an immersion blender. Stir in half of the cilantro.
To serve, ladle the lentils into a bowl and garnish with the remaining cilantro. Serve with the toasted naan and cucumber salad on the side. Enjoy!

name: Curried Salmon with Eggplant Puree & Lemony Arugula
instructions: Preheat the oven to the broil setting and position the rack in the upper third of the oven.
Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the arugula if it came pre-washed.)
Halve the eggplant lengthwise and place the halves cut-side-up in a baking dish.

Place the eggplant in the oven and broil until browned on top, 4 to 5 minutes. Then, flip the halves over and continue to broil until the flesh is tender, another 8 to 10 minutes. Once done, remove from the oven and set aside to cool.
Juice the lemon; divide evenly between a small bowl and a medium salad bowl.
To the lemon juice in the salad bowl, add olive oil, Dijon, salt, and pepper; whisk together.
Add the arugula to the salad bowl and toss to thoroughly coat with the dressing; set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the salmon dry with paper towels and place on a plate; rub with curry powder, salt, and pepper on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add coconut oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Carefully place the salmon, skin-side-down, in the skillet; cook until the flesh is opaque and flaky, 3 to 4 minutes per side (depending on thickness). Once done, transfer the salmon to a plate.
Trim off and discard the root end of the garlic; peel and mince or press the garlic. Add to the small bowl with the lemon juice.
Scoop the eggplant flesh out of the skin and transfer to a small saucepan; discard the skin.
To the eggplant, add the lemon juice and garlic mixture, olive oil, salt, and pepper; purée the mixture with a hand blender or mash with a potato masher until smooth.
To serve, divide the eggplant purée between plates, place the salmon on top, and add the arugula salad on the side. Enjoy!

name: Curried Shrimp Stir-Fry with Noodles, Zucchini, Bell Pepper & Cilantro
ingredients: ¾ lb raw peeled shrimp, fresh or frozen
instructions: Fill a medium saucepan about halfway with hot water (from the tap); cover and bring to a boil over high heat.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Once the water in the pan is boiling, remove from heat and add rice noodles. Soak for 10 minutes, or according to package directions, then drain in a colander and rinse under cold water; set aside.

Meanwhile, if using frozen shrimp, place them in a colander and run under cold water to thaw them slightly and remove any ice crystals. (If using fresh shrimp, skip this step.) Place the shrimp on a clean towel or paper towels and pat dry.
Juice lime into a small bowl. Add water, soy sauce, sugar, and spices; whisk to combine the sauce and set aside.
Peel and mince ginger and garlic; place in a medium bowl.
