Peel, trim, and slice carrot crosswise into thin rounds; add to the bowl with ginger and garlic.
Trim, seed, and medium dice bell pepper; add to the bowl.
Trim and medium dice zucchini; add to the bowl and set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add shrimp, salt, and pepper; cook until the shrimp are opaque, 1-2 minutes per side. Remove to a plate and loosely cover with aluminum foil.
Return skillet to medium-high heat, add more oil, and swirl to coat the bottom; add veggies and salt. Stir-fry until starting to soften, 3-4 minutes.
Add drained noodles and sauce to the skillet with the veggies. Continue to cook, tossing frequently, until the liquid is absorbed and noodles are warmed through, 1-2 minutes more.
Meanwhile, shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add cilantro to the skillet, along with cooked shrimp, and toss to combine; remove from heat.
To serve, divide noodles, shrimp, and veggies between plates or bowls. Enjoy!

name: Curry-Lime Butternut Squash & Cauliflower Soup with Crispy Chickpeas
ingredients: 16 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
½ (13.5 fl oz) can coconut milk
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel, halve, and small dice onion. Place in a medium bowl.
Trim and peel squash; halve lengthwise, scrape out the seeds, and medium dice the flesh. Add to the bowl with the onion.
Separate cauliflower into bite-sized florets and cut stems into smaller pieces. Add to the bowl.
Preheat a medium saucepan over medium-high heat.
Once the pan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add veggies, curry powder, and salt; cook, stirring occasionally, until starting to brown, about 15 minutes. (Reserve bowl for later use.)
Meanwhile, drain and rinse chickpeas. Transfer to a baking sheet pan and pat dry with paper towels.
Add whole (unpeeled) garlic cloves to the baking sheet with the chickpeas. Drizzle with oil, then season with curry powder and salt. Stir to coat and spread out in an even layer.
Place baking sheet in the oven and roast, stirring chickpeas halfway through, until crispy and golden, 15-18 minutes.

When the veggies in the saucepan are starting to brown, add broth and coconut milk; bring to a simmer. Once simmering, reduce heat to medium and continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until veggies are very tender, about 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, zest and juice half of the lime into the reserved bowl. (Cut remaining lime into wedges and set aside for serving.)
Peel and mince ginger. Add to the bowl with the lime zest and juice.

When the chickpeas and garlic are done, remove from oven. Carefully transfer roasted garlic to the cutting board. Using the back of a spoon, press on the cloves to remove the skins; add garlic to the bowl. Set aside the crispy chickpeas.

Once the veggies are tender, remove soup from heat. Add lime, ginger, and roasted garlic to the pan. Use a hand blender to purée the soup until smooth. Alternatively, use a potato masher to crush the veggies (the soup will be chunkier).
Divide the soup between bowls and top with crispy chickpeas. Serve with lime wedges for squeezing and enjoy!

name: "Currywurst" Sausage Wrap with Red Cabbage, Bell Pepper & Apple Slaw
instructions: Preheat a grill pan, outdoor grill, or regular skillet over medium-high heat.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Once the pan is hot, coat with oil; add sausages and cook, turning occasionally, until cooked through, 12-15 minutes. Remove from heat.
While the sausages are cooking, place ketchup, water, Worcestershire, vinegar, and spices in a small bowl. Whisk to combine the sauce and set aside.
Juice lemon into a medium bowl; add yogurt, mayo, and spices. Whisk to combine the dressing.
Quarter cabbage lengthwise, then cut out and discard the core; slice crosswise into thin (shred-like) strips and add to the bowl with the dressing.
Quarter, core, and small dice apple; add to the bowl.
Trim, halve, seed, and slice bell pepper into thin strips; add to the bowl and toss to combine the slaw. Set aside.
When the sausages are done, transfer to a cutting board and slice crosswise into thin rounds.
Warm tortillas in a skillet, oven, or microwave (optional).
Place tortillas on a flat surface and top each with a small portion of slaw; arrange sausage slices on top and drizzle with sauce. Roll tightly to close. (Reserve remaining slaw for serving.)
Cut wraps in half and divide between plates; serve with remaining slaw on the side. Enjoy!

name: "Deviled Egg" Pasta Salad with Cucumber, Bell Pepper, Celery & Parsley
instructions: Place eggs in a small saucepan, cover with hot water (from the tap) and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to a simmer and cook for 8 minutes. Drain and add ice or run under cold water to cool; set aside.

While the eggs are cooking, fill a medium saucepan halfway with water, cover, and bring to a boil. Uncover, add salt and pasta, and stir for a few seconds. Cook until desired firmness, 8-10 minutes. Drain pasta and rinse under cold water to cool completely; set aside.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim and small dice celery; place in a medium bowl.
Trim and medium dice cucumber; add to the bowl with the celery.
Trim, seed, and small dice bell pepper; add to the bowl.
Shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl.
Peel and mince shallot; add to the bowl and set aside.

Once the eggs have cooled, peel and halve lengthwise. Using a spoon, separate the yolks from the whites and place the yolks in a small bowl. Roughly chop the egg whites and add to the bowl with the veggies.
Gently mash the yolks with a fork. Add mayo, Dijon, vinegar, and spices to the bowl; stir to combine the dressing.
Add pasta and dressing to the bowl with the veggies; stir to combine the pasta salad.
To serve, divide pasta salad between plates or bowls. Enjoy!

name: Dijon-Caper Potato Salad with Pork Chops & Green Beans
instructions: Fill a large pot about halfway with hot water (from the tap); cover with a lid and bring to a boil over high heat.
Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the arugula if it came pre-washed.)
Trim ends from the green beans; cut potatoes in half.
Add beans to the boiling water and cook until tender-crisp, 1-2 minutes. Using tongs, remove the beans and transfer to a colander, leaving water on the heat. Rinse under cold water and set aside.
Add potatoes to the boiling water and cook until fork-tender, about 12 minutes.
Meanwhile, preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the pork chops dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with salt and pepper on both sides.
When the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add chops to the skillet and cook, flipping once, until browned on both sides and cooked through, 6-7 minutes. When done, transfer to a plate and cover with aluminum foil; set aside to rest.
Meanwhile, peel and mince the garlic; rinse and roughly chop the capers. Place both in a medium bowl.
Add oil, vinegar, Dijon, honey, salt, and pepper to the bowl; whisk to combine the dressing.
Drain potatoes and rinse under cold water to cool. Add potatoes and green beans to the bowl with the dressing and toss to combine.
Thinly slice the pork chops crosswise into strips.
To serve, divide arugula between plates, top with potato-bean salad and sliced pork. Enjoy!

name: Dijon Pork Chops with Roasted Brussels Sprouts & Grapes
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Wash brussels sprouts and grapes. Trim ends and halve the brussels sprouts. Pick grapes off the stems. Transfer to a sheet pan.
Drizzle with oil and season with thyme, salt, and pepper. Toss to coat.
Place in the oven and roast until browned and tender, 20 minutes.
In a medium bowl, whisk together Dijon, vinegar, maple syrup, thyme, salt, and pepper.
Add pork chops to marinade and toss to coat.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Coat bottom of skillet with oil. Add pork chops and cook until cooked through, 3-5 minutes per side, depending on thickness. Spoon any remaining marinade over top while cooking.
Remove sheet from oven, drizzle brussels sprouts and grapes with vinegar, and toss to coat.
To serve, place pork chops, brussels sprouts, and grapes on a plate. Enjoy!

name: Easy Korean Stew (Yukgaejang) with Bok Choy & Radishes
ingredients: 24 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
¾ lb striploin (New York strip) steak
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.

Halve chili pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon. Mince and place in a medium bowl. (Be careful, with chilies, do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Peel and mince garlic; add to the bowl along with oil, soy sauce, chili-garlic sauce, and salt. Whisk to combine the pepper paste.
Thinly slice steak into strips and place in another medium bowl. Add half of the pepper paste and toss to coat. Set aside to marinate.
Using a clean cutting board, trim off and discard root ends of the bok choy; separate into leaves and add to the bowl with the remaining pepper paste.
Trim and cut green onions into 1-inch pieces; add to the bowl with the bok choy.
Preheat a large pot over medium-high heat.
Meanwhile, trim and quarter the radishes; add to the bowl with the other veggies and toss to coat.
Once the pot is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add steak to the pot and cook, stirring frequently, until starting to brown, about 2 minutes.
Add broth and veggies to the pot, stirring to combine. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to a simmer and cook until steak is cooked through and veggies are tender, 3 minutes more.
Meanwhile, whisk egg and salt in a small bowl.
When the soup is done, slowly pour the egg into the pot, while gently stirring, to separate into strands. Remove from heat.
To serve, divide soup between bowls and enjoy!

name: Edamame Pasta Salad with Peas, Bell Pepper, Tomato, Arugula & Feta
ingredients: ½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled feta cheese
½ (8 oz) pkg sugar snap peas
instructions: Fill a medium saucepan halfway with hot water (from the tap), cover, and bring to a boil. Uncover, add salt and pasta, and stir for a few seconds. Cook until desired firmness, 8-10 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the arugula if it came pre-washed.)
Place edamame and peas in the colander and rinse under hot, running water (from the tap) to defrost; set aside to drain.
Peel and mince garlic; place in a medium bowl.
Add oil, vinegar, honey, Dijon, salt, and pepper to the bowl; whisk to combine the dressing.
Trim, seed, and halve bell pepper crosswise; slice into thin strips and add to the bowl with the dressing.
Halve tomatoes and add to the bowl.
Trim and halve snap peas crosswise; add to the bowl.
Shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl.
Add drained edamame and peas to the bowl.
When the pasta is done, drain and rinse under cold water to cool; add to the bowl.
Add arugula and feta to the bowl; toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide salad between plates or bowls. Enjoy!

name: Egg Salad & Spinach Sandwich with Grape Tomatoes
instructions: Place eggs in a small saucepan, cover with water, and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to a simmer and cook for 8 minutes. Drain hot water and add ice or run under cold water to cool.
Peel and mince garlic. In a medium bowl, prepared dressing by mixing together garlic, mayo, Dijon, dill, paprika, salt, and pepper.
Wash celery and green onions. Small dice celery and add to bowl with dressing. Trim and discard green onion roots ends, chop, and add to bowl.
Wash and dry spinach.
Wash tomatoes.
Toast bread.
Peel, medium dice, and add eggs to bowl with other ingredients. Stir to combine.
Place bread in pairs on a flat surface. Arrange spinach leaves over one slice of bread in each pair, then top with egg salad and a second slice of bread.
Serve sandwiches with tomatoes on the side and enjoy!

name: Egg & Walnut Caesar Salad with Parmesan Crisps & Creamy Dressing
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F.

Place the eggs in a small saucepan, cover with water, and bring to a full, rolling boil. Once boiling, remove the pan from the heat, cover, and let sit for 10 minutes. Drain and cover with cold water or ice to cool.
Coarsely grate ½ cup of Parmesan.
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Measure out 1 tbsp of the grated Parmesan and place in a pile on the sheet. Repeat with remaining cheese.
Place in the oven and bake until lightly browned, 5-7 minutes. Once done, remove from the oven and let them sit for a couple of minutes.
Finely grate ⅛ cup of Parmesan.
Peel and mince the garlic.
In a small bowl, prepare the dressing by whisking together the grated Parmesan, minced garlic, lemon juice, mayo, olive oil, Dijon, Worcestershire, salt, and pepper. Set aside.
Roughly chop the walnuts and transfer to a small bowl.
Wash and dry the lettuce. Halve lengthwise, then chop crosswise into 1 inch strips.
Peel and quarter the eggs. Gently peel the Parmesan crisps off of the parchment paper. Slice remaining ¼ lemon into wedges.
To serve, arrange a bed of romaine on a plate, add eggs, walnuts, and Parmesan crisps. Drizzle with dressing and lemon juice and enjoy!

name: Eggplant Melts with Fresh Mozzarella & Pan-Fried Chickpeas
ingredients: ½ (8 oz) pkg fresh mozzarella cheese
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F and place the rack in the center position.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Halve the eggplant lengthwise and place cut-side-up on a baking sheet. Rub with olive oil and season with salt and pepper.
Place the eggplant in the oven and roast until softened, 15 to 20 minutes.
Slice the tomato into rounds and place on a plate lined with paper towels.
Drain the mozzarella and pat dry with paper towels; slice into rounds.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Drain and rinse the chickpeas; transfer to paper towels or a clean towel and pat dry.
Add coconut oil to the skillet and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add the chickpeas to the skillet and shake to distribute. Cook the chickpeas, shaking occasionally, until they are golden brown and crispy, 5 to 7 minutes.
In a medium bowl, combine and mix together paprika, cumin, and salt.
Using a slotted spoon, transfer the chickpeas to a paper towel lined plate.
Remove the baking sheet from the oven. Top the eggplant halves with tomato and fresh mozzarella slices.
Return the eggplant to the oven and bake until the cheese has melted, another 3 to 5 minutes.
Add the chickpeas to the bowl with the spices and toss to coat.
To serve, divide the eggplant melts and chickpeas between plates. Enjoy!

name: Eggplant, Tomato & Chickpea Stew with Couscous & Feta
ingredients: 12 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled feta cheese
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim and discard the ends of the eggplant; medium dice the eggplant (cut into ½-inch cubes) and transfer to a medium bowl.
Preheat a sauté pan over medium heat.
Peel and small dice the onion (cut into ¼-inch cubes).
Add olive oil to the pan and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add the onion to the pan; cook, stirring frequently, until softened, 3 to 5 minutes.
Peel and mince (or crush) the garlic.
Add broth to a small saucepan and bring to a boil.
Add the garlic to the pan; stir until fragrant, 15 to 30 seconds.

Add the eggplant, diced tomatoes, and broth to the pan; season with cumin, salt, pepper, and curry powder. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to medium-low; cook, stirring occasionally, until the eggplant is tender, 8 to 10 minutes.
Once the water is boiling, remove the saucepan from the heat. Add salt and couscous and stir. Cover the saucepan and let it sit for 10 minutes.
While the eggplant cooks, drain and rinse the chickpeas in a colander.
Place the feta in a small bowl.
Pick the basil leaves off the stems; discard the stems and chop almost all of the leaves (save a few for garnishing).
Stir the chickpeas and chopped basil into the pan; cook for another 2 to 3 minutes.
Uncover the couscous and fluff with a fork.
To serve, spoon the couscous onto a plate, top with the stew, and garnish with the feta and remaining basil leaves. Enjoy!

name: Eggs Baked in Tomatoes  with Cheese, Cilantro, and Jalapeno Pepper
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Preheat an oven safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Peel and small dice onion. Peel and mince garlic.
Quarter the jalapeño pepper lengthwise; remove and discard the stem, seeds, and membranes. Finely dice half of the jalapeno pepper. Slice the remaining jalapeno peppers and set aside.
Once the skillet is hot, add coconut oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add onion, garlic, and minced jalapeno. Stirring frequently, cook until vegetables are softened, 3-4 minutes.
Halve grape tomatoes and add to the skillet.
Drain and rinse the black beans in a colander; set aside to drain further.
Add tomato sauce, black beans, oregano, chili powder and salt to the skillet; stir to combine. Reduce heat to low and continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until reduced in volume, 6-8 minutes.
Grate mozzarella cheese.
Gently crack the eggs into the skillet. Top with cheese and sliced jalapeno peppers. Bake until the tops of the whites are set but the yolks are still runny, 8 to 10 minutes.
Using a knife, shave the cilantro leaves off the stems at a downward angle, working away from your body; discard the stems and finely chop the leaves.
To serve, divide between plates, and garnish with cilantro. Enjoy!

name: "Everything Spice" Baked Salmon Rice Bowl with Avocado & Tomatoes
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add water and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Cook rice until liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
While the rice is cooking, transfer tomatoes to a baking sheet pan. Drizzle with oil and season with salt. Stir to coat and spread out in an even layer.
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast, stirring halfway through, until tomatoes are just beginning to burst, about 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, place seeds and spices in a small bowl; stir to combine the "everything spice" mixture.

Pat the salmon dry with paper towels, season with salt, and place, skin-side down, on a plate. Spread the top-side with Dijon, then sprinkle evenly with the spice mixture, pressing gently to adhere. (Reserve bowl for later use.)
When the tomatoes are starting to burst, remove from the oven. Add salmon to the baking sheet, nestling the fillets into the tomatoes.
Return baking sheet to the oven and continue to roast until the tomatoes are browned and salmon is cooked through, 7-8 minutes more. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, zest and juice lemon into the reserved bowl.
Shave dill leaves off the stems; discard stems and roughly chop the leaves. Add to the bowl with the lemon along with oil, salt, and pepper. Stir to combine the dressing and set aside.
Halve and pit avocado. Halve lengthwise and slice thinly while still in the skin, then scoop out with a spoon.
To serve, divide rice between bowls. Top with salmon, roasted tomatoes, avocado, and capers, then drizzle with dressing. Enjoy!

name: "Everything Spice" Crusted Salmon with Avocado, Cucumber & Caper Salad
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F. Coat a baking sheet pan with a thin layer of oil and set aside.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Place seeds and spices in a small bowl; stir to combine the "everything spice" mixture.
Pat the salmon dry with paper towels and place, skin-side down, on the baking sheet. Spread with Dijon, then sprinkle evenly with the spice mixture, pressing gently to adhere.
Place fish in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and bake until cooked through, 8-10 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, place oil, vinegar, capers, and salt in a medium bowl; stir to combine the dressing.
Peel, halve, and thinly slice onion crosswise into half-moons. Add to the bowl with the dressing.
Trim and slice cucumber crosswise into thin rounds. Add to the bowl.
Halve and pit avocado; cut crosswise while still in the skin, then scoop out with a spoon into the bowl.
Shave dill leaves off the stems; discard stems and roughly chop the leaves. Add to the bowl and stir to combine the salad.
To serve, divide the salmon and salad between plates. Enjoy!

name: "Everything Spice" Fried Egg Bowl with Spinach, Smoked Salmon & Toast
instructions: Preheat a skillet over medium heat.
While the skillet heats up, peel and mince shallot.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add the shallot and cook, stirring often, until softened, about 2 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel and mince garlic.

Add garlic, seeds, salt, and pepper to the skillet with the shallot. Continue to cook, stirring often, until the shallot and garlic become golden, 2-3 minutes more. Transfer "everything spice" to a small bowl to keep the garlic from overcooking. (Reserve skillet for later use.)
Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)
Trim and slice cucumber into thin rounds; place on a plate.
Halve tomatoes and add to the plate with the cucumber.
Zest lemon into another small bowl. Slice lemon into wedges, add to the plate with the veggies, and set aside.

Using a knife, shave dill leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl with the lemon zest along with goat cheese and crushed red pepper; mash with the back of a spoon to combine and set aside.
Return skillet to medium-high heat.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Gently crack eggs into the skillet and cook until the tops of the whites are set but the yolks are still runny, about 4 minutes. Remove from heat.
Meanwhile, halve rolls and toast if desired; spread with lemon-dill goat cheese.
Chop or tear salmon into bite-sized pieces.
Divide spinach between bowls. Top with cucumber, tomatoes, lemon wedges, eggs, and smoked salmon; sprinkle with "everything spice." Serve with goat cheese rolls on the side and enjoy!

name: Fajita-Style Pork Bowl with Bell Peppers, Onions, Kale & Lime Sauce
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Place spices in a small bowl and stir to combine the spice mix; set aside.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim, halve, seed, and slice bell peppers into thin strips; transfer to a baking sheet pan.
Peel, halve, and slice onion lengthwise into ¼-inch thick strips; add to the baking sheet with the bell pepper.

Pat pork chops dry with paper towels and place on a cutting board; thinly slice crosswise into bite-sized strips. Add to the baking sheet, sprinkle with ⅔ of the spice mix, then drizzle with oil; toss to combine and spread out in an even layer. (Reserve remaining spice mix for later use.)
Place baking sheet in the oven and roast until veggies start to soften, about 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, using a clean cutting board, fold kale leaves in half lengthwise and slice off the stems. Chop or tear leaves into bite-sized pieces and place in a medium bowl.
Drain and rinse beans in a colander. Add beans to the bowl with the kale along with oil and salt; toss to combine.
When the veggies are soft, add kale and beans to the baking sheet; toss to combine, then return to the oven and continue to bake until kale is tender and pork is cooked through, 5-6 minutes more.
Meanwhile, zest and juice lime into the bowl with the remaining spice mix; add yogurt and water, then stir to combine the sauce.
To serve, divide pork, beans, and veggies between bowls; drizzle with sauce and enjoy!

name: Falafel-Inspired Salad with Crispy Chickpeas & Lemon Tahini Dressing
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Drain and rinse chickpeas. Place on a clean towel or paper towels and pat dry, then transfer to a large bowl.
Add oil, sesame seeds, and spices to the bowl with the chickpeas; stir to combine.

Transfer chickpeas to a baking sheet pan and spread out in an even layer. Place in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and bake, stirring halfway through, until slightly crispy, about 15 minutes. (Reserve bowl for the salad.)
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel, trim, and coarsely grate carrot; transfer to the reserved bowl.
Trim and medium dice cucumber. Medium dice tomato; add both to the bowl with the carrot.
Trim off and discard tops and root ends of radishes; thinly slice and add to the bowl.
Cut romaine crosswise into thin (shred-like) strips and add to the bowl.
Shave cilantro and parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add both to the bowl and toss to combine the salad. Set aside.
Peel and mince garlic; place in a small bowl.
Juice lemon into the bowl with the garlic. Add tahini, water, Dijon, sugar, and spices; whisk to combine the dressing.
To serve, divide salad between plates. Top with crispy chickpeas and drizzle with dressing. Enjoy!

name: Fettuccine Alfredo with Asparagus
ingredients: 4 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Fill a medium saucepan halfway with water, cover, and bring to a boil. Uncover, add salt and pasta, and stir for a few seconds. Cook until desired firmness, 9-10 minutes.
Wash asparagus and snap off woody ends. Cut diagonally into 2 inch pieces. Add to pasta during the last 2-3 minutes of cooking time.
Heat a sauté pan over medium heat.
Peel and mince garlic.
Add butter to pan and swirl to coat. Add garlic and cook until fragrant, 15-30 seconds.
Sprinkle flour into pan and whisk until combined with the butter.
Add broth and whisk until smooth. Then add milk and stir until sauce is thickened, 4-5 minutes.
Finely grate ¼ cup of Parmesan.
Add Parmesan, salt, and pepper to sauce. Stir until smooth, then reduce heat to low until pasta is ready.
Drain pasta and asparagus in a colander, reserving about ½ cup of the pasta water.
Add pasta, asparagus, and ½ of the reserved pasta water to sauce. Toss to combine. Add more pasta water to thin out the sauce if desired.
Place on a plate, garnish with freshly ground pepper, and enjoy!

name: Fettuccine with Tomatoes, Ricotta & Lemony Dressed Arugula
instructions: Fill a medium saucepan halfway with hot water (from the tap), cover, and bring to a boil. Uncover, add salt and pasta, and stir for a few seconds. Cook until desired firmness, 8-10 minutes. (Reserve a ½-cup of pasta cooking water before draining.)
Meanwhile, preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, peel and mince garlic.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add garlic and crushed red pepper; cook, stirring frequently, until fragrant and golden, about 1 minute.

Add tomatoes and salt to the skillet; cook, stirring occasionally, until simmering. Once simmering, reduce heat to medium-low, and continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened, 12-15 minutes more.
Meanwhile, finely grate Parmesan. Place in a small bowl along with ricotta and salt, then stir to combine. Set aside.
Wash, dry, zest, and juice lemon into a medium bowl.
Peel and mince shallot. Add to the bowl with the lemon along with oil, salt, and pepper. Whisk to combine the dressing.
Wash and dry arugula (skip this step if it came pre-washed). Add to the bowl with the dressing and toss to coat.
Add drained pasta and reserved pasta water to the skillet with the sauce. Continue to cook, stirring frequently, until heated through, 1-2 minutes more. Remove from heat.
To serve, divide pasta and arugula between plates or bowls. Top pasta with ricotta and crushed red pepper. Enjoy!

name: Filipino Beef Skillet (Giniling) with Potatoes, Peppers & Raisins
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, peel and small dice potatoes.
Once the skillet is hot, add potatoes and ground beef; cook, breaking the meat apart with a spoon, until browned and crumbly, 3-4 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel, trim, and small dice carrot; place in a small bowl.
Peel, halve, and small dice onion; peel and mince garlic. Add both to the bowl with the carrot.
When the beef is done, add veggies to the skillet; continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until starting to soften, 6-7 minutes more.
While the veggies are cooking, trim, seed, and small dice bell peppers.
When the veggies are starting to soften, add bell peppers to the skillet along with tomato sauce, raisins, soy sauce, and spices. Stir to combine, cover, and bring to a simmer.
Once simmering, reduce heat to medium and cook, stirring occasionally, until the veggies are tender and liquid is mostly absorbed, 8-10 minutes. Remove from heat.
To serve, divide skillet between plates or bowls and enjoy!

name: Fish Tacos with Avocado-Peach Salsa
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.

Quarter the peaches lengthwise (around the pit) and twist the quarters to separate, then remove and discard the pit; small dice the quarters into ¼-inch cubes. Transfer to a medium bowl (that will hold the salsa).
Halve the avocado lengthwise and twist the halves to separate, then remove the pit with a knife or spoon; scoop out and small dice the flesh into ¼-inch cubes. Add to the salsa bowl.
Quarter the jalapeño pepper lengthwise; remove and discard the stem, seeds, and membranes. Finely dice the pepper and add to the salsa bowl.
Using a knife, shave the cilantro leaves off the stems at a downward angle, working away from your body; discard the stems and finely chop the leaves. Add to the salsa bowl.
Trim off and discard the ends of the shallot; peel and finely dice the shallot. Add to the salsa bowl.
Add olive oil to a nonstick skillet and preheat over medium heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the fish dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with chili powder, salt, and pepper on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add the fish; cook until it is cooked through and flakes easily, 2 to 4 minutes per side. Once done, transfer to a plate.
Juice the lime and add to the salsa bowl.
Season the salsa with salt and pepper; toss to combine.
Wrap the tortillas in damp paper towels and microwave until heated through, 15 to 30 seconds.
Using a fork or your hands, flake the fish.
To serve, divide the fish between the tortillas and top with the avocado-peach salsa. Enjoy!

name: Fish Tacos with Guacamole & Napa Cabbage Slaw
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Cut out and discard the core from the cabbage; halve the cabbage lengthwise, then thinly slice crosswise and transfer to a large bowl.
Small dice the tomato and add to the cabbage.
Halve and pit the avocado; cube the flesh while still in the skin. Scoop out the flesh into a small bowl.
Shave the cilantro leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves. Add ½ of the cilantro to the cabbage and the other ½ to the avocado.
Juice the lime into a small bowl; add ½ to the cabbage and the other ½ to the avocado.
Preheat a grill pan or skillet over medium heat.
Place the fish on a plate, drizzle with olive oil, and season with chili powder, salt, and pepper.
Place the fish in the grill pan or skillet; cook until opaque and golden brown, 2 to 3 minutes per side. Once done, transfer to a plate.
Season the avocado with salt and pepper; mash with a fork until smooth.
Season the cabbage mixture with salt and pepper; toss until well combined.
Place the tortillas on a plate and cover with a damp paper towel. Microwave for 30 to 60 seconds until they are warmed through. (This step is optional.)
Using your hands or a fork, flake the fish.
Divide the cabbage slaw among the tortillas (leaving any extra on the side), then add the fish, and spoon dollops of the guacamole on top. Enjoy!

name: Fish Tacos with Mango-Jalapeño Salsa & Lime Crema
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.

Peel the mangoes, then slice off the flesh from the pit, starting with the flatter sides; discard the pit and small dice the flesh (cut into ¼-inch cubes). Transfer to a medium bowl (that will hold the salsa).
Quarter the jalapeño pepper lengthwise; remove and discard the stem, seeds, and membranes. Finely dice the pepper and add to the salsa bowl.
Trim off and discard the ends of the onion and remove the outer layer; small dice the onion (cut into ¼-inch pieces) and add to the salsa bowl.
Add olive oil to a nonstick skillet and preheat over medium heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the sole fillets dry with paper towels and place on a plate. Season with chili powder, cumin, salt, and pepper on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add the fish fillets and cook until opaque throughout, 2 to 3 minutes per side. Once done, transfer to a plate. Cook in batches if necessary.
While the fish cooks, using a knife, shave the cilantro leaves off the stems at a downward angle, working away from your body; discard the stems and finely chop the leaves. Add to the salsa.
Juice the lime; add ½ of the juice to the salsa and the other ½ to a small bowl.
Season the salsa with salt and pepper; toss to combine.
Add yogurt to the bowl of lime juice and stir to combine.
Place the tortillas on a small plate and cover with a damp paper towel; microwave until heated through, 15 to 30 seconds.
Flake the fish with a fork.
To serve, divide the fish among the tortillas, top with the salsa, and drizzle with the crema. Enjoy!

name: Fish Tacos with Strawberry-Avocado Salsa
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim off and discard the stem ends of the strawberries; small dice the strawberries. Transfer to a medium bowl (that will hold the salsa).
Halve the avocado lengthwise and twist the halves to separate, then remove the pit with a knife or spoon; scoop out and small dice the flesh. Add to the salsa bowl.
Quarter the jalapeño pepper lengthwise; remove and discard the stem, seeds, and membranes. Finely dice the pepper and add to the salsa bowl.
Using a knife, shave the cilantro leaves off the stems at a downward angle, working away from your body; discard the stems and finely chop the leaves. Add to the salsa bowl.
Trim off and discard the ends of the shallot; peel and finely dice the shallot. Add to the salsa bowl.
Preheat a grill pan or regular skillet over medium-high heat.
While the grill pan / skillet heats up, pat the fish dry with paper towels and place on a plate. Rub with olive oil and season with chili powder, salt, and pepper on both sides.
Once the grill pan / skillet is hot, add the fish; cook until it is cooked through and flakes easily, 2 to 4 minutes per side. Once done, transfer to a plate.
Juice half of the lime and add to the salsa bowl; cut the remaining half into wedges for serving.
Season the salsa with salt and pepper; toss to combine.
Wrap the tortillas in damp paper towels and microwave until heated through, 15 to 30 seconds.
Using a fork or your hands, flake the fish.
To serve, divide the fish between the tortillas and top with the strawberry-avocado salsa; serve with lime wedges on the side. Enjoy!

name: Flank Steak with Italian-Style Spicy Fennel, Orange & Olive Salad
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Mince anchovy fillets. Place in a medium bowl along with oil, vinegar, and spices; whisk to combine the dressing.

Place steak on a plate, season with salt and pepper on both sides, then drizzle with half of the dressing. Turn to coat and set aside to marinate, 15 minutes. (Reserve remaining dressing for the next step.)
While the steak is marinating, peel, halve, and slice onion crosswise into thin half-moons. Add to the bowl with the remaining dressing.
Halve olives lengthwise and add to the bowl.
Cut off skin and white pith from orange; slice between the membranes to release segments. Add to the bowl and set aside.
When the steak is done marinating, preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add steak and cook until desired doneness, 2-4 minutes per side. Transfer to a clean plate and set aside to rest, about 5 minutes.

Meanwhile, trim off root end and stalks of the fennel, leaving only the white bulbs. Halve fennel bulbs lengthwise, then slice crosswise into thin half-moons. Add to the bowl with the olives and orange segments.
Pick parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems. Add leaves to the bowl and gently stir to combine the salad.
Thinly slice steak against the grain.
To serve, divide steak and salad between plates or bowls. Enjoy!

name: Flank Steak Street Tacos with Cilantro & Spicy Cabbage-Jalapeño Slaw
instructions: Place soy sauce, oil, and spices in a medium bowl. Stir to combine the marinade.

Pat steak dry with paper towels and place on a cutting board. Slice crosswise into thin strips, then cut each strip into bite-sized pieces. Add to the bowl with the marinade, stir to coat, and set aside for 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Using a clean cutting board, shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Place half in another medium bowl. (Reserve remaining cilantro for serving.)
Juice lime into the bowl with the cilantro. Add oil and salt, then whisk to combine the dressing.

Halve jalapeño pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon to reduce spice level. Slice crosswise into thin half-moons and add to the bowl with the dressing. (Be careful with jalapeños; do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Trim off and discard root end of cabbage; halve lengthwise, then slice crosswise into thin (shred-like) strips. Add to the bowl and toss to combine the slaw; set aside
When the steak is done marinating, preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.

Once the skillet is hot, add steak and cook, undisturbed, until browned, 2-3 minutes. Turn and continue to cook until desired doneness, 1-2 minutes more. Transfer to a plate and set aside to rest, about 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel, halve, and mince onion. Set aside for serving.
Warm tortillas in another skillet, oven, or microwave (optional).
To serve, divide tortillas and slaw between plates. Top tortillas with steak, hot sauce, onion, and reserved cilantro. Enjoy!

name: Fresh Corn, Peach, Avocado & Goat Cheese Salad with Garlic Breadsticks
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Peel and mince garlic; place in a small bowl along with oil and spices. Stir to combine the garlic oil.

Drizzle garlic oil over the flatbread, cut into 1½-inch wide strips, and transfer to a baking sheet pan. Place in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and bake until crispy, 8-10 minutes. Remove from the oven.
Meanwhile, place oil, vinegar, honey, salt, and pepper in a medium bowl; whisk to combine the dressing.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Remove husks and silks from the corn. Using a knife, carefully slice corn kernels off the cobs; add to the bowl with the dressing.
Quarter peach lengthwise (around the pit); twist to separate and remove pit. Medium dice and add to the bowl.
Halve and pit avocado; scoop out with a spoon and medium dice the flesh. Add to the bowl.
Peel and small dice onion. Add to the bowl.
Shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl.
Pick basil leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and thinly slice into ribbons. Add to the bowl.
Crumble goat cheese into the bowl and gently stir to combine the salad.
To serve, divide salad and breadsticks between plates or bowls. Enjoy!

name: Fresh Corn "Polenta" with Fried Eggs & Goat Cheese-Arugula Salad
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the arugula if it came pre-washed.)
Remove husks and silks from corn. Using your hands, snap each ear in half. Working over a large bowl, coarsely grate corn off of the cob, catching all of the kernels and corn juices in the bowl.
Preheat a medium saucepan over medium heat.

Once the saucepan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add corn and its juices to the saucepan, along with cream, salt, and pepper. Cook, stirring frequently, until the corn is cooked and most of the liquid has evaporated, 3-4 minutes. Reserve bowl for later use.
Meanwhile, finely grate Parmesan. Add to the saucepan with the corn and stir to combine the polenta. Cover and remove from heat.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, place oil, vinegar, salt, and pepper in the reserved bowl. Whisk to combine the dressing.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Gently crack eggs into the skillet and season with salt and pepper. Cook until the tops of the whites are set but the yolks are still runny, about 4 minutes.
Meanwhile, trim green onions; cut crosswise into ¼-inch pieces at an angle. Add to the bowl with the dressing.
Halve tomatoes. Add to the bowl along with the arugula and toss to combine the salad.
Crumble goat cheese.
To serve, divide polenta, eggs, and salad between plates. Top the salad with goat cheese and enjoy!

name: Fresh Creamed Corn Fettuccine with Lettuce, Cucumber & Tomato Salad
ingredients: 4 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
½ (5 oz) pkg spring mix (mixed greens)
instructions: Fill a medium saucepan halfway with hot water (from the tap); cover and bring to a boil over high heat. Uncover, add salt and pasta, and stir for a few seconds. Cook until desired firmness, 8-10 minutes. Reserve ½-cup cooking water before draining; set aside.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the mixed greens if they came pre-washed.)
Remove husks and silks from the corn. Using a knife, carefully slice corn kernels off the cobs and place in a medium bowl.
Peel and mince garlic; peel and small dice half the onion (reserving the rest for later use). Add both to the bowl with the corn.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add corn, garlic, onion, broth, and salt; cook, stirring occasionally, until corn starts to soften and break down, 8-10 minutes. (Reserve bowl for the next step.)
Meanwhile, place oil, vinegar, and spices in the reserved bowl; whisk to combine the dressing.
Thinly slice remaining onion. Trim and halve cucumber lengthwise; slice crosswise into thin half-moons. Add both to the bowl with the dressing.
Halve tomatoes and add to the bowl; set aside.
Cut cream cheese into small pieces. Finely grate Parmesan.
When the corn is ready, add cream cheese and Parmesan to the skillet. Bring to a simmer and cook, stirring often, until cheese melts and the sauce thickens slightly, 2-3 minutes.
Transfer pasta to the skillet and toss to combine; add reserved pasta water, a few tablespoons at a time, if necessary, to reach a saucy consistency. Remove from heat.
Add mixed greens to the bowl with the veggies and toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide pasta and salad between plates. Enjoy!

name: Fried Cauliflower Rice with Bacon, Spinach, Mushrooms & Eggs
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, small dice bacon.

Once the skillet is hot, add bacon and cook, stirring occasionally, until crispy, 4-5 minutes. Using a slotted spoon, remove crispy bacon to a paper towel-lined plate; set aside. (Reserve skillet with drippings for later use.)

Using a clean cutting board, cut the cauliflower head into quarters, then trim off and discard the leaves and thick stem. Using a box grater or food processor, coarsely grate the cauliflower and place in a medium bowl; set aside.
Thinly slice mushrooms.
Return skillet (with drippings) to medium-high heat. Add mushrooms and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, trim and cut green onions crosswise into thin pieces. Add half to the bowl with the cauliflower and set the other half aside for garnish.
When the mushrooms are soft, add cauliflower, green onion, and oil to the skillet. Cook, stirring occasionally, until cauliflower is soft and beginning to brown, about 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel and mince ginger and garlic. Place both in a small bowl along with soy sauce and maple syrup; whisk to combine the sauce.

When the cauliflower is done, add spinach to the skillet in handfuls, waiting for the spinach to wilt slightly before adding the next handful. Add sauce, stir to combine, and continue to cook until heated through, about 30 seconds. Remove from heat and cover to keep warm.
Preheat another skillet over medium-high heat.

Once the skillet is hot, add additional oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Gently crack eggs into the skillet and cook until the tops of the whites are set but the yolks are still runny, about 4 minutes. Remove from heat and season with salt.
To serve, divide cauliflower rice and eggs between plates. Garnish rice with crispy bacon, reserved green onion, and sesame seeds. Enjoy!

name: Fried Egg Rice Bowl with Pickled Carrot & Ginger-Green Onion Sauce
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add water and salt, then bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Cook rice until liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim green onions and cut crosswise into thin pieces; place in a small bowl.
Peel and mince ginger; add to the bowl with the green onion along with oil, vinegar, soy sauce, and chili-garlic sauce. Stir to combine the sauce and set aside.
Place additional vinegar, water, sugar, and salt in another small bowl; stir to combine the pickling liquid.
Peel, trim, and coarsely grate carrots; add to the bowl with the pickling liquid, stir to combine, and set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Gently crack eggs into the skillet and cook until the tops of the whites are set but the yolks are still runny, about 4 minutes. Remove from heat.
Meanwhile, trim and thinly slice cucumber crosswise into rounds.
Halve and pit avocado; scoop out with a spoon and small dice the flesh.
To serve, divide the rice, eggs, pickled carrots, cucumber, and avocado between bowls. Top with ginger-green onion sauce and enjoy!

name: Garlic-Avocado Toast with Marinated Mozzarella, Basil & Side Salad
ingredients: ½ (6 oz) jar artichoke hearts, marinated
½ (8 oz) pkg fresh mozzarella cheese
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Mince the sun-dried tomatoes and place in a small bowl. Add oil and spices; stir to combine the marinade.
Cut mozzarella into ½-inch cubes and add to the bowl with the marinade; gently toss to coat the cheese and set aside.
Preheat oven to broil on high and position rack in the upper third of the oven.
Peel and mince garlic; place in a medium bowl along with oil, vinegar, honey, salt, and pepper. Whisk to combine the dressing.
Trim, seed, and mince bell pepper; add to the bowl with the dressing.
Mince artichokes and add to the bowl.
Chop or tear lettuce leaves into bite-sized pieces and add to the bowl. Toss to combine the salad and set aside.
Peel and mince additional garlic; place in another small bowl along with oil, salt, and pepper. Stir to combine the garlic oil.
Slice buns in half and place, cut-side up, on a baking sheet pan. Drizzle with garlic oil.
Place buns in the oven and toast until golden, 1-2 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, pick basil leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and thinly slice into ribbons. Set aside.
Halve and pit the avocado; slice thinly while still in skin, then scoop out with a spoon. Arrange avocado slices on top of the garlic toast.
To serve, divide garlic-avocado toast and salad between plates; spoon marinated mozzarella over the toasts and garnish with basil. Enjoy!

name: Garlic-Dijon Ribeye with Warm Zucchini, Tomato, Mint & Feta Salad
ingredients: ½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled feta cheese
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.

Trim zucchini, quarter lengthwise, then slice crosswise into 2-inch long pieces; transfer to a baking sheet pan. Drizzle with oil, season with salt and pepper, and toss to coat; spread out in an even layer.
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast, tossing halfway through, until zucchini is fork-tender, 20-25 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, peel and mince garlic; place in a small bowl along with oil, vinegar, Dijon, salt, and pepper. Whisk to combine the marinade.
Cut steak into portions, place on a plate, and drizzle with marinade on both sides; turn to coat and set aside.
While the steaks are marinating, zest and juice lemon into a medium bowl. Add oil, salt, and pepper; whisk to combine the dressing.
Using a clean cutting board, peel and mince additional garlic; peel and mince shallot. Add both to the bowl with the dressing.
Slice tomato lengthwise into wedges; add to the bowl, stir to coat, and set aside.
Preheat a grill pan, outdoor grill, or regular skillet over medium-high heat.
Once the grill pan is hot, add steaks and cook until desired doneness, 2-5 minutes per side. Remove to a clean plate.
While the steaks are cooking, pick mint leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves.
When the zucchini is done, add to the bowl with the dressing and tomatoes. Add mint and toss to combine the warm salad.
To serve, divide steak and salad between plates; sprinkle feta over salad and enjoy!

name: Garlic Dill Yogurt with Arugula & Fried Eggs
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the arugula if it came pre-washed.)
Preheat a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat.
Coarsely chop walnuts. Toast walnuts until fragrant (2-4 minutes). Stir in red pepper flakes and butter until melted. Set walnuts aside in a bowl and return skillet to the heat.
Add coconut oil to the skillet and swirl to coat the bottom.
Gently crack the eggs into the skillet. Cook until the tops of the whites are set but the yolks are still runny, 3 to 4 minutes. Once done, separate the eggs. Cook in batches if necessary.
Trim off the root ends of the garlic; peel and mince or press the garlic. Transfer to a medium bowl.
Shave the dill leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves. Add to the medium bowl with the garlic.
Add plain yogurt, olive oil, salt and pepper to the medium bowl and stir until smooth and well combined.
In a medium bowl, toss arugula with remaining olive oil and salt.
Toast flatbread if desired.
To serve, divide yogurt, flat bread, arugula, and eggs between plates. Top with walnuts and enjoy!

name: Garlic & Lemon Seared Steak Bites with Zucchini Noodles
ingredients: 4 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
¾ lb striploin (New York strip) steak
instructions: Wash and dry lemon; zest and juice into a medium bowl.
Peel and mince garlic; add to the bowl with the lemon.
Add broth, soy sauce, and spices to the bowl; whisk to combine the sauce and set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the steak dry with paper towels, then cut into 1-inch cubes.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add steak and cook, stirring occasionally, until desired doneness, 3-4 minutes for medium. Transfer to a plate and set aside.
Meanwhile, wash zucchini, trim ends, and use a julienne (or regular) peeler to make noodles. Use a paper towel or a clean cloth to squeeze excess moisture out of the zucchini noodles.
Add sauce to the skillet and whisk. Cook, stirring frequently, until the mixture is reduced by about half, 3-4 minutes.

Stir in butter and, once melted, add zucchini noodles. Cook, stirring constantly, until just tender, 2-3 minutes. Use tongs to remove from skillet and portion onto plates, leaving the excess sauce in the pan.
Return steak to the skillet and toss to coat in the sauce.
To serve, transfer steak to plates with the noodles and top with any remaining sauce. Enjoy!

name: Garlic Paprika Chicken Drumsticks with Avocado, Tomato & Greens Salad
ingredients: ½ (5 oz) pkg spring mix (mixed greens)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 500°F. Line a baking dish with foil.
Peel and mince or press the garlic; transfer to a medium bowl.
Add lime juice, olive oil, paprika, salt, and pepper to the minced garlic and mix well.
Add the chicken drumsticks to the garlic-paprika mixture and toss until well coated. Place the drumsticks in the baking dish.
Place the drumsticks in the oven and bake, flipping halfway through cooking time, until they are cooked through and browned, 25-30 minutes.
In a small bowl, prepare the dressing by whisking together lime juice, olive oil, Dijon, salt, and pepper.
Wash and dry the mixed greens.
Wash and halve the tomatoes.
Halve and pit the avocado; scoop out the flesh and medium dice.
To serve, arrange the greens on plates, top with tomatoes and avocado, and drizzle with the dressing. Add chicken drumsticks to the side. Enjoy!

name: Garlic Parmesan Chicken Wings with Spicy Roasted Carrot
ingredients: 1 lb chicken wings, split with tips removed
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
In a medium bowl, mix together oregano, thyme, cumin, and salt. Add chicken wings and toss to coat.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Coat bottom of skillet with oil. Add chicken wings and brown on both sides, 2-3 minutes per side. Reduce heat to medium-low and cook, occasionally flipping, until cooked through, 10-12 minutes.
Wash and dry carrots; trim ends and thinly slice, using a mandoline or knife, into rounds.
Brush a sheet pan with oil to prevent sticking. Transfer carrots to sheet. Drizzle with oil and season with salt and pepper; toss to coat.
Spread out in a single layer and place in the oven. Bake until crispy, 10-12 minutes. Watch carefully because they can burn quickly.

Wash and dry parsley. Shave leaves off the stems, discard the stems and mince the leaves. Peel and mince garlic. Grate ⅛ cup of Parmesan. In a medium bowl, mix together parsley, garlic, Parmesan, and salt.
Add chicken wings to bowl and toss to coat.
To serve, place chicken wings and carrots on a plate. Enjoy!

name: Garlic-Parmesan Pork Chops with Spinach, Mushrooms & Zucchini Noodles
ingredients: 4 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)
Trim zucchini and use a julienne (or regular) peeler to make noodles. Place in a small bowl and set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat pork chops dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with salt and pepper on both sides.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add chops and pan-fry until golden brown and cooked through, 3-4 minutes per side. Transfer chops to a clean plate and loosely cover with aluminum foil. (Reserve skillet for later use.)
Meanwhile, thinly slice mushrooms.
Peel and mince garlic.
Return skillet to medium heat and add more oil. Add mushrooms and garlic to the skillet and cook, stirring occasionally, until mushrooms begin to soften, 4-5 minutes.
While the mushrooms are cooking, cut cream cheese into small pieces.
Finely grate Parmesan.

Add cream cheese, Parmesan, broth, and spices to the skillet; stir until cheese is melted and combined. Bring to a simmer and continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens, 3-4 minutes.
Add spinach and zucchini noodles to the skillet in handfuls, waiting for them to wilt slightly before adding the next handful.
Return pork chops to the skillet and turn to coat in sauce.
To serve, divide saucy veggies and pork chops between plates. Enjoy!

name: Garlic-Rosemary Chicken Drumsticks with Sautéed Brussels Sprouts
ingredients: 4 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Preheat the oven to 450°F and position the rack in the center. Place a baking dish (one that is big enough to hold the chicken) inside the oven to warm up.
Trim off and discard the stem ends of the Brussels sprouts, then remove the outer layer of leaves; halve the sprouts lengthwise (or quarter if they are large).
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat dry the chicken with paper towels and place on a plate, then generously season with salt and pepper.
Add coconut oil to the skillet and swirl to coat the bottom.

Place the drumsticks in the skillet; cook, turning every 1 minute or so, until the they are browned on all sides (but not cooked through). Once done, remove the baking dish from the oven and transfer the chicken to it.
While the chicken cooks, one by one, holding a sprig of rosemary at its top, run you fingers down it to remove the leaves. Discard the sprigs and chop the leaves.
Trim off and discard the root end of the garlic; peel and mince or press the garlic.
Juice the lemon into a small bowl.

Once the chicken has been transferred, return the skillet to the stove and reduce the heat to medium. Add the rosemary, garlic, ½ of the lemon juice, and ½ of the broth to the skillet. Deglaze the skillet by scraping up browned bits from the bottom.
Pour the skillet sauce over top of the chicken. Place the chicken in the oven and bake until it is cooked through, about 10 minutes.
Add more coconut oil to the skillet.
Add the Brussels sprouts to the skillet and cook until they are lightly browned, 2 to 3 minutes.
Once the sprouts are browned, add the remaining broth and season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the sprouts are tender and the liquid has evaporated, 3 to 4 minutes.
To serve, place the chicken and Brussels sprouts on a plate. Enjoy!

name: Garlic-Rosemary Lamb Chops with Roasted Asparagus & Mushrooms
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and mince garlic; transfer to a small bowl.
Slide rosemary leaves off the sprigs; discard sprigs and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl with the garlic, along with oil, salt, and pepper; stir to combine.
Pat lamb chops dry with paper towels, place on a plate, and coat both sides with half the garlic-rosemary oil; set aside.
Snap or cut off the woody ends of the asparagus. Transfer spears to a baking sheet pan.
Remove stems and slice mushrooms into ¼-inch pieces; add to the baking sheet with the asparagus.
Drizzle remaining garlic-rosemary oil over the veggies, toss to coat, and place in the oven. Bake, tossing once, until fork-tender, 10-12 minutes.
Meanwhile, preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add chops and cook, flipping once, until desired doneness, 4-5 minutes for medium-rare. Transfer to a clean plate and cover loosely with foil.
To serve, divide veggies and lamb chops between plates. Enjoy!

name: Garlic & Sage Chicken Thighs with Maple Roasted Acorn Squash
instructions: Preheat oven to 500°F and position rack in the centre.
Peel and mince garlic. In a medium bowl, mix together the minced garlic, olive oil, sage, salt, and pepper.
Wash and thinly slice lemon.
Add chicken and lemon slices to bowl; toss to coat. Set aside.
Heat a saucepan over medium heat. Add butter, maple syrup, chill powder, salt, and pepper. Simmer for 2-3 minutes while you prepare the squash.
Wash and halve squash lengthwise. Scoop out the seeds and cut crosswise into ¼ inch thick slices.
Lightly coat a baking sheet with olive oil.
Add squash slices to baking sheet and pour butter-maple mixture over top. Toss to coat and arrange slices in a single layer.
Place chicken and lemon slices on top of squash. Place in the oven and roast until squash is tender and chicken is cooked though, 12-15 minutes.
Serve chicken thighs with squash on the side. Enjoy!

name: Garlicky Bean, Swiss Chard, Bell Pepper & Almond Sauté with Eggs
instructions: Preheat a skillet over medium heat.
While the skillet heats up, wash, dry, trim, and seed bell peppers; slice lengthwise into thin strips.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add peppers and salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, until tender and starting to brown, about 10 minutes.

While the peppers are cooking, fill a medium saucepan about halfway with hot water (from the tap); add vinegar, cover with a lid, and bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Once the water in the pan is boiling, reduce heat to medium-low.

Meanwhile, wash and dry chard; fold leaves in half lengthwise and slice off the stems. Cut leaves crosswise into thin (shred-like) strips and thinly slice the stems, keeping them separate. Place leaves in a medium bowl and stems in a small bowl.
Peel and thinly slice garlic. Add to the bowl with the stems and set aside.
Drain and rinse beans; set aside to drain further.
When the peppers are tender, add chard stems, garlic, smoked paprika, and salt to the skillet. Cook, stirring occasionally, until garlic is fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Add beans to the skillet and continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until warmed through, about 30 seconds.
Add chard leaves to the skillet in handfuls, waiting for the leaves to wilt slightly before adding the next handful. Add vinegar and stir to combine. Remove from heat and set aside.
Gently crack eggs into two additional small bowls (two eggs per bowl).

Adjust the heat of the saucepan as necessary so that the water is simmering. Gently tip bowls into the pan, sliding the eggs carefully into the water. Cook until whites are set but yolks are still soft, 2½-3 minutes. Using the slotted spoon, transfer eggs to a plate, then season with salt and pepper.
Meanwhile, roughly chop almonds.
To serve, divide veggies between plates or bowls; top with almonds and poached eggs. Enjoy!

name: Garlicky Shrimp Scampi with Bell Pepper & Spaghetti
ingredients: 4 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
¾ lb raw peeled shrimp, fresh or frozen
instructions: Fill a medium saucepan halfway with water, cover, and bring to a boil. Uncover, add salt and pasta, and stir for a few seconds. Cook until desired firmness, 8-10 minutes.
If using frozen shrimp, place in a medium bowl, cover with cold water, and set aside to thaw. If using fresh shrimp, skip this step.
Wash and dry bell peppers and parsley.
Seed and cut bell peppers into small strips. Shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Peel and mince garlic.
Drain shrimp in a colander and rinse under cold water until there are no more ice chunks. Spread out on a clean towel and pat dry.
Add butter to skillet and let it melt. Add shrimp and cook, stirring frequently, until opaque and pink, 2-3 minutes. Transfer to a plate.
Reduce heat to medium and add more butter to skillet. Then add garlic, bell peppers, and crushed red pepper. Cook, stirring frequently, until peppers are tender-crisp, 2-3 minutes.
Add broth to skillet and cook until it reduces, 1-2 minutes.
Finely grate ⅛ cup of Parmesan.
Drain pasta in a colander.
Add pasta, shrimp, parsley, and Parmesan to skillet. Pour in remaining broth and drizzle with lemon juice. Season with salt and pepper and toss until well combined.
Serve pasta on a plate or in a bowl and enjoy!

name: Garlicky Spaghetti Parmesan Carbonara
ingredients: ¾ fl oz heavy whipping cream
instructions: Fill a large pot halfway with water, season water with salt, cover and bring to a boil. Add pasta and stir for a few seconds. Cook, uncovered, until desired firmness, 8-10 minutes.
While pasta is cooking, preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Chop the bacon into 1-inch pieces; add to the skillet and cook until crispy, 4-5 minutes. Once done, transfer to a plate lined with paper towels. Reserve 1 tbsp of bacon fat.
Meanwhile, crack the eggs into a medium bowl; add 1 ½ tbsp cream and whisk to combine.
Finely grate Parmesan and transfer to the bowl with egg mixture. Season with salt and pepper; whisk to combine.
When pasta is done, drain in a colander, reserving ½ cup of cooking liquid.
Trim off and discard the root ends of the garlic; peel and mince or press the garlic.
Add the reserved bacon fat to empty pasta pot. Return pot to heat, reduce heat to low. Add garlic, stirring until fragrant, about 1-2 minutes.
Return pasta and bacon to pot. Remove pot from heat, add the egg mixture to pasta, stirring frequently. Stir just until the egg mixture begins to thicken, 3-4 minutes.
If the sauce seems dry, add some of the reserved pasta water 1 tbsp at a time, until rich and creamy.
Wash and dry parsley. Shave leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves. Reserve a small amount for garnish and add the rest to the pot with the pasta.
To serve, divide pasta between bowls and garnish with remaining parsley. Enjoy!

name: Gazpacho (Chilled Veggie Soup) with Lemon-Parsley Shrimp Salad Toasts
ingredients: 4 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
¾ lb raw peeled shrimp, fresh or frozen
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.

If using frozen shrimp, place them in a colander and run under cold water to thaw them slightly and remove any ice crystals. (If using fresh shrimp, skip this step.) Place the shrimp on a clean towel or paper towels and pat dry. Set aside.
Medium dice bread and transfer to a medium bowl.
Peel, trim, and large dice cucumber; add to the bowl with the bread.
Trim, seed, and large dice bell pepper. Large dice tomatoes; add both to the bowl.
Peel and roughly chop garlic; add to the bowl along with broth, oil, vinegar, and spices; stir to combine the soup mixture.

Working in batches, transfer the soup mixture to a blender; blend on high until semi-smooth. Once blended, transfer gazpacho to a container with a lid and refrigerate until ready to serve. (Reserve bowl for later use.)
Preheat oven to broil on high and position rack about 6-inches from the top.

Transfer shrimp to a baking sheet pan lined with aluminum foil; drizzle with oil and season with salt and pepper. Place baking sheet in the oven and broil, flipping once, until shrimp are opaque and cooked through, 3-4 minutes. Remove from oven.
While the shrimp are cooking, mince capers. Place in the reserved bowl along with mayo and crushed red pepper.
Juice lemon into the bowl with the capers and stir to combine.
Shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl (reserving a small handful for serving).

Carefully remove cooked shrimp from the baking sheet by lifting the corners of the foil and transferring the foil sheet to a flat surface. Arrange additional bread slices on the baking sheet, place in the oven, and broil until toasted, 1-2 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, roughly chop the cooked shrimp; add to the bowl with the lemon-mayo mixture and stir to combine. Divide shrimp salad between toast slices and spread out in an even layer.
Divide gazpacho between bowls; drizzle with additional oil and sprinkle with reserved parsley. Serve with shrimp salad toasts on the side and enjoy!

name: "General Tso's" Tempeh with Green Onion, Bok Choy, Sesame Seeds & Rice
ingredients: 12 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add broth and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Cook rice until liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
While the rice is cooking, trim and cut green onions crosswise into thin pieces. Place ⅔ in a small bowl. (Reserve remaining green onions for serving.)
Peel and mince ginger. Add to the bowl with the green onions along with broth, cornstarch, soy sauce, maple syrup, and ketchup. Stir to combine the stir-fry sauce and set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, slice tempeh crosswise into ½-inch thick strips. Season with salt.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add tempeh in a single layer and cook, flipping once, until browned and warmed through, 4-5 minutes. Transfer to a plate. (Reserve skillet for later use.)
Meanwhile, trim and cut bok choy crosswise into bite-sized pieces.
Return the skillet to medium heat, add more oil, and swirl to coat the bottom. Add bok choy and salt, then stir-fry until softened, 3-4 minutes.

Add stir-fry sauce to the skillet. Bring to a boil and continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens, 2-3 minutes more. Remove from heat, add tempeh, and stir to combine; cover to keep warm.
To serve, divide rice and stir-fry between plates or bowls. Top with reserved green onions and sesame seeds. Enjoy!

name: Ginger Chicken Meatball Stir-Fry with Noodles, Snap Peas & Cashews
instructions: Fill a medium saucepan about halfway with hot water (from the tap); cover and bring to a boil over high heat.
Once the water in the pan is boiling, remove from heat and add rice noodles. Soak for 10 minutes, or according to package directions, then drain in a colander and rinse under cold water; set aside.
Meanwhile, place soy sauce, fish sauce, water, honey, and spices in a small bowl; whisk to combine the sauce and set aside.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and mince ginger; place in a medium bowl along with chicken, additional soy sauce, and pepper. Using your hands, mix well to combine.
Using a tablespoon measure, form the chicken mixture into rounded meatballs and place on a plate.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom; add meatballs and cook, turning occasionally, until golden brown and cooked through, 6-8 minutes. Transfer to a clean plate and loosely cover with aluminum foil. (Reserve skillet with cooking juices for later use.)
Meanwhile, peel, trim, and slice carrot crosswise into thin rounds; halve snap peas crosswise. Place both in another small bowl.
Trim and slice green onions crosswise into ¼-inch pieces; add to the bowl with the other veggies.
Return skillet to medium-high heat, add more oil, and swirl to coat the bottom. Add veggies and stir-fry until fork-tender, 3-4 minutes.
While the veggies are cooking, shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves.
When the veggies are done, add noodles, sauce, and cilantro to the skillet; cook, stirring frequently, until the noodles are coated and warmed through, 2-3 minutes.
Meanwhile, roughly chop cashews.
To serve, divide noodles, veggies, and meatballs between bowls; top with cashews and enjoy!

name: Ginger-Lime Chicken Skewers with Grape, Grapefruit & Avocado Salad
instructions: If using wooden skewers, place 4-6 skewers in a shallow dish of water to soak until you are ready to use them.
Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the mixed greens if they came pre-washed.)
Zest lime into a medium bowl (set lime aside for later use).
Peel and mince shallot; place half in the bowl with the lime zest (set remaining shallot aside).
Peel and grate or mince ginger. Add to the bowl with the lime zest along with mayo, salt, and pepper; stir to combine the marinade.
Pat the chicken dry with paper towels and cut into bite-sized pieces; transfer to the bowl with the marinade, stir to coat, and set aside.
Meanwhile, juice lime into another medium bowl. Add remaining shallot, oil, fish sauce, sugar, and Dijon; whisk to combine the dressing and set aside.
Preheat a grill pan, outdoor grill, or regular skillet over medium-high heat.
While the grill pan heats up, thread chicken onto skewers and place on a plate; alternatively, you can cook the chicken pieces directly on the grill pan without using skewers.
Once the grill pan is hot, add the skewers and cook, turning occasionally, until chicken is cooked through, 8-10 minutes. Remove to a clean plate.
While the chicken is cooking, using a clean cutting board, halve grapes and add to the bowl with the dressing.
Cut off skin and white pith from the grapefruit. Slice between the membranes to release segments; cut into bite-sized pieces and add to the bowl.
Halve and pit the avocado; slice crosswise while still in the skin and scoop out with a spoon. Add to the bowl along with the mixed greens and toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide salad and skewers between plates or bowls. Enjoy!

name: Ginger-Lime Salmon Cake Lettuce Wraps with Spicy Mayo
ingredients: 1 (7.5 oz) can wild pink salmon, traditional style
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Zest and juice the lime into a medium bowl.
Peel and grate or mince the ginger; peel and mince garlic. Transfer both to the bowl with the lime.

Quarter jalapeño pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon. Finely dice and add to the bowl. (Be careful, with jalapeños, do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing).
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves and add to the bowl.
Trim off and discard ends of the green onions; cut the onions crosswise into ¼-inch pieces at an angle. Add half to the bowl; reserve the rest for garnish.
Drain salmon. Add to the bowl along with the egg, mayonnaise, bread crumbs, and salt; mash with a fork to combine.
Preheat a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat.
Using a ¼ cup measure, portion and form the salmon mixture into ½-inch thick patties.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Place patties in the skillet and cook until browned on the outside and warmed through, about 3 minutes per side. Remove to a plate.
Meanwhile, halve and pit avocado; slice lengthwise and crosswise while still in the skin and scoop out with a spoon.
Trim off and discard ends of the carrot. Using a julienne (or regular) peeler, peel the carrot into thin noodle-like sticks.
In a small bowl mix together chili-garlic sauce and mayonnaise.
Separate the lettuce into leaves. Pile leaves, in stacks of two per wrap, onto plates. Divide carrots, salmon cakes, and avocado between leaves; top with spicy mayo and reserved green onion. Enjoy!

name: Ginger Pork & Green Bean Stir-Fry over Cauliflower Rice with Sesame
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.

Cut cauliflower head into quarters; using a box grater, hold the stem end of the cauliflower and coarsely grate. (Alternatively, transfer cauliflower to the bowl of a food processor; pulse until rice-like in consistency.) Transfer to a baking sheet pan.
Trim and thinly slice green onions crosswise. Add half to the baking sheet with the cauliflower and place half in a small bowl.
Peel and mince ginger. Sprinkle half over the cauliflower and add half to the bowl with the green onion.
Drizzle oil over the cauliflower and season with salt. Stir to combine, then spread out in an even layer.
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast, stirring cauliflower halfway through, until rice is tender and golden, 18-20 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, preheat a skillet over high heat.
While the skillet heats up, trim and halve green beans crosswise.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add green beans and cook, stirring frequently, until starting to brown and soften, 4-6 minutes.
Add pork and salt to the skillet. Cook, breaking the meat apart with a spoon, until the pork is browned and crumbly and green beans are tender, 4-5 minutes.
Meanwhile, add soy sauce, chili-garlic sauce, sesame seeds, and maple syrup to the bowl with the green onion and ginger. Stir to combine the stir-fry sauce.
When the green beans and pork are done, reduce heat to low. Add stir-fry sauce and cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Remove from heat.
To serve, divide cauliflower rice and stir-fry between plates or bowls. Enjoy!

name: Ginger Pork, Mushroom & Avocado Lettuce Wraps with Pickled Green Onion
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Place vinegar, sugar, and salt in a small bowl; stir to combine the pickling liquid.
Trim and cut green onions crosswise into thin pieces. Add to the bowl with the pickling liquid, stir to combine, and set aside.
Roughly chop mushrooms. Place in a medium bowl and set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add pork and salt; cook, breaking the meat apart with a spoon, until browned and crumbly, 5-7 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel and mince ginger and garlic. Place both in another small bowl along with sesame seeds, soy sauce, and additional vinegar. Stir to combine the sauce.
When the pork is done, add the mushrooms to the skillet. Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until mushrooms start to brown, 4-5 minutes.
Meanwhile, halve and pit avocado; using a spoon, scoop out the flesh and slice crosswise into thin half-moons.
When the mushrooms are done, add sauce to the skillet and stir to combine. Continue to cook until heated through, about 30 seconds. Remove from heat.
Separate the lettuce into leaves. Pile leaves, in stacks of two per wrap, onto plates. Fill each wrap with the pork mixture, then top with pickled green onions and avocado. Enjoy!

name: Ginger-Soy Chicken with Mozzarella, Bacon, Bell Peppers & Mushrooms
ingredients: ¾ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and mince ginger and garlic; place both in a small bowl along with soy sauce, vinegar, and honey. Whisk to combine the sauce.

Holding a knife parallel to the cutting board, cut the chicken in half horizontally to form thin fillets; arrange in a baking dish. Pour half of the sauce over the chicken and turn to coat (reserve remaining sauce for later use).
Place baking dish in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and bake until chicken is almost cooked through, 15-18 minutes.
Meanwhile, preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add bacon and cook until crispy, 3-5 minutes per side. Remove bacon to a paper towel-lined plate. (Reserve skillet with drippings for later use.)
While the bacon cooks, using a clean cutting board, trim, seed, and thinly slice bell peppers; place in a medium bowl.
Thinly slice mushrooms and add to the bowl with the bell peppers.
Peel, halve, and slice onion into thin half-moons; add to the bowl.
Return skillet (with drippings) to medium heat; add veggies and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, 6-7 minutes.
Meanwhile, thinly slice cheese.
When the chicken is almost cooked through, remove from oven. Change oven setting to broil on high.
Layer chicken with bacon and cheese. Return baking dish to the oven and broil until cheese is melted and chicken is cooked through, about 5 minutes; remove from oven.
When the veggies are done, add remaining sauce to the skillet, stir to combine, and continue to cook until heated through, 1-2 minutes more. Remove from heat.
To serve, divide veggies and chicken between plates or bowls. Enjoy!

name: Gingered Pumpkin Bisque with Shrimp
ingredients: 16 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
½ (15 oz) can pure pumpkin purée
¾ lb raw peeled shrimp, fresh or frozen
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel the carrot, then trim off the ends; discard the peels and trimmings. Medium dice the carrot (cut into ½-inch cubes). Transfer to a medium bowl.
Trim off and discard the ends of the celery; medium dice the celery (cut into ½-inch cubes). Add to the bowl with the carrots.
Preheat a medium saucepan over medium heat.
