instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.

Medium dice potatoes. Transfer to a medium saucepan, add salt, cover with water, and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to medium and cook until potatoes can be easily pierced with a fork, 10-12 minutes. Drain and set aside.
Peel and grate or mince the ginger. Transfer half of the ginger to a blender; place the other half in a small bowl.

Quarter the jalapeño pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs of the jalapeño with a spoon. Finely dice; add half to the blender and half to the small bowl. (Be careful, with jalapeños, do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing).
Juice lemon into the blender.

Shave the cilantro leaves off the stems; discard the stems. Add cilantro to the blender, along with coconut, water, salt, chili powder, and sugar. Blend on high until smooth and creamy. Transfer cilantro chutney to a small bowl and set aside. Rinse blender.

Pick mint leaves off the stems; discard the stems. Transfer mint leaves to the blender along with yogurt, water, sugar, and spices. Blend on high until smooth and creamy. Transfer mint raita to a small bowl and set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat.
Peel and mince the onion.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add reserved ginger, jalapeño, and onion to the skillet; cook, stirring constantly, until softened, 3-5 minutes.
Add cooked potatoes, water, Dijon, and spices to the skillet; mash with a fork or potato masher, leaving some small pieces whole.
Add peas, and cook, stirring often, until peas are tender and potatoes are soft and fragrant, 2-3 minutes.
Toast pita if desired, then slice in half and carefully open using your fingers. Fill each pita with an equal portion of the potato filling.
To serve, divide spiced potato pockets between plates. Enjoy with cilantro chutney and mint raita on the side!

name: Indian-Style Fried Rice with Turkey, Carrots, Green Onions & Cashews
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add broth and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Cook rice until liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
While the rice is cooking, peel, trim, and small dice carrots. Place in a medium bowl.
Trim, seed, and small dice bell pepper. Add to the bowl with the carrots.
Peel and mince ginger and garlic. Add both to the bowl.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, trim and cut green onions crosswise into thin pieces. Add half to the bowl and set aside. (Reserve remaining green onions for serving.)
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add turkey and spices; cook, breaking the meat apart with a spoon, until browned and crumbly, 4-5 minutes.
Meanwhile, roughly chop cashews.

When the turkey is done, add veggies to the skillet. Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, 4-5 minutes. Remove from heat, add peas, and stir to combine; cover and set aside until the rice is done.
When the rice is done, add to the skillet. Return skillet to medium-high heat and continue to stir-fry until warmed through, 1-2 minutes more. Remove from heat.
To serve, divide fried rice between plates or bowls; top with cashews, chili-garlic sauce, and reserved green onions. Enjoy!

name: Italian Chicken-Gnocchi Skillet with Broccoli, Snap Peas & Lemon
ingredients: ¾ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
½ (8 oz) pkg sugar snap peas
instructions: Fill a medium saucepan about halfway with hot water (from the tap); cover with a lid and bring to a boil over high heat.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Once the water in the pan is boiling, add gnocchi and salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, until gnocchi begins to float to the surface, about 3 minutes. Drain in a colander and set aside.
While the gnocchi are cooking, peel, halve, and small dice onion. Peel and mince garlic. Place both in a small bowl.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat chicken dry with paper towels and cut into bite-sized pieces.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add onion, garlic, chicken, and spices. Cook, stirring frequently, until chicken is golden and cooked through, about 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, separate broccoli into bite-sized florets and cut stems into smaller pieces. Add broccoli and snap peas to the skillet. Cook, stirring frequently, until tender-crisp, 4-5 minutes.
Zest and juice lemon into the skillet, then add cooked gnocchi and stir to combine. Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until gnocchi is warmed through, 2-3 minutes. Remove from heat.
To serve, divide gnocchi, veggies, and chicken between plates or bowls. Enjoy!

name: Italian Chicken with Roasted Sweet Potatoes & Tomato-Mozzarella Salad
ingredients: ¾ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
½ (8 oz) pkg fresh mozzarella cheese
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and cut sweet potato lengthwise into ¼-inch thick strips; place in a medium bowl. Add oil and salt, toss to coat, then spread out on a baking sheet pan. (Reserve bowl for later use.)
Place sweet potato in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and bake, tossing once, until golden and fork-tender, about 25 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, place vinegar, oil, salt, and pepper in the reserved bowl; whisk to combine the dressing.
Halve tomatoes lengthwise and add to the bowl with the dressing.
Trim, seed, and medium dice bell pepper; add to the bowl.
Medium dice mozzarella and add to the bowl.
Pick basil leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and thinly slice into ribbons; add to the bowl, stir to combine the salad, and set aside.
Pat chicken dry with paper towels. Holding a knife parallel to the cutting board, cut the chicken in half horizontally to form thin fillets. Season both sides with spices.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add chicken and pan-fry until golden brown and cooked through, 3-4 minutes per side. Remove from heat and cover to keep warm.
To serve, divide chicken, sweet potatoes, and salad between plates. Enjoy!

name: Italian Sausage-Cabbage Stew with Tomato, Carrot, Parmesan & Toast
ingredients: 16 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim off and discard root end of cabbage; halve lengthwise, then slice crosswise into thin (shred-like) strips. Place in a medium bowl and set aside.
Preheat a medium saucepan over medium heat.
While the pan heats up, peel, halve, and small dice onion. Peel and mince garlic.
Once the pan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add onion, garlic, ground sausage, salt, and pepper. Cook, breaking the meat apart with a spoon, until browned and crumbly, 4-5 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel, trim, and halve carrot lengthwise, then cut crosswise into thin half-moons. Add to the bowl with the cabbage.
Trim and thinly slice celery crosswise. Add to the bowl.
When the sausage is done, add veggies, broth, and tomatoes to the pan. Stir to combine the stew and bring to a simmer over medium-high heat.
Meanwhile, shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add half to the pan and stir to combine (set remaining parsley aside for serving).
Once the stew is simmering, reduce heat to medium and continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until the veggies are soft, about 8 minutes. Remove from heat.
While the stew is cooking, preheat oven to broil on high and position the rack in the upper third of the oven.
Arrange bread slices on a baking sheet pan. Drizzle with oil, then sprinkle with Italian seasoning. Place in the oven and broil until toasted, 1-2 minutes. Remove from oven and cut toasts in half.
Finely grate Parmesan.
Divide stew between bowls; sprinkle with Parmesan and reserved parsley. Serve with toast on the side and enjoy!

name: Italian Sausage Soup with Rotini Pasta, Bell Pepper, Tomato & Spinach
ingredients: 16 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Peel, halve, and small dice onion.
Peel and mince garlic.
Preheat a medium saucepan over medium heat.
While the pan heats up, use the tip of a knife to slice down the length of each sausage; peel off casings and discard.
Once the pan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add onion, garlic, sausage, and spices; cook, breaking the meat apart with a spoon, until sausage is brown and crumbly, 5-7 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry bell pepper; using a clean cutting board, trim, seed, and small dice.
When the sausage is done, add bell pepper to the pan and stir to combine. Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until starting to soften, 3-4 minutes more.
Add broth, tomatoes, water, pasta, and vinegar to the pan; stir to combine. Cover and bring to a boil; once boiling, reduce heat to medium, and simmer until pasta is cooked through, about 8 minutes.
While the soup is simmering, wash and dry the spinach (skip this step if the spinach came pre-washed), then roughly chop.
Finely grate Parmesan.
Add spinach to the soup in handfuls, waiting for the spinach to wilt slightly before adding the next handful. Stir to combine and remove from heat.
To serve, divide the soup between bowls and top with Parmesan. Enjoy!

name: Italian Stuffed Zucchini Boats with Ground Beef, Tomatoes & Mozzarella
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Wash and halve zucchini lengthwise. Scrape out and discard the soft flesh from the middle of each half.
Place zucchini halves in a baking dish cut side up. Rub with a little olive oil and season with a little salt and pepper. Place in the oven and bake while you prepare the filling, 15-20 minutes.
Heat a sauté pan over medium-high heat.
Wash and small dice mushrooms. Wash and small dice tomato. Peel and mince onion and garlic.
Coat bottom of pan with oil. Add onion, garlic, and mushrooms. Stirring frequently, cook until vegetables are softened, 3-4 minutes.
Add beef and, breaking apart with a spoon, cook until browned and crumbly, 3-4 minutes.
Add diced tomato, tomato sauce, Italian seasoning, salt, and pepper. Cook until most of the liquid has evaporated, 2-3 minutes.
Coarsely grate ½ cup of mozzarella.
Remove dish from oven. Fill zucchini halves with beef mixture and sprinkle with cheese. Place back in the oven and bake until cheese melts, 4-5 minutes.
Wash and dry parsley. Shave leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves.
To serve, place zucchini boats on a plate and garnish with parsley. Enjoy!

name: Italian-Style Macaroni Soup with Beef, Carrot, Celery & Bell Pepper
ingredients: 24 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Preheat a medium saucepan over medium-high heat.

Once the pan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat. Add the beef and spices; cook, breaking the meat apart with a spoon, until browned and cooked through, about 5 minutes. Using a slotted spoon, transfer beef to a plate and set aside. (Reserve saucepan with drippings for later use.)
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim, seed, and small dice bell pepper. Place in a medium bowl.
Peel, trim, and small dice carrot. Add to the bowl with the bell pepper.
Trim and small dice celery. Add to the bowl.
Return the saucepan (with drippings) to medium-high heat.
While the pan is heating, peel, halve, and medium dice onion. Peel and mince garlic. Add both to the bowl.
Once the pan is hot, add the veggies and cook, stirring occasionally, until starting to soften, 3-4 minutes.

Return beef to the pan along with broth, tomatoes, pasta, and Worcestershire. Stir to combine the soup, cover, and bring to a boil. Once boiling, reduce heat to medium and simmer until pasta is cooked through, about 8 minutes.
Meanwhile, shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves.
Once the pasta is done, add half of the parsley to the soup and stir to combine. Remove from heat. (Reserve remaining parsley for serving.)
To serve, divide soup between bowls and sprinkle with reserved parsley. Enjoy!

name: Italian Tofu with Creamy Bell Pepper Rice & Orange-Olive Arugula Salad
ingredients: 10 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.

Cut tofu in half along the long side. Sandwich tofu between clean towels or paper towels and place on a baking sheet pan. Place a cutting board with something heavy on top and set aside to press out excess water.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the arugula if it came pre-washed.)
Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a medium saucepan. Add broth and salt to the pan; bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
While the broth is heating up, trim, seed, and mince bell pepper.

Once the broth comes to a boil, add bell pepper and stir to combine; cover the saucepan and reduce heat to low. Cook bell pepper-rice until liquid is mostly absorbed, 18-20 minutes. Once done, remove from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, place oil and spices in a medium bowl; stir to combine the spice paste.
Medium dice tofu, add to the bowl with the spice paste, and gently stir to coat. Transfer tofu to a baking sheet and spread out in a single layer. (Reserve bowl for later use.)
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and bake, tossing halfway through, until tofu is golden brown, about 20 minutes. Remove from oven.
While the tofu is cooking, peel and mince garlic. Place in the reserved bowl along with oil, vinegar, and spices; whisk to combine the dressing.
Peel and thinly slice shallot into rings. Add to the bowl with the dressing.
Cut off skin and white pith from the orange; slice between the membranes to release segments. Add to the bowl.
Halve olives lengthwise. Add to the bowl along with the arugula and toss to combine the salad. Set aside.
Finely grate Parmesan. When the bell pepper-rice is done, add Parmesan to the pan and stir until creamy and combined.
To serve, divide tofu, creamy bell pepper-rice, and salad between plates. Enjoy!

name: Italian Tuna Salad Lettuce Wraps with Cannellini Beans & Olives
ingredients: 1 (6 oz) can chunk light tuna in water
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Drain and rinse the beans in a colander; set aside to drain further.
Zest and juice lemon into a medium bowl.
Peel and mince shallot; add to the bowl with the lemon and stir to combine.
Trim celery and thinly slice crosswise at an angle; add to the bowl.
Thinly slice sun-dried tomatoes and add to the bowl.
Drain and thinly slice artichokes; add to the bowl.
Halve olives lengthwise and add to the bowl.
Cut cheese into small cubes; add to the bowl.
Shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves. Add most of the parsley to the bowl (reserve a small amount for garnish).
Drain and flake tuna. Add to the bowl along with beans, mayo, and pepper. Stir to combine the salad.
Separate the lettuce into leaves. Pile leaves, in stacks of two per wrap, onto plates. Top with tuna salad and garnish with reserved parsley. Enjoy!

name: Italian Turkey Meatball Sandwich with Mozzarella & Homemade Marinara
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Wash and dry parsley. Shave leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves. Place half in a medium bowl, reserving the rest for garnish.
Peel and mince shallot and garlic. Transfer both to the bowl with the parsley.
Add turkey, egg, bread crumbs, and spices to the bowl with the parsley and mix with your hands until well combined.

Coat baking dish with a thin layer of oil. Using a tablespoon measure, form the meat mixture into rounded meatballs and place in the dish. Place the dish in the oven and bake until cooked through, 15-18 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel additional garlic and place in a blender.
Drain tomatoes and add to the blender along with sugar and spices. Blend on high until almost smooth.
Combine tomato purée and oil in a medium saucepan over medium-low heat; cook, stirring often, until sauce is thick and garlic is cooked through, 5-8 minutes.
Meanwhile, coarsely grate mozzarella; finely grate Parmesan. Transfer both to a small bowl and toss to combine; set aside.
When the meatballs are done, carefully transfer them to the pan with the tomato sauce; stir to combine.
Set oven temperature to broil on high and position rack in the upper third of the oven.
Split the rolls in half and place on a baking sheet pan, cut-side facing up. Place in the oven and cook until lightly toasted, 1-2 minutes. Remove from the oven.

Set the tops of the rolls aside, leaving the bottoms on the baking sheet pan. Sprinkle bottom of rolls with half of the cheese. Divide meatballs and sauce between the rolls and top with remaining cheese. Place in the oven and broil to melt the cheese, about 1 minute.
To serve, sprinkle reserved parsley and crushed red pepper over each sandwich. Close sandwiches and divide between plates. Enjoy!

name: Italian Wedding Soup with Turkey Meatballs & Kale
ingredients: 32 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim off and discard the ends of the celery; small dice the celery (cut into ¼-inch cubes) and transfer to a medium bowl.
Peel the carrot, then trim off the ends; discard the peels and trimmings. Small dice the carrot (cut into ¼-inch cubes) and add to the bowl with the celery.
Preheat a medium saucepan over medium heat.
While the saucepan heats up, trim off and discard the ends of the onion and remove the outer layer; small dice the onion (cut into ¼-inch pieces) and add to the bowl with the celery and carrot.
Trim off and discard the root ends of the garlic; peel and mince or press the garlic. Add to the bowl with the other vegetables.
Once the saucepan is hot, add olive oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add the carrot, celery, onion, and garlic to the saucepan; season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are softened, 5 to 6 minutes.
Finely grate about ¾ cup of Parmesan and transfer to a small bowl.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat.

In a medium bowl, combine the ground turkey, ¾ of the grated Parmesan (save the rest for garnishing), salt, and pepper; mix together until well combined. Form the mixture into meatballs, each about 1 inch in diameter.
Once the skillet is hot, add olive oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add the meatballs to the skillet; cook, turning occasionally, until browned on all sides (they don't need to be cooked through), 5 to 7 minutes. Once done, transfer to a bowl.
Once the vegetables are softened, add broth, Italian seasoning, and crushed red pepper to the saucepan and bring the mixture to a boil.
Cut out and discard the center stems from the kale leaves; slice the leaves crosswise into 1-inch strips and transfer to a large bowl.
Once boiling, add the kale and meatballs to the saucepan; season with additional salt and pepper. Reduce the heat to a simmer and cook until the meatballs are cooked through, 6 to 8 minutes.
Using a knife, shave the parsley leaves off the stems at a downward angle, working away from your body; discard the stems and finely chop the leaves. Stir the parsley into the soup.
To serve, divide the soup between bowls and garnish with the remaining Parmesan. Enjoy!

name: Japanese Ginger Beef Skillet with Mushrooms, Peas, Green Onions & Rice
ingredients: 4 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add water and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Cook rice until liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and mince ginger and garlic. Place both in a small bowl along with broth, soy sauce, cornstarch, fish sauce, and sugar. Whisk to combine the sauce and set aside.
Thinly slice mushrooms.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add mushrooms and salt; cook, stirring occasionally, until golden brown, 3-4 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel, trim, and coarsely grate carrot.
When the mushrooms are done, add carrot, beef, additional salt, and pepper to the skillet. Cook, breaking the meat apart with a spoon, until browned and crumbly, 4-5 minutes.
While the beef is cooking, place peas in a colander and rinse under hot, running water (from the tap) to defrost; set aside to drain further.
Trim and cut green onions crosswise into thin pieces.

When the beef is done, add the sauce, peas, and half of the green onions to the skillet (reserve remaining green onions for serving). Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until sauce has thickened, about 1 minute. Remove from heat.
To serve, divide rice and beef skillet between plates or bowls; top with reserved green onions. Enjoy!

name: Japanese-Style Breaded Tofu (Katsu) with Sesame Veggie Slaw & Rice
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F.

Cut tofu in half along the long side. Sandwich tofu between clean towels or paper towels and place on a baking sheet pan. Place a cutting board with something heavy on top and set aside to press out excess water.
Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add water and salt, then bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
Meanwhile, place mayo and spices in a small bowl. Whisk to combine the curried mayo.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Cook rice until liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
While the rice is cooking, cut the tofu planks in half crosswise and return to the baking sheet.

Spread half of the curried mayo over the top side of the tofu, sprinkle with half of the bread crumbs (pressing gently to adhere), and drizzle with half of the oil. Carefully flip tofu and repeat with remaining mayo, bread crumbs, and oil. (Reserve bowl for later use.)
Place tofu in the oven and bake, turning halfway through, until the breading is crispy and golden brown, 15-18 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, place ketchup, soy sauce, maple syrup, chili-garlic sauce, and garlic powder in the reserved bowl. Whisk to combine the "tonkatsu" sauce and set aside.
Place additional mayo, vinegar, soy sauce, oil, and chili-garlic sauce in a medium bowl. Whisk to combine the dressing.
Wash, dry, trim, and quarter cucumber lengthwise, then cut crosswise into thin pieces. Add to the bowl with the dressing.
Wash, dry, trim, and thinly slice radishes. Add to the bowl, along with the broccoli slaw, and toss to combine.
To serve, divide rice, tofu, and slaw between plates or bowls; drizzle sauce over tofu and enjoy!

name: Japanese-Style Broccoli Slaw Pancake (Okonomiyaki) with Crispy Sausage
ingredients: 4 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and mince ginger and garlic. Transfer both to a medium bowl.
Add eggs and broth to the bowl with the ginger and garlic; whisk to combine and set aside.
Place flour, baking powder, and salt in another medium bowl; whisk to combine. Gradually add the egg mixture to the bowl with the flour, whisking to create a smooth batter.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat.
While the skillet heats up, add broccoli slaw to the bowl with the batter and stir until thoroughly combined.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add half the pancake batter (1¼-cups per pancake) to the skillet and smooth out into a large, ½-inch thick pancake. Cook, flipping once, until golden brown and cooked through, 3-4 minutes per side. Remove to a plate and cover with foil.
While the pancake is cooking, preheat a medium saucepan over medium-high heat.
While the pan heats up, use the tip of a knife to slice down the length of each sausage. Peel off casings and discard.
Add sausage meat to the pan and cook, breaking apart with a spoon, until crispy and cooked through, 5-7 minutes. Remove from heat, cover, and set aside.
Once the first pancake is done cooking, add more oil to the skillet and repeat with remaining batter.
Meanwhile, chop chives into small pieces and set aside.
Juice the lime into a small bowl. Add mayo and chili-garlic sauce; whisk to combine the spicy mayo.
To serve, place a pancake on each plate. Top with crispy sausage, drizzle with spicy mayo, and sprinkle with chives. Enjoy!

name: Jerk Chicken Drumsticks with Sweet & Savory Piña Colada Salad
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and mince ginger, garlic, and shallot. Place in a medium bowl along with soy sauce, oil, and spices; stir to combine the rub.
Preheat a grill pan, outdoor grill, or skillet over medium-high heat.
Pat chicken dry with paper towels and add to the bowl with the rub; turn to coat.
Once the grill pan is hot, coat with oil. Add chicken and grill, turning occasionally, until cooked through, 15-20 minutes. Remove to a plate and cover with foil.
Meanwhile, preheat oven to 400°F.
Juice lime into another medium bowl.
Trim green onions; cut crosswise into ¼-inch pieces at an angle. Add to the bowl with the lime juice.
Pick mint leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl.
Cut off skin from pineapple, core, and cut into bite-sized pieces. Add to the bowl.
Seed and small dice bell pepper; add to the bowl and toss to combine the salad.
Spread coconut on a baking sheet pan, place in the oven, and toast until golden, 2-3 minutes.
To serve, divide chicken and salad between plates. Sprinkle salad with toasted coconut and enjoy!

name: Kale Caesar Burger with Crisp Apple & Parmesan Salad
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and mince garlic; mince anchovy fillets. Divide both evenly between two medium bowls; set one bowl aside.
Add beef, salt, and pepper to the first bowl with garlic and anchovy. Use your hands to thoroughly combine. Form into 2 equal-sized patties, place on a plate, and set aside.
Zest and juice lemon into the second bowl with garlic and anchovy. Add mayo and whisk to combine the dressing.
Quarter and core apple, then thinly slice each quarter; add to the bowl with the dressing.
Fold kale leaves in half lengthwise and slice off the stems. Chop or tear leaves into bite-sized pieces, add to the bowl with the dressing, and toss to combine the salad. Set aside.
Preheat a grill pan, outdoor grill, or regular skillet over medium-high heat.

Once the grill pan is hot, coat with oil. Place burger patties on the grill and cook, undisturbed, for 5 minutes; flip patties, and grill an additional 3-4 minutes, until cooked through. Once done, transfer to a clean plate.
Meanwhile, finely grate Parmesan.
Toast buns on the grill pan (if desired).
Place a burger on the bottom half of each bun; top with half the Parmesan and a small portion of salad. Close with the top half of each bun.
To serve, divide burgers and remaining salad between plates. Top salad with remaining Parmesan and enjoy!

name: Kale-Potato Cakes with Lemon Aioli & Arugula Salad
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the arugula if it came pre-washed.)
Peel and chop the potatoes into 1-inch cubes; peel and smash the garlic (press firmly with the flat side of a knife or bottom of a pot).
Place the potatoes and garlic in a medium saucepan, season with salt, and cover with water. Cover with a lid and place on the stove at high heat; bring the water to a boil.
Fold leaves of kale in half lengthwise and slice off the stems. Chop or tear leaves into bite-sized pieces.
When the potato water comes to a boil, uncover, turn down to medium, and cook until potatoes are almost done, 8 minutes. Add kale to the pot and cook 2 minutes more.
Meanwhile, grate the zest from the lemon and transfer to a small bowl, then juice the lemon into a medium salad bowl.
Grate cheese and set aside.
Add oil, maple syrup, Dijon, salt, and pepper to the salad bowl with the lemon juice; whisk to combine the dressing.
Halve the grape tomatoes and add them to the bowl with the dressing. Chop green onions into ¼-inch pieces, set aside.
Once potatoes and kale are done, drain and return to the pot. Cook, shaking the pan occasionally, over medium-low heat until dry, about 2 minutes; remove from heat.
Using a potato masher or fork, mash potato and kale until almost smooth, with a few small chunks remaining. Add bread crumbs, cheese, egg, green onions, Dijon, salt, and pepper; stir to combine.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Meanwhile, add mayonaise, garlic powder, and paprika to the small bowl with the lemon zest and mix to make the aioli.

Once the skillet is hot add oil. Using a ⅓ measuring cup for each cake, drop potato mixture into the pan, pressing to make ½-inch thick rounds. Cook 3 minutes on each side, until crisp and golden; set aside. Cook in batches if necessary.
Toss arugula with salad dressing and tomatoes.
To serve, divide potato cakes and salad between plates. Serve with aioli and enjoy!

name: Kale Salad with Chicken, Apple, Dates, Pumpkin Seeds & Crispy Parmesan
ingredients: ¾ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F. Line a baking sheet pan with parchment paper and set aside.
Peel and mince shallot and garlic. Place both in a medium bowl along with oil, vinegar, mayo, Dijon, salt, and pepper. Whisk to combine the dressing.

Wash and dry kale. Fold leaves in half lengthwise and slice off the stems; finely chop leaves. Add to the bowl with the dressing. Using your hands, massage kale with the dressing until wilted, 1-2 minutes. Set aside.
Finely grate Parmesan. Place in a pile on the baking sheet and spread out into a 6-inch circle.

Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and bake until Parmesan is lightly browned and crisp, 5-7 minutes. (Watch carefully as the Parmesan can burn quickly.) Remove from the oven and set aside to cool.
Meanwhile, preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, holding a knife parallel to the cutting board, cut the chicken in half horizontally to form thin fillets. Season with salt and pepper on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add chicken and pan-fry until golden brown and cooked through, 3-4 minutes per side. Remove from heat.
Meanwhile, wash and dry apple; using a clean cutting board, quarter, core, and thinly slice. Add to the bowl with the kale.
Roughly chop dates and add to the bowl. Toss to combine the salad.
Thinly slice chicken into strips.
Break the crispy Parmesan into bite-sized pieces.
To serve, divide the salad between plates or bowls and top with sliced chicken, pumpkin seeds, and crispy Parmesan. Enjoy!

name: Kale Salad with Nutty Middle Eastern Spiced "Dukkah" Eggs & Flatbread
instructions: Mince walnuts.
Preheat a small saucepan over medium heat.
While the pan heats up, peel and mince garlic.

Once the pan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add walnuts, garlic, sesame seeds, and spices to the pan. Cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant and toasted, 1-2 minutes. Transfer the "dukkah" spice mix to a small bowl to keep the garlic from overcooking. (Reserve pan for next step.)

Wipe the saucepan clean with paper towels. Place eggs in the pan, cover with water (from the tap), and bring to a boil; reduce heat to a simmer and cook for 8 minutes. Drain hot water and add ice or run under cold water to cool; set aside.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and mince additional garlic; place in a medium bowl.
Zest and juice lemon into the bowl with the garlic, then add oil, salt, and pepper; whisk to combine the dressing.

Fold kale leaves in half lengthwise and slice off the stems. Chop or tear leaves into bite-sized pieces and add to the bowl with the dressing; using your hands, massage kale with the dressing until wilted, 1-2 minutes.
Trim and halve cucumber lengthwise, then slice crosswise into thin half-moons; halve tomatoes. Add both to the bowl.
Shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl, toss to combine the salad, and set aside.
Peel eggs, roll in the dukkah to coat, and halve lengthwise. (Reserve remaining dukkah for the flatbread.)
Toast flatbread if desired; drizzle with oil, sprinkle with remaining dukkah, and cut into wedges.
To serve, divide salad, eggs, and flatbread between plates or bowls. Enjoy!

name: Kale Salad with Poached Eggs, Beans & Warm Bacon-Shallot Dressing
instructions: Wash and dry kale. Fold leaves in half lengthwise and slice off the stems. Stack leaves on top of one another, then cut crosswise into thin (shred-like) ribbons. Place in a medium bowl.
Sprinkle salt into the bowl with the kale. Using your hands, massage kale until slightly wilted, 1-2 minutes.
Drain and rinse beans in a colander. Add to the bowl with the wilted kale and set aside.
Peel and mince shallot. Place in a small bowl and set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, small dice bacon.

Once the skillet is hot, add bacon and cook, stirring occasionally, until crispy, 4-5 minutes. Using a slotted spoon, remove crispy bacon to a paper towel-lined plate; set aside. (Reserve skillet with drippings for later use.)

Meanwhile, fill a medium saucepan about halfway with hot water (from the tap); add vinegar, cover with a lid, and bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Once the water in the pan is boiling, reduce heat to medium-low.
Gently crack eggs into two additional small bowls (two eggs per bowl).

Adjust the heat of the saucepan as necessary so that the water is simmering. Gently tip bowls into the pan, sliding the eggs carefully into the water. Cook until whites are set but yolks are still soft, 2½-3 minutes. Using the slotted spoon, transfer eggs to the plate with the bacon.
Return skillet (with drippings) to medium heat. Add oil, shallot, pepper, and salt; cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, 2-3 minutes.

Once the shallot has softened, remove from the heat. Whisk in the vinegar and Dijon, scraping the bottom of the skillet to incorporate any browned bits. Drizzle warm dressing into the bowl with the kale and beans. Toss to combine.
To serve, divide the salad between plates or bowls. Top with crispy bacon and poached eggs. Enjoy!

name: Kale Salad with Pork Sausage, Grapes, Pumpkin Seeds & Cheddar
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, juice lemon into a medium bowl.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add sausages and cook, turning occasionally, until browned and cooked through, 10-15 minutes. Remove from heat.
Meanwhile, add oil, honey, salt, and pepper to the bowl with the lemon juice; whisk to combine the dressing.
Fold kale leaves in half lengthwise and slice off the stems. Chop or tear leaves into bite-sized pieces and add to the bowl with the dressing. Using your hands, massage the dressing into the kale.
Halve grapes and add to the bowl with the kale.
Small dice cheese and set aside for serving.
When the sausages are done, transfer to a cutting board and slice crosswise into bite-sized rounds.
Add sausage and pumpkin seeds to the bowl with the kale; toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide salad between plates and top with diced cheese. Enjoy!

name: Kidney Bean, Bell Pepper & Carrot Coconut Curry with Cilantro Naan
ingredients: ½ (13.5 fl oz) can coconut milk
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Drain and rinse beans in a colander; set aside to drain further.
Peel, halve, and small dice onion. Peel, trim, and small dice carrot. Place both in a small bowl.
Preheat a medium saucepan over medium heat.
While the pan heats up, trim, seed, and small dice bell pepper. Add to the bowl with the other veggies.
Once the pan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add veggies and salt; cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, 4-5 minutes. (Reserve bowl for the next step.)
Meanwhile, peel and mince ginger and garlic. Small dice tomatoes. Add both to the reserved bowl.
Once the veggies are soft, add ginger, garlic, tomato, and spices to the pan. Cook, stirring frequently, until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add beans, coconut milk, and water to the pan; bring to a simmer. Once simmering, reduce heat to low and cook, stirring occasionally, until beans are tender and curry has thickened, about 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, preheat oven to broil on high and position rack in the upper third of the oven.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves.
Arrange naan on a baking sheet pan and place in the oven; broil, flipping once, until golden brown and toasted, 1-2 minutes.
Remove naan from the oven, spread with oil, and sprinkle with half of the cilantro; cut into wedges. (Reserve remaining cilantro for the curry.)
When the curry is done, remove from heat. Add reserved cilantro and stir to combine.
Divide curry between bowls and serve with naan on the side. Enjoy!

name: Kidney Bean Chili with Melty Cheddar & Cornbread Topping
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Wash and small dice bell pepper. Peel and mince garlic. Peel and small dice onion.

Wash and quarter the jalapeño lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon. Finely mince. (Be careful, with jalapeños, do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing).
Preheat a large ovenproof skillet over medium heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add butter and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add bell pepper, garlic, onion, and jalapeño to the skillet; cook, stirring frequently, until softened, 3-5 minutes.
Meanwhile, drain and rinse beans.
Add beans, tomatoes, water, tomato paste, and spices to the skillet. Reduce heat to low and cook, stirring occasionally, while you prepare the cornbread batter.
Melt butter in a microwave or saucepan. Once melted, add to a medium bowl.

Add milk and egg to the bowl with the butter and whisk to combine. In a separate medium bowl, stir together cornmeal, flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt. Gradually add wet ingredients to the bowl with the dry ingredients and stir to combine.
Coarsely grate cheddar.
Sprinkle cheese over the bean mixture. Pour cornbread batter on top and smooth into a thin layer with a spatula.
Place skillet in the oven and bake until cornbread is golden and cooked through, about 20 minutes.
To serve, divide chili and cornbread between bowls and enjoy!

name: Kidney Bean Curry (Rajma Chawal) with Rice & Mango-Cucumber Salad
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add water and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Cook rice until liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
While the rice is cooking, peel and mince ginger and garlic. Place both in a medium bowl and set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, peel, halve, and small dice onion.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add onion and cook, stirring occasionally, until beginning to soften, about 3 minutes.
While the onion is cooking, medium dice tomatoes. Add to the bowl with the ginger and garlic.
When the onion is soft, add ginger, garlic, tomatoes, and spices to the skillet. Cook, stirring occasionally, until tomato is soft, about 5 minutes. (Reserve bowl for the next step.)
Meanwhile, shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Place in the reserved bowl (setting aside a small handful for serving).
Juice lime into the bowl with the cilantro. Add oil, salt, and pepper; stir to combine the dressing and set aside.

Drain and rinse beans in a colander. When the tomato is soft, add beans and water to the skillet; stir to combine the curry and bring to a boil over high heat. Once boiling, reduce heat to medium and simmer, stirring occasionally, until curry has thickened, about 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel mango and slice flesh away from the pit, starting with the flat sides; medium dice. Add to the bowl with the dressing.
Trim and medium dice the cucumber. Add to the bowl, stir to combine the salad, and set aside.
When the curry is done, remove from heat. Add yogurt and stir to combine.
To serve, divide rice, curry, and salad between plates or bowls; top curry with reserved cilantro. Enjoy!

name: Korean-Style Beef Rice Bowl with Cucumbers
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add water to the saucepan; bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
In a medium salad bowl, combine and whisk together rice vinegar, honey, and crushed red pepper.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce the heat to low. Cook the rice until the liquid is fully absorbed, 15 to 18 minutes. Once done, remove the rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Trim off and discard the ends of the cucumber; slice the cucumber crosswise into very thin rounds. Add to the salad bowl and toss.
Peel and grate or mince the ginger. Transfer to a small bowl.
Trim off and discard the root end of the garlic; peel and mince or press the garlic. Add to the bowl with the ginger.
To the ginger and garlic, add soy sauce, sesame oil, and honey.
Preheat a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat.
Trim off and discard the ends of the green onions; cut the onions crosswise into ¼-inch pieces at an angle. Transfer to a small bowl.
Once the skillet is hot, add the ground beef to the skillet; cook, breaking apart with a spoon, until browned and crumbly, 3 to 4 minutes.
Add the soy sauce mixture and about ¾ of the green onions (save the rest for garnishing) to the beef; stir to combine and cook for an additional 1 to 2 minutes.
Uncover the rice and fluff with a fork.
To serve, divide the rice, beef, and cucumbers between plates; garnish with the remaining green onions and chili-garlic sauce. Enjoy!

name: Korean-Style Steak Skewers with Spicy Cucumber & Carrot Salad
ingredients: ¾ lb striploin (New York strip) steak
instructions: If using wooden skewers, place 4-6 skewers in a shallow dish of water to soak until you are ready to use them.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim green onions; mince half and place in a medium bowl. Slice the other half crosswise into ¼-inch pieces, place in another medium bowl, and set aside.
Peel and mince ginger and garlic; add to the bowl with the minced green onions, along with vinegar, soy sauce, honey, fish sauce, oil, and chili-garlic sauce. Whisk to combine the marinade.
Pat steak dry with paper towels and cut into 1-inch cubes; add to the bowl with the marinade, turn to coat, and set aside.
Add soy sauce, oil, vinegar, sesame seeds, honey, chili powder, and cayenne to the bowl with the sliced green onion; whisk to combine the dressing.
Using a clean cutting board, trim and halve cucumber lengthwise, then slice crosswise into thin half-moons; add to the bowl with the dressing.
Trim, seed, and small dice bell pepper; peel, trim, and coarsely grate carrot. Add both to the bowl and stir to combine the salad. Set aside.
Preheat a grill pan, outdoor grill, or regular skillet over medium-high heat.
While the grill pan heats up, thread steak onto skewers and place on a plate, reserving marinade for later use. (If you don't have skewers, you can cook the steak directly on the grill pan.)
Once the grill pan is hot, coat with oil; add the skewers and cook, turning occasionally, until the steak is cooked through, 8-10 minutes. Remove to a clean plate.
Meanwhile, pour reserved marinade into a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat, then reduce heat to low, and simmer until sauce is slightly thickened, 3-4 minutes; remove from heat.
To serve, divide skewers and salad between plates; drizzle skewers with sauce and enjoy!

name: "Kung Pao" Pork Meatballs with Peppers, Peanuts & Cauliflower Rice
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.

Cut cauliflower head into quarters; using a box grater, hold the stem end of the cauliflower and coarsely grate. (Alternatively, transfer cauliflower to the bowl of a food processor; pulse until rice-like in consistency.) Place in a medium bowl.
Add oil and salt to the bowl with the cauliflower rice, then stir to combine. Transfer to a baking sheet pan and spread out in an even layer. (Reserve bowl for later use.)
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast, stirring cauliflower halfway through, until rice is tender and golden, 15-18 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, peel and mince ginger. Place in the reserved bowl along with pork, bread crumbs, chili-garlic sauce, and salt; using your hands, mix well to combine.
Using a tablespoon measure, form the pork mixture into rounded meatballs and place on a plate.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, trim and cut green onions crosswise into thin pieces. Place in a clean medium bowl and set aside.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom; add meatballs and cook, turning occasionally, until golden brown and cooked through, 6-8 minutes. Transfer to a clean plate. (Reserve skillet for later use.)
While the meatballs are cooking, trim, seed, and medium dice bell pepper. Trim and thinly slice celery crosswise. Add both to the bowl with the green onions.
Drain and rinse water chestnuts. Add to the bowl.
Return skillet to medium-high heat, add more oil, and swirl to coat the bottom. Add veggies, water chestnuts, and peanuts; stir-fry until veggies are tender-crisp, 3-4 minutes.
Meanwhile, place water, vinegar, soy sauce, chili-garlic sauce, cornstarch, and sugar in a small bowl. Stir to combine the sauce.
Return meatballs to the skillet along with the sauce. Bring to a boil and cook, stirring frequently, until sauce has thickened and meatballs are warmed through, about 1 minute. Remove from heat.
To serve, divide cauliflower rice, meatballs, veggies, and sauce between plates or bowls. Enjoy!

name: "Kung Pao" Tofu with Bell Peppers, Celery & Cashews over Rice
instructions: Cut tofu in half along the long side. Sandwich tofu between clean towels or paper towels and place on a baking sheet pan. Place a cutting board with something heavy on top and set aside to press out excess water.
Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add water and salt, then bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Cook rice until liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, medium dice tofu. Place in a medium bowl, sprinkle with cornstarch and salt, then gently toss to coat.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add the tofu and cook, turning every few minutes, until golden brown and crispy, about 10 minutes; remove to a plate. (Reserve bowl for later use.)
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim, seed, and large dice bell peppers. Trim and large dice celery. Place both in the reserved bowl and set aside.
Peel and mince ginger and garlic. Place both in a small bowl.
Trim and cut green onions crosswise into 1-inch pieces. Add to the bowl with the ginger and garlic.

When the tofu is done, return skillet to medium-high heat, add more oil, and swirl to coat the bottom. Add the bell pepper and celery; cook, stirring occasionally, until tender-crisp, about 5 minutes.
While the veggies are cooking, add water, soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, chili-garlic sauce, additional cornstarch, and oil to the small bowl. Whisk to combine the sauce.
When the veggies are done, add crispy tofu, sauce, and cashews to the skillet. Bring the sauce to a boil and cook, stirring frequently, until thickened, about 1 minute. Remove from heat.
To serve, divide rice and stir-fry between bowls. Enjoy!

name: Lamb Chops with Middle Eastern Cilantro Sauce (Chermoula) & Veggies
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and mince garlic; transfer to a small bowl.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl with the garlic.
Juice lemon into the bowl. Add oil and spices; stir to combine the chermoula and set aside.
Peel, trim, and thinly slice carrots into ¼-inch thick rounds. Transfer to a baking sheet pan.
Trim and halve zucchini lengthwise; cut crosswise into ½-inch thick half-moons and add to the baking sheet with the carrots.
Drizzle veggies with oil and season with salt and pepper. Toss to combine, then spread out in a single layer.
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast, stirring halfway through, until veggies are fork-tender, about 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the lamb chops dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with salt and pepper on both sides.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add lamb chops and cook, flipping once, until cooked through, 5-6 minutes. Remove to a plate, cover loosely with aluminum foil, and rest 5 minutes.
To serve, divide lamb chops and roasted veggies between plates; drizzle with chermoula and enjoy!

name: Lamb Chops with Minty Cucumber & Tomato Salad
instructions: Place the lamb chops on a plate; rub with olive oil and season with salt and pepper on both sides; set aside.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Cut the cucumber in half crosswise, then cut quarter lengthwise into 4 wedges; cut the wedges crosswise into bite-sized chunks. Transfer to a large bowl.
Halve the tomatoes and add to the bowl.
Pick the mint leaves off the stems; discard the stems. Stack the leaves and cut crosswise into thin ribbons; add to the bowl.
Preheat a grill pan or skillet over medium heat.
While the pan/skillet heats up, peel and small dice the onion; add to the bowl.
Place the lamb chops on the grill or skillet and cook until desired doneness, 2 to 5 minutes per side.
Halve the lemon and juice one half over the salad. Cut the other half into wedges for serving.
Drizzle the salad with olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Toss to combine.
To serve, place the salad on plate, add the lamb chops on the side, and squeeze the lemon wedges over the lamb. Enjoy!

name: Lamb in Tomato Sauce with Rosemary White Bean Purée
ingredients: 4 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Heat a sauté pan over medium-high heat.
Season lamb with salt and pepper.
Coat bottom of pan with oil. Add lamb and cook until browned, 2-3 minutes per side.
Wash rosemary. Pick leaves off the stems. Peel and mince garlic.
Transfer lamb to a plate and return pan to stove. Add more oil and ½ of the rosemary and garlic (save the rest for the mash). Cook until fragrant, 15-30 seconds.
Add tomatoes, broth, salt, and pepper; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to a simmer and cook for 2-3 minutes.
Return lamb to pan and cook with the sauce until it is fully cooked through, 5-6 minutes.
Heat a small saucepan over medium heat.
Grate 1 tsp of lemon zest. Drain and rinse beans; place on paper towels and pat dry.
Coat bottom of saucepan with oil. Add lemon zest and remaining rosemary and garlic. Stir and cook for about 1 minute.
Add beans and broth. Cook until heated through, 3-4 minutes.
Drizzle with juice from the lemon and season with salt and pepper. Mash until smooth.
To serve, place lamb, tomato sauce, and bean mash on a plate. Enjoy!

name: Lebanese Lentils, Rice & Fried Onions (Mujadara) with Chopped Salad
ingredients: 20 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled feta cheese
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse lentils under cold water; drain and transfer to a medium saucepan. Add broth and salt, then bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce heat to a simmer, cover, and cook for 10 minutes (the lentils will not be cooked all the way through).
Meanwhile, preheat a skillet over medium-low heat.
While the skillet heats up, peel, halve, and thinly slice onion into half-moons.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add the onion, cumin, and salt; cook, stirring occasionally, until soft and golden brown, about 15 minutes. Remove from heat and set aside.
While the onions are cooking, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and add to the saucepan with the lentils; return to a boil over high heat.

Once the liquid returns to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Cook lentils and rice until tender and liquid is mostly absorbed, 18-20 minutes more. Once done, remove from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel and mince garlic. Place in a medium bowl along with oil, vinegar, and spices; whisk to combine the dressing.
Trim and small dice cucumber; small dice tomato. Add both to the bowl with the dressing.
Stack lettuce leaves, one on top of another; halve lengthwise, then slice crosswise into thin (shred-like) strips. Add to the bowl.
Pick mint leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl.
Add feta to the bowl and toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide salad and the lentil-rice mixture between plates; top lentils and rice with fried onions. Enjoy!

name: Lebanese-Style Beef Kabobs with Cucumber-Tomato Salad & Paprika Yogurt
instructions: If using wooden skewers, place 4 skewers in a shallow dish of water to soak until you are ready to use them.
Peel and mince the garlic; transfer to a medium bowl.
Peel the onion. Thinly slice half of the onion and add to the bowl with the garlic. Mince remaining onion and place in a separate, medium bowl.
Add vinegar and salt to the bowl with the thinly sliced onion and garlic; stir to combine, then set aside to marinate.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves. Add half of the parsley to the bowl with the marinating onions.
Add remaining parsley, ground beef, and spices to the bowl with the minced onion; mix with your hands until well combined.

Using a ¼ cup measure, form the beef mixture into 8 short, sausage-like shapes, approximately 3-inches long; thread 2 onto each skewer. (Alternatively, you can cook directly on the grill/skillet without using skewers.)
Place kabobs closely together on a baking sheet pan. Drizzle oil over the kabobs, then rotate the kabobs to coat in a thin layer of oil.
Heat a grill pan, outdoor grill, or skillet over medium-high heat.
Meanwhile, combine yogurt, paprika, and salt in a small bowl and whisk to combine; set aside.
Coat the grill or skillet with oil; place kabobs on the grill, rotating every 2½-3 minutes, until browned and cooked through, 10-12 minutes. Transfer to a plate and loosely cover with foil.
Peel and medium dice the cucumber; medium dice the tomatoes. Add both to the bowl with the marinated onions.
Add oil, salt, and pepper to the bowl with the tomato and cucumber; stir to combine the salad.
To serve, divide salad and kabobs between plates. Enjoy with paprika yogurt on the side!

name: Lebanese-Style Beef Meatballs with Tahini Sauce, Peppers & Onions
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim, seed, and slice bell peppers lengthwise into thin strips. Transfer to a baking sheet pan.

Peel, halve, and slice onion lengthwise into thin strips; add to the baking sheet with the peppers. Drizzle veggies with oil, then season with salt and pepper; toss to coat and spread out in an even layer.
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast until veggies are starting to soften, 10-12 minutes.
Meanwhile, pick mint leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Place half in a medium bowl. (Reserve the other half for serving.)
Add beef, bread crumbs, egg, and spices to the bowl with the mint; use your hands to combine the beef mixture. Using a tablespoon, form the mixture into rounded meatballs and place on a plate.
When the veggies are soft, remove from the oven. Add meatballs to the baking sheet, nestling them into the veggies.
Return baking sheet to the oven and continue to roast until the veggies are golden brown and meatballs are cooked through, about 12 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, juice half of the lemon into a small bowl. Cut remaining lemon into wedges and set aside for serving.
Add tahini, water, pepper, and salt to the bowl with the lemon juice. Whisk to combine the sauce.
Divide veggies and meatballs between plates; drizzle meatballs with tahini sauce and sprinkle veggies with reserved mint. Serve with lemon wedges for squeezing. Enjoy!

name: Leek, Mushroom & Goat Cheese Frittata
instructions: Wash and thinly slice leek.
Heat a skillet over medium heat.
Preheat oven to broil setting and position rack about 6 inches from the top.
Melt butter in skillet. Add leek and season with salt pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, 4-5 minutes.
Wash and slice mushrooms. Peel and mince garlic.
Add mushrooms and garlic to skillet and cook, stirring frequently, until softened, 4-5 minutes.
Wash and dry parsley. Shave leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves.
In a medium bowl, whisk together eggs, water, ¾ of the parsley (save the rest for garnishing), salt, and pepper.
Crumble goat cheese and stir about ½ into egg mixture (save the rest for sprinkling overtop).

Spread out leek and mushrooms evenly in the skillet. Pour in egg mixture. As eggs set around the edge of the skillet, gently lift cooked portions with a spatula to allow uncooked egg to flow underneath. Cook until bottom and sides are firm but the top is still runny, 5-7 minutes.
Sprinkle with remaining goat cheese. Place skillet in the oven until the top is set and lightly browned, 2-3 minutes.
To serve, cut frittata into wedges, place on a plate, and garnish with remaining parsley. Enjoy!

name: Lemon-Basil Fettuccine with Seared Salmon & Broccoli
instructions: Fill a large pot halfway with hot water (from the tap). Add salt, cover, and bring to a boil over high heat. Once boiling, uncover, add pasta, and stir for a few seconds; cook until almost done, about 8 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel and mince garlic. Place in a medium bowl along with oil and spices.

If using salmon with skin, place the fillet, skin-side down, on a cutting board. Holding the tail end (or corner) firmly, use a knife to cut between the flesh and skin; continue to cut through the length of the fillet (take care not to cut through the skin); discard the skin.
Cut the salmon into 1-inch cubes. Add to the bowl with the garlic-oil, stir to coat, and set aside to marinate.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Using a clean cutting board, separate broccoli into bite-sized florets and cut stems into smaller pieces.

When the pasta is almost done, add broccoli to the pot. Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until pasta reaches desired firmness and broccoli is tender, 2-3 minutes more. Drain pasta and set aside. (Reserve a ¼-cup pasta water before draining.)
Meanwhile, preheat a skillet over medium heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add salmon and cook, turning occasionally, until cooked through, 3-4 minutes.
While the salmon is cooking, pick basil leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and thinly slice into ribbons.
When the salmon is done, juice lemon into the skillet.

Add drained pasta, broccoli, reserved pasta cooking water, and half of the basil to the skillet. Toss to combine and continue to cook until heated through, about 2 minutes. Remove from heat. (Reserve remaining basil for serving.)
To serve, divide pasta between plates or bowls and top with reserved basil. Enjoy!

name: Lemon-Basil Ricotta Pasta with Sautéed Zucchini & Parmesan
instructions: Fill a medium saucepan halfway with hot water (from the tap), cover, and bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Uncover, add salt and pasta, and stir for a few seconds. Cook until desired firmness, 8-10 minutes. (Reserve a ½-cup of cooking water before draining and set aside.)
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim and quarter zucchini lengthwise, then slice crosswise into ¼-inch thick pieces. Place in a medium bowl and set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, peel, halve, and small dice onion. Peel and mince garlic.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom; add onion and garlic. Cook, stirring frequently, until starting to soften, 2-3 minutes.
Add zucchini and salt to the skillet. Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until zucchini is tender, 6-8 minutes. (Reserve bowl for the next step.)
Meanwhile, zest and juice lemon into the reserved bowl.
Pick basil leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and thinly slice into ribbons. Add half to the bowl with the lemon. (Reserve remaining basil for serving.)
Finely grate Parmesan. Add half to the bowl along with the ricotta and spices. Stir to combine. (Reserve remaining Parmesan for serving.)

When the zucchini is done, add pasta, reserved pasta water, and ricotta mixture to the skillet. Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until the sauce coats the pasta and Parmesan has melted, about 2 minutes. Remove from heat.
To serve, divide the pasta between plates or bowls; top with reserved Parmesan and basil. Enjoy!

name: Lemon-Butter Chicken with Honey-Roasted Parsnips & Carrots
ingredients: ¾ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
instructions: Heat the oven to 450°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim and discard the stem ends and peel the carrots; quarter lengthwise into wedges and transfer to a baking sheet.
Trim and discard the stem ends and peel the parsnips; cut lengthwise into uniform wedges (about the same size as the carrots); add to the baking sheet.

Pinch the top of the rosemary stems with one hand while sliding the other hand down to remove the leaves; discard the stems and roughly chop the leaves. Sprinkle half of the rosemary over the vegetables (save the rest for the chicken).
Drizzle the vegetables with olive oil and honey and season with salt and pepper; toss to coat.
Spread the vegetables in an even layer and place the sheet in the oven. Roast, stirring once halfway through the cooking time, until browned and tender, 15 to 20 minutes.
Holding a knife parallel to the cutting board, cut the chicken in half horizontally to form thin fillets.
Season the chicken with salt and pepper on both sides.
Heat a skillet over medium heat.
Add butter to the skillet and swirl to coat the bottom.
Place the chicken in the skillet and cook until browned and cooked through, 3 to 4 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate.
Zest and juice half of lemon into a small bowl, then add the remaining rosemary. Thinly slice the other half into rounds.
Once the chicken has been transferred, add more butter and the lemon slices to the skillet. Cook the lemon, turning once, until lightly browned, 2 to 3 minutes.
Return the chicken to the skillet and pour in the lemon-rosemary sauce. Turn the chicken over a few times to coat it in the sauce. Cook until the juices are reduced, 1 to 2 minutes.
Divide the chicken and lemon slices between two plates (or one plate and one lunch container) and add the roasted vegetables on the side. Enjoy!

name: Lemon-Caper Spaghetti with Tofu, Asparagus, Bell Pepper & Parsley
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Cut tofu in half along the long side. Sprinkle each tofu plank with salt on both sides and sandwich between clean towels or paper towels; place on a baking sheet pan. Place a cutting board with something heavy on top and set aside to press out excess water.

Fill a medium saucepan halfway with hot water (from the tap), cover, and bring to a boil. Uncover, add salt and pasta, and stir for a few seconds. Cook until desired firmness, 8-10 minutes; drain and set aside.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Snap or cut off the woody ends of the asparagus; cut crosswise into 1-inch pieces and place in a small bowl.
Trim, seed, and slice bell pepper into thin strips; add to the bowl with the asparagus and set aside.
Cut the tofu planks in half, then cut each half into 2 triangles; place in a medium bowl. Sprinkle with flour and pepper on both sides.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom; add tofu and cook until golden, 2-3 minutes per side. Remove to a plate and loosely cover with aluminum foil. (Reserve skillet for later use.)
Meanwhile, peel and mince garlic.
When the tofu is done, return the skillet to medium heat; add more oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add garlic and additional flour; cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Zest and juice half of the lemon into the skillet; add broth, capers, salt, and pepper. Cook, stirring often, until the sauce has thickened, 2-3 minutes. (Reserve remaining lemon for the next step.)
While the sauce is cooking, cut the remaining lemon into wedges and set aside for serving.
Add asparagus and bell pepper to the skillet with the sauce; cook, stirring occasionally, until veggies are fork-tender, about 4 minutes.
Meanwhile, shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves.
When the veggies are done, add drained pasta and parsley to the skillet; toss to combine and continue to cook until heated through, 1-2 minutes more.
To serve, divide pasta, veggies, sauce, and tofu between plates or bowls. Squeeze lemon over top and enjoy!

name: Lemon Chicken & Asparagus Stir Fry with Cauliflower Rice
ingredients: ½ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
instructions: Wash the cauliflower and remove the leaves. Using a food processor or box grater, grate to rice-like texture. Transfer to a large bowl and set aside.
In a skillet, heat oil over medium-high heat. Add the cauliflower and cook, stirring occasionally, until the rice is slightly browned and tender, 7-10 minutes. Return to the bowl and set aside.
Peel and mince the garlic. Peel and mince or grate the ginger. Grate zest from the lemon.
In a small bowl, create a slurry by whisking together water with cornstarch until smooth. Add the minced garlic and ginger, lemon zest and juice, soy sauce, and honey and whisk together. Set aside.
Wash the asparagus and snap (or cut) off the woody ends. Cut on an angle into 2 inch pieces. Transfer to a bowl.
Cut the chicken into bite-sized pieces. Season with salt and pepper.
Once the cauliflower rice has been removed, add more oil to the skillet. Add the chicken and cook until browned and cooked through, 2-3 minutes. Transfer to a plate.
Once the chicken has been removed, add more oil to the skillet. Add asparagus and cook, stirring occasionally, until bright green and tender-crisp, 3-4 minutes.
Return the chicken to the skillet and pour in the sauce. Stir-fry until heated through and sauce thickens, 1-2 minutes.
Place cauliflower rice in a bowl and top with the stir fry. Enjoy!

name: Lemon-Cilantro Chicken Kebab with Veggie Rice Pilaf & Blueberry Salsa
instructions: If using wooden skewers, place 2-4 skewers in a shallow dish of water to soak until you are ready to use them.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel, trim, and small dice carrot; peel, halve, and small dice onion. Place both in a medium bowl.
Preheat a medium saucepan over medium heat.
While the pan heats up, trim and small dice zucchini; add to the bowl with the carrot and onion.
Once the pan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add veggies and spices; cook, stirring occasionally, until starting to soften, 2-3 minutes. (Reserve bowl for later use.)
While the veggies are cooking, using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water.

Add rice and water to the pan, stir to combine, and bring to a boil over high heat. Once the liquid comes to a boil, cover the pan and reduce heat to low. Cook rice pilaf until liquid is mostly absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove from heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.

Meanwhile, peel and mince garlic. Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Place garlic and half of the cilantro in the reserved bowl. (Place remaining cilantro in a small bowl and set aside for the salsa.)
Zest and juice lemon into the bowl with the garlic and cilantro, then add oil and spices; stir to combine the marinade.

Cut chicken into bite-sized pieces, add to the bowl with the marinade, and stir to coat. Thread chicken onto skewers and place on a plate; alternatively, you can cook the chicken pieces directly on the grill pan without using skewers.
Preheat a grill pan, outdoor grill, or regular skillet over medium-high heat.
Once the grill pan is hot, add the kebabs and cook, turning occasionally, until chicken is cooked through, 8-10 minutes. Remove to a clean plate.

Meanwhile, using a clean cutting board, quarter jalapeño pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon. Finely dice and add to the small bowl with the cilantro. (Be careful with jalapeños; do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Roughly chop blueberries and add to the bowl along with vinegar, oil, honey, salt, and pepper. Stir to combine the salsa and set aside.
To serve, divide rice pilaf, chicken kebabs, and blueberry salsa between plates. Enjoy!

name: Lemon-Curry Lentil Salad with Crunchy Cauliflower, Cucumber & Arugula
ingredients: 16 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.

Using a strainer, rinse lentils under cold water; drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add broth, cumin, and salt, then bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce heat to a simmer, cover, and cook until tender, 15-20 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the arugula if it came pre-washed.)

Remove leaves and thick stems from the cauliflower, then cut into bite-sized pieces. Transfer to a baking sheet pan, drizzle with oil, and season with spices. Toss to combine, then spread out in an even layer.
Place cauliflower in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast, tossing halfway through, until fork-tender and golden, about 15 minutes.
While the cauliflower is roasting, peel and mince garlic; place in a medium bowl.
Zest and juice lemon into the bowl with the garlic. Add oil and spices; whisk to combine the dressing.
Trim green onions and celery; cut both crosswise into ¼-inch pieces. Add to the bowl.
Trim and small dice cucumber. Add to the bowl.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl.
When the cauliflower is done, remove from the oven and set aside to cool, about 5 minutes.
When the lentils are done, drain in a colander, rinse with cold water, and add to the bowl with the dressing and veggies.
Add roasted cauliflower to the bowl and toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide arugula and lentil salad between plates. Top with pine nuts and enjoy!

name: Lemon-Dijon Chicken Wings with Bacon, Blue Cheese & Spinach Salad
ingredients: 1 lb chicken wings, split with tips removed
½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled blue cheese
instructions: Preheat oven to 475°F. Line a baking sheet pan with aluminum foil to make clean up easier (optional).
Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)
Zest lemon into a medium bowl, then add oil, Dijon, salt, and pepper; whisk to combine the marinade. (Set lemon aside for later use.)
Pat chicken wings dry with paper towels and add to the bowl with the marinade; toss to coat and spread out on the baking sheet in an even layer.
Place wings in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and bake, turning once, until cooked through, 20-25 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, medium dice bacon.
Once the skillet is hot, add bacon and cook, stirring occasionally, until crispy, 4-5 minutes. Using a slotted spoon, remove crispy bacon to a paper towel-lined plate.
While the bacon is cooking, juice reserved lemon into a clean medium bowl; add Dijon, salt, and pepper.
When the bacon is done, add drippings from the skillet to the bowl with the lemon juice and Dijon; whisk to combine the dressing.
Using a clean cutting board, peel, trim, and coarsely grate carrot; add to the bowl with the dressing.
Trim and medium dice cucumber; add to the bowl and set aside.
Right before serving, add crispy bacon, spinach, and blue cheese to the bowl with the dressing and veggies; toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide wings and salad between plates. Enjoy!

name: Lemon Dijon Drumsticks with Roast Potatoes & Spinach-Artichoke Salad
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F. Line a baking sheet pan with aluminum foil to make clean up easier (optional).
Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)
Peel and mince garlic; place in a medium bowl.
Juice lemon into the bowl with the garlic, then add oil, Dijon, and spices; whisk to combine the marinade.
Quarter potatoes and add to the bowl with the marinade.
Pat chicken dry with paper towels, add to the bowl, and toss to coat. Transfer potatoes and drumsticks to the baking sheet, arranging them in an even layer; drizzle any leftover marinade over top.
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and bake, turning halfway through, until potatoes and chicken are cooked through, 25-30 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, place mayo, oil, vinegar, Dijon, salt, and pepper in a clean medium bowl; whisk to combine the dressing.
Drain and thinly slice artichokes; add to the bowl with the dressing.
Right before serving, add spinach to the bowl and toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide chicken, potatoes, and salad between plates. Enjoy!

name: Lemon-Dill Greek Stuffed Chicken
ingredients: ¾ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled feta cheese
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Zest and juice lemon into a small bowl.
Shave dill leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl.
Peel and mince garlic; add to the bowl with oil and whisk to combine the marinade. Set aside.
Trim zucchini, halve lengthwise, and slice into thin half moons. Halve tomato and slice into half moons. Set aside on a plate.
Peel and slice onion into half rings.
Pat chicken dry with paper towels and season with salt and pepper. Make 5 crosswise slits in each breast, being careful not to cut through completely.
Place chicken on a large sheet pan and stuff each slit with a slice of zucchini, tomato, and onion. Add remaining veggies to the sheet pan next to the chicken.
Drizzle chicken and vegetables with the marinade.
Grate mozzarella. Sprinkle cheeses over the chicken and vegetables.
Place in the oven and bake for 20-25 minutes, until chicken is cooked through.
To serve, divide chicken and vegetables between plates. Enjoy!

name: Lemon-Garlic Chicken Drumsticks with Zucchini, Corn & Feta Salad
ingredients: ½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled feta cheese
instructions: Heat the oven to 500°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and mince the garlic; divide between two medium bowls.
Juice the lemon and divide between the two bowls.
Shave the parsley leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves. Divide the minced parsley between the two bowls.
Add olive oil, salt, and pepper to both of the bowls (divide the amounts between the two).
Add the chicken drumsticks to one of the bowls and toss to coat in the marinade.
Arrange the drumsticks in a baking dish and place in the oven (even if it is not fully heated yet). Bake, turning halfway through cooking time, until cooked through, 25-30 minutes.
Shuck the corn to remove the leaves and silk threads; stand the corn vertically in a large, empty bowl and slice the kernels off the cob.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Trim and discard the ends of the zucchini, medium dice the zucchini and add to the bowl with the corn.
Add olive oil to the skillet and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add the corn and zucchini to the skillet; cook, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are lightly browned and softened, 4 to 6 minutes. Once done, return the vegetables to the bowl to cool.
Place the feta into a small bowl.
Transfer the zucchini and corn to the other bowl with the dressing and stir to combine.
To serve, place the chicken drumsticks and salad on a plate and sprinkle the salad with the feta. Enjoy!

name: Lemon-Garlic Chicken Skewers with Cucumber, Peach, Basil & Feta Salad
ingredients: ½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled feta cheese
instructions: If using wooden skewers, place 4-6 skewers in a shallow dish of water to soak until you are ready to use them.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Zest lemon into a medium bowl (set lemon aside for later use).
Peel and mince garlic. Add to the bowl with the lemon zest along with mayo, salt, and pepper; stir to combine the marinade.
Pat the chicken dry with paper towels and cut into bite-sized pieces. Add to the bowl with the marinade, stir to coat, and set aside.
Preheat a grill pan, outdoor grill, or regular skillet over medium-high heat.
While the pan heats up, thread chicken onto skewers and place on a plate. Alternatively, you can cook the chicken pieces directly on the grill pan without using skewers.
Once the pan is hot, add the skewers and grill, turning occasionally, until chicken is cooked through, 8-10 minutes. Remove to a clean plate.
Meanwhile, using a clean cutting board, peel and mince shallot. Place in another medium bowl.
Juice lemon into the bowl with the shallot. Add oil, honey, Dijon, and spices; whisk to combine the dressing.
Trim and medium dice cucumber. Add to the bowl with the dressing.
Quarter peaches lengthwise (around the pit); twist quarters to separate, then remove and discard pits. Medium dice the flesh and add to the bowl.
Pick basil leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and thinly slice into ribbons. Add to the bowl, along with the feta, and stir to combine the salad.
To serve, divide salad and skewers between plates or bowls. Enjoy!

name: Lemon-Garlic Zucchini Salad with Walnuts & Ricotta Cheese
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.

Trim the zucchini ends. Using a spiralizer, julienne peeler (or regular peeler) peel into noodle-like sticks; transfer to colander and sprinkle with salt. Set the colander in a bowl to catch the excess moisture.
Grate all the zest from the lemon, then juice the lemon; transfer both to a medium bowl.
Peel and mince or press the garlic; transfer to the bowl, whisking together with oil, lemon juice, and pepper.
Place a skillet over medium heat. Coarsely chop walnuts. Toast walnuts until fragrant (2-4 minutes) stirring regularly.
