Halve the avocado lengthwise and twist the halves to separate, then remove the pit with a knife or spoon; scoop out and medium dice the flesh. Transfer to a small bowl.
Using a knife, shave the cilantro leaves off the stems at a downward angle, working away from your body; discard the stems and finely chop the leaves. Stir the cilantro into the soup.
To serve, divide the soup between bowls, then top with the avocado and tortilla crisps. Enjoy!

name: Mexican Spiced Salmon with Walnut Guacamole & Bell Pepper-Corn Sauté
instructions: Preheat oven to broil on high and position rack under the broiler.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim, seed, and small dice bell peppers; place in a small bowl.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl with the bell pepper and set aside.
Pat fish dry with paper towels and transfer to a baking sheet pan. Drizzle both sides with oil, arrange skin-side down, then season top side with spices.
Place baking sheet in the oven and broil until salmon is just opaque, about 5 minutes. Flip salmon and continue to broil until the skin is crispy, 3-4 minutes more. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, preheat a skillet over medium heat.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add bell pepper, cilantro, corn, salt, and pepper; cook, stirring occasionally, until veggies are tender, about 5 minutes. Remove from heat. (Reserve bowl for the next step.)
While the veggies are cooking, peel and mince shallot and garlic. Place both in the reserved bowl.
Juice half of the lime into the bowl with the shallot and garlic. (Cut remaining lime into wedges and set aside for serving.)
Halve and pit avocado; using a spoon, scoop the flesh into the bowl. Add spices and mash with a fork or potato masher until guacamole is smooth.
Roughly chop walnuts, add to the bowl with the guacamole, and stir to combine.
Divide salmon and veggies between plates; top salmon with guacamole and serve with lime wedges for squeezing. Enjoy!

name: Mexican Street Corn Salad with Black Beans, Radish, Feta & Lime Crema
ingredients: ½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled feta cheese
instructions: Preheat oven to broil on high and position rack under the broiler.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim and cut green onions crosswise into ¼-inch pieces; transfer to a baking sheet pan.

Add corn to the baking sheet; drizzle with oil, season with spices, and toss to combine. Place in the oven and broil, stirring halfway through, until veggies are lightly charred, 10-12 minutes. Remove from oven and set aside to cool.
Meanwhile, drain and rinse beans in a colander; set aside to drain further.
Zest lime into a small bowl. Add yogurt, water, and spices to the bowl and whisk to combine the crema. Set aside.
Juice the lime into a large salad bowl.
Peel and mince garlic; add to the bowl with the lime juice.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl (reserving a small handful for garnish).
Add oil, honey, salt, and pepper to the bowl; whisk to combine the dressing.
Seed and slice bell pepper into thin strips. Trim and thinly slice radishes. Add both to the bowl with the dressing.
Chop or tear romaine leaves into bite-sized pieces; transfer to the bowl, along with the beans, and toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide salad between plates or bowls, top with the corn mixture, and drizzle with lime crema. Sprinkle with feta and reserved cilantro. Enjoy!

name: Mexican Stuffed Peppers with Roasted Sweet Potatoes
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F. Position racks in the upper and lower thirds of the oven.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and mince garlic; place half in a medium bowl. (Set remaining garlic aside for later use.)
Juice lime into the bowl with the garlic, then add oil and spices; stir to combine the spice oil.

Quarter sweet potato lengthwise, then cut crosswise into ¼-inch thick pieces; add to the bowl with the spice oil and toss to combine. Transfer to a baking sheet pan and spread out in an even layer. (Reserve bowl for later use.)
Place baking sheet on lower rack of the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast, tossing halfway through, until fork-tender, about 25 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, trim, seed, and halve bell peppers lengthwise. Transfer to another baking sheet, cut-side up, and drizzle with oil.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Place half in the reserved bowl along with the remaining garlic. (Set the rest of the cilantro aside for serving.)
Add ground beef, tomato sauce, and spices to the bowl with the cilantro and garlic; stir to combine the filling.
Divide filling between pepper halves. Place baking sheet on upper rack of the oven; bake until the peppers are tender and beef is almost cooked through, about 15 minutes.
While the peppers are cooking, coarsely grate cheddar.
When the peppers are tender, remove from the oven and sprinkle with cheese. Return to the oven and continue to bake until the beef is cooked through and cheese is melted, 5 minutes more.
To serve, divide stuffed peppers and sweet potato between plates. Sprinkle with reserved cilantro and enjoy!

name: Mexican-Style Chicken, Corn, Jalapeño & Cilantro Soup with Feta
ingredients: 16 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled feta cheese
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel, halve, and small dice onion; peel and mince garlic. Place both in a small bowl.
Trim and small dice celery; trim, seed, and medium dice bell pepper. Add both to the bowl with the onion and garlic.
Preheat a medium saucepan over medium-high heat.

While the pan heats up, quarter jalapeño pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon. Small dice and add to the bowl with the veggies. (Be careful with jalapeños; do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Once the pan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add veggies and cook, stirring frequently, until softened, 3-4 minutes. (Reserve bowl for later use.)
Add flour and spices to the pan; continue to cook, stirring frequently, until fragrant, about 1 minute.

Add chicken, broth, and tomato sauce to the pan. Stir to combine, cover, and bring to a boil over high heat; once boiling, reduce heat to medium-low and simmer, stirring occasionally, until chicken is cooked through, 10-12 minutes.
Meanwhile, trim, halve, and thinly slice radishes crosswise; place in the reserved bowl. Drizzle with vinegar, sprinkle with salt, and stir to combine; set aside to marinate.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves.

When the chicken is done, remove thighs to a plate using tongs (continue to simmer soup over low heat). Shred the chicken using two forks; use one fork to hold the chicken and the other fork to pull and shred the meat.
Return shredded chicken to the pan, along with cilantro, corn, and additional vinegar; stir to combine the soup and continue to simmer until warmed through, 2-3 minutes more.
To serve, divide soup between bowls; top with pickled radish and feta. Enjoy!

name: Mexican-Style Frittata with Bell Pepper, Cheddar & Avocado
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Preheat the oven to the broil setting and position the rack in the upper third of the oven.
Quarter the bell pepper lengthwise; remove and discard the stem, seeds, and membranes. Slice the quarters crosswise into small strips and transfer to a medium bowl.
Quarter the jalapeño pepper lengthwise; remove and discard the stem, seeds, and membranes. Finely dice the pepper and add to the bowl with the bell pepper.
Preheat an ovenproof skillet over medium heat.
Trim off and discard the ends of the onion and remove the outer layer; halve the onion lengthwise, then thinly slice crosswise. Add to the bowl with the peppers.
Trim off and discard the ends of the green onions; cut the onions crosswise into ¼-inch pieces at an angle. Transfer to a small bowl.
Once the skillet is hot, add olive oil and swirl to coat the bottom.

Add the peppers, onion, and about ¾ of the green onions (save the rest for garnishing) to the skillet; season with chili powder, cumin, salt, and pepper. Cook, stirring frequently, until the vegetables have softened, 4 to 6 minutes.
Coarsely grate about ½ cup of cheddar.
In a medium bowl, combine and whisk together the cheddar, eggs, water, salt, and pepper.

Pour the egg mixture into the skillet. While tilting the skillet with one hand, lift up the edges of the frittata with a spatula and let the eggs run underneath during the first few minutes of cooking. Cook until most of the frittata is set, but the top is still runny, 4 to 5 minutes.
Halve the avocado lengthwise and twist the halves to separate, then remove the pit with a knife or spoon; thinly slice the flesh crosswise (without piercing the skin) and scoop out.
Transfer the skillet to the oven and broil until the top is set and lightly browned, 2 to 3 minutes.
To serve, separate the frittata into wedges and divide between plates; top with avocado slices and remaining green onions. Enjoy!

name: Mexican Tomato Soup (Sopa de Fideo) with Pasta, Avocado & Feta
ingredients: 24 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled feta cheese
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and large dice onion. Large dice tomatoes; place both in a medium bowl.
Preheat a medium saucepan over medium-high heat.
While the pan heats up, peel and roughly chop garlic.

Once the pan is hot, add butter and swirl to coat the bottom. Add onion, tomatoes, garlic, and salt; cook, stirring occasionally, until veggies start to soften, about 5 minutes. Remove from heat. (Reserve bowl for next step.)
Meanwhile, peel, trim, and small dice carrot. Trim and cut green beans into 1-inch pieces. Place both in the reserved bowl and set aside.
Transfer the tomato-onion mixture to a blender and blend on high until smooth; set aside.
Use your hands to break the pasta into 1-inch pieces.
Return pan to the stove over medium-high heat; add more butter and swirl to coat the bottom. Add the pasta and cook, stirring constantly, until it turns golden, 1-2 minutes.

Add tomato-onion pureé, broth, tomato sauce, carrots, green beans, and spices to the pan. Stir to combine, bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to medium-low and cover the pan. Simmer, stirring occasionally, until pasta and vegetables are tender, 8-10 minutes.
Add peas to the soup during the last 2 minutes of cooking; continue to simmer until heated through, 1-2 minutes.
Meanwhile, halve and pit the avocado; scoop out flesh with a spoon and medium dice.
Cut lime into wedges.
Divide soup between bowls; top with avocado and feta. Serve with lime wedges on the side and enjoy!

name: Minestrone Soup with Kidney Beans, Green Beans, Carrots & Pasta
ingredients: 32 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel, trim, and small dice carrot; trim and small dice celery. Place both in a small bowl.
Preheat a medium saucepan over medium-high heat.
While the pan heats up, peel, halve, and small dice onion; peel and mince garlic. Add both to the bowl with the carrot and celery.
Once the pan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add veggies and spices; cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, 4-5 minutes.
Meanwhile, drain and rinse kidney beans; set aside to drain further.
When the veggies are soft, add broth and tomatoes; stir to combine the soup and bring to a boil.
Once the soup is boiling, add the kidney beans and pasta; stir to combine. Reduce heat to medium, cover, and cook, stirring occasionally until the pasta is partially cooked, about 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, trim and cut green beans into 1-inch pieces.
Add green beans to the soup and continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until pasta and veggies are tender, 3-5 minutes more.
To serve, divide soup between bowls and enjoy!

name: Mini Glazed Meatloaves with Mashed Potatoes & Roasted Carrots
instructions: Preheat the oven to 425°F.
Peel and mince onion; place in a medium bowl.
Add ground beef, egg, milk, bread crumbs, salt, and pepper to the bowl with the onions. Mix with your hands until well combined.
Place ketchup, Dijon, and brown sugar in a small bowl; whisk to combine.
Divide meatloaf mixture between 6 muffin cups and top with ketchup glaze. Place in the oven and bake until cooked through, 20-25 minutes.

Meanwhile, wash, peel, and medium dice potato. Transfer to a medium saucepan, cover with hot water (from the tap), and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to medium and cook until potatoes can be easily pierced with a fork, 10-12 minutes.

Wash, trim, and peel carrots. Slice lengthwise into quarters. Place on a baking sheet pan, drizzle with oil, and season with salt and pepper. Place in the oven and bake until golden and fork-tender, about 10 minutes.
When the potatoes are done, drain, and return to the pan.
Add milk, butter, salt, and pepper to the potatoes. Mash until smooth.
To serve, divide the meatloaves, roasted carrots, and mashed potatoes between plates. Enjoy!

name: Mini Tofu Shawarma with Cucumber-Tomato Salad & Mint Yogurt
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.

Cut tofu in half along the long side. Sandwich tofu between clean towels or paper towels and place on a baking sheet pan. Place a cutting board with something heavy on top and set aside to press out excess water.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Place oil and spices in a medium bowl; stir to combine the spice paste.
Medium dice tofu, add to the bowl with the spice paste, and gently toss to coat. Transfer tofu to a baking sheet and spread out in a single layer. (Reserve bowl for later use.)
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and bake, tossing halfway through, until tofu is golden brown, about 20 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, place vinegar, oil, salt, and pepper in the reserved bowl; whisk to combine the dressing.
Peel, halve, and thinly slice shallot; add to the bowl with the dressing.
Small dice tomato. Peel, trim, and small dice cucumber. Add both to the bowl and stir to combine the salad; set aside.
Pick mint leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Place in a small bowl.
Peel and mince garlic. Add to the bowl with the mint, along with yogurt, salt, and pepper; stir to combine the yogurt sauce.
Warm tortillas in a skillet, oven, or microwave (optional).
To serve, fill tortillas with tofu, cucumber-tomato salad, and mint yogurt. Divide between plates and enjoy!

name: Minted Asparagus Pea Soup with Seared Shrimp & Parmesan Crisps
ingredients: 16 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
½ lb raw peeled shrimp, fresh or frozen
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Drain shrimp in a colander and rinse under cold water until there are no more ice chunks. Spread out on a clean towel and pat dry. Skip this step if you are using fresh shrimp.
Wash the asparagus and snap (or cut) off the woody ends. Cut into 1-inch pieces and transfer to a baking sheet; drizzle with olive oil and bake in the oven for 10-12 minutes.

To make crisps, line a baking sheet with parchment paper and grate Parmesan cheese. Measure out 1 tbsp of the grated Parmesan and place in a pile on the sheet. Repeat with remaining cheese, keeping the piles a few inches apart.
Place in the oven and bake until lightly browned, 5-7 minutes. Watch carefully because they can burn quickly. Once done, remove from the oven and let them sit for a couple of minutes.
Trim, peel, and mince the shallot and garlic.
Preheat a large pot over medium heat.
When the pot is hot, add oil and swirl to coat. Add the shrimp; cook until opaque, about 3-4 minutes, stirring occasionally. Once done, transfer to a plate.
Return pot to heat, add oil, swirling to coat the bottom; add shallot and garlic. Cook, stirring frequently, until shallots are translucent, 2-3 minutes.
Wash mint. Pick leaves off the stems; discard the stems and finely mince the leaves. Add to pot.
Add peas, broth, salt, and pepper to the pot. Bring to a boil over high heat, then turn down to medium-high. Cook until peas have softened, 4-5 minutes.

Add the roasted asparagus and cream to the soup, reserving some asparagus for garnish. Using an immersion (hand) blender, purée the soup until smooth. Allow soup to heat through but not boil, 2-3 minutes more.
To serve, ladle soup into bowls and drizzle with more cream. Top with reserved asparagus, Parmesan crisps, and shrimp. Enjoy!

name: Mixed Green Salad with Sausage, Sweet Potato, Feta & Italian Dressing
ingredients: ½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled feta cheese
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the mixed greens if they came pre-washed.)
Peel and cut sweet potato into ½-inch cubes; transfer to a baking sheet pan. Drizzle with oil, season with salt and pepper, and toss to combine; spread out in an even layer.

Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast, stirring halfway through, until sweet potatoes are golden brown and fork-tender, about 20 minutes. Remove from oven and set aside to cool, about 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, slice the sausages crosswise into ½-inch thick rounds.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add sausage and cook, stirring occasionally, until golden brown and crispy, 5-6 minutes. Use a slotted spoon to transfer the sausage to a paper towel-lined plate and set aside.
While the sausage is cooking, place oil, vinegar, sugar, and spices in a medium bowl. Whisk to combine the dressing.
Using a clean cutting board, halve tomatoes and add to the bowl with the dressing.
Add mixed greens to the bowl and toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide salad between plates or bowls; top with roasted sweet potato, crispy sausage, and feta. Enjoy!

name: Moroccan Chickpea, Apricot, Bell Pepper & Zucchini Curry with Couscous
ingredients: 16 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: In a small saucepan, bring broth to a boil. Once boiling, remove from heat, add couscous, and stir to combine. Cover and let stand for 10 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel, trim, and slice carrot crosswise into ¼-inch thick rounds. Place in a medium bowl.
Trim, seed, and thinly slice bell pepper. Add to the bowl with the carrot.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, peel, halve, and slice onion crosswise into thin half-moons. Peel and mince garlic. Add both to the bowl.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add the veggies and spices; cook, stirring occasionally, until the veggies start to soften, about 5 minutes. (Reserve bowl for the next step.)
Meanwhile, trim and halve zucchini lengthwise, then slice crosswise into ¼-inch thick half-moons. Place in the reserved bowl.
Roughly chop apricots and add to the bowl with the zucchini.
Drain and rinse chickpeas in a colander.
Once the veggies start to soften, add zucchini, apricots, chickpeas, tomatoes, broth, tomato paste, and sugar to the skillet. Stir to combine the curry and bring to a boil over high heat.
Once boiling, reduce heat to medium-low, and cook, stirring occasionally, until veggies and chickpeas are tender, 10-15 minutes.
Meanwhile, shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves.
When the curry is done, remove from heat, add half of the parsley, and stir to combine. (Reserve remaining parsley for serving.)
To serve, divide couscous and curry between plates or bowls. Top with reserved parsley and pine nuts. Enjoy!

name: Moroccan Fish, Carrot, Zucchini & Bell Pepper Skillet with Couscous
ingredients: 16 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: In a small saucepan, bring broth to a boil. Remove from heat, add couscous, and stir. Cover and let stand for 10 minutes. Uncover couscous and fluff with a fork.
Meanwhile, preheat a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat.
Pat the fish dry with paper towels and place on a plate. Season with salt and pepper on both sides.
Sprinkle flour over both sides of each fillet and press gently to adhere.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add fish to the skillet and cook until opaque and cooked through, about 3 minutes per side. Remove to a plate and cover with foil.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Seed and slice bell pepper into thin strips. Peel, halve, and thinly slice onion. Peel and thinly slice garlic.
Return skillet to medium-high heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add more oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add the bell pepper, onion, and garlic; cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel and thinly slice carrot. Trim and thinly slice zucchini. Add both to the skillet along with the spices. Cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant, about 1 minute.

Stir in the tomatoes, broth, tomato paste, and sugar. Increase temperature to high and bring to a boil; then reduce heat to medium and let simmer, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened, 2-3 minutes.
Shave the cilantro leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves. Add half of the cilantro to the skillet (reserve the rest for garnish).

Place fish fillets in the skillet over the vegetables, spooning a thin layer of sauce over the top to cover. Cover with a lid and let simmer until veggies are soft and fish is warmed through, about 5 minutes.
Cut the lemon into wedges.
To serve, divide couscous and vegetable-fish sauté between plates or bowls. Garnish with cilantro and lemon wedges. Enjoy!

name: Moroccan Style Chicken with Zucchini & Couscous
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Wash zucchini and tomatoes. Halve zucchini lengthwise, then slice crosswise into half rounds. Medium dice tomatoes. Peel and small dice onion. Peel and mince garlic.
Heat a sauté pan over medium-high heat.
In a small saucepan, bring broth to a boil. Remove from heat, add couscous, and stir. Cover and let stand for 10 minutes.
Coat bottom of pan with oil. Add chicken and cook until lightly browned but not cooked through, 1-2 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate.
Return pan to stove and add more oil. Add onion, garlic, and zucchini. Stirring frequently, cook until vegetables begin to soften, 2-3 minutes.

Return chicken to pan. Add tomatoes, honey, cinnamon, cumin, salt, and pepper. Stir to combine and bring to a boil. Reduce heat, cover, and cook until chicken is cooked through and zucchini is tender, 8-10 minutes.
Wash and dry cilantro. Shave leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves. Add ½ to pan (save the rest for garnishing) while the ingredients cook.
Uncover couscous and fluff with a fork.
To serve, place couscous on a plate, top with chicken and sauce, and garnish with remaining cilantro. Enjoy!

name: Moroccan-Style Turkey Meatball Stew with Carrot Couscous & Herbs
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel, trim, and coarsely grate carrot; place in a small saucepan.
Add broth to the pan with the carrot, cover, and bring to a boil over high heat.
Once boiling, remove pan from the heat, add couscous, and stir to combine. Cover and let stand for 10 minutes; fluff with a fork right before serving.
Meanwhile, shave cilantro leaves off the stems; pick mint leaves off the stems. Discard stems and mince the leaves. Place half of the herbs in a medium bowl and set remainder aside for serving.
Peel and mince garlic; add to the bowl with the herbs along with turkey and spices. Using your hands, mix well to combine.
Using a tablespoon measure, form the turkey mixture into rounded meatballs and place on a plate.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add meatballs and cook, turning often, until just browned on all sides, 4-5 minutes (the meatballs will not be cooked all the way through). Once done, transfer to a clean plate. (Reserve skillet for later use.)
Meanwhile, peel, halve, and small dice onion; trim and small dice celery.
Return the skillet to medium heat, add more oil, and swirl to coat the bottom. Add onion and celery; cook, stirring occasionally, until veggies start to soften, about 3 minutes.
While the veggies are cooking, medium dice tomatoes; add to the skillet along with the tomato sauce, water, and spices. Stir to combine and bring the stew to a boil over high heat.

Once the stew is boiling, reduce heat to medium, then return meatballs (and any accumulated juices) to the skillet; continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until meatballs are cooked through, 5-6 minutes more.
When the meatballs are done, juice lemon into the skillet, stir to combine, and remove from heat.
To serve, divide couscous and meatball stew between plates or bowls; sprinkle with reserved herbs and enjoy!

name: Mozzarella & Bruschetta Grilled Chicken with Balsamic Glaze
ingredients: ¾ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
½ (8 oz) pkg fresh mozzarella cheese
instructions: Place a small saucepan on medium-high heat; add balsamic vinegar and brown sugar; stir until sugar is dissolved. Cook until reduced by half, or until thick enough to coat the back of a spoon, 10-15 minutes. Once done, remove from heat.
Holding a knife parallel to the cutting board, cut the chicken breasts in half horizontally, forming thin fillets.
Mix the spices together in a small bowl. Rub chicken fillets with the spice mixture on both sides.
Heat a grill pan or skillet over medium-high heat.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
When hot, coat grill pan with oil.
Place the chicken fillets in the grill pan; cook until they are golden brown and cooked through, 5-6 minutes per side. Once done, remove from heat.
Preheat oven to broil and position rack under the broiler. Line a baking sheet with foil for easy clean-up (optional).
Small dice the tomatoes and transfer to a medium bowl.
Peel and mince the shallots and garlic and add to the bowl with the tomatoes.
Pick basil leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and thinly slice into ribbons. Add to the bowl with the tomatoes. Add the oil, salt, and pepper and stir to combine. Set aside.
Slice the fresh mozzarella.
Place cooked chicken on the baking sheet pan. Top with sliced mozzarella. Place in the oven and cook for 2-3 minutes, until the cheese begins to melt.
To serve, divide the chicken between plates, top with tomato mixture, and a drizzle of balsamic glaze. Enjoy!

name: Mozzarella, Prosciutto, Corn & Arugula Flatbread Pizza
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Place corn in a medium bowl and cover with hot water from the tap.
Peel and mince garlic; transfer to a small bowl. Add oil and stir to combine.
Using a strainer or colander, drain the corn and transfer to a clean towel; pat dry.
Grate cheese.
Place the flatbreads on a baking sheet and spread with the garlic oil.
Layer cheese, corn, and prosciutto onto the flatbreads.
Place pizza in the oven and bake, until the cheese is golden and melted, about 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the basil and arugula. (Skip the arugula if it came pre-washed.) Pick basil leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and thinly slice into ribbons.
When pizza is done top with arugula, basil, and crushed red pepper.
To serve, cut pizza into wedges and divide between plates. Enjoy!

name: Mu Shu-Style Pork with Broccoli Slaw & Mushrooms over Jasmine Rice
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add water and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Cook rice until liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash, dry, and thinly slice mushrooms; transfer to a medium bowl and set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the pork chops dry with paper towels and place on a cutting board; thinly slice crosswise into bite-sized strips and season with salt and pepper.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add pork strips and stir-fry until browned and cooked through, 4-5 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel and mince garlic; place in a small bowl along with soy sauce, cornstarch, peanut butter, chili-garlic sauce, oil, vinegar, honey, and spices. Whisk to combine the sauce and set aside.
When the pork is done, use a slotted spoon to transfer the strips to a plate and set aside.
Return skillet to medium-high heat, add more oil, and swirl to coat the bottom. Add mushrooms and cook, stirring occasionally, until they start to soften, about 3 minutes.
Add broccoli slaw and sauce to the skillet; continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until the veggies are tender-crisp and sauce thickens, 2-3 minutes.
Return pork to the skillet, along with any accumulated juices; stir to combine and cook until heated through, about 1 minute. Remove from heat.
To serve, divide rice and pork stir-fry between plates. Enjoy!

name: Mushroom, Cheddar & Jalapeño Quesadilla with Poppy Seed Fruit Salad
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Juice lime into a medium bowl; add yogurt, poppy seeds, and sugar. Whisk to combine the dressing and set aside.
Remove stems from mushrooms and carefully scrape out the gills; halve and slice crosswise into ¼-inch thick pieces.
Preheat a large skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, peel and mince garlic.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom; add mushrooms, garlic, and spices. Cook, stirring occasionally, until soft, 4-5 minutes; remove from heat.

Meanwhile, halve jalapeño pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon. Slice crosswise into thin half-moons. (Be careful with jalapeños; do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Trim green onions and cut crosswise into ¼-inch pieces.
Coarsely grate cheese.

To assemble the quesadillas, lay tortillas on a flat surface and divide mushrooms, jalapeño, green onion, and cheese between them, arranging on one half of each tortilla; fold in half to close. (Reserve skillet for the next step.)
Wipe the skillet clean with paper towels and return to medium-high heat.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Place assembled quesadillas in the skillet and cook, flipping halfway through, until golden on both sides, 5-6 minutes. Remove to a plate.
Meanwhile, using a clean cutting board, quarter, core, and medium dice apple; add to the bowl with the dressing.
Trim, peel, and medium dice kiwis; add to the bowl, along with the blueberries, and stir to combine the fruit salad.
Cut each quesadilla into wedges and divide between plates. Serve with fruit salad on the side and enjoy!

name: Mushroom & Olive Stuffed Pizza Burgers with Lemon-Artichoke Salad
ingredients: ½ (6 oz) jar artichoke hearts, marinated
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and mince garlic; transfer to a medium bowl.
Juice lemon into the bowl with the garlic. Add oil, Dijon, salt, and pepper; whisk to combine the dressing.
Drain and thinly slice artichoke hearts. Add to the bowl with the dressing, toss to coat, and set aside.
Mince olives and mushrooms; place both in another medium bowl.
Add beef and spices to the bowl with the olives; mix with your hands until well to combined. Form into two, 1-inch thick patties, and place on a plate. Set aside.
Preheat a grill pan, outdoor grill, or regular skillet over medium-high heat.
Meanwhile, cut tomato into thick slices and season both sides with salt and basil.
Once the grill pan is hot, coat with oil. Add tomatoes and grill until lightly charred, about 1 minute per side. Transfer to a plate.
Meanwhile, slice cheese.

Place burger patties on the pan and grill, undisturbed, for 5 minutes. Flip patties and top with cheese and grilled tomatoes; continue to grill until cooked through, 5 minutes more. Transfer to the plate used for the tomatoes.
Meanwhile, chop or tear romaine leaves into bite-sized pieces; add to the bowl with the artichokes and toss to combine the salad.
If desired, place buns, cut-side down, on the grill pan to toast, 1-2 minutes.
Assemble pizza burgers and divide between plates. Serve with salad on the side and enjoy.

name: Mushroom, Onion & Mozzarella Frittata with Lemony Arugula
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the arugula if it came pre-washed.)
Peel and small dice onion; peel and mince garlic. Transfer both to a medium bowl.
Thinly slice the mushrooms.
Preheat an ovenproof skillet over medium heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add onion and garlic to the skillet and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 3 minutes. Reserve bowl for later.
Increase heat to medium-high and add mushrooms; season with salt and thyme. Cook, stirring occasionally, until mushrooms are softened and liquid has evaporated, about 7 minutes.
Meanwhile, roughly grate the cheese.
Combine eggs, half the cheese, salt, and pepper in the reserved bowl; whisk to combine.
Preheat oven to broil on high.

Spread the mushrooms evenly in the skillet. Reduce heat to medium-low and pour in the egg mixture. As eggs set around the edge of the skillet, gently lift cooked portions with a spatula to allow uncooked egg to flow underneath. Cook until bottom and sides are firm but the top is still runny, 5-7 minutes.
Sprinkle remaining cheese over the frittata. Place skillet in the oven until the top is set, 2-3 minutes.
Meanwhile, juice the lemon into a medium salad bowl. Add oil, maple syrup, salt, and pepper; whisk to combine the dressing. Add arugula and toss to combine the salad.
To serve, cut frittata into wedges and place on plates; top with arugula and enjoy!

name: Mushroom Sandwich with Avocado-Mayo Spread, Arugula, Tomato & Carrot
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the arugula if it came pre-washed.)
Place oil, soy sauce, vinegar, maple syrup, paprika, and pepper in a small bowl. Whisk to combine the marinade.
Remove mushroom stems and carefully scrape out the gills. Transfer to a baking sheet pan, drizzle with marinade, and turn to coat. (Reserve bowl for later use.)
Place mushrooms in the oven and roast until tender, 10-12 minutes. Remove from oven and set aside.
Meanwhile, halve and pit the avocado. Slice thinly while still in skin, then scoop out into the reserved bowl.
Add nutritional yeast, mayo, and spices to the bowl with the avocado; mash with a potato masher or fork until smooth. Set avocado mayo aside.
Slice tomato. Peel, trim, and coarsely grate the carrot. Transfer both to a plate and set aside.
Toast bread if desired.
Slice mushrooms into strips.
Place bread slices on a flat surface and spread evenly with avocado mayo. Top half the slices with mushrooms, tomato, carrot, and arugula. Cover sandwiches with remaining bread slices.
To serve, divide sandwiches between plates and enjoy!

name: Naked Wonton Soup with Bok Choy & Green Onions
ingredients: 28 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Pour broth, oil, and sauces into a large pot and heat over medium-high.
Peel and mince garlic. Peel and mince or grate ginger. Add half of each to the pot and transfer the rest to a medium bowl.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves. Transfer half to the medium bowl and set the other half aside in a small bowl.
Trim and finely chop green onions. Add half to the medium bowl and half to the small bowl.
Add pork, egg, sauces, and pepper to the medium bowl and mix with your hands until well combined.
Using a tablespoon measure, form the pork mixture into rounded meatballs and place on a plate.
Once the broth begins to boil, turn down to a simmer. Carefully add the meatballs (a few at a time, to avoid splashing) to the pot. Simmer until pork is cooked through, 5-6 minutes.
Meanwhile, trim bok choy and slice in half lengthwise. Add to the soup along with the remaining cilantro and green onion.
Return soup to a simmer and cook until bok choy is tender, 4-5 minutes more.
To serve, divide soup between bowls and enjoy!

name: Napa Cabbage, Pork & Bell Pepper Stir Fry
instructions: In a small bowl, combine and whisk together water, soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, and cornstarch.
Thinly slice the pork chops crosswise into strips; transfer to a medium bowl.
Pour ½ of the sauce over the pork; toss to coat and set aside.
Wash and dry the cutting board, knife, and fresh produce.
Halve the cabbage lengthwise and cut out the core; chop crosswise into bite-sized pieces (about 1-inch-wide). Transfer to a large bowl.
Cut the bell pepper into 4 wedges lengthwise, then remove and discard the seeds. Thinly slice into strips lengthwise and add to the bowl of cabbage.
Trim and discard the ends of the green onions; chop the onions into ¼-inch pieces. Separate the white parts from the greens and transfer to two small bowls.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, peel and mince or grate the ginger; add to the white parts of the green onions.
Peel and mince the garlic; add to the onions and ginger.
Add coconut oil to the skillet and swirl to coat the bottom.
Place the pork strips in the skillet; cook until browned, 1 to 2 minutes per side. Once done, transfer to a plate.
Once the pork has been transferred, add more coconut oil to the skillet.
Add the ginger, garlic, and white parts of green onions; cook until fragrant, 15 to 30 seconds.
Add the bell pepper and cabbage to the skillet. Cook, stirring regularly, until the vegetables are tender-crisp and lightly browned, 3 to 4 minutes.

Add the pork (along with any juices), remaining sauce, and ½ of the remaining green onions (save the rest for garnishing) to the skillet; stir to combine and cook until the sauce is slightly thickened, 1 to 2 minutes.
Divide the stir fry between bowls and sprinkle with the remaining green onions. Enjoy!

name: New Potato, Asparagus & Egg Salad with Lemon-Mustard Vinaigrette
instructions: Heat the oven to 450°F and position rack in the center.
Place the eggs in a small saucepan and fill with enough water to cover the eggs by about 1 inch. Cover the saucepan and bring to a full rolling boil over high heat.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Cut the potatoes lengthwise into 4 wedges and transfer to a baking sheet.
Snap or cut off and discard the woody ends of the asparagus; cut the spears into 1-inch pieces and add to the potatoes.
Drizzle the potatoes and asparagus with olive oil and season with salt and pepper; toss to coat, then spread out in an even layer.
Place the sheet in the oven and roast until the vegetables are tender, 10 to 15 minutes. Once done, remove from the oven.

Once the water in the saucepan in boiling, remove the pan from the heat, cover, and let it sit for 8 minutes. Drain and place the saucepan under cold running water for 1 to 2 minutes to allow the eggs to cool. Alternatively, add ice to the saucepan.
Juice the lemon into a large bowl, then add olive oil, Dijon, salt, and pepper; whisk together. Set aside.
Peel, halve lengthwise, then thinly slice the shallot; add to the bowl.
Measure out the almonds and add to the bowl.
Measure out the capers and add to the bowl.
Transfer the roasted vegetables to the bowl and toss to coat.
Peel and quarter the eggs lengthwise.
To serve, divide the salad between plates and place the egg wedges overtop. Enjoy!

name: New York Strip Steak with Bell Pepper & Creamed Spinach
ingredients: ¾ lb striploin (New York strip) steak
instructions: Fill a large pot about halfway with hot water (from the tap), cover, and bring to a boil.
While the water is heating, finely grate Parmesan; cut cream cheese into small pieces. Place both in a medium bowl and set aside.
Peel, halve, and small dice onion. Peel and mince garlic.
Wash the spinach (skip this step if it came pre-washed).
Once the water in the pot is boiling, uncover, add salt and spinach, and stir until wilted, about 30 seconds. Drain in a colander and rinse with cold water to cool. (Reserve pot for next step.)
Return pot to medium heat. Once the pot is hot, add butter and swirl to coat the bottom. Add onion, garlic, salt, and pepper to the pot; cook, stirring occasionally, until onion is soft, 3-4 minutes.
Meanwhile, using your hands, squeeze as much water from the spinach as you can. Add spinach to the bowl with the Parmesan and cream cheese.
Once the onion is soft, add Parmesan, cream cheese, spinach, and milk to the pot. Cook, stirring frequently, until cheeses melt and combine, 2-3 minutes. Remove from heat and cover to keep warm.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the steak dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with salt and pepper on both sides.

Once the skillet is hot, add butter and swirl to coat the bottom. Add steak to the skillet and cook until desired doneness, 2-5 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate and loosely cover with aluminum foil. (Reserve skillet for later use.)
Meanwhile, wash and dry bell pepper; trim, seed, and slice into thin strips.
Return skillet to medium heat; add more butter and swirl to coat the bottom. Add bell pepper and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, 4-5 minutes.
While the pepper is cooking, reheat the spinach, if necessary. (Return the pot to low heat and cook, stirring occasionally, until warmed through, 2-3 minutes.)
Thinly slice steak against the grain.
Divide steak between plates and top with peppers; serve with spinach on the side. Enjoy!

name: New York Strip Steak with Roasted Asparagus & New Potato Salad
ingredients: ¾ lb striploin (New York strip) steak
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F and position rack in the center. Place a baking sheet in the oven to warm up.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Cut the potatoes into ¼-inch-thick slices. Remove the baking sheet from the oven and add the potatoes.
Snap or cut off and discard the woody ends of the asparagus; cut the spears into 2-inch pieces. Add to the potatoes.
Drizzle the potatoes and asparagus with olive oil and season with salt and pepper; toss to coat, then spread out in an even layer.
Place the sheet in the oven and roast until the vegetables are tender, 12 to 15 minutes. Once done, remove from the oven.
Preheat a grill pan or skillet over medium-high heat.
Place the steak on a plate and season with salt and pepper.
Juice the lemon into a large bowl, then add olive oil, Dijon, salt, and pepper; whisk together. Set aside.
Coat the grill pan or skillet with coconut oil.
Place the steak in the grill pan or skillet; cook until desired doneness, 2 to 5 minutes per side. Once done, transfer to a plate and loosely cover with foil.
Chop the chives into ¼-inch pieces; transfer to the bowl with the dressing.
Transfer the roasted vegetables to the bowl with the dressing and toss to coat.
To serve, divide the steak and salad between plates. Enjoy!

name: NY Steak with Roasted Fennel, Grape, Walnut, Parmesan & Arugula Salad
ingredients: ¾ lb striploin (New York strip) steak
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the arugula if it came pre-washed.)
Trim off root end and stalks of the fennel, leaving only the white bulb. Halve fennel bulb lengthwise, then slice crosswise into thin half-moons. Transfer to a baking sheet pan.
Add grapes to the baking sheet with the fennel; drizzle with oil and season with spices. Stir to combine and spread out in an even layer.

Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated); roast, stirring halfway through, until fennel and grapes are lightly browned and tender, about 20 minutes. Remove from oven and set aside to cool, about 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the steak dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with salt and pepper on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add steak and cook until desired doneness, 2-5 minutes per side. Transfer to a clean plate and set aside to rest, about 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel and mince shallot. Place in a medium bowl along with additional oil, vinegar, Dijon, salt, and pepper. Whisk to combine the dressing.
Using a peeler, shave Parmesan into curls and add to the bowl with the dressing.
Roughly chop walnuts and add to the bowl.
Transfer cooled fennel and grapes to the bowl, along with arugula, and toss to combine the salad.
Thinly slice steak against the grain.
To serve, divide steak and salad between plates or bowls. Enjoy!

name: Olive Chicken with Roasted Onions, Bell Peppers & Artichokes over Rice
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add broth and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Cook rice until liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel and medium dice onion. Peel and thinly slice garlic. Transfer both to a medium bowl.
Wash, dry, seed, and medium dice bell pepper; add to the bowl with the onion and garlic.
Drain artichokes and add to the bowl.
Wash, dry, and juice lemon into the bowl. Add oil and spices, then toss to combine.
Transfer veggies to a baking sheet pan and spread out in a single layer. (Reserve bowl for next step.)
Mince olives and place in the reserved bowl; add oil and stir to combine the olive mixture.
Season both sides of the chicken with salt and pepper; nestle chicken in the veggies on the baking sheet. Spoon olive mixture over the chicken.
Place baking sheet in the oven and roast until chicken is cooked through and veggies are tender, about 20 minutes.
To serve, divide rice, roasted veggies, and chicken between plates. Enjoy!

name: One-Pan Cheesy Cauliflower & Broccoli Chicken
ingredients: ¾ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
4 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Cut chicken into bite-sized pieces.
Preheat a large skillet over medium heat.
Peel and small dice the onion.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add the chicken, onion, paprika, salt, and pepper to the skillet. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is cooked through, 5-7 minutes.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Cut the cauliflower into quarters, then trim off and discard the leaves and thick stem. Using a box grater or food processor, coarsely grate the cauliflower and transfer to a large bowl.
Separate broccoli into bite-sized florets and cut stems into smaller pieces. Add to bowl with the cauliflower.
Add the cauliflower, broccoli, and broth to the skillet and cover. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are tender, 5-7 minutes.
Coarsely grate the cheddar.
Once the vegetables are tender, remove skillet from the heat. Add cheese, yogurt, salt, and pepper; stir until smooth and creamy.
To serve, divide the chicken and vegetables between bowls. Enjoy!

name: One-Pot Creamy Taco Pasta with Turkey & Cheddar
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Seed and small dice the bell pepper.
Heat a large pot over medium heat.
Peel and small dice onion. Peel and mince garlic.

Once the pot is hot, add the oil, bell pepper, onion, garlic, and ground turkey. Break apart the turkey with a spoon until crumbly. Stirring occasionally, cook until turkey is cooked through and vegetables are tender, 5-7 minutes.

Add the pasta, tomatoes, water, and spices to the pot. Stir and bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce heat to medium-low and cook, stirring occasionally until pasta is cooked and most of the water is absorbed, 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, coarsely grate the cheddar.
Shave the cilantro leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves.
Once the pasta is done, remove from heat. If more than ¼ cup of liquid is remaining in the pot, carefully strain off excess liquid using a colander.
Add cheese, yogurt, and half of the cilantro to the pot with the pasta and stir until cheese is melted and creamy.
To serve, divide pasta between bowls. Garnish with remaining cilantro. Enjoy!

name: One-Pot Creamy Zucchini & Mushroom Pasta
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Add dried spaghetti to a large pot, off the heat, breaking noodles in half.
Remove the stems of the portobello mushrooms. Using a spoon, carefully scrape out the gills, making sure not to damage the rim of the mushrooms. Dice mushrooms into ½-inch cubes and add to the pot.
Trim and discard the ends of the zucchini; small dice the zucchini into ½-inch cubes and add to the pot.
Peel and mince or press the garlic; add to pot.
Remove the stem ends of the green onions. Slice in ¼-inch pieces and add to pot.
Slide the thyme leaves off the stems; discard the stems, add to the pot. Add butter and season everything with salt and pepper.
Add enough water to the pot just to cover noodles. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce heat to medium; water should remain at a low boil for the entire cooking process.

Ensure pasta is mostly submerged in cooking liquid while cooking. Stirring frequently, simmer, uncovered, until pasta is cooked through, vegetables have softened and liquid has reduced. About 8-10 minutes.
Finely grate Parmesan.
When pasta is done cooking drain any excess liquid from the pot using a colander.
Return pasta and veggies to the pot. Stir in heavy cream and Parmesan. Serve immediately. Enjoy!

name: Open-Faced Curried Tofu Salad Sandwiches with Lettuce & Cucumber
instructions: Cut tofu in half along the long side. Sandwich tofu between clean towels or paper towels and place on a baking sheet pan. Place a cutting board with something heavy on top and set aside to press out excess water.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Place mayo, nutritional yeast, Dijon, vinegar, and spices in a medium bowl; stir to combine the creamy dressing.
Crumble tofu with your fingers into the bowl with the dressing; using a fork, mash to combine the tofu mixture.
Peel, trim, and coarsely grate carrot; add to the bowl with the tofu mixture.
Trim and small dice celery; add to the bowl.
Trim, seed, and small dice bell pepper; add to the bowl. Stir to combine the tofu salad and set aside.
Preheat oven to broil on high and position rack under the broiler.
Peel and mince garlic; place in a small bowl along with oil and salt. Stir to combine the garlic oil.
Arrange bread on the baking sheet and drizzle with garlic oil. Place in the oven and broil until golden brown and toasted, 1-2 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, trim and slice cucumber crosswise into thin rounds.
Separate lettuce into leaves.
To serve, divide toast between plates; top with lettuce, tofu salad, and cucumber slices. Season cucumber with salt and pepper. Enjoy!

name: Open-Faced Muffuletta Sandwiches with Tapenade & Tomato Cucumber Salad
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Shave leaves off the stems of the parsley; discard the stems and mince the leaves. Place in a small bowl.
Finely chop the olives and sun-dried tomatoes; add to the bowl with the parsley.
Peel and mince garlic; add to the bowl with the olives along with oil and spices. Stir to combine the tapenade.
Add vinegar, oil, maple syrup, salt, and pepper to a medium bowl; whisk to combine the dressing.
Trim off the ends of the cucumber; slice crosswise into thin rounds. Add to the salad bowl with the dressing.
Halve the tomatoes and add to the salad bowl; stir to combine.
Trim and thinly slice the bell pepper into rounds.
Thinly slice cheese.
In a small bowl combine mayonnaise and vinegar; stir to combine.
Spread mayo over the bread and layer with cheese, prosciutto, bell pepper, and tapenade.
To serve, divide salad and sandwiches between plates. Enjoy!

name: Open-Faced Pesto Tofu Salad Sandwich with Tomato & Mixed Greens
ingredients: ½ (5 oz) pkg spring mix (mixed greens)
instructions: Cut tofu in half along the long side. Sandwich tofu between clean towels or paper towels and place on a baking sheet pan. Place a cutting board with something heavy on top and set aside to press out excess water.
Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the mixed greens if they came pre-washed.)
Place mayo, nutritional yeast, and spices in a medium bowl; whisk to combine the creamy dressing.
Finely chop pine nuts and add to the bowl with the creamy dressing.
Pick basil leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl.
Crumble tofu with your fingers into the bowl; using a fork, mash to combine the tofu salad. Set aside.
Preheat oven to broil on high and position rack under the broiler.
Slice tomatoes into rounds.
Arrange bread on a baking sheet. Place in the oven and broil until bread is golden brown and toasted, 1-2 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, place oil, vinegar, sugar, salt, and pepper in another medium bowl. Whisk to combine the vinaigrette.
Add mixed greens to the bowl with the vinaigrette and toss to coat.
To serve, divide toast between plates; top with dressed greens, tofu salad, and tomato slices. Season tomatoes with salt and pepper. Enjoy!

name: Open-faced Vietnamese Fried Egg Banh Mi with Mango & Romaine Salad
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Place vinegar, water, sugar, and salt in a small saucepan; stir to combine. Bring the pickling liquid to a boil over high heat.
Meanwhile, peel, trim, and cut carrot into thin matchsticks. Trim and thinly slice radishes.
Once the pickling liquid has come to a boil, add carrots and radishes; stir to combine, remove from heat, and set aside to cool.
Peel and mince garlic. Place half the garlic in a small bowl (reserving the rest for the next step); add mayo and stir to combine the garlic aioli. Set aside.
Juice lime into a medium bowl; add remaining garlic, oil, sugar, fish sauce, and pepper. Whisk to combine the salad dressing.
Peel mango and slice flesh away from the pit, starting with the flat sides. Roughly chop and add to the bowl with the dressing; set aside.
Trim and slice cucumber crosswise into thin rounds. Transfer to a plate.

Thinly slice the jalapeño pepper into rounds; add to the plate with the cucumber. (Be careful, with jalapeños, do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing).
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add half to the bowl with the mango; place the other half on the plate with the veggies. Set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Gently crack eggs into the skillet and cook until the tops of the whites are set but the yolks are still runny, about 4 minutes. Remove from heat.
While the eggs are cooking, chop or tear romaine into bite-sized pieces and add to the bowl with the mango and cilantro. Toss to combine the salad.
Split rolls in half and toast, cut-side down, in another skillet over medium-high heat or in a toaster (optional).

Divide toasted rolls between plates; spread each half with a layer of garlic aioli, then top with cucumber, pickled carrots and radish, eggs, jalapeños, and cilantro. Drizzle with fish sauce and season with pepper. Serve with salad on the side and enjoy!

name: Orange-Glazed Chicken Thighs with Roasted Parmesan Cauliflower
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Wash, dry, and separate cauliflower into bite-sized florets. Transfer to a sheet pan.
Peel and mince garlic. Add ½ of the garlic (save the rest for the sauce), lemon juice, oil, salt, and pepper to cauliflower; toss to coat.
Place the cauliflower in the oven and roast until it is tender and browned on the bottom, 15-20 minutes.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Coat bottom of skillet with oil. Add chicken and cook until browned, 2-3 minutes per side.
Wash and halve orange. Juice ½ into a small bowl and slice the other ½ into wedges. Add honey, vinegar, and remaining garlic to bowl and mix.
Pour sauce over top chicken and add orange wedges. Cook until sauce thickens, 4-5 minutes. Flip chicken a few times to evenly coat in sauce.
Grate ⅛ cup Parmesan.
Remove cauliflower from oven, sprinkle with Parmesan, and toss to coat.
To serve, place chicken, orange slices, and cauliflower on a plate. Enjoy!

name: Orange Glazed Pork Chops with Almond Green Beans
instructions: Halve orange. Grate zest from 1 half into a medium bowl, then juice the half into the same bowl. Cut other half into wedges.
Peel and mince garlic. Add ½ of the garlic (save the rest for the beans), honey, salt, and pepper to bowl and mix.
Preheat broiler and place rack about 6 inches from the top.
Wash rosemary and add to bowl with marinade.
Add pork chops to marinade and turn to coat.
Place orange wedges in marinade.
Lightly coat a baking dish with olive oil. Place pork chops and orange wedges in dish, leaving rosemary in the marinade. Spoon ½ of the marinade over top the pork.

Place dish in the oven and broil until pork is golden on top, 7-9 minutes. Then flip pork and orange wedges, spoon remaining marinade over top pork, and add rosemary sprigs to the dish. Return to oven and broil until pork is cooked through, 7-9 minutes more.
Fill a medium saucepan halfway with water, cover, and bring to a boil.
Wash green beans and trim ends.
Add salt and green beans to boiling water. Cook until bright green and tender-crisp, 2-3 minutes. Drain in a colander and rinse under cold water. Transfer to a medium bowl.
Add remaining garlic, lemon juice, olive oil, almonds, salt, and pepper to green beans; toss.
Serve pork, orange wedges, and green beans on a plate and enjoy!

name: Orange Glazed Salmon with Cranberry Brussels Sprouts & Sweet Potatoes
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Grate zest from the orange. (Reserve orange for later use.)
Measure out and roughly chop the cranberries.
In a medium bowl, combine vinegar, honey, olive oil, salt, pepper, cranberries, and half of the orange zest.
Remove the outer layer of leaves from the Brussels sprouts, then trim off and discard the stem ends. Halve the sprouts lengthwise and add to vinegar mixture; toss until well coated.
Transfer Brussels sprouts to one half of a baking sheet pan and spread out in an even layer. (Reserve bowl for the next step.)

Peel and cut the sweet potatoes into ½-inch cubes; place in the reserved bowl. Toss with olive oil, salt, and pepper. Transfer to the other half of the baking sheet with the Brussels sprouts and spread out in an even layer.
Place baking sheet in the oven and roast, tossing halfway through, until veggies are tender, about 20 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, halve the orange. Juice half of the orange and slice the other half into rings.
Combine orange juice with remaining zest, honey, salt, and pepper.

Line a second sheet pan with aluminum foil. Place the salmon fillets, skin-side down, in the middle of the sheet pan. Drizzle the orange juice mixture over the salmon and top with slices of orange. Place in the oven and bake until salmon is cooked through, 12-14 minutes.
To serve, divide salmon and roasted veggies between plates, spoon warm orange sauce over top. Enjoy!

name: Orange-Spiced Chicken with Snap Peas, Carrots, Couscous & Peanuts
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
½ (8 oz) pkg sugar snap peas
instructions: In a small saucepan, bring broth to a boil. Remove from heat, add couscous, and stir; cover and let stand for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the chicken dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with salt and pepper on both sides.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add chicken to the skillet; cook, turning once, until golden brown on each side, 6-7 minutes (chicken will not be cooked through all the way).
Meanwhile, zest and juice orange into a small bowl.
Peel and mince garlic; add to the bowl with the orange juice.
Add water, sugar, soy sauce, ketchup, vinegar, and spices to the bowl; whisk to combine the sauce and set aside.
Peel, trim, and thinly slice carrots. Add carrots and snap peas to the skillet with the chicken.

Add sauce to the skillet and bring to a boil over high heat (reserve bowl for later use). Reduce heat and simmer, turning thighs occasionally, until chicken is cooked through and veggies are tender, about 10 minutes.
While the chicken cooks, roughly chop peanuts.
Trim green onions and cut into ¼-inch pieces.

In the reserved bowl, make a slurry by whisking water with cornstarch until smooth. Add to the skillet in a steady stream, while stirring constantly; continue to simmer, until sauce thickens, about 1 minute. Remove from heat.
To serve, divide chicken-vegetable sauté and couscous between plates or bowls. Top with peanuts and green onions. Enjoy!

name: Orzo Pasta Skillet with Cottage Cheese, Zucchini, Snap Peas & Basil
ingredients: 16 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
½ (8 oz) pkg sugar snap peas
instructions: Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, peel, halve, and small dice onion.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add onion and cook, stirring occasionally, until starting to soften, 2-3 minutes.

Add orzo, broth, and spices to the skillet; stir to combine and bring to a simmer. Once simmering, reduce heat to medium-low and cook, stirring occasionally, until liquid is mostly absorbed, about 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim and halve snap peas. Place in a medium bowl.
Trim and small dice zucchini. Add to the bowl with the snap peas.
Zest lemon into the bowl. Cut lemon into wedges and set aside for serving.
Pick basil leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and thinly slice into ribbons. Add half to the bowl. (Reserve remaining basil for serving.)
Place cottage cheese in a strainer and set strainer in a bowl to catch the excess liquid. Set aside to drain.
When the broth is mostly absorbed, add snap peas, zucchini, lemon zest, and basil to the skillet, then stir to combine. Return to a simmer and cook until veggies are tender, 3-4 minutes.
When the veggies are done, add cottage cheese to the skillet. Continue to cook, stirring frequently, until thickened, 2-3 minutes more. Remove from heat.
Divide orzo between plates or bowls, top with reserved basil, and drizzle with oil. Serve with lemon wedges for squeezing and enjoy!

name: Oven-Baked BBQ Chicken with Lime & Cilantro Slaw
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F and position a rack in the center. Line a sheet pan with aluminum foil (optional).
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and mince the garlic; transfer to a medium bowl.
Add ketchup, sugar, soy sauce, vinegar, and chili-garlic sauce to the bowl with the garlic and whisk together; add the chicken drumsticks and toss to coat.
Spread the ​chicken out in a single layer on the prepared sheet pan, setting aside any marinade remaining in the bowl. Place in the oven and roast for 15 minutes.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves.
Trim off and discard the ends of the green onions; cut the onions crosswise into ¼-inch pieces.
Zest and juice the lime into a medium bowl; add oil, honey, cilantro, green onion, salt, and pepper; whisk to combine the dressing.
Trim off and discard the root end of the cabbage; halve the cabbage lengthwise, then thinly slice crosswise into shreds. Add cabbage to the bowl with the dressing and toss to coat.
Remove the chicken from the oven, flip each drumstick, then spoon on the remaining marinade. Return chicken to the oven and bake until cooked through, about 15 minutes more.
To serve, divide slaw and chicken between plates. Enjoy!

name: Oven Roasted Chicken with Carrots, Cauliflower Rice & Green Harissa
ingredients: ¾ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F and position racks in the upper and lower thirds of the oven.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Cut the cauliflower head into quarters, then trim off and discard the leaves and thick stems. Using a box grater or food processor, coarsely grate the cauliflower and transfer to a baking dish.
In a medium bowl whisk together oil and spices to make a smooth paste. Add half of the spice paste to the baking dish with the cauliflower and stir to combine.
Pat dry the chicken breasts with paper towels and place in the bowl with the remaining spice paste; turn to coat.
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper and place the chicken on top.
Grate all of the zest from the lemon; add to a small bowl and set aside. Cut the lemon into wedges and add to the pan with the chicken.

Place the chicken on the upper rack of the oven and the cauliflower rice on the rack below. Bake until the cauliflower rice has softened and the chicken is golden brown and cooked through, about 20 minutes.

While the chicken and cauliflower cook, quarter the jalapeño pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs of the jalapeño with a spoon. Finely mince and add to the bowl with the lemon zest. (Be careful, with jalapeños, do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing).
Shave the cilantro leaves off the stems; discard the stems and finely mince the leaves. Peel and mince garlic.
To make the harissa, add cilantro, garlic, olive oil, and spices to the bowl with the jalapeno and zest; stir to combine.
Peel the carrots; then using the peeler, run it along the carrot to make long, noodle-like strips; add carrot strips to a medium bowl with 1 tbsp of the harissa; toss to coat.
When the chicken is done, slice into strips.
To serve, divide chicken, crisp carrots, and cauliflower rice between plates. Drizzle remaining harissa over the chicken and serve with warm lemon wedges. Enjoy!

name: Pan-Fried Chicken Breast with Lemony Mushroom & Herb Rice
ingredients: ¾ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Preheat a sauté pan over medium heat.
While the pan heats up, trim off and discard the ends of the shallot; peel and mince the shallot.
Trim off and discard the root end of the garlic; peel and mince or press the garlic.
Once the pan is hot, add olive oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add the shallot and garlic to the pan; cook, stirring frequently, until softened, 3 to 4 minutes.
While the shallot and garlic cook, thinly slice the mushrooms lengthwise from cap to stem.
Add the mushrooms to the pan and season with salt and pepper; cook, stirring frequently, until the mushrooms are tender and the liquid has evaporated, 5 to 7 minutes.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the chicken breasts dry with paper towels and place on a plate; generously season with salt and pepper on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add olive oil and swirl to coat the bottom.

Carefully place the chicken breasts in the skillet; cook until the chicken is golden brown and cooked through (check doneness with a thermometer or cut into the chicken with a knife), 6 to 8 minutes per side. Once done, transfer the chicken to plate and tent with foil to keep warm.

Once the mushrooms are tender, add the rice and broth to the pan; stir and scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15-18 minutes.
While the chicken and rice cook, zest and juice the lemon; transfer to a small bowl.
Using a knife, shave the parsley leaves off the stems at a downward angle, working away from your body; discard the stems and finely chop the leaves. Add to the bowl with the lemon zest and juice.
Once the rice is cooked, add the lemon zest, juice, parsley, and olive oil; stir to combine.
To serve, divide the rice and chicken between plates. Enjoy!

name: Pan-Fried Chicken with Sautéed Sugar Snap Peas & Sweet Potato Mash
ingredients: ½ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
instructions: Fill a medium saucepan about halfway with water, cover, and bring to a boil.

Wash, peel, and medium dice the sweet potatoes; add to the saucepan. Once the water is boiling, cook until the potatoes are very tender when pierced with a fork, 10-15 minutes. Drain and return to saucepan.
Wash the snap peas and lemon. Cut the lemon into wedges. Peel and mince the garlic.
Heat a skillet over medium heat.
Slice chicken in half horizontally to form thin fillets. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Melt butter in the skillet. Add the minced garlic and cook until fragrant, 15-30 seconds. Add the chicken and cook until golden brown and cooked through, 3-4 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate.
Add more butter to the skillet, followed by the sugar snap peas. Cook, stirring occasionally, until bright green and tender-crisp, 2-3 minutes. Season with salt and pepper and remove from heat.
Add the remaining butter to the potatoes and season with salt and pepper. Mash with a potato masher (or a fork) until smooth.
Slice the chicken crosswise on an angle.
To serve, place the mashed potatoes, sautéed peas, and chicken on a plate. Garnish with the lemon wedges and enjoy!

name: Pan-Fried Chicken Thighs with Thai-Inspired Kale, Carrot & Peanut Salad
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the chicken thighs dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add coconut oil and swirl to coat the bottom.

Carefully place the chicken thighs in the skillet; sear on both sides until golden brown, 2 to 3 minutes per side. Then, reduce the heat to medium and continue to cook until they are cooked through, 3 to 5 minutes total. Once done, transfer to a plate and cover with foil to keep warm.
Cut out and discard the kale stems; halve the leaves lengthwise, then chop crosswise into ¼-inch-thick strips. Transfer to a large salad bowl.
Peel the carrot, then trim off the ends; discard the peels and trimmings. Using a box grater, coarsely grate the carrot. Add to the salad bowl.
Trim off and discard the ends of the green onions; cut the onions crosswise into ¼-inch pieces at an angle. Add to the salad bowl.
Juice the lime and transfer to a small bowl.
To the lime juice, add peanut butter, water, soy sauce, honey, sesame oil, and crushed red pepper; whisk together.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss to coat.
To serve, divide the chicken thighs and salad between plates; sprinkle the salad with sesame seeds. Enjoy!

name: Pan-Fried Cod with Asparagus & Carrot Purée
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel the carrots, then trim off the ends; discard the peels and trimmings. Cut the carrots crosswise into 1-inch chunks and transfer to a small saucepan.
Cover the carrots with hot water (from the tap) by about 1 inch; bring to a boil over high heat.
Snap or cut off and discard the woody ends of the asparagus; cut the spears into 2-inch pieces at an angle and transfer to a bowl.

Once the water in the saucepan is boiling, reduce the heat slightly and simmer until the carrots are tender when pierced with a knife, 15 to 20 minutes. Once the carrots are cooked, reserve ½ cup of cooking water and drain the carrots in a colander. Return the carrots to the saucepan.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the cod dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add coconut oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Carefully place the cod in the skillet; cook until it is opaque throughout and flakes easily, 2 to 4 minutes per side (depending on thickness). Once done, transfer to a plate.
Trim off and discard the root end of the garlic; peel and mince or press the garlic.

Once the cod has been transferred, add more coconut oil to the skillet, then add the asparagus and season with salt and pepper. Cook the asparagus, stirring occasionally, until bright green and tender-crisp, 3 to 5 minutes. Once done, remove the skillet from the heat.

To the carrots, add ½ of the reserved cooked water, garlic, butter, salt, and pepper; mash with a potato masher or purée with a hand blender until smooth. Add more cooking water to thin out the mash if needed.
To serve, divide the carrot purée between plates, then top with the asparagus and cod. Enjoy!

name: Pan-Fried Cod, Citrus Fruit, Avocado & Arugula Salad with Rice
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add broth and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Cook rice until liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove rice from the heat and spread it out on a baking sheet pan to cool slightly, about 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the arugula if it came pre-washed.)
Cut orange in half; zest and juice one half into a medium bowl. (Set remaining orange aside for later use.)
Juice lime into the bowl with the orange zest and juice. Add oil, honey, salt, and crushed red pepper; whisk to combine the dressing.
Peel and thinly slice shallot into rings; peel and mince garlic. Add both to the bowl with the dressing.
Cut off skin and white pith from the remaining orange and the grapefruit; slice into thin rounds. Add both to the bowl and set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the cod dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with salt and pepper on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add fish and pan-fry until golden brown and cooked through, 3-4 minutes per side. Remove from heat.
Meanwhile, trim, halve, and slice cucumber crosswise into thin half-moons; add to the bowl with the dressing and citrus fruit.
Halve and pit avocado; scoop out with a spoon and medium dice the flesh. Add to the bowl.
Once the cod is done, use your fingers to flake the fish into bite-sized pieces; add to the bowl.
Add arugula to the bowl and gently toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide cooled rice between bowls and top with cod and citrus salad. Enjoy!

name: Pan-Fried Pork Chops with Apple & Kale Sauté
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Quarter the apple lengthwise, then cut out the core and stem from each section; cut each quarter lengthwise into 4 thin wedges and transfer to a small bowl.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the pork chops dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add coconut oil and swirl to coat the bottom.

Place the pork chops in the skillet and sear until they develop a nice crust, 2 to 3 minutes per side. Then, reduce the heat to medium and cook the chops, flipping occasionally, until they are cooked through (test using a thermometer or cut into a chop with a knife), another 3 to 5 minutes. Once done, transfer the pork to a plate.
While the pork chops cook, trim off and discard the ends of the shallot; peel and halve the shallot lengthwise, then thinly slice crosswise into half-rounds and leave on cutting board.
Once the pork has been transferred, add the shallot to the skillet; cook, stirring frequently, until softened, 2 to 3 minutes.
Add the apple slices to the skillet; cook, stirring occasionally, until they are lightly browned and just tender, 3 to 4 minutes.
While the apples cook, cut out and discard the stems from each kale leaf; chop leaves crosswise into 1-inch strips.
Add the kale and ¼ cup of water to the skillet; cook, stirring frequently, until it is wilted, 3 to 4 minutes. Once done, remove from the heat.
Drizzle the kale with apple cider vinegar and season with salt and pepper.
To serve, divide the pork chops and sauté between plates. Add a dollop of mustard on the side for the pork if desired. Enjoy!

name: Pan-Fried Pork Chops with Basil Peach Salsa & Green Beans
instructions: Fill a medium saucepan about halfway with water, cover, and bring to a boil.
Place the pork chops on a plate, rub both sides with chili powder, and season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Wash the green beans, then trim off and discard the ends.
Once the water in the saucepan is boiling, add the green beans and cook until bright green and tender-crisp, 2-3 minutes. Drain in a colander and rinse under cold water. Set aside to drain further.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Add coconut oil to the skillet and swirl to coat the bottom. Add the pork chops and cook until browned and cooked through, 3-4 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate and let them rest for 2-3 minutes.
Peel and mince or press the garlic.

Once the chops have been removed, reduce the heat to medium and add more coconut oil to the skillet. Add the garlic and cook until fragrant, 15-30 seconds. Add the green beans and season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring frequently, for 2-3 minutes. Remove from heat.
Wash the peach, halve, core, and small dice; transfer to a medium bowl.
Peel and mince the shallot; add to the bowl.
Wash and dry the basil. Pick the leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl.
Drizzle lime juice over the salsa and season with salt and pepper. Mix well.
To serve, place pork chops on plates, spoon peach salsa over top, and add green beans to the side. Enjoy!

name: Pan-Fried Pork Chops with Maple-Roasted Acorn Squash
instructions: Preheat the oven to 450°F and place the rack in the center position. Place a baking sheet in the oven to warm up.

Wash and halve the squash lengthwise; trim off the ends, then scoop out the seeds and cut the halves crosswise into ¼-inch-thick slices. Remove the baking sheet from the oven and transfer the squash to it.
Drizzle the squash with olive oil and maple syrup and season with salt and pepper; toss to coat, then arrange in a single layer.
Place the squash in the oven and bake until it is tender, 18 to 20 minutes.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat dry the pork chops with paper towels and place on a plate; season generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add coconut oil and swirl to coat the bottom.

Place the pork chops in the skillet and sear until they develop a nice crust, 1 to 2 minutes per side. Then, reduce the heat to medium and cook the chops, flipping occasionally, until they are cooked through (test using a thermometer or cut into a chop with a knife), another 4 to 6 minutes.
To serve, arrange the squash slices and pork chop on a plate. Enjoy!

name: Pan-Fried Pork Chops with Roasted Broccoli & Sweet Potato Mash
instructions: Preheat the oven to 450°F and position rack in the centre. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Fill a medium saucepan about halfway with water, cover, and bring to a boil.

Wash, peel, and medium dice the sweet potatoes; add to the water in the saucepan. Once the water is boiling, cook the potatoes until tender when pierced with a fork, 8-10 minutes. Drain in a colander and return back to saucepan.
Wash the broccoli and cut into bite-sized florets; transfer to the baking sheet.
Peel and mince the garlic. Wash the lemon and grate the zest from it.
