Peel additional garlic and place in a blender.
Juice half of the lemon into the blender with the garlic (reserve the other half of the lemon for the salad dressing).
Drain and rinse chickpeas; add to the blender along with water, tahini, and spices. Blend on high until hummus is smooth; set aside.
Trim and small dice cucumber; small dice tomato. Place both in a medium bowl.
Shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl with the cucumber and tomato; stir to combine the veggie topping and set aside.
Juice remaining lemon into another medium bowl. Add oil, honey, and spices; whisk to combine the dressing. Add mixed greens and toss to combine the salad.
To assemble the "nachos," spoon hummus, garlic yogurt, and veggie topping over the pita chips. Sprinkle with feta.
To serve, divide "nachos" and salad between plates. Enjoy!

name: Poached Chicken Salad with Cranberries, Pistachios & Garlic Croutons
ingredients: ¾ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Holding a knife parallel to the cutting board, cut the chicken in half horizontally to form thin fillets.

Place chicken, salt, and pepper in a medium saucepan and cover with water by 1-inch; bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer until chicken is cooked through, 8-10 minutes. Transfer chicken to a plate to cool.
Using a clean cutting board, peel and mince garlic; transfer to a medium bowl. Add oil and spices, then whisk to combine.
Cut bread into bite-sized pieces and add to the bowl; toss to coat. Transfer to a baking sheet pan. Reserve bowl for later use.
Place croutons in the oven and cook, tossing halfway through, until golden and crisp, 6-8 minutes. Remove from oven and set aside to cool.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the mixed greens if they came pre-washed.)
Trim and medium dice celery; place in the reserved bowl.
Zest lemon into the bowl with the celery.
Roughly chop pistachios; add to the bowl along with yogurt, cranberries, and spices. Stir to combine and set aside.
Juice the lemon into another medium bowl. Add oil and whisk to combine the dressing.
Add mixed greens and croutons to the bowl with the dressing; toss to combine.
Using two forks, shred chicken and add to the bowl with the yogurt mixture. Mix well to combine.
To serve, place salad greens on a plate and top with chicken salad. Enjoy!

name: Poached Halibut with Roasted Bok Choy & Acorn Squash in Coconut Broth
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
½ (13.5 fl oz) can coconut milk
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Halve acorn squash lengthwise, trim off the ends, then scoop out the seeds. Cut into ½-inch thick wedges and place on a baking sheet pan.

Trim the bok choy ends and cut in half lengthwise; add to the baking sheet with the squash. Drizzle with oil and season with salt and pepper. Toss to coat, then spread the veggies out in a single layer.
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast, flipping veggies halfway through, until fork-tender, about 20 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, pat the halibut dry with paper towels and place, skin-side down, on a plate; season the top-side with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Peel and mince ginger and garlic.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, peel, halve, and thinly slice shallot into half-moons.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add ginger, garlic, shallot, and chili-garlic sauce; cook, stirring frequently, until starting to soften, 1-2 minutes.
Add broth, coconut milk, sugar, and fish sauce to the skillet. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce heat to a simmer.

Place halibut fillets, skin-side down, in the broth. Spoon some of the broth over the tops of the fillets, then cover the skillet; poach the fish until opaque and cooked through, about 5 minutes, depending on the thickness of each fillet. Remove from heat.
While the fish is cooking, cut lime into wedges.
Divide roasted veggies, halibut, and coconut broth between bowls. Serve with lime wedges and enjoy!

name: Poached Tofu with Scallion-Ginger Sauce, Noodles, Carrots & Bok Choy
instructions: Cut tofu in half along the short side to make 2 smaller "blocks." Place in a medium saucepan and cover with hot water (from the tap). Bring to a boil over high heat. Once boiling, reduce to a simmer and cook until tofu is warmed through, about 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, fill a large pot about halfway with hot water (from the tap), cover, and bring to a boil over high heat.
While the water comes to a boil, wash and dry the fresh produce.

Once the water in the pot is boiling, remove from heat. Carefully pour water into a medium, heat-proof bowl, and add rice noodles. Soak for 10 minutes (or prepare according to package instructions). Drain in a colander and set aside. (Reserve pot for later use.)
Meanwhile, peel and mince ginger and garlic. Place both in a small bowl.
Trim and cut green onions crosswise into thin pieces. Add to the bowl with the ginger and garlic along with soy sauce, oil, sugar, and crushed red pepper. Stir to combine the sauce and set aside.
Trim and separate bok choy into leaves. Place in a medium bowl.
Peel and trim carrots; run the peeler along each carrot to make long, noodle-like strips. Add to the bowl with the bok choy.
Return pot to medium-high heat. Once hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom; add bok choy, carrot, and soy sauce. Stir-fry until veggies are fork-tender, 3-4 minutes.
Add drained noodles to the pot and stir to combine. Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until warmed through, 1 minute more. Remove from heat.
To serve, divide noodles and veggies between bowls. Top with poached tofu and drizzle with sauce. Enjoy!

name: Polenta with Goat Cheese, Prosciutto, Swiss Chard & Sun-Dried Tomatoes
ingredients: 24 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: In a small saucepan, bring broth to a boil. Reduce heat to low and gradually add polenta in a thin steady stream, while whisking, until the polenta is incorporated; add salt. Cover and cook, stirring occasionally, until polenta is soft and the texture is creamy, 15-25 minutes.

Meanwhile, wash and dry chard; fold leaves in half lengthwise and slice off the stems. Cut leaves into bite-sized pieces and thinly slice the stems, keeping them separate. Place leaves in a medium bowl and stems in a small bowl.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat.
While the skillet heats up, peel and thinly slice garlic. Add to the bowl with the stems and set aside.
Once the skillet is hot, add prosciutto and cook until crispy, about 1 minute per side. Remove to a plate and set aside. (Reserve skillet for the next step.)

Return skillet to medium heat, add butter, and swirl to coat the bottom. Add chard stems, garlic, salt, and pepper to the skillet; cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 3 minutes. (Reserve bowl for later use.)
Meanwhile, roughly chop sun-dried tomatoes. Add to the skillet and stir to combine.

Add chard leaves to the skillet in handfuls, waiting for the leaves to wilt slightly before adding the next handful. Cook, stirring occasionally, until warmed through and tender, about 1 minute. Remove from heat.
Wash, dry, and pick basil leaves off the stems; roll up crosswise, and thinly slice into ribbons. Place in the reserved small bowl.
Crumble goat cheese into the bowl with the basil and stir to combine.
When the polenta is done, add butter, pepper, and half of both the basil and goat cheese to the pan, then stir to combine (reserve remaining basil and goat cheese for serving).
To serve, divide polenta and Swiss chard sauté between bowls. Crumble prosciutto over top, then sprinkle with reserved basil and goat cheese. Enjoy!

name: Pork Chop, Dijon Roasted Cabbage & Arugula-Pear Salad with Blue Cheese
ingredients: ½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled blue cheese
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the arugula if it came pre-washed.)
Place Dijon, oil, water, honey, salt, and pepper in a medium bowl; whisk to combine the Dijon sauce.

Halve cabbage lengthwise and cut out the core; slice crosswise into 1-inch thick wedges. Transfer to a baking sheet pan, then drizzle both sides of the cabbage with Dijon sauce. (Reserve bowl for later use.)
Place baking sheet in the oven and roast, gently flipping cabbage halfway through, until tender and golden around the edges, 18-20 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat pork chops dry with paper towels. Place on a plate and season both sides with salt and pepper.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add chops and pan-fry until golden brown and cooked through, 3-4 minutes per side. Remove to a clean plate, loosely cover with aluminum foil, and set aside.
While the chops are cooking, place oil, vinegar, Dijon, and salt in the reserved bowl; whisk to combine the dressing.
Peel, halve, and slice onion into thin half-moons; add to the bowl with the dressing and toss to combine.
Quarter, core, and thinly slice pear; add to the bowl.
Roughly chop walnuts and add to the bowl.
Just before serving, add arugula and blue cheese to the bowl; toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide roasted cabbage, chops, and salad between plates. Enjoy!

name: Pork Chop with Honey-Dijon Apples, Parsley Potatoes & Mixed Greens
ingredients: 4 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
½ (5 oz) pkg spring mix (mixed greens)
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the mixed greens if they came pre-washed.)

Halve potatoes, place in a medium saucepan, cover with hot water (from the tap), and bring to a boil. Once boiling, reduce heat to medium and simmer until potatoes can be easily pierced with a fork, 10-12 minutes. Drain and return to the saucepan; cover to keep warm.
Meanwhile, preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the pork chops dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with salt and pepper on both sides.

Once the skillet is hot, add butter and swirl to coat the bottom. Add chops and pan-fry until golden brown and cooked through, 3-4 minutes per side. Transfer to a clean plate and loosely cover with aluminum foil.
While the chops are cooking, peel, halve, and thinly slice onion into half-moons; peel and mince garlic. Place both in a medium bowl.
Quarter and core apple, then slice into ¼-inch thick wedges; add to the bowl with the onion and garlic.

When the chops are done, return the skillet (with cooking juices) to medium-low heat. Add onion, garlic, and apple; cook, stirring occasionally, until the onion and apple are soft, 4-5 minutes. (Reserve bowl for the next step.)
Meanwhile, place vinegar, mayo, Dijon, honey, salt, and pepper in the reserved bowl; whisk to combine the dressing.
Halve tomatoes lengthwise and add to the bowl with the dressing; set aside.
When the onion and apple are soft, add broth, Dijon, and honey to the skillet; bring to a simmer and cook, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened, 3-4 minutes. Remove from heat.
Meanwhile, shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves.
Return the saucepan with potatoes to low heat; add butter, parsley, and salt. Cook, stirring frequently, until butter and parsley coat the potatoes, 1-2 minutes. Remove from heat.
Add mixed greens to bowl with dressing and tomatoes; toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide pork chops, apple sauté, potatoes, and salad between plates. Enjoy!

name: Pork Chop with Jalapeño Basil Salsa & Strawberry-Tomato Arugula Salad
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the arugula if it came pre-washed.)
Juice lime into a small bowl.
Peel and mince garlic and shallot; add to the bowl with the lime juice along with oil, honey, and salt.

Quarter jalapeño pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon. Mince and add to the bowl. (Be careful with jalapeños; do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Pick basil leaves off the stems, discard stems, and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl and stir to combine the salsa; set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat pork chops dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with salt and pepper on both sides.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add chops and pan-fry until golden brown and cooked through, 3-4 minutes per side. Transfer chops to a clean plate and loosely cover with aluminum foil.
Meanwhile, place oil, vinegar, honey, salt, and pepper in a medium bowl. Whisk to combine the dressing.
Trim and quarter strawberries lengthwise; add to the bowl with the dressing.
Halve tomatoes; add to the bowl along with the arugula and toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide pork chops and salad between plates; spoon salsa over the chops and enjoy!

name: Pork Chop & Pinto Bean Salad (Cowboy Caviar) with Cilantro Dressing
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Drain and rinse beans; set aside to drain further.
Juice lime into a medium bowl. Add oil, honey, and spices; whisk to combine the dressing and set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the pork chops dry with paper towels and place on a plate. Season with spices on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add chops and pan-fry until golden brown and cooked through, 3-4 minutes per side. Transfer to a clean plate.
Meanwhile, peel and mince shallot; add to the bowl with the dressing.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl.

Quarter jalapeño pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon. Mince and add to the bowl. (Be careful with jalapeños; do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Trim, seed, and small dice bell pepper; add to the bowl.
Small dice tomato and add to the bowl.
Halve and pit avocado; scoop out with a spoon and small dice the flesh. Add to the bowl, along with the beans, and stir to combine the salad.
To serve, divide chops and bean salad between plates. Enjoy!

name: Pork Chop with Spiced Dates, Prosciutto, Green Beans & Sweet Potato
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.

Wash and dry sweet potato, then peel and large dice; place on a baking sheet pan, drizzle with oil, and season with spices. Toss to combine and spread out in an even layer on one half of the baking sheet.
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast until sweet potatoes start to soften, about 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel and mince garlic; mince dates. Place both in a small bowl along with oil and spices; stir to combine the date topping and set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the pork chops dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with salt and pepper on both sides.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom; add chops and cook until golden, about 2 minutes per side. Once golden, transfer to a clean plate (the pork will not be cooked all the way through). Reserve skillet with juices for later use.
Divide date topping between chops and layer each with two slices of prosciutto.

Remove sweet potatoes from the oven and toss; add layered pork chops to the other half of the baking sheet. Return baking sheet to the oven and roast until sweet potatoes are tender and chops are cooked through, 8-10 minutes more. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, wash, dry, and trim green beans.
Peel and mince additional garlic.

Return the skillet to medium-high heat, add more oil, and swirl to coat the bottom; add beans and salt. Stir-fry until lightly charred and fork-tender, 3-4 minutes. Add garlic and continue to cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant, about 30 seconds; remove from heat.
To serve, divide layered pork chops, sweet potatoes, and green beans between plates. Enjoy!

name: Pork Chops with Blackberry Sauce & Lemon Arugula Salad
instructions: Heat a grill pan, outdoor grill, or skillet over medium-high heat.
Wash blackberries.
Season pork generously with salt and pepper.
Coat grill or bottom of skillet with oil. Place pork on grill/skillet and cook until cooked through, 4-6 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate and loosely cover with foil.
Heat a small saucepan over medium heat.

Coat bottom of saucepan with oil. Add blackberries, vinegar, honey, and salt. Reduce heat to medium-low and, stirring occasionally, cook until sauce thickens and some of the berries collapse, 10-12 minutes.
Grate 1 tsp of lemon zest. In a medium bowl, prepare dressing by whisking together lemon zest and juice, olive oil, honey, salt, and pepper.
Wash and dry arugula. Add to bowl with dressing and toss to coat.
Shave or grate ⅛ cup of Parmesan.
To serve, place pork chops on a plate and spoon blackberry sauce over top. Add salad on the side and garnish with Parmesan and pine nuts. Enjoy!

name: Pork Chops with Brussels Sprouts, Apple & Almond Salad
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Place pork chops in a small baking dish. Season with salt and pepper.
In a small bowl, whisk together maple syrup, Dijon, and vinegar.

Spoon about ½ of the sauce over the pork chops. Place in the oven and bake for 10 minutes. Then flip pork, spoon remaining sauce over top, and continue to bake until pork is cooked through, another 10-15 minutes.
Peel and mince garlic. Wash brussels sprouts, trim root ends, and chop into shred-like pieces.
Heat a skillet over medium heat.

Coat bottom of skillet with oil. Add garlic and cook until fragrant, 15-30 seconds. Add brussels sprouts and, stirring occasionally, cook until softened, 2-3 minutes. Remove from heat and set aside to cool.
In a medium bowl, prepare dressing by whisking together lemon juice, olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Wash, core, and cut apple into thin medium pieces. Add to bowl with dressing.
Roughly chop almonds and add to bowl.
Add brussels sprouts to bowl and toss salad.
To serve, place pork chops and salad on a plate. Enjoy!

name: Pork Chops with Cherry Balsamic Sauce, Couscous & Green Beans
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Place couscous in a medium bowl.

Pour broth in a small saucepan, cover, and bring to a boil over high heat. Remove from heat, pour broth into the bowl with the couscous, and stir. Cover tightly with aluminum foil and let stand for 10 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Meanwhile, peel and mince shallot. Peel and mince garlic.
Return saucepan to medium heat. Once the saucepan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add shallot and garlic to the saucepan and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, 3-4 minutes.
Add cherries, vinegar, and salt to the saucepan. Cook, stirring occasionally, until cherries have softened and balsamic is slightly reduced, 8-10 minutes. Cover and remove from heat.
Meanwhile, preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Pat pork chops dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with salt and pepper on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Place chops in the skillet and cook, flipping once, until browned and cooked through, 6-7 minutes. Remove to a clean plate and cover with foil.
Meanwhile, wash, dry, and trim green beans.
Wipe the skillet clean with paper towels and return to medium heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add green beans and season with salt and pepper. Cook, tossing frequently, until bright green and tender-crisp, 4-5 minutes.
Slice pork chops against the grain.
To serve, divide couscous, green beans, and pork chops between plates. Top chops with cherry sauce and enjoy!

name: Pork Chops with Pears & Blue Cheese
ingredients: 4 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled blue cheese
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Quarter the pears lengthwise, then cut out the core and stem from each section; cut each quarter lengthwise into 4 thin wedges.
Trim off and discard the ends of the onion and remove the outer layer; halve lengthwise, then cut the halves into 4 wedges.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Halve the pork chops horizontally to form thin fillets; pat dry with paper towels and place on a plate. Season generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add coconut oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Place the pork fillets in the skillet; cook until golden brown, 3 to 4 minutes per side. Once done, transfer to a plate.
Once the pork has been transferred, reduce the heat to medium. Add the pears and onions to the skillet; cook, stirring frequently, until they are softened and lightly browned, 4 to 6 minutes.
Add broth to the skillet and scrape up any browned bits from the bottom.
Return the pork fillets to the skillet and arrange among the pears and onions.
Top the mixture with blue cheese and continue to cook until the pork is cooked through and the cheese begins to melt.
To serve, divide the pork and pear mixture between plates and spoon the pan sauce overtop. Enjoy!

name: Pork Chops with Sautéed Apples & Brussels Sprouts
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim off and discard the ends of the shallot; peel and small dice the shallot (cut into ¼-inch pieces). Transfer to a small bowl.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the pork chops dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add coconut oil and swirl to coat the bottom.

Place the pork chops in the skillet and sear until they develop a nice crust, 2 to 3 minutes per side. Then, reduce the heat to medium and cook the chops, flipping occasionally, until they are cooked through (test using a thermometer or cut into a chop with a knife), another 3 to 5 minutes. Once done, transfer the pork to a plate.
While the pork chops cook, trim off and discard the stems ends of the Brussels sprouts, then remove the outer layer of leaves; quarter the sprouts lengthwise.
Once the pork has been transferred, add the shallot to the skillet; cook, stirring frequently, until softened, 2 to 3 minutes.

Add the Brussels sprouts to the skillet; cook until they have a nice sear on one side, 4 to 6 minutes. Then, give them a stir and continue cooking until they are browned all over and tender on the inside, another 4 to 6 minutes.
While the Brussels sprouts cook, quarter the apple lengthwise, then cut out the core and stem from each section; large dice the apple (cut into ¾-inch cubes).
In the last few minutes of cooking time, add the apples to the Brussels sprouts; cook, stirring occasionally, until the apples are softened, 3 to 4 minutes.
Drizzle the sprouts and apples with apple cider vinegar and season with salt and pepper; toss to combine.
To serve, divide the pork chops and the sautéed Brussels sprouts and apples between plates. Add a dollop of Dijon to the side for dipping the pork if desired. Enjoy!

name: Pork Chops & Sweet Potato Mash with Citrus Baby Greens Salad
ingredients: 4 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
½ (5 oz) pkg spring mix (mixed greens)
instructions: Wash and medium dice sweet potatoes (without peeling). Place in a medium saucepan, cover with water, and bring to a boil. Cook until tender, 10-15 minutes.
Heat broiler and position rack about 6 inches from the top.
Place pork chops in a baking dish. Rub with olive oil and season with salt and pepper.
Place in the oven and broil until pork is cooked through, 7-9 minutes per side.
Wash and dry greens. Transfer to a medium bowl.

Slice off top and bottom from orange, then cut off the skin and white pith from the sides so you can see the orange flesh. Cut in between the membranes to release the segments and add to bowl with greens.
Add cranberries to bowl with greens and orange.
In a small bowl, prepare salad dressing by whisking together olive oil, vinegar, Dijon, salt, and pepper.
Peel and mince garlic.
Drain potatoes and return to saucepan. Add broth, olive oil, garlic, salt, and pepper; mash until smooth.
Serve pork with mash and salad on the side. Drizzle dressing over salad and enjoy!

name: Pork, Green Bean & Bell Pepper Stir Fry with Cashews
instructions: Fill a medium saucepan about halfway with water, cover, and bring to a boil.
Wash the green beans and trim ends; transfer to a bowl. Once the water in the saucepan is boiling, add the beans and cook until bright green and tender-crisp, 3-4 minutes. Drain and set aside.
Wash, seed, and slice the bell pepper lengthwise into strips; transfer to a medium bowl. Peel and mince the garlic; add to bowl. Peel and mince or grate the ginger; add to bowl.
Wash the green onions, trim ends, and thinly slice on a angle; transfer to a small bowl.
In a small bowl, prepare the sauce by whisking together soy sauce, vinegar, and honey. Set aside.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Thinly slice the pork chops crosswise into bite-sized strips; transfer to a small bowl. Add soy sauce and toss to coat.
Add oil to the skillet and swirl to coat bottom. Add the pork and stir-fry until browned, 1-2 minutes. Transfer to a plate.
Add more oil to the skillet, then add the pepper, garlic, ginger, and green beans. Stir fry until the pepper is tender-crisp, 2-3 minutes.
Return pork to the skillet and pour in the sauce. Stir-fry until well combined, 1-2 minutes.
Roughly chop the cashews.
Place stir fry in a bowl and garnish with sliced green onions and chopped cashews. Enjoy!

name: Pork Lo Mein with Bell Pepper & Sugar Snap Peas
instructions: Fill a medium saucepan halfway with water, cover, and bring to a boil. Uncover, add salt and pasta, and stir for a few seconds. Cook until desired firmness, 8-10 minutes.
In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, vinegar, sesame oil, cornstarch, honey, and crushed red pepper. Set aside.
Thinly slice pork crosswise into strips; transfer to a small bowl.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Peel and mince garlic. Peel and mince or grate ginger.
Wash peas and bell pepper. Seed and slice the pepper into strips.
Coat bottom of skillet with oil. Add pork and stir fry until no longer pink, 2-3 minutes. Transfer to a plate.
Once pork has been transferred, coat skillet with more oil. Add garlic, ginger, peas, and pepper; stir fry until peas are bright green and pepper is tender-crisp, 2-3 minutes.
Drain pasta in a colander.
Add pork, pasta, and sauce to skillet. Toss until noodles are well coated and sauce thickens, 1-2 minutes.
To serve, place lo mein on a plate and enjoy!

name: Pork, Portobello Mushroom & Zucchini Noodle Soup with Sesame Seeds
ingredients: 32 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Remove stems and scrape out the gills of the mushrooms; small dice, place in a medium bowl, and set aside.
Preheat a medium saucepan over medium-high heat.
Once the pan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add pork, salt, and pepper; cook, breaking the meat apart with a spoon, until browned and crumbly, 4-5 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel and mince ginger and garlic; add both to the bowl with the mushrooms.
When the pork is done, add mushrooms, ginger, and garlic to the pan. Cook, stirring occasionally, until veggies are soft and fragrant, 3-4 minutes.
Add broth and soy sauce to the pan; stir to combine, cover, and bring the soup to a boil over high heat. Once boiling, reduce heat to medium-low and simmer until flavors blend, about 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, trim zucchini and use a julienne (or regular) peeler to make noodles.
When the soup is done, add zucchini noodles to the pan, stir to combine, and remove from heat.
To serve, divide soup between bowls, drizzle with oil, and sprinkle with sesame seeds. Enjoy!

name: Pork Sausage "Cassoulet" with White Beans, Fennel & Thyme Bread Crumbs
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim off root end and stalks of the fennel, leaving only the white bulb. Halve fennel bulb lengthwise, then slice crosswise into thin half-moons. Place in a medium bowl.
Trim, seed, and medium dice bell pepper. Add to the bowl with the fennel.
Peel, halve, and mince onion; peel and mince garlic. Add both to the bowl.
Preheat an ovenproof skillet over medium-high heat.

While the skillet heats up, slide thyme leaves off the stems; discard the stems. Add half to the bowl with the veggies. Mince remaining thyme leaves, place in a small bowl, and set aside for later use.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add veggie-thyme mixture and spices; cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, 4-5 minutes.
Meanwhile, drain and rinse beans.
When the veggies are done, add beans, tomato sauce, and water to the skillet. Stir to combine, then nestle sausages into the stew.
Place skillet in the oven and bake, turning sausages and stirring beans halfway through, until sausages are golden and cooked through, 18-20 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, add bread crumbs to the bowl with the minced thyme and stir to combine.
To serve, divide cassoulet between plates or bowls and top with bread crumbs. Enjoy!

name: Pork Sausage Ragù with Zucchini, Spinach & Basil over Spaghetti Squash
instructions: Preheat oven to 500°F and place rack in the center position. Line a baking sheet pan with aluminum foil to make cleanup easier (optional).
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)
Trim squash, halve lengthwise, and scrape out the seeds. Rub the inside of the squash with oil and season with salt and pepper; arrange halves, cut-side down, on the baking sheet.
Place squash in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast until tender, so a knife can easily pierce through the flesh, 20-25 minutes.
While the squash roasts, preheat a medium saucepan over medium heat.
Once the pan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add the sausage and cook, breaking it apart with a spoon, until browned and crumbly, 4-5 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel and mince garlic; place in a medium bowl.
Trim and medium dice zucchini; small dice tomato. Add both to the bowl with the garlic.
Once the pork is browned, add veggies and spices to the pan; cook, stirring occasionally, until veggies soften, 2-3 minutes. (Reserve bowl for later use.)
Add tomato sauce to the pan; stir to combine the sauce and continue to cook until slightly thickened, 3-4 minutes more.
Meanwhile, roughly chop spinach; pick basil leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and thinly slice into ribbons. Place both in the reserved bowl.

When the sauce is done, add spinach and basil to the pan in handfuls, waiting for the spinach to wilt slightly before adding the next handful. Stir to combine, remove from heat, and cover to keep warm.
Finely grate Parmesan.

Remove squash from the oven; allow to cool slightly, about 5 minutes. Scrape the inside of the squash with a fork to separate into spaghetti-like strands. (Use an oven mitt or towel to hold it with your other hand.)
To serve, divide squash and ragù between plates or bowls; top with Parmesan and enjoy!

name: Pork Sausages with Sautéed Apples & Potato Mash
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat.
Peel the potatoes, then halve lengthwise and crosswise; transfer the quarters to a small saucepan. Cover with hot water (from the tap) by about 1 inch and bring to a boil over high heat.
Place the sausages on a plate and rub with a little olive oil.

Once the skillet is hot, add the sausages. Cook, turning occasionally, until the sausages are browned and cooked through, 10 to 15 minutes. Once done, transfer to a plate and cover with foil to keep warm.
Quarter the apples lengthwise, then cut out the core and stem from each section; cut each quarter lengthwise into 4 thin wedges.

Once the water in the saucepan is boiling, reduce the heat to medium and cook until the potatoes are tender when pierced with a knife, 8 to 12 minutes. Once done, reserve about ½ cup of liquid and drain the rest. Cover the saucepan to keep warm.
Once the sausages have been transferred, add the apples to the skillet. Cook, stirring frequently, until they are lightly browned and softened, 4 to 6 minutes. Once done, remove from the heat.
Add ½ of the reserved liquid, butter, salt, and pepper to the potatoes; mash with a potato masher until smooth. Add more liquid to thin out the mash if needed.
To serve, divide the mashed potatoes, sautéed apples, and sausages between plates. Enjoy!

name: Pork Skewers with Jalapeño Blueberry Sauce & Feta-Pecan Mixed Greens
ingredients: ½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled feta cheese
½ (5 oz) pkg spring mix (mixed greens)
instructions: If using wooden skewers, place 4-6 skewers in a shallow dish of water to soak until you are ready to use them.
Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the mixed greens if they came pre-washed.)

Quarter jalapeño pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon to reduce spice level. Mince and place in a small saucepan. (Be careful with jalapeños; do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Add blueberries to the pan with the jalapeño along with maple syrup, vinegar, ketchup, Worcestershire, and salt. Stir to combine.

Set pan over high heat and bring to a boil. Once boiling, reduce heat to medium-low and simmer, stirring occasionally, until saucy and thickened, 6-8 minutes. Remove from heat and allow to cool slightly.
Meanwhile, pat the pork dry with paper towels and cut into 1-inch cubes. Place in a medium bowl along with oil and spices; stir to coat.
Preheat a grill pan, outdoor skillet, or regular skillet over medium-high heat.
While the pan heats up, thread pork onto skewers and place on a plate. Alternatively, you can cook the pork pieces directly on the grill pan without using skewers.
Once the pan is hot, add the skewers and grill, turning occasionally, until pork is cooked through, about 8 minutes. Remove to a clean plate.
Meanwhile, using a clean cutting board, peel and mince shallot. Place in a clean medium bowl along with oil, vinegar, Dijon, salt, and pepper; stir to combine the dressing.
Place corn in the colander and rinse under hot water (from the tap) to defrost. Add to the bowl with dressing.
Roughly chop pecans. Add to the bowl along with mixed greens and feta. Gently toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide skewers and salad between plates. Top skewers with sauce and enjoy!

name: Pork-Stuffed Pita with Creamy Apple Chutney & Parmesan Zucchini Spears
ingredients: 4 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and mince ginger, garlic, and shallot; transfer to a small bowl.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat.
While the skillet heats up, quarter, core, and small dice apple; add to the bowl with the ginger, garlic, and shallot.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom; add ginger, garlic, shallot, and apple. Cook, stirring occasionally, until golden and soft, 5-6 minutes. (Reserve bowl for later use.)
Meanwhile, finely grate Parmesan.
Trim zucchini and quarter lengthwise, then halve crosswise; arrange on a baking sheet pan. Drizzle with oil, season with spices, and sprinkle with Parmesan.
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast until zucchini is fork-tender, 12-15 minutes; remove from oven.

When the apple is soft, add broth, vinegar, sugar, and spices to the skillet; stir to combine the chutney and bring to a simmer over medium-high heat. Once simmering, reduce heat to low and cook, stirring occasionally, until thickened, about 10 minutes.
When the chutney is done, transfer to the reserved bowl and set aside. Wipe the skillet clean with paper towels and return to medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat pork chops dry with paper towels and place on a cutting board; thinly slice crosswise into bite-sized strips, then season with salt and pepper.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom; add pork and stir-fry until browned and cooked through, 3-4 minutes. Remove from heat.
Meanwhile, add yogurt to the chutney and stir to combine.
Using a clean cutting board, cut pitas in half and carefully open the pockets; stuff each pocket with creamy chutney and pork.
To serve, divide pitas and zucchini between plates. Enjoy!

name: Pork Tacos with Pico de Gallo & Guacamole
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Quarter the tomatoes and transfer to a medium bowl.
Quarter the jalapeño pepper lengthwise; remove and discard the seeds and white membranes. Finely dice the pepper and add to the bowl.

Shave the cilantro leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves. Add half of the cilantro to the bowl with the tomatoes and pepper and transfer the rest to a small bowl (for the guacamole).
Peel and small dice the onion; add to the medium bowl.
Peel and mince the garlic; add half to the medium bowl and the other half to the small bowl.
Halve the avocado lengthwise and twist to open, then remove the pit with a knife or spoon; scoop out and large dice the flesh. Add to the small bowl.
Juice the lime and divide between the two bowls.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Slice the pork chops crosswise into thin strips and transfer to a medium bowl.
Season the pork with chili powder, salt, and pepper; toss to coat.
Add coconut oil to the skillet and swirl to coat the bottom.
Place the pork strips in the skillet; cook until browned and cooked through, 2 to 3 minutes per side.
Season the salsa with salt and mix to combine.
Season the guacamole with salt and pepper; mash with a fork until smooth.
Wrap the tortillas in a damp towel and microwave until heated through, 30 to 60 seconds.
To serve, spread the guacamole in the middle of the tortillas, add the pork strips, and top with the pico de gallo. Enjoy!

name: Pork Tacos with Roasted Veggies, Fresh Salsa & Lime Crema
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F. Line a baking sheet pan with aluminum foil to make clean up easier (optional).
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Place spices in a medium bowl; stir to combine the spice mix.
Peel and halve onion. Mince half and place in a small bowl; set aside. Thinly slice remaining onion and transfer to the baking sheet.

Trim, seed, and slice bell pepper lengthwise into strips; add bell pepper and corn to the baking sheet with the sliced onion. Sprinkle veggies with half of the spice mix and drizzle with oil; toss to combine. (Reserve remaining spice mix for the pork.)
Spread veggies out in an even layer. Place in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast until softened, 18-20 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, zest lime into another small bowl; add yogurt, salt, and pepper. Whisk to combine the lime crema and set aside. (Reserve lime for next step.)
Juice half of the reserved lime into the bowl with minced onion; cut the remaining lime into wedges and set aside for serving.

Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Halve tomatoes. Add both to the bowl with onion and lime juice along with oil, salt, and pepper; stir to combine the salsa and set aside.
Grate cheddar.
Pat pork chops dry with paper towels, then thinly slice into bite-sized strips. Place in the bowl with remaining spice mix, and toss to coat.

Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat. Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom; add the pork and cook, stirring occasionally, until golden brown and cooked through, 5-6 minutes. Remove from heat.
Warm tortillas in another skillet, oven, or microwave (optional).
Divide tortillas between plates, then fill with pork, veggies, and cheese. Serve with fresh salsa, lime crema, and lime wedges. Enjoy!

name: Portobello Mushroom Egg Bakes with Asparagus & Parmesan Quinoa
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F and place the rack in the middle position.
In a small saucepan, combine the quinoa and broth; bring to a boil.
Wash and dry the mushrooms; remove the stems and carefully scrape out the gills, making sure not to damage the rim of the mushrooms.
Place the mushrooms on the baking sheet; rub with olive oil.
Once the quinoa is boiling, reduce heat to a simmer and cover; cook for 15 minutes. Once cooked, remove from the heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Break an egg into each mushroom cap and season with salt and pepper.
Place the mushrooms in the oven and bake for 8 minutes.

Wash and dry the asparagus. Snap (or cut) off and discard the woody ends; cut the spears on an angle into 1-inch pieces. Transfer to a large bowl, drizzle with olive oil, and season with salt and pepper; toss to coat.
Finely grate ¼ cup of Parmesan.
After the 8 minutes are up, remove the sheet pan from the oven temporarily. Arrange the asparagus on the sheet around the mushrooms.
Return the sheet to the oven and continue to bake until the eggs are cooked and the asparagus is tender, 7 to 10 more minutes.
Uncover the quinoa and fluff with a fork. Add the asparagus and Parmesan; stir until well combined.
Divide the mushrooms and quinoa between two plates (or one plate and one lunch container). Enjoy!

name: Portobello Mushroom "Parmesan" with Zucchini, Olive & Pine Nut Salad
instructions: Preheat oven to broil on high and position rack in the upper third of the oven.

Wash, dry, and remove stems from portobello mushrooms, then carefully scrape out the gills. Transfer to a baking sheet pan, rub with oil, and season with salt and pepper on both sides; arrange cap-side up.
Place mushrooms in the oven and broil until starting to soften, about 6 minutes. Remove from oven.

Meanwhile, peel and mince garlic. Place in a small saucepan along with tomato sauce, crushed red pepper, and salt. Stir to combine the sauce and bring to a simmer over high heat. Once simmering, remove from heat and set aside.
While the sauce is heating, finely grate Parmesan. Place in a medium bowl along with bread crumbs and spices, then stir to combine the Parmesan topping.
Using tongs, carefully flip the mushrooms, cap-side down. Spread evenly with warm tomato sauce and sprinkle with Parmesan topping. (Reserve bowl for later use.)
Return baking sheet to the oven and continue to broil until the mushrooms are soft and cheese topping is golden brown, 4-5 minutes more. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, place oil, vinegar, and spices in the reserved bowl. Whisk to combine the dressing.
Peel, halve, and slice shallot lengthwise into thin strips. Add to the bowl with the dressing.
Roughly chop olives. Add to the bowl.
Wash, dry, and trim zucchini, then run a vegetable peeler along the length of the zucchini to make ribbons. Add to the bowl, along with the pine nuts, and toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide the mushrooms and salad between plates. Enjoy!

name: Portobello-Tomato Melts with Simple  Greens
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spring mix if it came pre-washed.)
In a medium bowl, prepare the dressing by whisking together oil, vinegar, Dijon, salt, and pepper.
Remove the stems of the mushrooms and carefully scrape out the gills using a spoon.
Toss mushrooms in the dressing, making sure both sides are well coated; leave the mushrooms in the dressing to marinate and set aside.
Preheat oven to broil and position rack under the broiler.
Pick basil leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and thinly slice into ribbons.
Slice the tomato.
Grate the cheese.
Remove mushrooms from the dressing, shaking off excess; transfer mushrooms, stem side down, to a baking sheet lined with aluminum foil. (Reserve remaining dressing for the salad.)
Place mushrooms under the broiler and cook until tender, 2-3 minutes per side.
Peel and mince garlic; place in a small bowl, add oil and mix to combine.
Drizzle bread with oil and garlic mixture.

Remove mushrooms from oven and pour off any excess moisture. Place mushrooms back on the sheet pan, stem side up, and fill with tomato slices and cheese. Add bread to the baking sheet next to the mushrooms; return to the broiler until cheese is melted and bread is toasted, 1-2 minutes.
Add spring mix, sliced almonds, and half the basil to the bowl with the remaining dressing, toss to combine.
To serve, divide salad and toast between plates; top toast with broiled mushroom and garnish with remaining basil. Enjoy!

name: Portuguese Sausage, Potato & Leafy Greens Soup (Caldo Verde)
ingredients: 32 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Preheat a medium saucepan over medium-high heat.
While the pan heats up, cut the sausages into ½-inch thick pieces.
Once the pan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add sausage and pan-fry, stirring occasionally, until browned and cooked through, 5-6 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)
When the sausage is done, remove to a plate using a slotted spoon and set aside.

Using a clean cutting board, trim off the root end and dark green top of the leek, leaving only the white and pale green parts. Cut in half lengthwise and rinse under running water, separating the layers to remove dirt and grit. Slice crosswise into ¼-inch thick pieces; place in a medium bowl.
Small dice tomato and add to the bowl with the leek.
Peel and mince garlic; add to the bowl.
Return the pan (with cooking juices) to medium-high heat and add more oil. Add leek, tomato, garlic, and spices; cook, stirring occasionally, until veggies start to soften, about 5 minutes.
While the veggies cook, peel, quarter, and slice potatoes into ½-inch thick pieces.
Add potatoes and broth to the pan; stir to combine and bring to a boil over high heat.

Meanwhile, fold kale leaves in half lengthwise and slice off the stems. Chop or tear leaves into bite-sized pieces; add to the soup. Once the soup comes to a boil, reduce heat to a simmer, and cook until potatoes and kale are tender, 8-10 minutes.
While the soup cooks, roughly chop spinach and set aside.
When the potatoes and kale are tender, add cooked sausage and spinach to the soup and continue to simmer until spinach is wilted and sausage is heated through, 2-3 minutes more. Remove from heat.
To serve, divide soup between bowls and enjoy!

name: Potato, Bacon & Kale Frittata
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Preheat the oven to the broil setting and position the rack in the upper third of the oven.
Preheat an ovenproof skillet over medium heat.
Cut the bacon crosswise into ¼-inch-thick strips.

Once the skillet is hot, add the bacon strips. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the bacon is crispy, 4 to 6 minutes. Once done, transfer to a plate lined with paper towels, leaving the drippings in the skillet.
While the bacon cooks, trim off and discard the ends of the shallot; peel and halve the shallot lengthwise, then thinly slice crosswise into half-rounds.
Once the bacon has been transferred, add the shallot to the skillet; cook, stirring frequently, until softened, 2 to 3 minutes.
While the shallot cooks, medium dice the potato (cut into ½-inch cubes).
Add the potatoes to the skillet; cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, 6 to 8 minutes.
While the potatoes cook, cut out and discard the kale stems; chop the leaves crosswise into 1-inch strips.
Add the kale to the skillet; cook, stirring, until it is wilted but still green, 4 to 5 minutes.
While the kale cooks, in a medium bowl, combine and whisk together the eggs, water, salt, and pepper.

Pour the egg mixture into the skillet and top with the bacon. While tilting the skillet with one hand, lift up the edges of the frittata with a spatula and let the egg mixture run underneath during the first few minutes of cooking. Cook until most of the frittata is set, but the top is still runny, 4 to 5 minutes.
Transfer the skillet to the oven and broil until the top is set and lightly browned, 2 to 3 minutes.
To serve, separate the frittata into wedges and divide between plates. Enjoy!

name: Potato & Red Pepper Hash with Fried Eggs & Parmesan
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and large dice the potatoes into ¾-inch cubes; transfer to a bowl.
Preheat a (stainless steel or cast-iron) skillet over medium heat.
Quarter the bell pepper lengthwise; remove and discard the stem, seeds, and membranes. Large dice the pepper into ¾-inch cubes and transfer to a separate medium bowl.
Once the skillet is hot, add coconut oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add the potatoes to the skillet; cook, stirring occasionally, until the potatoes are tender, 8 to 10 minutes.
Trim off and discard the ends of the onion and remove the outer layer; small dice the onion into ¼-inch pieces. Add to the bell pepper.
Trim off and discard the root end of the garlic; peel and mince or press the garlic. Add to the bell pepper and onion.
Add the bell pepper, onion, and garlic to the skillet; cook, stirring frequently, until the vegetables are tender and browned, 4 to 6 minutes.
Add coconut oil to a nonstick skillet and preheat over medium heat.
Gently crack the eggs into the skillet. Cook until the tops of the whites are set but the yolks are still runny, 3 to 4 minutes. Once done, separate the eggs. Cook in batches if necessary.
Season the hash with salt and pepper; stir to combine and remove from the heat.
Finely grate ½ cup of Parmesan.
To serve, divide the hash between plates, top with the fried eggs, and sprinkle with the Parmesan. Season with additional salt and pepper if desired. Enjoy!

name: Potato, Walnut & Sun-Dried Tomato "Chorizo" Tacos with Avocado Cream
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Small dice potato into ¼-inch cubes.
Preheat a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add potatoes and salt; cook, stirring often, until golden and crisp, about 12 minutes.
Meanwhile, finely chop the walnuts and transfer to a small bowl.
Peel and mince the garlic. Mince the sun-dried tomatoes; add both to the bowl with the walnuts.
Add water, sugar, and spices to the bowl with the walnuts and stir to combine.
When the potatoes are done, add the walnut mixture to the skillet; cook, stirring often, until the liquid has evaporated, about 4 minutes. Remove from the heat.
Juice the lime into a blender.
Halve and pit the avocado; slice crosswise while still in the skin and scoop out into the blender.
Shave the cilantro leaves off the stems; discard the stems and add leaves to the blender.
Peel garlic; add to the blender along with almond milk and salt. Blend on high until smooth; set avocado cream aside.
Trim off and discard the ends of the green onions; cut the onions crosswise into ¼-inch pieces at an angle.
Small dice the tomato.
Wrap the tortillas in damp paper towels and microwave until heated through, 15-30 seconds.
To serve, divide the tortillas between plates and fill with potato-walnut mixture. Top with green onion, tomato, and avocado cream. Enjoy!

name: Potato, Zucchini & Kidney Bean Bake with Avocado Pico de Gallo
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Quarter potatoes and transfer to a baking sheet pan; drizzle with oil and season with spices. Toss to coat and spread out in an even layer.
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast until potatoes start to soften, about 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, drain and rinse beans; place in a medium bowl.
Trim and large dice zucchini; add to the bowl with the beans. Drizzle with oil, season with spices, and toss to combine.
When the potatoes have softened, remove from oven; add beans and zucchini to the baking sheet. Toss to combine and spread out in an even layer. (Reserve bowl for later use.)
Return baking sheet to the oven and continue to roast until veggies are fork-tender, 10-12 minutes more. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, juice lime into the reserved bowl.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Peel and mince garlic. Add both to the bowl with the lime juice.

Quarter jalapeño pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon. Mince and add to the bowl. (Be careful with jalapeños; do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Small dice tomato and add to the bowl.
Halve and pit avocado; scoop out with a spoon and small dice the flesh. Add to the bowl and stir to combine the pico de gallo.
To serve, divide roasted veggies and beans between plates or bowls; top with yogurt and pico de gallo. Enjoy!

name: Prosciutto, Asparagus, Pea & Goat Cheese Frittata with Mixed Salad
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Place in a medium bowl.
Add eggs, pepper, and salt to the bowl with the parsley. Whisk to combine.
Crumble the goat cheese. Add half to the bowl with the egg. (Set remaining cheese aside for the salad.)
Chop (or tear) prosciutto into bite-sized pieces. Add to the bowl, stir to combine, and set aside.

Trim off the root end and dark green top of the leek, leaving only the white and pale green parts. Cut the leek in half lengthwise and rinse under running water, separating the layers to remove any dirt and grit. Slice crosswise into ¼-inch thick pieces. Place in another medium bowl.
Preheat an ovenproof skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, snap (or cut) off the woody ends of the asparagus; cut spears into bite-sized pieces. Add to the bowl with the leek.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add leek, asparagus, peas, pepper, and salt; cook, stirring occasionally, until veggies are bright green and starting to soften, about 3 minutes. (Reserve bowl for later use.)
Meanwhile, preheat oven to broil on high and position rack in the upper third of the oven.

When the veggies are soft, reduce heat to medium and pour the egg mixture into the skillet. As eggs set around the edge of the skillet, gently lift cooked portions with a spatula to allow uncooked egg to flow underneath. Cook until bottom and sides are firm but top is still runny, about 5 minutes.
While the frittata is cooking, place additional oil, vinegar, salt, and pepper in the reserved bowl. Whisk to combine the dressing and set aside.
Place skillet in the oven and broil until top of the frittata is just set, 2-3 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, trim and thinly slice radishes. Add to the bowl with the dressing.
Separate lettuce into leaves. Chop (or tear) leaves into bite-sized pieces. Add to the bowl, along with the reserved goat cheese, and toss to combine the salad.
Cut frittata into wedges and divide between plates. Serve with salad on the side and enjoy!

name: Prosciutto, Pear & Blue Cheese Sandwich with Spinach-Mushroom Salad
ingredients: ½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled blue cheese
instructions: Preheat oven to broil on high and position rack about 6-inches from the top.
Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)
Place oil, vinegar, Dijon, honey, salt, and pepper in a medium bowl; whisk to combine the dressing.
Thinly slice mushrooms and add to the bowl with the dressing; set aside.
Arrange bread slices on a baking sheet pan, place in the oven, and broil until toasted, 1-2 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, peel and thinly slice shallot.
Quarter, core, and thinly slice pear.

Spread mayo and Dijon over half of the toasted bread slices. Layer a small handful of spinach, shallot, pear, prosciutto, and blue cheese over top (reserving remaining spinach for the salad). Close with remaining toast slices.
Add remaining spinach to the bowl with the dressing and mushrooms; toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide sandwiches and salad between plates. Enjoy!

name: Prosciutto, Strawberry & Goat Cheese Toasts with Arugula Salad
instructions: Preheat oven to broil on high and position rack under the broiler.
Crumble goat cheese into a small bowl and set aside to soften.
Meanwhile wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the arugula if it came pre-washed.)
Arrange bread slices on a baking sheet pan. Place in the oven and broil, flipping halfway through, until toasted, 1-2 minutes. Remove toast from the oven and set aside. (Keep the broiler on.)
Pick basil leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and thinly slice into ribbons. Transfer to a medium bowl.
Add vinegar, oil, honey, and spices to the bowl with the basil; whisk to combine the marinade.
Trim and thinly slice strawberries. Add to the bowl with the marinade, toss to combine, and set aside.
Peel and mince garlic; add to the bowl with the goat cheese and mash with a fork to combine.
Spread goat cheese mixture evenly over the toast. Return baking sheet to the oven and broil until the cheese browns slightly, 1-2 minutes. Remove from the oven.
Using a slotted spoon, remove strawberries from the marinade and arrange on top of the toast. (Reserve leftover marinade for the salad.)
Chop or tear prosciutto into bite-sized pieces and place on top of toast.
Add arugula to the bowl with the reserved marinade and toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide toasts and salad between plates. Enjoy!

name: Prosciutto-Wrapped Asparagus with Herbed Cheese & Mashed Potatoes
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.

Peel and medium dice potatoes; place in a medium saucepan and cover with hot water (from the tap). Cover and bring to a boil over high heat; once boiling, reduce to a simmer and cook until soft, 10-12 minutes.
While the potatoes are cooking, snap (or cut) off woody ends of the asparagus. Transfer to a baking sheet pan, drizzle with oil, and spread out in an even layer.

Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast until asparagus is just tender, 5-7 minutes, depending on the thickness of the spears. Remove baking sheet from oven and set aside to cool slightly, about 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, using a box grater, coarsely grate cream cheese into a small bowl.
Shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl with the cream cheese.
Chop chives into small pieces. Add to the bowl along with salt and pepper, then stir to combine.
Lay prosciutto on a flat surface and spread each slice evenly with the cream cheese mixture.

When the asparagus is cool enough to handle, divide into 6 equal piles. Wrap each pile with a slice of the prepared prosciutto, gently pressing the cream cheese-side around the asparagus to secure. Arrange, seam-side down, on the baking sheet.
Return baking sheet to the oven and continue to roast until prosciutto is golden and asparagus is fork-tender, about 5 minutes. Remove from oven and let cool slightly, about 5 minutes.
When the potatoes are done, drain in a colander and return to the pan. Add oil, salt, and pepper, then using a potato masher, mash until smooth.
To serve, divide mashed potatoes and prosciutto-wrapped asparagus between plates. Enjoy!

name: Prosciutto Wrapped Basil-Salmon Kabobs with Cauliflower Rice
instructions: If using wooden skewers, place 6-8 skewers in a shallow dish of water to soak until you are ready to use them.
Meanwhile, preheat a skillet over medium heat.
Peel and small dice onion. Peel and mince garlic.
When the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add onion and garlic; cook, stirring often, until it begins to soften, 3-4 minutes.

Meanwhile, wash and dry the cauliflower. Cut the cauliflower head into quarters, then trim off and discard the leaves and thick stem. Using a box grater or food processor, coarsely grate the cauliflower.
Add cauliflower and salt to the skillet. Continue to cook, stirring often, until cauliflower is lightly golden and cooked through, 5-7 minutes.

Meanwhile, wash and dry the basil. Pick basil leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and mince. Place half of the basil in a medium bowl along with oil, salt, and pepper; stir to combine the marinade. (Reserve remaining basil for the cauliflower rice.)

If using salmon with skin, place the fillet, skin-side down, on a cutting board. Holding the tail end firmly, use a knife to cut between the flesh and skin; continue to cut through the length of the fillet (take care not to cut through the skin); discard the skin. If you don’t have a tail end, start at one corner of the fillet and work your way in until the knife is between the skin and flesh.
Cut the salmon crosswise into 1-inch strips and transfer to the bowl with the marinade. Turn to coat.

Thread one strip of salmon onto each skewer; wrap a piece of prosciutto around each salmon skewer and place on a plate. Alternatively, you can cook the salmon directly on the grill pan without using skewers.
Preheat a grill pan, outdoor grill, or skillet over medium-high heat.
Once the grill pan is hot, coat with oil. Place kabobs on the grill and cook, rotating every 1½-2 minutes, until salmon is opaque and cooked through, 6-8 minutes.
Once the cauliflower rice is done, remove from heat and stir in the reserved basil.
To serve, divide cauliflower rice and kabobs between plates. Serve mayonnaise on the side for dipping and enjoy!

name: Prosciutto-Wrapped Chicken with Warm Lentil, Pepper & Zucchini Salad
ingredients: ¾ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
instructions: Using a strainer, rinse lentils under cold water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan; add water and salt. Cover and bring to a boil over high heat. Once boiling, remove lid, reduce heat to a simmer, and cook until tender, 15-20 minutes. Drain and set aside.

Meanwhile, holding a knife parallel to the cutting board, cut the chicken in half horizontally to form thin cutlets. Season both sides with spices, then wrap each cutlet with two slices of prosciutto.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add cutlets and pan-fry until prosciutto is crisp and chicken is cooked through, 3-4 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate and loosely cover with aluminum foil. (Reserve skillet for later use.)
While the chicken is cooking, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Using a clean cutting board, trim, seed, and small dice bell pepper. Place in a medium bowl.
Trim and small dice zucchini. Add to the bowl with the bell pepper.
Peel, halve, and small dice onion. Add to the bowl.
Shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl.

Return skillet to medium-high heat. Once the skillet is hot, add more oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add veggies, parsley, and spices; cook, stirring occasionally, until veggies have softened, 4-5 minutes.
Add drained lentils and vinegar to the skillet with the veggies, then stir to combine. Remove from heat.
Slice chicken into thin strips.
To serve, divide warm lentil salad between plates or bowls and top with chicken. Enjoy!

name: Prosciutto-Wrapped Cod with Tomato, Corn, Peach & Goat Cheese Salad
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Place oil, vinegar, salt, and crushed red pepper in a medium bowl. Whisk to combine the dressing.
Halve tomatoes lengthwise, then cut into ½-inch thick wedges. Add to the bowl with the dressing.
Quarter peaches lengthwise (around the pit); twist quarters to separate, then remove and discard pits. Slice each quarter into ½-inch thick wedges. Add to the bowl and set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat cod dry with paper towels and cut into portions (if necessary). Season with salt and pepper, then wrap 2 slices of prosciutto around each portion.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add cod and cook until golden on one side, 3-4 minutes; flip and continue to pan-fry until the fish is cooked through and the prosciutto is crisp, 3-4 minutes more. Remove to a plate.
Meanwhile, place corn in the colander and rinse under hot water (from the tap) to defrost. Add to the bowl with the tomatoes and peaches.
Pick basil leaves off the stems; discard stems and tear the leaves. Add to the bowl.
Crumble goat cheese into the bowl, then gently stir to combine the salad.
To serve, divide prosciutto-wrapped cod and salad between plates. Enjoy!

name: Pumpkin & Beef Chili with Green Onions & Cool Yogurt
ingredients: ½ (15 oz) can pure pumpkin purée
instructions: Heat a medium saucepan over medium-high heat.
Peel and small dice onion. Peel and mince garlic.
Coat bottom of saucepan with oil. Add ground beef. Breaking apart with a spoon, cook until browned, 2-3 minutes.
Add onion and garlic to saucepan. Reduce heat to medium. Stirring frequently, cook until onion softens, 3-4 minutes.
Drain and rinse beans.
In a small bowl, mix together chili powder, cumin, cinnamon, salt, and pepper.
Add spice mixture, beans, tomatoes, and pumpkin purée to saucepan. Stir to combine and simmer for 10-15 minutes.
Wash green onions, trim and discard root ends, and chop. Stir ½ into the chili and save the rest for garnishing.
Serve chili in a bowl, garnish with remaining green onions and spoonfuls of yogurt. Enjoy!

name: Pumpkin-Black Bean Soup with Sweet Potatoes & Tender Kale
ingredients: 24 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
½ (13.5 fl oz) can coconut milk
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and mince ginger and garlic. Peel and small dice onion.

Quarter jalapeño pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs of the jalapeño with a spoon. Finely dice. (Be careful, with jalapeños, do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing).
Heat a large pot over medium heat.
Once the pot is hot, add the oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add ginger, garlic, onion, and jalapeño to the pot; cook, stirring occasionally, 3-4 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel and dice sweet potato into ½-inch pieces.
Drain and rinse beans.
Add sweet potato, beans, broth, tomatoes with their juices, pumpkin, coconut milk, and spices to the pot. Stir to combine.
Bring to a boil over high heat, reduce heat to medium-low, and simmer until vegetables are tender, 15-20 minutes.
Meanwhile, shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Set aside.
Fold kale leaves in half lengthwise and slice off stems. Chop or tear leaves into bite-sized pieces and add to pot during the last 5 minutes of cook time.
Juice lime into the pot and stir to combine.
Divide the soup between bowls and top with cilantro. Enjoy!

name: Pumpkin & Ricotta Pasta Bake with Kale, Parmesan & Chives
ingredients: 6 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
½ (15 oz) can pure pumpkin purée
instructions: Fill a medium saucepan halfway with water, cover, and bring to a boil. Uncover, add salt and pasta, and stir for a few seconds. Cook until desired firmness, 8-10 minutes.
Peel and mince garlic. Peel and small dice the onion
Heat a sauté pan over medium-low heat.
Coat bottom of pan with oil. Add garlic, onion, sage, and thyme. Cook until soft, 3-4 minutes.

Meanwhile, wash kale leaves, then fold in half lengthwise and slice off the stems. Chop or tear leaves into bite-sized pieces. Add to the pan with the onions; cook, stirring often, until kale begins to wilt, 4-5 minutes.
Add broth, pumpkin, ricotta, salt, and pepper. Stir to combine. Simmer, stirring occasionally, while pasta is cooking.
Preheat oven to broil and position rack 4 inches under the broiler.
Wash and chop chives into small pieces.
Grate ¼ cup of Parmesan.
Add ½ of the chives and Parmesan (save the rest for garnishing) to pan and stir to combine.
Drain pasta, add to pan with sauce, and stir to combine.
Place pan in the oven and broil until slightly browned, 3-4 minutes.
To serve, place pasta on a plate and garnish with remaining chives and Parmesan. Enjoy!

name: Pumpkin Soup with Goat Cheese & Chickpea-Kale Sauté
ingredients: 20 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
½ (15 oz) can pure pumpkin purée
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Drain and rinse the chickpeas; set aside to drain further.
Preheat a medium saucepan over medium heat.
While the saucepan heats up, trim off and discard the ends of the onion and remove the outer layer; small dice the onion into ¼-inch pieces.
Once the saucepan is hot, add olive oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add the onion to the saucepan; cook, stirring frequently, until softened, 3 to 4 minutes.
Trim off and discard the root ends of the garlic; peel and mince or press the garlic. Transfer to a small bowl.
Add ½ of the garlic, cinnamon, and crushed red pepper to the saucepan; stir until fragrant, 15 to 30 seconds.
Add the pumpkin purée and broth to the saucepan; stir to incorporate and season with salt and pepper. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 10 to 15 minutes.
Preheat a nonstick skillet over medium heat.
While the skillet heats up, cut out and discard the kale stems; chop the leaves into 1-inch pieces.
Once the pan is hot, add olive oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add the remaining garlic and crushed red pepper to the pan; stir until fragrant, 15 to 30 seconds.
Add the kale to the skillet and toss with the garlic and olive oil; cook until it is tender, 4 to 6 minutes.
Crumble the goat cheese and place in a small bowl.
Add the chickpeas to the kale and season the mixture with salt and pepper; mix together and continue to cook until the chickpeas are heated through, 1 to 2 minutes.
Juice the lemon and drizzle over the kale and chickpeas.
Using an immersion (hand) blender, purée the soup until smooth.
To serve, divide the soup between bowls and top with the goat cheese; serve with the sautéed chickpeas and kale on the side. Enjoy!

name: Pumpkin & Turkey Chili with Kale & Cannellini Beans
ingredients: ½ (15 oz) can pure pumpkin purée
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Quarter the jalapeño pepper lengthwise; remove and discard the stem, seeds, and membranes. Finely dice the pepper and transfer to a medium bowl.
Preheat a medium saucepan over medium-high heat.
While the saucepan heats up, trim off and discard the ends of the onion and remove the outer layer; small dice the onion (cut into ¼-inch pieces). Add to the bowl with the pepper.
Once the saucepan is hot, add coconut oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add the ground turkey to the saucepan; cook, breaking apart with a spoon, until browned and crumbly, 3 to 4 minutes. Once done, transfer to a bowl, leaving some of the juices in the saucepan.
Once the turkey has been transferred, add the pepper and onion to the saucepan; cook, stirring frequently, until softened, 3 to 4 minutes.
Drain and rinse the beans in a colander.
Trim off and discard the root end of the garlic; peel and mince or press the garlic.
Add the garlic, chili powder, cumin, and oregano to the saucepan; stir until fragrant, 15 to 30 seconds.
Return the turkey to the saucepan, then add in the beans, diced tomatoes, and pumpkin purée; season with salt and pepper. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce to a simmer and cook for 10 minutes.
Cut out and discard the kale stems; chop leaves crosswise into bite-sized pieces. Stir the kale into the chili while it is cooking.
To serve, divide the chili between bowls and top with spoonfuls of Greek yogurt. Enjoy!

name: Puttanesca Pasta Salad with Tuna, Anchovies & Artichokes
ingredients: 1 (6 oz) can chunk light tuna in water
instructions: Fill a large pot halfway with water, cover, and bring to a boil. Uncover, add salt and pasta, and stir for a few seconds. Cook until desired firmness, 8-10 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel and mince the garlic and shallot; place both in a large bowl.
Finely mince anchovy fillets; add to the bowl along with oil, vinegar, and spices. Whisk to combine the dressing.
Drain and thinly slice artichokes; add to the bowl with the dressing.
Halve olives lengthwise and add to the bowl.
Roughly chop capers and add to the bowl.
Wash, dry, and halve tomatoes; add to the bowl.
Wash and dry parsley. Shave leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl and stir to combine.
Drain pasta in a colander and rinse under cold water; add to the bowl.
Drain tuna, flake with a fork, and add to the bowl. Gently toss the salad to combine.
To serve, divide pasta salad between bowls or plates. Garnish with pine nuts and enjoy!

name: Quick & Cheesy French Onion Soup
ingredients: 24 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Preheat a large pot over medium heat.
Peel and very thinly slice onions, using a mandoline slicer if desired.
When the pot is warm, melt butter until foamy. Add onions to the pot and season with salt to help them release their moisture. Cook until tender, stirring occasionally, 4-5 minutes.
Add broth, water, soy sauce, Worcestershire, pepper, and thyme; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover and simmer, 10-15 minutes.
While soup is simmering, slice bread (if required) and grate cheese; set aside.
Preheat oven to broil and position rack under the broiler.
Divide soup into oven-safe bowls or ramekins, place bowls on a baking sheet pan. Top with bread slices and cheese.
Place under broiler until cheese is golden brown, about 1 minute. Watch it carefully as it can burn easily.
When the soup is brown and bubbly, carefully remove from oven using oven mitts and place bowls on a plate. Enjoy!

name: Quick Pickled Spicy Shrimp & Avocado Salad with Buttered Toast Points
ingredients: ¾ lb raw peeled shrimp, fresh or frozen
instructions: Wash and dry thyme. Add thyme sprigs, water, vinegar, salt, and coriander to a medium saucepan; cover and bring to a boil over high heat.
If using frozen shrimp, place them in a colander and run under cold water to thaw them slightly and remove any ice crystals. (If using fresh shrimp, skip this step.)

Once the liquid comes to a boil, uncover, add shrimp, and stir for a few seconds. Remove from heat, and let the shrimp pickle in the cooking liquid while you prepare the rest of the salad, about 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Grate the zest from the lemon and transfer to a medium bowl, then juice the lemon into the same bowl.
Peel and mince the garlic; transfer to the bowl.
Add additional vinegar, oil, salt, and pepper to the bowl and whisk to combine the dressing.
Thinly slice the jalapeño into rounds (be careful, with jalapeños, do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing).
Peel and thinly slice the shallot into rings. Add shallots and jalapeños to the bowl with the dressing.
Seed and slice bell pepper into thin strips. Peel and medium dice the cucumber. Peel and thinly slice the carrot into rounds. Add vegetables to the bowl with the dressing.
Halve and pit the avocado; scoop out the flesh and medium dice. Add to the bowl.
Drain the shrimp and discard the liquid. Remove tails, then add shrimp to the bowl with the vegetables and stir to combine the salad; set aside.
Toast and butter the bread, then slice on the diagonal to make toast points.
To serve, divide shrimp salad between bowls. Enjoy with a side of buttered toast points for dipping.

name: Quinoa Black Bean Chili with Parmesan-Date Kale Salad & Dijon Dressing
instructions: Drain and rinse beans; set aside.
Preheat a medium saucepan over medium heat.
Meanwhile, peel and small dice onion; peel and mince garlic.
Once the pan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add the onion and garlic; cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 2 minutes.

Add beans, corn, tomatoes, quinoa, water, chili powder, and salt to the pan. Stir to combine the chili and bring to a boil over high heat; reduce heat to low, cover, and cook until the liquid is absorbed and quinoa is tender, about 20 minutes.
While the chili is cooking, place oil, vinegar, Dijon, salt, and pepper in a medium bowl; whisk to combine the dressing.
Wash and dry kale; fold leaves in half lengthwise and slice off the stems. Chop or tear leaves into bite-sized pieces and add to the bowl with the dressing.
Small dice dates and add to the bowl along with the pumpkin seeds.
Grate or shave Parmesan with a vegetable peeler and add to the bowl with the kale; toss to combine the salad.
Divide chili between bowls and top with a dollop of yogurt; serve with salad on the side and enjoy!

name: Quinoa Bowl with Kale Chips, Marinated Chickpeas & Tahini Dressing
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F.
In a small saucepan, combine quinoa and broth; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to a simmer, cover, and cook for 15 minutes. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Fold kale leaves in half lengthwise and slice off the stems; chop or tear leaves into large bite-sized pieces and place in a medium bowl.

Add nutritional yeast, oil, vinegar, and salt to the bowl with the kale; using your hands, toss the leaves well to coat. Transfer to a baking sheet pan and spread out in a single layer. (Reserve bowl for later use.)
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and bake, tossing once, until the kale is crispy, 10-12 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, drain and rinse chickpeas; set aside to drain further.
Zest and juice half of the lemon into the reserved bowl. (Reserve remaining lemon for the dressing.)
Peel and mince garlic. Add to the bowl with the lemon juice along with oil, maple syrup, Dijon, and spices; stir to combine the marinade. Add chickpeas, stir to combine, and set aside to marinate.
Peel and mince additional garlic; place in a small bowl.
Juice the reserved lemon into the bowl with the garlic. Add tahini, water, maple syrup, Dijon, salt, and pepper; whisk to combine the dressing and set aside.
Trim and quarter cucumber lengthwise, then cut crosswise into ¼-inch thick pieces.
Trim and thinly slice radishes.
To serve, divide quinoa, kale chips, chickpeas, cucumber, and radish between bowls. Drizzle with lemon-tahini dressing and enjoy!

name: Quinoa Bowl with Roasted Carrots, Garlic-Lime Chickpeas & Cumin Yogurt
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Preheat the oven to 425°F and place the rack in the center position. Line a sheet pan with parchment paper (optional).
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel carrots, cut in half lengthwise, and add to the baking sheet.
Drizzle oil and honey over carrots and sprinkle with spices. Place carrots in the oven and cook, until tender, 15-20 minutes.
In a small saucepan, combine quinoa and broth; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to a simmer, cover, and cook for 15 minutes. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, shave the parsley leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves. Add to a medium bowl (reserving some for garnish).
Peel and mince garlic. Zest the lime and add both to the bowl with the parsley. Add salt, pepper, and oil; stir to combine.
Drain and rinse chickpeas. Add to the lime zest mixture​, along with the corn, and toss to coat. Add to the baking sheet for the last 5 minutes of cooking.
Juice the lime into a small bowl. Add yogurt, cumin, and salt; whisk to combine.
To serve, divide quinoa between bowls, add roasted carrots, chickpeas, and corn. Drizzle with cumin yogurt and top with reserved parsley. Enjoy!

name: Quinoa Bowl with Salmon Skewers, Spinach, Radish & Chili-Garlic Sauce
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: If using wooden skewers, place 4-6 skewers in a shallow dish of water to soak until you are ready to use them.
In a small saucepan, combine quinoa and broth; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to a simmer, cover, and cook for 15 minutes. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, place vinegar, oil, chili-garlic sauce, honey, and salt in a small bowl; whisk to combine the sauce.
