If using salmon with skin, place the fillet, skin-side down, on a cutting board. Holding the tail end (or corner) firmly, use a knife to cut between the flesh and skin; continue to cut through the length of the fillet (take care not to cut through the skin); discard the skin.

Cut the salmon into 1-inch cubes and thread onto the skewers; place on a plate, drizzle with half of the sauce, and turn to coat. If you don't have skewers, you can cook the salmon directly on the grill pan. (Reserve remaining sauce for later use.)
Preheat a grill pan or regular skillet over medium-high heat.
Once the grill pan is hot, add skewers and grill, turning every 1½-2 minutes, until salmon is opaque and cooked through, 6-8 minutes. Transfer to a clean plate.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)
Using a clean cutting board, trim and thinly slice radishes; place on another clean plate.
Trim and slice cucumber crosswise into thin rounds; add to the plate with the radish and set aside.
Add mayo to the bowl with the reserved sauce and whisk to combine.
To serve, divide quinoa between bowls; top with spinach, radish, cucumber, and salmon skewers. Drizzle with sauce and enjoy!

name: Quinoa Burrito Bowls with Fresh Strawberry Salsa
ingredients: 16 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: In a small saucepan, combine quinoa and broth; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to a simmer, cover, and cook 15 minutes. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, 5 minutes.
Drain and rinse the beans in a colander; set aside to drain further.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and small dice onion.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Peel and mince the garlic.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add the onion and garlic to the skillet and cook, stirring occasionally, until soft, about 3 minutes.
Remove stems and roughly chop strawberries; place in a medium bowl.
Add drained beans, frozen corn, broth, and spices to the skillet. Cook, stirring occasionally, until heated through, about 5 minutes.

Quarter the jalapeño pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs of the jalapeño with a spoon. Finely dice and add to the bowl with the strawberries. (Be careful, with jalapeños, do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing).
Shave the cilantro leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl with the strawberries.
Juice half the lime into the bowl with the strawberries; cut the other half into wedges.
Peel and mince the shallot; add to the bowl. Stir to combine the salsa.
To serve, divide quinoa between bowls, top with bean mixture, salsa, and lime wedges. Enjoy!

name: Quinoa-Butternut Squash Stew with Peanuts, Raisins, Spinach & Cilantro
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)
Trim and peel squash; halve lengthwise, scrape out seeds, and small dice. Place in a small bowl.
Trim, seed, and small dice bell pepper; add to the bowl with the squash and set aside.
Preheat a medium saucepan over medium heat.
While the pan heats up, peel, halve, and small dice onion; peel and mince garlic.
Once the pan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add onion and garlic; cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 2 minutes.

Add squash, bell pepper, tomatoes, water, quinoa, and spices to the pan. Stir to combine the stew and bring to a boil over high heat; once boiling, reduce heat to low, cover, and cook until squash and quinoa are tender, about 20 minutes. (Reserve bowl for next step.)
Meanwhile, roughly chop spinach and place in the reserved bowl.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves.
When the quinoa is tender, add spinach to the pan in handfuls, waiting for the spinach to wilt slightly before adding the next handful.

Add peanut butter, additional water, raisins, and half of the cilantro to the stew. Stir to combine and continue to cook until warmed through, about 3 minutes. (Reserve remaining cilantro for serving.)
Meanwhile, roughly chop peanuts. Slice lime into wedges.
Divide stew between bowls; top with reserved cilantro and peanuts. Serve with lime wedges for squeezing over and enjoy!

name: Quinoa Minestrone with Kale & Crispy Italian-Spiced Chickpeas
ingredients: 32 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Drain and rinse chickpeas. Place on paper towels and pat dry; transfer to a medium bowl. Add oil and spices to the bowl and toss to combine.

Transfer chickpeas to a baking sheet and spread out in an even layer. Place in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and bake, stirring halfway through, until crispy, about 20 minutes. Reserve bowl for later use.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.

Trim off the root ends and the dark green top of the leek, leaving only the white and pale green parts. Cut the leek in half lengthwise and rinse under running water, separating the layers to remove any dirt and grit. Slice crosswise into ½-inch half-moons; transfer to the medium bowl.
Peel, trim, and slice carrots into ¼-inch rounds. Trim celery and slice crosswise into ¼-inch pieces. Transfer both to the bowl with the leeks.
Preheat a large pot over medium-high heat.
Once the pot is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add leeks, carrots, celery, and spices to the pot; cook, stirring occasionally, until vegetables begin to soften slightly, 2-3 minutes.
Peel and mince garlic.

Add garlic, broth, tomatoes, and quinoa to the pot and stir to combine; increase the heat to high and bring the liquid to a simmer. Once simmering, reduce the heat to medium-low, cover the pot with a lid, and cook for 7 minutes.

Fold kale leaves in half lengthwise and slice off the stems. Chop or tear leaves into bite-sized pieces. Add kale to the pot and cook until kale is soft and quinoa is cooked through, about 7 more minutes.
Shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves.
Finely grate Parmesan.
To serve, divide the soup between bowls. Top each bowl with a pile of crispy chickpeas; garnish with parsley, Parmesan, and crushed red pepper. Enjoy!

name: Quinoa "Risotto" with Garden Veggies, Basil & Parmesan
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: In a small saucepan, combine quinoa and broth. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15 minutes. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)
Trim ends and medium dice eggplant. Transfer to a medium bowl, add salt, and toss to coat; set aside.
Medium dice tomatoes and place in a large bowl.
Seed and medium dice bell pepper; add to the bowl with the tomatoes.
Trim ends and medium dice zucchini; add to the bowl with the tomatoes.
Preheat a large skillet over medium heat.
Peel and mince onion and garlic.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add onion and garlic. Stirring frequently, cook until onion begins to soften, 2-3 minutes.

Using a clean towel or paper towel, squeeze the eggplant to release excess moisture. Add eggplant to the skillet along with the chopped veggies, corn, tomato sauce, and salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, until veggies begin to soften, 12-14 minutes.
Meanwhile, finely grate Parmesan.
Pick basil leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and thinly slice into ribbons.
Add spinach to the skillet in handfuls, waiting for the spinach to wilt slightly before adding the next handful. Add quinoa and half of the Parmesan; stir to combine.
To serve, divide the risotto between bowls and garnish with remaining Parmesan and basil. Enjoy!

name: Quinoa-Spinach Salad with Shrimp, Strawberries, Basil, Feta & Almonds
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled feta cheese
¾ lb raw peeled shrimp, fresh or frozen
instructions: In a small saucepan, combine quinoa and broth; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to a simmer, cover, and cook for 15 minutes. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)

If using frozen shrimp, place them in a colander and run under cold water to thaw them slightly and remove any ice crystals. (If using fresh shrimp, skip this step.) Place the shrimp on a clean towel or paper towels and pat dry.
Zest and juice lemon into a medium bowl. Add oil, maple syrup, salt, and pepper; whisk to combine the dressing.
Peel, halve, and thinly slice shallot into half-moons. Add to the bowl with the dressing and stir to combine.
Trim, seed, and small dice bell pepper; add to the bowl.
Trim and quarter strawberries lengthwise; add to the bowl.
Pick basil leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and thinly slice into ribbons; add to the bowl (reserving a small handful for garnish).
Add feta to the bowl and set aside.
Transfer the cooked quinoa to a baking sheet pan. Spread out in an even layer and let cool for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add shrimp and season with salt and pepper; cook until opaque, 1-2 minutes per side. Once done, transfer to a plate.
Add cooled quinoa to the bowl with the dressing and salad fixings; gently stir to combine.
To serve, divide spinach between plates; top with quinoa salad, shrimp, almonds, and reserved basil. Enjoy!

name: Quinoa Tabbouleh Salad with Grape Tomatoes & Cucumber
ingredients: 12 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: In a small saucepan, combine quinoa and broth; bring to a boil. Reduce heat a simmer, cover, and cook for 15 minutes. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Peel and mince garlic. In a large bowl, prepare dressing by whisking together garlic, lemon juice, oil, salt, pepper, and cumin.

Wash and dry tomatoes, cucumber, parsley, and mint. Halve and add tomatoes to bowl with dressing. Medium dice and add cucumber to bowl. Shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard the stems, mince the leaves, and add to bowl. Pick mint leaves off the stems; discard the stems, mince the leaves, and add to bowl.
Uncover quinoa, fluff with a fork, and drain any excess liquid. Add quinoa to bowl and toss salad.
To serve, place salad in a bowl. Enjoy!

name: Raspberry-Basil Quinoa Spinach Salad with Orange, Pecans & Goat Cheese
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: In a small saucepan, combine quinoa and broth; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to a simmer, cover, and cook for 15 minutes. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)
Peel orange, separate into segments, and roughly chop the flesh. Place in a medium bowl along with the spinach.
Peel, halve, and slice shallot crosswise into thin half-moons. Add to the bowl with the orange and spinach.
Pick basil leaves off the stems. Roll half of the basil leaves up crosswise, thinly slice into ribbons, and add to the bowl. Place remaining (whole) basil leaves in a blender.

Add half of the raspberries to the bowl and set aside. Add remaining raspberries to the blender with the basil along with oil, vinegar, water, Dijon, honey, salt, and pepper. Blend on high until smooth, then set dressing aside.
Transfer the cooked quinoa to a baking sheet pan. Spread out in an even layer and let cool for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, roughly chop pecans.
Once the quinoa is cool, add to the bowl, along with the pecans, and toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide salad between plates or bowls. Crumble goat cheese over top and drizzle with dressing. Enjoy!

name: Red Cabbage, Quinoa & Edamame Salad with Asian Peanut-Herb Dressing
instructions: In a small saucepan, combine quinoa, water, and salt; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to a simmer, cover, and cook for 15-18 minutes. Transfer cooked quinoa to a baking sheet pan and spread out in a thin layer to cool.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)
Place edamame in a colander and rinse under hot, running water (from the tap) to defrost; set aside to drain.
Zest and juice lime into a large salad bowl.
Peel and mince garlic and ginger; transfer both to the salad bowl.
Trim and mince green onions; add to the bowl.
Pick mint leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl.
Roughly chop peanuts and add half to the bowl (reserve the rest for garnish).
Add soy sauce, oils, and crushed red pepper to the bowl; whisk to combine the dressing.
Halve the cabbage lengthwise and cut out the core; thinly slice crosswise and add to the bowl with the dressing. Using tongs, toss cabbage with the dressing to thoroughly coat.
Add spinach, edamame, and quinoa to the bowl; toss once more to combine the salad.
Halve and pit the avocado; slice crosswise while still in the skin and scoop out with a spoon.
To serve, divide salad between plates or bowls. Top with avocado and reserved peanuts. Enjoy!

name: Red Lentil Coconut Curry with Peppers & Avocado
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
½ (13.5 fl oz) can coconut milk
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Heat a large pot over medium heat.
Peel and mince the garlic and shallot. Peel and mince or grate the ginger.
Once the pot is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add the garlic, shallot, and ginger to the pot and cook, stirring occasionally, 2-3 minutes.

Quarter the jalapeño pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs of the jalapeño with a spoon. Finely dice (Be careful, with jalapeños, do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing).
Small dice the bell pepper. Add the jalapeño, bell pepper, curry powder, and salt to the pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, 2-3 minutes.

Add the diced tomatoes, coconut milk, and broth to the pot. Stir and bring to a boil over high heat, then add the red lentils. Reduce heat to medium-low and cook, stirring occasionally, until lentils are tender, 22-25 minutes.
Meanwhile, halve and pit the avocado; slice crosswise while still in the skin and scoop out with a spoon.
Shave the cilantro leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves.
To serve, divide the lentil curry between bowls; top with sliced avocado and minced cilantro. Enjoy!

name: Red Lentil Soup with Sweet Potato, Pear, Coconut Milk & Lime
ingredients: 24 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
½ (13.5 fl oz) can coconut milk
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Rinse the lentils in a colander or strainer; set aside to drain.
Peel and small dice onion; transfer to a medium bowl.
Peel, trim, and small dice carrot; add to the bowl with the onion.
Preheat a medium saucepan over medium heat.
While the pan heats up, trim and small dice celery; add to the bowl with the other veggies.
Once the pan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add onion, carrot, celery, and spices to the pan; cook, stirring occasionally, until the veggies soften, 3-4 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel and small dice sweet potato.
Zest lime and then cut into wedges (set wedges aside for serving).
Add lentils, sweet potato, lime zest, broth, and coconut milk to the pan; stir to combine and bring to a boil over medium-high heat.
Peel, quarter, core, and small dice pear; add to the soup. Once the soup comes to a boil, reduce heat to a simmer, and cook until veggies and lentils are tender, about 15 minutes.
Divide soup between bowls and serve with lime wedges on the side. Enjoy!

name: Red Lentil Tacos with Veggie-Herb Salad, Quick Pickled Onions & Feta
ingredients: 12 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled feta cheese
instructions: Peel and slice half the onion into thin half-rings. Small dice remaining onion. Peel and mince garlic.
Place sliced onion in a small bowl along with vinegar and salt. Toss to combine and set aside.
Preheat a small saucepan over medium heat. Once the pan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add diced onion and garlic to the pan; cook, stirring frequently, until onion begins to soften, 3-4 minutes.
Rinse lentils under cold water and add to the pan along with the broth. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce heat to a simmer and cook until tender, 15-20 minutes.
Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the arugula if it came pre-washed.)
Juice lemon into a large bowl. Add olive oil and salt; stir to combine.
Shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard the stems and roughly chop the leaves. Add to the bowl.
Shave dill leaves off the stems; discard the stems and roughly chop the leaves. Add to the bowl.
Roughly chop arugula and add to the bowl.
Trim and small dice cucumber and tomatoes; add to the bowl.
Halve olives and add to bowl. Toss to combine the salad.
Once lentils are done, drain off excess liquid and return to pan. Add paprika and salt; stir to combine.
To serve, divide tortillas between plates and fill with lentils. Top with salad, pickled onions, and feta. Enjoy!

name: Rib Eye Steak with Buttery Sautéed Mixed Vegetables
instructions: Wash green beans, carrot, and bell pepper.
Trim green bean ends and transfer to a large bowl. Seed and slice pepper into strips lengthwise; add to bowl. Trim ends, peel, and thinly slice carrot on the diagonal; add to bowl.
Heat a grill pan, outdoor grill, or skillet over medium-high heat.
Season steak with salt and pepper on both sides.
Coat grill or skillet with oil. Add steak and cook until desired doneness, 2-5 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate and loosely cover with foil.
Heat a separate skillet over medium heat.
Peel and mince garlic.
Melt butter in skillet and add garlic; cook until fragrant, 15-30 seconds. Add vegetables and cook, stirring often, until tender-crisp, 5-6 minutes. Season with salt and pepper; toss to coat.
Serve steak with sautéed vegetables on the side. Enjoy!

name: Ribeye with Spicy "Cowboy" Butter, Butternut Squash & Brussels Sprouts
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim and peel squash; halve lengthwise, scrape out the seeds, and medium dice. Transfer to a baking sheet pan.
Trim and halve Brussels sprouts lengthwise. Add to the baking sheet with the squash.
Zest lemon into a small bowl (set aside for later use). Juice lemon over the veggies, then season with salt and pepper; toss to combine and spread out in an even layer.
Cut butter into small pieces and sprinkle over the veggies.
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast, tossing halfway through, until the veggies are fork-tender, 20-25 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, preheat a grill pan, outdoor grill, or regular skillet over medium-high heat.
While the pan heats up, pat the steak dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with salt and pepper on both sides.
Once the pan is hot, coat with butter. Add steak and grill until desired doneness, 2-5 minutes per side. Transfer to a clean plate and set aside to rest, 5 minutes.
While the steak is cooking, peel and mince shallot and garlic. Add both to the bowl with the lemon zest.
Cut additional butter into small pieces and add to the bowl along with Dijon and spices. Mash with the back of a spoon to combine the "cowboy" butter.
Thinly slice steak against the grain.
To serve, divide steak and veggies between plates. Top steak with cowboy butter and enjoy!

name: Ribeye Steak with Asparagus, Almond & Goat Cheese Salad
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Snap or cut off and discard the woody ends of the asparagus; cut the spears into 2-inch pieces at an angle. Transfer to a medium bowl and set aside.
Fill a medium saucepan about halfway with hot water (from the tap); cover with a lid and bring to a boil over high heat.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the steak dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add the almonds. Cook, stirring frequently to avoid burning, until fragrant and lightly toasted, 3 to 4 minutes. Once done, transfer to a small bowl.
Once the almonds have been transferred, increase the heat to medium-high. Add coconut oil and swirl to coat the bottom.

Carefully place the steak in the skillet; flipping every 15 to 30 seconds, cook the steak until desired doneness (5 to 7 minutes for medium-rare). (Use a thermometer or cut into the steak to check the doneness.) Once done, transfer the steak to a plate and let it rest for 5 to 10 minutes.

Once the water in the saucepan is boiling, uncover and season with salt. Add the asparagus and cook until bright green, 2 to 4 minutes (depending on the thickness of the spears). Drain in a colander and run under cold water to stop the cooking process. Set aside to drain further.
Grate all of the zest from the lemon, then juice it. Add the zest and juice to the bowl that held the asparagus.
To the lemon zest and juice, add olive oil, Dijon, salt, and pepper; whisk together.
Add the asparagus to the bowl with the dressing and toss to coat.
Crumble goat cheese into a small bowl.
To serve, divide the steak and asparagus between plates, then top the asparagus with the crumbled goat cheese and toasted almonds.

name: Ribeye Steak with Roasted Mushroom & Sun-Dried Tomato Arugula Salad
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the arugula if it came pre-washed.)
Quarter mushrooms and transfer to a baking sheet pan.
Peel and mince garlic; add to the baking sheet with the mushrooms. Drizzle with oil and vinegar, then season with salt and pepper. Stir to combine and spread out in an even layer.
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast, stirring once, until mushrooms are browned and tender, about 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, zest and juice lemon into a medium bowl. Add additional oil, Dijon, honey, salt, and pepper. Whisk to combine the dressing and set aside.
Preheat a grill pan, outdoor grill, or regular skillet over medium-high heat.
While the grill pan heats up, pat the steak dry with paper towels and place on a plate. Season with salt and pepper on both sides.

Once the grill pan is hot, coat with oil. Add steak and grill until desired doneness, 2-5 minutes per side. Transfer steak to a clean plate, loosely cover with aluminum foil, and set aside to rest, 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel, halve, and slice shallot crosswise into thin half-moons. Roughly chop sun-dried tomatoes. Place both in a small bowl.
Pick basil leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and thinly slice into ribbons. Add to the bowl with the shallot and sun-dried tomato.
Finely grate Parmesan. Add to the bowl and stir to combine.
Once the mushrooms are tender, remove from oven and top with the Parmesan mixture. Return to the oven and continue to roast until Parmesan has melted, 3-4 minutes more.
Meanwhile, thinly slice steak.
Once the Parmesan has melted, remove mushrooms from oven. Add to the bowl with the dressing, along with the arugula, and toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide salad between plates or bowls and top with steak. Enjoy!

name: Ribeye Steak with Sweet Potato Wedges & Arugula-Walnut Salad
instructions: Preheat the oven to 500°F and place the rack in the center position. Place a baking sheet in the oven to warm up.
Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the arugula if it came pre-washed.)
Cut the sweet potatoes into ½-inch-thick wedges (about 8 to 10 wedges per potato). Remove the baking sheet from the oven and transfer the potatoes to it.
Drizzle the potatoes with olive oil and season with salt and pepper; toss to coat, then spread out in a single layer.
Place the potatoes in the oven and bake for 10 minutes, then flip them over and continue to bake until they are tender, another 5 to 10 minutes.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat dry the steak with paper towels and place on a plate. Season the steak generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add coconut oil and swirl to coat the bottom.

Carefully place the steak in the skillet; flipping every 15 to 30 seconds, cook the steak until desired doneness (5 to 7 minutes for medium-rare). (Use a thermometer or cut into the steak to check the doneness.) Once done, transfer the steak to a plate and let it rest for 5 to 10 minutes.
Once the steak is done, in a salad bowl, combine and whisk together olive oil, balsamic vinegar, and Dijon.
Roughly chop the walnuts and add to the salad bowl.
Add the arugula to the salad bowl and toss to coat.
To serve, arrange the steak, sweet potato wedges, and the arugula-walnut salad on a plate. Enjoy!

name: Rich Cauliflower Mac & Cheese with Sausage
instructions: Wash cauliflower and cut off the leaves. Separate into small florets and cut the thick stems into smaller pieces. Transfer to a medium saucepan.
Add hot water (from the tap) to the pan, so that the cauliflower is just covered. Bring to a boil over high heat. Cook until fork-tender, 4-5 minutes. Drain and set aside.
Meanwhile, preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, roughly chop the sausage.

Once the skillet is hot, add butter and swirl to coat the bottom; add the sausage. Cook, stirring often, until browned and cooked through, 4-5 minutes. Once done, transfer to a plate and reduce heat to low.
Meanwhile, using a clean cutting board, wash, dry, and chop chives into small pieces; set aside.
Coarsely grate cheddar. Finely grate Parmesan.
Peel and mince garlic.
Melt more butter in skillet. Add garlic and stir until fragrant, 1-2 minutes.
Stir in cream, Dijon, paprika, and pepper.
When the cream is warmed, add cheddar and Parmesan. Cook, stirring well, until the cheese is melted and the mixture is smooth.
Add cauliflower to the cheese sauce and stir until well coated. Sprinkle with sausage and chives. Enjoy!

name: Ricotta & Spinach Pasta with Toasted Pine Nuts
instructions: Fill a medium saucepan about halfway with hot water (from the tap); cover with a lid and bring to a boil over high heat.
Trim off and discard the ends of the onion and remove the outer layer; small dice the onion (cut into ¼-inch pieces) and transfer to a small bowl.
Trim off and discard the root ends of the garlic; peel and mince or press the garlic. Add to the bowl with the onion.
Finely grate ½ cup of Parmesan. Transfer to a small bowl.
Preheat a sauté pan over medium heat.

When the water in the saucepan comes to a boil, uncover the pan and season the water with salt, then add the pasta and stir for a few seconds. Cook the pasta, uncovered, for 11 to 12 minutes (or according to package directions). Once cooked, drain the pasta in a colander, reserving ½ cup of the cooking water.
Add the pine nuts to the pan; cook, stirring constantly, until they are golden brown, 3 to 5 minutes. Transfer to a small bowl.
Once the pine nuts have been transferred, add olive oil to the pan and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add the onion and garlic to the pan; cook, stirring frequently, until the onion is softened, 3 to 5 minutes.
Add the spinach to the pan and season the mixture with salt and pepper; cook, tossing frequently, until the spinach is wilted, 1 to 2 minutes.
Add the ricotta to the pan and stir until it is thoroughly mixed with the spinach.
Add the pasta, about ½ of the Parmesan, and reserved cooking water to the pan; cook, stirring constantly, until the pasta is well combined, 1 to 2 minutes.
To serve, divide the pasta between bowls, garnish with the remaining Parmesan, and sprinkle with the toasted pine nuts. Enjoy!

name: Roast Butternut Squash with Fresh Mozzarella & Couscous-Arugula Salad
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
½ (8 oz) pkg fresh mozzarella cheese
instructions: Preheat oven to 500°F and place rack in the center position. Line a baking sheet pan with aluminum foil to make cleanup easier (optional).
Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the arugula if it came pre-washed.)

Trim butternut squash ends, halve crosswise, then cut each piece in half lengthwise; scoop out the seeds. Rub the inside of each squash piece with oil and season with salt and pepper; arrange pieces, cut-side down, on the baking sheet.
Place squash in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast until tender, so a knife can easily pierce through the flesh, 20-25 minutes.
While the squash is roasting, place couscous in a medium bowl.

Pour broth into a skillet, cover, and bring to a boil over high heat. Remove from heat, pour into the bowl with the couscous, and stir (reserve skillet for later use). Tightly cover the bowl with foil and let stand for 10 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Meanwhile, peel, halve, and thinly slice onion crosswise; trim, seed, and medium dice bell pepper.
Return the skillet to medium-high heat. Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom; add veggies and spices. Cook, stirring occasionally, until soft, 4-5 minutes. Remove from heat.
While the veggies are cooking, thinly slice mozzarella.
When the squash is done, remove from the oven and turn the pieces over, cut-side facing up. Change the oven to broil on high and position rack in the upper third of the oven.
Divide mozzarella between squash pieces and return to the oven; broil until mozzarella is golden and melted, 1-2 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, pick basil leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and thinly slice into ribbons.
Add cooked veggies, basil, arugula, pine nuts, and vinegar to the bowl with the couscous. Stir to combine the couscous salad.
To serve, divide butternut squash and couscous salad between plates or bowls. Enjoy!

name: Roast Chicken Thighs with Oregano Aioli & Beet-Cucumber Salad
ingredients: ½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled feta cheese
instructions: Preheat the oven to 450°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel, trim, and medium dice beets; place in a small saucepan and cover with hot water (from the tap). Cover and bring to a boil over high heat.
Meanwhile, peel and mince garlic; place in a small bowl along with mayo and spices. Stir to combine the aioli.
Once the water in the saucepan is boiling, reduce to a simmer and cook until beets are fork-tender, 12-14 minutes.

While the beets are cooking, pat chicken dry with paper towels and transfer to a baking sheet pan. Remove half of the aioli and divide between the chicken, spreading evenly over each thigh; season with salt and pepper. (Reserve remaining aioli for serving.)
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast until chicken is cooked through, 18-20 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, place oil, vinegar, and spices in a medium bowl; whisk to combine the dressing.
Shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl with the dressing.
Trim and medium dice cucumber; add to the bowl and set aside.
When the beets are done, drain and run under cold water to cool; set aside to drain further.
Just before serving, add beets and feta to the bowl with the dressing; stir to combine the salad.
To serve, divide chicken and salad between plates; top chicken with reserved aioli. Enjoy!

name: Roast Chicken Thighs with Tomato-Zucchini Couscous & Goat Cheese
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
In a medium saucepan, bring broth to a boil. Once boiling, remove from heat, add couscous and salt, and stir to combine. Cover and let stand for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel, halve, and large dice onion; transfer to a baking sheet pan.
Trim and quarter zucchini lengthwise, then slice crosswise into ¼-inch thick pieces; add to the baking sheet with the onion, along with the tomatoes.
Peel and mince garlic; sprinkle over the veggies, then drizzle with oil and season with spices. Toss to combine and spread out in an even layer.
Pat chicken dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with salt and pepper on both sides. Add chicken to the baking sheet and nestle into the veggies.
Place baking sheet in the oven and roast until veggies are tender and chicken is cooked through, 18-20 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, roughly chop olives; pick basil leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and thinly slice into ribbons. Add both to the pan with the couscous.
Juice lemon into the pan and stir to combine. Cover to keep warm.
Just before serving, transfer roasted veggies to the saucepan with the couscous and stir to combine.
To serve, divide veggie couscous and chicken thighs between plates; crumble goat cheese over couscous. Enjoy!

name: Roasted Asparagus with Fried Eggs & Homemade Romesco Sauce
ingredients: ½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled feta cheese
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Wash, dry, and snap or cut off woody ends of the asparagus and transfer to a baking sheet pan.
Wash, dry, trim, seed, and thinly slice bell pepper; add to the baking sheet with the asparagus. Drizzle veggies with oil, season with salt and pepper, and toss to coat.
Place veggies in the oven and roast until slightly charred and fork-tender, 10-12 minutes. Remove from the oven and set aside.
Meanwhile, preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Gently crack eggs into the skillet and season with salt and pepper. Cook until the tops of the whites are set but yolks are still runny, about 4 minutes.
While the eggs are cooking, peel and mince garlic; transfer to a blender.
Add roasted peppers, sun-dried tomatoes, almonds, oil, vinegar, and paprika to the blender. Blend until smooth.
To serve, divide asparagus, eggs, and Romesco sauce between plates. Top with feta and enjoy!

name: Roasted Broccoli Pasta with Lemon, Mint, Pistachios & Parmesan
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.

Separate broccoli into bite-sized florets; cut stems into smaller pieces. Transfer to a baking sheet pan, drizzle with oil, then season with salt and pepper. Toss to coat and spread out in an even layer.
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast until the broccoli is starting to soften, 6-7 minutes.

While the broccoli is roasting, fill a large pot halfway with hot water (from the tap), cover, and bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Uncover, add salt and pasta, and stir for a few seconds. Cook until desired firmness, 8-10 minutes.
Meanwhile, roughly chop pistachios.
Once the broccoli has started to soften, remove from the oven. Sprinkle with pistachios, stir to combine, and spread out in an even layer.
Return baking sheet to the oven. Continue to roast until broccoli is tender and lightly charred and pistachios are toasted, 10-12 minutes more. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, finely grate Parmesan and place in a small bowl.
Zest and juice lemon into the bowl with the Parmesan.
Pick mint leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add half to the bowl along with the spices. (Reserve remaining mint for serving.)
When the pasta is done, reserve a ⅓-cup of cooking water, then drain. Return pasta and reserved cooking water to the pot.

Add roasted broccoli, pistachios, and Parmesan mixture to the pot. Set the pot over medium-high heat and cook, stirring often, until liquid has evaporated and Parmesan is melted, 1-2 minutes. Remove from heat.
To serve, divide pasta between plates or bowls and sprinkle with reserved mint. Enjoy!

name: Roasted Broccoli Salad with Beans, Peppers, Pickled Onions & Pine Nuts
ingredients: ½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled feta cheese
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim, seed, and slice bell pepper lengthwise into thin strips. Transfer to a baking sheet pan.
Separate broccoli into bite-sized florets. Add to the baking sheet with the bell pepper, drizzle with oil, and season with salt; stir to coat and spread out in an even layer.
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast, stirring halfway through, until veggies are starting to char, 20-25 minutes. Remove from oven and set aside to cool.
Meanwhile, place vinegar, sugar, and salt in a small bowl; stir to combine the pickling liquid.
Peel, halve, and slice onion crosswise into thin half-moons. Add to the bowl with the pickling liquid, stir to combine, and set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add pine nuts and cook, stirring often, until golden and fragrant, about 3 minutes. Transfer to another small bowl and set aside to cool.
Place oil, vinegar, salt, and crushed red pepper in a medium bowl. Whisk to combine the dressing.
Drain and rinse beans in a colander. Add to the bowl with the dressing.
Pick mint leaves off the stems; discard stems and roughly chop the leaves. Add to the bowl.
Add cooled veggies, pickled onions, pine nuts, and feta to the bowl. Gently stir to combine the salad.
To serve, divide the salad between plates or bowls. Enjoy!

name: Roasted Carrot, Lentil & Feta Salad with Butter Lettuce
ingredients: 12 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled feta cheese
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F and position rack in the centre.
Rinse lentils under cold water and transfer to a small saucepan. Cover with broth and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to a simmer and, stirring occasionally, cook until just tender, 15-20 minutes.
Wash carrots, trim ends, and peel. Halve lengthwise and thinly slice on the diagonal into ¼ inch thick half rounds; transfer to a baking sheet.
Peel and thinly slice onion into half rings; add to sheet.
Drizzle carrots and onion with olive oil and season with cumin, salt, and pepper; toss to coat.
Place carrots in the oven and roast, tossing halfway through cooking, until tender, 10-15 minutes.
Peel and mince garlic. In a salad bowl, prepare dressing by whisking together the minced garlic, olive oil, vinegar, honey, Dijon, salt, and pepper.
Wash and dry lettuce. Tear into smaller pieces and add to salad bowl.
Wash and dry parsley. Shave leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves. Add to salad bowl.
Assemble salad by adding carrots and lentils to salad bowl and tossing.
Serve by placing salad on a plate and sprinkle with feta. Enjoy!

name: Roasted Carrot Salad with Lentils, Arugula, Pumpkin Seeds, Mint & Feta
ingredients: ½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled feta cheese
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F. Line a baking sheet pan with aluminum foil to make cleanup easier (optional).

Using a strainer, rinse lentils under cold water; drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add water and salt, cover, then bring to a boil over high heat. Once boiling, remove lid, reduce heat to a simmer, and cook until tender, 15-20 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the arugula if it came pre-washed.)
Peel, trim, and slice carrots crosswise into ½-inch thick pieces. Transfer to the baking sheet, drizzle with oil, and sprinkle with spices. Toss to coat, then spread out in an even layer.
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast carrots, stirring halfway through, until golden brown and fork-tender, 18-20 minutes. Remove from oven.
While the carrots are roasting, place oil, vinegar, and spices in a medium bowl; whisk to combine the dressing.
Peel, halve, and thinly slice shallot into half-moons; peel and mince garlic. Add both to the bowl with the dressing.
Trim and slice celery crosswise into thin pieces; add to the bowl.
Pick mint leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl.
Halve and pit avocado; scoop out with a spoon and medium dice the flesh. Add to the bowl and stir to combine.
When the lentils are done, drain in a colander, rinse with cold water, and add to the bowl.
Just before serving, add roasted carrots, arugula, and pumpkin seeds to the bowl; toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide salad between plates or bowls and top with feta. Enjoy!

name: Roasted Cauliflower & Black Bean Burrito Bowl with Cilantro Lime Rice
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add broth and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce the heat to low. Cook the rice until the liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove the rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Remove leaves and thick stems from cauliflower; cut into bite-sized florets and set aside.
In a small bowl, combine the spices.

Place the cauliflower on the baking sheet. Drizzle with oil and sprinkle with half of the seasoning mixture; toss to coat. Spread out in a single layer. Place in the oven and roast for 20 minutes, flipping once halfway through.
Small dice the onion.
Heat a large skillet over medium heat. Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add the onion to the skillet; cook, stirring frequently, until softened, 3-4 minutes.
Drain and rinse the black beans in a colander.
Add the black beans, corn, and the rest of the seasoning mixture to the skillet and cook, stirring frequently, until the corn is softened, 3-4 minutes. Remove from heat and set aside.
Small dice the tomato.
Halve and pit the avocado. Slice thinly while still in skin, then scoop out with a spoon.
Shave the cilantro leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves. When the rice is finished, add half of the cilantro to the rice.
Juice half of the lime into the rice and stir to combine. Slice the rest of the lime into wedges for garnish.
To serve, divide the rice between bowls. Top with cauliflower, bean mixture, diced tomatoes, cilantro, avocado slices, and lime wedges. Enjoy!

name: Roasted Cauliflower Tacos with Broccoli-Mango Slaw & Cilantro Sauce
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F. Line a baking sheet pan with aluminum foil to make cleanup easier (optional).
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and mince garlic; place in a medium bowl.
Add oil and spices to the bowl with the garlic; whisk to combine the spice oil.

Cut leaves from the cauliflower, separate into bite-sized florets, and cut the thick stems into smaller pieces; add to the bowl with the spice oil and toss to coat. Transfer to the baking sheet and spread out in an even layer. (Reserve bowl for later use.)
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast, tossing halfway through, until cauliflower is golden brown and tender, 15-20 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, peel mango and slice flesh away from the pit, starting with the flat sides. Small dice and place in the reserved bowl.

Quarter jalapeño pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon. Small dice and add to the bowl with the mango. (Be careful with jalapeños; do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add half of the cilantro to the bowl. (Place remaining cilantro in a small bowl and set aside for the sauce.)
Juice half of the lime into the bowl with the mango. Add broccoli slaw, pumpkin seeds, and salt; toss to combine the slaw and set aside. (Reserve remaining lime for the next step.)
Juice reserved lime into the bowl with the cilantro; add yogurt and salt. Whisk to combine the sauce and set aside.
Warm tortillas in a skillet, oven, or microwave (optional).
To serve, divide tortillas between plates; fill with slaw, cauliflower, and sauce. Enjoy!

name: Roasted Chickpea & Tomato Salad with Arugula & Feta
ingredients: ½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled feta cheese
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Drain and rinse chickpeas. Place on paper towels and pat dry.
Peel and thinly slice onion into half rings. Wash and halve tomatoes.
Place chickpeas, onion, and tomatoes on a baking sheet pan. Drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Toss to coat.
Place in the oven and roast until chickpeas are golden and tomatoes begin to collapse, 10-15 minutes.
Peel and mince garlic. In a small bowl, prepare dressing by whisking together garlic, lemon juice, olive oil, Dijon, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Wash and dry arugula. Transfer to a large bowl.
Add chickpeas, onion, tomatoes, and feta to bowl with arugula and toss.
To serve, arrange salad on a plate and drizzle with dressing. Enjoy!

name: Roasted Chickpeas, Brussels Sprouts & Carrots with Polenta
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Heat the oven to 500°F. Lightly coat a baking sheet with olive oil.

In a small saucepan, bring broth and water to a boil. Reduce heat to low and gradually add polenta in a thin steady stream, while whisking constantly, until the polenta is incorporated into the liquid. Cook, stirring occasionally, until grains are soft and the texture is creamy, 15-25 minutes.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim and quarter Brussels sprouts. Transfer to the baking sheet.
Trim and peel carrots; halve lengthwise and cut into ¼-inch-thick pieces on an angle. Transfer to the baking sheet.
Drain and rinse the chickpeas; place on a clean towel (or paper towels) and pat dry. Transfer to the baking sheet.
Toss the vegetables and chickpeas and spread out evenly on the sheet. Place in the oven and roast until the vegetables are tender and chickpeas are golden brown, 15 to 20 minutes.
Slide the thyme leaves off the stems; discard the stems and chop the leaves.
Peel and mince the garlic.
In a small bowl, combine and whisk together the thyme, garlic, oil, vinegar, salt, and pepper.
Remove the sheet from the oven. Pour the sauce over the vegetables and chickpeas; toss to coat.
Place the sheet back in the oven and continue to cook until the vegetables are tender, about 5 minutes more.
Add oil to the polenta and season with salt and pepper; stir to combine.
Divide the polenta between plates and top with the roasted vegetables and chickpeas. Enjoy!

name: Roasted Corn & Bean Tostadas with Broccoli Slaw
instructions: Preheat oven to broil and position rack under the broiler.
Remove the husks from the corn and brush with oil. Place on the top rack in the oven and cook for 6-8 minutes, flipping halfway through, until the corn begins to turn golden brown.
Wash and dry the fresh produce. Skip the broccoli slaw if it came pre-washed.
Small dice the tomato and set aside.
Shave the cilantro leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves. Set aside.
When the corn is done cooking, remove from oven and let cool for 5-6 minutes, until slightly warm to the touch.
Preheat oven to 400°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

Drizzle both sides of the tortillas with oil and sprinkle with salt; place in a single layer on baking sheet. Bake for 10-15 minutes, flipping halfway through, until the tortillas are crispy and lightly browned on both sides.
While tortillas bake, drain and rinse the beans in a colander; add to a medium bowl.
Juice one lime into the bowl with the beans.
Add oil, spices, and water to the bowl. Use a fork or potato masher to mash the mixture until smooth.
When the tortillas are done, remove from the oven and set aside.
Stand corn upright on a cutting board and use a sharp knife to carefully cut kernels off of the cob.
Cut the remaining lime into wedges.
To assemble, top the tortillas with bean mixture, tomatoes, broccoli slaw, roasted corn, and cilantro. Garnish with a lime wedge and enjoy!

name: Roasted Eggplant Flatbread with Mozzarella, Basil & Lemony Arugula
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the arugula if it came pre-washed.)
Trim and cut eggplant into ¾-inch cubes; transfer to a baking sheet pan. Drizzle with oil and season with spices; toss to coat, then spread out in a single layer.
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast, stirring halfway through, until eggplant is soft and browned, about 20 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, arrange flatbreads on another baking sheet. Place in the oven and bake, flipping halfway through, until slightly crispy, about 8 minutes. Remove from oven and set aside.
While the flatbreads are toasting, juice lemon into a medium bowl. Add oil, Dijon, honey, salt, and pepper; whisk to combine the dressing and set aside.
Place tomato sauce and spices in a small bowl; whisk to combine and set aside.
Coarsely grate mozzarella.
When the eggplant is done, prepare the flatbreads. Spread tomato sauce over each flatbread; top with mozzarella and eggplant.
Return flatbreads to the oven and bake until warmed through and cheese is melted, about 5 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, add arugula to the bowl with the dressing and toss to coat.
Pick basil leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and thinly slice into ribbons.
Slice flatbreads, divide between plates, and sprinkle with basil. Serve with lemony arugula on the side and enjoy!

name: Roasted Eggplant Pasta Alla Norma
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Wash and large dice eggplant. Transfer to a sheet pan. Drizzle with oil and season with oregano, salt, and pepper; toss to coat.
Place in the oven and, stirring halfway though, bake until softened and browned, about 20 minutes.
Fill a medium saucepan halfway with water, cover, and bring to a boil. Uncover, add salt and pasta, and stir for a few seconds. Cook until desired firmness, 8-10 minutes.
Heat a sauté pan over medium heat.
Peel and mince onion and garlic.
Coat bottom of pan with oil. Add onion and, stirring frequently, cook until softened, 4-5 minutes.
Wash and dry basil. Pick leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and thinly slice into ribbons.
Add garlic and pepper to pan. Stir until fragrant, 15-30 seconds.
Add tomatoes, vinegar, sugar, spices, and ½ of the basil (save the rest for garnishing). Cook for 4-6 minutes.
Shave or grate ⅛ cup of Parmesan.
Drain pasta and add to pan with tomatoes. Add eggplant and toss to combine.
To serve, place pasta in a shallow bowl or on a plate. Garnish with remaining basil and sprinkle with Parmesan. Enjoy!

name: Roasted Eggplant Pitas with Tzatziki & Quick Pickled Onions
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Large dice the eggplant. Transfer to a parchment lined sheet pan. Drizzle with oil and season with salt, pepper, and oregano; toss to coat. Bake for 20 minutes.
Use a grater to coarsely grate the cucumber. Transfer to a medium bowl. Add the salt, stir, and let sit for 5 minutes.
Peel and mince garlic.
Peel and thinly slice onion into half rings. Add to a small bowl along with the vinegar and salt. Toss to combine and set aside.
Halve and thinly slice the tomato.
Shave leaves off the parsley stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves.

Gather the grated cucumber in the middle of a clean dish towel and gently squeeze out the water. Add the cucumber back to the medium bowl. Stir in the minced garlic, yogurt, salt, and dill. Juice the lemon and add to the mixture. Set aside.
To assemble, slice the pita bread into halves and open the pocket. Stuff with roasted eggplant, sliced tomato, onion, parsley, and cucumber sauce. Enjoy!

name: Roasted Fennel-Quinoa Salad with Arugula, Dates, Pistachios & Feta
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled feta cheese
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
In a small saucepan, combine quinoa and broth; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to a simmer, cover, and cook for 15 minutes. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the arugula if it came pre-washed.)

Trim off root end and stalks of the fennel, leaving only the white bulbs. Halve fennel bulbs lengthwise, then slice crosswise into thin half-moons. Transfer to a baking sheet pan, drizzle with oil, then season with salt and pepper. Stir to combine and spread out in an even layer.

Place fennel in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast, stirring halfway through, until slightly browned and tender, about 20 minutes. Remove from oven and set aside to cool, about 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, juice lemon into a medium bowl. Add oil, maple syrup, and spices, then whisk to combine the dressing.
Trim and halve radishes, then slice crosswise into thin half-moons. Add to the bowl with the dressing.
Shave dill leaves off the stems; discard stems and roughly chop the leaves. Add to the bowl.
Roughly chop dates and pistachios. Add both to the bowl.
Transfer the cooked quinoa to another baking sheet. Spread out in an even layer and let cool for 5 minutes.
Add cooled fennel and quinoa to the bowl, along with arugula and feta, then toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide salad between plates or bowls. Enjoy!

name: Roasted Garlic, Mushroom & Cauliflower Fettuccine with Walnuts
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Separate cauliflower into bite-sized florets and cut stems into smaller pieces; transfer to a baking sheet pan.
Quarter mushrooms and add to the baking sheet with the cauliflower. Drizzle with oil, season with salt and pepper, and toss to combine; spread out in an even layer.
Peel garlic, place in the center of a small square of aluminum foil, and drizzle with oil; fold foil around garlic to close the packet. Add to the baking sheet with the veggies.
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast, tossing veggies halfway through, until golden brown and tender (and garlic is soft), 15-20 minutes. Remove from oven.

While the veggies are roasting, fill a medium saucepan halfway with hot water (from the tap), cover, and bring to a boil. Uncover, add salt and pasta, and stir for a few seconds. Cook until desired firmness, 8-10 minutes. Drain and return pasta to the pan. (Reserve ½-cup pasta cooking water.)
Meanwhile, shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Place in a small bowl.
Small dice tomato; add to the bowl with the parsley.
Finely grate Parmesan; add to the bowl.
Once the garlic is ready, carefully open the packet; use a fork to mash the roasted garlic. Add to the bowl.

Juice lemon into the pan with the pasta; add roasted veggies, parsley, tomato, Parmesan, roasted garlic, and reserved pasta water. Return to low heat and cook, stirring occasionally, until pasta is heated through and cheese is melted, 2-3 minutes.
Meanwhile, roughly chop walnuts.
To serve, divide pasta between plates or bowls and top with chopped walnuts. Enjoy!

name: Roasted Garlic Rosemary Chicken & Pears with Butternut Squash Mash
ingredients: 4 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Peel and mince garlic. In a medium bowl, mix together ½ of the garlic (save the rest for the mash), oil, rosemary, salt, and pepper.
Place chicken in bowl and toss to coat.
Wash, core, and slice pears into wedges.
Fill a medium saucepan halfway with water and bring to a boil.
Transfer chicken and pears to a baking dish. Place in the oven and roast for 15 minutes. Then broil until lightly browned, an additional 3-4 minutes.
Wash and peel squash. Halve, scrape out and discard the seeds, and medium dice the flesh.
Add squash to saucepan once water is boiling. Cook until very tender, 10-12 minutes.
Drain and return back to saucepan. Add broth, oil, salt, pepper, and remaining garlic. Mash until smooth.
To serve, arrange squash mash on a plate and place chicken thighs and pears on top. Enjoy!

name: Roasted Halibut with Asparagus, Tomatoes & Lemon-Caper Dill Sauce
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F. Position racks in the upper and lower thirds of the oven.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Cut butter into small pieces and place in a small bowl; set aside.

Snap or cut off woody ends of the asparagus; halve tomatoes. Transfer both to a baking sheet pan, spreading them out in an even layer. Season with salt and pepper, then sprinkle ⅓ of the butter over veggies.
Place baking sheet on lower rack of the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast, tossing halfway through, until crisp-tender, 12-15 minutes. Remove from the oven.
Meanwhile, pat halibut dry with paper towels, cut into portions (if necessary), and transfer to another baking sheet. Season with spices, then sprinkle ½ of the remaining butter over fish.
Place baking sheet on upper rack of the oven and roast until fish is cooked through, about 12 minutes. Remove from the oven.
While the fish is roasting, preheat a small saucepan over medium heat.
While the pan heats up, using a clean cutting board, peel and mince garlic.
Once the pan is hot, add remaining butter and swirl to coat the bottom. Add garlic and cook, stirring frequently, until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Zest and juice lemon into the pan with the garlic; add cream, capers, salt, and pepper. Bring sauce to a simmer and cook, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened, 3-4 minutes.
Meanwhile, using a knife, shave dill leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves.
Add half of the dill (reserving the rest for garnish) to the sauce and stir to combine.
To serve, divide fish and veggies between plates; spoon sauce over fish and sprinkle with reserved dill. Enjoy!

name: Roasted Moroccan-Spiced Drumsticks with Kale, Parsley & Feta Salad
ingredients: ½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled feta cheese
instructions: Preheat the oven to 450°F. Line a baking sheet pan with aluminum foil to make cleanup easier (optional).
Peel and mince garlic; place in a medium bowl, along with oil and spices, and whisk to combine the marinade.
Add chicken to the bowl with the marinade and turn to coat. Transfer drumsticks to the baking sheet, spreading them out in a single layer.
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast, turning once, until the chicken is golden brown and cooked through, 30-35 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Juice lemon into a clean medium bowl. Add oil, salt, and pepper; whisk to combine the dressing.
Fold kale leaves in half lengthwise and slice off the stems. Finely chop leaves and add to the bowl with the dressing; using your hands, massage kale with the dressing until wilted, 1-2 minutes.
Shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl.
Trim and quarter cucumber lengthwise, then cut crosswise into ¼-inch thick pieces; add to the bowl.
Halve tomatoes; add to the bowl, along with feta, and toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide chicken and salad between plates. Enjoy!

name: Roasted Paprika Chicken Thighs with Carrots & Potatoes
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Wash potatoes and carrots. Large dice the potatoes. Halve carrots lengthwise, then cut crosswise into thirds. Transfer to a sheet pan.
Drizzle with oil and season with salt and pepper; toss to coat.
Place in the oven and roast while you prepare the chicken, 5-10 minutes.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Season chicken with paprika, salt, and pepper.
Coat bottom of skillet with oil. Add chicken and cook until browned, 1-2 minutes per side.
Remove sheet from oven and place chicken in the middle. Return to oven and roast until chicken is cooked through and vegetables are tender, 10-15 minutes.
Wash and dry thyme. Slide leaves off the stems; discard the stems.
Remove sheet from oven and sprinkle with thyme; toss to coat.
To serve, place chicken and vegetables on a plate. Enjoy!

name: Roasted Root Vegetable Salad with Goat Cheese & Walnuts
instructions: Preheat oven to 475°F and position rack in the centre. Place a baking sheet pan in the oven to warm up.
Peel, cut into thin wedges, and transfer onion to a large bowl.
Wash and dry beets, carrots, celery, potato, and thyme.

Peel and cut beets into thin wedges; add to bowl with onion. Peel and cut carrots diagonally into ¼ inch thick rounds; add to bowl. Cut celery crosswise into ¼ inch thick pieces; add to bowl. Cut potato into thin wedges; add to bowl. Slide leaves off most of the thyme stems (saving a couple stems for garnishing); add to bowl.
Drizzle vegetables with olive oil and season with salt, and pepper; toss to coat.
Remove sheet from oven and, using a paper towel, rub with a little olive oil. Place vegetables on sheet and spread out. Place in the oven and roast until vegetables are tender, 15-20 minutes.
Heat a skillet over medium heat.
Roughly chop walnuts.
Add walnuts to skillet and, stirring constantly, cook until toasted, 2-3 minutes.
Peel and mince garlic. In a small bowl, prepare dressing by whisking together garlic, olive oil, vinegar, Dijon, salt, and pepper.
Serve salad on a plate or in a bowl, sprinkle with walnuts, crumble goat cheese over top, drizzle with dressing, and garnish with remaining thyme. Enjoy!

name: Roasted Salmon & Asparagus with Balsamic-Butter Sauce
instructions: Preheat the oven to 425°F and position rack in the centre. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Peel and mince the garlic.

Wash the asparagus and snap (or cut) off the woody ends. Transfer to the baking sheet. Drizzle with olive oil and season with the minced garlic and salt and pepper; toss to coat. Spread out in a single layer, leaving room for the salmon in the middle.
Place the salmon fillets, skin-side down, in the middle of the baking sheet. Rub with olive oil and season with salt and pepper.
Place in the oven and bake until the salmon is opaque and the asparagus is tender, 10-15 minutes.
In a small saucepan, melt the butter over medium heat. Let it brown slightly, then remove from heat. Stir in the balsamic vinegar and soy sauce. Cover to keep warm.
To serve, arrange asparagus on a plate and place the salmon on top. Spoon the balsamic-butter sauce over top. Enjoy!

name: Roasted Salmon with Garlic Buttered Leeks
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F and position rack in the centre.
Pat salmon dry with a paper towel and place, skin-side down, on a baking sheet. Rub with olive oil, drizzle with lemon juice, and season with salt and freshly ground pepper. Set aside.
Wash leeks and trim ends. Slice on the diagonal into ¼ inch thick pieces.
Heat a skillet over medium heat.
Peel and mince garlic.
Place salmon in the oven and roast until it's opaque, 10-15 minutes (depending on thickness).

Melt butter in skillet. Add garlic and stir until fragrant, 15-30 seconds. Add leeks and season with thyme, salt, and freshly ground pepper; stir to coat in the butter. Reduce heat to low and cook, stirring occasionally, until leeks are tender, about 10 minutes.
Serve salmon with buttered leeks on the side. Drizzle with juice from remaining ¼ lemon and enjoy!

name: Roasted Salmon & Tomatoes with Minted Pea Puree
instructions: Preheat the oven to 425°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Cut each of the tomatoes into 8 wedges; transfer to a medium bowl.
Drizzle the tomatoes with olive oil and season with salt and pepper; toss to coat.
Pat the salmon dry with paper towels and place, skin-side down, on a baking sheet (that is also big enough to hold the tomatoes).
Rub the salmon with olive oil and season with salt and pepper.
Transfer the tomatoes to the baking sheet and arrange in a single layer around the salmon.

Place the sheet in the oven; cook until the salmon is cooked through, 10 to 12 minutes, and the tomatoes are tender, 12 to 15 minutes. Remove the salmon from the oven once it is done and continue to cook the tomatoes.
Preheat a small saucepan over medium heat.
Peel and mince (or press) the garlic.
Once the saucepan is heated, add butter and the garlic. Cook until the butter has melted and the garlic is fragrant, 15 to 30 seconds.
Add the peas to the saucepan and mix with the butter; cook until the peas are warmed through but still bright green, 4 to 6 minutes. Once done, remove the saucepan from the heat.
While the peas cook, pick the mint leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves.
Add the minced mint to the peas and season with salt and pepper. Mash the peas with an immersion blender, potato masher, or fork until smooth.
To serve, place the minted pea purée, salmon, and tomatoes on a plate. Enjoy!

name: Roasted Sole with Honey Lemon Broccoli & Almond-Raisin Couscous Pilaf
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F. Position racks in the upper and lower thirds of the oven.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel, trim, and grate carrot; place in a small saucepan.
Add broth to the pan with the carrot, cover, and bring to a boil over high heat.
Once boiling, remove broth from the heat, add couscous and garlic powder, and stir to combine. Cover and let stand for 10 minutes.

Meanwhile, separate broccoli into bite-sized florets and cut stems into smaller pieces. Transfer to a baking sheet pan, drizzle with oil, and season with spices; toss to combine, then spread out in an even layer.
Place baking sheet on lower rack of the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast until broccoli is lightly charred and fork-tender, 12-15 minutes. Remove from oven.
While the broccoli is roasting, place spices in a small bowl and stir to combine.
Pat the fish dry with paper towels and place on another baking sheet; season with spice mix on both sides and drizzle with oil. (Reserve bowl for later use.)
Place baking sheet on upper rack of the oven and roast fish until flakey and cooked through, about 10 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, juice lemon into the reserved bowl; add honey and oil. Whisk to combine the honey-lemon sauce.
When the broccoli is done, drizzle the honey-lemon sauce over top and toss to coat.
Fluff couscous with a fork, then add almonds and raisins; gently stir to combine.
To serve, divide fish, couscous, and broccoli between plates. Enjoy!

name: Roasted Sweet Potato & Black Bean Salad with Arugula & Bell Pepper
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Wash, peel, and medium dice potatoes. Transfer to a baking sheet pan. Drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and pepper; toss to coat.
Place in the oven and roast until tender, 15-20 minutes.
Drain and rinse beans. Place on paper towels and pat dry.
Peel and mince garlic. In a small bowl, prepare dressing by whisking together garlic, lime juice, olive oil, vinegar, Dijon, honey, cumin, salt, and pepper.
Wash and dry arugula.
Wash, seed, and medium dice bell pepper.
To serve, arrange a bed of arugula on a plate, top with potatoes, beans, and bell pepper. Drizzle with dressing and enjoy!

name: Roasted Tomato, Onion & Mozzarella Flatbread with Arugula-Caper Salad
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F. Place oven racks in the upper and middle positions.
Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the arugula if it came pre-washed.)

Peel, halve, and slice onion lengthwise into ¼-inch thick pieces; halve tomatoes. Transfer both to a baking sheet pan, drizzle with oil, and season with spices. Toss to combine, then spread out in an even layer.
Place baking sheet on the upper rack of the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast, tossing halfway through, until veggies soften, about 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, arrange flatbreads on another baking sheet. Place on the lower rack and bake, flipping halfway through, until slightly crispy, about 8 minutes. Remove from oven and set aside.
While the flatbreads are baking, juice lemon into a medium bowl.
Peel and mince garlic; mince capers. Add both to the bowl with the lemon juice along with oil, Dijon, salt, and pepper; whisk to combine the dressing.
Trim, seed, and small dice bell pepper; add to the bowl with the dressing and set aside.
Coarsely grate mozzarella.
Pick basil leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and thinly slice into ribbons.
When the veggies are done, sprinkle mozzarella over the flatbreads; top with the roasted veggies and half of the basil. (Reserve remaining basil for serving.)
Return flatbreads to the oven and bake until warmed through and cheese is melted, about 5 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, add arugula to the bowl with the dressing and bell pepper; toss to combine the salad.
Slice flatbreads, divide between plates, and sprinkle with reserved basil. Serve with salad on the side and enjoy!

name: Roasted Tomato Pasta with Asparagus, Parmesan, Basil & Pine Nuts
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Place tomatoes in a baking dish and arrange in a single layer. Cut butter into small pieces and dot over the tomatoes. Drizzle with vinegar and season with salt and pepper.
Place baking dish in the oven and roast, tossing halfway through, until tomatoes begin to burst, about 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, fill a medium saucepan halfway with hot water (from the tap), cover, and bring to a boil. Uncover, add salt and pasta, and stir for a few seconds. Cook until almost done, about 6 minutes.
While the pasta is cooking, snap or cut off the woody ends of the asparagus. Cut into 1-inch pieces and set aside.
Finely grate Parmesan and set aside.

Add asparagus to the pan with the pasta and continue to cook until pasta reaches desired firmness and asparagus is tender, about 3 minutes. Drain pasta and asparagus in a colander, reserving ½-cup of pasta cooking water. (Reserve saucepan for later use.)
Meanwhile, pick basil leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and thinly slice into ribbons.
Return the saucepan to low heat. Add roasted tomatoes, drained pasta, and asparagus; cook, stirring occasionally, until tomatoes coat the pasta, 3-4 minutes.
Add Parmesan to the pan and stir until melted.
Add reserved pasta water, a few tablespoons at a time, if necessary, to reach a saucy consistency.
To serve, divide pasta between bowls, top with pine nuts, and enjoy!

name: Roasted Veggie, Dried Fruit & Pistachio Quinoa Bowl with Curry Yogurt
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
In a small saucepan, combine quinoa and broth; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to a simmer, cover, and cook for 15 minutes. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Snap or cut off the woody ends of the asparagus and cut into 2-inch pieces. Place on a baking sheet pan.
Trim and cut the zucchini crosswise into thin rounds; add to the baking sheet. Drizzle veggies with oil, season with spices, and toss to coat.
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast until veggies are fork-tender, about 15 minutes. Remove from the oven.
Meanwhile, zest and juice lime into a small bowl. Add yogurt and spices; whisk to combine the sauce.
Coarsely chop pistachios and place in another small bowl along with the raisins.
Medium dice apricots and add to the bowl with the pistachios; stir to combine.
To serve, divide quinoa between bowls and top with roasted veggies; sprinkle with fruit and nut mix. Drizzle with sauce and enjoy!

name: Roasted Zucchini Tuna Melts
ingredients: 2 (6 oz) cans chunk light tuna in water
instructions: Preheat the oven to 450°F and position rack in the centre.

Wash and dry the zucchini. Halve lengthwise and, using a spoon, scrape out the centre and reserve for later. Place the halves cut-side up on the baking sheet. Rub with olive oil and season with salt and pepper.
Place in the oven and bake until just tender when pierced with a fork, 10-15 minutes.
Small dice the reserved zucchini flesh; transfer to a large bowl.
Wash the celery, trim ends, and small dice; add to the bowl with the zucchini. Peel and mince the garlic; add to the bowl.
Add tuna, lemon juice, olive oil, dill, salt, and pepper to the bowl with vegetables and mix together.
Finely grate ½ cup of Parmesan.
Once the zucchini is done, take it out of the oven. Turn on the broiler and position rack in the upper third of the oven.
Fill the zucchini halves with the tuna mixture and sprinkle with the grated Parmesan. Return to the oven and broil until the cheese has browned, 2-3 minutes.
Cut the remaining ¼ lemon into wedges for serving.
To serve, place the zucchini tuna melts on a plate and garnish with lemon wedges. Enjoy!

name: Romaine Salad with Crispy Smoked Salmon, Egg & Lemon-Caper Dressing
instructions: Place eggs in a small saucepan, cover with water, and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to a simmer and cook for 8 minutes. Drain hot water and add ice or run under cold water to cool.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Zest and juice lemon into a medium bowl.
Peel and mince garlic; add to the bowl with the lemon zest.
Mince capers; add to the bowl along with cream, mayo, Dijon, honey, salt, and pepper. Whisk to combine the dressing and set aside.
Preheat a large skillet over medium-high heat.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Working in batches if necessary, add smoked salmon slices to the skillet in a single layer; cook, flipping once, until crispy, about 4 minutes. Remove to a paper towel-lined plate and set aside.
Meanwhile, peel, halve, and thinly slice shallot; add to the bowl with the dressing.
Trim and thinly slice radishes; add to the bowl.
Medium dice tomato and add to the bowl.
Halve avocado and remove pit; scoop out the flesh and medium dice. Add to the bowl.
Chop or tear lettuce into bite-sized pieces; add to the bowl and toss to combine the salad.
Peel and slice eggs crosswise into thin rounds. Chop or tear crispy smoked salmon into bite-sized pieces.
To serve, divide salad between plates or bowls; top with eggs and crispy smoked salmon. Enjoy!

name: Roman Egg Drop Soup (Stracciatella) with Olive, Tomato & Avocado Salad
ingredients: 32 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)
Mince olives and sun-dried tomatoes; transfer both to a small bowl along with oil, vinegar, salt, and pepper. Stir to combine the tapenade and set aside.
Pour broth into a medium saucepan, add spices, and bring to a boil over medium heat. Once boiling, reduce to a simmer.
Meanwhile, pick basil leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and thinly slice into ribbons; transfer to a medium bowl.
Finely grate Parmesan; add to the bowl with the basil (setting a small handful aside for garnish).
Juice lemon into the bowl.
Add eggs to the bowl and whisk until well blended; set aside.
Roughly chop spinach.
Add spinach to the simmering broth in handfuls, waiting for the spinach to wilt slightly before adding the next handful.
Slowly pour the egg mixture into the soup, while gently stirring, to separate into ribbons. Simmer until the egg is cooked through, 2-3 minutes; cover and remove from heat.
Meanwhile, halve and pit the avocado. Slice thinly while still in skin and scoop out with a spoon. Thinly slice tomatoes.
Arrange avocado and tomato slices on plates and spoon tapenade over top.
Divide soup between bowls and top with reserved Parmesan. Serve with salad on the side and enjoy!

name: Rosemary Chicken Thighs with Roasted Winter Vegetables
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F. Position rack in the center.
Wash carrots, turnip, and potato.

Slice carrots diagonally into ¼ inch thick pieces and transfer to a baking sheet pan. Peel turnip, halve lengthwise, slice crosswise into ¼ inch thick half rounds, and add to pan. Halve potato lengthwise, slice crosswise into ¼ inch thick half rounds, and add to pan. Peel onion, cut into thin wedges, and add to pan.
Place pan in the oven and begin roasting vegetables while you prepare the sauce and chicken, about 10 minutes.
Peel and mince garlic. Wash rosemary and slide leaves off most of the stems (leave a couple stems for garnishing).
In small bowl, prepare sauce by combining garlic, rosemary leaves, olive oil, Dijon, thyme, salt, and pepper.

Remove pan from oven. Place chicken thighs over top vegetables. Drizzle sauce over top and toss chicken and vegetables until well coated. Then return to oven and roast until vegetables are tender and chicken is cooked through, about 15 minutes.
Remove pan from oven. Change oven setting to broil and position rack about 6 inches from the top. Return pan to oven and broil until chicken and vegetables are lightly golden, 2-3 minutes.
Place vegetables and chicken thighs on a plate. Garnish with remaining rosemary stems and enjoy!

name: Rosemary-Parmesan Crusted Chicken with Olive, Pine Nut & Arugula Salad
ingredients: ¾ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F. Line a baking sheet pan with aluminum foil to make cleanup easier (optional). Coat with a thin layer of oil.
Finely grate Parmesan and place in a medium bowl.
Add bread crumbs and spices to the bowl with the Parmesan; stir to combine the coating.
Crack egg into another medium bowl and beat with a whisk or fork.

Pat chicken dry with paper towels and place on a cutting board. Holding a knife parallel to the cutting board, cut the chicken in half horizontally to form thin cutlets. Sprinkle flour over both sides to coat.
Dip chicken cutlets, one at a time, into the egg; shake off excess, then dredge in the bread crumb coating, pressing to adhere. Transfer to the baking sheet.
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and bake, flipping halfway through, until the chicken is golden and cooked through, 15-18 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the arugula if it came pre-washed.)
Using a clean cutting board, slice half of the lemon into wedges and set aside for serving. Juice remaining lemon into a clean medium bowl.
Add oil, Dijon, maple syrup, salt, and pepper to the bowl with the lemon juice; whisk to combine the dressing.
Trim, halve, and thinly slice cucumber crosswise into half-moons; add to the bowl with the dressing.
Trim, peel, halve, and thinly slice carrot crosswise into half-moons; add to the bowl.
Halve olives; add to the bowl along with the arugula and pine nuts. Toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide chicken and salad between plates. Squeeze lemon over the chicken and enjoy!

name: Rosemary Pork Chops with Balsamic-Strawberry Sauce & Green Beans
instructions: Fill a medium saucepan about halfway with water, cover, and bring to a boil.
While the water comes to a boil, wash the fresh produce.
Trim and discard the ends of the green beans; transfer the beans to a medium bowl and set beside the stove.
Slide the rosemary leaves off the stems; discard the stems and roughly chop the leaves. Transfer to a small bowl.
Peel and mince the garlic; add to the rosemary.
Add olive oil to the rosemary and garlic; mix together.

Once the water in the saucepan is boiling, add the green beans. Cook until bright green and tender-crisp, 3 to 4 minutes. Once done, drain in a colander and rinse under cold water to stop the cooking process. Set aside to drain further.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat.
Place the pork chops on a plate and season with salt and pepper, then rub with the rosemary and garlic mixture.
Place the pork chops in the hot skillet and pour in the remaining oil mixture; cook until cooked through, 3 to 5 minutes per side (depending on their thickness). Once done, transfer to a plate.
While the pork cooks, trim and discard the stem ends of the strawberries; slice the strawberries and transfer to a medium bowl.

Once the pork chops have been transferred, add the strawberries, balsamic vinegar, and honey to the skillet. Cook, scraping up any browned bit from the bottom of the skillet, until the strawberries have softened and the sauce is slightly thickened, 5 to 6 minutes.
Transfer the green beans to a bowl and season with salt and pepper; toss to mix.
To serve, place the green beans and pork chops on a plate and spoon the balsamic-strawberry sauce over top. Enjoy!

name: Rosemary Salmon, Butternut Squash & Creamy Portobello Mushroom Rice
