Return skillet to medium heat. Once hot, add chili oil and cook until sizzling and fragrant, about 30 seconds. Remove from heat and immediately drizzle over the zucchini noodles. Toss to coat.
Thinly slice steak against the grain.
To serve, divide steak and zucchini noodles between plates. Enjoy!

name: Seared Striploin with Blue Cheese Butter & Lemony Zucchini-Leek Sauté
ingredients: ½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled blue cheese
¾ lb striploin (New York strip) steak
instructions: Place blue cheese, butter, and thyme in a small bowl; set aside to soften.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.

Trim off the root end and dark green top of the leek, leaving only the white and pale green parts. Cut the leek in half lengthwise and rinse under running water, separating the layers to remove any dirt and grit. Slice crosswise into ¼-inch thick pieces and place in another small bowl.
Peel and mince garlic; add to the bowl with the leek and set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the steak dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with salt and pepper on both sides.

Once the skillet is hot, add butter and swirl to coat the bottom. Add steak to the skillet and cook until desired doneness, 2-5 minutes per side. Transfer steak to a clean plate and loosely cover with aluminum foil.
Meanwhile, trim and halve zucchini lengthwise, then cut crosswise into ¼-inch thick half-moons.
When the steak is done, return the skillet to medium-high heat, add more butter, and swirl to coat the bottom. Add the leek, garlic, and spices; sauté until soft and golden, 3-4 minutes.
Add zucchini and water to the skillet; continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until the liquid is evaporated and zucchini is fork-tender, 5 minutes more.
While the zucchini is cooking, gently mash the softened butter, blue cheese, and thyme with the back of a spoon to combine.
When the zucchini is done, juice lemon into the skillet, stir to combine, and remove from heat.
Thinly slice steak against the grain.
To serve, divide steak and veggie sauté between plates; top steak with blue cheese butter and enjoy!

name: Sesame Beef, Asparagus & Carrot Lettuce Wraps with Cilantro
ingredients: ¾ lb striploin (New York strip) steak
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Snap or cut off the woody ends of the asparagus and cut into 1-inch pieces.
In a small saucepan, bring a ½-inch of water to a boil over high heat. Add asparagus and cook, uncovered, until crisp-tender, 3-5 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel and mince or grate ginger; transfer to a medium bowl.
Add soy sauce, oil, and vinegar to the bowl with the ginger; whisk to combine the dressing.
When the asparagus is done, drain and add to the bowl with the dressing; set aside.
Preheat a grill pan, outdoor grill, or regular skillet over medium-high heat.
While the grill pan heats up, pat the steak dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with salt and pepper on both sides.

Once the grill pan is hot, coat with oil. Add steak and grill until desired doneness, 2-5 minutes per side. Transfer to a clean plate, cover loosely with aluminum foil, and set aside to rest for about 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel and trim carrots. Using a julienne (or regular) peeler, peel carrots into thin noodle-like sticks; add to bowl with the asparagus.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves.
Slice lime into wedges.
Thinly slice steak against the grain and add to the bowl with the vegetables. Toss to combine.

Separate the lettuce into leaves. Pile leaves, in stacks of two per wrap, onto plates. Fill with steak, vegetables, and cilantro; sprinkle with sesame seeds. Serve with lime wedges on the side and enjoy!

name: Sesame Chicken & Broccoli with Basmati Rice
ingredients: ½ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add water and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
In a medium bowl, whisk together egg and cornstarch.
Cut chicken into bite-sized pieces. Add to egg mixture and toss to coat. Set aside.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce the heat to low. Cook the rice until the liquid is fully absorbed, 15 to 18 minutes. Once done, remove the rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Wash and cut broccoli into same-size florets. Cut remaining stalks into smaller pieces. Wash, trim root ends, and chop green onions.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Peel and mince garlic. In a small bowl, prepare sauce by whisking together garlic, honey, soy sauce, oil, and seeds. Set aside.
Coat bottom of skillet with oil. Add chicken and cook until golden brown, 2-3 minutes per side. Transfer to a bowl.
Return skillet to stove and add more oil. Add broccoli and, stirring frequently, cook until tender and bright green, 3-4 minutes.
Return chicken to skillet, pour in sauce, and add onions. Stir and cook until sauce thickens, 1-2 minutes. Remove from heat.
Uncover rice and fluff with a fork.
To serve, place rice in a bowl and top with stir fry. Enjoy!

name: Sesame Crusted Chicken with Snap Pea, Cucumber & Cilantro Salad
ingredients: ¾ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and mince ginger; place in a medium bowl.
Juice lime into the bowl with the ginger.

Quarter jalapeño pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon. Mince and add to the bowl. (Be careful with jalapeños; do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl along with oil and salt; whisk to combine the dressing and set aside.
Place sesame seeds and cornstarch another medium bowl; stir to combine.

Pat chicken dry with paper towels and place on a cutting board. Holding a knife parallel to the cutting board, cut the chicken in half horizontally to form thin cutlets; season with salt and pepper on both sides.
Spread mayo over both sides of the chicken, then dredge in the sesame coating, pressing gently to adhere. Transfer to a plate.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom; add the chicken and cook until the coating is golden and chicken is cooked through, 3-4 minutes per side. Remove from heat.
Meanwhile, using a clean cutting board, trim and quarter cucumber lengthwise, then cut crosswise into thin pieces. Add to the bowl with the dressing.
Cut snap peas crosswise into thin pieces, add to the bowl, and toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide chicken and salad between plates. Enjoy!

name: Sesame Crusted Cod with Green Bean-Bell Pepper Sauté & Rice
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add water and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Cook rice until liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim green beans, place in a medium bowl, and set aside.
Pat the cod dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with salt and pepper on both sides.
Place egg and cornstarch in another medium bowl; beat with a whisk or fork until smooth.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat.
While the skillet heats up, place sesame seeds on another plate. Dip cod in the egg mixture, then dredge in the sesame seeds, pressing gently to adhere; return to the plate.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add cod and pan-fry until golden brown and cooked through, 3-4 minutes per side. Transfer to a clean plate and loosely cover with aluminum foil. (Reserve skillet for later use.)
Meanwhile, trim, seed, and slice bell pepper lengthwise into thin strips; add to the bowl with the green beans.
Peel and mince ginger and garlic; add both to the bowl.
Return skillet to medium heat, add more oil, and swirl to coat the bottom. Add veggies, salt, and pepper; cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, 6-7 minutes. Remove from heat.
To serve, divide rice between plates or bowls; top with cod and veggies. Enjoy!

name: Sesame Encrusted Salmon over Tahini-Parmesan Caesar Salad with Apple
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Zest the lemon into a large salad bowl. Juice half of the lemon into the same bowl. Cut remaining lemon into wedges and set aside.
Add water, tahini, Dijon, oil, salt, and pepper to the bowl with lemon juice and zest; whisk until the dressing becomes smooth and glossy.
Peel and finely mince garlic. Finely mince anchovy fillet; transfer both to the salad bowl.
Finely grate half of the Parmesan and add to the salad bowl (set the rest aside for garnish). Stir to combine and set aside.
Pat the salmon fillets dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with salt and pepper.
Combine the egg and cornstarch into a medium bowl; beat with a whisk or fork until smooth and frothy.
Preheat a nonstick skillet over medium heat.

While the skillet is heating, dip the skinless side of the salmon into the egg mixture and place back on the plate, skin-side down. Sprinkle sesame seeds over the surface of the fish, pressing down gently with your fingers to adhere.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom.

Add salmon to the skillet, sesame-seed side down, and cook until crust is firm and seeds are golden brown, about 3 minutes. Flip and cook until salmon is cooked through and skin is crispy, 5-7 minutes longer. Remove skillet from the heat.
Meanwhile, chop or tear the romaine into bite-sized pieces and transfer to the bowl with the dressing.
Wash, core, and thinly slice the apple; add to the bowl and toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide salad and salmon between bowls or plates. Grate reserved Parmesan over top and garnish with lemon wedges. Enjoy!

name: Sesame-Ginger Orzo Pasta Salad with Shrimp, Carrot & Bell Pepper
ingredients: ¾ lb raw peeled shrimp, fresh or frozen
instructions: Fill a medium saucepan halfway with hot water (from the tap), cover, and bring to a boil. Uncover, add salt and orzo, and stir for a few seconds. Cook until desired firmness, about 8 minutes. Drain and rinse under cold water to cool. Set aside.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and mince ginger. Place in a medium bowl along with soy sauce, vinegar, oil, sesame seeds, honey, and spices. Whisk to combine the dressing.
Peel, trim, and coarsely grate carrot. Add to the bowl with the dressing.
Trim and cut green onions crosswise into thin pieces. Add to the bowl.
Trim and quarter cucumber lengthwise, then cut crosswise into thin pieces.
Trim, seed, and small dice bell pepper. Add to the bowl and set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.

While the skillet heats up, if using frozen shrimp, place them in a colander and run under cold water to thaw them slightly and remove any ice crystals. (If using fresh shrimp, skip this step.) Place the shrimp on a clean towel or paper towels and pat dry.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add shrimp, salt, and pepper; cook, stirring occasionally, until just opaque, 2-3 minutes. Remove from heat.
Meanwhile, add cooled orzo to the bowl with the veggies and dressing. Stir to combine the salad.
To serve, divide orzo pasta salad between plates or bowls. Top with shrimp and enjoy!

name: Sesame Roasted Chickpea & Veggie Bowl with Quinoa
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
In a small saucepan, combine quinoa and broth; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to a simmer, cover, and cook for 15 minutes. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Drain and rinse the chickpeas; set aside to drain further.
Trim and halve zucchini lengthwise, then slice crosswise into half rounds. Transfer to a medium bowl.
Separate broccoli into bite-sized florets and cut stems into smaller pieces. Add to the bowl with the zucchini.
Quarter mushrooms and add to the bowl.
Peel and mince garlic and ginger; add to the bowl along with oil, salt, and pepper. Toss to combine, transfer to a baking sheet pan, and spread out in an even layer.
Place veggies in the oven and roast until starting to brown, about 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, place chickpeas, oil, and soy sauce in the bowl used for the veggies; stir to coat.
Once the veggies are starting to brown, add seasoned chickpeas to the baking sheet; return to the oven and continue to bake until the veggies are fork-tender, 5 minutes more.
Place additional soy sauce, maple syrup, and chili-garlic sauce in the bowl; whisk to combine the sauce.
To serve, divide quinoa between bowls. Top with roasted chickpeas, veggies, and sesame seeds. Drizzle with sauce and enjoy!

name: Sesame Salmon over Warm Spinach, Curried Cauliflower & Cucumber Salad
instructions: Preheat the oven to 425°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Cut leaves off the cauliflower, separate into small florets, and cut the thick stems into smaller pieces; transfer to a baking sheet pan.
Drizzle cauliflower with oil and season with curry powder; toss to combine and spread out in an even layer.
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast until the cauliflower starts to soften, about 12 minutes.
Meanwhile, juice lemon into a medium bowl; add mayo, Dijon, salt, and pepper. Whisk to combine the dressing.
Trim and halve cucumber lengthwise; thinly slice crosswise into half-moons. Add to the bowl with the dressing and set aside.
Pat the salmon dry with paper towels and place on a plate; coat both sides with oil and season with salt and pepper on the top side.

Remove baking sheet from the oven, stir the cauliflower, and push to one side. Place salmon on the other side of the baking sheet and return to the oven. Bake until salmon is cooked through and cauliflower is tender, 10-15 minutes. Remove from the oven.
While the salmon is cooking, preheat a skillet over medium heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add sesame seeds and toast, stirring often, until golden, 2-3 minutes; remove from heat.
Once done, add the roasted cauliflower and spinach to the bowl with the dressing and cucumber. Toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide salad between plates or bowls; top with salmon and sesame seeds. Enjoy!

name: Sesame Shrimp Stir-Fry with Egg, Asparagus, Bok Choy, Edamame & Rice
ingredients: ¾ lb raw peeled shrimp, fresh or frozen
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add water and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Cook rice until liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.

If using frozen shrimp, place them in a colander and run under cold water to thaw them slightly and remove any ice crystals. (If using fresh shrimp, skip this step.) Place the shrimp on a clean towel or paper towels and pat dry.
Trim green onions and cut crosswise into ¼-inch pieces; place in a medium bowl.
Snap or cut off woody ends of the asparagus; cut into 1-inch pieces and add to the bowl with the green onion.
Trim bok choy and cut crosswise into 1-inch strips; add to the bowl and set aside.
Peel and mince ginger; set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, place eggs, salt, and pepper in a small bowl; whisk to combine.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Pour eggs into the skillet; scramble using a combination of stirring and folding. Cook until eggs are no longer runny, 2-3 minutes. Remove eggs to a plate and set aside.
Return the skillet to medium-high heat, add more oil, and swirl to coat the bottom. Add ginger and cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Add shrimp, veggies, and edamame to the skillet; cook, stirring occasionally, until veggies are tender and shrimp are cooked through, 5-7 minutes.
Return eggs to the skillet. Add soy sauce and sesame seeds; stir to combine and remove from heat.
To serve, divide rice and shrimp stir-fry between plates or bowls. Enjoy!

name: Sesame Tofu & Snap Pea Stir-Fry with Basmati Rice
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Season the rice with salt and add water; bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce the heat to low. Cook the rice until the liquid is fully absorbed, 15 to 18 minutes. Once done, remove the rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Halve the sugar snap peas at an angle and transfer to a medium bowl.
Trim off and discard the ends of the green onions; cut the onions crosswise into ¼-inch pieces at an angle. Transfer to a small bowl.
Trim off and discard the root ends of the garlic; peel and mince or press the garlic. Add to the bowl with the snap peas.
Drain the tofu and pat dry with paper towels; cut into ¾-inch cubes.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat.
Add the sesame seeds to the skillet; toast, stirring frequently, until golden brown, 2 to 3 minutes. Once done, transfer to a small bowl.
Once the sesame seeds have been transferred, increase the heat to medium-high and add coconut oil to the skillet.
Add the tofu to the skillet; cook, stirring occasionally, until golden brown, 4 to 6 minutes. Once done, transfer to a bowl.

Once the tofu has been transferred, add more coconut oil to the skillet, followed by the snap peas and garlic. Cook, stirring frequently, until the peas are bright green and slightly softened, 2 to 3 minutes.
In a small bowl, combine and whisk together cornstarch, water, soy sauce, rice vinegar, honey, and sesame oil.

Return the tofu to the skillet, add about ¾ of the green onions (save the rest for garnishing), and pour in the sauce. Cook, stirring constantly, until the mixture is well coated with the sauce, 1 to 2 minutes. Once done, remove from the heat.
Uncover the rice and fluff with a fork.
To serve, divide the rice between bowls, top with the stir fry, and sprinkle with the remaining green onions and toasted sesame seeds. Enjoy!

name: Sesame Tuna Rice Bowl with Lettuce, Cucumber, Radish & Avocado
ingredients: 2 (6 oz) cans chunk light tuna in water
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add water and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Cook rice until liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
While the rice is cooking, trim and cut green onions crosswise into thin pieces. Place half in a small bowl. (Reserve remaining green onions for serving.)
Drain tuna, add to the bowl with the green onion, and flake with a fork. Add mayo, oil, vinegar, soy sauce, and chili-garlic sauce; stir to combine and set aside.
Place additional mayo, vinegar, soy sauce, sugar, and garlic powder in another small bowl. Whisk to combine the dressing and set aside.
Trim and quarter cucumber lengthwise, then cut crosswise into bite-sized pieces. Place on a plate.
Trim and slice radishes crosswise into thin rounds. Add to the plate with the cucumber.
Halve and pit avocado; using a spoon, scoop out the flesh and medium dice. Add to the plate.
Halve lettuce lengthwise, then slice crosswise into thin (shred-like) strips.
Divide rice, tuna, and veggies between bowls; top with reserved green onions and sesame seeds. Serve with dressing on the side and enjoy!

name: Sheet Pan Asian Chicken Drumsticks with Broccoli & Spiced Walnuts
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F, position a rack in the center position and another in the bottom position. Line two baking sheet pans with aluminum foil (optional).
Peel and mince garlic and ginger; transfer to a large bowl.
Add soy sauce, oil, chili-garlic sauce, and sugar to the bowl and whisk to combine the marinade. Add the chicken and toss to coat.
Spread chicken out in a single layer on a prepared sheet pan. Place on the bottom rack of the oven and roast until the chicken is cooked through, 30-35 minutes. Reserve marinade.
Wash broccoli and cut into small, bite-sized florets. Thinly slice the thicker stem. Transfer to a medium bowl.
Toss broccoli with soy sauce and oil. Spread out in a single layer on the other baking sheet and place in the oven for 5-8 minutes while you prepare the nuts.
Remove chicken from the oven. Use tongs to flip each drumstick. Spoon on remaining marinade, and return to the oven.
Roughly chop walnuts. In a small bowl, toss walnuts with water to moisten.
In another small bowl, stir together sugar, cinnamon, and cayenne pepper. Toss moistened walnuts in the spice mixture.
Remove the broccoli pan from the oven and sprinkle the walnuts on top. Return the pan to the oven for an additional 5-8 minutes or until broccoli is tender-crisp, and walnuts are toasted.
To serve, arrange chicken, broccoli, and walnuts on a plate. Enjoy!

name: Sheet Pan Chicken with Maple-Thyme Squash & Brussels Sprouts
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim and peel the squash. Halve lengthwise, scrape out seeds, and medium dice the flesh. Transfer to a baking sheet pan.
Trim and halve Brussels sprouts; add to the baking sheet with the squash.
Slide thyme leaves off the stems; discard stems and sprinkle leaves over the veggies.
Peel and mince garlic; sprinkle over the veggies.
Drizzle veggies with oil and maple syrup; season with salt and pepper. Toss to combine and spread out in a single layer.
Season both sides of the chicken with salt and pepper; nestle chicken in the veggies on the baking sheet.
Place baking sheet in the oven; bake until the chicken is cooked through and veggies are tender, about 20 minutes.
To serve, divide roasted veggies and chicken between plates. Enjoy!

name: Sheet Pan Chicken Tikka Masala with Roasted Cauliflower & Red Onion
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Peel and mince or grate the ginger. Peel and mince or press the garlic. Set half of the garlic aside.
In a medium bowl, combine ginger, tomato paste, cumin, paprika, cayenne, and salt, with half of the garlic, and yogurt. Add chicken and toss to coat.

Wash cauliflower and cut off the leaves. Separate into small florets and cut the thick stems into smaller pieces; transfer to a sheet pan. Peel and cut onion into ½-inch pieces; add to the sheet pan with the cauliflower.
Toss cauliflower and onion on the pan with oil and season with salt and pepper. Arrange in a single layer and place in the oven. Roast until the cauliflower is fork-tender (about 18-20 minutes).
Transfer the chicken to a sheet pan, spreading the pieces out in a single layer. Place the pan in the oven and roast until cooked through (18-20 minutes).
Meanwhile, combine olive oil, paprika, cumin, salt, and remaining yogurt and garlic in a medium small bowl.
Wash and dry parsley. Shave leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves. Once cooked, remove the cauliflower from the oven and toss with fresh parsley.
To serve, arrange the chicken and vegetables on plates, and top chicken with a dollop of yogurt sauce. Enjoy!

name: Sheet Pan Gnocchi Bake with Bacon, Mushrooms, Arugula & Green Peas
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Wash, dry, and quarter mushrooms. Place in a medium bowl.
Peel, halve, and slice onion lengthwise into thin strips. Peel and mince garlic. Add both to the bowl with the mushrooms.
Small dice bacon and add to the bowl.
Add gnocchi, oil, and spices to the bowl. Stir to combine, transfer to a large baking sheet pan, and spread out in an even layer.
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast, stirring halfway through, until gnocchi is golden brown and bacon is crispy, about 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, place Dijon, vinegar, Worcestershire, and honey in a small bowl. Stir to combine the sauce.
Wash and dry arugula (skip this step if it came pre-washed).
When the gnocchi is done, remove from the oven. Add the sauce, arugula, and peas to the baking sheet; stir to combine and spread out in an even layer.
Return baking sheet to the oven and continue to roast until arugula is wilted and peas are warmed through, 2-3 minutes. Remove from oven.
To serve, divide gnocchi bake between plates or bowls. Enjoy!

name: Sheet Pan Lemony Chicken & Potatoes
ingredients: ½ lb chicken thighs, boneless skinless
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F and position the rack in the center. Line a baking sheet pan with parchment paper.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Halve the new potatoes and cut the cauliflower into florets. Toss in a bowl with olive oil, salt, and pepper. Arrange in a single layer on the baking sheet pan and bake for 15 minutes.
Season the chicken with salt and pepper on both sides, set aside.
Grate all of the zest from the lemon, then juice the lemon into a small bowl.
Peel and mince the garlic, add to bowl with the lemon juice and zest. Add olive oil, mustard, honey, and oregano and whisk together.
Quarter and thinly slice the red onion. Remove the sheet pan from the oven and add onions on top, dispersing evenly.
Lay the chicken on top of the vegetables and drizzle evenly with the lemon sauce.
Return the sheet pan to the oven and bake until chicken is golden brown and cooked through, about 20 minutes.
To serve, divide chicken and vegetables between plates and top with sauce from pans. Enjoy!

name: Sheet Pan Pork Chops with Apricots, Red Cabbage & Blue Cheese
ingredients: ½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled blue cheese
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F. Line a baking sheet with aluminum paper (optional).
Wash cabbage, quarter, and cut off core. Thinly slice crosswise into shreds and transfer to a medium bowl. Toss with oil, balsamic vinegar, salt, and pepper.
Use tongs to transfer cabbage to a baking sheet pan, leaving the excess vinegar in the bowl. Spread cabbage out in an even layer on a baking sheet and place in the oven.
Slice the apricots in half lengthwise. Add to the bowl and toss in the remaining oil and vinegar; allow to soak in the vinegar mixture while the cabbage cooks.
Wash and dry thyme. Slide leaves off the stems; discard the stems.

Pat the pork chops dry, rub with olive oil, and season with salt, pepper, and thyme. Arrange on a baking sheet and place in the oven. Roast until pork chops are cooked through and cabbage is fork-tender (18-20 minutes).
During the last 5 minutes of cooking, sprinkle the apricots and the blue cheese over the cabbage.
To serve, arrange a bed of cabbage, apricots, and blue cheese on a plate and top with a pork chop. Enjoy!

name: Sheet Pan Roasted Chicken & Veggie Pitas with Lemony Yogurt
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Zest lemon into a small bowl, add yogurt, and whisk to combine. Set aside.
Peel and mince garlic; place a medium bowl.
Juice lemon into the bowl with the garlic. Add oil, honey, and spices; whisk to combine.
Cut the chicken into small bite-sized pieces and add to the bowl.
Peel, halve, and thinly slice the sweet potato into half rounds; add to the bowl.
Peel, trim, and cut the onion into thick wedges; add to the bowl and toss to coat.

Transfer chicken and veggies to a baking sheet pan and arrange in a single layer. Place in the oven and bake, tossing once, until the chicken is cooked through and veggies are fork-tender, 20-25 minutes.
Meanwhile, trim and thinly slice the cucumber; place in another medium bowl along with the salt and pepper.
Shave the cilantro leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves. Add half to the bowl with the cucumber and toss to combine; reserve the other half for garnish.
Toast pitas if desired.
To serve, divide pitas between plates and spread with lemon yogurt. Top with chicken, veggies, cucumbers, and remaining cilantro. Enjoy!

name: Sheet Pan Salmon with Honey-Dijon Roasted Kale & Potatoes
instructions: Preheat the oven to 450°F and place the rack in the center position.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Medium dice the potatoes and transfer to a sheet pan.
Drizzle the potatoes with olive oil and season with salt and pepper; toss thoroughly to coat, then arrange in a single layer.
Place the potatoes in the oven and roast for 10 minutes while you prepare the kale and salmon.
In a large bowl, combine and whisk together olive oil, Dijon, honey, salt, and pepper.
Cut out and discard the kale stems; chop leaves crosswise into 1-inch strips. Add the kale to the bowl with the dressing and toss to coat.
Pat dry the salmon with paper towels and place on a plate; rub with olive oil and season with salt and pepper.
Remove the sheet pan from the oven. Evenly spread the kale over the potatoes, then top with the salmon.
Return the pan to the oven; roast until the salmon is cooked through and the kale is crispy; 8 to 10 minutes.
To serve, divide the potatoes and kale between plates and top with the salmon. Enjoy!

name: Sheet Pan Shrimp Fajita Rice Bowl with Avocado, Lime & Cilantro
ingredients: ¾ lb raw peeled shrimp, fresh or frozen
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add water and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Cook rice until liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
While the rice is cooking, juice half of the lime into a medium bowl. Cut remaining lime into wedges and set aside for serving.
Add oil, soy sauce, and spices to the bowl with the lime juice. Stir to combine the spice paste and set aside.
Trim, seed, and slice bell peppers lengthwise into thin strips. Transfer to a baking sheet pan.

Peel, halve, and slice onion crosswise into ½-inch thick half-moons. Add to the baking sheet with the peppers. Drizzle with half of the spice paste, stir to coat, and spread out in an even layer. (Set remaining spice paste aside for later use.)
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast, stirring halfway through, until peppers are fork-tender, 15-18 minutes.

Meanwhile, if using frozen shrimp, place them in the colander and run under cold water to thaw them slightly and remove any ice crystals. (If using fresh shrimp, skip this step.) Place the shrimp on a clean towel or paper towels and pat dry.
Add shrimp to the bowl with the reserved spice paste. Gently toss to coat.

When the veggies are tender, remove from the oven. Add shrimp to the baking sheet and toss to combine. Return baking sheet to the oven and continue to roast until veggies are browned and shrimp are cooked through, about 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, halve and pit avocado; using a spoon, scoop out the flesh and slice crosswise into thin half-moons.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and roughly chop the leaves.
When the veggies and shrimp are done, remove from the oven. Add half of the cilantro to the baking sheet and stir to combine. (Reserve remaining cilantro for serving.)
Divide rice between bowls. Top with shrimp, veggies, avocado, and reserved cilantro. Serve with lime wedges and enjoy!

name: Sheet Pan Steak, Bell Pepper, Onion & Carrot Fajitas with Lime Crema
ingredients: ¾ lb striploin (New York strip) steak
instructions: Preheat the oven to 450°F. Line a baking sheet pan with aluminum foil to make cleanup easier (optional).
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Place spices in a small bowl and stir to combine.
Pat steak dry with paper towels and place in the center of the baking sheet; drizzle with oil and sprinkle with half of the spice mixture on both sides (reserve remaining spices for the veggies).
Trim, seed, and slice bell peppers lengthwise into strips; place in a medium bowl.
Peel, halve, and slice onion into ½-inch thick half-moons; add to the bowl with the peppers.
Peel, trim, and quarter carrot lengthwise, then cut crosswise into 3-inch long pieces; add to the bowl.

Sprinkle remaining spice mixture over the veggies, drizzle with oil, and toss to combine. Add veggies to the baking sheet, spreading out in an even layer around the steak. (Reserve spice bowl for next step.)
Juice half of the lime over steak and veggies; juice the other half into the reserved bowl.
Place the baking sheet in the oven and roast, stirring veggies and flipping steak halfway through, until veggies are tender and steak is cooked to desired doneness, 13-15 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, add yogurt and spices to the bowl with the lime juice; whisk to combine the lime crema.
When the steak and veggies are done, transfer steak to the cutting board and thinly slice against the grain.
Warm tortillas in a skillet, oven, or microwave (optional).
To serve, divide tortillas between plates; fill with steak and veggies, then drizzle with lime crema. Enjoy!

name: Sheet Pan Sticky Sesame Chicken with Roasted Broccoli & Peppers
ingredients: ¾ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
½ (8 oz) pkg sugar snap peas
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Pat the chicken breasts dry with paper towels, rub with olive oil, season generously with salt and pepper on both sides and place in the middle of a parchment paper lined baking sheet.
Peel and medium dice the onion. Cut the sugar snap peas crosswise (at an angle) into 1-inch pieces and add to a mixing bowl.
Cut the bell pepper into quarters lengthwise; remove and discard the seeds and white membranes. Medium dice the pepper, add to the bowl with the onion.
Separate broccoli into bite-sized florets and cut stems into bite-sized pieces and add to bowl with other vegetables.
Drizzle the vegetables with oil and season with salt and pepper; toss to coat, then arrange in a single layer on baking sheet around the chicken breasts. Bake in the oven for 20 minutes.
Heat a small saucepan over medium heat. Once the pan is hot, add coconut oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Peel and mince the garlic. Peel and mince or grate the ginger. Add to the saucepan; cook, stirring until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Add soy sauce, honey, sesame oil, sesame seeds and water to the saucepan. Bring sauce to a boil, then reduce heat to low, stirring frequently.
Combine cornstarch with water in a small bowl and pour into sauce. Let sauce thicken for 2-3 minutes then remove from heat and set aside.
Remove chicken from oven, drizzle sauce over top and return to oven for another 5 minutes or until sauce is sticky and chicken is cooked through.
To serve, slice chicken into strips. Divide between plates and sprinkle sesame seeds over top. Enjoy!

name: Sheet Pan Sweet Potato Hash with Peppers, Fried Eggs & Paprika Aioli
ingredients: ½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled feta cheese
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and medium dice sweet potato; transfer to a large baking sheet pan.
Trim, seed, and medium dice bell peppers; add to the baking sheet with the sweet potato.

Halve chili pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon. Slice crosswise into thin half-moons and add to the baking sheet. (Be careful with chili peppers; do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Peel, halve, and slice onion crosswise into thin half-moons. Add to the baking sheet with the other veggies, drizzle with oil, and season with spices; toss to combine and spread out in an even layer.
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast, stirring halfway through, until veggies are golden and fork-tender, 18-20 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel and mince garlic. Place in a small bowl along with mayo, vinegar, soy sauce, and spices; stir to combine the aioli and set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Gently crack eggs into the skillet and cook until the tops of the whites are set but the yolks are still runny, about 4 minutes. Remove from heat and season with salt and pepper.
While the eggs are cooking, shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves.
When the veggies are done, remove from the oven, sprinkle with half of the cilantro, and stir to combine. (Reserve remaining cilantro for serving.)
To serve, divide veggies and eggs between plates or bowls; top with aioli, remaining cilantro, and feta. Enjoy!

name: Sheet Pan Turkey Meatballs with Roasted Apples, Plums & Basil Yogurt
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F. Coat one half of a baking sheet pan with a thin layer of oil.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Halve plums lengthwise (around the pit); twist halves to separate, then remove and discard pits. Cut each half into ½-inch thick slices. Place in a medium bowl.
Quarter, core, and slice apples into ¼-inch thick wedges. Add to the bowl with the plums.
Peel, halve, and slice onion lengthwise into ¼-inch thick strips. Add to the bowl along with oil, salt, and pepper, then stir to combine.
Transfer fruit and onions to the unoiled half of the baking sheet and spread out in an even layer. Set aside. (Reserve bowl for the next step.)
Pick basil leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and thinly slice into ribbons. Divide between the reserved medium bowl and a small bowl. (Set small bowl aside for later use.)
Add turkey, bread crumbs, egg, and spices to the medium bowl with the basil. Using your hands, mix well to combine.
Using a tablespoon measure, form the turkey mixture into rounded meatballs. Arrange on the oiled half of the baking sheet.
Place baking sheet in the oven and bake, tossing fruit and turning meatballs halfway, until meatballs are cooked through and fruit is fork-tender, 15-18 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, add yogurt, mayo, water, and spices to the small bowl with the basil. Stir to combine.
To serve, divide yogurt and roasted fruit between plates; top yogurt with meatballs. Enjoy!

name: Short-Cut Spanakopita with Greek Tomato-Cucumber Salad
instructions: Fill a large pot about halfway with hot water (from the tap); cover with a lid and bring to a boil over high heat.
Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)
Peel and thinly slice ⅓ of the onion; transfer to a medium bowl. Add vinegar and set aside to marinate.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat.
Mince remaining onion.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add the minced onion and cook, stirring often, until softened, 3-4 minutes. Transfer to a separate, medium bowl. Save skillet for later use.

When the water in the pot comes to a boil, remove lid, add the spinach and stir for a few seconds. Cook the spinach, uncovered, until wilted, 30-60 seconds. Once done, drain the spinach in a colander and rinse under cold water.
Shave parsley and dill leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves. Add both to the bowl with the cooked onion.
Grate the cheddar and add to the bowl with the cooked onion.

Using your hands, squeeze as much water from the spinach as you can, then transfer to a cutting board. Roughly chop spinach and add to the bowl with the cooked onion. Add feta, oil, and spices to the bowl and mix with your hands to thoroughly combine.
To assemble the pies, lay the tortillas on a flat surface and divide the spinach mixture between them; press the mixture firmly onto one half of each tortilla; fold in half.
Wipe the skillet clean and return to medium heat. Add oil, swirl to coat, and lay the assembled pies in the pan. Cook until golden, 2-3 minutes per side. Remove from the heat and slice into wedges.
Meanwhile, cut the tomato into wedges. Peel and trim the ends of the cucumber, then thinly slice into rounds. Add to the bowl with the sliced onion.
Add olives, oil, and spices to the bowl and stir to combine the salad.
To serve, divide spinach pie and cucumber-tomato salad between plates. Enjoy!

name: Shredded BBQ Tofu Bun with Creamy Cabbage, Radish, Celery & Chive Slaw
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Coarsely grate tofu and transfer to a baking sheet pan. Drizzle with oil and season with spices; stir to coat and spread out in an even layer.
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and bake, stirring halfway through, until tofu is golden and just starting to dry out, about 20 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Juice lime into a medium bowl.
Chop chives into small pieces. Add to the bowl with the lime juice along with yogurt, mayo, and spices. Stir to combine the dressing.
Trim off and discard root end of cabbage; halve lengthwise, then slice crosswise into thin (shred-like) strips. Add to the bowl with the dressing.
Trim and halve radishes lengthwise, then cut crosswise into thin half-moons. Add to the bowl.
Trim and thinly slice celery crosswise. Add to the bowl, stir to combine the slaw, and set aside.
Place ketchup, vinegar, sugar, soy sauce, Dijon, salt, and pepper in a medium saucepan; stir to combine the BBQ sauce.
Bring sauce to a boil over medium-high heat. Once boiling, reduce heat to low and continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened, 2-3 minutes. Remove from heat.
When the tofu is done, add to the pan with the BBQ sauce and stir to combine.
Toast the buns if desired.
Place bottom half of each bun on a plate; top with BBQ tofu and a small portion of the slaw. Close with the top half of each bun and serve with remaining slaw on the side. Enjoy!

name: Shrimp & Asparagus Fried Rice
ingredients: ¾ lb raw peeled shrimp, fresh or frozen
instructions: Rinse the rice in a colander and transfer to a small saucepan. Add water and salt; bring to a boil.
Place the shrimp in a medium bowl.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Once the water is boiling, reduce the heat to low, stir, and cover. Cook until the liquid is absorbed, 12 to 15 minutes. Remove from the heat and let the rice stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Snap or cut off and discard the woody ends of the asparagus; cut the spears into 1-inch pieces. Transfer to a medium bowl.
Peel and mince or grate the ginger; transfer to a small bowl.
Peel and mince the garlic; add to the ginger.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat.
Trim off and discard the ends of the green onions; chop the onions into ¼-inch pieces. Transfer to a small bowl.
Add coconut oil to the skillet and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add the shrimp to the skillet; cook until opaque, 1 to 2 minutes per side. Once done, transfer to a plate.
Add more coconut oil to the skillet, followed by the garlic, ginger, and white parts of the green onions. Cook until fragrant, 15 to 30 seconds.
Add the asparagus and cook, stirring frequently, until bright green and just tender, 2 to 3 minutes.
Return the shrimp to the skillet and add most of the remaining green onions (save some for garnishing); stir to combine.
Add the cooked rice to the skillet; cook, stirring constantly, until any leftover moisture evaporates, 1 to 2 minutes.
Add soy sauce, sesame oil, and squeeze the lime over top; stir to combine.
Divide the stir fry between plates or bowls and sprinkle with the remaining green onions. Enjoy!

name: Shrimp, Avocado & Grapefruit Salad
ingredients: ¾ lb raw peeled shrimp, fresh or frozen
instructions: If using frozen shrimp, place in a medium bowl, cover with water, and set aside to thaw. If using fresh shrimp, skip this step.
Wash and dry the lettuce and then tear into bite-sized pieces.

Wash and quarter grapefruit. Peel and slice 3 of the quarters into wedges (save 1 for the dressing). Halve and pit avocado; thinly slice flesh while still in skin and scoop out (save a quarter of the avocado for the dressing).
Wash and juice the lime and remaining grapefruit wedge into a small bowl; add saved avocado and mash thoroughly. Add honey, salt, and pepper; whisk to combine and set aside.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Peel and mince garlic.
Drain and rinse shrimp under cold water until there are no more ice chunks. Place on paper towels and pat dry. If using fresh shrimp, skip this step.
Coat bottom of skillet with oil. Add garlic and cook until fragrant, 15-30 seconds. Add shrimp and cook until opaque, 2-3 minutes.
To serve, arrange lettuce on a plate and top with avocado, grapefruit, and shrimp. Drizzle with dressing and enjoy!

name: Shrimp, Bell Pepper & Mushroom Stir Fry with Basmati Rice
ingredients: ¾ lb raw peeled shrimp, fresh or frozen
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Season the rice with salt and add water; bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
If using frozen shrimp, place in a medium bowl, cover with cold water, and set aside to thaw. If using fresh shrimp, skip this step.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce the heat to low. Cook the rice until the liquid is fully absorbed, 15 to 18 minutes. Once done, remove the rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Wash bell peppers and mushrooms. Seed and slice peppers into strips. Slice mushrooms. Transfer to a bowl.
Peel and mince garlic. Peel and mince or grate ginger.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Drain shrimp in a colander and rinse under cold water until there are no more ice chunks. Spread out on a clean towel and pat dry.
Coat bottom of skillet with oil. Add shrimp and cook, stirring frequently, until opaque and pink, 2-3 minutes. Transfer to a plate.
Once shrimp have been transferred, add more oil to skillet. Add garlic, ginger, bell peppers, and mushrooms. Stir fry until peppers are tender-crisp, 3-4 minutes.
In a small bowl, prepare sauce by whisking together soy sauce, vinegar, sesame oil, honey, and cornstarch.
Return shrimp to skillet and pour in the sauce. Stir fry until sauce thickens, 1-2 minutes.
Uncover the rice and fluff with a fork.
Serve by placing rice in a bowl or on a plate and adding stir fry over top. Enjoy!

name: Shrimp, Bell Pepper & Tomato Gumbo with Green Onion Rice
ingredients: 16 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
¾ lb raw peeled shrimp, fresh or frozen
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add broth and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Cook rice until liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.

If using frozen shrimp, place them in a colander and run under cold water to thaw them slightly and remove any ice crystals. (If using fresh shrimp, skip this step.) Place the shrimp on a clean towel or paper towels and pat dry.
Preheat a skillet over medium-low heat.
While the skillet heats up, peel and mince garlic; place in a small bowl.
Once the skillet is hot, add butter and swirl to coat the bottom. Add flour and cook, stirring occasionally, until butter is fully melted and mixture is golden brown, about 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, trim and thinly slice green onions crosswise; add half to the bowl with the garlic. (Set remaining green onions aside for the rice.)
Trim and small dice celery; trim, seed, and small dice bell pepper. Add both to the bowl with the garlic and green onion.
When the flour mixture is golden brown, add veggies to the skillet and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, 3-4 minutes.
Add broth and spices to the skillet; bring to a boil over high heat. Once boiling, reduce heat to medium and cook, stirring frequently, until thickened, 2-3 minutes.
Add shrimp and tomatoes to the skillet; stir to combine the gumbo. Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until shrimp are cooked through, 3-4 minutes more. Remove from heat.
Just before serving, add remaining green onion to the rice, and gently stir to combine.
To serve, divide green onion rice and gumbo between bowls. Enjoy!

name: Shrimp Burrito Bowl with Cilantro-Lime Rice & Pico de Gallo
ingredients: ¾ lb raw peeled shrimp, fresh or frozen
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add water and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce the heat to low. Cook the rice until the liquid is fully absorbed, 15 to 18 minutes. Once done, remove the rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Quarter the grape tomatoes and transfer to a medium bowl (that will be used for the salsa).
Quarter the jalapeño pepper lengthwise; remove and discard the stem, seeds, and membranes. Finely dice the pepper and add to the salsa bowl.
Trim off and discard the ends of the onion and remove the outer layer; small dice the onion into ¼-inch pieces. Transfer one ½ to the salsa bowl and the other ½ to a separate medium bowl.
Quarter the bell pepper lengthwise; remove and discard the stem, seeds, and membranes. Small dice the pepper into ¼-inch pieces. Add to the medium bowl with the onion.
Juice the lime into a small bowl; add about ½ of the juice to the salsa bowl and save the rest for the rice.

Using a knife, shave the cilantro leaves off the stems at a downward angle, working away from your body; discard the stems and finely chop the leaves. Add about ½ of the cilantro to the salsa bowl and add the rest to the bowl with the remaining lime juice.
Season the salsa with salt; stir to combine and set aside.
Add coconut oil to a nonstick skillet and preheat over medium heat.

If using frozen shrimp, place them in a colander and run under cold water until there are no more ice chunks. Then, lay them out on a clean towel or paper towels and pat dry. If using fresh shrimp, skip the first step.
Once the skillet is hot, add the shrimp and cook until they are opaque, 1 to 2 minutes per side. Once done, transfer to a bowl and set aside to cool.

Once the shrimp has been transferred, add more coconut oil to the skillet followed by the onion and bell pepper. Cook, stirring frequently, until the vegetables are browned and softened, 2 to 3 minutes.
Uncover the rice and fluff with a fork. Add the remaining lime juice and cilantro to the rice and stir to combine.
To serve, arrange the rice, veggie mixture, shrimp, and salsa in a bowl. Enjoy!

name: Shrimp, Corn & Coconut Milk Chowder with Bell Pepper
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
½ (13.5 fl oz) can coconut milk
¾ lb raw peeled shrimp, fresh or frozen
instructions: If using frozen shrimp, place in a medium bowl, cover with water, and set aside to thaw. If using fresh shrimp, skip this step.

Wash potatoes and bell pepper. Peel and medium dice potatoes. Seed and medium dice pepper. Remove husks and silks from corn. Stand up in the middle of a medium bowl and slice kernels off the cob. Transfer everything to a medium bowl.
Heat a medium saucepan over medium heat.
Peel and small dice onion. Peel and mince garlic.
Coat bottom of saucepan with oil. Add onion and, stirring frequently, cook until softened, 3-4 minutes.
Add garlic, potatoes, bell pepper, and corn to saucepan. Stir to combine.
Add coconut milk, broth, cumin, coriander, salt, and pepper. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer until potatoes are tender, about 10 minutes.
Drain shrimp and rinse under cold water until there are no more ice chunks. Place on paper towels and pat dry. Add to saucepan while the chowder is cooking.
Toast bread if desired.
To serve, pour soup into a bowl and enjoy with bread on the side!

name: Shrimp Couscous with Tomatoes, Zucchini & Feta
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled feta cheese
1 lb raw peeled shrimp, fresh or frozen
instructions: In a small saucepan, bring broth to a boil over high heat. Remove from heat, add couscous, and stir. Cover and let stand for 10 minutes then fluff with a fork.

If using frozen shrimp, place them in a colander and run under cold water to thaw them slightly and remove any ice crystals. (If using fresh shrimp, skip this step.) Place the shrimp on a clean towel or paper towels and pat dry.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Halve tomatoes. Cut peppers into quarters, remove seeds and membranes and slice into strips. Medium dice the zucchini into ½-inch cubes. Transfer cut veggies into a medium bowl.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Peel and mince garlic.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add the shrimp and garlic to the skillet; cook until shrimp are opaque, 1-2 minutes per side. Once done, transfer to a plate.
Return skillet to the heat, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add peppers, zucchini, tomato, and oregano to the skillet, stirring occasionally until vegetables soften, 3-4 minutes.
Shave dill leaves from stalk; discard stalk and mince leaves.
Once veggies are soft add broth, scraping up any browned bits, and cook until most of the liquid has evaporated, 4-5 minutes.
Add dill to the skillet, along with the shrimp and any accumulated juices; allow to cook for 1 minute more.
To serve, divide couscous between plates and top with the shrimp, veggies, and crumbled feta. Enjoy!

name: Shrimp Fettuccine with "Tikka Masala" Sauce, Zucchini, Peppers & Peas
ingredients: ¾ lb raw peeled shrimp, fresh or frozen
instructions: Fill a medium saucepan halfway with hot water (from the tap); cover and bring to a boil over high heat. Uncover, add salt and pasta, and stir for a few seconds. Cook until desired firmness, 8-10 minutes. Reserve a ½-cup cooking water before draining; set aside.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.

If using frozen shrimp, place them in the colander and run under cold water to thaw them slightly and remove any ice crystals. (If using fresh shrimp, skip this step.) Place the shrimp on a clean towel or paper towels and pat dry.
Peel, halve, and small dice onion; trim, seed, and medium dice bell pepper. Place both in a medium bowl.
Trim and halve zucchini, then cut crosswise into ¼-inch thick half-moons; add to the bowl with the other veggies.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add veggies and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, 4-5 minutes. (Reserve bowl for the next step.)
Meanwhile, place sugar and spices in the reserved bowl; stir to combine the spice mix.
Peel and mince ginger and garlic; add both to the bowl with the spice mix, along with the shrimp, and toss to coat.
When the veggies are soft, add seasoned shrimp to the skillet; continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until shrimp are just starting to turn opaque, 1-2 minutes.
Add tomato sauce, peas, and cream to the skillet; stir to combine and bring to a simmer. Once simmering, reduce heat to low and continue to cook until shrimp are cooked through, 2-3 minutes more.
Transfer drained pasta to the skillet and toss to combine; add reserved pasta water, a few tablespoons at a time, if necessary, to reach a saucy consistency. Remove from heat.
To serve, divide pasta between plates or bowls. Enjoy!

name: Shrimp Louie Salad with Hard-Boiled Egg, Lettuce, Avocado & Tomato
ingredients: ¾ lb raw peeled shrimp, fresh or frozen
instructions: Place eggs in a small saucepan, cover with water, and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to a simmer and cook for 8 minutes. Drain hot water and add ice or run under cold water to cool; set aside.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Zest and juice lemon into a small bowl; add oil, honey, chili-garlic sauce, Worcestershire, and spices. Whisk to combine the sauce.

If using frozen shrimp, place them in the colander and run under cold water to thaw them slightly and remove any ice crystals. (If using fresh shrimp, skip this step.) Place the shrimp on a clean towel or paper towels and pat dry.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, place shrimp in a medium bowl, drizzle with half of the sauce, and toss to coat. (Reserve remaining sauce for later use.)
Once the skillet is hot, add shrimp and any sauce left in the bowl; cook until opaque, 1-2 minutes per side. Remove from heat and set aside to cool slightly.
Meanwhile, roughly chop capers; add to the bowl with the remaining sauce along with mayo and ketchup. Whisk to combine the creamy dressing and set aside.
Trim and thinly slice radishes; place on a plate.
Halve tomatoes and add to the plate with the radish.
Peel and quarter eggs; add to the plate.
Halve and pit avocado; scoop out with a spoon and medium dice the flesh. Add to the plate.
Chop or tear lettuce into bite-sized pieces.
Divide lettuce between plates or bowls; top with radish, tomato, egg, avocado, and shrimp. Serve with creamy dressing on the side and enjoy!

name: Shrimp & Napa Cabbage Stir-Fry with Jasmine Rice
ingredients: ¾ lb raw peeled shrimp, fresh or frozen
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Season the rice with salt and add water; bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and grate or mince the ginger; transfer to a small bowl.
Trim off and discard the root end of the garlic; peel and mince or press the garlic and transfer to the bowl with the ginger.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce the heat to low. Cook the rice until the liquid is fully absorbed, 15 to 18 minutes. Once done, remove the rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Trim off and discard the ends of the green onions; cut the onions crosswise into ¼-inch pieces at an angle and transfer to a small bowl.
Trim off and discard the root end of the cabbage; half the cabbage lengthwise, then chop crosswise into 1-inch pieces.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.

If using frozen shrimp, place them in a colander and run under cold water to thaw them slightly and remove any ice crystals. (If using fresh shrimp, skip this step.) Place the shrimp on a clean towel or paper towels and pat dry.
Once the skillet is hot, add coconut oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add the shrimp to the skillet and stir-fry until lightly browned and almost cooked through, 2 to 4 minutes. Once done, transfer to a bowl or plate.
Once the shrimp have been transferred, add more oil to the skillet, followed by the garlic, ginger, and crushed red pepper; stir until fragrant, 15 to 30 seconds.
Add the cabbage to the skillet; cook, stirring frequently, until the cabbage is softened, 2 to 3 minutes.
While the cabbage cooks, in a small bowl, combine and whisk together soy sauce, sesame oil, honey, and cornstarch.

Return the shrimp to the skillet along with any accumulated juices, add about ¾ of the green onions (save the rest for garnishing), and pour the sauce overtop; stir-fry until the ingredients are well combined, about 1 minute.
Uncover the rice and fluff with a fork.
To serve, spoon the rice onto a plate, top with the stir-fry, and garnish with the remaining green onions. Enjoy!

name: Shrimp Po'Boy with Spicy Mayo & Lemon-Dijon Garden Salad
ingredients: ¾ lb raw peeled shrimp, fresh or frozen
instructions: If using frozen shrimp, place them in a colander and run under cold water to thaw them slightly and remove any ice crystals. (If using fresh shrimp, skip this step.) Place the shrimp on a clean towel or paper towels and pat dry.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and mince garlic. Transfer to a small bowl.
Juice half the lemon into the bowl with the garlic. Add mayonnaise, chili-garlic sauce, and salt; whisk to combine and set the spicy mayo aside.
In a medium bowl, combine bread crumbs, flour, and spices. Add shrimp and toss to combine.
Preheat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add shrimp to the skillet; cook until opaque, 1-2 minutes per side. Once done, transfer to a paper-towel lined plate.
Meanwhile, juice the other half of the lemon into a large bowl. Add oil, vinegar, Dijon, honey, and spices; whisk to combine the dressing.
Separate the lettuce leaves. Set aside 2 large leaves per sandwich; chop or tear remaining leaves into bite-sized pieces and add to the bowl with the dressing.
Trim carrot and peel into thin noodle-like sticks using a julienne (or regular) peeler. Add to the salad bowl.
Slice half of the tomato and set aside for the sandwiches. Small dice the other half and add to the salad bowl. Toss to combine the salad.
Toast buns if desired.
Place the bottom half of a bun on each plate. Layer with lettuce, shrimp, tomato, and spicy mayo; close with top half of the bun. Serve salad on the side and enjoy!

name: Shrimp and Sausage Boil with Corn, Baby Potatoes, and Fresh Thyme
ingredients: ½ lb raw peeled shrimp, fresh or frozen
instructions: Fill a large pot about halfway with hot water (from the tap); and place over high heat.
Add seasoning to the pot, cover with a lid, and bring to a boil.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Halve the potatoes and add to the pot. Prick the sausages with a fork and add to the pot.
Once water is boiling reduce the heat to medium-high. Make sure the water continues to bubble, but not over boil.
Trim the ends off of the beans, halve them, and set them aside.
Remove the husks and silks from the corn. Cut the corn into 1 inch long rounds - use a large knife to cut right through the cob. Add the corn to the pot.
Drain shrimp in a colander and rinse under cold water until there are no more ice chunks. Spread out on a clean towel and pat dry.

Shrimp and beans cook for a very short time, be sure the potatoes are almost tender and the sausage is cooked through before adding them (8-10 minutes). Add the beans to the pot, followed by the shrimp and cook for another 2-4 minutes.
Using a large colander strain out the water. Using tongs, remove the sausage and slice diagonally into ¼ inch rounds.
Return all ingredients to the pot and toss with butter, thyme, salt, and pepper (save some thyme for garnishing).
To serve, arrange on a plate, sprinkle with thyme, and enjoy!

name: "Shrimp Scampi" Caesar Salad with Kale, Romaine & Toasted Bread Crumbs
ingredients: ¾ lb raw peeled shrimp, fresh or frozen
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Zest half of the lemon into a medium bowl. (Reserve remaining lemon for later use.)

Cut butter into small pieces. Add to the bowl with the lemon zest along with bread crumbs, salt, and pepper; stir to combine. Transfer bread crumb mixture to a baking sheet pan and spread out in an even layer. (Reserve bowl for later use.)

Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't need to be fully heated) and bake, stirring halfway through, until bread crumbs are golden and toasted, about 5 minutes. Remove from oven and set aside to cool.

Meanwhile, if using frozen shrimp, place them in the colander and run under cold water to thaw them slightly and remove any ice crystals. (If using fresh shrimp, skip this step.) Place the shrimp on a clean towel or paper towels and pat dry.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat.
While the skillet heats up, peel and thinly slice garlic.
Once the skillet is hot, add additional butter and swirl to coat the bottom. Add garlic and spices; cook, stirring occasionally, until garlic is golden and fragrant, 1-2 minutes.
Meanwhile, shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves.

When the garlic is golden, juice half of the lemon into the skillet, then add parsley and shrimp. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the shrimp are opaque and cooked through, about 3 minutes. Remove from heat. (Reserve remaining lemon for the next step.)
While the shrimp are cooking, juice remaining lemon into the reserved bowl.
Finely grate Parmesan. Add to the bowl with the lemon juice.
Peel and mince additional garlic; mince anchovy fillets. Add both to the bowl along with mayo, Dijon, salt, and pepper. Whisk to combine the dressing.
Fold kale leaves in half lengthwise and slice off the stems. Chop or tear kale and lettuce leaves into bite-sized pieces. Add both to the bowl with the dressing and toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide salad between plates or bowls; top with shrimp scampi and bread crumbs. Enjoy!

name: "Shrimp Scampi" Pita Pizza with Cucumber, Bell Pepper & Romaine Salad
ingredients: ¾ lb raw peeled shrimp, fresh or frozen
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.

If using frozen shrimp, place them in the colander and run under cold water to thaw them slightly and remove any ice crystals. (If using fresh shrimp, skip this step.) Place the shrimp on a clean towel or paper towels and pat dry.
Shave parsley leaves off stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves. Place half in a medium bowl. (Set remaining parsley aside for the pizzas.)
Add mayo, vinegar, oregano, and salt to the bowl with the parsley. Stir to combine the dressing.
Trim, seed, and small dice bell pepper. Add to the bowl with the dressing.
Trim and quarter cucumber lengthwise, then cut crosswise into thin pieces. Add to the bowl and set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat.
While the skillet heats up, peel and mince shallot and garlic.
Once the skillet is hot, add butter and swirl to coat the bottom. Add shrimp, shallot, garlic, salt, and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, until shrimp are opaque, 2-3 minutes.
When the shrimp are done, zest and juice lemon into the skillet. Stir to combine and remove from heat.
Coarsely grate cheese.

Arrange pitas on a baking sheet pan. Top with shrimp and sauce from the skillet, then sprinkle with cheese. Place in the oven and bake until the cheese is melted, 4-5 minutes. Remove from oven and cut into wedges.
Meanwhile, chop or tear lettuce into bite-sized pieces. Add to the bowl with the dressing and veggies; toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide pizzas and salad between plates. Sprinkle pizzas with reserved parsley and enjoy!

name: Shrimp Scampi with Spaghetti Squash
ingredients: ¾ lb raw peeled shrimp, fresh or frozen
instructions: Preheat the oven to 500°F and place the rack in the center position. Line a baking sheet with aluminum foil to make cleanup easier (optional).
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Halve the squash lengthwise and scrape out the seeds. Rub each half with olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Place halves, cut side down, on a baking sheet.
Place the squash in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast until tender so a knife can easily pierce though the flesh, 18 to 20 minutes.

While the squash cooks, using a knife, shave the parsley leaves off the stems at a downward angle, working away from your body; discard the stems and finely chop the leaves. Transfer the parsley to a small bowl.
Grate all of the zest from the lemon, then juice the lemon. Add the zest and juice to the bowl with the parsley.
Trim off and discard the root ends of the garlic; peel and mince or press the garlic.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat.

If using frozen shrimp, place them in a colander and run under cold water to thaw them slightly and remove any ice crystals. (If using fresh shrimp, skip this step.) Place the shrimp on a clean towel or paper towels and pat dry.
Once the skillet is hot, add olive oil and butter and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add the garlic and crushed red pepper to the skillet; stir until fragrant, 15 to 30 seconds.
Add the shrimp to the skillet; cook, tossing occasionally, until opaque and cooked through, 2 to 4 minutes total.
Add the lemon zest, lemon juice, and parsley to the shrimp; season with salt and pepper and stir to combine.

Remove the squash from the oven and allow to cool slightly, about 5 minutes. Using a fork, scrape the squash flesh to make spaghetti-like strings (use an oven mitt or towel to hold it with your other hand).
To serve, top the squash with the shrimp scampi. Enjoy!

name: Shrimp & Spinach Linguine with Roasted Red Pepper Sauce
ingredients: ¾ lb raw peeled shrimp, fresh or frozen
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Fill a large pot about halfway with hot water (from the tap); cover with a lid and bring to a boil over high heat.
Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)

If using frozen shrimp, place them in a colander and run under cold water to thaw them slightly and remove any ice crystals. (If using fresh shrimp, skip this step.) Place the shrimp on a clean towel or paper towels and pat dry.

When the water in the pot comes to a boil, uncover the pot and season the water with salt, then add the pasta and stir for a few seconds. Cook the pasta, uncovered, for 11-12 minutes (or according to package directions). Once done, drain the pasta in a colander.
Peel and chop onion into 2-inch pieces; peel garlic. Spread out on a baking sheet.
Cut the bell peppers lengthwise; remove and discard the seeds and white membrane and chop into 2-inch pieces. Chop tomatoes into quarters and place on the baking sheet along with the peppers.

Drizzle veggies with oil and season with salt and pepper; place in the oven and roast for 13-14 minutes. During that last 3-4 minutes of cooking, change the setting to broil and cook until they begin to char slightly.
Meanwhile, heat a skillet over medium-high heat. Once the skillet is hot, add butter and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add shrimp to the pan, season with salt and pepper. Cook until golden brown and pink all the way through, about 2-3 minutes.
Finely grate Parmesan.
When vegetables are done cooking let cool for 3-4 minutes. Once cooled, peel the skin off the peppers and tomatoes and discard them.
Add vegetables to the blender and blend until mostly smooth. Add half the Parmesan and season with salt and crushed red pepper. Pulse to combine.
Return pasta to the pot, add shrimp, sauce and spinach and stir to until spinach is wilted slightly.
To serve, divide pasta between plates, top with remaining Parmesan. Enjoy!

name: Shrimp Tacos with Mango Salsa, Cabbage, Avocado & Spicy Yogurt
ingredients: ¾ lb raw peeled shrimp, fresh or frozen
instructions: If using frozen shrimp, place them in a colander and run under cold water to thaw them slightly and remove any ice crystals. (If using fresh shrimp, skip this step.) Place the shrimp on a clean towel or paper towels and pat dry.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Zest and juice lime into a medium bowl.
Peel mango and slice the flesh away from the pit, starting with the flat sides. Medium dice and add to the bowl with the lime.
Shave the cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl.

Quarter jalapeño pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon. Finely dice and add to the bowl. (Be careful, with jalapeños, do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Peel and mince onion; add to the bowl along with salt and pepper. Stir to combine the salsa and set aside.
Place yogurt, chili-garlic sauce, and salt in a small bowl; whisk to combine and set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Peel and mince garlic.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add garlic and stir until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Add shrimp to the skillet and season with salt and pepper. Cook until opaque, 1-2 minutes per side. Once done, chop into small pieces and set aside.
Meanwhile, trim off and discard the root end of the cabbage; quarter cabbage lengthwise and remove the core. Slice crosswise into thin strips.
Halve and pit the avocado; slice crosswise while still in the skin and scoop out with a spoon.
Warm tortillas in another skillet, oven, or microwave (optional).
To serve, divide tortillas between plates, top with cabbage, avocado, shrimp, salsa, and spicy yogurt. Enjoy!

name: Shrimp Tostadas with Guacamole & Pico de Gallo
ingredients: ¾ lb raw peeled shrimp, fresh or frozen
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F.
If using frozen shrimp, place them in a colander and run under cold water until there are no more ice chunks; set aside to drain. If using fresh shrimp, skip this step.

Drizzle both sides of the tortillas with oil and sprinkle with salt; place on a baking sheet. Bake for 10-15 minutes, flipping halfway through, until the tortillas are crispy and lightly browned on both sides.
In a medium bowl, combine the spices and oil.
Toss shrimp in spice mixture and set aside.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and mince garlic; add to a medium bowl. Halve avocado and remove pit; scoop out the flesh into the bowl with garlic.
Shave the cilantro leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves. Add half to the bowl with avocado and the other half to another medium bowl for the pico de gallo.
Juice the the lime into the bowl with avocado; add salt and pepper and mash with a fork until smooth.
Peel and small dice the shallot; small dice the tomatoes. Add both to the bowl with the cilantro for the pico de gallo.

Quarter the jalapeño pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs of the jalapeño with a spoon. Finely dice and add to the pico de gallo. (Be careful, with jalapeños, do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.) Season with salt and pepper and stir to combine.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Once the pan is hot add shrimp; cook until opaque, 1-2 minutes per side.
To serve, divide the tortillas between plates, top with guacamole, shrimp, and pico de gallo.  Enjoy!

name: Shrimp & Zucchini Coconut Curry with Basmati Rice
ingredients: ½ (13.5 fl oz) can coconut milk
¾ lb raw peeled shrimp, fresh or frozen
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Season the rice with salt and add water; bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.

If using frozen shrimp, place them in a colander and run under cold water until there are no more ice chunks. Then, lay them out on a clean towel or paper towels and pat dry. If using fresh shrimp, skip the first step.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce the heat to low. Cook the rice until the liquid is fully absorbed, 15 to 18 minutes. Once done, remove the rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Preheat a sauté pan over medium-high heat.
While the pan heats up, trim off and discard the ends of the onion and remove the outer layer; small dice the onion (cut into ¼-inch pieces).
Once the pan is hot, add coconut oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add the onion to the pan; cook, stirring frequently, until slightly softened, 3 to 4 minutes.
While the onion cooks, trim off and discard the ends of the zucchini; quarter the zucchini lengthwise, then slice crosswise into ¼-inch-thick pieces.
Add the zucchini to the pan; cook, stirring occasionally, until slightly softened, 2 to 3 minutes.
While the zucchini cooks, trim off and discard the root end of the garlic; peel and mince or press the garlic. Transfer to a small bowl.
Peel and grate or mince the ginger. Add to the bowl with the garlic.
Add the garlic, ginger, curry powder, turmeric, salt, and pepper to the pan; cook, stirring, until fragrant, 15 to 30 seconds.
Add the coconut milk, and fish sauce to the pan; bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to medium-low and cook for 2 to 3 minutes.
Using a knife, shave the cilantro leaves off the stems at a downward angle, working away from your body; discard the stems and finely chop the leaves.
Add the shrimp and ¾ of the cilantro (save the rest for garnishing) to the pan; cook until the shrimp are opaque and pink, 3 to 4 minutes, then remove from the heat.
Uncover the rice and fluff with a fork.
To serve, divide the rice between bowls, top with the shrimp and zucchini curry, and garnish with the remaining cilantro. Enjoy!

name: Simple Butter Chicken with Peas & Basmati Rice
ingredients: ¾ lb chicken thighs, boneless skinless
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Season the rice with salt and add water; bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
Pat the chicken dry with paper towel, cut into bite-sized (1-inch) pieces, and set aside.
Once the water for the rice is boiling, reduce the heat to low, stir, and cover. Cook until the liquid is absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Remove from the heat and let the rice stand, covered, 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, mix spices in a small bowl.
Using a clean cutting board, peel and small dice onion.
Heat a large skillet over medium heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add butter and swirl to coat the bottom. Add the onions and cook, stirring often, until softened, 3-4 minutes.
Wash, peel, and mince or grate ginger. Peel and mince garlic.
Add ginger, garlic, and spices to the onions and cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant, 30 seconds.
Using a strainer or colander, drain the diced tomatoes, pressing with the back of a spoon to extract as much liquid as possible; discard liquid.
Add additional butter, chicken, diced tomatoes, and cream to the skillet. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to medium; cover and cook until chicken is cooked through, 6-8 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry cilantro. Shave leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves.
Using a strainer or colander, rinse the frozen peas under running water. Add peas to the butter chicken, stir, and remove from heat.
To serve, divide rice and butter chicken between bowls; garnish with cilantro and enjoy!

name: Simple Sweet Chili Salmon with Sesame Broccoli & Rice
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F. Line a baking sheet pan with parchment paper.
Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add broth and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce the heat to low. Cook the rice until the liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove the rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, place vinegar, sugar, water, chili-garlic sauce, and salt in a skillet. Whisking occasionally, bring to a boil over high heat.
In a small bowl, make a slurry by whisking water with cornstarch until smooth.
Add cornstarch slurry to the skillet in a steady stream while whisking quickly. Cook, whisking continuously, until the sweet chili sauce thickens, about 30 seconds. Remove from heat.
Place salmon, skin-side down, on the baking sheet. Spoon the sweet chili sauce evenly over each filet.
Place salmon in the oven and bake until opaque and flaky, 10-15 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry broccoli. Separate into bite-sized florets and cut stems into smaller pieces.
Rinse skillet and wipe dry with paper towels; place over medium heat.
