Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add broccoli and stir-fry until bright green and tender-crisp, 4-5 minutes. Remove from heat.
To serve, divide rice, salmon, and broccoli between plates or bowls. Enjoy!

name: Sirloin with Creamy Dijon Sauce, Lemon-Garlic Kale, Couscous & Chives
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
¾ lb striploin (New York strip) steak
instructions: In a small saucepan, bring broth to a boil. Once boiling, remove from heat, add couscous and salt, and stir to combine. Cover and let stand for 10 minutes; fluff with a fork right before serving.
Meanwhile, place oil, Dijon, mayo, vinegar, water, sugar, salt, and pepper in a small bowl; whisk to combine the Dijon sauce and set aside.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Fold kale leaves in half lengthwise and slice off the stems; chop or tear leaves into bite-sized pieces. Place in a medium bowl and set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the steak dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with salt and pepper on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add steak and cook until desired doneness, 2-5 minutes per side. Transfer to a clean plate and loosely cover with aluminum foil.
While the steak is cooking, chop chives into small pieces; add half to the bowl with the kale (reserving the rest for garnish).
Peel and mince garlic; add to the bowl.
When the steak is done, return skillet to medium-high heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add more oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add kale, chives, garlic, salt, and crushed red pepper; cook, stirring often, until kale is tender, 3-4 minutes.
Juice lemon into the skillet with the kale and stir to combine; remove from heat.
Thinly slice steak against the grain.
To serve, divide couscous, steak, and kale between plates. Drizzle Dijon sauce over the steak and garnish with reserved chives. Enjoy!

name: Sirloin Steak with Basil Compound Butter, Roasted Potatoes & Snap Peas
ingredients: ¾ lb striploin (New York strip) steak
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F. Line a baking sheet pan with aluminum foil.
Cut butter into small pieces, place in a small bowl, and set aside to soften.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.

Slice potatoes crosswise into ¼-inch thick rounds. Transfer to the baking sheet, season with spices, and spread out in a single layer; dot potatoes with ⅓ of the butter. (Reserve remaining butter for later.)
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast, tossing halfway through, until the potatoes are fork-tender and golden, 20-25 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, zest lemon into the bowl with the remaining butter. Cut lemon into wedges and set aside for serving.
Peel and mince garlic; add to the bowl with the butter.

Pick basil leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and thinly slice into ribbons; add to the bowl. Mash the butter, garlic, and basil together with the back of a spoon until smooth. Set the compound butter aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the steak dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with salt and pepper on both sides.

Once the skillet is hot, add butter and swirl to coat the bottom. Add steak and cook until desired doneness, 2-5 minutes per side. Transfer to a clean plate, loosely cover with aluminum foil, and set aside to rest.
Return the skillet to medium-high heat. Add more butter and swirl to coat the bottom. Add snap peas, salt, and pepper; stir-fry until the peas are fork-tender, about 4 minutes.
Thinly slice steak against the grain.
To serve, divide roasted potatoes, steak, and snap peas between plates. Top steak with compound butter and squeeze lemon over the peas. Enjoy!

name: Skillet Dijon Chicken & Mushrooms with Asparagus
ingredients: ½ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
4 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Fill a sauté pan about three-quarters of the way full with water, cover, and bring to a boil.
Wash the asparagus and snap (or cut) off and discard the woody ends.
Once the water in the pan is boiling, add the asparagus and cover. Cook until bright green and tender, 3-4 minutes. Drain and thoroughly rinse under cold water to stop the cooking process. Set aside.
Heat a skillet over medium heat.
Slice the chicken in half horizontally to form thin fillets. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Add butter to the skillet and swirl to coat bottom. Add the chicken and cook until golden brown and cooked through, 3-4 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate.
Wash and slice the mushrooms. Peel and finely dice the shallot.

Once the chicken has been removed, add more butter to the skillet. Add the mushrooms and shallot. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the mushrooms are tender and any liquid has evaporated, 5-6 minutes.
Peel and mince the garlic.
Add the garlic and thyme and cook until fragrant, 15-30 seconds.
Add the broth and scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Stir in the cream and Dijon and season with salt and pepper.
Return the chicken to the skillet and bring to a boil. Simmer until the sauce is thickened, 4-5 minutes.
Arrange asparagus on a plate and top with the chicken and mushrooms. Enjoy!

name: Skillet Eggplant, Beef & Feta Moussaka with Lemon Arugula Salad
ingredients: ½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled feta cheese
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat.
While the skillet warms up, peel and small dice the onion into ¼-inch pieces; transfer to a small bowl.
Add the ground beef to the skillet; cook, breaking apart with a spoon, until crumbly and browned, 2 to 4 minutes. Once done, transfer the beef to a bowl and leave the juices in the skillet.
While the beef cooks, peel and mince the garlic; transfer to a small bowl.
Once the beef has been transferred, add the onion to the skillet; cook, stirring frequently, until softened, 3 to 5 minutes.
While the onion cooks, trim and discard the ends of the eggplant; medium dice the eggplant into ½-inch cubes and transfer to a medium bowl.
Add olive oil to the skillet, followed by the garlic, eggplant, and diced tomatoes; season with cinnamon, salt, and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the eggplant is tender, 8 to 10 minutes.
While the eggplant cooks, shave the parsley leaves off the stems; discard the stems and roughly chop the leaves.
Juice the lemon into a small bowl.
Add olive oil, Dijon, salt, and pepper to the lemon juice; whisk together.
Return the ground beef to the skillet and stir in half of the parsley (save the rest for garnishing).

To serve, place the moussaka on a plate, sprinkle with the feta and remaining parsley, and season with additional salt and pepper to taste. Add the arugula on the side and drizzle with the dressing. Enjoy!

name: Smoked Salmon, Asparagus, Goat Cheese & Dill Frittata with Green Salad
ingredients: ½ (5 oz) pkg spring mix (mixed greens)
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the mixed greens if they came pre-washed.)
Using a knife, shave dill leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Transfer to a medium bowl.
Add eggs, salt, and pepper to the bowl with the dill; whisk to combine.
Chop or tear salmon into bite-sized pieces; add to the bowl.
Crumble goat cheese into the bowl; stir to combine and set aside.
Snap or cut off the woody ends of the asparagus. Slice crosswise into ½-inch pieces and place in another medium bowl.
Preheat an ovenproof skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, trim green onions and cut crosswise into ¼-inch pieces.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add asparagus, green onions, salt, and pepper to the skillet; cook, stirring often, until asparagus is crisp-tender, about 3 minutes. (Reserve bowl for the salad.)
Meanwhile, preheat oven to broil on high and position rack in the upper third of the oven.

Pour the egg mixture into the skillet with the veggies; gently stir to combine. As eggs set around the edge of the skillet, gently lift cooked portions with a spatula to allow uncooked egg to flow underneath. Cook until bottom and sides are firm but the top is still runny, 5-6 minutes.
Place skillet in the oven and broil until the top is set, 2-3 minutes. Remove from oven.
While the frittata is cooking, peel and mince garlic. Place in the reserved bowl along with oil, vinegar, Dijon, honey, salt, and pepper; whisk to combine the dressing.
Halve tomatoes. Trim and medium dice cucumber; add both to the bowl with the dressing.
Finely chop walnuts and add to the bowl along with the mixed greens; toss to combine the salad.
Cut frittata into wedges and divide between plates. Serve with salad on the side and enjoy!

name: Smoked Salmon Bowl with Ginger Rice, Edamame, Mango & Avocado
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and grate or mince the ginger.
Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add ginger, water, and salt; bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce the heat to low. Cook the rice until the liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove the rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, place edamame in the colander and rinse under hot, running water (from the tap) to defrost; set aside to drain.
Combine vinegar, sesame seeds, sugar, and salt in a medium bowl; whisk to dissolve the sugar.
Trim cucumber and thinly slice crosswise into rounds. Add to the bowl with the vinegar mixture.
Trim off and discard tops and root ends of radishes; thinly slice and add to the bowl with the cucumber. Stir to combine the salad.
Peel mango and slice flesh away from the pit, starting with the flat sides. Medium dice and set aside.
Combine chili-garlic sauce and mayonnaise in a small bowl; whisk until smooth.
Halve and pit the avocado. Slice thinly while still in skin, then scoop out, keeping avocado halves intact. Fill avocado halves with spicy mayo.
Divide rice, edamame, mango, and cucumber-radish salad between bowls; top with smoked salmon and an avocado half. Serve with soy sauce on the side and enjoy!

name: Smoked Salmon, Cream Cheese & Cucumber Roll-Ups with Side Salad
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Cut cream cheese into small pieces and place in a small bowl.
Using a knife, shave dill leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl with the cream cheese.
Peel and mince garlic; add to the bowl. Use the back of a spoon to soften and combine the cream cheese mixture.
Juice lemon into the bowl. Add yogurt, salt, and pepper; stir to combine and set aside.
Trim and halve cucumber lengthwise, then cut crosswise into (thin) half-moons.
Lay tortillas on a flat surface. Using a spatula, spread cream cheese mixture evenly over each tortilla.
Top tortillas with half of the cucumbers (reserve remaining cucumbers for the salad) and the salmon; roll tightly to close and cut crosswise into pieces. Set aside.
Place oil, vinegar, salt, and pepper in a medium bowl; whisk to combine the dressing.
Add reserved cucumbers to the bowl with the dressing.
Trim, seed, and thinly slice bell pepper; add to the bowl.
Chop or tear lettuce leaves into bite-sized pieces; add to the bowl, along with the pine nuts, and toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide roll-ups and salad between plates. Enjoy!

name: Smoked Salmon Salad with Edamame, Mango, Pear, Avocado & Pecans
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the mixed greens if they came pre-washed.)
Place edamame in the colander and rinse under hot, running water (from the tap) to defrost; set aside to drain.
Juice lemon into a medium bowl. Add oil, vinegar, Dijon, maple syrup, salt, and pepper; whisk to combine the dressing.
Peel mango and slice flesh away from the pit, starting with the flat sides; medium dice and add to the bowl with the dressing.
Halve and pit avocado; slice crosswise while still in the skin and scoop out with a spoon. Add to the bowl.
Quarter, core, and medium dice pear; add to the bowl.
Roughly chop pecans and add to the bowl.
Chop or tear salmon into bite-sized pieces and add to the bowl.
Add mixed greens and edamame to the bowl; toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide salad between plates or bowls and enjoy!

name: Smoked Salmon Sandwich with Lettuce, Tomato, Avocado & Chopped Salad
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Place mayo, vinegar, and spices in a medium bowl. Whisk to combine the dressing.
Trim and small dice celery. Add to the bowl with the dressing.
Trim and medium dice cucumber. Add to the bowl.
Separate lettuce leaves; set aside one leaf per sandwich. Chop or tear remaining leaves into bite-sized pieces and add to the bowl.
Add broccoli slaw to the bowl, toss to combine the salad, and set aside.
Thinly slice tomato and place on a plate.
Halve and pit avocado; cut crosswise while still in the skin, then scoop out with a spoon. Add to the plate with the tomato.
Toast bread if desired.
To assemble the sandwiches, spread each bread slice with additional mayo. Layer half of the slices with the reserved lettuce, tomato, avocado, and smoked salmon; close with remaining slices.
To serve, divide salad and sandwiches between plates. Enjoy!

name: Smoked Salmon Sushi Stacks with Ginger Rice & Avocado-Cucumber Salad
ingredients: ½ (8 oz) pkg sugar snap peas
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and grate or mince ginger; transfer to a small saucepan.
Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to the saucepan with the ginger. Add water and salt; bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce the heat to low. Cook the rice until the liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove the rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel and mince garlic; transfer to a medium bowl along with mayo and whisk to combine.
Trim and thinly slice green onions; add to the bowl with the mayo.
Trim, seed, and small dice bell pepper; add to the bowl.
Chop or tear salmon into small pieces and add to the bowl. Stir to combine the salmon mixture and set aside.
Place sesame seeds, oil, vinegar, soy sauce, sugar, chili powder, and salt in another medium bowl. Whisk to combine the dressing.
Trim and medium dice cucumber; add to the bowl with the dressing.
Cut the snap peas crosswise into ¼-inch pieces; add to the bowl.
Uncover the rice and fluff with a fork. Add vinegar and sugar; stir to combine, then spread the rice out on a baking sheet pan to cool, about 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, halve and pit the avocado; scoop out flesh with a spoon and medium dice. Add to the bowl with the other veggies and gently stir to combine the salad.

Place a ⅓-cup of the salmon mixture in a small cup or bowl; top with a ½-cup of rice and press gently to secure. Once the stack is complete, flip the cup or bowl onto a plate; tap on the bottom to loosen the stack. If the rice is sticking, run a knife around the edge before flipping.
Repeat with remaining salmon mixture and rice, creating 2 stacks per plate.
To serve, divide salad between plates and enjoy!

name: Smoky Bacon-Wrapped Chicken Thighs with Roasted Zucchini & Asparagus
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
In a small bowl, combine chili powder, paprika, onion powder, cinnamon, salt, and pepper.
Pat the chicken dry with paper towel; sprinkle chicken with half of the spice blend. Wrap each thigh in 1-2 strips of bacon, place in a baking dish, and sprinkle with the remaining spice blend.
Place chicken in the oven and bake until chicken is golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature of chicken reaches 165°F), 20-25 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim off and discard the ends of the zucchini; medium dice the zucchini (cut into ½-inch cubes) and transfer to a medium bowl.
Snap or cut off and discard the woody ends of the asparagus; transfer to the medium bowl.
Trim off and discard the root ends of the green onions; cut the onions crosswise into ¼-inch pieces at an angle and transfer to the medium bowl.
Pick the mint leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves. Save some of the mint for garnish and add the rest to the medium bowl.
Juice the lemon and add the juice to the medium bowl.

Drizzle the vegetables with olive oil and season with salt and pepper; toss to coat, then arrange in a single layer on a baking sheet and place in the oven. Cook until vegetables are fork tender, 12-15 minutes.
Remove both pans from oven. Change oven setting to broil and position rack near the top. Return chicken pan to oven and broil until bacon crisps, 2-3 minutes.
To serve, divide the chicken and vegetables between plates and garnish with fresh mint. Enjoy!

name: Smoky Sausage & Zucchini Noodle Skillet with Tomato-Cream Sauce
instructions: Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, peel, halve, and small dice onion; peel and mince garlic.
Once the skillet is hot, add onion, garlic, sausage, and spices. Cook, breaking the meat apart with a spoon, until browned and crumbly, 4-5 minutes.
While the sausage is cooking, wash, dry, and trim zucchini; run a vegetable peeler along the length of the zucchini to make ribbons.

When the sausage is done, add zucchini noodles, tomato sauce, and cream to the skillet. Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until zucchini noodles are soft and sauce has thickened, 3-4 minutes more. Remove from heat.
Meanwhile, finely grate Parmesan.
To serve, divide skillet between plates or bowls. Top with Parmesan and enjoy!

name: Smothered Cheesy Bean Burrito with Enchilada Sauce & Lime Crema
ingredients: 4 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Coat a baking dish with a thin layer of oil and set aside.
Coarsely grate cheese. Place half in a small bowl and set aside for burrito topping. (Reserve remaining cheese for the next step.)
Drain and rinse beans in a colander. Transfer to a medium bowl along with the reserved cheese and spices; stir to combine the filling.

Place tortillas on a flat surface and divide filling down the center of each one. Roll tortillas tightly to close and transfer to the baking dish, seam-side down. (The burritos should not be touching.)
Place baking dish in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and bake until burritos are slightly crispy and heated through, about 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, preheat a medium saucepan over medium-high heat.
While the pan heats up, peel and mince shallot.
Once the pan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add shallot to the pan and cook, stirring often, until it begins to soften, 1-2 minutes.
Add flour and spices to the pan with the shallot; continue to cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant, 30-60 seconds.

Slowly whisk tomato sauce and broth into the pan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened, about 3 minutes. Remove enchilada sauce from heat, cover, and set aside.

Remove baking dish from the oven; pour enchilada sauce over the burritos and top with remaining cheese. Return to the oven and continue to bake until sauce is bubbly and cheese is melted, 8-10 minutes. Remove from oven. (Reserve bowl for the lime crema.)
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Juice lime into the reserved bowl; add yogurt and salt. Whisk to combine the lime crema and set aside.
Stack lettuce leaves, one on top of the other; halve lengthwise, then slice crosswise into thin (shred-like) strips. Transfer to a plate.
Small dice tomato. Trim green onions and cut crosswise into ¼-inch pieces; add both to the plate with the lettuce.
To serve, divide burritos and sauce between plates. Drizzle burritos with lime crema; top with lettuce, tomato, and green onions. Enjoy!

name: Smothered Pork Chops in Creamy Onion Gravy with Broccoli & Mushrooms
ingredients: 6 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: In a medium bowl, stir together flour and spices; remove 1 tablespoon seasoned flour and set aside for later use.
Pat pork chops dry with paper towels, add to the bowl with the flour, and toss to coat.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat. Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add chops to the skillet; cook until golden brown, about 2 minutes per side. Once golden, transfer to a plate and loosely cover with aluminum foil (the pork will not be cooked all the way through).
Meanwhile, peel and thinly slice onion into half rings.
Return skillet to medium heat. Once hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add onions, salt, and pepper to the skillet. Cook, stirring occasionally, until onions are soft and slightly caramelized, 10-15 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry broccoli. Separate into bite-sized florets and cut stems into smaller pieces; place in another medium bowl.
Wash, dry, and thinly slice mushrooms. Peel and mince garlic. Add both to the bowl with the broccoli.
Add reserved flour to the skillet and stir to coat onions. Cook, stirring frequently, about 1 minute.
Add broth and cream to the skillet, stir to combine, and bring to a simmer. Once simmering, reduce heat to low and cook, stirring occasionally, until sauce begins to thicken, 4-5 minutes.
Return pork chops to the skillet and turn to coat in sauce. Cover and simmer until chops are cooked through, 5 minutes more.
Meanwhile, heat another skillet over medium-high heat. Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add veggies, salt, and pepper to the skillet; stir-fry until broccoli is bright green and tender-crisp, 4-5 minutes.
To serve, divide pork chops, sauce, and veggies between plates. Enjoy!

name: Soba Noodle Salad Bowl with Steak, Bok Choy, Broccoli Slaw & Ginger
ingredients: ¾ lb striploin (New York strip) steak
instructions: Fill a medium saucepan about halfway with hot water (from the tap); add salt, cover with a lid, and bring to a boil over high heat.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Once the water in the saucepan is boiling, add the noodles. Cook noodles according to package directions, about 5 minutes. Once done, drain and rinse thoroughly under cold water.
Meanwhile, zest and juice lime into a medium bowl.
Peel and mince ginger. Add to the bowl with the lime juice along with soy sauce, chili-garlic sauce, and oil. Stir to combine the dressing and set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the steak dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with salt and pepper on both sides.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add steak and cook until desired doneness, 2-5 minutes per side. Transfer to a clean plate and set aside to rest, about 5 minutes. (Reserve skillet with cooking juices for later use.)
While the steak is cooking, trim and cut bok choy in half lengthwise.
Return skillet (with cooking juices) to medium-high heat. Add bok choy, salt, and pepper; cook, flipping occasionally, until tender, 5-6 minutes. Remove from heat.
Meanwhile, trim and thinly slice radishes. Add to the bowl with the dressing.

Pick mint leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add half to the bowl along with the cooled noodles and broccoli slaw. Toss to combine the noodle salad. (Reserve remaining mint for serving.)
Thinly slice steak against the grain.
To serve, divide noodle salad between bowls; top with steak and bok choy. Sprinkle with reserved mint and enjoy!

name: Soba Noodle Soup with Tofu, Edamame, Mushroom, Green Onion & Ginger
ingredients: 32 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Cut tofu in half along the long side. Sandwich tofu between clean towels or paper towels and place on a baking sheet pan. Place a cutting board with something heavy on top and set aside to press out excess water.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Thinly slice mushrooms and place in a small bowl.
Preheat a medium saucepan over medium heat.
While the pan heats up, peel and mince ginger and garlic; add both to the bowl with the mushrooms.
Once the pan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add mushrooms, ginger, and garlic; cook, stirring occasionally, until mushrooms are lightly browned, 5-6 minutes.
Meanwhile, cut tofu into ½-inch cubes.
When the mushrooms are done, add broth to the pan and bring to a boil over medium-high heat.

Once the broth is boiling, add tofu, noodles, edamame, and soy sauce; stir to combine the soup. Bring to a simmer over medium heat and continue to cook until noodles are tender and tofu is warmed through, 5 minutes more. Remove from heat.
Meanwhile, trim green onions and cut crosswise into thin pieces; add to the soup and stir to combine.
To serve, divide soup between bowls and enjoy!

name: Soba Noodles with Garlicky Green Sauce, Scallion Oil & Avocado
instructions: Fill a medium saucepan about halfway with hot water (from the tap); add salt, cover with a lid, and bring to a boil over high heat.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)

Once the water is boiling, add spinach and cook until bright green and just tender, about 15 seconds. Using tongs, transfer spinach to the colander, and set aside to drain (reserve boiling water in pan for the next step).
Add the noodles to the pan and cook according to package directions, about 5 minutes. Once done, drain in the colander. (Reserve pan for later use.)
While the noodles are cooking, transfer drained spinach to a blender. (Reserve colander for the noodles.)
Juice lime into the blender.

Add nutritional yeast, soy sauce, oil, and garlic powder to the blender. Blend on high until sauce is smooth, adding water, 1 teaspoon at a time, if needed to reach a drizzling consistency. Set green sauce aside.
Trim and thinly slice green onions crosswise.
Wipe the pan used for the noodles clean with paper towels and return to medium heat.

Once the pan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add green onions, crushed red pepper, and salt; cook, stirring frequently, until bright green and just tender, about 30 seconds. Remove from heat.
Transfer drained noodles to a medium bowl. Add green sauce, then stir to coat noodles; add additional water, a tablespoon at a time, if necessary, to coat the noodles in sauce.
Halve and pit avocado; using a spoon, scoop out the flesh and slice crosswise into thin pieces. Season with salt.
To serve, divide noodles and avocado between plates or bowls; top noodles with scallion oil. Enjoy!

name: Soft Beef Tacos with Shredded Romaine, Cheddar & Spicy Salsa
instructions: Heat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Wash and dry lettuce, tomatoes, jalapeño, and green onions.
Add beef to the skillet and, breaking apart with a spoon, cook until beef is browned and crumbly, 3-4 minutes.
Add chili powder, cumin, salt, and pepper to skillet and stir to combine with the beef. Remove skillet from heat.
Slice the lettuce crosswise into thin (shred-like) strips. Small dice the tomatoes. Seed and mince the jalapeño. Trim and discard root ends and chop green onions.
In a small bowl, prepare the salsa by mixing together tomatoes, jalapeño, onions, lime juice, salt, and pepper.
Grate ½ cup of cheddar.
To serve, fill tortillas with shredded lettuce, ground beef, and salsa. Sprinkle cheddar over top. Enjoy!

name: Southern-Style Tomato Sandwich with Parmesan & Pine Nut Kale Salad
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F.

Place pine nuts on a baking sheet pan and spread out in an even layer. Place in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and toast, stirring every 2-3 minutes, until golden brown, 5-8 minutes. Remove from oven and set aside to cool.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Place oil, vinegar, salt, and pepper in a small baking dish; whisk to combine the marinade.
Slice tomatoes into ¼-inch thick rounds; add to the dish with the marinade, turn to coat, and set aside.
Peel and mince garlic; place in a medium bowl.
Juice lemon into the bowl with the garlic. Add oil, Dijon, maple syrup, salt, and pepper; whisk to combine the dressing.
Fold kale leaves in half lengthwise and slice off the stems. Finely chop leaves and add to the bowl with the dressing.
Turn oven to broil on high and position rack under the broiler.
While the broiler heats up, finely grate Parmesan and add to the bowl with the kale.
Roughly chop toasted pine nuts. Add to the bowl and toss to combine the salad; set aside. (Reserve baking sheet for next step.)
Arrange bread on the baking sheet. Place in the oven and toast, flipping once, until golden brown, 1-2 minutes. Remove from the oven.
Spread each slice of toast with a thick layer of mayo. Top half of the slices with marinated tomatoes, then close with remaining toast slices.
To serve, divide tomato sandwiches and salad between plates. Enjoy!

name: Southwest Chicken Salad with Creamy Yogurt Dressing
ingredients: ½ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Cut tortillas into thin strips and place on a baking sheet pan. Drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Toss to coat, then spread out in a single layer.
Place in the oven and bake until golden and crispy, 10-12 minutes.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Slice chicken in half horizontally to form thin fillets. Season with salt and pepper.
Coat bottom of skillet with oil. Add chicken and cook until cooked through, 2-3 minutes per side.
In a small bowl, prepare dressing by whisking together yogurt, salt, chili powder, garlic powder, pepper, cumin, and paprika.
Remove husks and silks from corn. Stand up vertically in the middle of a large bowl and slice kernels off the cob.

Wash and dry lettuce, bell pepper, tomato, and green onions. Chop lettuce crosswise into 1 inch strips and transfer to the bowl with corn. Seed, medium dice, and add bell pepper to bowl. Medium dice and add tomato to bowl. Trim and discard root ends, chop onions, and add to bowl. Halve and pit avocado; scoop out and medium dice the flesh and add to bowl.
Drain and rinse beans. Place on paper towels and pat dry. Add to bowl.
Add tortillas strips to bowl and pour dressing over top. Toss salad until well combined.
Slice chicken into strips.
To serve, place salad on a plate and top with chicken slices. Enjoy!

name: Southwest Salmon Chowder with Potato, Corn, Bell Pepper & Avocado
ingredients: 24 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
1 (7.5 oz) can wild pink salmon, traditional style
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and small dice potatoes; place in a small bowl.
Trim, seed, and small dice bell pepper; add to the bowl with the potato and set aside.
Preheat a medium saucepan over medium-high heat.
While the pan heats up, peel, halve, and small dice onion.
Once the pan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add potato, bell pepper, and onion; cook, stirring occasionally, until starting to soften, 3-4 minutes.
Sprinkle flour and spices over the veggies; continue to cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add broth and milk to the pan, stir to combine, and bring to a simmer. Once simmering, reduce heat to medium, and cook until potatoes are tender, 10-12 minutes.
Meanwhile, slice lime into wedges and set aside for serving.
Halve and pit avocado; slice crosswise while still in the skin and scoop out with a spoon.
When the soup is done, drain and break salmon into chunks; add to the pan, along with the corn, and stir to combine. Cook until heated through, 3-4 minutes more. Remove from heat.
Divide soup between bowls, top with avocado, and sprinkle with additional chili powder. Serve with lime wedges for squeezing and enjoy!

name: Southwest White Chicken Chili with Avocado & Crusty Bread
ingredients: ½ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Heat a medium saucepan over medium heat.
Peel and small dice onion. Peel and mince garlic. Wash, seed, and mince jalapeño.
Coat bottom of saucepan with oil. Add onion, garlic, and jalapeño. Stirring frequently, cook until onion is softened, 3-4 minutes.
Cut chicken into bite-sized pieces.
Drain and rinse beans.
Add chicken to saucepan and, stirring occasionally, cook until no longer pink, 2-3 minutes.
Wash and dry cilantro. Shave leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves.

Add beans, broth, ½ of the cilantro (save the rest for garnishing), cumin, oregano, salt, and pepper. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to medium-low and simmer, stirring occasionally, for about 10 minutes.
Toast bread.
Halve and pit avocado; scoop out and medium dice.
To serve, add chili to a bowl and garnish with avocado and remaining cilantro. Enjoy!

name: Southwestern Black Bean Cakes with Guacamole & Corn
instructions: Drain and rinse beans.
Wash and dry jalapeño and cilantro. Seed and mince jalapeño. Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves.
Transfer beans to a medium bowl and mash with a fork. Add egg, jalapeño, ½ of the cilantro (save the rest for the guacamole), bread crumbs, cumin, salt, and pepper. Mix until well combined.
Heat a skillet over medium heat.
Halve and pit avocado; scoop out the flesh into a medium bowl. Add remaining cilantro, lime juice, salt, and pepper. Mash with a fork until smooth.
Measure out corn.
Coat bottom of skillet with oil. Add corn and cook until heated through, 2-3 minutes. Transfer to a bowl.
Shape black bean mixture into 6-8 patties and place on a plate.
Once corn has been transferred, wipe skillet and coat with more oil. Add patties and cook until browned and crisp, 3-4 minutes per side.
Peel and mince garlic. Add garlic, lime juice, salt, and pepper to corn; mix to combine.
Serve black bean cakes with guacamole and corn. Enjoy!

name: Soy-Ginger Salmon with Sesame Napa Cabbage Slaw
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Juice the lime into a small bowl.
Peel and mince the ginger; transfer to a medium bowl.
Add half of the lime juice (save the rest for the salad), soy sauce, and olive oil to the ginger; whisk together.
Place the salmon, skin-side-up, in the sauce. Set the bowl aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat.
Once the skillet is warm, measure out the sesame seeds and add to the skillet. Cook, stirring frequently, until they are golden brown, 2 to 3 minutes. Once done, transfer to a small bowl.
Add olive oil to the skillet and swirl to coat the bottom.
Place the salmon, skin-side down, in the skillet; cook for 3 to 4 minutes on one side, then flip and pour in the remaining sauce. Continue to cook until the flesh is opaque, another 2 to 3 minutes.
Combine the remaining lime juice, olive oil, sesame oil, soy sauce, and honey in a large bowl; whisk together.
Halve the cabbage lengthwise, then cut out and discard the core; thinly slice crosswise and add to the large bowl.
Trim the ends and peel the carrots; discard the trimmings and coarsely grate the carrots. Add to the cabbage.
Toss the salad until well combined.
To serve, arrange the salad on a plate and place the salmon on top. Enjoy!

name: Spaghetti al Limone (Lemon Pasta) with Basil & Garlic-Roasted Veggies
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F.

Fill a medium saucepan halfway with water (from the tap), cover, and bring to a boil. Uncover, add salt and pasta, and stir for a few seconds. Cook until desired firmness, 8-10 minutes. (Reserve ¼-cup cooking water before draining and set aside.)
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and mince garlic. Place in a medium bowl along with oil, salt, and pepper; stir to combine the garlic oil.

Separate broccoli into bite-sized florets and cut stems into smaller pieces. Transfer to a baking sheet pan, drizzle with half of the garlic oil (reserving the rest for the kale), toss to coat, and spread out in an even layer.
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast broccoli while you prepare the kale.
Fold kale leaves in half lengthwise and slice off the stems. Chop or tear leaves into bite-sized pieces, add to the bowl with reserved garlic oil, and toss to coat.

Remove baking sheet from the oven, add seasoned kale, and toss to combine with the broccoli. Return baking sheet to the oven and continue to roast until veggies are tender-crisp, 8-10 minutes more. Remove from oven.
While the veggies are roasting, zest and juice lemon into a small bowl. Add cream, oil, salt, and crushed red pepper; whisk to combine the lemon cream.
Finely grate Parmesan, add to the bowl with the lemon cream, and stir to combine. Set aside.
Pick basil leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and thinly slice into ribbons. Set aside.

Return drained pasta to the pan and place over medium heat. Stir in the Parmesan-lemon cream and reserved pasta water; cook, stirring gently, until cheese has melted and sauce has thickened slightly, 2-3 minutes. Remove from heat.
Stir basil into the pasta.
To serve, divide pasta and veggies between plates or bowls. Top pasta with additional crushed red pepper and enjoy!

name: Spaghetti "Carbonara" with Tempeh, Parsley & Lemony Kale Salad
instructions: Fill a medium saucepan halfway with hot water (from the tap). Add salt, cover, and bring to a boil over high heat. Once boiling, uncover, add pasta, and stir for a few seconds; cook until desired firmness, 8-10 minutes. Drain pasta and set aside. (Reserve a ½-cup pasta water before draining.)
Meanwhile, preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, small dice tempeh. Place in a small bowl, drizzle with soy sauce, then season with smoked paprika and salt. Stir to coat.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add tempeh and cook, stirring occasionally, until golden, 4-5 minutes. Transfer tempeh to a plate and set aside. (Reserve skillet for later use.)
Meanwhile, finely grate Parmesan. Divide between two medium bowls.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add half to one of the bowls with the Parmesan. (Reserve remaining parsley for serving.)
Add egg, pepper, and salt to the bowl with the Parmesan and parsley. Whisk to combine the egg mixture and set aside.
Juice lemon into the remaining bowl with the Parmesan. Add oil, crushed red pepper, and salt. Whisk to combine the dressing.

Fold kale leaves in half lengthwise and slice off the stems; cut leaves crosswise into thin (shred-like) pieces. Add to the bowl with the dressing and, using your hands, massage kale until wilted, 1-2 minutes. Set aside.
When the pasta is done, return skillet to medium-high heat. Add drained pasta and cook, tossing frequently, until warmed through, about 1 minute. Remove from heat.

Carefully transfer warmed pasta to the bowl with the egg mixture. Tossing continuously, combine pasta with the egg mixture until pasta is glossy and evenly coated, 1-2 minutes. (The heat of the pasta will cook the egg.)
Add tempeh to the bowl with the pasta and toss once more to combine. Add reserved pasta water, 1 tablespoon at a time, if necessary, to loosen the pasta.
To serve, divide pasta and kale salad between plates or bowls. Top pasta with reserved parsley and enjoy!

name: Spaghetti Puttanesca
instructions: Fill a medium saucepan halfway with water, cover, and bring to a boil. Uncover, add salt and pasta, and stir for a few seconds. Cook until desired firmness, 8-10 minutes.
Heat a skillet over medium heat.
Peel and mince garlic. Halve olives. Measure out capers.
Coat bottom of skillet with oil. Add garlic, olives, capers, oregano, and crushed red pepper. Stir and cook for 1-2 minutes.
Add tomatoes and bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer the sauce while the pasta cooks.
Wash basil. Pick leaves off the stems; discard the stems and thinly slice the leaves into ribbons.
Drain pasta in a colander.
Add pasta to sauce and drizzle with olive oil. Stir in the basil and season with salt and pepper. Toss to combine.
To serve, add pasta to a shallow bowl or plate and enjoy!

name: Spaghetti with Roasted Bacon, Brussels Sprouts, Mushrooms & Parmesan
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Fill a large pot halfway with hot water (from the tap), cover, and bring to a boil. Uncover, add salt and pasta, and stir for a few seconds. Cook until desired firmness, 8-10 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash, dry, trim, and halve Brussels sprouts lengthwise. Transfer to a baking sheet pan.
Wash, dry, and quarter mushrooms. Add to the baking sheet with the Brussels sprouts.
Small dice bacon and add to the baking sheet. Drizzle with oil and maple syrup, then season with spices. Stir to combine and spread out in an even layer.
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast, stirring halfway through, until veggies are tender and bacon is cooked through, 15-20 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, finely grate Parmesan.
When the pasta is done, reserve a ⅓-cup of cooking water, then drain. Return pasta and reserved cooking water to the pot; set aside until the veggies are done.

Add roasted veggies, bacon, Parmesan, and Dijon to the pot, then set over medium-high heat. Cook, stirring often, until the liquid has evaporated and Parmesan has melted, about 1 minute. Remove from heat.
To serve, divide pasta between plates or bowls. Enjoy!

name: Spaghetti with Spinach, Peas, Asparagus, Poached Eggs & Parmesan
instructions: Fill a medium saucepan halfway with hot water (from the tap), cover, and bring to a boil. Uncover, add salt and pasta, and stir for a few seconds. Cook until desired firmness, 8-10 minutes. Drain and set aside.

Meanwhile, fill another medium saucepan about halfway with hot water (from the tap); add vinegar, cover with a lid, and bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Once the water in the pan is boiling, reduce heat to medium-low.
While the water is heating, wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)
Trim and cut green onions crosswise into thin pieces. Place in a medium bowl.
Snap (or cut) off woody ends of the asparagus; cut into 1-inch pieces. Add to the bowl with the green onions.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat.
While the skillet heats up, peel and mince garlic. Add garlic and peas to the bowl.
Once the skillet is hot, add butter and swirl to coat the bottom. Add veggies, salt, and pepper; cook, stirring occasionally, until fork-tender, 5-6 minutes. (Reserve bowl for the next step.)
Meanwhile, finely grate Parmesan. Place in the reserved bowl and set aside.
Gently crack eggs into two additional small bowls (two eggs per bowl).

Adjust the heat of the saucepan as necessary so that the vinegar water is simmering. Gently tip bowls into the pan, sliding the eggs carefully into the water. Cook until whites are set but yolks are still soft, 2½-3 minutes. Using a slotted spoon, transfer eggs to a plate.
When the veggies are done, add spinach to the skillet in handfuls, waiting for it to wilt slightly before adding the next handful.
Zest and juice lemon into the skillet, then add drained spaghetti. Continue to cook, tossing occasionally, until warmed through, 1-2 minutes more. Remove from heat.
To serve, divide pasta and eggs between bowls. Top with Parmesan and enjoy!

name: Spaghetti Squash "Pad Thai" with Shrimp
ingredients: ¾ lb raw peeled shrimp, fresh or frozen
instructions: Preheat the oven to 500°F and place the rack in the center position. Line a baking sheet with aluminum foil to make cleanup easier (optional).
Wash and dry the fresh produce.

Trim off and discard ends of the squash; halve the squash lengthwise and scrape out the seeds from each half. Rub the inside of the squash with olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Arrange the squash halves cut-side-down on the baking sheet.
Place the squash in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast until tender so a knife can easily pierce through the flesh, 20-25 minutes.
Trim off and discard the ends of the green onions; cut crosswise into ¼-inch pieces at an angle. Transfer to a small bowl.
Shave the cilantro leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl with the green onion and set aside.

If using frozen shrimp, place them in a colander and run under cold water to thaw them slightly and remove any ice crystals. (If using fresh shrimp, skip this step.) Place the shrimp on a clean towel or paper towels and pat dry; transfer to a medium bowl.
Preheat a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat.
Peel and mince shallot. Peel and mince garlic. Add shallot, garlic, salt, and pepper to the bowl with the shrimp and toss to coat.

When the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add shrimp in a single layer and cook until lightly golden, 1½-2 minutes per side; transfer to a plate and cover with aluminum foil to keep warm.

Once tender, remove the squash halves from the oven; allow to cool slightly, about 5 minutes. Scrape the inside of the squash with a fork to separate into spaghetti-like strands. (Use an oven mitt or towel to hold it with your other hand).
While the squash cools, juice the lime into a small bowl. Add fish sauce, soy sauce, maple syrup, vinegar, oil, and cayenne to bowl with lime juice; whisk to combine the sauce.
Return skillet to medium-high heat; add spaghetti squash, shrimp, and sauce to the skillet and cook until heated through, about 2 minutes.
To serve, divide the pad Thai between plates or bowls and garnish with green onions, cilantro, and peanuts. Enjoy!

name: Spaghetti with Turkey Bolognese
instructions: Fill a medium saucepan about halfway with water, cover, and bring to a boil.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim and discard the ends of the celery; small dice the celery and transfer to a medium bowl.
Peel and small dice the onion; add to the celery.
Preheat a sauté pan over medium heat.
Peel and mince the garlic; transfer to a small bowl.
Add olive oil to the pan and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add the celery and onion to the pan; cook, stirring occasionally, until they begin to soften, 2 to 4 minutes.
While the vegetables cook, pick the basil leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves.
Add the garlic to the pan; cook until fragrant, 15 to 30 seconds.
Once the water is boiling, season with salt and add the pasta. Cook the pasta until desired firmness, 8 to 10 minutes. Once done, drain in a colander.
Add the ground turkey to the pan; cook, breaking apart with a spoon, until browned and crumbly, 2 to 4 minutes.
Add the diced tomatoes and tomato sauce to the pan; season with salt, pepper, and crushed red pepper. Increase the heat to medium-high and let the sauce simmer until thickened, 4 to 6 minutes.
Stir the basil and spaghetti into the sauce.
To serve, place the pasta into a bowl. Enjoy!

name: Spanakopita-Inspired Flatbread with Creamy Feta, Spinach, Lemon & Dill
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)
Zest lemon into a small bowl. Add ⅔ of the feta, yogurt, oil, pepper, and salt. Mash with a fork until semi-smooth and combined, then set aside. (Reserve lemon and remaining feta for later use.)

Arrange flatbreads on a baking sheet pan. Place in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and bake, flipping halfway through, until flatbreads are slightly crispy, about 8 minutes. Remove from oven and set aside.
Meanwhile, juice reserved lemon into another small bowl.
Trim and thinly slice green onions crosswise. Add to the bowl with the lemon juice.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, shave dill leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl along with oil and salt, then stir to combine.

Once the skillet is hot, add lemon-oil mixture. Add spinach to the skillet in handfuls, waiting for spinach to wilt slightly before adding the next handful. Cook, stirring frequently, until wilted, about 2 minutes. Remove from heat.
Spread the creamy feta over each flatbread, then top with sautéed greens and reserved feta.
To serve, cut flatbreads into wedges and divide between plates. Enjoy!

name: Spanish Potato & Onion Frittata with Spinach Salad
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach and chives if they came pre-washed.)
Using a mandoline or knife, slice the potatoes into very thin slices and transfer to a colander. Sprinkle with salt and toss to coat; set aside in the sink or on a plate to drain.
Heat a non-stick skillet over medium high heat.
Peel and thinly slice onion into half rings. Peel and mince (or press) the garlic.

Once the skillet is hot, add olive oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add onion, garlic, thyme, and oregano to the pan, stirring until soft and golden brown, 4-5 minutes; remove from skillet and set aside.
Meanwhile, shake excess water from the potato slices and quickly pat dry with a paper towel.

Add more oil and the potatoes to the pan; turn the heat down to low and cover with a lid. Cook potatoes, stirring occasionally, until tender, 5-7 minutes. Once cooked, spread onion in a layer on top of the potatoes.
While the potatoes are cooking, crack the eggs into a medium bowl, add water and season with salt and pepper. Whisk to combine.
Pour the egg mixture into the skillet gently so you don't disturb the potatoes. Cover with a lid and cook until the base and sides are set, about 5-6 minutes.
Preheat oven to broil and position rack under the broiler.
While frittata is cooking on the stove, combine balsamic, oil, honey, Dijon, salt, and pepper in a large bowl to make the dressing for the salad.
Peel the carrot, then trim off the ends. Using a box grater, coarsely grate. Medium dice tomato and add both to the bowl with the dressing.
Once frittata edges are set transfer the pan to the oven and broil until the center eggs are firm and the top becomes golden brown, 5-7 minutes.
Add spinach to the bowl with the dressing and toss to combine.
Chop chives into small pieces.

When frittata is done cooking, remove from oven and place a cutting board on top of the skillet. Using oven mitts, flip the pan to turn the frittata out onto the cutting board so that potatoes are facing up.
To serve, cut frittata into wedges and divide between plates. Garnish with chives and serve with spinach salad. Enjoy!

name: Spanish Rice with Pinto Beans, Tomatoes, Avocado & Cilantro
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel, trim, and small dice carrot. Place in a medium bowl.
Trim and small dice celery. Add to the bowl with the carrot.
Preheat a medium saucepan over medium heat.
While the pan heats up, peel, halve, and small dice onion. Add to the bowl.
Once the pan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add veggies and spices; cook, stirring occasionally, until starting to soften, 2-3 minutes. (Reserve bowl for the next step.)
Meanwhile, drain and rinse beans. Place in the reserved bowl and set aside.

Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain. When the veggies are soft, add rice to the pan; cook, stirring constantly, until rice is slightly translucent, 1-2 minutes.
Add beans, tomatoes, and broth to the pan. Stir to combine and bring to a boil over high heat.

Once the liquid in the saucepan comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Simmer until rice is tender and the liquid is mostly absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
When the rice is almost done, halve and pit avocado; using a spoon, scoop out the flesh and thinly slice. Set aside for serving.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add half of the cilantro to the rice and stir to combine (reserve the rest for serving).
To serve, divide rice between plates or bowls; top with avocado and reserved cilantro. Enjoy!

name: Spanish-Style Baked Beans with Olives, Parsley Chimichurri & Flatbread
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Halve grape tomatoes. Place in a small bowl.
Trim, seed, and small dice bell pepper. Add to the bowl with the tomatoes.
Preheat an ovenproof skillet over medium heat.
While the skillet heats up, peel and mince garlic. Add to the bowl.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add tomatoes, bell pepper, garlic, and spices to the skillet. Cook, stirring occasionally, until tomatoes are starting to burst, 7-8 minutes. (Reserve bowl for later use.)
Meanwhile, drain and rinse beans.
Halve olives lengthwise.

When the veggies are done, add beans, olives, broth, and vinegar to the skillet, then stir to combine. Place skillet in the oven and bake until beans are tender and sauce has thickened slightly, 15-20 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Place in the reserved bowl.
Peel and mince additional garlic. Add to the bowl with the parsley along with oil, vinegar, oregano, and salt. Stir to combine the chimichurri and set aside.

When the beans have about 5 minutes left, cut flatbread into wedges and arrange on a baking sheet pan. Add to the oven and bake until warmed through and slightly golden, 4-5 minutes. Remove from oven.
To serve, divide beans and flatbread wedges between plates or bowls. Drizzle beans with chimichurri and enjoy!

name: Spice-Rubbed Pork Chop with Garlicky Bacon, Kale & Mushroom Sauté
instructions: Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add bacon and cook until crispy, 3-5 minutes per side. Remove to a paper towel-lined plate, leaving the drippings in the skillet.
Meanwhile, preheat the broiler to high and position rack about 6 inches from the top.
Place spices in a small bowl and stir to combine the spice rub.
Pat pork chops dry with paper towels and place on a broiler pan; season with spice rub on both sides. (Reserve bowl for later use.)

Place pork chops in the oven and broil, flipping halfway through, until chops are no longer pink in the center and are browned at the edges, 12-14 minutes, or until they reach an internal temperature of 145°F. Remove from the oven and let rest for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash, dry, and thinly slice mushrooms; place in the reserved bowl and set aside.
Peel and thinly slice garlic.
Return skillet (with bacon drippings) to medium heat. Once the skillet is hot, add mushrooms and garlic; cook, stirring occasionally, until mushrooms are soft and golden, 6-7 minutes.
While the mushrooms are cooking, wash and dry kale. Fold leaves in half lengthwise and slice off the stems; chop or tear leaves into bite-sized pieces.
When the mushrooms are done, add kale, water, salt, and pepper to the skillet; stir to combine and cover. Cook until the kale is wilted and tender, 1-2 minutes; remove from heat.
Meanwhile, chop or crumble bacon into pieces.
Add bacon to the skillet with the veggies and stir to combine.
To serve, divide pork chops and veggie sauté between plates. Enjoy!

name: Spiced Beet, Butternut & Chickpea Bowl with Rice Pilaf & Lemon Yogurt
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim, peel, and cut beet into ½-inch cubes. Transfer to a baking sheet pan.
Trim and peel butternut squash. Halve lengthwise, scrape out seeds, and cut flesh into ½-inch cubes; add to the baking sheet with the beet.
Drain and rinse chickpeas; add to the baking sheet.
Drizzle veggies and chickpeas with oil and sprinkle with spices. Toss to coat and spread out in an even layer. Place in the oven and roast, stirring halfway through, until fork-tender, 20-25 minutes.
Meanwhile, using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add water and spices; bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Cook rice until liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
While the rice cooks, juice lemon into a small bowl. Add yogurt, maple syrup, and spices to the bowl; whisk to combine the lemon yogurt.
Pick cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves.
Add almonds and half the cilantro to the cooked rice; stir to combine the pilaf. (Reserve remaining cilantro for garnish.)
To serve, divide rice pilaf, veggies, and chickpeas between bowls. Drizzle with lemon yogurt, sprinkle with reserved cilantro, and enjoy!

name: Spiced Honey Chicken with Sauteed Snap Peas, Carrots, & Cabbage
ingredients: ¾ lb chicken thighs, boneless skinless
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F.
Peel and mince garlic; combine with chili garlic sauce, soy sauce, honey, and sesame oil in a small bowl; whisk to combine.

Place chicken in a baking dish, making sure to unroll the thigh pieces and lay them flat. Drizzle with half the marinade and place in the oven. Reserve the remaining, untouched marinade for later. Bake chicken until cooked through and golden, 20 minutes, flipping once halfway through.
While chicken is cooking, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Preheat a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Peel and thinly slice onion into half rings.
Once the skillet is hot, add coconut oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add onion to the skillet and stir-fry until tender, 2-3 minutes.
Peel and grate or julienne the carrot.
Add peas and carrots to the skillet with the onions and stir-fry, 2-3 minutes more.
Trim off and discard the root end of the cabbage; halve the cabbage lengthwise, then thinly slice crosswise.
Add cabbage and remaining marinade to skillet and stir-fry until cabbage is just wilted, 1-2 minutes.
To serve, divide stir-fried vegetables between plates; top with chicken and sesame seeds. Enjoy!

name: Spiced Pakistani-Style Chicken Curry with Bell Pepper, Spinach & Rice
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add broth and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Cook rice until liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
While the rice cooks, juice the lime into a medium bowl. Add spices and stir to combine the marinade.
Pat the chicken dry with paper towels and cut into bite-size pieces. Add to the bowl with the marinade and stir to combine; set aside.
Using a clean cutting board, peel and mince ginger and garlic.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat.
While the skillet heats up, peel and small dice onion.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add ginger, garlic, and onion; cook, stirring often, until onion is soft, 3-4 minutes.
Add chicken to the skillet and cook, stirring occasionally, until partially cooked through, 4-5 minutes.
Meanwhile, trim, seed, and medium dice bell pepper.

Add bell pepper, tomato sauce, and water to the skillet. Stir to combine and bring to a boil over high. Once boiling, reduce heat to medium-low; simmer, stirring occasionally, until chicken is cooked through, 15-18 minutes.
Meanwhile, shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves.

When the chicken is done, remove from heat. Stir handfuls of spinach into the skillet, waiting for the spinach to wilt slightly before adding the next handful. Add half the cilantro (reserving the rest for garnish) and stir to combine.
To serve, divide rice and chicken curry between bowls. Top with reserved cilantro and enjoy!

name: Spiced Pork, Apple, Celery & Cranberry Stuffed Acorn Squash
ingredients: 4 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Preheat oven to 500°F and place rack in the center position. Line a baking sheet pan with aluminum foil to make cleanup easier (optional).
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Halve acorn squash lengthwise, trim ends, then scoop out the seeds. Rub the inside of the squash with oil and season with salt and pepper; arrange halves, cut-side down, on the baking sheet.
Place squash in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast until tender, so a knife can easily pierce through the flesh, 20-25 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, peel, halve, and small dice onion; peel and mince garlic. Place both in a medium bowl.
Quarter and core apple, then medium dice; add to the bowl with the onion and garlic.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, trim and small dice celery; add to the bowl with the veggies and apple.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add veggies, apple, pork, and spices; cook, breaking the meat apart with a spoon, until browned and crumbly, 5-6 minutes.

When the pork is done, add broth, cranberries, and sugar; stir to combine and bring to a simmer. Once simmering, reduce heat to medium-low and continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened, 2-3 minutes more. Cover and remove from heat.
To serve, divide squash halves between plates and fill with the pork and veggie stuffing. Enjoy!

name: Spiced Red Lentil, Carrot & Tomato Soup with Guacamole-Radish Toast
ingredients: 24 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel, halve, and small dice onion; peel and mince garlic. Place both in a small bowl.
Preheat a medium saucepan over medium-high heat.
While the pan heats up, peel, trim, and small dice carrot; trim and small dice celery. Add both to the bowl with the onion and garlic.
Once the pan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add veggies and cook, stirring occasionally, until starting to soften, 3-4 minutes. (Reserve bowl for later use.)
Using a strainer or colander, rinse lentils under cold water; drain and set aside.

When the veggies have softened, add lentils, broth, tomatoes, and spices to the pan; stir to combine, cover, and bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Once boiling, reduce heat to a simmer, cover, and cook, stirring occasionally, until lentils are tender, 15-20 minutes.
Meanwhile, halve and pit avocado. Scoop out the flesh and place in the reserved bowl; mash with a fork.
Peel and mince additional garlic; add to the bowl with the avocado.
Juice half of the lemon into the bowl; add salt, stir to combine the guacamole, and set aside. (Reserve remaining lemon for the soup.)

Preheat oven to broil on high and position rack under the broiler. Arrange bread slices on a baking sheet pan and place in the oven; broil until toasted, flipping halfway, 1-2 minutes. Remove from oven.
Trim and small dice radishes.
Once the lentils are tender, juice remaining lemon into the pan and stir to combine the soup. Remove from heat.
Divide guacamole between toast slices and top with radish; season with salt and pepper.
Divide soup between bowls and serve with guacamole-radish toast on the side. Enjoy!

name: Spiced Sirloin with Quinoa, Sweet Pepper, Tomato, & Herb Salad
ingredients: ¾ lb striploin (New York strip) steak
instructions: In a small bowl, combine spices. Pat the steak dry with paper towel, season both sides with spice mixture, and set aside.
In a small saucepan, combine quinoa and water; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to a simmer, cover, and cook for 15 minutes. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and mince shallot and garlic. Add both to a medium bowl.
Grate zest from half of the lemon; juice the entire lemon. Place zest and juice into the bowl with the garlic and shallot. Add olive oil, salt, and pepper; whisk to combine the dressing.
Halve the grape tomatoes and add to the bowl with the dressing.
Preheat a grill pan or regular skillet over medium-high heat.
Medium dice the bell pepper and add to the bowl with the dressing and tomatoes.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Place seasoned steaks on the pan and cook until preferred degree of doneness, 3-4 minutes per side for medium. Remove steaks from the pan and allow to rest for 5 minutes.
Shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl with the vegetables.
Once the quinoa is finished, fluff with a fork and add to the bowl with the dressing and vegetables. Toss to combine.
To serve, slice steak into thin strips and divide between plates along with the salad. Enjoy!

name: Spiced Sweet Potato-Chickpea Bake with Spinach, Carrot & Feta Salad
ingredients: ½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled feta cheese
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)
Drain and rinse chickpeas; set aside to drain further.
Place oil, sesame seeds, spices, and sugar in a medium bowl; stir to combine the spice oil.
Peel, trim, and slice sweet potato crosswise into ½-inch thick rounds. Add to the bowl with the spice oil along with chickpeas; using your hands, gently toss to coat.
Transfer chickpeas and sweet potato to a baking sheet pan, then spread out in a single layer. (Reserve bowl for later use.)

Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast, flipping sweet potato halfway through, until sweet potato is tender and chickpeas are crisp, about 20 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, wipe reserved bowl clean with paper towels.
Using a knife, shave dill leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Place in the bowl.
Juice lemon into the bowl with the dill.
Add feta, yogurt, mayo, water, salt, and pepper to the bowl; whisk to combine the dressing. (Add additional water, 1 teaspoon at a time, if necessary, to reach a drizzling consistency.)
Peel, trim, and julienne or coarsely grate carrots; add to the bowl with the dressing.
Roughly chop spinach, add to the bowl, and toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide chickpeas, sweet potato, and salad between plates. Enjoy!

name: Spiced Turkey Bowl with Basil Slaw, Cucumber, Avocado & Sesame Sauce
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, peel and mince garlic.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add garlic, turkey, and spices; cook, breaking the turkey apart with a spoon, until browned and crumbly, 4-5 minutes. Remove from heat.
Meanwhile, peel and mince ginger; place in a small bowl along with tahini, oil, vinegar, water, soy sauce, and maple syrup. Whisk to combine the sauce and set aside.
Pick basil leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and thinly slice into ribbons. Place in a medium bowl (reserving a small amount for garnish).
Peel, trim, and coarsely grate carrot; add to the bowl with the basil, along with broccoli slaw, and toss to combine.
Trim and thinly slice cucumber crosswise into rounds.
Halve and pit avocado. Slice thinly while still in the skin, then scoop out with a spoon.
To serve, divide slaw between bowls; top with turkey, cucumber, avocado, and reserved basil. Drizzle sauce over top and enjoy!

name: Spiced Veggie, Lentil & Chickpea Soup (Harira) with Cilantro Yogurt
ingredients: 32 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Rinse chickpeas and lentils in a colander or strainer; set aside to drain.
Peel and small dice onion; peel and mince garlic. Place both in a small bowl.
Peel, trim, and small dice carrot; add to the bowl with onion and garlic.
Preheat a medium saucepan over medium heat.
While the pan heats up, trim and small dice celery; add to the bowl with the other veggies.

Once the pan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add onion, garlic, carrot, celery, spices, and sugar to the pan; cook, stirring occasionally, until the veggies soften, 4-5 minutes. (Reserve bowl for later use.)
Add chickpeas, lentils, broth, and tomatoes to the pan; stir to combine, cover, and bring to a boil over medium-high heat.
Once the soup comes to a boil, reduce heat to a simmer and cover; cook, stirring occasionally, until lentils are tender, 15-20 minutes.
Meanwhile, juice lemon into the reserved bowl; add water, flour, and egg. Whisk to combine the thickening liquid.

Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add half of the cilantro to the thickening liquid and whisk to combine; set aside. (Reserve remaining cilantro for the next step.)
Place remaining cilantro in another small bowl. Add yogurt and water; stir to combine the cilantro yogurt and set aside.
When the lentils are tender, slowly pour the thickening liquid into the soup while gently stirring. Simmer until soup thickens, 2-3 minutes.
To serve, divide soup between bowls and top with cilantro yogurt. Enjoy!

name: Spicy African Peanut Curry with Sweet Potato, Kale, Cilantro & Rice
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add water and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, add salt, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Cook rice until liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and mince garlic and ginger; transfer to a medium bowl.

Quarter jalapeño pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon. Finely dice and add to the bowl with the garlic; set aside. (Be careful with jalapeños; do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Preheat a medium saucepan over medium heat.
While the pan heats up, peel and small dice onion.
Once the pan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add onion and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel and medium dice sweet potato.
Add garlic, ginger, jalapeño, curry powder, and salt to the pan. Cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant, about 1 minute. (Reserve bowl for later.)

Add broth, tomatoes, peanut butter, and sweet potato to the pan. Stir to combine and bring to a simmer over medium-high heat. Reduce heat and simmer, stirring occasionally, until sweet potato begins to soften, about 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, fold kale leaves in half lengthwise and slice off the stems. Chop or tear leaves into bite-sized pieces, place in the reserved bowl, and set aside.
Coarsely chop peanuts. Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Set both aside.
Add kale to the simmering curry and stir to combine. Continue to simmer, stirring occasionally, until veggies are tender, about 5 minutes.
While the curry finishes cooking, slice lime into wedges.
To serve, divide rice and curry between bowls; top with peanuts, cilantro, and a squeeze of lime. Enjoy!

name: Spicy Asian Pork, Bok Choy & Snap Pea Stir-Fry over Jasmine Rice
ingredients: 4 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add water and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Cook rice until liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
While the rice cooks, place broth, chili-garlic sauce, soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, and cornstarch in a small bowl; whisk to combine the sauce and set aside.
Trim and cut bok choy crosswise into 1-inch strips; place in a medium bowl.
Halve snap peas crosswise and add to the bowl with the bok choy; set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add pork and cook, breaking the meat apart with a spoon, until browned and crumbly, 4-5 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel and mince ginger and garlic. Add both to the bowl with the veggies.
Trim green onions and cut crosswise into ¼-inch pieces; add half to the bowl. (Reserve remaining green onions for serving.)
When the pork is done, add veggies, ginger, garlic, salt, and pepper to the skillet; stir-fry until veggies soften, about 3 minutes.
Add sauce to the skillet and continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens, 2-3 minutes more. Remove from heat.
To serve, divide rice and stir-fry between plates; sprinkle with reserved green onion and enjoy!

name: Spicy Bacon, Eggplant & Mushroom Pasta (Amatriciana) with Parsley
instructions: Fill a medium saucepan halfway with hot water (from the tap), cover, and bring to a boil. Uncover, add salt and pasta, and stir for a few seconds. Cook until desired firmness, 8-10 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim and small dice eggplant; quarter mushrooms. Transfer both to a medium bowl and set aside.
Preheat a large skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, small dice bacon.

Once the skillet is hot, add bacon and cook, stirring occasionally, until crispy, 4-5 minutes. Using a slotted spoon, transfer bacon to a paper towel-lined plate, leaving the drippings in the skillet.
While the bacon cooks, using a clean cutting board, peel and mince shallot and garlic.

Return the skillet (with bacon drippings) to medium heat. Once the skillet is hot, add eggplant, mushrooms, shallot, garlic, and salt; cook, stirring occasionally, until eggplant and mushrooms are soft and golden, 7-8 minutes.
When the pasta is done, drain in a colander and return to the pan; cover and set aside.
Shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves.
Finely grate Parmesan.
When the veggies are done, add tomato sauce and spices to skillet. Stir to combine the veggie sauce and bring to a simmer; cook, stirring occasionally, until warmed through, about 2 minutes.
Add veggie sauce, bacon, and half of the parsley (reserving the rest for garnish) to the pan with the pasta; stir to combine.
To serve, divide pasta between plates or bowls; top with reserved parsley, additional crushed red pepper, and Parmesan. Enjoy!

name: Spicy Beef Bell Peppers with Cheese, Mixed Greens & Cilantro Dressing
ingredients: ½ (5 oz) pkg spring mix (mixed greens)
instructions: Preheat oven to broil on high and position rack about 6-inches from the top.
Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the mixed greens if they came pre-washed.)
Trim, seed, and halve bell peppers lengthwise. Transfer to a baking sheet pan, drizzle with oil, season with salt and pepper, then arrange cut-side down.
Place baking sheet in the oven and broil until peppers are tender and charred, 5-6 minutes. Remove from oven and set aside to cool.
Meanwhile, preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.

While the skillet heats up, quarter chili pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon. Finely dice. (Be careful with chili peppers; do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Once the skillet is hot, add the ground beef and chili pepper; cook, breaking the meat apart with a spoon, until the beef is browned and cooked through, 3-4 minutes.
While the beef is cooking, shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Place half in a medium bowl and set aside (reserve remaining cilantro for the next step).
Add reserved cilantro and spices to the skillet with the beef; stir to combine and remove from the heat.
Coarsely grate mozzarella.
Divide beef mixture between pepper halves and top with cheese. Return baking sheet to the oven and broil until cheese is melted and bubbly, 2-3 minutes.
Meanwhile, add oil, vinegar, and spices to the bowl with the cilantro; stir to combine the dressing.
Add mixed greens to the bowl with the dressing and toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide stuffed peppers and salad between plates. Enjoy!

name: Spicy Beef & Cheddar Bell Pepper "Nachos" with Tomatoes and Jalapeños
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Peel and mince garlic.

Once the skillet is hot, add ground beef and spices. Cook, breaking the meat apart with a spoon, until the beef is browned and no longer pink, 3-4 minutes. Stir in the garlic, then remove skillet from the heat.
Cut the bell peppers lengthwise into quarters; remove and discard the seeds and white membrane. Slice each quarter crosswise into 3 or 4 pieces to make the "chips."
Line a baking sheet with aluminum foil. Place bell pepper pieces, skin-side down, in a single layer on the baking sheet.
Preheat oven to broil on high; position rack under the broiler.
Grate the cheese.
Thinly slice the jalapeño into rounds. (Be careful, with jalapeños, do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing).
Top the bell pepper slices with an even layer of ground beef, cheese, and jalapeños.
Place the baking sheet in the oven; cook until cheese is melted and bubbly, 3-5 minutes.
Meanwhile, shave the cilantro leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves.
Small dice the tomato. Cut the lime into wedges.
To serve, divide the nachos between plates. Garnish with cilantro, tomatoes, and lime wedges. Enjoy!

name: Spicy Bibimbap Style Cauliflower Stir-Fry with Beef, Veggies & Eggs
instructions: Place eggs in a small saucepan, cover with water, and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to a simmer and cook for 4 minutes. Drain hot water and add ice or run under cold water to cool.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.

Once the skillet is hot, add ground beef and cook, breaking apart with a spoon, until browned and cooked through, 3-4 minutes. Remove skillet from the heat and, using a slotted spoon, transfer beef to a plate and set aside.

Meanwhile, cut the cauliflower head into quarters, then trim off and discard the leaves and thick stem. Using a box grater or food processor, coarsely grate the cauliflower and place in a medium bowl.
Thinly slice mushrooms and add to the bowl with the cauliflower.
Peel, trim, and coarsely grate carrot; add to the bowl.
Return the skillet (with leftover cooking juices) to medium-high heat, add oil, and swirl to coat the bottom. Add veggies and stir to combine.

Add spinach to the skillet in handfuls, waiting for the spinach to wilt slightly before adding the next handful. Once all the spinach has wilted, flatten the veggie mixture in an even layer and cook, without stirring, until a brown crust forms on the bottom, about 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel and mince the garlic and ginger.
Trim green onions and cut crosswise into ¼-inch pieces.
Place garlic, ginger, onions, tomato paste, vinegar, oil, maple syrup, soy sauce, sesame seeds, and crushed red pepper in the bowl used for the veggies. Whisk to combine the sauce.
Drizzle sauce over the veggies, stir to combine, cover, and cook until the veggies are tender, 3-4 minutes.
Return beef to the skillet, stir to combine and continue to cook, until heated through, 1-2 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel and halve the eggs.
To serve, divide stir-fry between bowls or plates and top with eggs. Enjoy!

name: Spicy Black Bean Cauliflower Rice Bowl with Corn, Avocado & Feta
ingredients: ½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled feta cheese
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
