Cut cauliflower head into quarters; using a box grater, hold the stem end of the cauliflower and coarsely grate. (Alternatively, transfer cauliflower to the bowl of a food processor; pulse until rice-like in consistency.) Place in a medium bowl.
Trim and thinly slice green onions crosswise. Add half to the bowl with the cauliflower. (Place remaining onions on a plate and set aside.)
Add oil and spices to the bowl, then stir to combine. Transfer cauliflower rice to a baking sheet pan and spread out in an even layer. (Reserve bowl for later use.)
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast, stirring cauliflower halfway through, until rice is tender and golden, 15-18 minutes.
Meanwhile, shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and roughly chop the leaves. Place half in the reserved bowl. (Add remaining cilantro to the plate with the onions.)
Juice half of the lime into the bowl with the cilantro. Cut remaining lime into wedges and add to the plate.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, drain and rinse beans in a colander.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add beans, corn, and spices; cook, stirring occasionally, until beans and corn are warmed through and spices are fragrant, 3-5 minutes. Remove from heat, add feta, and stir to combine.
Meanwhile, halve and pit avocado; using a spoon, scoop out the flesh. Slice crosswise into thin pieces. Add to the plate.
When the cauliflower is done, remove from the oven. Add lime and cilantro mixture, then stir to combine.
Divide cauliflower rice between bowls; top with spicy bean sauté, reserved cilantro, green onions, and avocado. Serve with lime wedges for squeezing and enjoy!

name: Spicy Bombay Chicken Skillet with Potato, Tomato, Zucchini & Cilantro
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Halve potatoes, place in a medium saucepan, and cover with hot water (from the tap). Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, and simmer until potatoes are fork-tender, 10-15 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel and mince ginger and garlic; place both in a medium bowl.
Peel, halve, and medium dice onion; add to the bowl with the ginger and garlic.
Trim, seed, and medium dice bell pepper; add to the bowl.
Trim and halve zucchini lengthwise, then cut crosswise into ¼-inch thick half-moons; add to the bowl.

Halve jalapeño pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon. Small dice and add to the bowl. (Be careful with jalapeños; do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Preheat a large skillet over medium heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Cut into bite-sized pieces.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add veggies and chicken; cook, stirring occasionally, until chicken is golden brown and almost cooked through, 6-7 minutes.
Meanwhile, using a clean cutting board, shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves.

When the chicken is done, add half of the cilantro (reserving the rest for garnish), tomatoes, pine nuts, and spices to the skillet; stir to combine. Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens, 3-4 minutes more.
When the potatoes are done, drain and add to the skillet; stir to combine and remove from heat.
To serve, divide the chicken skillet between plates or bowls and top with reserved cilantro. Enjoy!

name: Spicy "Buffalo" Wings with Veggie Sticks & Blue Cheese Dressing
ingredients: 1 lb chicken wings, split with tips removed
½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled blue cheese
instructions: Preheat oven to 475°F. Line a baking sheet pan with aluminum foil to make clean up easier (optional).
Pat chicken wings dry with paper towels, place on the baking sheet, and drizzle with oil. Season with salt and pepper, toss to combine, and spread out in an even layer.
Place wings in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and bake, turning once, until cooked through, 20-25 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, place blue cheese in a small bowl; add mayo, water, vinegar, salt, and pepper. Whisk to combine the dressing and set aside.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim and quarter cucumber lengthwise, then cut crosswise into 3-inch pieces; place on a plate.
Peel, trim, and quarter carrot lengthwise, then cut crosswise into 3-inch long pieces; add to the plate with the cucumber.
Trim, seed, and slice bell pepper into thin strips; add to the plate and set aside.

Place oil, chili-garlic sauce, and vinegar in a small saucepan; whisk to combine the sauce and bring to a simmer over medium heat. Once simmering, remove from heat and cover with a lid to keep warm. (If the sauce separates, whisk together once more, right before serving.)
When the wings are done, drizzle with the warm sauce and toss to coat.
To serve, divide wings, veggies, and dressing between plates. Enjoy!

name: Spicy Carrot Flatbread with Arugula, Apricots, Almonds & Minted Yogurt
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the arugula if it came pre-washed.)
Peel, trim, and slice carrots into ¼-inch thick rounds. Place in a medium bowl along with maple syrup, oil, and salt; toss to coat.

Transfer carrots to a baking sheet pan and spread out in a single layer. Place in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and bake, tossing halfway through, until fork-tender, about 12 minutes. Remove from oven and set aside to cool. (Reserve bowl for later use.)

While the carrots are roasting, arrange flatbreads on another baking sheet. Add to the oven and bake, flipping halfway through, until slightly crispy, about 8 minutes. Remove from the oven and set aside to cool.
Meanwhile, pick mint leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Place in a small bowl along with yogurt and salt; stir to combine and set aside.
Peel and mince the garlic. Transfer to the reserved bowl.
Juice lime into the bowl with the garlic; add oil, maple syrup, salt, and crushed red pepper. Whisk to combine the dressing.
Thinly slice apricots and add to the bowl with the dressing.
Roughly chop almonds and set aside.
Once the carrots have cooled to room temperature, transfer to the bowl with the dressing.
Add arugula to the bowl and toss to combine the salad.
Divide minted yogurt between flatbreads and spread out in an even layer. Top each flatbread with carrot-arugula salad and slice into wedges.
To serve, divide flatbreads between plates. Sprinkle with almonds and drizzle with vinegar. Enjoy!

name: Spicy Chicken Parmesan with Sautéed Garlicky Kale
ingredients: ¾ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
instructions: Wash and dry kale. Fold leaves in half lengthwise and slice off the stems. Chop or tear leaves into bite-sized pieces and place in a medium bowl.
Peel and thinly slice garlic. Add to the bowl with the kale and set aside.
Wash, dry, and pick basil leaves off the stems; roll up crosswise and thinly slice into ribbons. Place half in a small bowl. (Set remaining basil aside for serving.)
Add tomato sauce, Italian seasoning, and crushed red pepper to the bowl with the basil. Stir to combine the sauce and set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, holding a knife parallel to the cutting board, cut the chicken in half horizontally to form thin fillets. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add chicken cutlets and pan-fry until golden and cooked through, 3-4 minutes per side.
While the cutlets are cooking, preheat oven to broil on high and position rack in the upper third of the oven.
Coarsely grate cheeses into another medium bowl and stir to combine.
When the cutlets are done, transfer to a baking dish. Pour tomato sauce over chicken and top with cheeses. (Reserve skillet for later use.)
Place baking dish in the oven and broil until the sauce is warmed through and cheese is melted, 2-3 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, wipe the skillet clean with paper towels, then return to medium-high heat.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add garlic and kale to the skillet in handfuls, waiting for kale to wilt slightly before adding the next handful. Season with crushed red pepper and salt. Continue to cook, stirring frequently, until the kale is tender, 1-2 minutes more.
Remove skillet from the heat, add vinegar, and stir to combine.
To serve, divide the chicken, sauce, and kale between plates. Top chicken with reserved basil. Enjoy!

name: Spicy Chicken & Scrambled Egg Wrap with Mango-Spinach Salad
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)
Peel and mince shallot and garlic; place both in a medium bowl.
Juice lime into the bowl with the shallot and garlic, then add oil and spices; whisk to combine the dressing.
Peel mango and slice flesh away from the pit, starting with the flat sides; medium dice and add to the bowl with the dressing. Set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, trim, seed, and small dice bell pepper.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom; add bell pepper, chicken, and spices. Cook, breaking the meat apart with a spoon, until browned and crumbly, 4-5 minutes.
Meanwhile, crack eggs into a small bowl and whisk until smooth.

When the chicken is done, pour eggs into the skillet. Scramble the eggs using a combination of stirring and folding, making sure to bring in all the mixture from the edges of the pan. Cook until the eggs are no longer runny; remove from heat.
While the eggs are cooking, add spinach to the bowl with the dressing and mango; toss to combine the salad.
Place tortillas on a flat surface and divide chicken-egg scramble between them; roll tightly to close.
Cut wraps in half and divide between plates. Serve with salad on the side and enjoy!

name: Spicy Chicken Stir-Fry with Noodles, Mushrooms, Bell Pepper & Broccoli
ingredients: ¾ lb chicken thighs, boneless skinless
instructions: Fill a medium saucepan halfway with hot water (from the tap) and bring to a boil. Remove from heat and add rice noodles. Soak for 10 minutes or according to package directions. Drain in a colander and rinse.
Meanwhile, preheat a skillet over medium heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat chicken dry with paper towels and slice crosswise into thin strips. Sprinkle with cornstarch, salt, and pepper.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add chicken and stir-fry until cooked through, 4-5 minutes. Transfer chicken to a plate and loosely cover with aluminum foil. (Reserve skillet with drippings for later use.)
While the chicken is cooking, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Using a clean cutting board, thinly slice mushrooms. Place in a medium bowl.
Trim, seed, and slice bell pepper lengthwise into thin strips. Add to the bowl with the mushrooms.
Separate broccoli into bite-sized florets and cut stems into smaller pieces. Add to the bowl.
Peel and mince ginger and garlic. Add both to the bowl.
Return skillet (with drippings) to medium heat. Once the skillet is hot, add veggies, salt, and pepper; stir-fry until veggies are fork-tender, 5-6 minutes. (Reserve bowl for the next step.)
While the veggies are cooking, place soy sauce, water, fish sauce, chili-garlic sauce, and cornstarch in the reserved bowl. Whisk to combine the stir-fry sauce.
When the veggies are done, add sauce to the skillet. Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until sauce has thickened, 2-3 minutes more.
Meanwhile, trim green onions and cut crosswise into thin pieces.
Once the sauce has thickened, add drained noodles, chicken, and green onions to the skillet. Toss to combine and continue to cook until warmed through, 1-2 minutes more. Remove from heat.
To serve, divide stir-fry between plates or bowls. Enjoy!

name: Spicy Chickpea Stew (Chana Masala) with Rice & Cilantro-Lime Raita
ingredients: 16 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add broth and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Cook rice until liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
While the rice is cooking, peel and mince garlic and ginger; place in a small bowl.

Quarter jalapeño pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon. Mince and add to the bowl with the garlic and ginger; set aside. (Be careful with jalapeños; do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Preheat a medium saucepan over medium heat.
While the pan heats up, peel and small dice onion.
Once the pan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add onion and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 3 minutes.
Meanwhile, drain and rinse chickpeas in a colander. Set aside to drain further.
Add garlic, ginger, jalapeño, and spices to the pan with the onion. Continue to cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant, about 1 minute. (Reserve bowl for later use.)

Add chickpeas, broth, and diced tomatoes to the pan; stir to combine and bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Once boiling, reduce to a simmer and cook, stirring occasionally, until chickpeas are soft and stew has thickened, about 15 minutes.
While the stew cooks, juice half the lime into the reserved bowl. Cut remaining lime into wedges and set aside for serving.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl with the lime juice along with yogurt, salt, and pepper; whisk to combine the raita.
When the stew is done, add spinach to the pan in handfuls, waiting for the spinach to wilt slightly before adding the next handful.
Divide rice and chickpea stew between bowls; serve with lime wedges and raita on the side. Enjoy!

name: Spicy Chili-Garlic Caramelized Pork Bowl with Carrots, Cucumber & Rice
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add broth and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Cook rice until liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and mince garlic and ginger.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Meanwhile, trim green onions and cut crosswise into ¼-inch pieces; place in a small bowl and set aside.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add garlic, ginger, chili-garlic sauce, and salt; cook, stirring occasionally, until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add pork to the skillet and cook, breaking apart with a spoon, until the pork begins to brown, 3-4 minutes.
Add sugar and fish sauce to the skillet with the pork, stir to combine, and continue to cook, undisturbed, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, trim, halve lengthwise, and cut cucumber crosswise into thin half-moons.

Stir the pork, then continue to cook, undisturbed, until the sugar begins to caramelize and the pork becomes dark brown, 4-5 minutes more. Remove from heat and stir in half of the green onions (reserving the rest for garnish).
While the pork finishes cooking, peel and trim the carrot; using the peeler, run it along the carrot to make long, noodle-like strips. Roughly chop into bite-sized pieces.
To serve, divide rice between bowls. Top with pork, cucumbers, carrots, and remaining green onions. Enjoy!

name: Spicy Chili-Garlic Chicken & Broccoli Rice Bowl
ingredients: ¾ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
instructions: Preheat the oven to 425°F and position rack in the center.
Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add water and salt; bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.

Once the liquid for the rice comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce the heat to low. Cook the rice until the liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove the rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Cut chicken into bite-sized pieces. Add to a medium bowl and sprinkle with cornstarch and salt; toss to coat. Add chicken to one half a baking sheet, then place in the oven and bake for 10 minutes.
Peel and mince garlic; place in a medium bowl.
Wash broccoli. Separate into bite-sized florets and cut stems into smaller pieces.

Remove the chicken from the oven and toss; add broccoli to the other half of the baking sheet. Drizzle broccoli with sesame oil and season with salt and pepper. Return tray to the oven until chicken and broccoli are cooked, about 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, add honey, chili-garlic sauce, vinegar, and sesame oil to the bowl with the garlic; whisk until well combined.
Wash the green onions, trim off and discard the ends; cut the onions crosswise into ¼-inch pieces.
When the chicken is done add to the bowl with the sauce and toss to coat.
To serve, divide rice, chicken, and broccoli between bowls. Top with green onions and sesame seeds and enjoy!

name: Spicy Edamame Salad with Creamy Ginger-Peanut Dressing & Avocado
instructions: Fill a medium saucepan about halfway with hot water (from the tap); cover and bring to a boil over high heat.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Once the water in the saucepan is boiling, add edamame and cook until tender, about 5 minutes. Drain and rinse under cold water. Set aside to drain further.
Meanwhile, peel and mince or grate ginger; transfer to a medium bowl.
Add peanut butter, water, soy sauce, vinegar, and chili-garlic sauce to the bowl with the ginger; whisk to combine the dressing.
Trim and slice cucumber into thin rounds; add to the bowl with the dressing.

Quarter chili pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon. Thinly slice and add to the bowl. (Be careful, with chili peppers, do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Halve and pit the avocado; slice crosswise while still in the skin and scoop out with a spoon. Add to the bowl.
Cut romaine crosswise into thin (shred-like) strips; add to the bowl.
Add edamame to the bowl and toss to combine the salad.
Roughly chop peanuts.
To serve, divide salad between plates or bowls, top with peanuts, and enjoy!

name: Spicy Ginger-Lime Chicken Thighs with Sweet Potatoes & Asparagus
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and medium dice sweet potatoes; transfer to a baking sheet pan.
Snap or cut off the woody ends of the asparagus; add to the baking sheet with the potatoes.
Drizzle oil over veggies and season with salt and pepper; toss to combine, then spread out in an even layer. Place in the oven and bake until vegetables are fork-tender, 15-20 minutes.
Meanwhile, preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with salt and pepper on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom.

Add chicken to the skillet; cook until golden brown, about 2 minutes per side. Once golden, transfer to a clean plate and loosely cover with aluminum foil (the chicken will not be cooked all the way through).
Meanwhile, peel and mince ginger.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves.

Return skillet to medium heat. Juice lime into the skillet. Add ginger, half of the cilantro (reserving the rest for garnish), oil, chili-garlic sauce, honey, and coriander. Stir to combine the sauce.
Return chicken to the skillet, along with any accumulated juices. Cover and simmer until chicken is cooked through, 8-10 minutes.
To serve, divide chicken and vegetables between plates. Sprinkle with reserved cilantro and enjoy!

name: Spicy Ginger-Soy Rice Bowl with Tofu, Mushrooms & Brussels Sprouts
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.

Cut tofu in half along the long side. Sandwich tofu between clean towels or paper towels and place on a large baking sheet pan. Place a cutting board with something heavy on top and set aside to press out excess water.
Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add water and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Cook rice until liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.

Peel and mince ginger. Place in a medium bowl along with soy sauce, chili-garlic sauce, oil, and maple syrup. Whisk to combine the marinade. Transfer half of the marinade to a small bowl and set aside for serving.
Medium dice tofu, add to the medium bowl with the marinade, and gently stir to coat. Set aside. (Wipe baking sheet dry with paper towels and reserve for the next step.)
Trim and thinly slice Brussels sprouts crosswise. Transfer to the reserved baking sheet.
Thinly slice mushrooms and add to the baking sheet with the Brussels sprouts.

Trim off root end and dark green top of the leek, leaving only the white and pale green parts. Cut leek in half lengthwise and rinse under running water, separating the layers to remove any dirt and grit. Slice crosswise into ¼-inch thick pieces. Add to the baking sheet.
Drizzle veggies with oil and season with salt. Toss to combine, then spread out in an even layer on one half of the baking sheet.
Transfer tofu to the other side of the baking sheet and spread out in an even layer. Drizzle with any leftover marinade in the bowl.
Place baking sheet in the oven and roast, stirring halfway through, until veggies are tender and tofu is golden, about 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, roughly chop cashews.
When the veggies and tofu are done, remove from the oven. Sprinkle cashews over veggies and toss to combine.
To serve, divide rice, tofu, and veggies between plates or bowls; drizzle with remaining marinade. Enjoy!

name: Spicy Grilled Chicken with Tomato-Cilantro Salsa & Mexican Corn Salad
ingredients: ½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled feta cheese
instructions: Place hot sauce, oil, honey, and spices in a medium bowl. Stir to combine the marinade.
Add chicken to the bowl with the marinade, stir to coat, and set aside.
Preheat a grill pan, outdoor grill, or skillet over medium-high heat.
While the pan heats up, remove husks and silks from corn. Using your hands, snap each ear in half.
Once the pan is hot, add corn cobs and grill, rotating occasionally, until slightly charred, 4-5 minutes. Remove to a plate and allow to cool slightly. (Reserve pan for later use.)
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Zest and juice lime into another medium bowl.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl with the lime.
Peel and mince shallots. Add to the bowl, along with the spices, and stir to combine the lime dressing. Transfer half of the dressing to a third medium bowl, then set both bowls aside.
Return the grill pan to medium-high heat. Once the pan is hot, add chicken and grill until charred and cooked through, 3-4 minutes per side. Once done, add to the plate with the corn.
Meanwhile, quarter tomatoes. Trim, seed, and medium dice bell pepper. Add both to one of the bowls with the dressing, stir to combine the salsa, and set aside.
Working over the bowl with the remaining lime dressing, coarsely grate corn off of the cob, catching all of the kernels and juices in the bowl.
Add feta, yogurt, and mayo to the bowl with the corn. Stir to combine the corn salad.
To serve, divide chicken, corn salad, and tomato salsa between plates. Enjoy!

name: Spicy Honey Butter Shrimp with Sautéed Kale & Creamy Cheddar Rice
ingredients: 6 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
¾ lb raw peeled shrimp, fresh or frozen
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add broth and milk; bring the mixture to a simmer over medium-high heat.
Meanwhile, coarsely grate cheese, transfer to a small bowl, and set aside.
Once the liquid comes to a simmer, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Cook until liquid is partially absorbed and the rice is tender, 15-18 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry kale. Fold leaves in half lengthwise and slice off the stems. Chop or tear leaves into bite-sized pieces and set aside.

If using frozen shrimp, place them in a colander and run under cold water to thaw them slightly and remove any ice crystals. (If using fresh shrimp, skip this step.) Place the shrimp on a clean towel or paper towels and pat dry.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add butter, honey, and chili-garlic sauce; whisk to combine.
Add shrimp to the skillet and cook until opaque, 1-2 minutes per side. Once done, transfer shrimp and butter sauce to a medium bowl; cover with foil.
When the rice is tender, with some liquid remaining, add the cheese and stir to combine. Remove from the heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Return the skillet to medium-high heat, add more butter, and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add kale to the skillet in handfuls, waiting for the kale to wilt slightly before adding the next handful. Season with salt and pepper; cook, stirring often, until soft, 4-5 minutes.
To serve, divide rice, kale, and shrimp between bowls. Drizzle with honey butter and enjoy!

name: Spicy Italian Sausage & Mixed Pepper Skillet with Rice
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add water and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Cook rice until liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, cut the sausages into 1-inch pieces.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add sausage and pan-fry, stirring occasionally, until browned and cooked through, about 8 minutes.
Meanwhile, using a clean cutting board, seed and slice bell peppers into thin strips. Transfer to a medium bowl.

Halve jalapeño pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon. Thinly slice and add to the bowl with the bell peppers. (Be careful with jalapeños; do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Peel and mince garlic. Peel, halve, and thinly slice onion into half moons; add both to the bowl with the peppers.
When the sausages are done, remove to a plate.
Return the skillet to medium heat, add additional oil, and swirl to coat the bottom. Add the veggies and spices; cook, stirring occasionally, until soft and browned, about 10 minutes.
Stir sausages into the skillet and continue to cook until heated through, about 3 minutes. Remove from heat.
To serve, divide rice and sausage-pepper skillet between plates. Enjoy!

name: Spicy Italian-Style Sausage Bake with Peppers, Eggplant & Pine Nuts
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F and position rack in the upper third of the oven.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim, seed, and slice bell peppers lengthwise into thin strips. Transfer to a baking sheet pan.
Trim and medium dice eggplant. Add to the baking sheet with the bell pepper.
Peel, halve, and slice onion lengthwise into thin strips; add to the baking sheet.
Drizzle veggies with oil and season with spices; toss to coat and spread out in an even layer.
Add sausages to the baking sheet, nestling them into the veggies.

Place the baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and bake, stirring veggies and flipping sausages halfway through, until veggies are tender and sausages are nearly cooked through, about 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, preheat a skillet over medium heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add pine nuts. Cook, stirring constantly, until golden brown, 3-5 minutes. Transfer to a small bowl and set aside.
When the veggies and sausages are nearly done, change the oven to broil on high. Broil until veggies and sausages are browned, about 3 minutes.
Meanwhile, shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and roughly chop the leaves.
Remove baking sheet from the oven, add half of the parsley and vinegar, then toss to combine. (Reserve remaining parsley for serving.)
To serve, divide sausages and veggies between plates. Top with toasted pine nuts and reserved parsley. Enjoy!

name: Spicy "Jalapeño Popper" Burger with Grilled Bell Pepper Salad
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.

Quarter jalapeño pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon. Finely dice and place in a medium bowl. (Be careful with jalapeños; do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Coarsely grate cheese into the bowl with the jalapeño. Add ground beef and spices; mix with your hands until well combined. Form into 2 equal-sized patties, place on a plate, and set aside.
Preheat a grill pan, outdoor grill, or regular skillet over medium-high heat.
While the grill pan heats up, quarter, trim, and seed bell pepper. Place in another medium bowl, drizzle with oil, and sprinkle with salt; toss to combine.
Once the grill pan is hot, add bell pepper and cook, turning occasionally, until charred and fork-tender, about 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, place oil, vinegar, Dijon, salt, and pepper in the bowl used for the peppers. Whisk to combine the dressing.
When the peppers are done, transfer to a cutting board to cool.
Place burger patties on the grill pan and cook, undisturbed, for 5 minutes; flip patties, and grill an additional 2-3 minutes, until cooked through. Once done, transfer to a clean plate.
Once the peppers are cool enough to handle, roughly chop and transfer to the bowl with the dressing.
Separate the lettuce leaves. Set aside 1 leaf per burger and chop or tear remaining leaves into bite-sized pieces; add chopped lettuce to the bowl with the peppers and toss to combine the salad.
Slice tomato into rounds.
If desired, place buns, cut-side down, on the grill pan to toast, 1-2 minutes.
Place bottom half of a bun on each plate, spread with ketchup, then top with burgers, lettuce, and tomato slices. Close with the top half of the bun and serve with salad on the side. Enjoy!

name: Spicy Mapo Tofu with Ground Pork, Mushrooms, Spinach & Green Onion
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add water and salt; bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce the heat to low. Cook the rice until the liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove the rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Slice the mushrooms and set aside.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add ground pork and cook, breaking the meat apart with a spoon, until the pork begins to brown, 3-4 minutes.
Meanwhile, drain and dice tofu into ½-inch cubes; add to the skillet with the pork.
Peel and mince or grate ginger; peel and mince garlic.
Add ginger and garlic to the skillet; cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant, 30-60 seconds.
Add mushrooms, soy sauce, vinegar, and chili-garlic sauce to the skillet; continue to cook, stirring often, until the mushrooms begin to soften, 4-5 minutes.
Meanwhile, in a small bowl, make a slurry by whisking water with cornstarch until smooth.
Trim green onions; cut crosswise into ¼-inch pieces. Add most of the green onions to the skillet (reserve a small amount for garnish).
Add spinach to the skillet in handfuls, waiting for the spinach to wilt slightly before adding the next handful.
Add the cornstarch slurry to the skillet in a steady stream while stirring quickly. Cook, stirring often, until the sauce thickens, 1-2 minutes. Remove from heat.
To serve, divide rice and tofu-pork mixture between bowls or plates. Garnish with reserved green onions and enjoy!

name: Spicy Mexican-Style Ground Beef Frittata with Pico de Gallo
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel, halve, and mince onion; place half in a small bowl. Set remaining onion aside for later use.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl with the onion.
Small dice tomatoes and add to the bowl.

Quarter jalapeño pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon. Mince and add to the bowl. (Be careful with jalapeños; do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Juice lime into the bowl, then add salt and pepper. Stir to combine the pico de gallo and set aside.
Preheat an ovenproof skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, peel and mince garlic.
Once the skillet is hot, add reserved onion, garlic, ground beef, and spices to the skillet. Cook, breaking the meat apart with a spoon, until browned and crumbly, 4-5 minutes.
Meanwhile, preheat oven to broil on high and position rack under the broiler.
Trim, seed, and medium dice bell pepper. Add to the skillet and continue to cook until the pepper starts to soften, 2-3 minutes more.
While the bell pepper is cooking, place eggs, salt, and pepper in a medium bowl; whisk to combine.

When the bell pepper is tender, reduce heat to medium-low; pour the egg mixture into the skillet. As eggs set around the edge of the skillet, gently lift cooked portions with a spatula to allow uncooked egg to flow underneath. Cook until bottom and sides are firm but top is still runny, 5-7 minutes.
Meanwhile, coarsely grate mozzarella.
Sprinkle mozzarella over the frittata. Place skillet in the oven and broil until top of the frittata is set and cheese is melted, 3-4 minutes; remove from oven.
To serve, cut frittata into wedges and divide between plates; top with pico de gallo. Enjoy!

name: Spicy Orange Beef & Broccoli Stir-Fry
ingredients: ¾ lb striploin (New York strip) steak
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add water and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce the heat to low. Cook the rice until the liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes.
Peel and mince the garlic. Peel and mince or grate the ginger. Set both aside in a small bowl.
Use a grater to zest the orange and transfer to the bowl with the garlic and ginger. Juice the orange into a separate small bowl.
Heat the oil in a small saucepan over medium-low heat. Once the oil is hot, add the garlic, ginger, orange zest, and chili-garlic sauce. Sauté until ingredients soften, 2-3 minutes.

Add orange juice, brown sugar, rice vinegar, and soy sauce to the saucepan. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer, uncovered and stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens and reduces by half, about 10 minutes.
Preheat a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat.
Slice the steak against the grain into ½-inch strips.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom.

Add the beef to the skillet and cook, without stirring, for 1 minute. Then turn the beef pieces over and cook, stirring occasionally, 2-3 minutes for medium-rare. Transfer beef to a plate and set aside.
Meanwhile, separate broccoli into bite-sized florets. Return the skillet to medium heat and add the broccoli. Stir-fry until tender-crisp, about 7 minutes.
Trim off and discard the ends of the green onions; cut the onions crosswise into ¼-inch pieces at an angle.
Add the beef back into the skillet with the broccoli. Add green onions and orange sauce to the skillet and stir well.
To serve, divide the rice into bowls and top with the beef and veggie mixture. Enjoy!

name: Spicy Orange Tofu & Broccoli with Basmati Rice
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Season the rice with salt and add water; bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
Wash orange and grate ½ tbsp of zest into a small bowl, then juice orange into the same bowl. Add water, soy sauce, rice vinegar, honey, chili-garlic sauce, and cornstarch to bowl and whisk together.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce the heat to low. Cook the rice until the liquid is fully absorbed, 15 to 18 minutes. Once done, remove the rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Heat a skillet over medium heat.
Drain tofu and pat dry with paper towels. Medium dice.
Coat bottom of skillet with oil. Add tofu and cook, stirring occasionally, until golden brown, 7-9 minutes. Transfer to a plate.
Peel and mince garlic.
Wash broccoli. Separate into bite-sized florets and cut stem into smaller pieces.
Once tofu has been transferred, coat skillet with more oil. Add garlic and broccoli. Cook, stirring occasionally, until tender-crisp and bright green, 3-4 minutes.
Return tofu to skillet and pour in sauce. Stir to coat until sauce thickens, 1-2 minutes.
Uncover the rice and fluff with a fork.
Serve broccoli and tofu over top rice and enjoy!

name: Spicy Peanut Pork Stir-Fry with Bok Choy, Mango & Broccoli Slaw
instructions: Peel and mince garlic; place in a medium bowl.
Add soy sauce, oil, and crushed red pepper to the bowl with the garlic; whisk to combine the marinade.
Slice pork chops crosswise into ½-inch thick strips, add to the bowl with the marinade, toss to coat, and set aside.
While the pork marinates, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Using a clean cutting board, peel and mince ginger; place in a small bowl.
Juice lime into the bowl with the ginger; add peanut butter, fish sauce, water, honey, and spices. Whisk to combine the peanut sauce and set aside.
Place oil, soy sauce, vinegar, honey, and chili-garlic sauce in another medium bowl; whisk to combine the dressing and set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add pork strips and marinade; stir-fry until browned and cooked through, 4-5 minutes.
Meanwhile, trim and thinly slice bok choy crosswise into shred-like strips; add to the bowl with the dressing.
Peel mango and slice flesh away from the pit, starting with the flat sides; large dice and add to the bowl.
Add broccoli slaw to the bowl and toss to combine.
When the pork is done, add peanut sauce, stir to combine, and cook until sauce is warmed through and pork is coated, about 1 minute. Remove from heat.
To serve, divide pork stir-fry and slaw between plates. Sprinkle pork with additional crushed red pepper and enjoy!

name: Spicy Peanut Tofu Bowl with Kale & Savory Sesame Rice
instructions: Cut the tofu in half along the long side. Sandwich the tofu between clean towels or paper towels and place side by side on a baking sheet. Place a cutting board with something heavy on top and set aside to press out excess water.
Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add water and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
Peel and mince the garlic. In a medium bowl, combine garlic, sesame oil, soy sauce, and maple syrup to make a marinade for the tofu.

Once the liquid with the rice comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce the heat to low. Cook the rice until the liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove the rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, cut the tofu planks in half and then cut each half into 4 triangles. Place tofu in the bowl with the marinade and gently toss until well coated. Set aside.
Wash and dry kale. Fold leaves in half lengthwise and slice off the stems. Chop or tear leaves into bite-sized pieces and transfer to a salad bowl.
Wash, trim, and peel the carrot; coarsely grate and set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Wash, peel, and mince or grate the ginger.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add the tofu and the marinade.  Cook until golden brown, 2-3 minutes per side.
Meanwhile, prepare the peanut sauce by whisking together ginger, peanut butter, chili-garlic sauce, soy sauce, maple syrup, and hot water in a small bowl.

Once the tofu is cooked, transfer to a plate, returning the skillet to the heat. Add kale and water to the skillet and cover with a lid. Allow to steam for 1 minute covered then uncover, stirring occasionally, for 1 minute more.
Uncover the rice, fluff with a fork, and add sesame oil. Fold the oil into the rice.
To serve, divide rice between bowls, top with tofu, grated carrot, and kale; drizzle with peanut sauce and sprinkle with sesame seeds. Enjoy!

name: Spicy Peruvian Roast Chicken with Sweet Potatoes & Cilantro-Feta Salsa
ingredients: ½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled feta cheese
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F. Position racks in the upper and lower thirds of the oven. Line a baking sheet pan with aluminum foil.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and slice sweet potatoes into ½-inch thick rounds. Place in a medium bowl, drizzle with oil, and season with salt and pepper. Toss to coat.
Arrange sweet potatoes on the baking sheet in a single layer. Place on the lower rack of the oven and bake, flipping halfway through, until fork-tender, 20-25 minutes.
Meanwhile, zest and juice half the lime into the bowl used for the sweet potatoes. Set remaining lime aside.
Peel and mince garlic. Add to the bowl along with oil, sugar, and spices. Stir to combine the spice paste.
Preheat an ovenproof skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels and add to the bowl with the spice paste; turn to coat.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add chicken and cook on one side until golden brown and caramelized, 4-5 minutes. Flip and cook for 1 minute more, then remove from heat (the chicken will not be cooked all the way through).
Transfer the skillet to the upper rack of the oven and roast until chicken is cooked through, about 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, juice remaining lime into a small bowl.

Quarter jalapeño pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon. Mince and add to the bowl with the lime juice. (Be careful, with jalapeños, do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl.
Peel and mince additional garlic. Add to the bowl along with feta, oil, sugar, cumin, and salt. Stir to combine the salsa.
To serve, divide sweet potatoes and chicken between plates. Spoon salsa over chicken and enjoy!

name: Spicy Pork Pad Thai with Sugar Peas, Lime & Cilantro
ingredients: ½ (8 oz) pkg sugar snap peas
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.

Fill a medium saucepan halfway with water and bring to a boil. Remove from heat and add rice noodles. Soak for 10 minutes or according to package directions. Then using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice noodles under cold, running water.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
When the skillet is hot, add pork and, breaking apart with a spoon, cook until browned and crumbly, 4-6 minutes.
Meanwhile, juice half the lime into a small bowl. Add sauces and sugar; whisk to combine.
Peel and mince garlic.
Slice peas and green onions crosswise into ¼-inch pieces at an angle.
Add garlic and vegetables to the skillet and cook, stirring frequently, until they begin to soften, about 3 minutes.
Push pork and veggies to the edge of the skillet and crack the egg in the center. Scramble until the egg is lightly set, then mix in with the pork and veggies.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves. Add cilantro to the skillet, reserving some for garnish.
Add noodles and sauce to the skillet. Stir until coated and warmed through, 1-3 minutes.
Cut remaining lime into wedges.
To serve, divide Pad Thai between bowls and garnish with remaining cilantro and lime wedges.

name: Spicy Pork Tacos with Kiwi, Cucumber & Avocado Salsa
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim, peel, and small dice kiwis; place in a small bowl.
Halve, pit, and scoop out the avocado flesh with a spoon; small dice and add to the bowl with the kiwi.
Trim and small dice cucumber; add to the bowl.
Juice lime into the bowl, then season with salt and crushed red pepper. Stir to combine the salsa and set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.

While the skillet heats up, quarter jalapeño pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon. Finely dice. (Be careful with jalapeños; do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add jalapeño, pork, and spices; cook, breaking apart with a spoon, until browned and crumbly, 4-5 minutes. Remove from heat.
Meanwhile, warm tortillas in another skillet, oven, or microwave (optional).
To serve, divide tortillas between plates and fill with spicy pork. Top with salsa and enjoy!

name: Spicy Sausage, Mushroom & Bell Pepper Quinoa Bowl with Wilted Spinach
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: In a small saucepan, combine quinoa and broth; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to a simmer, cover, and cook for 15 minutes. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)
Thinly slice mushrooms and transfer to a small bowl.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, slice the sausages crosswise into ½-inch thick rounds.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add sausage and cook, stirring occasionally, until starting to brown, about 4 minutes. Use a slotted spoon to transfer the sausage to a plate (the sausage will not be cooked all the way through).
Meanwhile, using a clean cutting board, peel and mince garlic; peel and medium dice onion. Add both to the bowl with the mushrooms.

Return skillet (with cooking juices) to medium-high heat; add veggies and Italian seasoning. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the mushrooms have softened, about 6 minutes. (Reserve bowl for the next step.)

While the mushrooms are cooking, quarter jalapeño pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon. Finely dice and place in the reserved bowl. (Be careful with jalapeños; do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Trim, seed, and medium dice bell pepper; add to the bowl with the jalapeño.
Add jalapeño, bell pepper, browned sausage, salt, and pepper to the skillet; cook, stirring occasionally, until the bell pepper starts to soften and sausage is cooked through, about 4 minutes.
Add spinach to the skillet in handfuls, waiting for the spinach to wilt slightly before adding the next handful.
To serve, divide quinoa, sausage, and veggies between bowls. Enjoy!

name: Spicy Seared Lamb Chops with Cucumbers, Peaches, Almonds & Yogurt
instructions: Preheat a skillet over medium heat.
While the skillet heats up, roughly chop almonds.
Once the skillet is hot, add the almonds; cook, stirring constantly, until lightly browned, 2-3 minutes. Transfer to a medium bowl and set aside to cool. (Reserve skillet for later use.)
Place spices in a small bowl. Stir to combine the spice rub.
Return the skillet to medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the lamb chops dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with the spice rub on both sides. (Reserve bowl for later use.)

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add chops and sear, flipping once, until cooked through, 5-6 minutes. Remove to a clean plate, loosely cover with aluminum foil, and set aside to rest.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Zest and juice half of the lemon into the reserved bowl. Cut remaining lemon into wedges and set aside for serving.
Meanwhile, pick parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems. Mince half of the leaves and add to the bowl with the lemon. Roughly chop remaining leaves and set aside for serving.
Add yogurt and salt to the bowl, then whisk to combine the lemony yogurt. Set aside.
Trim and medium dice cucumber. Add to the bowl with the almonds.
Quarter peaches lengthwise (around the pit); twist quarters to separate, then remove and discard pits. Medium dice the flesh and add to the bowl. Season the salad with salt, then stir to combine.
Divide chops and lemony yogurt between plates. Top yogurt with the salad and reserved parsley, then drizzle with honey. Serve with lemon wedges for squeezing and enjoy!

name: Spicy Sesame Soba Noodles with Kale, Green Onion & Soft-Boiled Eggs
instructions: Place eggs in a small saucepan, cover with water, and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to a simmer and cook for 4 minutes. Drain hot water and add ice or run under cold water to cool.
Meanwhile, fill a large pot about halfway with hot water (from the tap); cover and bring to a boil over high heat.
While the water heats up, wash and dry kale. Fold leaves in half lengthwise and slice off the stems. Stack leaves on top of one another, then cut crosswise into thin (shred-like) ribbons.

Once the water in the pot is boiling, uncover, add kale, and stir. Cook until bright green and wilted, about 15 seconds. Transfer kale to a colander using a slotted spoon. (Reserve pot of water for the next step.)
Return water to a boil. Once the water is boiling, add noodles and cook according to package directions, about 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash, dry, and trim green onions; cut crosswise into thin pieces and set aside.
Place tahini, water, soy sauce, chili-garlic sauce, and oil in a medium bowl. Whisk to combine the sauce and set aside.
When the noodles are done, drain in the colander over the kale. Rinse thoroughly under cold water and set aside to drain further.
Peel and quarter the eggs.
Add noodles, kale, and half of the green onions to the bowl with the sauce; toss to combine. (Reserve remaining green onions for serving.)
To serve, divide the noodles and kale between plates or bowls. Top with remaining green onions, sesame seeds, and eggs. Enjoy!

name: Spicy Shrimp Curry with Tomatoes, Spinach & Cilantro over Rice
ingredients: 12 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
½ (13.5 fl oz) can coconut milk
¾ lb raw peeled shrimp, fresh or frozen
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add broth and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Cook rice until liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)

If using frozen shrimp, place them in a colander and run under cold water to thaw them slightly and remove any ice crystals. (If using fresh shrimp, skip this step.) Place the shrimp on a clean towel or paper towels and pat dry.
Small dice tomatoes; place in a small bowl and set aside.
Preheat a medium saucepan over medium heat.
While the pan heats up, peel, halve, and small dice onion.
Once the pan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add onion and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 3 minutes.
While the onion cooks, peel and mince ginger and garlic.
Add ginger, garlic, sugar, and spices to the pan with the onion. Continue to cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant, about 1 minute.

Add tomatoes, coconut milk, and broth to the pan; stir to combine the curry and bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Once boiling, reduce to a simmer and cook, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened, about 8 minutes.
While the curry cooks, cut lime into wedges and set aside for serving.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves.

Once the curry has thickened, add shrimp and half of the cilantro (reserving the rest for garnish) to the pan; stir to combine. Return to a simmer and cook, stirring occasionally, until the shrimp are cooked through, 3-4 minutes.
Add spinach to the pan in handfuls, waiting for the spinach to wilt slightly before adding the next handful; stir to combine.
Divide rice and shrimp curry between bowls; sprinkle with reserved cilantro and serve with lime wedges. Enjoy!

name: Spicy Sichuan-Style "Dan Dan" Zucchini Noodles with Pork & Peanuts
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim zucchini; use a julienne (or regular) peeler to make noodles. Transfer to a baking sheet pan, drizzle with oil, then season with salt and pepper. Toss to coat and spread out in an even layer.
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated), and roast, tossing halfway through, until zucchini is tender, about 10 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, trim and cut green onions crosswise into thin pieces.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, peel and mince garlic.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add green onion, garlic, pork, salt, and pepper. Cook, breaking the meat apart with a spoon, until browned and crumbly, 4-5 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel and mince ginger and additional garlic. Place both in a small bowl.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and roughly chop the leaves. Add half of the cilantro to the bowl with the ginger and garlic. (Reserve remaining cilantro for serving.)
Add tahini, water, soy sauce, vinegar, chili-garlic sauce, and additional oil to the bowl. Whisk to combine the sauce.
When the pork is done, add cooked zucchini noodles and sauce to the skillet; stir to combine. Cook, stirring frequently, until sauce is warmed through, about 1 minute. Remove from heat.
Roughly chop peanuts.
To serve, divide pork zucchini noodles between plates or bowls; top with reserved cilantro and peanuts. Enjoy!

name: Spicy Sweet Potato & Black Bean Burrito
ingredients: 16 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and small dice onion. Small dice bell pepper.
Heat a large pot over medium heat. Once the pot is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add onion and bell pepper to the pot; cook, stirring frequently, until softened, 3-4 minutes.
Peel and small dice sweet potato.
Add sweet potato and broth to the pot and bring to a boil; reduce heat and simmer, 10 minutes, until potatoes are fork-tender.
Drain and rinse beans in a colander; set aside to drain further.
Grate cheddar. Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves.
Once potatoes are tender, drain vegetables; return them to the pot and place on low heat.
Add beans, cheddar, cilantro, yogurt, and spices to the pot. Stir to combine and remove from the heat.
Lay tortillas on a flat surface. Divide vegetable mixture evenly and place in the middle of each tortilla. Fold in sides of tortilla and roll tightly.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Lay burritos seam side down and cook for 2-3 minutes on each side, until golden brown and crispy.
Remove burritos from heat, cut in half, and enjoy!

name: Spicy Taco Beef Lettuce Wraps with Fajita Peppers, Onions & Avocado
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, peel, halve, and small dice onion. Place in a medium bowl.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add the beef and cook, breaking it apart with a spoon, until browned and crumbly, 5-6 minutes.
Meanwhile, trim, seed, and small dice bell peppers. Add to the bowl with the onion.
When the beef is done, add onion, bell pepper, and spices to the skillet. Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until veggies start to soften, 3-4 minutes more.
While the veggies are cooking, cut lime into wedges and set aside for serving.
When the veggies are soft, add water to the skillet. Cook, stirring occasionally, until sauce is thickened, 1-2 minutes. Remove from heat.
Meanwhile, halve and pit avocado; using a spoon, scoop out the flesh and slice crosswise into thin half-moons.
Separate the lettuce into leaves. Pile leaves, in stacks of two per wrap, onto plates. Fill each wrap with beef, veggies, and avocado. Serve with lime wedges and enjoy!

name: Spicy Thai Basil Chicken with Baby Spinach & Rice
ingredients: 4 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
¾ lb chicken thighs, boneless skinless
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add water and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)
In a medium bowl, combine the broth, soy sauce, fish sauce, and brown sugar. Whisk to combine the sauce and set aside.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce the heat to low. Cook the rice until the liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove the rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Roughly chop the chicken thighs into ½-inch pieces.

Peel and mince the garlic and shallot. Quarter the jalapeño pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs of the jalapeño with a spoon. Finely dice and set aside. (Be careful, with jalapeños, do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing).
Heat a large skillet over high heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add chicken and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes, then add the garlic, shallot, and jalapeño. Continue cooking on high heat for 2-3 more minutes, stirring often.
Chop the baby spinach into small pieces.
Pour the sauce into the skillet. Cook on high, stirring often, until the sauce thickens and glazes the meat, 8-12 minutes. Remove from heat.
Pick basil leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and thinly slice into ribbons. Reserve a few leaves for garnish.
Add the baby spinach (one handful at a time) and basil to the skillet and stir until wilted.
To serve, divide the rice and chicken between bowls. Garnish with reserved basil and enjoy!

name: Spicy Thai Coconut Chicken Soup (Tom Kha Gai)
ingredients: ¾ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
24 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
½ (13.5 fl oz) can coconut milk
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and thinly slice onion into half rings.
Heat a large pot over medium heat.
Peel and mince ginger and garlic.
Once the pot is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add onion, ginger, garlic, and chili-garlic sauce to the pot. Cook, stirring frequently, until onion begins to soften, 2-3 minutes.
Add broth, coconut milk, sugar, fish sauce, and salt to the pot. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce heat to a simmer.
Thinly slice mushrooms.
Slice chicken crosswise into thin strips.
Add mushrooms and chicken to the pot and continue to simmer until chicken is cooked through, 10-12 minutes.
Meanwhile, using a fresh cutting board, trim green onions; cut crosswise into ¼-inch pieces.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems.
When the soup is done, juice lime into the pot and stir to combine.
To serve, divide soup between bowls. Top with green onions and cilantro. Enjoy!

name: Spicy Thai Coconut Pumpkin Soup
ingredients: 16 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
½ (13.5 fl oz) can coconut milk
½ (15 oz) can pure pumpkin purée
instructions: Heat a large pot over medium heat.
Meanwhile, peel and small dice onion. Trim off and discard the root ends of the garlic and press or mince.
Once the pot is hot, add coconut oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add the onion and garlic to the pot.
Wash and peel the carrot, then trim off the ends. Using a box grater, coarsely grate the carrot and add to pot.
Wash the cilantro and shave the cilantro leaves off the stems. Chop the stems into small pieces and add to the pot. Mince the leaves and set half aside for garnish, add the rest to the pot.
Season mixture with salt and pepper. Cook until all vegetables have softened, 3-4 minutes.
Reduce heat to low. Wash, peel and mince or grate the ginger. Add to the pot.
Add pumpkin, honey and cayenne pepper, stirring to combine.
Shake can of coconut milk vigorously before opening. Add half the can to the soup and reserve a few tablespoons for garnish.
Add broth and bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer stirring occasionally, 8-10 minutes.
Meanwhile, melt butter and oil over medium heat in a small saucepan.
Peel and thinly slice the shallot into rings. Add to pan breaking it up as you go.

Turn heat up to medium-high. Cook until shallots are starting to darken around the edges, about 2 minutes. Reduce heat to low and continue to cook until golden brown and crispy, 2-3 minutes more. Watch carefully as they can burn easily.
Transfer shallots to a paper towel-lined plate and discard oil. Season with salt.
Using an immersion (hand) blender, purée the soup until smooth.
Wash and cut the lime into wedges.
To serve, ladle soup into bowls. Top with a swirl of coconut milk, crispy shallots, cilantro leaves and a squeeze of lime. Enjoy!

name: Spicy Thai-Inspired Meatball Salad with Kale, Peppers & Fresh Herbs
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; pick mint leaves off the stems. Discard stems and mince the leaves. Divide herbs between two medium bowls.

Add beef and spices to one of the bowls with the herbs (set the other bowl aside for the dressing); use your hands to combine the beef mixture. Using a scant tablespoon, form the mixture into mini meatballs and place on a plate.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom; add meatballs and cook, turning occasionally, until cooked through, about 5 minutes. Remove from heat.
Meanwhile, peel and mince garlic; add to the second bowl with the herbs.
Juice lime into the bowl, then add oil, fish sauce, sugar, soy sauce, and pepper; whisk to combine the dressing.

Fold kale leaves in half lengthwise and slice off the stems; chop or tear leaves into bite-sized pieces and add to the bowl with the dressing. Using your hands, massage kale with the dressing until wilted, 1-2 minutes.

Halve chili pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon. Thinly slice and add to the bowl. (Be careful with chilis; do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Trim, seed, and halve bell pepper crosswise, then slice into thin strips; add to the bowl.
Peel, halve, and slice shallot into thin half-moons; add to the bowl.
Halve and pit avocado; scoop out with a spoon and medium dice the flesh. Add to the bowl and gently toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide salad between plates or bowls; top with meatballs and enjoy!

name: Spicy Tofu Rice Bowl with Broccoli, Mushrooms & Soy-Tahini Dressing
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F and arrange rack in the upper third of the oven.

Cut tofu in half along the long side. Sandwich tofu between clean towels or paper towels and place on a large baking sheet pan. Place a cutting board with something heavy on top and set aside to press out excess water.
Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add water and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Cook rice until liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, place soy sauce, chili-garlic sauce, oil, and maple syrup in a medium bowl. Whisk to combine the marinade.
Medium dice tofu, add to the bowl with the marinade, and gently stir to coat. Set aside to marinate. (Wipe baking sheet dry with paper towels and reserve for later use.)
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Separate broccoli into bite-sized florets and cut stems into smaller pieces. Transfer to the reserved baking sheet.
Quarter mushrooms and add to the baking sheet with the broccoli. Drizzle veggies with oil and season with salt. Toss to combine, then spread out in an even layer on one half of the baking sheet.
Transfer tofu to the other half of the baking sheet, spreading out in a single layer. Drizzle with any marinade left in the bowl. (Reserve bowl for later use.)
Place baking sheet in the oven and roast, stirring halfway through, until veggies are tender and tofu is golden, about 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, trim and cut green onions crosswise into thin pieces. Set aside.
Place tahini, vinegar, maple syrup, soy sauce, and water in the reserved bowl. Whisk to combine the sauce and set aside.
When the veggies and tofu are nearly done, change the oven to broil on high. Broil until veggies and tofu are golden brown, 2-3 minutes.
Remove baking sheet from the oven, add half of the green onions, and toss to combine. (Reserve remaining green onions for serving.)
To serve, divide the rice, tofu, and veggies between plates or bowls. Drizzle with sauce and top with the remaining green onion. Enjoy!

name: Spicy Tomato-Rice Coconut Cream Soup with Zucchini, Beans & Cilantro
ingredients: 16 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
½ (13.5 fl oz) can coconut milk
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and mince garlic and ginger.
Preheat a medium saucepan over medium heat.
While the saucepan heats up, peel and small dice onion.
Once the pan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add garlic, ginger, onion, chili-garlic sauce, and salt; cook, stirring occasionally, until onion begins to soften, 3-4 minutes.
Add broth, tomatoes, and coconut milk to the pan. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce heat to low and simmer, stirring occasionally, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, trim and halve zucchini lengthwise, then slice crosswise into half rounds.
Drain and rinse beans.
Purée the soup with an immersion (hand) blender or regular blender. Return puréed soup to the pan and stir in zucchini, beans, and rice.
Bring soup to a boil over high heat, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer, stirring occasionally, until rice is tender, 15-18 minutes.
Meanwhile, shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves.
To serve, divide soup between bowls and top with cilantro. Enjoy!

name: Spicy Tuna Sushi Stack with Sticky Rice & Avocado
ingredients: 1 (6 oz) can chunk light tuna in water
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add water and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce the heat to low. Cook the rice until the liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove the rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Trim and discard the ends of the cucumber; halve the cucumber lengthwise, then cut in ½-inch cubes. Add to a bowl.
Cut the bell pepper into quarters lengthwise; remove and discard the seeds and white membranes. Small dice the pepper. Add to a bowl with the cucumber.
Season vegetables with soy sauce and sesame oil. Add sesame seeds and stir to combine.
Halve and pit the avocado; cube the flesh into ½-inch cubes while still in the skin. Scoop out the flesh and set aside.
Uncover the rice and fluff with a fork. Add vinegar and salt and stir to combine. Spread out rice on a baking sheet to cool, about 5-10 minutes.
Drain tuna, add to a new bowl, and flake with a fork. Add chili-garlic sauce and mayo and stir to combine.
Using a 1 cup measure, fill up to the ⅓ mark with veggies and avocado, then to the ½ way mark with tuna, and finally the rest of the way with rice.

Once the stack is complete, flip the measuring cup onto a large plate. Tap on the bottom of the cup to loosen the stack. If the rice is sticking, run a knife around the edge before flipping. Serve immediately, 2-stacks per person. Enjoy!

name: Spicy Turkey Meatballs with Mashed Sweet Potatoes & Apple-Carrot Slaw
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F. Coat a baking dish with a thin layer of oil.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and mince garlic and ginger; transfer both to a medium bowl.
Trim and mince green onions; transfer half to the bowl with the garlic (set remaining green onions aside for the slaw).
Add ground turkey, soy sauce, chili-garlic sauce, sugar, salt, and pepper to the bowl. Mix with your hands until well combined.

Using a scant ¼-cup measure, form the turkey mixture into meatballs and place in the baking dish. Place in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and bake until meatballs are cooked through, 15-18 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel and medium dice the sweet potatoes. Transfer to a medium saucepan, cover with hot water (from the tap), and bring to a simmer over medium-high heat.
Once the liquid in the saucepan is simmering, reduce heat to medium, cover, and cook until the potatoes are tender, about 10 minutes.
While the potatoes are cooking, place oil, vinegar, Dijon, salt, and pepper in a clean medium bowl; whisk to combine the dressing.
Trim, peel, and grate carrot; transfer to the bowl with the dressing.
Quarter, core, and coarsely grate apple; add to the bowl.
Add reserved green onions to the bowl and toss to combine the slaw.
When the potatoes are done, remove from heat, and drain in a colander. Return to the pan and add butter, maple syrup, salt, and pepper; mash with a potato masher until smooth.
To serve, divide sweet potato mash, meatballs, and slaw between plates. Enjoy!

name: Spicy Turkey Meatballs with Peanut-Broccoli Slaw & Rice
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add water and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
In a medium bowl, combine the ground turkey, bread crumbs, egg, and spices; mix with your hands until well combined.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce the heat to low. Cook the rice until the liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove the rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.

Coat the bottom of a baking dish with oil. Using a tablespoon measure, form the turkey mixture into rounded meatballs and place in the dish. Place in the oven and bake until golden and cooked through 15-18 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel and mince the garlic; wash, peel, and mince or grate the ginger. Place in another small saucepan.
Add soy sauce, vinegar, oil, chili-garlic sauce, and honey to the saucepan with the ginger and garlic; whisk to combine the sauce for the meatballs.
Bring the sauce to boil over medium-high heat, stirring frequently; reduce heat to low and continue to cook, stirring occasionally, 2 minutes more. Remove from heat.
Peel and mince garlic; add to a medium bowl along with water, peanut butter, vinegar, and soy sauce. Whisk to combine the dressing.
Add broccoli slaw to bowl with dressing and toss to combine.
Remove meatballs from oven, drizzle with sauce, and toss to coat.
To serve, divide rice and peanut slaw between plates. Top rice with meatballs and sauce. Sprinkle with sesame seeds and enjoy!

name: Spicy Turkey Rice Bowl with Butternut Squash, Radish & Lemon Sauce
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a medium saucepan; add water, salt, and pepper.
Trim and peel squash; halve lengthwise, scrape out seeds, and small dice the flesh. Add to the saucepan with the rice (do not stir). Bring to a boil over high heat.
Meanwhile, place vinegar, maple syrup, and spices in a small bowl; whisk to combine the marinade.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Cook rice and squash until liquid is fully absorbed and squash is tender, about 18 minutes. Once done, remove rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
While the rice and squash are cooking, trim off and discard tops and root ends of radishes; thinly slice and add to the bowl with the marinade. Toss to coat and set aside.
Juice lemon into another small bowl; add yogurt and spices. Whisk to combine the lemon sauce and set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add ground turkey and cook, breaking apart with a spoon, until browned and crumbly, 5-6 minutes.
Meanwhile, trim and thinly slice green onions crosswise.
Add water and spices to the skillet with the turkey; continue to cook, stirring often, until sauce is reduced by half, about 1 minute. Remove from heat.
To serve, divide rice and squash between bowls; top with turkey, marinated radishes, and green onion. Drizzle with lemon sauce and enjoy!

name: Spicy Vietnamese Pork Noodle Bowls with Carrot, Cucumber & Radish
instructions: Fill a large pot about halfway with hot water (from the tap); cover and bring to a boil over high heat.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and mince garlic and ginger; transfer to a small bowl.

Quarter chili pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon. Mince and add to the bowl with the garlic and ginger. (Be careful, with chilies, do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Juice lime into the bowl with the garlic and ginger. Add vinegar, fish sauce, soy sauce, and sugar; whisk to combine the dressing.
Once the water in the pot is boiling, remove from heat and add rice noodles. Soak for 10 minutes, or according to package directions, then drain in a colander and rinse under cold water.
Meanwhile, pat pork chops dry with paper towels. Place in a medium bowl and pour ⅓ of the dressing over the chops; turn to coat.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add pork chops and cook until golden brown and cooked through, 3-4 minutes per side. Discard marinade.
Meanwhile, trim and halve cucumber lengthwise, then slice crosswise into half-moons. Transfer to a plate.
Peel and coarsely grate carrot; transfer to the plate with the cucumber.
Trim and thinly slice radishes; add to the plate.
Trim green onions and cut crosswise into ¼-inch pieces; add to the plate.
Thinly slice pork chops against the grain.
To serve, divide noodles, pork, and veggies between bowls. Drizzle with remaining dressing and enjoy!

name: Spicy Vietnamese-Style Pork Meatballs with Broccoli Slaw & Peanuts
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Juice lime into a small bowl. Add soy sauce, fish sauce, chili-garlic sauce, sugar, and cornstarch; whisk to combine the sauce and set aside.
Peel and mince ginger and garlic; place both in a medium bowl.
Pick mint leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl with the ginger and garlic.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl.
Add pork, egg, bread crumbs, fish sauce, and spices to the bowl. Using your hands, mix well to combine.
Using a tablespoon measure, form the pork mixture into rounded meatballs and place on a plate.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom; add meatballs and cook, turning occasionally, until golden brown and cooked through, 6-8 minutes.
Meanwhile, trim and halve cucumber lengthwise, then cut crosswise into thin half-moons. Transfer to a clean plate.
Separate the lettuce into leaves and roughly chop or tear into bite-size pieces; add to the plate with the cucumber.
Roughly chop peanuts.
When the meatballs are done, add sauce to the skillet and turn to coat. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens slightly and coats meatballs, 3-4 minutes. Remove from heat.
To serve, divide cucumbers, lettuce, and broccoli slaw between bowls. Top with saucy meatballs and sprinkle with peanuts. Enjoy!

name: Spicy Vietnamese-Style Steak Salad with Carrots, Radishes & Cashews
ingredients: ¾ lb striploin (New York strip) steak
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Juice lime into a small bowl.
Peel and mince shallot and garlic. Add both to the bowl with the lime juice along with fish sauce, soy sauce, sugar, and crushed red pepper. Whisk to combine the dressing and set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the steak dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with salt and pepper on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add steak and cook until desired doneness, 2-5 minutes per side. Transfer to a clean plate and set aside to rest, about 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel and trim carrots; run the peeler along each carrot to make long, noodle-like strips. Place in a medium bowl.
Trim and thinly slice radishes. Add to the bowl with the carrot.
Chop or tear lettuce leaves into bite-sized pieces; add to the bowl.
Pick cilantro and mint leaves off the stems; discard stems and roughly chop the leaves. Add both to the bowl.
Roughly chop cashews. Add to the bowl, gently toss to combine the salad, and set aside.
Thinly slice steak against the grain.
Divide salad and steak between plates or bowls. Drizzle with dressing and enjoy!

name: Spinach, Artichoke & White Bean Stuffed Peppers
ingredients: ½ (6 oz) jar artichoke hearts, marinated
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)

Cut off the top ½-inch of each pepper; remove seeds, stems, and white membranes. Small dice remaining top portion of the peppers and set aside. Place the whole peppers on a baking sheet pan and rub with oil.
Preheat a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Peel and small dice onion. Peel and mince garlic.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add diced peppers, onion, garlic, and salt to the skillet; cook, stirring frequently, until softened, 3-4 minutes.
Meanwhile, drain and roughly chop artichokes.
Finely grate Parmesan.
Drain and rinse the beans in a colander; set aside to drain further.
Add spinach to the skillet in handfuls, waiting for the spinach to wilt slightly before adding the next handful.
Add artichokes, Parmesan, beans, and yogurt to the skillet. Stir to combine.
Fill peppers with equal portions of the bean mixture.
Grate mozzarella and sprinkle over the peppers. Place in the oven and bake until peppers are tender and cheese is melted, about 15 minutes.
To serve, divide peppers between plates and enjoy!

name: Spinach, Carrot & Rice Noodle Soup with Crispy Tofu
