ingredients: 32 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Cut tofu in half along the long side. Sandwich tofu between clean towels or paper towels and place on a baking sheet pan. Place a cutting board with something heavy on top and set aside to press out excess water.
Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)
Peel and trim carrots, then slice crosswise into thin rounds. Place in a small bowl and set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat.
While the skillet heats up, medium dice tofu. Place in a medium bowl, sprinkle with salt and cornstarch, then gently toss to coat.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add tofu and pan-fry, turning occasionally, until browned and crispy, 5-7 minutes. Return crispy tofu to the bowl.
Meanwhile, preheat a medium saucepan over medium heat.
While the pan heats up, peel and mince ginger and garlic.
Once the pan is hot, add additional oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add ginger and garlic; cook, stirring occasionally, until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add broth to the pan and bring to a boil over medium-high heat.
Once the broth is boiling, add carrots, noodles, and soy sauce; stir to combine the soup. Bring to a simmer over medium heat and continue to cook until noodles are tender, 8-10 minutes more.
Meanwhile, trim green onions and cut crosswise into thin pieces; add to the soup and stir to combine.
Add spinach to the soup in handfuls, waiting for the spinach to wilt slightly before adding the next handful. Stir to combine and remove from heat.
To serve, divide soup between bowls. Top with crispy tofu and enjoy!

name: Spinach, Mushroom & Feta Frittata with Grape Tomatoes
ingredients: ½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled feta cheese
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)
Slice the mushrooms; transfer to a small bowl.
Peel and small dice the onion; transfer to a small bowl.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat.
Preheat the oven to the broil setting.
Add olive oil to the skillet and swirl to coat the bottom. Add the diced onion and cook, stirring frequently, until translucent, 2 to 3 minutes.
Add more olive oil and the mushrooms to the skillet; cook, stirring occasionally, until the mushrooms are tender, 3 to 4 minutes.
While the mushrooms cook, in a large bowl, combine and whisk together the eggs, water, salt, and black pepper.
Add the spinach (a handful at a time) to the skillet and stir until wilted, 1 to 2 minutes.
Pour the egg mixture over top the vegetables and sprinkle with the feta cheese.

While tilting the skillet with one hand, lift up the edges of the frittata with a spatula and let the eggs run underneath during the first few minutes of cooking. Cook until most of the frittata is set, but the top is still runny, 4 to 5 minutes.
Transfer the skillet to the oven and broil until the top is set and lightly browned, 2 to 3 minutes.
Separate the frittata into wedges and divide between two plates (or one plate and one lunch container). Serve with the grape tomatoes on the side. Enjoy!

name: Spinach Salad with Veggie Sausage, Lentils & Lemon-Dijon Dressing
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Using a strainer, rinse lentils under cold water and place in a small saucepan; add broth and bring to a boil over high heat.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Cook lentils until tender, about 15 minutes; drain and rinse with cold water (from the tap) to cool. Set aside.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Zest and juice lemon into a medium bowl; add oil, Dijon, maple syrup, and spices. Whisk to combine the dressing.
Peel, halve, and slice shallot into thin half-moons; add to the bowl with the dressing.
Trim and medium dice cucumber; add to the bowl.
Shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl and set aside.
Preheat a grill pan, outdoor grill, or regular skillet over medium-high heat.
Once the grill pan is hot, coat with oil. Place sausages on the pan and cook, turning occasionally, until warmed through, about 5 minutes (or cook according to package instructions).
When the sausages are done, transfer to a cutting board and slice crosswise into thin rounds.
Add lentils, sausage, and spinach to the bowl with the dressing and veggies; toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide salad between plates or bowls. Enjoy!

name: Spinach, Shrimp & Avocado Salad with Zesty Lemon Vinaigrette
ingredients: ¾ lb raw peeled shrimp, fresh or frozen
instructions: If using frozen shrimp, place in a medium bowl, cover with water, and set aside to defrost. If using fresh shrimp, skip this step.
Wash and dry the fresh produce. Halve the tomatoes. Halve and pit the avocado; thinly slice the flesh crosswise while still in the skin and scoop out with a spoon. Peel and mince the garlic.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Drain the shrimp in a colander and run under cold water to melt any remaining ice chunks. Place on a clean towel (or paper towels) and pat dry.
Add oil to the skillet and swirl to coat bottom. Add the minced garlic and cook until fragrant, 15-30 seconds. Add the shrimp and cook until opaque, 1-2 minutes per side.
In a small bowl, prepare the dressing by whisking together lemon juice, olive oil, honey, salt, and pepper.
To serve, arrange a bed of spinach on a plate, top with the tomatoes, avocado and shrimp, and drizzle with the dressing. Enjoy!

name: Spinach & Tomato Frittata with Fresh Mozzarella
ingredients: ½ (8 oz) pkg fresh mozzarella cheese
instructions: Preheat oven to broil and position rack under the broiler.
Wash and dry spinach and tomato. Slice the tomato into rounds. Peel and mince garlic.
Thinly slice mozzarella.
Heat a skillet over medium heat.
In a medium bowl, whisk together eggs, water, Italian seasoning, salt, and pepper.
Coat bottom of skillet with oil. Add garlic and spinach. Cook until spinach begins to wilt, 1-2 minutes.

Pour in egg mixture. As eggs set around the edge of the skillet, gently lift cooked portions with a spatula to allow uncooked egg to flow underneath. Cook until bottom and sides are firm but the top is still runny, 8-10 minutes.
Add tomato and mozzarella.
Place skillet in the oven and broil until the top is set, 2-3 minutes.
To serve, cut frittata into wedges and place on a plate. Enjoy!

name: Steak with Arugula, Caramelized Onions & Balsamic Mushrooms
instructions: Heat a sauté pan over medium heat.
Peel and thinly slice onion into half rings.
Coat bottom of pan with oil. Add onions and, stirring frequently, cook until softened and starting to brown, about 10 minutes.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Wash and slice mushrooms.
Season steak generously with salt and pepper.
Coat bottom of skillet with oil. Place steak in the skillet and cook until desired doneness, 2-5 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate and loosely cover with foil.
Add mushrooms to pan with onion. Season with salt and pepper. Stirring occasionally, cook until tender, 5-6 minutes.
Wash and dry arugula.
Add vinegar to onion and mushrooms. Scrape up browned bits from the bottom of the pan and stir until liquid thickens, 2-3 minutes.
Thinly slice steak against the grain.
To serve, arrange a bed of arugula on a plate, add onion and mushrooms, and top with steak slices. Enjoy!

name: Steak, Asparagus & Bell Pepper Stir Fry
ingredients: ¾ lb striploin (New York strip) steak
instructions: In a small bowl, make a slurry by whisking water with cornstarch until smooth. Add soy sauce, sesame oil, and red pepper; whisk together. Set aside.

Wash the fresh produce. Snap (or cut) off woody ends from the asparagus, then cut on an angle into 2 inch pieces; transfer to a large bowl. Seed and cut the bell pepper into 2 inch strips; add to the bowl with asparagus. Trim green onion ends and chop on an angle; transfer to a small bowl.
Peel and mince or grate the ginger. Peel and mince the garlic. Transfer both to a small bowl.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Slice the steak into thin strips.
Add oil to the skillet and swirl to coat bottom. Add the steak strips and cook until browned, 1-2 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate.

Once steak has been transferred, add more oil to the skillet. Add the asparagus, bell pepper, ginger, and garlic. Cook, stirring frequently, until vegetables are crisp-tender and lightly browned, 2-3 minutes.
Return beef to the skillet and add green onions and sauce. Cook until sauce is slightly thickened, 1-2 minutes.
To serve, place stir fry in a bowl and enjoy!

name: Steak, Asparagus & Strawberry Salad with Balsamic-Poppy Seed Dressing
ingredients: ¾ lb striploin (New York strip) steak
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the mixed greens if they came pre-washed.)

Snap or cut off woody ends of the asparagus; cut into bite-sized pieces. Transfer to a baking sheet pan, drizzle with oil, and sprinkle with salt and pepper; toss to combine and spread out in an even layer.
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast until asparagus is tender-crisp, 8-10 minutes. Remove from oven and set aside to cool.
Meanwhile, preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat steak dry with paper towels and season with spices on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add steak and cook until desired doneness, 2-5 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate and loosely cover with aluminum foil.
Meanwhile, place oil, vinegar, sugar, poppy seeds, Dijon, and spices in a medium bowl. Whisk to combine the dressing.
Trim and slice strawberries crosswise into ¼-inch thick pieces; add to the bowl with the dressing.
Trim off and discard tops and root ends of radishes; thinly slice and add to the bowl.
Pick basil leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and thinly slice into ribbons; add to the bowl.
Add roasted asparagus and mixed greens to the bowl; toss to combine the salad.
Thinly slice steak against the grain.
To serve, divide salad between plates. Top with steak and enjoy!

name: Steak, Bell Pepper & Apricot Skewers with Creamy Cucumber-Mint Salad
ingredients: ¾ lb striploin (New York strip) steak
instructions: If using wooden skewers, place 4-6 skewers in a shallow dish of water to soak until you are ready to use them.
Place yogurt, oil, and spices in a medium bowl; whisk to combine the marinade.
Cut steak into 1-inch cubes, add to the bowl with the marinade along with the apricots and stir to coat; set aside.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Pick mint leaves off the stems; discard stems and, using a clean cutting board, mince the leaves. Place half in a small bowl (reserving the rest for garnish).
Add yogurt, oil, and salt to the bowl with the mint and whisk to combine the dressing.
Trim, halve, and slice cucumber crosswise into thin half-moons; add to the bowl with the dressing and stir to combine the salad. Set aside.
Peel, halve, and cut onion into 1½-inch wide pieces. Trim, seed, and cut bell pepper into 1½-inch pieces. Add both to the bowl with the steak and apricots; stir to coat.
Preheat a grill pan or regular skillet over medium-high heat.

While the grill pan heats up, thread steak, apricots, onion, and bell pepper onto skewers, alternating ingredients; place on a plate. (If you don't have skewers, you can cook the steak, apricots, and veggies directly on the grill pan.)
Once the grill pan is hot, coat with oil; add the skewers and cook, turning occasionally, until the steak is cooked through and veggies are fork-tender, 8-10 minutes. Remove to a clean plate.
To serve, divide skewers and salad between plates; sprinkle with reserved mint and enjoy!

name: Steak with Black Pepper-Dijon Sauce, Roasted Asparagus & Carrots
ingredients: ¾ lb striploin (New York strip) steak
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the asparagus. Snap or cut off woody ends, then cut into bite-sized pieces. Transfer to a baking sheet pan.
Wash, dry, peel, and slice carrot into thin rounds. Add to the baking sheet with the asparagus.
Peel and mince garlic and shallot; sprinkle both over the veggies. Drizzle with oil, season with salt, and toss to combine.
Place baking sheet in the oven and roast veggies, tossing once, until fork-tender, 12-15 minutes.
Meanwhile, preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the steak dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with salt and pepper on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add steak and cook until desired doneness, 2-5 minutes per side. Remove to a clean plate and loosely cover with foil.

Return skillet to medium-high heat; add cream, Dijon, salt, and pepper. Whisk to combine the sauce and bring to a simmer. Cook until heated through and slightly thickened, 1-2 minutes. Remove from the heat.
Meanwhile, thinly slice steak into strips.
To serve, divide steak and veggies between plates. Top steak with sauce and enjoy!

name: Steak Fajita Cauliflower Rice Bowl with Avocado & Cilantro
ingredients: ¾ lb striploin (New York strip) steak
instructions: Preheat the oven to 450°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Juice half of the lime into a medium bowl. Cut remaining lime into wedges and set aside for serving.
Add oil, soy sauce, and spices to the bowl with the lime juice. Stir to combine the spice paste and set aside.

Pat steak dry with paper towels and place in the center of a baking sheet pan; drizzle with half of the spice paste, turning the steak to coat on both sides (reserve remaining spice paste for the veggies).
Trim, seed, and slice bell peppers lengthwise into thin strips. Add to the bowl with the remaining spice paste.
Peel, halve, and slice onion crosswise into ½-inch thick half-moons. Add to the bowl, then toss veggies in the spice paste to coat.
Add veggies to the baking sheet, arranging them in an even layer around the steak.
Place baking sheet in the oven and roast, stirring veggies and flipping steak halfway through, until veggies are tender and steak is cooked to desired doneness, 13-15 minutes. Remove from oven.

Meanwhile, cut cauliflower head into quarters; using a box grater, hold the stem end of the cauliflower and coarsely grate. (Alternatively, transfer cauliflower to the bowl of a food processor; pulse until rice-like in consistency.)
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add cauliflower and salt; cook, stirring often, until cauliflower is lightly golden and cooked through, 5-7 minutes. Remove from heat.

While the cauliflower rice is cooking, shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and roughly chop the leaves. Add half to the cauliflower rice and stir to combine. (Set remaining cilantro aside for serving.)
Halve and pit avocado; using a spoon, scoop out the flesh and slice crosswise into thin half-moons. Set aside.
Transfer steak to the cutting board and thinly slice against the grain.
Divide cauliflower rice, steak, veggies, and avocado between bowls; sprinkle with reserved cilantro. Serve with lime wedges for squeezing and enjoy!

name: Steak Kabobs with Mediterranean Spice Rub & Cauliflower Tabouli Salad
ingredients: ¾ lb striploin (New York strip) steak
instructions: If using wooden skewers, place 4 skewers in a shallow dish of water to soak until you are ready to use them.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Cut the cauliflower head into quarters, then trim off and discard the leaves and thick stem. Using a box grater or food processor, coarsely grate the cauliflower.
Preheat a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add cauliflower, salt, and pepper; cook, stirring occasionally, until crisp-tender, 4-5 minutes. Transfer cauliflower to a baking sheet pan and spread out in an even layer to cool.
Meanwhile, combine spices in a medium bowl; stir to combine.
Cut the steak into 1½-inch cubes; transfer to the bowl with the spices and toss to coat; set aside.
Heat a grill pan, outdoor grill, or skillet over medium-high heat.
Thread steak onto the skewers and place on a plate. Alternatively, you can cook the steak pieces directly on the grill/skillet without using skewers.
Coat the grill or skillet with oil; place kabobs on the grill, rotating every 2½ minutes, until browned and cooked through, about 10 minutes. Transfer to a plate and loosely cover with foil.
Meanwhile, grate the zest from the lemon and transfer to a medium bowl, then juice the lemon into the same bowl. Add the cauliflower and stir to combine.
Peel and mince garlic. Trim off and discard the ends of the green onions; cut the onions crosswise into ¼-inch pieces. Transfer both to the bowl with the cauliflower.
Peel and small dice the cucumber. Small dice the tomatoes; add both to the bowl with the cauliflower.

Shave parsley leaves off the stems; pick mint leaves off the stems. Discard the stems and mince the leaves. Add herbs, oil, salt, and pepper to the bowl with the cauliflower and stir to combine the tabouli salad.
To serve, divide tabouli between plates or bowls. Place steak kabobs on top and enjoy!

name: Steak & Kale Caesar Salad with Creamy Parmesan Dressing
ingredients: ¾ lb striploin (New York strip) steak
instructions: Wash and dry the kale leaves and lemon.
One kale leaf at a time, cut along the sides of the tough center ribs, then pull out and discard the ribs. When all the leaves are trimmed, chop them into 1-inch pieces and transfer to a large bowl.
Cut the lemon in half; juice one half into a small bowl (that is big enough for making the dressing) and cut the other half into wedges for serving.
Finely grate ¼ cup of Parmesan.
Trim off and discard the root end of the garlic; peel and mince or press the garlic.
Add ½ of the grated Parmesan (save the rest for garnishing), the minced garlic, yogurt, Dijon, Worcestershire, salt, and pepper to the bowl with the lemon juice; whisk together until smooth.
Pour the dressing over the kale and toss to combine. If the kale is tough, massage it with your hands to soften it.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat.
While the skillet heats up, cut the bun or roll into ¾-inch cubes.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom.

Add the bread cubes to the skillet; sprinkle with salt and toss to coat in the oil, then arrange in a single layer. Toast the bread, tossing occasionally, until the bread cubes are golden brown, 4 to 5 minutes. Once done, transfer the croutons to a bowl and return the skillet to the stove.
Wipe out the skillet with a paper towel and heat over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat dry the steak with paper towels and season it generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom.

Carefully place the steak in the skillet; flipping every 15 to 30 seconds, cook the steak for 4 to 6 minutes for medium-rare, or until desired doneness. (Use a thermometer or cut into the steak to check the doneness.) Once done, transfer the steak to a plate and let it rest for 5 to 10 minutes.
Slice the steak against the grain into thin strips.
To serve, arrange a bed of the kale on a plate and top with the croutons, remaining Parmesan, and steak slices. Garnish with lemon wedges for squeezing over the top.

name: Steak with Mashed Turnip, Potato & Carrot Medley
ingredients: 4 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Fill a medium saucepan halfway with water, cover, and bring to a boil.
Wash turnip, potatoes, and carrots. Peel, large dice, and add to saucepan. Once boiling, cook until vegetables are tender, 10-12 minutes.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Wash and dry basil. Pick leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and thinly slice into ribbons.

Coat bottom of skillet with oil. Season steak with salt and pepper on both sides. Place in the skillet and cook until desired doneness, 2-5 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate and loosely cover with foil.
Drain vegetables and return back to saucepan. Add broth, oil, ½ of the basil (save the rest for garnishing), salt, and pepper. Mash until smooth.
Thinly slice steak against the grain.
To serve, place mash on a plate, add steak slices, and sprinkle with remaining basil. Enjoy!

name: Steak & Mushroom Stir Fry with Cauliflower Rice
ingredients: ¾ lb striploin (New York strip) steak
instructions: Peel and mince or grate ginger. In a medium bowl, prepare marinade by whisking together the minced ginger, water, soy sauce, vinegar, cornstarch, and pepper.
Thinly slice steak and place in marinade; toss to coat and set aside.
Wash and remove leaves from cauliflower. Using a food processor or grater, grate to rice-like texture.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat.

Add oil to skillet and swirl to coat bottom. Add cauliflower and cook, stirring frequently, until warmed through and slightly tender, 5-6 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Transfer to a bowl and cover with foil to keep warm.
Wash mushrooms and green onions. Thinly slice mushrooms. Trim ends and thinly slice onions on the diagonal. Peel and mince garlic.

Once cauliflower rice has been transferred, add more oil to skillet. Remove steak slices from marinade, reserving the marinade in the bowl, and add to skillet. Cook until browned, 1-2 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate.
Add garlic, mushrooms, ½ of the green onions (save the rest for garnishing), and reserved marinade to skillet. Cook, stirring frequently, until mushrooms are tender and sauce has thickened.
Wash and dry spinach.
Return steak and add spinach to skillet. Stir until spinach is wilted and ingredients are well combined.
Serve stir fry over cauliflower rice and garnish with remaining green onions. Enjoy!

name: Steak, Roasted Carrots & Red Onion with Chimichurri Sauce
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Peel and cut onion into 8 wedges. Transfer to a sheet pan. Wash and peel carrots. Slice into thirds crosswise, then halve or quarter lengthwise. Add to sheet.
Drizzle with oil and season with salt and pepper; toss to coat.
Arrange in a single layer and place in the oven. Roast, tossing once halfway through, until carrots are tender, 15-20 minutes.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Wash and dry parsley. Shave leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves. Peel and mince garlic.
Coat bottom of skillet with oil. Season steak with salt and pepper. Add to skillet and cook until desired doneness, 2-5 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate and loosely cover with foil.
In a small bowl, prepare sauce by whisking together parsley, garlic, oil, vinegar, salt, and pepper.
To serve, place steak, carrots, and onion on a plate and drizzle with chimichurri sauce. Enjoy!

name: Steak with Roasted New Potatoes & Sugar Snap Peas
ingredients: ½ (8 oz) pkg sugar snap peas
instructions: Preheat the oven to 450°F and place the rack in the centre position.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Quarter the potatoes and transfer to a baking sheet.
Drizzle the potatoes with olive oil and season with salt and pepper; toss to coat then spread out in a single layer.
Place the potatoes in the oven and roast, tossing halfway through cooking time, until they are tender and browned, 20 to 25 minutes.
Halve the snap peas and transfer to a bowl. Add to the baking sheet with the potatoes halfway through cooking time.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the steak dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add coconut oil and swirl to coat the bottom.

Carefully place the steak in the skillet; flipping every 15 to 30 seconds, cook the steak until desired doneness (5 to 7 minutes for medium-rare). (Use a thermometer or cut into the steak to check the doneness.) Once done, transfer the steak to a plate and let it rest for 5 to 10 minutes.
To serve, divide the steak and roasted vegetables between plates. Enjoy!

name: Steak Salad with Celery, Tomatoes, Blue Cheese & Garlic-Chive Crostini
ingredients: ½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled blue cheese
¾ lb striploin (New York strip) steak
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the mixed greens if they came pre-washed.)
Peel and mince garlic. Trim and chop chives into small pieces.
Place half of the garlic and half of the chives in a small bowl (reserving the rest for the next step); add oil, salt, and crushed red pepper. Stir to combine the garlic-chive oil and set aside.
Juice lemon into a medium bowl. Add remaining garlic and chives, oil, Dijon, honey, salt, and pepper to the bowl; whisk to combine the dressing and set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the steak dry with paper towels and place on a plate. Season with salt and pepper on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add steak to the skillet and cook until desired doneness, 2-5 minutes per side. Transfer to a clean plate and let rest, about 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, preheat oven to broil on high; position the rack in the upper third of the oven.
Halve tomatoes. Trim and thinly slice celery crosswise; add both to the bowl with the dressing.
Add mixed greens and blue cheese to the bowl and toss to combine the salad. Set aside.

Slice roll in half and place on a baking sheet pan, cut-side up; drizzle with the garlic-chive oil. Place in the oven and toast until golden, 1-2 minutes. Remove from the oven and cut each round in half.
Thinly slice steak against the grain.
To serve, divide salad, steak, and crostini between plates or bowls. Enjoy!

name: Steak Salad with Walnuts, Goat Cheese & Blueberry-Basil Dressing
ingredients: ¾ lb striploin (New York strip) steak
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the mixed greens if they came pre-washed.)
Preheat a grill pan, outdoor grill, or regular skillet over medium-high heat.
While the pan heats up, pat the steak dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with salt and pepper on both sides.
Once the pan is hot, coat with oil. Add steak and cook until desired doneness, 2-5 minutes per side. Transfer steak to a clean plate, loosely cover with aluminum foil, and set aside to rest.
Meanwhile, pick basil off the stems and place in a blender.
Add half of the blueberries (reserve remaining blueberries for the salad), vinegar, water, oil, Dijon, honey, salt, and pepper to the blender. Blend on high until smooth, then set dressing aside.
Trim and quarter cucumber lengthwise, then cut crosswise into thin pieces; place in a medium bowl.
Roughly chop walnuts and add to the bowl with the cucumber.
Add mixed greens and remaining blueberries to the bowl. Toss to combine the salad.
Thinly slice steak against the grain.
To serve, divide salad and steak between plates or bowls. Crumble goat cheese over top and drizzle with dressing. Enjoy!

name: Steak with Spicy West African Tomato Salsa, Peanuts & Cauliflower Rice
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.

Cut cauliflower head into quarters; using a box grater, hold the stem end of the cauliflower and coarsely grate. (Alternatively, transfer cauliflower to the bowl of a food processor; pulse until rice-like in consistency.) Place in a medium bowl.
Add oil, salt, and pepper to the bowl with the cauliflower, then stir to combine. Transfer cauliflower rice to a baking sheet pan and spread out in an even layer. (Reserve bowl for later use.)
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast, stirring cauliflower halfway through, until the rice is golden and tender, about 15 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the steak dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with salt and pepper on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add steak and cook until desired doneness, 2-5 minutes per side. Transfer to a clean plate and set aside to rest, 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel and mince shallot and garlic. Place both in the reserved bowl.
Juice lime into the bowl with the shallot, then add oil, Dijon, salt, and pepper. Whisk to combine the dressing.
Small dice tomato. Add to the bowl with the dressing.
Trim, seed, and small dice bell pepper. Add to the bowl.

Quarter jalapeño pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon to reduce spice level, then mince. Add to the bowl, stir to combine the salsa, and set aside. (Be careful with jalapeños; do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Thinly slice steak against the grain.
To serve, divide steak and cauliflower rice between plates. Top steak with salsa and peanuts. Enjoy!

name: Steak & Spinach Salad with Sauteed Mushrooms, Grape Tomatoes & Corn
instructions: Heat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Wash, dry, and quarter mushrooms. Peel and mince garlic.
Coat bottom of skillet with oil. Season steak generously with salt and pepper. Place in skillet and cook until desired doneness, 2-5 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate and loosely cover with foil.

Return skillet to stove and reduce heat to medium. Add more oil, garlic, and mushrooms. Season with salt and pepper. Stirring occasionally, cook until mushrooms are golden, 3-4 minutes. Remove from heat and set aside to cool.
In a small bowl, prepare dressing by whisking together oil, vinegar, Dijon, honey, salt, and pepper.
Remove husks and silks from corn. Hold vertically in the middle of a medium bowl and slice kernels off the cob.
Wash and dry spinach and tomatoes. Halve the tomatoes. Add both to bowl with corn.
Add mushrooms and toss salad.
Slice steak against the grain.
To serve, arrange salad on a plate, top with steak slices, and drizzle with dressing. Enjoy!

name: Sticky Asian Cauliflower Bites with Carrot & Snap Pea Slaw
ingredients: 4 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F. Line a baking sheet pan with aluminum foil and coat with a thin layer of oil.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Remove leaves and thick stems from the cauliflower; separate the head into bite-sized florets.
Whisk eggs, salt, and pepper in a medium bowl. Add ⅓ of the cauliflower florets to the bowl and toss to dredge.

Transfer florets, shaking off excess egg, to another medium bowl; add ⅓ of the bread crumbs and toss to coat, pressing gently to adhere. Transfer to the baking sheet and repeat twice more with remaining cauliflower.
Place cauliflower in the oven and cook until golden and fork-tender, about 25 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel and mince garlic; transfer to a medium bowl along with oil, vinegar, maple syrup, soy sauce, and chili-garlic sauce. Whisk to combine the dressing.
Quarter cabbage lengthwise, then cut out and discard the core; thinly slice crosswise and add to the bowl with the dressing.
Peel, trim, and coarsely grate carrot; halve snap peas. Add both to the bowl, toss to combine the salad, and set aside.
Peel and mince ginger and additional garlic.
Preheat a small saucepan over medium heat.
Once the saucepan is hot, add oil, ginger, and garlic to the saucepan; cook, stirring often, until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add broth, soy sauce, maple syrup, vinegar, and chili-garlic sauce to the saucepan; whisk to combine the sauce and bring to a simmer over medium-high heat.

Meanwhile, in a small bowl, make a slurry by whisking water with cornstarch until smooth. Add to the saucepan in a steady stream, while whisking constantly; continue to simmer, until thick, about 2 minutes. Remove from heat.
To serve, divide salad and roasted cauliflower between plates. Top cauliflower bites with sauce and enjoy!

name: Sticky Lemon-Pepper Wings with Creamy Kale & Brussels Sprout Salad
ingredients: 1 lb chicken wings, split with tips removed
instructions: Preheat oven to 500°F. Coat a baking sheet pan with a thin layer of oil.
Pat chicken wings dry with paper towels and place in a medium bowl. Sprinkle with cornstarch, salt, and pepper, then toss to coat. Transfer to the baking sheet and spread out in an even layer.
Place wings in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and bake, turning once, until cooked through, 20-25 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Zest lemon into a clean medium bowl. Juice lemon into another medium bowl and set aside for the wing sauce.
Add mayo, oil, Dijon, salt and pepper to the bowl with the lemon zest; whisk to combine the dressing.
Fold kale leaves in half lengthwise and slice off the stems; cut leaves crosswise into thin (shred-like) pieces. Add to the bowl with the dressing.
Trim and thinly slice Brussels sprouts. Add to the bowl.
Using your hands, massage the greens with dressing until wilted, 1-2 minutes. Set aside.
Add honey, pepper, and salt to the bowl with the lemon juice, then whisk to combine the sauce.
When the wings are done, remove from the oven. Add to the bowl with the sauce and toss to coat.
To serve, divide wings and salad between plates. Enjoy!

name: Stir-Fried Pork, Pineapple & Bell Pepper with Basmati Rice
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Season the rice with salt and add water; bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
In a medium bowl, whisk together soy sauce, vinegar, honey, and cornstarch.
Thinly slice pork into strips. Add to bowl with sauce and toss to coat.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce the heat to low. Cook the rice until the liquid is fully absorbed, 15 to 18 minutes. Once done, remove the rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Peel and mince garlic. Peel and mince or grate ginger. Peel and medium dice onion.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Wash bell pepper and pineapple. Seed and large dice the pepper. Cut off skin from pineapple, core, and cut into bite-sized pieces.
Coat bottom of skillet with oil. Add pork, reserving sauce in bowl, and stir fry until no longer pink, 2-3 minutes. Transfer to a plate.
Coat skillet with more oil. Add garlic, ginger, onion, and pepper. Stir fry until pepper is tender-crisp, 2-3 minutes.
Wash and dry cilantro. Shave leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves.
Add pork, pineapple, and sauce to skillet. Toss to coat and stir fry for 1-2 minutes.
Remove from heat and stir in cilantro.
Uncover the rice and fluff with a fork.
Place rice on a plate, top with stir fry, and enjoy!

name: Strawberry, Bacon & Spinach Salad with Feta & Poppy Seed Dressing
ingredients: ½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled feta cheese
instructions: Heat a skillet over medium heat.
Add the bacon to the skillet and cook until crispy, 3-5 minutes per side.
Wash and dry the spinach. Wash the strawberries, trim the tops, and thinly slice.
In a small bowl, prepare the dressing by whisking together mayo, vinegar, honey, poppy seeds, salt, and pepper.
Measure out the almonds.
Once the bacon is cooked, crumble or chop into small pieces.
Arrange a bed of spinach on a plate, top with the strawberries, bacon, feta, and almonds, and drizzle with the dressing. Enjoy!

name: Strawberry & Black Bean Quinoa Bowl with Feta
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled feta cheese
instructions: In a small saucepan, combine the quinoa and broth; bring to a boil over high heat.
Drain and rinse the black beans in a colander; set aside to drain further.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce the heat to low. Cook the quinoa for 15 minutes. Once done, remove the quinoa from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Juice the lime into a medium bowl (that will be used to mix the strawberries and jalapeño pepper).
To the lime juice, add olive oil, honey, salt, and pepper; whisk together.
Trim off and discard the stem ends of the strawberries; medium dice the strawberries and add to the bowl with the dressing.
Quarter the jalapeño pepper lengthwise; remove and discard the stem, seeds, and membranes. Finely dice the pepper and add to the strawberries; toss with the dressing.
Uncover the quinoa and fluff with a fork.
To serve, arrange the quinoa, black beans, strawberry- jalapeño mixture, and feta in a bowl. Enjoy!

name: Strawberry Panzanella (Italian Bread Salad) with Chicken, Feta & Mint
ingredients: ¾ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled feta cheese
instructions: Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, holding a knife parallel to the cutting board, cut the chicken in half horizontally to form thin fillets. Season with spices on both sides.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add chicken and pan-fry until golden brown and cooked through, 3-4 minutes per side. Remove to a plate. (Reserve skillet with drippings for later use.)
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Using a clean cutting board, peel and mince shallot. Place in a medium bowl along with oil, vinegar, Dijon, honey, salt, and pepper. Whisk to combine the dressing.
Trim and quarter strawberries. Add to the bowl with the dressing.
Halve grape tomatoes. Add to the bowl.
Trim and quarter cucumber lengthwise, then cut crosswise into bite-sized pieces. Add to the bowl.
Pick mint leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add half to the bowl and set aside. (Reserve remaining mint for serving.)
Cut or tear bread into bite-sized pieces.

Return skillet (with drippings) to low heat, add more oil, and swirl to coat the bottom. Add bread and cook, stirring occasionally, until croutons are golden and toasted, 4-5 minutes. Remove from heat.
Add croutons to the bowl and stir to combine the salad.
Slice chicken into thin strips.
To serve, divide panzanella salad between plates; top with chicken, feta, and reserved mint. Enjoy!

name: Strawberry-Peach Quinoa Salad with Cucumber, Goat Cheese & Pistachio
instructions: In a small saucepan, combine quinoa, water, and salt; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to a simmer, cover, and cook for 15 minutes. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Zest and juice lemon into a medium bowl.
Peel and mince shallot. Add to the bowl with the lemon along with oil, salt, and pepper. Whisk to combine the dressing.
Trim and slice strawberries lengthwise into ¼-inch thick pieces. Add to the bowl with the dressing.
Trim and medium dice cucumber. Add to the bowl.
Quarter peach lengthwise (around the pit); twist quarters to separate, then remove and discard pit. Medium dice the flesh and add to the bowl.
Pick mint leaves off the stems; discard stems and roughly chop the leaves. Add to the bowl.
Roughly chop pistachios and add to the bowl.
Crumble goat cheese into the bowl and set aside.
When the quinoa is done, transfer to a baking sheet pan. Spread out in an even layer and let cool for 5 minutes. Once cool, add to the bowl and stir to combine the salad.
To serve, divide the salad between plates or bowls. Enjoy!

name: Strawberry, Spinach & Quinoa Salad with Balsamic Vinaigrette
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: In a small saucepan, combine quinoa and broth. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15 minutes. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Wash and dry spinach and basil. Thinly slice the leaves into ribbons and transfer to a large bowl.
Wash, trim and discard stem ends, and slice strawberries. Add to bowl with spinach and basil.
In a small bowl, prepare dressing by whisking together oil, vinegar, Dijon, honey, salt, and pepper.
Heat a skillet over medium heat.
Coat bottom of skillet with oil. Add almonds and, stirring constantly, cook until golden brown, 1-2 minutes.
Uncover quinoa and fluff with a fork. Drain any excess liquid and add to bowl with other ingredients. Toss salad.
To serve, arrange salad on a plate, crumble goat cheese over top, sprinkle with almonds, and drizzle with dressing. Enjoy!

name: Strip Steak & Bell Pepper Fajitas with Guacamole & Butter Lettuce
ingredients: ¾ lb striploin (New York strip) steak
instructions: Wash and dry bell peppers. Seed, slice into thin strips, and transfer to a bowl.
Peel, thinly slice into half rings, and add onion to bowl with peppers. Peel and mince garlic; add ½ to bowl with vegetables and place the other ½ into a medium bowl for preparing guacamole.
Halve avocado and remove pit; scoop out the flesh into bowl with garlic.
Wash and dry cilantro. Shave leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves. Add ½ to bowl with avocado and save the rest for garnishing.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Season steak generously with salt and pepper.
Coat bottom of skillet with oil. Add steak and cook until desired doneness, 2-5 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate and loosely cover with foil.
Add lime juice, salt, and pepper to avocado. Mash with a fork until smooth. Set aside.
After steak has been transferred add more oil to skillet. Add peppers, onion, and garlic from bowl. Stirring frequently, cook until peppers are tender-crisp, 4-5 minutes.
Wash and dry lettuce.
Cut remaining ½ lime into wedges.
Thinly slice steak against the grain.
Return steak slices and any juices to skillet. Season with chili powder, cumin, salt, and pepper. Stir and cook for 1-2 minutes.
To serve, fill lettuce leaves with fajita mix. Garnish with guacamole, remaining cilantro, and lime wedges. Enjoy!

name: Strip Steak & Bell Pepper Fajitas with Guacamole
ingredients: ¾ lb striploin (New York strip) steak
instructions: Wash and dry bell peppers. Seed and slice into thin strips. Peel and thinly slice onion into half rings. Peel and mince garlic.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Season steak generously with salt and pepper.
Coat bottom of skillet with oil. Add steak and cook until desired doneness, 2-5 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate and loosely cover with foil.

Once the steak has been transferred, reduce the heat to medium and add sliced onion, peppers, and ½ of the garlic (save the rest for the guacamole) to the skillet. Stirring frequently, cook until vegetables are tender-crisp, 4-5 minutes.
Wash and dry cilantro and lime. Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves.

Halve and pit avocado; medium dice the flesh while still in skin and scoop out into a medium bowl. Add ½ of the cilantro (save the rest for garnishing), remaining garlic, lime juice, salt, and pepper. Mash with a fork until smooth.
Thinly slice steak against the grain.
Add steak slices and any juices to skillet. Season with chili powder, cumin, salt, and pepper. Stir and cook for 1-2 minutes.
In another skillet or pan, warm tortillas for 20-30 seconds per side if desired.
Cut remaining lime into wedges.
To serve, place tortillas on a plate and fill with fajita filling. Garnish with guacamole, remaining cilantro, and lime wedges. Enjoy!

name: Strip Steak & Brussels Sprouts Stir Fry with Jalapeño Pepper
ingredients: ¾ lb striploin (New York strip) steak
instructions: Wash brussels sprouts, carrot, jalapeño, and green onions.
Trim, peel, and slice carrot on the diagonal into ¼ inch rounds. Transfer to a bowl.
Halve, seed, and thinly slice jalapeño crosswise. Peel and mince garlic. Peel and mince or grate ginger. Transfer all to a small bowl.
Trim green onion root ends and slice on the diagonal. Add whites to bowl with jalapeño, garlic, and ginger; transfer the greens to a separate bowl and save for garnishing.
Trim rough ends of brussels sprouts and halve lengthwise. Transfer to a separate bowl.
In a small bowl, prepare sauce by whisking together soy sauce, vinegar, water, and cornstarch.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Thinly slice steak into strips.
Coat bottom of skillet with oil. Add steak strips in a single layer and cook until browned, 2-3 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate.
Add more oil to skillet, followed by brussels sprouts. Cook, stirring occasionally, until golden brown, 2-3 minutes. Transfer to plate with steak.

Add more oil to skillet, followed by green onion whites, jalapeño, garlic, and ginger. Stir and cook until fragrant, 15-30 seconds. Add carrot and cook, stirring occasionally, until tender, 2-3 minutes.
Return steak and sprouts to skillet and add sauce. Cook, stirring occasionally, until sauce is thickened, 2-3 minutes.
To serve, place stir fry on a plate and garnish with remaining green onions. Enjoy!

name: Strip Steak with Fried Egg, Bell Pepper-Onion Medley & Jalapeño Aioli
ingredients: ¾ lb striploin (New York strip) steak
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim, seed, and medium dice bell peppers. Transfer to a baking sheet pan.
Peel, halve, and medium dice onion; add to the baking sheet with the bell pepper. Drizzle veggies with oil, season with salt and pepper, then toss to combine and spread out in an even layer.
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast, stirring veggies halfway through, until fork-tender, about 15 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the steak dry with paper towels and place on a plate. Season with salt and pepper on both sides.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add steak and cook until desired doneness, 2-5 minutes per side. Transfer steak to a clean plate, loosely cover with aluminum foil, and set aside to rest. (Reserve skillet for later use.)

Meanwhile, quarter jalapeño pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon. Mince and place in a small bowl. (Be careful with jalapeños; do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Add mayo, garlic powder, and salt to the bowl with the jalapeño. Stir to combine the aioli and set aside.
When the steak is done, wipe the reserved skillet clean with paper towels, then return to medium heat.

Once the skillet is hot, add additional oil, and swirl to coat the bottom. Gently crack eggs into the skillet and cook until the tops of the whites are set but yolks are still runny, about 4 minutes. Remove from heat and season with salt.
Thinly slice steak against the grain.
To serve, divide, steak, veggies, fried eggs, and aioli between plates. Enjoy!

name: Strip Steak with Roasted Hot Honey Butternut Squash & Arugula Salad
ingredients: ¾ lb striploin (New York strip) steak
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the arugula if it came pre-washed.)

Trim and peel squash; halve lengthwise, scrape out the seeds, and medium dice the flesh. Transfer to a baking sheet pan, drizzle with oil, and season with salt. Toss to coat and spread out in an even layer.
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast, stirring halfway through, until squash is golden and fork-tender, about 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the steak dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with salt on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add steak and cook until desired doneness, 2-5 minutes per side. Transfer to a clean plate and set aside to rest, about 5 minutes.
When the squash is done, remove from the oven, then drizzle with honey and hot sauce. Stir to coat and set aside to cool slightly, about 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, zest and juice lemon into a medium bowl.
Peel and mince shallot. Add to the bowl with the lemon along with oil, salt, and pepper. Whisk to combine the dressing.
Add arugula and cooled squash to the bowl with the dressing, then toss to combine the salad.
Thinly slice steak against the grain.
To serve, divide steak and salad between plates or bowls. Enjoy!

name: Striploin Steak with Balsamic Bell Peppers
ingredients: ¾ lb striploin (New York strip) steak
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Quarter the bell peppers lengthwise; remove and discard the stem, seeds, and membranes. Cut the quarters lengthwise into ¼-inch-thick strips. Transfer to a medium bowl.
Trim off and discard the ends of the onion and remove the outer layer; cut lengthwise into ¼-inch-thick wedges. Add to the bowl with the bell peppers.
Trim off and discard the root end of the garlic; peel and mince or press the garlic. Add to the bowl with the peppers and onion.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the steak dry with paper towels and place on a plate. Season with salt and pepper on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add coconut oil and swirl to coat the bottom.

Carefully place the steak in the skillet; flipping every 15 to 30 seconds, cook the steak until desired doneness (5 to 7 minutes for medium-rare). (Use a thermometer or cut into the steak to check the doneness.) Once done, transfer the steak to a plate and let it rest for 5 to 10 minutes.
Once the steak has been transferred, reduce the heat to medium and add more coconut oil to the skillet.

Add the peppers, onion, and garlic to the skillet and season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the peppers are just tender and lightly browned, 3 to 5 minutes. Once done, remove from the heat.
Drizzle the peppers with balsamic vinegar and toss to coat.
To serve, divide the steak and bell peppers between plates.

name: Striploin Steak with Bell Pepper, Tomato & Basil Panzanella Salad
ingredients: ¾ lb striploin (New York strip) steak
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim off and discard the root end of the garlic; peel and mince or press the garlic. Transfer to a large salad bowl.
To the garlic, add olive oil, red wine vinegar, Dijon, salt, and pepper; whisk together and set aside.
Quarter the bell peppers lengthwise; remove and discard the stems, seeds, and membranes. Large dice the peppers (cut into ¾-inch cubes) and transfer to a medium bowl.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat.
Cut the bun into 1-inch cubes.
Once the skillet is hot, add olive oil and the bread cubes. Cook, tossing occasionally, until the bread is crisp and lightly browned, 4 to 6 minutes. Once done, transfer to a bowl.
Pat the steak dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
Once the bread cubes have been transferred, increase the heat to medium-high. Once heated, add coconut oil and swirl to coat the bottom.

Carefully place the steak in the skillet; flipping every 15 to 30 seconds, cook the steak until desired doneness (5 to 7 minutes for medium-rare). (Use a thermometer or cut into the steak to check the doneness.) Once done, transfer the steak to a plate and let it rest for 5 to 10 minutes.
Once the steak has been transferred, add the bell peppers to the skillet. Cook, tossing occasionally, until just tender, 3 to 4 minutes. Once done, return to the bowl.
Halve the grape tomatoes crosswise and add to the salad bowl.

Pick the basil leaves off the stems; discard the stems and slice the leaves into a chiffonade by stacking them and rolling tightly into a cigar, then slicing crosswise into thin ribbons. Add to the salad bowl.
Add the bell peppers and bread to the salad bowl; toss to combine.
Slice the steak against the grain into thin strips.
To serve, divide the steak strips and salad between plates. Enjoy!

name: Striploin Steak with Mashed Potatoes & Garlicky Spinach Sauté
ingredients: ¾ lb striploin (New York strip) steak
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)
Peel and quarter the potatoes lengthwise (into wedges); transfer to a small saucepan. Cover with hot water (from the tap) by about 1 inch and bring to a boil over high heat.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the steak dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add coconut oil and swirl to coat the bottom.

Carefully place the steak in the skillet; flipping every 15 to 30 seconds, cook the steak until desired doneness (5 to 7 minutes for medium-rare). (Use a thermometer or cut into the steak to check the doneness.) Once done, transfer the steak to a plate, leaving any juices in the skillet, and let it rest for 5 to 10 minutes.

Once the water in the saucepan is boiling, reduce the heat to medium and cook until the potatoes are tender when pierced with a knife, 8 to 12 minutes. Once done, reserve about ½ cup of liquid and drain the rest. Cover the saucepan to keep warm.
Trim off and discard the root ends of the garlic; peel and mince or press the garlic.

Once the steak has been transferred, reduce the heat to medium and add the garlic and spinach to the skillet; season with salt and pepper. Stir until the spinach is just wilted, 1 to 2 minutes, then remove from the heat.
Add ½ of the reserved liquid, butter, salt, and pepper to the potatoes; mash with a potato masher until smooth. Add more liquid to thin out the mash if needed.
To serve, divide the mashed potatoes between plates and top with the spinach sauté, then add the steak on the side. Enjoy!

name: Striploin Steak with Roasted Carrot, Beet & Feta Salad
ingredients: ½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled feta cheese
¾ lb striploin (New York strip) steak
instructions: Preheat the oven to 500°F. Place the rack in the center position.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel the carrots, then trim off the ends; discard the peels and trimmings. Cut the carrots into ¼-inch-thick rounds (at an angle). Transfer the carrots to a baking sheet.

Trim off and discard the ends of the beets; peel and cut the beets into ¼-inch thick wedges. (To avoid staining, line your cutting board with paper towels before handling the beets.) Transfer the beets to the baking sheet.

One by one, holding a sprig of thyme at its top, run you fingers down it to remove the leaves. Discard the sprigs and chop the leaves. Sprinkle ¾ of the leaves over the carrots and beets (save the rest for garnishing).
Drizzle the carrots and beets with olive oil and season with salt and pepper; toss to coat, then arrange in a single layer.
Place the baking sheet in the oven and roast until the carrots and beets are tender, 15 to 20 minutes.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the steak dry with paper towels and place on a plate. Season generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add coconut oil and swirl to coat the bottom.

Carefully place the steak in the skillet; flipping every 15 to 30 seconds, cook the steak until desired doneness (5 to 7 minutes for medium-rare). (Use a thermometer or cut into the steak to check the doneness.) Once done, transfer the steak to a plate and let it rest for 5 to 10 minutes.
Measure out the feta.
To serve, place the steak on a plate, arrange the roasted vegetables on the side and sprinkle with the feta and remaining thyme. Enjoy!

name: Striploin Steak with Warm Potato, Corn & Snap Pea Salad
ingredients: ¾ lb striploin (New York strip) steak
½ (8 oz) pkg sugar snap peas
instructions: Preheat the oven to 450°F. Place the rack in the center position.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Medium dice the potatoes (cut into ½-inch cubes) and transfer to a baking sheet.
Add the corn to the potatoes.
Drizzle the potatoes and corn with olive oil and season with salt and pepper; toss to coat, then arrange in a single layer.
Place the sheet in the oven and roast, tossing halfway through cooking time, until the potatoes are tender when pierced with a fork, 20 to 25 minutes.
Trim off and discard the root end of the garlic; peel and mince or press the garlic. Transfer to a medium bowl (that is big enough to hold the potato salad).
Add mayonnaise, paprika, salt, and pepper to the bowl with the garlic and mix together.
Cut the sugar snap peas crosswise (at an angle) into ¼-inch pieces and add to the salad bowl.
Trim off and discard the ends of the green onions; cut the onions crosswise (at an angle) into ¼-inch pieces and add to the salad bowl.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the steak dry with paper towels and place on a plate. Season with salt and pepper on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add coconut oil and swirl to coat the bottom.

Carefully place the steak in the skillet; flipping every 15 to 30 seconds, cook the steak until desired doneness (5 to 7 minutes for medium-rare). (Use a thermometer or cut into the steak to check the doneness.) Once done, transfer the steak to a plate and let it rest for 5 to 10 minutes.
Once the potatoes are tender, remove them from the oven and transfer to the salad bowl. Gently mix the ingredients together.
Slice the steak against the grain into strips.
To serve, divide the salad and steak slices between plates. Enjoy!

name: Striploin Steak with Warm Potato, Snap Pea & Dill Salad
ingredients: ¾ lb striploin (New York strip) steak
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.

Quarter potatoes, transfer to a baking sheet pan, and drizzle with oil. Season with salt and pepper, toss to combine, and spread out in an even layer. Place in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast until starting to soften, about 15 minutes.

Meanwhile, using a knife, shave dill leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Place in a medium bowl, then add mayo, vinegar, Dijon, and spices; whisk to combine the dressing and set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the steak dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with salt and pepper on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add steak and cook until desired doneness, 2-5 minutes per side. Transfer steak to a clean plate and loosely cover with aluminum foil.
While the steak is cooking, peel, halve, and slice shallot into ¼-inch thick half-moons.

When the potatoes have started to soften, remove from the oven. Add shallot and snap peas, toss to combine, then spread out in an even layer. Return to the oven and roast until veggies are fork-tender, 10-12 minutes more. Remove from oven.
When the veggies are done, add to the bowl with the dressing and toss to combine the potato salad.
Thinly slice steak against the grain.
To serve, divide steak and warm potato salad between plates. Enjoy!

name: "Stuffed Bell Pepper" Soup with Turkey, Rice, Spinach, Dill & Parmesan
ingredients: 32 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Preheat a medium saucepan over medium-high heat.

Once the pan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add turkey, salt, and pepper to the pan; cook, breaking apart with a spoon, until browned and crumbly, 3-4 minutes. Transfer turkey to a plate and set aside. (Reserve saucepan for later use.)
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)
Trim and small dice celery; peel, trim, and small dice carrot. Place both in a medium bowl.
Trim, seed, and slice bell pepper into thin strips, then cut crosswise into bite-sized pieces. Add to the bowl with the celery and carrot.
Peel, halve, and small dice onion; add to the bowl.
Return the saucepan to medium-high heat.
While the pan heats up, peel and mince garlic; add to the bowl with the veggies.
Once the pan is hot, add more oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add veggies and spices; sauté, stirring occasionally, until starting to soften, 3-4 minutes. (Reserve bowl for later use.)

Return turkey to the pan along with broth, tomatoes, and rice; stir to combine and bring to a boil over high heat. Once boiling, reduce heat to low and simmer, stirring occasionally, until rice is soft and veggies are tender, about 12 minutes.
Meanwhile, roughly chop spinach and place in the reserved bowl.
Using a knife, shave dill leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl with the spinach and set aside.
Finely grate Parmesan and set aside.
When the soup is done, add spinach and dill to the pan in handfuls, waiting for the spinach to wilt slightly before adding the next handful. Stir to combine and remove from the heat.
To serve, divide soup between bowls and top with Parmesan. Enjoy!

name: Stuffed Mexican Sweet Potatoes
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F and place the rack in the center position.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.

Cut sweet potato in half lengthwise. Rub the inside and outside of the potato with oil and season with salt. Place cut side down on a baking sheet pan and pierce skin all over with a fork. Bake for 25 minutes until sweet potatoes are fork tender.
Meanwhile, preheat a medium saucepan over medium heat. When heated, add butter to the pan.
Peel and small dice the onion. Peel and mince or press the garlic. Add to onions and garlic to the pan; cook, stirring frequently, until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Drain and rinse beans in a colander. Add to pan with the onion and garlic.
Drain diced tomatoes using the colander and discard juice. Add tomatoes to pan.
Season the bean mixture with chili powder, cumin, salt, and cayenne pepper. Stir until fragrant, 15 to 30 seconds.
Turn heat up to medium-high and cook, stirring occasionally, until the beans are warmed through and tender, 5 minutes. Mash some of the beans with a potato masher.
Remove the sweet potatoes from the oven when fork-tender. Let cool for 5 minutes.
Scrape out the flesh of the sweet potatoes, leaving the skins intact and a thin layer of potato inside, set skins aside.
Add the sweet potato flesh to a bowl with the bean mixture, stir to combine.
Grate cheddar cheese.
Halve and pit the avocado; slice avocado crosswise while still in the skin and scoop out with a spoon.
Shave the cilantro leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves.
Trim and discard root ends of green onions, and chop.
To serve, return the bean mixture to the sweet potato skins. Top with cheese, avocado, cilantro and green onion. Squeeze lime over top. Enjoy!

name: Stuffed Peppers with Spiced Indian Beef & Cucumber-Corn Salad
instructions: Preheat oven to broil on high and position rack in the upper third of the oven.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.

Trim, seed, and halve bell peppers lengthwise. Transfer to a baking sheet pan, drizzle with oil, and season with salt; arrange cut-side down. Place baking sheet in the oven and broil, flipping once, until peppers are lightly charred and tender, 6-8 minutes. Remove from oven.

Meanwhile, quarter jalapeño pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon to reduce spice level. Mince and divide between a small and medium bowl. (Be careful with jalapeños; do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Peel and mince ginger and garlic. Add both to the small bowl with the jalapeño, along with tomato paste and spices. Stir to combine the spice paste and set aside.
Juice lime into the medium bowl with the jalapeño. Add honey, cumin, and salt, then stir to combine the dressing.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, peel, halve, and mince onion. Add half to the medium bowl with the dressing and set aside for the salad. (Reserve remaining onion for the next step.)
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add reserved onion and salt; cook, stirring occasionally, until beginning to soften and brown, 3-4 minutes.
Add beef to the skillet and cook, breaking it apart with a spoon, until browned and crumbly, 4-5 minutes.
Meanwhile, trim and medium dice cucumber. Add to the bowl with the dressing.
Rinse corn under hot water (from the tap) to thaw. Add to the bowl.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and roughly chop the leaves. Add half to the bowl and stir to combine the salad; set aside. (Reserve remaining cilantro for later use.)
When the beef is done, add spice paste to the skillet. Cook, stirring frequently, until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add peas, water, vinegar, and reserved cilantro to the skillet. Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until peas are warmed through, about 1 minute. Remove from heat.
Stuff pepper halves with beef mixture, then divide between plates. Serve with salad on the side and enjoy!

name: Sun-Dried Tomato Chicken with Broccoli, Pine Nuts & Parmesan
ingredients: ¾ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
instructions: Fill a medium saucepan about halfway with hot water (from the tap). Add salt, cover with a lid and bring to a boil over high heat.
Wash the broccoli and cut the florets into bite-sized pieces. Peel and small dice (or julienne) the stems.

Once the water comes to a boil, uncover, add broccoli florets and stems, and stir for a few seconds. Cook until crisp-tender, about 3 minutes. Once done, drain in a colander and then lay the broccoli on a clean towel and pat dry.
Cut chicken into 1-inch pieces. Season with spices and toss to coat.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat. When the skillet is hot, add olive oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add the chicken to the skillet; cook, stirring occasionally, until the pieces are browned and cooked through, 4-6 minutes. Transfer chicken to a plate.
Meanwhile, peel and small dice onion. Peel and mince garlic.
Thinly slice sun-dried tomatoes.
Add oil, onion, garlic, tomatoes, and crushed red peppers to the skillet. Cook, stirring frequently, until onions are translucent, about 3 minutes.
Finely grate Parmesan.
Add the broccoli and chicken to the skillet and continue to cook, stirring continuously, until broccoli and chicken are heated through, about 2 minutes.
To serve, divide between plates and top with Parmesan cheese and pine nuts. Enjoy!

name: Sun-Dried Tomato Fettuccine with Olives, Pine Nuts, Arugula & Parmesan
instructions: Fill a large pot halfway with hot water (from the tap), cover, and bring to a boil. Uncover, add salt and pasta, and stir for a few seconds. Cook until desired firmness, 8-10 minutes. (Reserve a ¼-cup of cooking water before draining.) Return pasta and reserved cooking water to the pot.
Meanwhile, wash and dry arugula (skip this step if it came pre-washed). Set aside.
Wash, dry, and juice lemon into a small bowl.
Peel and mince garlic. Add to the bowl with the lemon juice.
Roughly chop olives and sun-dried tomatoes. Add both to the bowl.
Finely grate Parmesan. Add to the bowl along with pine nuts, oil, and spices; stir to combine the pasta seasoning.
When the pasta is done, add pasta seasoning to the pot. Set over medium heat and cook, stirring often, until warmed through and sauce coats pasta, 1-2 minutes.
Add arugula to the pot in handfuls, waiting for it to wilt slightly before adding the next handful. Remove from heat.
To serve, divide pasta between plates or bowls. Enjoy!

name: Sun-Dried Tomato Pasta with Spinach & Fresh Basil
instructions: Boil water in a kettle. (If you do not have a kettle, boil water in a saucepan, starting with hot tap water.)
In a small bowl, pour boiling water over cashews and set aside to soak.
Fill a medium saucepan halfway with water, cover, and bring to a boil. Uncover, add salt and pasta, and stir for a few seconds. Cook until desired firmness, 8-10 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)
Halve the tomatoes and set aside in a small bowl.
Pick basil leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and slice into ribbons. Add to the bowl with the tomatoes, setting some aside to use as garnish.
Thinly slice the sun-dried tomatoes and add to the bowl.
Juice the lemon into a blender. Peel and mince garlic; add to the blender.
Add additional sun-dried tomatoes, oil, salt, and pepper to the blender.
Add cashews, and the water you soaked them in, to the blender. Blend on high speed for several minutes until smooth.

Place spinach in a large colander in the sink. When the pasta is cooked, carefully empty into the colander over the spinach to drain and to wilt the spinach. Return the pasta and spinach to the pan and stir in the cashew-cream, dried and fresh tomatoes, and basil.
To serve, divide pasta between plates, garnish with reserved basil, and enjoy!

name: Sun-Dried Tomato Turkey Meatballs with Sautéed Garlicky Kale & Ricotta
instructions: Preheat the oven to 425°F. Coat a baking dish with a thin layer of oil and set aside.
Finely grate Parmesan. Place in a small bowl along with ricotta, salt, and pepper; stir to combine. Set aside.
Wash, dry, and shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Place half in a medium bowl. (Reserve the other half for serving.)

Roughly chop sun-dried tomatoes. Add to the bowl with the parsley along with half of the cheese mixture, turkey, bread crumbs, egg, and spices. Using your hands, mix well to combine. (Reserve remaining cheese mixture for serving.)
Using a tablespoon measure, form the turkey mixture into rounded meatballs and place in the baking dish.
Place baking dish in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and bake until meatballs are lightly browned and nearly cooked through, about 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry kale. Fold leaves in half lengthwise and slice off the stems. Chop or tear leaves into bite-sized pieces and place in a clean medium bowl.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, peel and thinly slice garlic. Add to the bowl with the kale.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add garlic and kale to the skillet in handfuls, waiting for kale to wilt slightly before adding the next handful. Cook, stirring frequently, until the kale is tender, 1-2 minutes more. (Reserve bowl for later use.)
Add vinegar, crushed red pepper, and salt to the skillet with the kale; stir to combine. Remove from heat and cover with a lid to keep warm.
Place tomato sauce, Italian seasoning, and additional crushed red pepper in the reserved bowl. Stir to combine the sauce.

When the meatballs are lightly browned, remove from oven. Pour tomato sauce over meatballs, return to oven, and continue to bake until the sauce is warm and meatballs are cooked through, 2-3 minutes more. Remove from oven.
To serve, divide meatballs, sauce, kale, and reserved cheese mixture between plates or bowls. Top with reserved parsley and enjoy!

name: Sweet Chili Salmon Sandwich with Avocado & Ginger-Tahini Dressed Salad
instructions: Place vinegar, sugar, water, chili-garlic sauce, and salt in a small saucepan; whisk to combine. Set over medium-high heat and bring to a boil, whisking occasionally.
Meanwhile, in a small bowl, make a slurry by whisking water with cornstarch until smooth.

Once the sauce is boiling, add cornstarch slurry to the pan in a steady stream while whisking quickly. Cook, whisking constantly, until the sweet chili sauce thickens, about 30 seconds. Remove from heat, cover, and set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat salmon dry with paper towels and place skin-side down on a plate; season the top side with salt and pepper.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add salmon, skin-side down, and cook, flipping once, until skin is crispy and flesh is opaque, 3-4 minutes per side. Transfer to a clean plate and set aside.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and mince ginger; place in a medium bowl. Add tahini, vinegar, soy sauce, oil, and chili-garlic sauce. Whisk to combine the dressing.
Trim and thinly slice radishes; add to the bowl with the dressing.
Trim and halve cucumber lengthwise, then cut crosswise into thin half-moons. Add to the bowl and set aside.
Halve and pit avocado; scoop out with a spoon and thinly slice. Add to the plate with the salmon.
Toast buns if desired.
Separate lettuce leaves; set aside two leaves per sandwich. Chop or tear remaining leaves into bite-sized pieces, then add to the bowl with the dressing and veggies. Toss to combine the salad.
Place the bottom half of a bun on each plate. Top with salmon, sweet chili sauce, avocado, and reserved lettuce leaves; close with the top half of each bun. Serve with salad on the side and enjoy!

name: Sweet Potato & Black Bean Chili with Avocado
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and small dice the onion into ¼-inch pieces; transfer to a small bowl.
Peel and mince the garlic; transfer to a small bowl.
Preheat a medium saucepan over medium heat.
Drain and rinse the beans; set aside.
Once the saucepan is warm, add coconut oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add the onion to the saucepan; cook, stirring frequently, until softened, 3 to 5 minutes.
While the onion cooks, peel and medium dice the sweet potatoes into ½-inch cubes; leave on cutting board.
Add the garlic and sweet potatoes to the saucepan and stir to combine; cook, stirring occasionally, for 2 to 4 minutes.
Add the beans to the saucepan and season with chili powder, cumin, salt, and pepper. Stir until fragrant, 15 to 30 seconds.

Add the diced tomatoes to the saucepan and stir to combine. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to medium-low and cover with a lid. Cook the chili until the sweet potatoes are tender, 5 to 7 minutes.
While the chili cooks, halve the avocado lengthwise and twist to open, then remove the pit with a knife or spoon; scoop out and medium dice the flesh. Transfer to a small bowl.
Shave the cilantro leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves. Stir half into the chili and transfer the rest to a small bowl (for garnishing).
To serve, spoon the chili into a bowl and garnish with the avocado and remaining cilantro. Enjoy!

name: Sweet Potato & Black Bean Salad with Avocado Dressing & Feta
ingredients: ½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled feta cheese
½ (5 oz) pkg spring mix (mixed greens)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 450°F and place the rack in the center position.
Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the mixed greens if they came pre-washed.)
Peel and medium dice the sweet potatoes into ½-inch cubes; transfer to a medium bowl.
Drizzle the potatoes with olive oil and season with chili powder, cumin, salt, and pepper; toss to coat. Transfer the mixture to a sheet pan and spread out in a single layer.
Place the potatoes in the oven and roast, tossing once halfway through cooking time, until the potatoes are tender and lightly browned, 15 to 20 minutes.
Drain and rinse the beans in a colander; set aside to drain further.
Scoop out the avocado flesh and transfer to a medium bowl; mash with a fork until smooth.
Trim off and discard the root end of the garlic; peel and mince or press the garlic. Add to the bowl with the mashed avocado.
Juice the lime and add to the bowl.
Add olive oil, salt, and pepper to the bowl; mix the dressing until well combined. Alternatively, use a hand blender to make a very smooth dressing.
Place the feta in a small bowl.
Using a knife, shave the cilantro leaves off the stems at a downward angle, working away from your body; discard the stems and finely chop the leaves. Transfer to a large salad bowl.
Add the sweet potatoes and beans to the salad bowl; toss to combine.
To serve, divide the mixed greens between dishes, top with the salad and feta, and drizzle with the dressing. Mix together and enjoy!

name: Sweet Potato Burrito Bowl with Kidney Bean Chili, Cheddar & Avocado
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F. Line a baking sheet pan with aluminum foil and set aside.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.

Peel and cut sweet potato lengthwise into 1-inch thick wedges (4-6 pieces per potato, depending on size), then transfer to the baking sheet. Drizzle with oil and season with spices; toss to coat and spread out in an even layer.
Place sweet potato wedges in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and bake, flipping halfway through, until fork-tender, about 25 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, drain and rinse beans; set aside to drain further.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, peel, halve, and small dice onion; peel and mince garlic.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add onion, garlic, and corn; cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, 3-4 minutes.
While the veggies are cooking, trim, seed, and small dice bell pepper.
Add beans, bell pepper, tomatoes, and spices to the skillet; stir to combine the chili and bring to a simmer.
Once the chili is simmering, reduce heat to medium and cook, stirring occasionally, until veggies are tender and sauce has thickened, 5-6 minutes. Remove from heat.
Meanwhile, coarsely grate cheese.
Halve and pit avocado. Slice thinly while still in skin, then scoop out with a spoon.
To serve, divide sweet potato wedges between plates or bowls; top with chili, cheese, and avocado. Enjoy!

name: Sweet Potato Chickpea Bowls with Maple-Tahini Sauce
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.

Peel the sweet potatoes and onions; cut both into 1-inch pieces. Transfer a medium bowl; add oil, salt, and pepper, and toss to coat. Place veggies on a baking sheet and bake, until softened, about 10 minutes. Reserve bowl for later use.
Meanwhile, drain and rinse the chickpeas; set aside to drain further.

Separate broccoli into bite-sized florets and cut stems into smaller pieces. Place broccoli in the medium bowl, add oil, salt, and pepper, and toss to coat. Add to baking sheet with the sweet potatoes, tossing to combine; bake until cooked through, about 10 more minutes. Reserve bowl for later use.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Combine spices in a small bowl.
When the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add chickpeas and spices to the skillet and toss to coat. Cook, stirring occasionally, until chickpeas are golden and fragrant, about 10 minutes. When done, set aside.

Meanwhile, fold kale leaves in half lengthwise and slice off the stems. Chop or tear leaves into bite-sized pieces and transfer to the medium bowl; add oil, salt, and pepper and toss to combine. Add to the baking sheet and cook until wilted, about 5 more minutes.
Juice lemon into a small bowl; add tahini, maple syrup, and water, whisking to combine the dressing. Add additional water as needed to reach a drizzling consistency.
To serve, divide roasted vegetables and chickpeas between bowls. Drizzle with tahini-maple dressing and enjoy!

name: Sweet Potato-Edamame Rice Bowl with Broccoli Slaw & Almond-Lime Sauce
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add water and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Cook rice until liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and medium dice sweet potato; transfer to a baking sheet pan, drizzle with oil, and season with spices. Toss to combine, then spread out in an even layer.
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast, tossing once, until sweet potatoes are fork-tender, about 20 minutes. Remove from oven.
While the sweet potatoes are roasting, place edamame in a colander and rinse under hot water (from the tap) to thaw. Set aside to drain.
Peel and mince ginger and garlic; place both in a small bowl.

Juice lime into the bowl with the ginger and garlic; add almond butter, water, and soy sauce. Whisk to combine the sauce, adding additional water, 1 teaspoon at a time, if necessary, to reach a drizzling consistency. Set sauce aside.
Trim, seed, and cut bell pepper into thin strips; transfer to a plate.
