Trim and cut green onions crosswise into ¼-inch pieces; add to the plate with the bell pepper.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves.
When the rice is done, add cilantro and stir to combine.
To serve, divide rice, roasted sweet potatoes, broccoli slaw, edamame, bell pepper, and green onions between bowls. Drizzle with sauce and enjoy!

name: Sweet Potato & Lentil Stew with Crusty Bread
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Heat a medium saucepan over medium heat.
Peel and small dice onion. Peel and mince garlic and ginger.
Coat bottom of saucepan with oil. Add onion and, stirring frequently, cook until softened, 3-4 minutes.
Rinse lentils under cold water.
Wash potatoes and tomato. Peel and large dice the potatoes. Medium dice the tomato.
Add garlic, ginger, cumin, turmeric, curry, coriander, and salt to saucepan. Stir for about 1 minute.
Add potatoes, tomatoes, lentils, and broth. Bring to a simmer and cook until potatoes and lentils are tender, 15-20 minutes.
Toast bread.
To serve, add stew to a bowl and have with bread on the side. Enjoy!

name: Sweet Potato-Onion Quesadilla with Corn, Tomato & Lime Mixed Greens
ingredients: ½ (5 oz) pkg spring mix (mixed greens)
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the mixed greens if they came pre-washed.)
Peel and small dice sweet potato. Transfer to a baking sheet pan, drizzle with oil, and season with spices. Stir to coat and spread out in an even layer.
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast, stirring halfway through, until sweet potatoes are browned and fork-tender, about 15 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, preheat a large skillet over medium-low heat.
While the skillet heats up, peel, halve, and slice onion crosswise into thin half-moons.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add onion, salt, and pepper; cook, stirring occasionally, until onions are soft and golden brown, about 10 minutes. Remove from heat.
While the onion is cooking, juice lime into a medium bowl. Add oil, honey, salt, and pepper; whisk to combine the dressing.
Rinse corn under hot water (from the tap) to thaw. Add to the bowl with the dressing.
Halve grape tomatoes. Add to the bowl, along with pumpkin seeds, and set aside.
Coarsely grate cheese.

Place tortillas on a flat surface and divide onion, sweet potato, and cheese between them, arranging the filling on one half of each tortilla; fold in half to close. (Reserve skillet for the next step.)
Wipe the skillet clean with paper towels and return to medium heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add quesadillas and cook until cheese is melted and tortillas are golden, 2½-3 minutes per side. Remove to a plate.
Meanwhile, add mixed greens to the bowl and toss to combine the salad.
Cut each quesadilla into wedges and divide between plates; serve with salad on the side. Enjoy!

name: Sweet Potato "Patatas Bravas" with Spinach, Beans & Garlic Aioli
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)
Peel and large dice sweet potatoes. Transfer to a baking sheet pan.

Peel and mince garlic. Add half to the baking sheet with the sweet potatoes, along with nutritional yeast, oil, and spices; toss to combine, then spread out in an even layer. Place remaining garlic in a small bowl and set aside.
Place sweet potatoes in the oven and bake, flipping halfway through, until fork-tender, 18-20 minutes.
Meanwhile, juice lime into the bowl with the garlic; add mayo and whisk to combine the aioli. Set aside.
Small dice tomato. Peel and small dice shallot.
Heat a medium saucepan over medium-high heat.

Once the saucepan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add tomatoes, shallot, vinegar, chili-garlic sauce, paprika, and salt; cook, stirring frequently, until tomatoes have softened and reduced, 3-4 minutes.
Meanwhile, drain and rinse beans in a colander; set aside to drain further.
Add spinach to the pan in handfuls, waiting for the spinach to wilt slightly before adding the next handful.
Add beans to the pan and stir to combine. Continue to cook until heated through, 2-3 minutes.
To serve, divide sweet potatoes and veggie-bean sauté between bowls. Drizzle with aioli and enjoy!

name: Sweet Potato Patties with Smoked Salmon & Creamy Greek Salad
ingredients: ½ (4 oz) pkg crumbled feta cheese
instructions: In a medium bowl, whisk the egg.
Wash, peel, and coarsely grate the sweet potatoes. Use a paper towel or a clean cloth to squeeze out the excess moisture and add to the bowl with the egg.
Peel and mince shallot. Add to the bowl along with flour, salt, and pepper; stir to combine.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom.

Using a ¼ cup measure, form the potato mixture into patties. Working in batches if necessary, add patties to the skillet and flatten into ½-thick circles using the back of a spatula. Cook, flipping once, until golden and cooked through, 6-8 minutes. Remove to a paper towel-lined plate.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Using a knife, shave the dill leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves. Place in a medium bowl.
Add yogurt, feta, vinegar, capers, and honey to the bowl with the dill; whisk to combine the dressing.
Halve olives and add to the bowl with the dressing.
Halve tomatoes lengthwise and add to the bowl.
Trim cucumber; quarter lengthwise, then slice crosswise into ¼-inch thick pieces. Add to the bowl and toss to combine the salad.
To serve, divide patties, salmon, and salad between plates. Enjoy!

name: Sweet Potato, Spinach & White Bean Curry with Quinoa
ingredients: 4 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: In a small saucepan, combine the quinoa, salt, and water; bring to a boil over high heat.
While the liquid comes to a boil, wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce the heat to low. Cook the quinoa for 15 minutes. Once done, remove the quinoa from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Peel and medium dice the potatoes (cut into ½-inch cubes); transfer to a bowl.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, trim off and discard the ends of the onion and remove the outer layer; small dice the onion (cut into ¼-inch pieces).
Once the skillet is hot, add coconut oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add the onion to the skillet; cook, stirring frequently, until it is softened, 3 to 5 minutes.
While the onion cooks, trim off and discard the root ends of the garlic; peel and mince or press the garlic.
Peel and grate or mince the ginger.
Add the garlic, ginger, and curry powder to the onion; stir until fragrant, 15 to 30 seconds.

Add the sweet potatoes, tomato sauce, broth, and salt to the skillet; stir to combine and reduce the heat to medium-low. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 10 minutes before adding the remaining ingredients.
While the curry cooks, using a knife, shave the parsley leaves off the stems at a downward angle, working away from your body; discard the stems and roughly chop the leaves.
Drain and rinse the beans.
Add the beans, spinach, ¾ of the parsley (save the rest for garnishing), and yogurt to the curry; stir to combine and continue cooking until the potatoes are tender, another 5 to 7 minutes.
Uncover the quinoa and fluff with a fork.
To serve, place the quinoa on a plate or in a bowl, top with the curry, and garnish with the remaining parsley leaves. Enjoy!

name: Sweet & Sour Meatballs with Pineapple & Bell Pepper
ingredients: 4 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: In a medium bowl, combine beef, bread crumbs, salt, and pepper. Mix well.
Peel and medium dice onion. Wash, seed, and medium dice bell peppers. Cut off skin from pineapple, core, and cut into bite-sized pieces.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Form beef mixture into small meatballs and place on a plate.
Coat bottom of skillet with oil. Add meatballs and, turning often, cook until browned on all sides, 3-4 minutes. Transfer to a plate.
In a small bowl, prepare sauce by whisking together broth, vinegar, honey, soy sauce, and cornstarch.
Return skillet to stove and add more oil. Add onion and bell peppers. Stirring frequently, cook until tender-crisp, 2-3 minutes.
Stir in pineapple and cook for about 1 minute.
Pour in sauce and return meatballs to skillet. Season with salt and pepper. Stir to combine and cook until sauce is thickened, 3-4 minutes.
To serve, place in a bowl. Enjoy!

name: Sweet & Sour Shrimp with Rice Noodles, Carrots and Peppers
ingredients: 4 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
¾ lb raw peeled shrimp, fresh or frozen
instructions: If using frozen shrimp, place them in a colander and run under cold water to thaw them slightly and remove any ice crystals. (If using fresh shrimp, skip this step.) Place the shrimp on a clean towel or paper towels and pat dry.
Fill a medium saucepan halfway with water and bring to a boil. Remove from heat and add rice noodles. Soak for 10 minutes or according to package directions. Then drain in a colander and rinse.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.

Peel the carrots; then using the peeler, run it along the carrot to make long, noodle-like strips. Seed and slice bell pepper into thin strips. Trim ends of celery and slice into small pieces. Transfer all to a medium bowl.
Trim off and discard the ends of the green onions; cut the onions crosswise into small pieces. Add half of the onions to the bowl with the sliced vegetables (reserving the rest for garnish).
Heat a large pot over medium heat.
Peel and mince or grate the ginger. Peel and mince the garlic.
Once the pot is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add the sliced vegetables, ginger, garlic, and black pepper to the pot. Sauté until soft, 4-5 minutes.
Trim off and discard the root end of the cabbage; halve the cabbage lengthwise, then thinly slice crosswise.
Add the cabbage and shrimp to the pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, until cabbage softens and shrimp is cooked through, 2-3 minutes.
Juice the lime into a small bowl. Add the cornstarch and whisk together.

Juice the orange into the pot; add broth, sugar, soy sauce, and fish sauce. Bring to a boil over high heat, then stir in the cornstarch mixture. Reduce heat to low, add rice noodles, and simmer, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened, 1-2 minutes.
Divide between bowls, garnish with remaining green onion, and enjoy!

name: Sweet & Sour Thai Chicken Vegetable Soup
ingredients: ¾ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
½ (13.5 fl oz) can coconut milk
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Cut chicken into 1-inch pieces, set aside.
Heat coconut oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Peel and mince the garlic. Peel and mince or grate the ginger. Add both to the pot.
Add to the pot turmeric and crushed red pepper, stirring until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Add chicken pieces to pot, stirring occasionally.
Peel and thinly slice carrot on the bias. Cut the bell pepper lengthwise into quarters; remove and discard the seeds and white membrane then slice thinly. Add veggies to the pot.
Remove the stems from the mushroom and carefully scrape out the gills with a spoon, making sure not to damage the rim of the mushrooms. Cut cap in half, thinly slice and add to the pot.
Cook chicken and vegetables, stirring occasionally, until vegetables are tender, about 5-7 minutes.
Add broth, coconut milk, fish sauce, honey, and vinegar and stir to combine.
Bring soup to boil and then reduce heat to low. Simmer for 8-10 minutes, allowing the chicken to cook fully and flavors to blend.
Shave the cilantro leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves.
Juice the lime and add to the pot right before serving, stir to combine.
To serve, divide soup between bowls and garnish with cilantro. Enjoy!

name: Taco Lettuce Wraps with Cheddar
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce (skip the lettuce until the next step).
Trim off and discard the root end of the lettuce; separate the leaves, then wash and dry them. Transfer to a plate.
Trim off and discard the ends of the green onions; cut the onions crosswise into ¼-inch pieces at an angle and transfer to a small bowl.
Quarter the grape tomatoes and transfer to a small bowl.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Trim off and discard the ends of the onion and remove the outer layer; small dice the onion (cut into ¼-inch pieces).
Once the skillet is hot, add coconut oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add the onion to the skillet; cook, stirring frequently, until softened, 3 to 4 minutes.
Trim off and discard the root end of the garlic; peel and mince or press the garlic.
Add the garlic, chili powder, cumin, salt, and pepper to the onion; stir until fragrant, 15 to 30 seconds.
Add the ground beef to the skillet and; cook, breaking apart with a spoon, until browned and crumbly, 4 to 5 minutes.
Coarsely grate ½ cup of cheddar.
To serve, double up the lettuce leaves and fill with the ground beef mixture, tomatoes, cheddar, and green onions. Alternatively, combine all of the ingredients in a bowl to make a salad. Enjoy!

name: Tandoori Chicken Burger with Cucumber Raita & Spinach-Apple Salad
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the spinach if it came pre-washed.)
Peel and mince ginger and garlic. Place both in a medium bowl.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl with the ginger and garlic.
Add chicken, bread crumbs, and spices to the bowl; mix with your hands until well combined. Form the chicken mixture into 2 equal-sized patties, place on a plate, and set aside.
Preheat a grill pan, outdoor grill, or regular skillet over medium-high heat.

Once the grill pan is hot, coat with oil. Add burger patties and cook, undisturbed, for 5 minutes; flip patties and cook an additional 5-7 minutes, until cooked through. Once done, transfer to a clean plate.
Meanwhile, trim and coarsely grate cucumber. Use paper towels or a clean cloth to squeeze excess moisture out of the grated cucumber.
Place cucumber in a small bowl, then add yogurt and salt. Whisk to combine the raita and set aside.
Juice lime into in a clean medium bowl. Add oil, honey, and salt; whisk to combine the dressing.
Quarter, core, and thinly slice apple. Add to the bowl with the dressing, along with the spinach, and toss to combine the salad.
Toast buns if desired.
To assemble the burgers, spread the bottom half of each bun with half of the raita. Layer with burger patties and remaining raita, then close with the top half of the buns.
Divide burgers and salad between plates. Enjoy!

name: Tangy Peanut Soba Noodle Salad with Crispy Tofu
instructions: Fill a medium saucepan about halfway with hot water (from the tap); cover with a lid and bring to a boil over high heat.
While the water comes to a boil, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Drain and medium dice (cut into ¾-inch cubes) the tofu; place the cubes on paper towels and pat dry.
Once the skillet is hot, add sesame oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add the tofu to the skillet; cook, stirring occasionally, until golden brown, 5 to 6 minutes. Once done, transfer the tofu to a plate.

Once the water in the saucepan is boiling, add the noodles; cook according to package directions, about 5 to 7 minutes. Once done, drain the noodles in a colander and rinse under cold water; set aside.
Juice the lime into a small bowl (that will be used for the salad dressing).
Peel and grate or mince the ginger; add the ginger to the small bowl.
Trim off and discard the root ends of the garlic; peel and mince or press the garlic and add to the small bowl.

Using a knife, shave the cilantro leaves off the stems at a downward angle, working away from your body; discard the stems and finely chop about ¾ of the leaves (save the rest for garnishing). Add the chopped cilantro to the small bowl.
To make the dressing, add peanut butter, soy sauce, honey, sesame oil, and crushed red pepper to the small bowl; whisk the ingredients together.
Peel the carrots, then trim off the ends; discard the peels and trimmings. Using a box grater, coarsely grate the carrots and transfer to a large bowl.
Halve the sugar snap peas at an angle and add to the large bowl.
Add the noodles and tofu to the large bowl with the carrots and peas and pour the dressing over top; toss until everything is well coated with the sauce.
To serve, place the noodle mixture into a bowl and garnish with the remaining cilantro leaves. Enjoy!

name: Tempeh Tacos with Tomato-Radish Salsa & Cilantro Lime Aioli
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Zest and juice lime. Divide between a small and medium bowl.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Divide between the bowls. (Set medium bowl aside for later use.)
Add mayo and spices to the small bowl, then stir to combine the lime aioli. Set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, peel, halve, and mince onion. Add half to the medium bowl with the lime and cilantro, then set aside. (Reserve remaining onion for the next step.)

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Using your fingers, crumble tempeh into the skillet, then add reserved onion, salt, and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the tempeh is browned and onion is soft, about 5 minutes.

Reduce heat to medium. Add tomato sauce, water, nutritional yeast, and spices to the skillet, then stir to combine. Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens, about 5 minutes. Remove from heat.

Meanwhile, quarter jalapeño pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon to reduce spice level. Mince and add to the medium bowl. (Be careful with jalapeños; do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Small dice tomatoes. Add to the bowl.
Trim and halve radishes, then slice crosswise into thin half-moons. Add to the bowl, along with salt and pepper, then stir to combine the salsa. Set aside.
Warm tortillas in another skillet or microwave (optional).
To serve, divide tortillas between plates; fill with saucy tempeh and salsa. Drizzle with lime aioli and enjoy!

name: Teriyaki Chicken with Bok Choy, Cashews & Coconut Rice
ingredients: ½ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
½ (13.5 fl oz) can coconut milk
instructions: Heat a medium saucepan over high heat. Add coconut milk, water, and salt and bring to a boil.
Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir in the rice, and reduce the heat to low. Cover and cook until the rice is tender and all liquid has been absorbed, about 12 minutes.
Peel and mince the garlic. Peel and mince or grate the ginger.
In a medium bowl, create a slurry by whisking together water and cornstarch until smooth. Add soy sauce, honey, and the minced garlic and ginger to make the teriyaki sauce.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Cut the chicken into bite-sized pieces. Season with salt and pepper.
Once the skillet is hot, add coconut oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add the chicken and cook until browned and cooked through, 4-5 minutes.
Wash bok choy, trim ends, and chop into 1-inch pieces.

Add the bok choy to the skillet; cook, tossing frequently, until the bok choy is wilted and tender, 2-4 minutes. Add the teriyaki sauce. Cook, stirring often, until the sauce is slightly thickened, 2-3 minutes.
To serve, divide the rice between bowls, top with the stir fry, and sprinkle with cashews. Enjoy!

name: Teriyaki Chicken Drumsticks with Sautéed Sugar Snap Peas
instructions: Preheat the oven to 500°F, position rack in the centre, and place a baking sheet inside to warm up.
Peel and mince the garlic. Peel and mince or grate the ginger.
In a medium bowl, whisk together water and cornstarch. Add the minced garlic and ginger, honey, rice vinegar, and soy sauce; whisk again.
Add the chicken to the sauce and toss to coat.
Remove baking sheet from the oven and line with foil. Add the chicken, reserving the sauce in the bowl.
Place in the oven and bake until chicken is golden brown and cooked through, 25-30 minutes. Spoon teriyaki sauce over the chicken a couple times during cooking until there is no more sauce left.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Wash the snap peas.
Add oil to the skillet and swirl to coat bottom. Add the peas and season with salt and pepper. Cook, tossing occasionally, until bright green and tender-crisp, 4-5 minutes.
Serve chicken drumsticks with sugar snap peas on the side. Sprinkle with sesame seeds and enjoy!

name: Teriyaki Mushroom  Bowl with Carrots & Quick Pickled Cucumbers
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add water and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
Drain and rinse the beans in a colander; set aside to drain further.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce the heat to low. Cook the rice until the liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove the rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
In a medium bowl, combine vinegar, sugar, and salt. Thinly slice the cucumber, add to the bowl, and toss to coat.
Peel and mince the garlic and the ginger; place in a small bowl. Add soy sauce, brown sugar, and sesame oil to make the teriyaki sauce.
Remove the stems of the portobello mushrooms; scrape out the gills using a spoon. Cut mushrooms in half and then slice crosswise into thin strips.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Peel and thinly slice onion into half rings.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add the yellow onions and cook for about 2 minutes. Add the mushrooms and continue cooking until the mushrooms have started to soften, about 6 minutes.
Add beans and teriyaki sauce to the skillet and cook 3 minutes more.
Trim green onions and cut crosswise into ¼-inch pieces at an angle.
Peel and coarsely grate the carrot.
Uncover the rice and fluff with a fork, and drizzle with sesame oil and sprinkle with sesame seeds. Fold the oil and seeds into the rice.
To serve, divide rice between bowls and top with mushrooms, cucumbers, carrots, and green onions. Enjoy!

name: Teriyaki Salmon Meatballs with Broccoli, Carrot & Rice Pilaf
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
1 (7.5 oz) can wild pink salmon, traditional style
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and mince the onion. Transfer half to a large bowl and set aside. Transfer the rest to a medium saucepan.
Chop broccoli into small pieces. Peel, trim, and small dice carrot. Add both to the saucepan with the onion.
Add rice and broth to the pan with the veggies, stirring to combine. Bring to a boil over high heat.
Meanwhile, drain salmon and place in the bowl with the onion. Add bread crumbs, egg, salt, and pepper; mix well to combine.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, scrape down the edges of the saucepan so that all of the rice grains are in the liquid. Cover the saucepan, reduce heat to low, and cook until the liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Coat a baking dish with a thin layer of oil. Form the salmon mixture into 2-inch rounded meatballs and place them in the baking dish. Place the dish in the oven and bake until set, about 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel and mince garlic and ginger.
Combine garlic, ginger, soy sauce, honey, and vinegar in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil over high heat and cook until slightly thickened, 1-2 minutes.
In a small bowl, make a slurry by whisking water with cornstarch until smooth.
Add cornstarch slurry to the saucepan in a steady stream while stirring quickly. Cook, stirring often, until sauce thickens, 1-2 minutes. Remove from heat.
Once the salmon meatballs are done, pour the teriyaki sauce over the meatballs and gently toss to coat.
To serve, divide rice and salmon meatballs between plates. Garnish with sesame seeds and enjoy!

name: Teriyaki Turkey Burger with Grilled Onions & Pineapple-Broccoli Slaw
ingredients: 4 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Peel and mince ginger and garlic; place both in a small saucepan.
Add broth, soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, and chili-garlic sauce to the saucepan with the ginger and garlic; whisk to combine. Place over high heat and bring to a boil.

Meanwhile, in a small bowl, make a slurry by whisking water with cornstarch until smooth. Once the liquid in the saucepan comes to a boil, add slurry in a steady stream while whisking quickly. Let boil for 1 minute, then remove teriyaki sauce from heat and set aside.
Preheat a grill pan, outdoor grill, or regular skillet over medium-high heat.
While the pan heats up, peel and slice onion crosswise into thin rings. Transfer to a plate, drizzle with oil, and season with salt on both sides.

Once the pan is hot, add the onions and grill, flipping once, until tender and lightly charred, 3-4 minutes. Return onions to the plate and loosely cover with aluminum foil. (Reserve pan for the burger patties.)

Meanwhile, place turkey, bread crumbs, salt, pepper, and half of the teriyaki sauce in a medium bowl; mix with your hands until well combined. Form the turkey mixture into 2 equal-sized patties and place on another plate. (Reserve remaining teriyaki sauce for serving.)

When the onions are done, return the pan to medium-high heat and coat with oil. Add burger patties and cook, undisturbed, for 5 minutes; flip patties, and cook an additional 5-6 minutes, until cooked through. Add to the plate with the onions and re-cover with foil.
While the patties are cooking, place additional oil, soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, and chili-garlic sauce in a clean medium bowl; whisk to combine the dressing.
Cut off skin from pineapple; quarter, core, and medium dice. Add to the bowl with the dressing.
Trim and thinly slice bok choy crosswise into shred-like strips; add to the bowl, along with the broccoli slaw, and toss to combine.
Toast buns if desired.

Place bottom half of each bun on a plate; layer with burger patties, remaining teriyaki sauce, onions, and a small portion of the slaw. Close with the top half of each bun and serve with remaining slaw on the side. Enjoy!

name: Tex-Mex Salad Flatbread with Beans, Corn & Avocado Ranch Dressing
ingredients: ½ (5 oz) pkg spring mix (mixed greens)
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce. (Skip the mixed greens if they came pre-washed.)
Halve and pit the avocado. Slice thinly while still in skin, then scoop out into a small bowl and mash with a fork until smooth.
Juice half of the lime into the bowl with the avocado; cut remaining lime into wedges and set aside.
Add yogurt, honey, and spices to the bowl; whisk to combine the dressing and set aside.
Small dice tomato and place in a large bowl.
Peel and small dice onion; add to the bowl with the tomatoes.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl.
Place corn in a colander and run under cold water to thaw. Drain and rinse beans in the colander with the corn; set aside to drain further.
Place pitas on a baking sheet pan and drizzle with oil. Place in the oven and bake until pitas are toasted, 2-3 minutes.
Meanwhile, add corn, beans, and mixed greens to the bowl with the tomatoes; toss to combine the salad.
Coarsely grate cheddar.
To serve, divide pitas between plates, then top with salad, cheese, and dressing. Place lime wedges on the side and enjoy!

name: Thai Beef with Carrot-Basil Salad & Jasmine Rice
instructions: Rinse the rice in a colander and transfer to a small saucepan. Add water and salt; bring to a boil.
While the rice comes to a boil, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Once the water is boiling, reduce the heat to low, stir, and cover. Cook until the liquid is absorbed, 10 to 15 minutes. Remove from the heat and let it stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Pick the basil leaves off the stems; discard the stems and transfer the leaves to a small bowl.
Juice 1 ½ of the limes into a small bowl and cut the remaining half into wedges (for serving).
Trim the stem ends of the carrots and peel; discard the trimmings and julienne or coarsely grate the carrots. Transfer to a medium bowl.
Halve the jalapeño lengthwise and remove and discard the seeds; thinly slice the halves crosswise. Transfer to a small bowl.
Peel and mince the garlic; add to the bowl of jalapeño.
Heat a skillet over medium heat.
Add coconut oil to the skillet and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add the jalapeño and garlic; cook until fragrant, 15 to 30 seconds.
Add the beef and season with salt and pepper. Cook, breaking apart into smaller pieces, until cooked through and browned, 3 to 5 minutes.
While the beef cooks, add half of the basil leaves and half of the lime juice to the carrots; toss to combine.
Add water and the remaining basil leaves to the beef; cook, stirring, until the basil wilts, 1 to 2 minutes.
In a small bowl, combine and whisk together soy sauce, fish sauce, honey, and the remaining lime juice.
Divide the rice between two bowls (or one bowl and one lunch container), top with the beef and carrot-basil salad, and drizzle with the soy dressing. Serve lime wedges alongside for squeezing. Enjoy!

name: Thai Beef Patties with Minty Pineapple-Cucumber Salad & Peanuts
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim and cut green onions crosswise into thin pieces. Divide between two medium bowls, then set one bowl aside for the salad.

Peel and mince garlic. Add to the remaining bowl with the green onions along with beef, bread crumbs, egg, fish sauce, chili-garlic sauce, and spices. Use your hands to combine the beef mixture. Using a ¼-cup measure, form the mixture into ½-inch thick patties and place on a plate.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add patties and cook, flipping once, until golden and cooked through, 3-4 minutes per side. Remove to a clean plate.
Meanwhile, add fish sauce, vinegar, salt, and pepper to the remaining bowl with the green onions. Whisk to combine the dressing.
Cut off skin from pineapple; quarter, core, and cut the flesh into bite-sized pieces. Add to the bowl with the dressing.
Trim and quarter cucumber lengthwise, then cut crosswise into bite-sized pieces. Add to the bowl.
Pick mint leaves off the stems; discard stems and roughly chop the leaves. Add to the bowl and stir to combine the salad.
To serve, divide patties and salad between plates or bowls. Top salad with peanuts and enjoy!

name: Thai Chicken & Bell Pepper Lettuce Wraps with Peanut Sauce
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Cut the bell pepper lengthwise into quarters; remove and discard the seeds and white membrane. Small dice the pepper and transfer to a medium bowl.
Shave the cilantro leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves. Transfer to a small bowl and set aside.
Juice the lime into a small bowl.
Peel and mince the garlic; add to the lime juice.
Measure out the peanuts and roughly chop; transfer to a small bowl.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat.
Cut the chicken into small bite-sized pieces, then season with salt and pepper.
Add coconut oil to the skillet and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add the chicken to the skillet; cook, stirring occasionally, until golden brown and cooked through, 3 to 4 minutes. Once done, transfer to a medium bowl.
Separate the lettuce head into leaves and place on a plate.

Once the chicken has been transferred, add more coconut oil to the skillet followed by the bell pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, until tender-crisp, 3 to 4 minutes. Once done, add to the bowl of chicken and mix together.

To make the sauce, add peanut butter, soy sauce, honey, sesame oil, and crushed red pepper to the lime juice and minced garlic and whisk together. If the sauce is too thick, add a little bit of water.
To serve, scoop the chicken and pepper mixture into lettuce leaves, then top with the peanut sauce, cilantro, and peanuts. Enjoy!

name: Thai Chicken & Mango Salad with Jalapeño-Peanut Dressing
ingredients: ½ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim and discard the lettuce core; chop the lettuce into bite-sized pieces and transfer to a large bowl.
Cut the bell pepper into quarters lengthwise; remove and discard the seeds and white membranes. Medium dice the pepper and add to the bowl.
Peel the mango and slice the flesh away from the pit, starting with the flat sides. Medium dice the mango and add to the bowl.
Shave the cilantro leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl.
Measure out and chop the peanuts; add to the bowl.
Cut the jalapeño into quarters lengthwise; remove and discard the seeds and white membranes. Mince the pepper and transfer to a medium bowl.
Juice the lime and add the juice to the bowl with the jalapeño.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat.
Cut the chicken into bite-sized cubes, then season with salt and pepper.
Add coconut oil to the skillet and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add the chicken to the skillet; cook until it is cooked through and golden brown; 3 to 4 minutes per side.

While the chicken cooks, prepare the dressing by adding peanut butter, soy sauce, water, honey, and sesame oil to the bowl with the jalapeño and lime juice; whisk together until smooth. If the dressing is too thick, add more water to thin it out.
Add the chicken to the salad and toss to combine.
To serve, place the salad in a bowl and drizzle with the jalapeño-peanut dressing. Enjoy!

name: Thai Chicken & Zucchini Noodle Salad with Spicy Peanut Sauce
ingredients: ¾ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
instructions: Peel and mince or press the garlic. Peel and mince or grate the ginger. In a medium bowl, prepare the dressing by whisking together the minced garlic and ginger, peanut butter, soy sauce, water, lime juice, and crushed red pepper. Set aside.

Wash and dry the carrots and zucchini. Trim off and discard the ends of the carrots and zucchini. Using a julienne (or regular) peeler, peel the carrots and zucchini into thin noodle-like sticks; transfer them to a large bowl and set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium heat.
Holding a knife parallel to the cutting board, cut the chicken in half horizontally to form thin fillets. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Add coconut oil to the skillet and swirl to coat the bottom. Add the chicken and cook until golden brown and cooked through, 3-4 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate and set aside to cool.

Once the chicken has been removed, add more coconut oil to the skillet. Then add the carrot and zucchini noodles. (Keep the bowl nearby.) Cook the vegetables, stirring constantly, until just tender, 2-3 minutes. Transfer back to the original bowl.
Wash and dry the cilantro. Shave the leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl with the noodles.
Cut the chicken into bite-sized cubes and add to the bowl. Toss the salad until well combined.
To serve, place the salad in bowls, pour the sauce over top, and sprinkle with sesame seeds. Enjoy!

name: Thai Coconut Chicken Soup with Mushrooms & Bell Pepper
ingredients: ½ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
½ (13.5 fl oz) can coconut milk
instructions: Wash and dry mushrooms and bell pepper. Thinly slice mushrooms. Seed and small dice pepper. Transfer both to a medium bowl.
Peel and mince garlic and ginger. Grate 1 tsp of lime zest.
Heat a small saucepan over medium heat.
Cut chicken into bite-sized pieces.
Coat bottom of saucepan with oil. Add chicken and, stirring frequently, cook until cooked through, 3-4 minutes. Transfer to a plate.

Return saucepan to stove. Add more oil, garlic and ginger. Stir until fragrant, 15-30 seconds. Add mushrooms, bell pepper, lime zest and juice. Stirring frequently, cook until vegetables are tender, 2-3 minutes.
Add broth, coconut milk, fish sauce, honey, and chicken. Simmer for about 5 minutes.
Toast bread.
Wash and dry cilantro. Shave leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves. Cut remaining ½ lime into wedges.
To serve, pour soup into a bowl, garnish with cilantro and squeeze lime juice, and have bread on the side. Enjoy!

name: Thai Coconut Shrimp Curry with Basmati Rice
ingredients: ½ (13.5 fl oz) can coconut milk
¾ lb raw peeled shrimp, fresh or frozen
instructions: Rinse rice in a strainer until water runs clear and transfer to a small saucepan. Add water and salt. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, stir, and cover. Cook until liquid is absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
If using frozen shrimp, place in a medium bowl, cover with cold water, and set aside to thaw. If using fresh shrimp, skip this step.
Heat a sauté pan over medium-high heat.
Wash, seed, and julienne (cut into thin sticks) bell pepper. Wash and small dice tomatoes.
Coat bottom of pan with oil. Add pepper and, stirring frequently, cook until tender-crisp, 2-3 minutes.
Peel and mince garlic and ginger.
Add garlic, ginger, curry, and red pepper to pan. Cook until fragrant, 15-30 seconds.
Add tomatoes and coconut milk. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to medium and simmer until sauce thickens slightly, 5-6 minutes.
Wash and dry cilantro. Shave leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves.
Drain and rinse shrimp under cold water until there are no more ice chunks. Place on paper towels and pat dry. If using fresh shrimp, skip this step.
Add shrimp and ½ of the cilantro (save the rest for garnishing) to pan and stir. Cook until shrimp are opaque, 2-3 minutes.
Add lime juice and season with salt. Remove from heat.
Cut remaining lime into wedges.
Uncover rice and fluff with a fork.
To serve, place rice in a bowl, top with curry, and garnish with remaining cilantro and lime wedges. Enjoy!

name: Thai-Inspired Turkey Burgers with Napa Cabbage Slaw
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Place the ground turkey in a medium bowl.
Quarter the jalapeño pepper lengthwise; remove and discard the stem, seeds, and membranes. Finely dice the pepper and add to the turkey.

Using a knife, shave the cilantro leaves off the stems at a downward angle, working away from your body; discard the stems and finely chop the leaves. Add ½ of the cilantro to the turkey mixture and the other ½ to a large salad bowl (that will be used for the slaw).
Juice the lime; pour ½ into the bowl with the turkey mixture and the other ½ into the salad bowl.
Peel and grate or mince the ginger; add to the turkey mixture.
Preheat a grill pan or skillet over medium heat.
While the pan / skillet heats up, add soy sauce to the turkey mixture and mix the ingredients until well combined. Form the turkey mixture into 2 patties.
Once the pan / skillet is hot, add coconut oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Place the patties in the pan / skillet; cook until they are cooked through and browned, 3 to 5 minutes per side. Once done, transfer the patties to a plate.
Add soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, and honey to the salad bowl; whisk the dressing.
Trim off and discard the root end of the cabbage; halve the cabbage lengthwise, then thinly slice crosswise and add to the salad bowl.

Peel the carrots, then trim off the ends; discard the peels and trimmings. Using a box grater, coarsely grate the carrots and add to the salad bowl. Toss the salad until well coated with the dressing.
Toast the burger buns (optional).
To serve, place the bottom half of a bun on a plate, top with a patty and some of the slaw, and close with the top half of the bun. Serve with the remaining slaw on the side. Enjoy!

name: Thai Peanut Chicken Wraps with Broccoli Slaw
ingredients: ½ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
instructions: Heat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Slice chicken in half horizontally to form thin fillets. Season with salt and pepper.
Coat bottom of skillet with oil. Add broccoli slaw and, stirring frequently, cook until tender-crisp, 2-3 minutes. Transfer to a bowl.
Peel and mince garlic and ginger.
Return skillet to stove and add more oil. Add chicken and cook until cooked through, 2-3 minutes per side.
In a small bowl, prepare sauce by whisking together the minced garlic and ginger, peanut butter, honey, soy sauce, and water.
Roughly chop peanuts.
Add peanuts and sauce to bowl with broccoli and toss to coat.
Wash and dry bell pepper. Seed and slice into thin strips.
Thinly slice chicken into strips.
Heat skillet over medium heat.
Divide broccoli slaw, bell pepper, and chicken among tortillas. Roll up tightly and place seam side down in skillet. Cook until golden brown, 1-2 minutes per side.
To serve, place wraps on a plate. Enjoy!

name: Thai Pineapple Fried Rice with Chicken
ingredients: ½ lb chicken breasts, boneless skinless
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add water and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
Slice skin from pineapple, core, and cut into bite-sized pieces. Transfer to a bowl.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce the heat to low. Cook the rice until the liquid is fully absorbed, 15 to 18 minutes. Once done, remove the rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Peel and thinly slice onion into half rings. Peel and mince garlic. Wash and dry cilantro. Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Cut chicken into bite-sized pieces and season with salt.
Coat bottom of skillet with oil. Add chicken and, stirring occasionally, cook until cooked through, 2-3 minutes. Transfer to a plate.
Return skillet to stove and add more oil. Add onion, garlic, and crushed red pepper. Stirring frequently, cook until onion is softened, 2-3 minutes.
Uncover the rice and fluff with a fork.
Add rice and fish sauce to skillet. Stir until well combined, 1-2 minutes.
Stir in chicken, pineapple, cashews, ½ of the cilantro (save the rest for garnishing), and soy sauce. Remove from heat.
To serve, place rice in a bowl and garnish with remaining cilantro. Enjoy!

name: Thai Pineapple Fried Rice with Shrimp
ingredients: ¾ lb raw peeled shrimp, fresh or frozen
instructions: Rinse rice in a stainer until water runs clear and transfer to a small saucepan. Add water and salt. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, stir, and cover. Cook until liquid is absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Remove from heat and uncover to cool.
If using frozen shrimp, place in a medium bowl, cover with cold water, and set aside to thaw. If using fresh shrimp, skip this step.

Wash and dry bell pepper and green onions. Seed and small dice pepper. Trim and discard root ends and slice green onions diagonally into small pieces. Peel and thinly slice onion into half rings. Peel and mince garlic.
Cut skin off pineapple, core, and cut into bite-sized pieces.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Drain shrimp and rinse under cold water until there are no more ice chunks. Place on paper towels and pat dry.
Coat bottom of skillet with oil. Add shrimp and cook until pink, 2-3 minutes. Transfer to a plate.
Return skillet to stove and add more oil. Add bell pepper and red onion and, stirring frequently, cook until softened, 2-3 minutes.
Toss rice into a colander to drain off any excess water.
Add garlic, ¾ of the green onions (save the rest for garnishing), and red pepper to skillet. Stir and cook until fragrant, 15-30 seconds.
Stir in rice and fish sauce. Cook until heated through and well combined, 1-2 minutes.
Stir in shrimp and any juices, pineapple, cashews, and soy sauce.
To serve, place rice on a plate or in a bowl and garnish with remaining green onions. Enjoy!

name: Thai Scallop & Veggie Sauté with Spicy Peanut Sauce
ingredients: 16 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add broth and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce the heat to low. Cook the rice until the liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove the rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
While the rice cooks, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Separate broccoli into bite-sized florets and cut stems into smaller pieces.
Slice the zucchini into ¼-inch rounds.
Peel and thinly slice the carrot into ¼-inch rounds.
Peel and thinly slice onion into half rings.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Juice the lime into a medium bowl. Peel and mince the garlic and ginger and add them to the bowl with the lime juice.

Once the skillet is hot add the broccoli, zucchini, carrot, and onion. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are crisp-tender; 7-9 minutes. Once done, transfer to a medium bowl or large plate.
While veggies cook, finish preparing the dressing by whisking the peanut butter, soy sauce, water, and crushed red pepper into the bowl with the garlic, ginger, and lime juice. Set aside.
Pat the scallops dry with a paper towel. Season with salt and pepper.
Return the skillet to the heat, add the oil, and carefully add the scallops in a single layer; cook until they develop a nice sear and are opaque throughout, 1-2 minutes per side.
To serve, divide the rice into bowls. Top with sautéed vegetables and scallops; drizzle with peanut sauce and sprinkle with sesame seeds. Enjoy!

name: Thai-Style Omelet (Kai Jeow) with Spicy Cucumber-Herb Salad & Rice
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add broth and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Cook rice until liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Place oil, vinegar, fish sauce, sugar, and salt in a medium bowl; whisk to combine the dressing.
Peel, trim, and halve cucumber lengthwise; cut crosswise into thin half-moons. Add to the bowl with the dressing.

Thinly slice the chili pepper into rounds; add to the bowl with the cucumber. (Be careful with chili peppers; do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; pick mint leaves off the stems. Discard stems, roughly chop the leaves, and add to the bowl. Stir to combine the salad and set aside.
Trim green onions and cut crosswise into ¼-inch pieces. Place in another medium bowl.
Crack eggs into the bowl with the green onions. Add fish sauce and whisk to combine the egg batter.
Preheat a skillet over medium high heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom.

Add half the egg batter (a scant 1 cup per omelet) to the skillet and swirl to cover the bottom. As eggs begin to set, use a spatula to pull the cooked edges towards the center of the skillet. Then tilt the skillet, allowing the uncooked egg to move to the edges. Cook until set, about 3 minutes.
Fold the omelet in half and remove to a plate; cut in half. Loosely cover with aluminum foil.
Return skillet to medium heat and add more oil. Repeat with remaining egg batter.
To serve, divide rice, salad, and omelets between plates. Spoon chili-garlic sauce over the omelets and enjoy!

name: Thai Turkey Burger with Cucumber-Lettuce Salad, Spicy Mayo & Peanuts
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Divide between two medium bowls. (Set one bowl aside for the salad.)
Peel and mince ginger and shallot. Add both to the remaining bowl with the cilantro.

Quarter jalapeño pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon to reduce spice level. Mince and add to the bowl. (Be careful with jalapeños; do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Add turkey, bread crumbs, and fish sauce to the bowl, then mix with your hands until well combined. Form the turkey mixture into 2 equal-sized patties and place on a plate.
Preheat a grill pan, outdoor grill, or regular skillet over medium-high heat.

Once the pan is hot, coat with oil. Add burger patties and cook, undisturbed, for 5 minutes; flip patties and cook an additional 5-7 minutes, until cooked through. Once done, transfer to a clean plate.
Meanwhile, juice lime into the reserved bowl with the cilantro. Add oil, honey, and spices, then whisk to combine the dressing.
Trim, seed, and small dice bell pepper. Add to the bowl with the dressing.
Trim and quarter cucumber lengthwise, then cut crosswise into bite-sized pieces. Add to the bowl.
Chop (or tear) lettuce into bite-sized pieces. Add to the bowl.
Roughly chop peanuts. Add to the bowl, toss to combine the salad, and set aside.
Place mayo and hot sauce in a small bowl. Stir to combine the spicy mayo.
Toast the buns if desired.
Spread spicy mayo over the bottom half of each bun; top with burger patties and a small handful of salad. Close with the top half of each bun. Serve with remaining salad on the side and enjoy!

name: Three Mushroom & Parmesan Pilaf
ingredients: 12 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Heat olive oil in skillet over medium heat. Trim off and discard the ends of the shallots; peel and finely dice the shallot. Add to the skillet, stirring regularly.
Wash and dry all of the mushrooms.
Remove the stems of the portobello mushrooms; scrape out the gills using a spoon. Dice into 1-inch cubes and add to the skillet.
Slice the remaining mushrooms and add to the skillet.
Peel and mince garlic. Add to the skillet.
Season mushroom mixture with thyme, rosemary, salt, and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, until mushrooms are tender and shallots are translucent, 5-6 minutes.
Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to skillet. Add broth and bring mixture to a boil.
Lower heat to medium-low. Cover with a tight-fitting lid and cook without disturbing for 15-20 minutes.
Wash and dry parsley. Shave leaves off the stems; discard the stems and mince the leaves.
When rice is cooked, stir in butter and Parmesan cheese until melted. Top with prepared parsley. Serve warm, enjoy!

name: Tilapia with Cilantro-Orange Zucchini & Bell Pepper Sauté over Rice
ingredients: 4 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add water and salt, then bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Cook rice until liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim and large dice zucchini; place in a small bowl.
Trim, seed, and large dice bell pepper; add to the bowl with the zucchini.
Peel, halve, and large dice onion; add to the bowl and set aside.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the tilapia dry with paper towels and place on a plate; sprinkle cornstarch, salt, and pepper over both sides, pressing gently to adhere.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add tilapia and cook, flipping once, until crispy and easily flakes with a fork, about 6 minutes. Remove to a clean plate and loosely cover with aluminum foil; set aside.
Meanwhile, zest and juice orange into another small bowl.

Shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl with the orange juice, along with broth, soy sauce, additional cornstarch, and spices. Whisk to combine the sauce.
Return skillet to medium-high heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add more oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add veggies and sauté until fork-tender, 6-7 minutes.
Add sauce to the skillet with the veggies; continue to cook, stirring often, until sauce is thickened, about 1 minute.
To serve, divide rice, tilapia, veggies, and sauce between plates. Enjoy!

name: Tilapia Fish Tacos with Grapefruit-Avocado Salsa
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.

Slice off a piece from both grapefruit ends, then place it flat on one of the ends and slice off the peel (from top to bottom), exposing the flesh. Working over a bowl to catch the juices, cut out the segments of flesh from between the membranes, then cut them into ½-inch pieces. Transfer the pieces (and any leftover juice) to a medium bowl.
Halve the avocado lengthwise and twist the halves to separate, then remove the pit with a knife or spoon; scoop out and medium dice the flesh into ½-inch cubes. Add to the bowl.
Quarter the jalapeño pepper lengthwise; remove and discard the stem, seeds, and membranes. Finely dice the pepper and add to the salsa bowl.
Using a knife, shave the cilantro leaves off the stems at a downward angle, working away from your body; discard the stems and finely chop the leaves. Add to the salsa bowl.
Trim off and discard the ends of the shallot; peel and mince the shallot. Add to the salsa bowl.
Preheat a nonstick skillet over medium heat.
Pat the fish dry with paper towels and place on a plate; rub with olive oil and season with salt and pepper on both sides.
Once the skillet is hot, add the fish and cook until opaque and cooked through, 2 to 3 minutes per side. Once done, transfer to a plate and flake with a fork.
Drizzle the salsa with olive oil and season with cumin, salt, and pepper.
Wrap the tortillas in damp paper towels and microwave until heated through, 15 to 30 seconds.
To serve, divide the flaked tilapia among the tortillas and top with the salsa. Enjoy!

name: Toasted Naan with Smoked Salmon-Goat Cheese Spread & Chopped Salad
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Zest lemon into a small bowl, then juice it into a medium bowl.
Using a knife, shave dill leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add half of the dill to each bowl.
Chop salmon into ¼-inch pieces and add to the small bowl with the lemon zest.
Crumble goat cheese into the bowl with the salmon. Add yogurt and crushed red pepper; mash with a fork to combine the spread and set aside.
Arrange naan on a baking sheet pan. Place in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and bake, flipping halfway through, until crispy, about 10 minutes. Remove from the oven.
Meanwhile, peel and mince garlic. Add to the medium bowl with the lemon juice, along with oil, maple syrup, salt, and pepper. Whisk to combine the dressing.
Trim green onions; cut crosswise into ¼-inch pieces and add to the bowl with the dressing.
Trim and medium dice the cucumber; add to the bowl.
Trim off and discard tops and root ends of radishes; thinly slice and add to the bowl.
Halve tomatoes and add to the bowl. Toss to combine the salad.
Divide salmon-goat cheese spread between toasted naan and smooth out in an even layer. Cut into quarters.
To serve, divide naan and salad between plates. Enjoy!

name: Tofu & Bell Pepper Fajitas with Guacamole
instructions: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Halve the avocado lengthwise and twist the halves to separate, then remove the pit with a knife or spoon; scoop out the flesh into a small bowl and mash with a fork until smooth.

Using a knife, shave the cilantro leaves off the stems at a downward angle, working away from your body; discard the stems and finely chop the leaves. Add about ½ of the cilantro to the avocado and transfer the rest to a small bowl.
Trim off and discard the root end of the garlic; peel and mince or press the garlic. Add to the avocado.
Cut the lime in half; juice one half and add to the avocado, then cut the other half into wedges and transfer to a small bowl.
Season the avocado and other ingredients with salt and pepper, then mix to combine and set aside.
In a small bowl, combine and mix together chili powder, cumin, salt, and pepper.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.

Drain the tofu and pat dry with paper towels; holding a knife parallel to the cutting board, cut the tofu in half horizontally, then cut each half lengthwise into ½-inch-thick strips and transfer to a plate. Sprinkle the tofu with the spice mixture and rub until the strips are evenly coated.
Once the skillet is hot, add coconut oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add the tofu strips to the skillet; cook, turning occasionally, until they are golden brown, 8 to 12 minutes total. Once done, transfer to a large plate. Cook in batches if necessary.
While the tofu cooks, quarter the bell peppers lengthwise; remove and discard the stem, seeds, and membranes. Cut the quarters lengthwise into ¼-inch-thick strips and transfer to a medium bowl.
Trim off and discard the ends of the onion and remove the outer layer; thinly slice the onion and add to the bowl with the peppers.

Once the tofu has been transferred, add more coconut oil to the skillet, followed by the bell peppers and onion. Cook, stirring frequently, until the vegetables are tender-crisp, 3 to 5 minutes. Once done, transfer next to the tofu.
Wrap the tortillas in damp paper towels and microwave until heated through, 15 to 30 seconds.
To serve, divide the tortillas between plates and fill with the tofu strips and vegetables. Spoon the guacamole on top, sprinkle with the remaining cilantro, and garnish with lime wedges. Enjoy!

name: Tofu, Bell Pepper & Spinach in Peanut Sauce with Basmati Rice
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add broth and water; bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
Wash and dry spinach. (Skip this step if the spinach came pre-washed.)
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Drain and pat dry tofu. Cut into ½ inch sticks.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce the heat to low. Cook the rice until the liquid is fully absorbed, 15 to 18 minutes. Once done, remove the rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Wash, seed, and slice pepper into strips.
Coat bottom of skillet with oil. Add tofu and pepper. Gently stir fry until pepper is tender and tofu is lightly browned, 5-6 minutes.
Peel and mince the garlic. Wash, peel, and mince the ginger. Place both in a bowl with peanut butter, soy sauce, chili-garlic sauce, water, and maple syrup. Whisk to combine.
Pour in sauce and add spinach to skillet. Remove from heat and stir until spinach is just wilted, 1-2 minutes.
Uncover the rice and fluff with a fork.
Place rice in a bowl and top with tofu and veggies. Enjoy!

name: Tofu & Bell Pepper Stir Fry with Jasmine Rice
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add water to the saucepan; bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Quarter the bell peppers lengthwise; remove and discard the stems, seeds, and membranes. Large dice the sections (cut into ¾-inch cubes) and transfer to a medium bowl.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce the heat to low. Cook the rice until the liquid is fully absorbed, 15 to 18 minutes. Once done, remove the rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, drain and large dice the tofu (cut into ¾-inch cubes); place the cubes on paper towels or a clean towel and pat dry.
Once the skillet is hot, add coconut oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add the tofu to the skillet; cook, stirring occasionally, until golden brown, 6 to 8 minutes. Once done, transfer the tofu to a plate or bowl.
While the tofu cooks, peel and grate or mince the ginger; transfer to a small bowl.
Trim off and discard the root ends of the garlic; peel and mince or press the garlic. Add to the bowl with the ginger.
Once the tofu has been transferred, add more coconut oil to the skillet followed by the bell peppers, ginger, and garlic. Stir-fry the peppers until they begin to soften, 2 to 4 minutes.
While the peppers cook, trim off and discard the ends of the green onions; cut the onions crosswise into ¼-inch pieces at an angle and transfer to a small bowl.
In a small bowl, whisk together cornstarch with 2 tsp of water, then add soy sauce, sesame oil, and honey and whisk again.

Return the tofu to the skillet, add ½ of the green onions (save the rest for garnishing), and pour the sauce over top. Stir-fry until the vegetables and tofu are coated in the sauce and the sauce has thickened, 1 to 2 minutes.
To serve, place the rice into a bowl, top with the stir fry, and garnish with the remaining green onions. Enjoy!

name: Tofu Burrito Bowl with Cilantro-Lime Rice & Pico de Gallo
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add water and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce the heat to low. Cook the rice until the liquid is fully absorbed, 15 to 18 minutes. Once done, remove the rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Quarter the grape tomatoes and transfer to a medium bowl (that will be used for the salsa).
Quarter the jalapeño pepper lengthwise; remove and discard the stem, seeds, and membranes. Finely dice the pepper and add to the salsa bowl.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, drain and large dice the tofu (cut into ¾-inch cubes); place the cubes on paper towels or a clean towel and pat dry.
Once the skillet is hot, add coconut oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add the tofu to the skillet and season with chili powder, cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper; cook, stirring occasionally, until golden brown, 8 to 10 minutes. Once done, transfer the tofu to a bowl.

While the tofu cooks, trim off and discard the ends of the onion and remove the outer layer; thinly slice one half of the onion and transfer to a medium bowl, then small dice (cut into ¼-inch pieces) the other half and add to the salsa bowl.
Quarter the bell pepper lengthwise; remove and discard the stem, seeds, and membranes. Cut the quarters lengthwise into ¼-inch-thick strips and add to the medium bowl with the onion.

Once the tofu has been transferred, add more coconut oil to the skillet followed by the onion and bell pepper. Cook, stirring frequently, until the vegetables are browned and softened, 2 to 3 minutes.
Juice the lime; add about ½ of the juice to the salsa bowl and the other ½ to the rice.

Using a knife, shave the cilantro leaves off the stems at a downward angle, working away from your body; discard the stems and finely chop the leaves. Add about ½ of the cilantro to the salsa bowl and the other ½ to the rice.
Season the salsa with salt and stir to combine.
Fluff the rice with a fork and stir to combine with the lime and cilantro.
To serve, arrange the rice, veggie mixture, tofu, and salsa in a bowl. Enjoy!

name: Tofu & Eggplant Stir Fry with Basmati Rice
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Season the rice with salt and add water; bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Pick the basil leaves off the stems; discard the stems and roughly chop the leaves. Transfer to a small bowl and set aside.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce the heat to low. Cook the rice until the liquid is fully absorbed, 15 to 18 minutes. Once done, remove the rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Trim off and discard the root ends of the garlic; peel and mince or press the garlic. Transfer to a small bowl.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, drain and large dice the tofu (cut into ¾-inch cubes); place the cubes on paper towels or a clean towel and pat dry.
Once the skillet is hot, add coconut oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add the tofu to the skillet and cook, stirring occasionally, until golden brown, 8 to 10 minutes. Once done, transfer the tofu to a bowl.
While the tofu cooks, trim off and discard the ends of the eggplant; large dice the eggplant (cut into ¾-inch cubes).
Once the tofu has been transferred, add more coconut oil to the skillet followed by the garlic. Cook the garlic until fragrant, 15 to 30 seconds.
Add the eggplant to the skillet; cook, stirring occasionally, until the eggplant is tender, 6 to 8 minutes.
In a medium bowl, combine and whisk together water, soy sauce, rice vinegar, honey, sesame oil, cornstarch, and crushed red pepper.

Add the tofu and about ¾ of the basil (save the rest for garnishing) to the skillet, then pour in the sauce; stir until the tofu and eggplant are thoroughly coated in the sauce the sauce has thickened, 1 to 2 minutes.
Uncover the rice and fluff with a fork.
To serve, divide the rice between plates or bowls, top with the stir fry, and garnish with the remaining basil. Enjoy!

name: Tofu Fried Rice with Carrots & Peas
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a small saucepan. Add water and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce the heat to low. Cook the rice until the liquid is fully absorbed, 15 to 18 minutes. Once done, remove the rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Wash carrots and green onions. Peel and small dice carrots. Trim and discard root ends and chop onions. Transfer both to a plate. Measure out peas.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Drain and medium dice tofu. Transfer to paper towels and pat dry.
Coat bottom of skillet with oil. Add tofu and season with salt. Stirring occasionally, cook until lightly browned, 3-4 minutes.
Peel and small dice onion. Peel and mince garlic.

Transfer tofu to a plate and return skillet to stove. Add more oil to skillet, followed by garlic, yellow onion, ½ of the green onions (save the rest for garnishing), carrots, and peas. Stirring often, cook until carrots are tender, 3-4 minutes.
In a small bowl, whisk egg.
Move vegetables to one side of skillet and pour egg on the other side. Scramble egg until cooked and mix with vegetables.
Uncover the rice and fluff with a fork.
Add rice, tofu, and soy sauce to vegetables. Stir until well combined and heated through, 1-2 minutes.
To serve, place fried rice in a bowl and garnish with remaining green onions. Enjoy!

name: Tofu Lovers' Hot & Sour Soup with Mushrooms
ingredients: 32 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Cut tofu in half along the long side. Sandwich tofu between clean towels or paper towels and place on a baking sheet pan. Place a cutting board with something heavy on top and set aside to press out excess water.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, transfer tofu planks to a plate; season with salt and coat with cornstarch on both sides.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add tofu to the skillet and pan-fry, flipping once, until crispy and golden brown, 5-6 minutes per side. Remove to a clean plate and set aside.
Meanwhile, peel and mince or grate the ginger. Transfer to a medium saucepan along with broth, vinegar, soy sauce, oil, chili-garlic sauce, and salt.
Remove portobello mushroom stem and scrape out the gills. Cut mushroom cap in half and then crosswise into thin strips. Add to the pan with the broth.
Thinly slice white mushrooms and add to the pan; stir to combine and bring to a boil over high heat.
Meanwhile, in a small bowl, make a slurry by whisking water with cornstarch until smooth.

Once the broth comes to a boil, add the cornstarch slurry in a steady stream while stirring quickly. (Reserve bowl for later use.) Return soup to a boil, then cover and reduce heat to medium-low; let simmer until soup thickens slightly and mushrooms begin to soften, 2-3 minutes.
Slice tofu into thin strips.
Whisk eggs and salt together in the reserved bowl. Slowly pour the egg mixture into the soup, while gently stirring, to separate into strands.
Add tofu to the soup and stir to combine; cover and remove from heat.
Trim green onions and cut crosswise into ¼-inch pieces; stir half of the green onions into the soup (reserving the rest for garnish).
To serve, divide soup between bowls and sprinkle with reserved green onions. Enjoy!

name: Tofu & Soba Noodle Stir Fry with Spinach & Mushrooms
instructions: Fill a medium saucepan halfway with water and bring to a boil. Add salt and noodles and stir for a few seconds. Cook according to package directions. Drain and rinse under cold water.
Drain and medium dice tofu; place on paper towels and pat dry. Transfer to a medium bowl, drizzle with soy sauce, and toss to combine.
Wash and dry spinach, mushrooms, and green onions. Thinly slice the mushrooms. Trim root ends and chop onions. Peel and mince garlic and ginger.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Coat bottom of skillet with oil. Add tofu and, stirring occasionally, cook until browned, 3-4 minutes. Transfer to a plate.
In a small bowl, prepare sauce by whisking together soy sauce, sesame oil, and honey.
Return skillet to stove and add more oil. Add garlic, ginger, and crushed red pepper. Cook until fragrant, 15-30 seconds.
Add mushrooms and cook until just tender, 2-3 minutes. Add spinach and gently stir until wilted, 1-2 minutes.
Return tofu to skillet. Add soba noodles, green onions, and sauce. Stir to combine and cook until heated through, 1-2 minutes.
To serve, place stir fry in a bowl. Enjoy!

name: Tomato-Basil Soup with Cheddar Grilled Cheese
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Remove butter from fridge and allow to soften in the microwave or on the counter.
Heat a medium saucepan over medium heat.
Peel and small dice onion. Peel and mince garlic.
Coat bottom of saucepan with oil. Add onion and garlic; begin cooking while you chop the carrot and celery.
Wash and thinly slice carrot and celery; add to saucepan. Stirring occasionally, cook until carrots and celery have softened, 6-7 minutes.
Wash and medium dice tomatoes.
Wash basil. Pick leaves off the stems; discard the stems and thinly slice the leaves into ribbons.
Add fresh and canned tomatoes, broth, salt, and pepper to saucepan. Stir and bring to a boil. Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for about 10 minutes.
Heat a skillet over medium-low heat.
Grate ½ cup of cheddar.
Spread butter onto 1 side of each bread slice and place buttered-side down on a flat surface.

Divide cheddar between 2 of the bread slices and top with the other slices. Place in the skillet and gently press down with a spatula. Cook until cheese is melted and bread is golden brown, 2-4 minutes per side.
Add basil to the soup and stir. Purée soup until smooth using a hand or regular blender.
Pour soup into a bowl and service with grilled cheese on the side. Enjoy!

name: Tomato, Kale & Cannellini Bean Skillet with Parmesan Polenta
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: In a small saucepan, bring broth and water to a boil. Reduce heat to low and gradually add polenta in a thin steady stream, while whisking, until the polenta is incorporated into the liquid. Cook, stirring occasionally, until polenta is soft and the texture is creamy, 15-25 minutes.
Meanwhile, drain and rinse beans in a colander; set aside to drain further.
Peel and small dice onion. Peel and mince garlic; place both in a medium bowl.
Wash, dry, seed, and medium dice bell pepper; add to the bowl with the onion and garlic.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add veggies and cook, stirring occasionally, until starting to soften, 3-4 minutes.
Add beans, tomatoes, and spices to the skillet; stir to combine, and cook until heated through, about 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash and dry kale. Fold leaves in half lengthwise and slice off the stems. Chop or tear leaves into bite-sized pieces.
Add kale to the skillet in handfuls, waiting for the kale to wilt slightly before adding the next handful. Cook, stirring occasionally, until tender, 3-5 minutes.
While the kale cooks, finely grate Parmesan.
Add half the Parmesan, salt, and pepper to the polenta and stir to combine. If the polenta is too firm, add hot water, 1 tablespoon at a time, until you reach a desired consistency.
To serve, divide polenta between bowls; top with veggie-bean skillet and remaining Parmesan. Enjoy!

name: Tomato, Mushroom & Kalamata Olive Penne with Parmesan
instructions: Fill a medium saucepan halfway with water, cover, and bring to a boil. Uncover, add salt and pasta, and stir for a few seconds. Cook until desired firmness, 8-10 minutes. Drain.
Wash tomatoes and mushrooms. Halve the tomatoes. Thinly slice the mushrooms. Peel and mince garlic.
Heat a sauté pan over medium heat.
Coat bottom of skillet with oil. Add garlic and crushed red pepper and cook until fragrant, 15-30 seconds.
Add tomatoes, mushrooms, Italian seasoning, salt, and pepper. Stirring occasionally, cook until mushrooms are tender and tomatoes are juicy, 2-3 minutes.
Shave or grate Parmesan cheese.
Add olives and pasta to pan and toss to combine.
To serve, place pasta on a plate or in a bowl and garnish with Parmesan. Enjoy!

name: Tomato-Spinach Orzo with Ground Turkey, Parmesan & Parsley
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, peel and mince shallot.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add shallot, turkey, and spices; cook, breaking the meat apart with a spoon, until browned and crumbly, 4-5 minutes.

Add broth, tomato sauce, and orzo to the skillet; stir to combine and bring to a simmer. Once simmering, reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and cook, stirring occasionally, until liquid is mostly absorbed and orzo is desired firmness, 10-15 minutes.
Meanwhile, finely grate Parmesan. Place in a small bowl.
Wash, dry, and shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl with the Parmesan, stir to combine, and set aside.
Wash and dry spinach (skip this step if it came pre-washed).
When the orzo is done, add spinach to the skillet in handfuls, waiting for it to wilt slightly before adding the next handful.
Add half of the Parmesan-parsley mixture to the skillet and stir to combine. Remove from heat. (Reserve remaining Parmesan mixture for serving.)
To serve, divide orzo between plates or bowls; top with reserved Parmesan mixture. Enjoy!

name: Tomato-White Bean Soup with Orzo, Kale & Parmesan
ingredients: 20 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Preheat a medium saucepan over medium heat.
While the pan heats up, peel, halve, and small dice onion.
Once the pan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add onion and salt; cook, stirring occasionally, until onion is soft, 5-7 minutes.
Meanwhile, drain and rinse beans.
Peel and thinly slice garlic.
When the onions are soft, add garlic and crushed red pepper to the pan. Cook, stirring occasionally, until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add beans, tomatoes, and broth to the pan. Bring the soup to a boil over medium-high heat. Once boiling, reduce heat to medium and simmer until slightly thickened, about 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, wash, dry, and fold kale leaves in half lengthwise and slice off the stems; cut leaves crosswise into thin (shred-like) pieces. Place in a medium bowl and set aside.
When the soup is slightly thickened, add orzo. Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until pasta is almost tender, 5-6 minutes more.
While the soup is cooking, finely grate Parmesan.

When the orzo is almost done, add kale to the pan in handfuls, waiting for it to wilt slightly before adding the next handful. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the kale and orzo are tender, about 1 minute. Remove from heat.
Add vinegar and half of the Parmesan to the soup, then stir to combine. (Reserve remaining Parmesan for serving.)
To serve, divide soup between bowls. Top with reserved Parmesan and drizzle with oil. Enjoy!

name: Tossed Skillet Lasagna with Zucchini, Carrot, Ricotta & Basil
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Fill a medium saucepan about halfway with hot water (from the tap); cover and bring to a boil over high heat.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.

Break lasagna noodles into thirds. Once the water in the pan is boiling, uncover, add salt and broken noodles, and stir for a few seconds. Cook until desired firmness, 8-10 minutes. Once done, drain in a colander and set aside.
While the noodles are cooking, trim the zucchini and carrot. Run the peeler along the zucchini and carrot to make long, noodle-like strips. Place both in a medium bowl.
Medium dice tomato; add to the bowl with the zucchini and carrot.
Preheat a skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, peel and mince garlic.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add veggies, garlic, and spices to the skillet; cook, stirring occasionally, until veggies are tender, 3-4 minutes.
Meanwhile, pick basil leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and thinly slice into ribbons.
Coarsely grate mozzarella.

When the veggies are done, add lasagna noodles, half of the basil, and tomato sauce to the skillet; stir to combine and continue to cook until heated through, about 2 minutes. Remove from heat. (Reserve remaining basil for serving.)
Top lasagna with dollops of ricotta and sprinkle with mozzarella.
Place skillet in the oven and bake until the mozzarella is melted and golden, 7-8 minutes. Remove from oven.
To serve, divide lasagna between plates or bowls and top with reserved basil. Enjoy!

name: Tropical Fruit & Quinoa Salad with Honey-Lime Dressing
ingredients: 12 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: In a small saucepan, combine quinoa and broth; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to a simmer, cover, and cook for 15 minutes. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Cut off skin from pineapple, core, and cut into bite-sized pieces. Transfer to a large mixing bowl.

Wash mango, kiwifruit, bell pepper, and jalapeño. Peel the mango, slice flesh away from pit, and medium dice. Peel and medium dice the kiwifruit. Seed and medium dice bell pepper. Seed and mince jalapeño. Peel and small dice onion. Add ingredients to bowl with pineapple.
Peel and mince garlic. In a small mixing bowl, prepare dressing by whisking together garlic, lime juice, oil, honey, salt, and pepper.
Trim green onions and cut crosswise into ¼-inch pieces at an angle.
Uncover quinoa, fluff with a fork, and add to bowl.
Pour dressing over top salad and toss.
